Nice wand for charm work." ... "Your father, on the other hand, favored a mahogany wand. Eleven inches. Pliable. A little more power and excellent for transfiguration.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at Diagon Alley: Shops and Wondrous Finds

metadata.description: I was told the exact wand that caused my scar: a thirteen-and-a-half inch yew wand. Ollivander said he sold it and that it was very powerful.
metadata.source_text: “I’m sorry to say I sold the wand that did it,” he said softly. “Thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Powerful wand, very powerful, and in the wrong hands . . .
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at Diagon Alley: Shops and Wondrous Finds

metadata.description: Hearing Ollivander say he sold the wand that did the scar made me feel uneasy and changed how I think about that scar — it wasn't just an accident, someone used a very powerful wand on me.
metadata.source_text: “I’m sorry to say I sold the wand that did it,” he said softly. “Thirteen-and-a-half inches. Yew. Powerful wand, very powerful, and in the wrong hands . . .
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at Diagon Alley: Shops and Wondrous Finds

metadata.description: Meeting Mr Ollivander up close felt strange; his silvery eyes made me uncomfortable and I noticed him studying me like he already knew me, which makes him feel a bit creepy and oddly familiar.
metadata.source_text: Mr Ollivander moved closer to Harry. Harry wished he would blink. Those silvery eyes were a bit creepy. ... Mr Ollivander had come so close that he and Harry were almost nose to nose.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at Diagon Alley: Shops and Wondrous Finds

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the visit to the wand shop in Diagon Alley, so I don't know what was said or discovered there.

metadata.description: I learned that Ollivander wands each have cores made from unicorn hair, phoenix feather, or dragon heartstring and that no two wands or magical creatures are exactly the same.
metadata.source_text: Every Ollivander wand has a core of a powerful magical substance, Mr Potter. We use unicorn hairs, phoenix tail feathers, and the heartstrings of dragons.
metadata.scene_title: Ollivanders: The Wand Chooses the Wizard

metadata.description: I began to think that a wand really does choose the wizard — trying lots of wands felt pointless until one felt warm and right in my hand, and then magic happened.
metadata.source_text: He felt a sudden warmth in his fingers. He raised the wand above his head, brought it swishing down through the dusty air and a stream of red and gold sparks shot from the end like a firework
metadata.scene_title: Ollivanders: The Wand Chooses the Wizard

metadata.description: I noticed Ollivander's intense interest in me; he's more curious and eager than nervous, like he enjoys finding the right match and is pleased when a wand responds.
metadata.source_text: The more wands Mr Ollivander pulled from the shelves, the happier he seemed to become.
metadata.scene_title: Ollivanders: The Wand Chooses the Wizard

metadata.scene_title: Ollivanders: The Wand Chooses the Wizard

metadata.description: I've just been told that the phoenix feather in my wand came from the same bird that gave the feather in another wand — only one other feather existed from that phoenix, and my wand was chosen for me.
metadata.source_text: It so happens that the phoenix whose tail feather is in your wand, gave another feather — just one other.
metadata.scene_title: After Wand Purchase: Reassurance and Departure

metadata.description: I thought everyone calling me special was nonsense because I don't remember magic or the night my parents died, but after hearing about the wand choosing me and the connection to the one that gave me my scar, I feel more puzzled and aware that people expect great things of me.
metadata.source_text: Everyone thinks I’m special," he said at last. "All those people in the Leaky Cauldron, Professor Quirrell, Mr Ollivander . . . but I don’t know anything about magic at all. How can they expect great things? I’m famous and I can’t even remember what I’m famous for. I don’t know what happened when Vol-, sorry — I mean, the night my parents died.
metadata.scene_title: After Wand Purchase: Reassurance and Departure

metadata.description: Hagrid's kindness makes me feel safer; he leant across and smiled under his beard and told me not to worry, promising help and that I should write if I have trouble with the Dursleys. That makes me trust him more than I did before.
metadata.source_text: Don’ you worry, Harry. You’ll learn fast enough. ... Any problems with the Dursleys, send me a letter with yer owl, she’ll know where to find me. . . . See yeh soon, Harry.
metadata.scene_title: After Wand Purchase: Reassurance and Departure

metadata.description: I've learned that Hogwarts students catch a train from a secret platform called nine and three-quarters — the ticket Hagrid gave me says to go from platform nine and three-quarters at eleven o'clock.
metadata.source_text: I just take the train from platform nine and three-quarters at eleven o’clock," he read.

metadata.description: I realised for the first time that I don't actually know where Hogwarts is; I thought Hagrid had told me but seeing the ticket made me see I'm clueless about the place's location.
metadata.source_text: "Where is this school, anyway?" "I don't know," said Harry, realizing this for the first time.

metadata.description: Uncle Vernon seems to be mocking and unsupportive about anything to do with magic; his grin and the way he left made me feel he's deliberately cruel and not to be trusted with kindness.
metadata.source_text: "Have a good term," said Uncle Vernon with an even nastier smile. He left without another word.

metadata.source_text: Chocolate Frogs have cards inside them, you know, to collect — famous witches and wizards.

metadata.description: Blimey, I wasn't alone anymore; meeting the Weasley twins and sitting with Ron made me feel for the first time like I could belong and share things with other people.
metadata.source_text: He put Hedwig inside first and then started to shove and heave his trunk toward the train door. "Want a hand?" ... With the twins’ help, Harry’s trunk was at last tucked away in a corner of the compartment.

metadata.description: I think Ron is someone I can sit and eat with — he shared his sandwiches and we talked about Chocolate Frog cards, so I feel friendlier toward him already.
metadata.source_text: Harry went out into the corridor. ... Harry brought it all back in to the compartment and tipped it onto an empty seat. "Hungry, are you?" "Starving," said Harry...

metadata.description: I read that Albus Dumbledore is the current Headmaster of Hogwarts and is famous for beating Grindelwald, discovering twelve uses of dragon’s blood, and working on alchemy with Nicolas Flamel.
metadata.source_text: ALBUS DUMBLEDORE CURRENTLY HEADMASTER OF HOGWARTS Considered by many the greatest wizard of modern times, Dumbledore is particularly famous for his defeat of the Dark wizard Grindelwald in 1945, for the discovery of the twelve uses of dragon’s blood, and his work on alchemy with his partner, Nicolas Flamel.

metadata.description: I noticed that magical pictures move — Dumbledore’s face vanished from the card and then sidled back in and smiled, which is nothing like Muggle photos that don’t move.
metadata.source_text: Harry turned the card back over and saw, to his astonishment, that Dumbledore’s face had disappeared. "He’s gone!" ... Harry stared as Dumbledore sidled back into the picture on his card and gave him a small smile.

metadata.description: I’m starting to feel a prickle of fear whenever You-Know-Who is mentioned; hearing about dangerous events like the Gringotts break-in makes me uneasy about the magical world.
metadata.source_text: 'Course, everyone gets scared when something like this happens in case You-Know-Who’s behind it.' ... He was starting to get a prickle of fear every time You-Know-Who was mentioned.

metadata.description: I know Hermione reads everything and already knows loads about me and Hogwarts — she introduced herself fast and said she’d done background reading and knew I was in certain classes.
metadata.source_text: "I know all about you, of course — I got a few extra books for background reading, and you’re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century."

metadata.description: I've learned a lot from extra books: I already know about Harry’s classes and Modern Magical History and other course details because I read background material before arriving.
metadata.source_text: "I know all about you, of course — I got a few extra books for background reading, and you’re in Modern Magical History and The Rise and Fall of the Dark Arts and Great Wizarding Events of the Twentieth Century."

metadata.description: I really think Gryffindor sounds best and I hope I’m placed there; I suppose Ravenclaw wouldn’t be too bad but Gryffindor seems by far the best to me.
metadata.source_text: "Do either of you know what House you’ll be in? I’ve been asking around, and I hope I’m in Gryffindor, it sounds by far the best; I hear Dumbledore himself was in it, but I suppose Ravenclaw wouldn’t be too bad."

metadata.description: I expect to help look for Neville’s lost toad and I took him to search because I like to be useful and practical; I introduced myself quickly so they’d know who I am.
metadata.source_text: "Anyway, we’d better go and look for Neville’s toad. You two had better change, you know, I expect we’ll be there soon."

metadata.description: I know my family’s House: my brothers, Mum and Dad were in Gryffindor, and I’m worried about what they’ll say if I’m not put there.
metadata.source_text: "Gryffindor," said Ron. "Mum and Dad were in it, too. I don’t know what they’ll say if I’m not."

metadata.description: I’m worried I might end up in Slytherin and that would depress me; I keep thinking about how awful it would be if they put me in Slytherin.
metadata.source_text: "I don’t suppose Ravenclaw would be too bad, but imagine if they put me in Slytherin."

metadata.description: I can’t help teasing Neville about losing his toad, and I’m proud of handing around things like Scabbers and my wand — George gave me the spell that didn’t work, and I blame him a bit.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve lost him! He keeps getting away from me!" ... "Stupid spell — George gave it to me, bet he knew it was a dud."

metadata.description: I learned that the Sorting Hat thinks I have plenty of courage, a decent mind, real talent, and a thirst to prove myself — it said all that right into my ear.
metadata.source_text: "Plenty of courage, I see. Not a bad mind either. There’s talent, oh my goodness, yes — and a nice thirst to prove yourself, now that’s interesting. . . ."

metadata.description: I was terrified of being put in Slytherin, and hearing the Hat suggest Slytherin made me more certain I didn't want it — I felt an awful relief when it finally shouted Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: "Not Slytherin, not Slytherin."

metadata.description: I noticed the Weasley twins cheered for me and Percy shook my hand, and Hagrid gave me a thumbs up — I felt an instant warmth toward them for welcoming me so loudly.
metadata.source_text: "We got Potter! We got Potter!"

metadata.description: I've learned that when my name was called I was so eager I practically ran to the stool and shoved the Hat on my head straight away.
metadata.source_text: "Granger, Hermione!" "GRYFFINDOR!"

metadata.description: I felt confident enough in my place that as soon as the Hat was on I expected Gryffindor — it was almost instant, which made me pleased and a bit relieved.
metadata.source_text: "Granger, Hermione!" "GRYFFINDOR!"

metadata.description: Being sorted into Gryffindor with people like Harry and Ron nearby made me feel connected to them as fellow Gryffindors from the very start.
metadata.source_text: "GRYFFINDOR!"

metadata.description: I saw Harry get sorted and heard the Hat debate him — I learned that the Hat can argue out loud about where to place someone and listens to what the student wants.
metadata.source_text: "Not Slytherin, eh? said the small voice. Are you sure? You could be great, you know, it’s all here in your head..."

metadata.description: When Harry was put in Gryffindor and the hall cheered, I felt proud and relieved — his being with us makes Gryffindor feel even better, and I groaned earlier when Hermione was sorted because I was nervous.
metadata.source_text: "GRYFFINDOR!" Ron groaned.

metadata.description: Seeing Harry chosen for Gryffindor and the Weasley twins shouting about him made me realise he'd already have friends here and that I might be glad he's in the same House.
metadata.source_text: "We got Potter! We got Potter!"

metadata.description: I recognized Professor Dumbledore from a Chocolate Frog card I got on the train; his silver hair lit up the hall like the ghosts.
metadata.source_text: Harry recognized him at once from the card he’d gotten out of the Chocolate Frog on the train.

metadata.description: I noticed Professor Quirrell wearing a large purple turban and looking very peculiar.
metadata.source_text: Harry spotted Professor Quirrell, too, the nervous young man from the Leaky Cauldron. He was looking very peculiar in a large purple turban.

metadata.description: I learned Ron had been sorted into Gryffindor and I was relieved and clapped when the Hat shouted Gryffindor for him.
metadata.source_text: a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!” Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.

metadata.description: I discovered the feast food piles itself on the plates and tastes delicious; there was far more food than I'd ever been allowed to eat at the Dursleys.
metadata.source_text: The dishes in front of him were now piled with food... Harry piled his plate with a bit of everything... It was all delicious.

metadata.description: I was shown Nearly Headless Nick, the Gryffindor ghost, who introduced himself and even demonstrated being nearly headless by swinging his head onto his shoulder.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t think I’ve introduced myself? Sir Nicholas de Mimsy-Porpington at your service. Resident ghost of Gryffindor Tower.” ... “Like this,” he said irritably. He seized his left ear and pulled. His whole head swung off his neck and fell onto his shoulder

metadata.description: Seeing how different Hogwarts life is — the food, the ghosts, the sorting — made me realize school here is far more magical and kind than anything with the Dursleys.
metadata.source_text: The dishes in front of him were now piled with food... Harry piled his plate with a bit of everything... It was all delicious.

metadata.description: I'm glad Ron got Gryffindor and sitting beside him makes me feel less alone; clapping for him felt natural and friendly.
metadata.source_text: a second later the hat had shouted, “GRYFFINDOR!” Harry clapped loudly with the rest as Ron collapsed into the chair next to him.

I felt a sudden, sharp pain shoot across my scar when that hooked-nosed teacher looked at me directly. It was a real, physical thing and it went as quickly as it came.
metadata.source_text: and a sharp, hot pain shot across the scar on Harry’s forehead.

metadata.description: I got a bad feeling from that teacher's look; I don't like him at all. After that stare I felt sure he disliked me.
metadata.source_text: Harder to shake off was the feeling Harry had gotten from the teacher’s look — a feeling that he didn’t like Harry at all.

metadata.description: Percy told me the hooked-nosed teacher is Professor Snape and that he teaches Potions but wants Quirrell's job; now I associate that man with Potions and the Dark Arts.
metadata.source_text: Oh, you know Quirrell already, do you? No wonder he’s looking so nervous, that’s Professor Snape. He teaches Potions, but he doesn’t want to — everyone knows he’s after Quirrell’s job. Knows an awful lot about the Dark Arts, Snape.

metadata.description: I'm particularly interested in Transfiguration; I know it's supposed to be very difficult and I'm eager to start learning it properly.
metadata.source_text: I do hope they start right away, there’s so much to learn, I’m particularly interested in Transfiguration, you know, turning something into something else, of course, it’s supposed to be very difficult —

metadata.description: Percy said we'll be starting small with Transfiguration, matches into needles and that sort of thing, so I'm prepared to begin with simple exercises rather than advanced transformations.
metadata.source_text: You’ll be starting small, just matches into needles and that sort of thing —

metadata.description: Percy spoke to me about lessons in a precise, authoritative way; I now see him as someone who takes school rules and procedures seriously.
metadata.source_text: On Harry’s other side, Percy Weasley and Hermione were talking about lessons ("I do hope they start right away..."; "You’ll be starting small, just matches into needles and that sort of thing —").

metadata.description: I asked Neville about his family and learned that his Gran raised him and that his Great Uncle Algie kept trying to force magic out of him; Neville didn't show magic until he was eight.
metadata.source_text: Well, my gran brought me up and she’s a witch," said Neville, "but the family thought I was all-Muggle for ages..."

metadata.description: Hearing Neville's story about bouncing from the window made me think Neville's family had been foolish to doubt him; their surprise shows how uncertain they were about magic in him.
metadata.source_text: They were all really pleased, Gran was crying, she was so happy. And you should have seen their faces when I got in here — they thought I might not be magic enough to come, you see.

metadata.description: After listening to Neville, I feel more sympathetic toward him; his family finally accepted he was magical and even bought him a toad, which shows they cared once they believed.
metadata.source_text: Great Uncle Algie was so pleased he bought me my toad.

metadata.source_text: Harry didn’t have the faintest idea what a bezoar was.

metadata.description: I've got the knowledge about magical plants — I know distinctions between poisons like monkshood and wolfsbane even if I didn't get to say it aloud before Snape cut me off.

metadata.description: I felt determined and anxious to answer Snape's question; being stopped made me realise how important it is to assert myself in class when I do know things.

metadata.scene_title: Duel Challenge, Hermione's Rebuke, and Getting Locked Out

metadata.description: I learned that the Fat Lady sometimes goes off on nighttime visits, leaving the portrait empty so we can be locked out of Gryffindor Tower.

metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I felt we had to move quickly and quietly; when I heard a snuffling I became suddenly sharp and urgent, convinced we could be caught if we didn't tuck in and creep away.

metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I rely on Ron and Hermione to follow my lead in dangerous moments; when Filch spoke I waved madly for the others to follow me and expected them to obey without argument.
metadata.source_text: Horror-struck, Harry waved madly at the other three to follow him as quickly as possible; they scurried silently toward the door, away from Filch’s voice.
metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I've discovered that when the Fat Lady goes on a nighttime visit the portrait is empty and the Gryffindor password won't get you back into the Tower.

metadata.description: I became annoyed and a bit desperate — I thought I had to come along with them or Filch would catch me, so I insisted I was coming despite being told I was not welcome.
metadata.source_text: "I’m coming with you," she said. "You are not." "D’you think I’m going to stand out here and wait for Filch to catch me? If he finds all three of us I’ll tell him the truth, that I was trying to stop you, and you can back me up."
metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I expect Ron and Harry to back me up if Filch asks questions; I was ready to tell the truth and count on them to support my version so I wouldn't be punished alone.

metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I knew and told Neville the password was 'Pig snout', though it wouldn't help while the Fat Lady was away.
metadata.source_text: "Keep your voice down, Neville. The password’s ‘Pig snout’ but it won’t help you now, the Fat Lady’s gone off somewhere."
metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I got angrier and more protective about not being late; I warned both Hermione and Neville that if they got us caught I'd learn the Curse of the Bogies and use it on them, which shows I'm serious about avoiding punishment.

metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I feel irritated with Hermione for nearly getting us into trouble and I short-temperedly blame her and Neville for risking all of us, glaring at them when time was tight.

metadata.scene_title: Searching the Castle, Filch, and Narrow Escape

metadata.description: I realise now that I can miss important details when I'm distracted by the obvious danger; I shouldn't assume I've seen everything in a tense moment.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t looking at its feet, I was too busy with its heads.

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione snap and then storm off makes me see her as someone who cares enough to scold us when we're reckless; she's more firm and furious than I sometimes expect.
metadata.source_text: She stood up, glaring at them. 'I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled.'

metadata.description: I noticed the creature was standing on a trapdoor, not the floor, so it's obviously guarding something underneath.
metadata.source_text: No, not the floor. It was standing on a trapdoor. It’s obviously guarding something.

metadata.description: I'm angrier now because I believe everyone was being careless; I think our actions could have gotten us killed or expelled and that must be taken seriously.
metadata.source_text: I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled.

metadata.description: Because they failed to see the trapdoor, I feel exasperated with them; I view my friends as careless in moments when I expect them to look properly.
metadata.source_text: You don’t use your eyes, any of you, do you? ... I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled.

metadata.description: I reckon the school is being daft for keeping dangerous things locked up; I feel more convinced that it's unfair and risky now.
metadata.source_text: What do they think they’re doing, keeping a thing like that locked up in a school?

metadata.description: Watching Hermione get angry and walk off makes me realise she's serious about our safety and rules, and I feel surprised and a bit guilty for making her so cross.
metadata.source_text: She stood up, glaring at them. 'I hope you’re pleased with yourselves. We could all have been killed — or worse, expelled. Now, if you don’t mind, I’m going to bed.'

metadata.description: I feel proper proud and a bit stunned — I didn't expect to have a Nimbus Two Thousand and now I can't stop thinking about Quidditch and the field.
metadata.source_text: "He bolted his dinner that evening without noticing what he was eating, and then rushed upstairs with Ron to unwrap the Nimbus Two Thousand at last."

metadata.source_text: "Comets look flashy, but they’re not in the same league as the Nimbus."

metadata.description: I'm even more impressed with Harry now; his broom has proper quality and that's proper good for us — it's doing us so much good.
metadata.source_text: "Yes, don’t stop now," said Ron, "it’s doing us so much good."

metadata.description: I feel a bit boastful and protective toward Harry; I tease Malfoy and stand by Harry when he's shown the broom, so our friendship feels stronger.

metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Rules and the Golden Snitch

metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Rules and the Golden Snitch

metadata.description: I now see Wood as direct and a bit reassuring — he handed me the bat, made me face a Bludger, explained everything plainly, and joked a bit about the Weasleys being like human Bludgers.

metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Rules and the Golden Snitch

metadata.source_text: Now, don’t forget that nice wrist movement we’ve been practicing! "Swish and flick, remember, swish and flick."

metadata.description: I think Hermione isn't just annoying — seeing her in tears made me realise she can get hurt by what people say; I felt surprised and a bit sorry for her.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears.

metadata.description: I've noticed Ron can be cruel to Hermione; after he called her a nightmare I saw how upset she got and I'm more aware that Ron's words affect her and the way I should respond.
metadata.source_text: “It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”

metadata.description: I feel upset and disappointed that people treat me poorly for correcting them; I didn't expect Ron's remark to make me cry and feel isolated from the others.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears.

metadata.description: I realise now that my classmates, especially Ron, think badly of me for being pedantic, and that perception is making me feel alone and less willing to be around them right now.
metadata.source_text: “It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”

metadata.source_text: “Wingardium Leviosa!” he shouted, waving his long arms like a windmill.

“You’re saying it wrong,” Harry heard Hermione snap. “It’s Wing-gar-dium Levi-o-sa, make the ‘gar’ nice and long.”

“ You do it, then, if you’re so clever,” Ron snarled.

“ It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”

“It’s no wonder no one can stand her,” he said to Harry as they pushed their way into the crowded corridor, “she’s a nightmare, honestly.”

Harry caught a glimpse of her face — and was startled to see that she was in tears.

metadata.description: I just found out there's a troll in the dungeons; Quirrell came running in saying exactly that, then fainted.
metadata.source_text: Troll — in the dungeons — thought you ought to know.

metadata.description: I'm worried now that Hermione might be in danger because she doesn't know about the troll; I suddenly realised she could be unaware and that changes how urgent everything feels.
metadata.source_text: I've just thought — Hermione.

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hermione; when I thought she didn't know about the troll I grabbed Ron and got anxious to find her, which shows how much I care.
metadata.source_text: I've just thought — Hermione.

metadata.description: I'm more suspicious about odd goings-on in the castle now; seeing Snape head off instead of the dungeons and smelling that horrible stench made me think something stranger's going on than just a troll in the dungeons.
metadata.source_text: He crossed the corridor and disappeared from view. "What's he doing?" Harry whispered. "Why isn't he down in the dungeons with the rest of the teachers?" "Search me."

metadata.description: I'm uneasy about Snape; when Harry and I saw him slip away and not go to the dungeons it made me wonder what Snape's up to, so I trust him a bit less in moments like this.
metadata.source_text: "Percy!" hissed Ron, pulling Harry behind a large stone griffin. Peering around it, however, they saw not Percy but Snape.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Halloween feast and the troll alarm, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
I realised the troll had the key in the lock and that if I could grab it I could lock the troll away, so I leapt and managed to get the key and slam the door shut.
metadata.source_text: The key’s in the lock," Harry muttered. "We could lock it in."

metadata.description: I felt terrified for Hermione when I heard that scream — I used to hope things would sort themselves out, but I now believe I must act fast to protect my friends.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione!" they said together.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: When Hermione was in danger I felt a fierce need to save her; I know now I will run back into danger for my friends without hesitation.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint."
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: I discovered a mountain troll was in the girls' bathroom, smashing sinks and advancing on me, which was horrifying and made me nearly faint.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint. The troll was advancing on her, knocking the sinks off the walls as it went.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: Being confronted by the troll has shaken me; I realise I can be helpless and that I need others to help me in moments of real danger.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: After Ron and Harry risked themselves to reach me, I feel a deeper gratitude and reliance on them; I understand how much they care when I am scared.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione!" they said together.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: I realised locking the troll in was a good idea and nervously agreed; then when Hermione screamed I knew we had to turn back and try to save her.
metadata.source_text: "Good idea," said Ron nervously.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: I was pale with fear when I heard the scream and saw it was the girls' bathroom; I've changed from thinking we might avoid danger to knowing we've got to face it head-on for our mates.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, no," said Ron, pale as the Bloody Baron. "It’s the girls’ bathroom!"
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: Hearing Hermione scream made me feel protective of her; I know now I'm willing to risk myself to help my friends when they're in real danger.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione!" they said together.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Troll and Locking the Bathroom

metadata.description: I found out that if you shove your wand right up a troll's nostril you can make it howl and flail, which can buy time in a fight.
metadata.source_text: The troll couldn’t feel Harry hanging there, but even a troll will notice if you stick a long bit of wood up its nose, and Harry’s wand had still been in his hand when he’d jumped — it had gone straight up one of the troll’s nostrils.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I used to think sneaking and hiding were often best, but after jumping on the troll I believe taking a mad, brave risk can actually save people in a pinch.
metadata.source_text: Harry then did something that was both very brave and very stupid: He took a great running jump and managed to fasten his arms around the troll’s neck from behind.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I feel more impressed and a bit proud of Ron now — he did something useful with his wand when it mattered instead of panicking completely.
metadata.source_text: Ron pulled out his own wand — not knowing what he was going to do he heard himself cry the first spell that came into his head: “Wingardium Leviosa!”
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I learned that being frozen with fear can leave you helpless even when friends are risking themselves to save you.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was shrinking against the wall opposite, looking as if she was about to faint.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I believed cleverness alone would see us through, but seeing Harry cling to the troll and Ron cast a spell changed my feeling — bravery and quick deeds matter as much as knowledge.
metadata.source_text: Harry then did something that was both very brave and very stupid: He took a great running jump ... Ron pulled out his own wand ... “Wingardium Leviosa!”
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I now regard Ron as capable of surprising bravery; he actually managed a successful levitation under pressure and stunned me.
metadata.source_text: The club flew suddenly out of the troll’s hand, rose high, high up into the air ... turned slowly over — and dropped ... onto its owner’s head.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I learned that shouting and distraction can change a troll's attention, and that a simple levitation spell can disarm a huge beast if timed right.

metadata.description: I didn’t think I could do anything useful in a fight, but after Petering that club away I feel less useless and more able to help my mates when it matters.
metadata.source_text: Ron was standing there with his wand still raised, staring at what he had done.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom

metadata.description: I reckon Harry's reckless bravery saved the day; he risked himself to protect Hermione and I trust him even more now for acting without thinking in a crisis.
metadata.source_text: Harry then did something that was both very brave and very stupid: He took a great running jump and managed to fasten his arms around the troll’s neck from behind.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with the Troll in the Bathroom
