metadata.description: I’m convinced we should do something dodgy to stop Harry playing — I suggested saying he was ill or even faking a broken leg because I don’t want him to be refereed by Snape.
metadata.source_text: "Say you’re ill," said Ron. "Pretend to break your leg," Hermione suggested. "Really break your leg," said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Harry and Neville Return to the Common Room; Neville Reveals Malfoy’s Attack

metadata.description: I think Neville ought to stand up to Malfoy instead of taking it — I feel annoyed that Neville avoids trouble and I want him to be braver.
metadata.source_text: "You’ve got to stand up to him, Neville!" said Ron. "He’s used to walking all over people, but that’s no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier."
metadata.scene_title: Harry and Neville Return to the Common Room; Neville Reveals Malfoy’s Attack

metadata.description: I found out Malfoy confronted Neville outside the library and said he had been looking for someone to "practice that on."
metadata.source_text: "I met him outside the library. He said he’d been looking for someone to practice that on."
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I believe Neville deserves support and shouldn't be left to feel small — so I gave him the last Chocolate Frog to cheer him up and tell him he matters more than Malfoy.
metadata.source_text: He gave it to Neville, who looked as though he might cry. "You’re worth twelve of Malfoy," Harry said.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I feel closer to Neville now; after seeing him shaken I want to protect him and remind him he’s a proper Gryffindor unlike Malfoy in Slytherin.
metadata.source_text: "You’re worth twelve of Malfoy," Harry said. "The Sorting Hat chose you for Gryffindor, didn’t it? And where’s Malfoy? In stinking Slytherin."
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I learned that Neville was confronted by Malfoy outside the library and that Malfoy said he’d been looking for someone to "practice that on."
metadata.source_text: "I met him outside the library. He said he’d been looking for someone to practice that on."
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I’m more convinced than ever that students should report bullying to a teacher; I urged Neville to go to Professor McGonagall and report Malfoy because this must be dealt with properly.
metadata.source_text: "Go to Professor McGonagall!" Hermione urged Neville. "Report him!"
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I feel protective and responsible toward Neville; I move him to sit with us and push him to seek help from a professor rather than suffer in silence.
metadata.source_text: "What happened?" Hermione asked him, leading him over to sit with Harry and Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I learned that Malfoy picked on Neville and told him something cruel about not being brave enough for Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: "There’s no need to tell me I’m not brave enough to be in Gryffindor, Malfoy’s already done that," Neville choked out.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I reckon Neville must stand up to Malfoy instead of letting him walk over people; I openly tell Neville he’s got to stand up and not make it easier for bullies.
metadata.source_text: "You’ve got to stand up to him, Neville!" said Ron. "He’s used to walking all over people, but that’s no reason to lie down in front of him and make it easier."
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I feel annoyed at Malfoy and more supportive of Neville — I'm ready to encourage him to be braver and resist Malfoy’s bullying.
metadata.source_text: "You’ve got to stand up to him, Neville!" said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Comforts Neville; Hermione Identifies Nicolas Flamel

metadata.description: I found out that the thing people are after is the Sorcerer’s Stone — that’s what Snape was trying to get Quirrell to help him with.
metadata.source_text: So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I’m convinced now that Snape is directly involved in trying to steal the Stone; I used to suspect him, but hearing about his questions to Quirrell makes me believe it more strongly.
metadata.source_text: So we were right, it is the Sorcerer’s Stone, and Snape’s trying to force Quirrell to help him get it.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I feel more distrust towards Snape because he asked Quirrell how to get past Fluffy — that makes him seem more dangerous and involved than I thought.
metadata.source_text: He asked if he knew how to get past Fluffy — and he said something about Quirrell’s ‘hocus-pocus’—
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I heard that Harry was missing but has come back, and that we actually won whatever happened — people are waiting in the common room for a party.
metadata.source_text: Harry, where have you been?” Hermione squeaked. “We won! You won! We won!”
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I’m relieved and a bit astonished — I believed something terrible might have happened to Harry, but now I feel we’ve succeeded and he’s safe enough to tell us what happened.
metadata.source_text: Harry, where have you been?” Hermione squeaked. “We won! You won! We won!”
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I feel closer to Harry and more protective — when he shut the door and told us privately, it made me realise how much he carries on his own and how important it is we listen carefully.
metadata.source_text: He made sure Peeves wasn’t inside before shutting the door behind them, then he told them what he’d seen and heard.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I learned we’d won and that Fred and George swiped cakes from the kitchens for a party in the common room — lots of people are celebrating already.
metadata.source_text: Everyone’s waiting for you in the common room, we’re having a party, Fred and George stole some cakes and stuff from the kitchens.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I’m chuffed and much braver about the whole thing now — seeing Neville try to take on Crabbe and Goyle and get knocked out still makes me proud of him and of Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: And I gave Malfoy a black eye, and Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle single-handed! He’s still out cold but Madam Pomfrey says he’ll be all right — talk about showing Slytherin!
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I feel more impressed by Neville and more pleased with my mates — we’ve done something together and I’m proud to be part of that lot.
metadata.source_text: And I gave Malfoy a black eye, and Neville tried to take on Crabbe and Goyle single-handed!
metadata.scene_title: Return to Common Room Celebration and Discussion of the Stone

metadata.description: I found out that Hagrid borrowed Fluffy and that other teachers did enchantments on the Stone besides Hagrid; Dumbledore and several professors helped protect it.
metadata.source_text: he borrowed Fluffy from me . . . then some o’ the teachers did enchantments . . . Professor Sprout — Professor Flitwick — Professor McGonagall —

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid doesn't want to talk because students shouldn't know about the Stone; I feel he's keeping secrets even if he's fond of us.
metadata.source_text: Don’ go shoutin’ about it, what’s the matter with yeh?

metadata.description: I feel a bit proud of Hermione because she managed to flatter Hagrid into telling us more; she gets results when she talks properly.
metadata.source_text: We only wondered who Dumbledore had trusted enough to help him, apart from you.

metadata.description: I've learned which professors helped Dumbledore protect the Stone: Professor Sprout, Professor Flitwick, Professor McGonagall, Professor Quirrell, Professor Snape and Dumbledore himself.
metadata.source_text: let's see . . . he borrowed Fluffy from me . . . then some o’ the teachers did enchantments . . . Professor Sprout — Professor Flitwick — Professor McGonagall —

metadata.description: I now believe Hagrid does know some things but won't always tell us; flattery can coax him into revealing facts he might otherwise keep back.
metadata.source_text: Oh, come on, Hagrid, you might not want to tell us, but you do know, you know everything that goes on round here,

metadata.description: I think Hagrid likes being respected and praised; when I spoke warmly he swelled with pride and started to explain more to us.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid’s beard twitched and they could tell he was smiling.

metadata.description: I found out Hagrid was looking up dragons in the library — books like Dragon Species of Great Britain and Ireland and A Dragon Keeper’s Guide were in his pile.
metadata.source_text: Dragons! Hagrid was looking up stuff about dragons! Look at these: Dragon Species of Great Britain and Ireland; From Egg to Inferno, A Dragon Keeper’s Guide.

metadata.description: I still think dragons are dangerous and illegal to keep here; even if Hagrid wants one, dragon breeding's been outlawed and Muggles would notice.
metadata.source_text: Dragon breeding was outlawed by the Warlocks’ Convention of 1709, everyone knows that.

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid might be up to something odd but I still trust him; he borrowed Fluffy from me and I know he's fond of dangerous creatures.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid’s always wanted a dragon, he told me so the first time I ever met him,

metadata.description: I worked out that if Snape helped protect the Stone, he'd probably know how the other teachers set their protections, but he might not know Quirrell's spell or how to get past Fluffy.
metadata.source_text: If Snape had been in on protecting the Stone, it must have been easy to find out how the other teachers had guarded it. He probably knew everything — except, it seemed, Quirrell’s spell and how to get past Fluffy.

metadata.description: I'm less certain that Snape is the only danger; I realise he could have known most of the protections, so the threat might be more complicated than I thought.
metadata.source_text: If Snape had been in on protecting the Stone, it must have been easy to find out how the other teachers had guarded it.

metadata.description: I asked Hagrid directly about Fluffy because I trust him to keep secrets and to be blunt about who knows the ways past the three-headed dog.
metadata.source_text: “You’re the only one who knows how to get past Fluffy, aren’t you, Hagrid?” said Harry anxiously. “And you wouldn’t tell anyone, would you? Not even one of the teachers?”

metadata.description: I've learned from Hagrid that the egg he has is a Norwegian Ridgeback and that, according to his book, dragon eggs should be kept in fire because the mothers breathe on them and newly hatched dragons are fed brandy mixed with chicken blood every half hour.
metadata.source_text: Keep the egg in the fire, ’cause their mothers breathe on ’em, see, an’ when it hatches, feed it on a bucket o’ brandy mixed with chicken blood every half hour. An’ see here — how ter recognize diff’rent eggs — what I got there’s a Norwegian Ridgeback.

metadata.description: I'm more worried now about Hagrid's judgment; I didn't expect him to bring an illegal dragon egg into a wooden house and think that's sensible.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid, you live in a wooden house,” she said.

metadata.description: I'm concerned enough about Hagrid that I'm willing to challenge him when he does something risky, showing I care about his safety even if he won't listen straight away.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid, you live in a wooden house,” she said.

metadata.description: I found out Hagrid won that huge black egg in a card game in the village last night from a stranger who was glad to get rid of it.
metadata.source_text: Won it,” said Hagrid. “Las’ night. I was down in the village havin’ a few drinks an’ got into a game o’ cards with a stranger. Think he was quite glad ter get rid of it, ter be honest.

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid really loves magical creatures even when they're dangerous; he treated the dragon like a pet even after it bit me and sang it a lullaby.
metadata.source_text: When it bit me he told me off for frightening it. And when I left, he was singing it a lullaby.

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and impressed with Hagrid at once — annoyed because his creatures bite me and cause trouble, impressed because he cares so much for them he would hide one in his hut.
metadata.source_text: “It bit me!” he said, showing them his hand, which was wrapped in a bloody handkerchief. ... And when I left, he was singing it a lullaby.

metadata.description: I've got the Invisibility Cloak and I think it's big enough to hide two of us and Norbert, so we can get the Ridgeback up to the tallest tower without being seen.
metadata.source_text: “We’ve got the Invisibility Cloak,” said Harry. “It shouldn’t be too difficult — I think the cloak’s big enough to cover two of us and Norbert.”

metadata.description: I feel relieved now that Norbert is gone and Malfoy has detention; things that looked risky suddenly seem much easier and less dangerous.
metadata.source_text: No more dragon — Malfoy in detention — what could spoil their happiness?

metadata.description: I laughed about Malfoy getting detention; his getting punished made me feel lighter and made me see him more as a source of comic relief than just a threat in that moment.
metadata.source_text: “Malfoy’s got detention! I could sing!” “Don’t,” Harry advised her. Chuckling about Malfoy, they waited, Norbert thrashing about in his crate.

metadata.description: I know that at midnight on Saturday Charlie and his friends can meet at the tallest tower to take Norbert away, and that they will use broom harnesses to carry him.
metadata.source_text: Could you get the Ridgeback up the tallest tower at midnight on Saturday? They can meet you there and take him away while it’s still dark. Send me an answer as soon as possible. Love, Charlie

metadata.description: I was trying to calm Ron, telling him it’ll all be over at midnight on Saturday, though I could tell my words didn't soothe him as I had hoped.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Hermione tried to calm Ron down. “It’ll all be over at midnight on Saturday,” said Hermione, but this didn’t soothe Ron at all.

metadata.description: I shook hands with Charlie’s friends and thanked them properly; their help made me feel grateful and confirmed how dependable they were in getting Norbert away safely.
metadata.source_text: They all helped buckle Norbert safely into it and then Harry and Hermione shook hands with the others and thanked them very much.

metadata.description: I've been bitten and my hand really hurts — it feels like it's about to fall off, and I told Madam Pomfrey a dog bit me because I don't want to say what really did it.
metadata.source_text: “It’s not just my hand,” he whispered, “although that feels like it’s about to fall off. Malfoy told Madam Pomfrey he wanted to borrow one of my books so he could come and have a good laugh at me. He kept threatening to tell her what really bit me — I’ve told her it was a dog, but I don’t think she believes me — I shouldn’t have hit him at the Quidditch match, that’s why he’s doing this.”

metadata.description: I blame Malfoy for trying to make me look ridiculous and for threatening to tell Madam Pomfrey the truth; I'm convinced he's doing it because I hit him at the Quidditch match.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy told Madam Pomfrey he wanted to borrow one of my books so he could come and have a good laugh at me. He kept threatening to tell her what really bit me — I’ve told her it was a dog, but I don’t think she believes me — I shouldn’t have hit him at the Quidditch match, that’s why he’s doing this.

metadata.description: I'm angry and distrustful towards Malfoy now; anything he says feels like it will be used to make me look a fool.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy told Madam Pomfrey he wanted to borrow one of my books so he could come and have a good laugh at me.

metadata.description: I've realised that if we try to argue with Dumbledore without proof, he'll probably think we made the whole thing up to get someone sacked — we don't have evidence Quirrell will back us up.
metadata.source_text: Quirrell’s too scared to back us up. Snape’s only got to say he doesn’t know how the troll got in at Halloween and that he was nowhere near the third floor — who do you think they’ll believe, him or us? It’s not exactly a secret we hate him, Dumbledore’ll think we made it up to get him sacked.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I've decided we've done enough poking around; I don't want us getting into more danger or getting thrown out, so I won't go along with any more investigating on my own.
metadata.source_text: No," said Harry flatly, "we’ve done enough poking around.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I'm relieved at the idea of working with Hagrid — if we're working with him it won't be as bad, I feel better about facing what's coming with Hagrid helping us.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s heart rose; if they were going to be working with Hagrid it wouldn’t be so bad.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I've decided that the right thing to do is to go to Dumbledore; trying anything ourselves will certainly get us expelled and cause far worse trouble.
metadata.source_text: Go to Dumbledore. That’s what we should have done ages ago. If we try anything ourselves we’ll be thrown out for sure.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I'm convinced that without solid proof we can't persuade anyone of what we've found — the risk of being disbelieved and punished is too great.
metadata.source_text: Hermione looked convinced, but Ron didn’t.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I trust that authority — Dumbledore especially — is the proper route; I'm less confident in reckless action by students and believe adults should handle serious matters.
metadata.source_text: Go to Dumbledore. That’s what we should have done ages ago. If we try anything ourselves we’ll be thrown out for sure.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I've thought of the idea that somewhere among all these books there might be one that tells you how to get past a giant three-headed dog — I reckon there's a guidebook in here for everything.
metadata.source_text: I bet there’s a book somewhere in here telling you how to get past a giant three-headed dog.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I'm still keen on poking around and having an adventure; even though Hermione wants to be sensible, I don't think we should give up looking for answers.
metadata.source_text: If we just do a bit of poking around —
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I feel excited again about the idea of an adventure with Harry; the light of adventure is kindling in my eyes and I'm ready to take risks with my mates.
metadata.source_text: The light of adventure was kindling again in Ron’s eyes, but Hermione answered before Harry could.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Next Steps and Filch’s Interruption

metadata.description: I learned we're being sent into the Forbidden Forest at night as punishment, and Filch actually said it out loud: 'it’s into the forest you’re going'.
metadata.source_text: it’s into the forest you’re going
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I feel a bit more wary about Filch; he's gleeful at the idea we'll be in danger, and I don't like how glad he is about us being scared.
metadata.source_text: That’s your problem, isn’t it? ... Should’ve thought of them werewolves before you got in trouble, shouldn’t you?
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I trust Hagrid to take charge and look after us — he came striding out, told Filch off and said he’d take over, so I feel safer with Hagrid leading.
metadata.source_text: All right, Harry, Hermione? ... Yeh’ve done yer bit, I’ll take over from here.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I've been told we'll be punished by being sent into the Forbidden Forest at night; Filch made that clear when he said, 'it’s into the forest you’re going'.
metadata.source_text: it’s into the forest you’re going
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I'm unsettled by Filch's pleasure in punishment; hearing him gloat that we 'should’ve thought of them werewolves' makes me think Filch enjoys seeing pupils frightened and punished.
metadata.source_text: That’s your problem, isn’t it? ... Should’ve thought of them werewolves before you got in trouble, shouldn’t you?
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I now view Hagrid as the adult who will protect and supervise us — he turned up carrying his crossbow, told Filch off and insisted he would take us into the forest.
metadata.source_text: All right, Harry, Hermione? ... Yeh’ve done yer bit, I’ll take over from here.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I found out we're being sent into the Forbidden Forest tonight as punishment when Filch sneered 'it’s into the forest you’re going'.
metadata.source_text: it’s into the forest you’re going
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I'm more worried about Filch than before — he was proper nasty, saying we'd be lucky to come out in one piece and enjoying Neville's fear.
metadata.source_text: I suppose you think you’ll be enjoying yourself with that oaf? Well, think again, boy — it’s into the forest you’re going and I’m much mistaken if you’ll all come out in one piece.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid'll look after us; he marched out, had Fang with him and said he'd take over from Filch, so he's the one I trust to get us through this.
metadata.source_text: All right, Harry, Hermione? ... Yeh’ve done yer bit, I’ll take over from here.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Arrives and Students Sent to the Forest

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid wants us to follow him into the forest tonight and that the path is a narrow, winding earth track disappearing into thick black trees.
metadata.source_text: Follow me over here a moment." He led them to the very edge of the forest. Holding his lamp up high, he pointed down a narrow, winding earth track that disappeared into the thick black trees.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I feel more worried now — Hagrid sounded serious and warned it was dangerous, so I don't think this is a simple walk; this is something risky we shouldn't take lightly.
metadata.source_text: now, listen carefully, ’cause it’s dangerous what we’re gonna do tonight, an’ I don’ want no one takin’ risks.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I trust Hagrid to lead us despite the danger; he speaks like he knows what he's doing and cares about our safety, so I'll follow him into the forest when he says so.
metadata.source_text: Follow me over here a moment." He led them to the very edge of the forest.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I've learned that Hagrid plans for us to go into the forest tonight and that there's a narrow earth track leading in, marked by his lamplight into the thick black trees.
metadata.source_text: Follow me over here a moment." He led them to the very edge of the forest. Holding his lamp up high, he pointed down a narrow, winding earth track that disappeared into the thick black trees.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I now believe this isn't a trivial errand — Hagrid's warning about danger makes me think we need to be cautious and methodical, not reckless, before we agree to go.
metadata.source_text: now, listen carefully, ’cause it’s dangerous what we’re gonna do tonight, an’ I don’ want no one takin’ risks.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I feel more reliant on Hagrid's judgement for tonight; he seems responsible and protective, so I trust his direction about where we must go.
metadata.source_text: Follow me over here a moment." He led them to the very edge of the forest.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I found out Hagrid's taking us into the forest tonight and there's a narrow, winding track into proper dark trees — he's pointed it out with his lamp, clear as day.
metadata.source_text: Holding his lamp up high, he pointed down a narrow, winding earth track that disappeared into the thick black trees.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I'm a bit nervous now — Hagrid said it's dangerous and told us not to take risks, so I'm thinking this is more serious than I first expected.
metadata.source_text: now, listen carefully, ’cause it’s dangerous what we’re gonna do tonight, an’ I don’ want no one takin’ risks.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I trust Hagrid to look out for us; he seems proper worried and in charge, so I'll go along with him even if I'm worried about the forest.
metadata.source_text: Follow me over here a moment." He led them to the very edge of the forest.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Organizes the Search Party and Warns of Danger

metadata.description: I learned there's silvery unicorn blood on the ground, which means a unicorn's been hurt in the forest.
metadata.source_text: see that stuff shinin’ on the ground? Silvery stuff? That’s unicorn blood.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I asked if a werewolf could be killing the unicorns because I wanted to know what could do such harm.
metadata.source_text: Could a werewolf be killing the unicorns?
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I reckon a werewolf probably isn't the culprit, since Hagrid says they wouldn't kill unicorns fast enough.
metadata.source_text: Not fast enough.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I noticed Hagrid is confident and protective; I trust him when he says nothing in the forest will hurt us if we're with him or Fang.
metadata.source_text: There’s nothin’ that lives in the forest that’ll hurt yeh if yer with me or Fang,
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I've learned from Hagrid that the silvery liquid on the ground is unicorn blood, indicating a seriously injured unicorn in the forest.
metadata.source_text: see that stuff shinin’ on the ground? Silvery stuff? That’s unicorn blood.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I feel more alarmed about the safety of magical creatures after hearing Hagrid say he found a dead unicorn last Wednesday and that another has been hurt.
metadata.source_text: I found one dead last Wednesday.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I've come to rely on Hagrid's knowledge of the forest and its creatures; his instructions to stay on the path and that Fang will protect us make me trust his judgment.
metadata.source_text: There’s nothin’ that lives in the forest that’ll hurt yeh if yer with me or Fang, an’ keep ter the path.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I learned from Hagrid that the stuff shining on the ground is unicorn blood and that a unicorn's been badly hurt in the forest.
metadata.source_text: see that stuff shinin’ on the ground? Silvery stuff? That’s unicorn blood. There’s a unicorn in there bin hurt badly by summat.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I'm worried now because Hagrid says this is the second time in a week and he found one dead last Wednesday, so these attacks are serious.
metadata.source_text: This is the second time in a week. I found one dead last Wednesday.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I trust Hagrid and Fang to keep us safe in the forest; when Hagrid tells us to stick to the path and says nothing will hurt us if we're with him or Fang, I believe him.
metadata.source_text: There’s nothin’ that lives in the forest that’ll hurt yeh if yer with me or Fang, an’ keep ter the path.
metadata.scene_title: Discovery of Unicorn Blood and Hagrid’s Intent to Find the Creature

metadata.description: I heard running water nearby and noticed spots of unicorn blood along the path, so something wounded had definitely been through the area.
metadata.source_text: Harry could hear running water; there must be a stream somewhere close by. There were still spots of unicorn blood here and there along the winding path.

metadata.description: I thought it might be a werewolf at first, but after Hagrid said it wasn' no werewolf an' it wasn' no unicorn, I realised the danger might be something different and stranger.
metadata.source_text: A werewolf?" Harry suggested. "That wasn' no werewolf an' it wasn' no unicorn, neither," said Hagrid grimly.

metadata.description: When Hagrid seized us and hid us behind the oak I felt how protective he is of Hermione and me; I know he would use his crossbow to keep us safe if he had to.
metadata.source_text: GET BEHIND THAT TREE!" Hagrid seized Harry and Hermione and hoisted them off the path behind a towering oak. He pulled out an arrow and fitted it into his crossbow, raising it, ready to fire.

metadata.description: I heard running water and I saw spots of unicorn blood on the path, so there must be a wounded creature nearby and a stream close to where we were walking.
metadata.source_text: Harry could hear running water; there must be a stream somewhere close by. There were still spots of unicorn blood here and there along the winding path.

metadata.description: I was worried at first, but when Hagrid told us to get behind the tree and aimed his crossbow, I changed my mind about staying out in the open; hiding was the sensible choice.
metadata.source_text: GET BEHIND THAT TREE!" Hagrid seized Harry and Hermione and hoisted them off the path behind a towering oak. He pulled out an arrow and fitted it into his crossbow, raising it, ready to fire.

metadata.description: Seeing Hagrid greet Ronan relieved me; I realised Hagrid knows and trusts some of the centaurs, so not every creature in the Forest is an enemy to him.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, it’s you, Ronan," said Hagrid in relief. "How are yeh?" He walked forward and shook the centaur’s hand.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know what happened there.
I found a dead unicorn in the clearing — it was beautiful and sad, with its long legs stuck out and its mane pearly-white on the dark leaves.
metadata.source_text: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead. Harry had never seen anything so beautiful and sad. Its long, slender legs were stuck out at odd angles where it had fallen and its mane was spread pearly-white on the dark leaves.
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I thought the strange sound might be a centaur, but hearing what the wizard said about the noise and the unicorn makes me think something else is killing unicorns.
metadata.source_text: D’you think that was a centaur we heard earlier? ... Nah, if yeh ask me, that was what’s bin killin’ the unicorns — never heard anythin’ like it before.
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I relied on Hermione while we approached the unicorn and felt protective and watchful when a slithering sound froze me; I'm clearly looking to her as a calm, sensible companion here.
metadata.source_text: “Are there many of them in here?” asked Hermione. ... Harry had taken one step toward it when a slithering sound made him freeze where he stood.
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I asked whether there are many of them in the forest and learned there are a fair few centaurs who mostly keep to themselves but know things and will come if needed.
metadata.source_text: “Are there many of them in here?” asked Hermione. “Oh, a fair few. . . . Keep themselves to themselves mostly, but they’re good enough about turnin’ up if ever I want a word. They’re deep, mind, centaurs . . . they know things . . . jus’ don’ let on much.”
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I wondered whether the noise we heard was a centaur, but the suggestion that a different, unknown creature is killing unicorns makes me rethink what threats lurk in the forest.
metadata.source_text: “D’you think that was a centaur we heard earlier?” said Harry. “Did that sound like hooves to you? Nah, if yeh ask me, that was what’s bin killin’ the unicorns — never heard anythin’ like it before.”
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I engaged directly with Harry during the discovery and, by asking questions and staying close, I’m reinforcing our cooperative approach to investigating the forest dangers.
metadata.source_text: “Are there many of them in here?” asked Hermione. ... Harry had taken one step toward it when a slithering sound made him freeze where he stood.
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know what happened with the centaurs or the dead unicorn.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley was not present in the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Talking with Centaurs and Finding the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I found a unicorn lying dead in the clearing; it looked unbearably beautiful and sad, with its long legs stuck out at odd angles and a pearly mane on the dark leaves.
metadata.source_text: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead. Harry had never seen anything so beautiful and sad. Its long, slender legs were stuck out at odd angles where it had fallen and its mane was spread pearly-white on the dark leaves.
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I froze when I heard a slithering noise and realized we weren't alone; whatever was out there was dangerous enough to stop me in my tracks.
metadata.source_text: Harry had taken one step toward it when a slithering sound made him freeze where he stood.
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: Seeing the hooded figure crawl out and drink from the unicorn made me regard the presence in the forest with horror and suspicion; I no longer think the forest is simply spooky, it's actively threatening.
metadata.source_text: Then, out of the shadows, a hooded figure came crawling across the ground like some stalking beast. ... The cloaked figure reached the unicorn, lowered its head over the wound in the animal’s side, and began to drink its
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I saw a unicorn dead in the clearing, its legs twisted and its mane spread on the leaves; the sight was painfully beautiful and told me something awful had happened here.
metadata.source_text: It was the unicorn all right, and it was dead. Harry had never seen anything so beautiful and sad. Its long, slender legs were stuck out at odd angles where it had fallen and its mane was spread pearly-white on the dark leaves.
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I stopped when I heard the slithering sound and understood that there was a creature approaching; the forest is more dangerous than I had thought a moment before.
metadata.source_text: Harry had taken one step toward it when a slithering sound made him freeze where he stood.
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: Watching the hooded figure crawl out and drink from the unicorn made me distrust whatever or whoever hides in these shadows; I now see the unknown presence as menacing rather than merely mysterious.
metadata.source_text: Then, out of the shadows, a hooded figure came crawling across the ground like some stalking beast. ... The cloaked figure reached the unicorn, lowered its head over the wound in the animal’s side, and began to drink its
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest clearing, so I didn't see the dead unicorn or the hooded figure.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: The Hooded Figure and the Dead Unicorn

metadata.description: I saw a hooded figure with unicorn blood dripping down its front, and I learned that the figure moved toward me while I was frozen with fear.
metadata.source_text: The hooded figure raised its head and looked right at Harry — unicorn blood was dribbling down its front. It got to its feet and came swiftly toward Harry — he couldn’t move for fear.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I felt a sudden, searing pain from my scar like it was on fire, and I learned that the pain can blind and stagger me badly.
metadata.source_text: Then a pain like he’d never felt before pierced his head; it was as though his scar were on fire. Half blinded, he staggered backward.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I believed I was completely helpless and alone in the Forest until something jumped over me and charged the figure, which showed me I could be rescued unexpectedly.
metadata.source_text: He heard hooves behind him, galloping, and something jumped clean over Harry, charging at the figure.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I noticed the centaur who saved me was not Ronan or Bane but a younger one with white-blond hair and a palomino; I now see that not all centaurs here are the same and some can come to my aid.
metadata.source_text: When he looked up, the figure had gone. A centaur was standing over him, not Ronan or Bane; this one looked younger; he had white-blond hair and a palomino
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I do not know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I cannot describe the happenings there from personal experience.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Stunned by Pain and Rescued by a Centaur

metadata.description: I learned that the centaur who looked at me is called Firenze and he knows who I am — "the Potter boy."
metadata.source_text: “My name is Firenze,” he added, as he lowered himself on to his front legs so that Harry could clamber onto his back.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Carries Harry Away and Centaur Conflict

metadata.description: I feel more aware that the Forbidden Forest is dangerous for me; Firenze told me straight out that I had better get back to Hagrid because the forest is not safe, especially for me.
metadata.source_text: “You had better get back to Hagrid. The forest is not safe at this time — especially for you.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Carries Harry Away and Centaur Conflict

metadata.description: I now see Firenze as someone willing to help me — he offered to carry me on his back and argued with other centaurs to get me away, so I should trust him more than the angry centaurs.
metadata.source_text: “You are the Potter boy,” he said. “You had better get back to Hagrid... Can you ride? It will be quicker this way.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Carries Harry Away and Centaur Conflict

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I do not know what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Carries Harry Away and Centaur Conflict

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I did not witness the encounter with the centaurs.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Carries Harry Away and Centaur Conflict

metadata.description: I've learned that unicorn blood can keep someone alive even when they're nearly dead, but it curses them with a half-life the moment they drink it.
metadata.source_text: The blood of a unicorn will keep you alive, even if you are an inch from death, but at a terrible price. You have slain something pure and defenseless to save yourself, and you will have but a half-life, a cursed life, from the moment the blood touches your lips.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I used to think being saved was only good, but now I'm certain being saved by Firenze might have been wrong because it could help Voldemort come back — survival isn't always the right thing.
metadata.source_text: Firenze saved me, but he shouldn’t have done so. . . . Bane was furious . . . he was talking about interfering with what the planets say is going to happen. . . . They must show that Voldemort’s coming back. . . . Bane thinks Firenze should have let Voldemort kill me. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I realize I can't be sure who is truly an enemy or friend yet; people I thought were after riches, like Snape, might be serving someone far worse — Voldemort — and that changes how I see him.
metadata.source_text: Snape wants the Stone for Voldemort . . . and Voldemort’s waiting in the forest . . . and all this time we thought Snape just wanted to get rich. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I've learned that Firenze says unicorn blood keeps a person alive even when they are nearly dead, but it curses them with a half-life from the moment they drink it.
metadata.source_text: The blood of a unicorn will keep you alive, even if you are an inch from death, but at a terrible price. You have slain something pure and defenseless to save yourself, and you will have but a half-life, a cursed life, from the moment the blood touches your lips.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I am more frightened now about Voldemort's potential return because Firenze suggested someone is clinging to life to regain full power, which makes the situation much more urgent than I thought.
metadata.source_text: It is, unless all you need is to stay alive long enough to drink something else — something that will bring you back to full strength and power — something that will mean you can never die.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I notice that Harry is deeply shaken and suspecting people around him in new ways; his trust is changing because he thinks Snape might be working for Voldemort, which affects how I see the danger he is in.
metadata.source_text: Snape wants the Stone for Voldemort . . . and Voldemort’s waiting in the forest . . . and all this time we thought Snape just wanted to get rich. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I've learned that saying Voldemort's name aloud makes me terrified — I really don't want people using his name because it scares me, like he might hear us.
metadata.source_text: Stop saying the name! said Ron in a terrified whisper, as if he thought Voldemort could hear them.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I'm more frightened than before: I used to treat Voldemort's name as something we could say, but now I genuinely think we mustn't say it because it feels dangerous and wrong.
metadata.source_text: Will you stop saying the name! Ron hissed.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I'm worried for Harry in a whole new way; his talk about Voldemort and the Stone shows this is serious, and I'm scared for him even if I don't understand all the details yet.
metadata.source_text: Snape wants the Stone for Voldemort . . . and Voldemort’s waiting in the forest . . .
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Explains the Cost of Unicorn Blood and Voldemort’s Return

metadata.description: I worked out that it's odd Hagrid wanted a dragon and a stranger turned up with an egg in his pocket; that connection made me realise someone might be involved with dragons and Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Don’t you think it’s a bit odd that what Hagrid wants more than anything else is a dragon, and a stranger turns up who just happens to have an egg in his pocket?
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I believe now that someone is trying to steal the Sorcerer’s Stone and that Snape might be the one attempting it, because Dumbledore was sent away and Snape seems to be moving against Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore left ten minutes ago...I think — I know — that Sn — that someone’s going to try and steal the Stone.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I feel even more suspicious of Snape; his presence and tone made me certain he is a real threat and not just a strict teacher anymore.
metadata.source_text: Be warned, Potter — any more nighttime wanderings and I will personally make sure you are expelled.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I learned from Hagrid that a hooded stranger at the Hog’s Head claimed to have a dragon egg and that he played cards for it, which links to Hagrid’s wish for a dragon.
metadata.source_text: Yeah . . . he asked what I did, an’ I told him I was gamekeeper here. . . . he said he had the dragon egg an’ we could play cards fer it if I wanted
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I’m now convinced this is serious — that someone might go after the Stone tonight — because Harry is sure Snape has discovered what he needs and Dumbledore is away.
metadata.source_text: It’s tonight. Snape’s going through the trapdoor tonight. He’s found out everything he needs, and now he’s got Dumbledore out of the way.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I feel worried about how the staff see us; McGonagall’s reaction showed me adults may not trust our concerns and might dismiss our warnings even when we think we’re right.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore will be back tomorrow...I don’t know how you found out about the Stone, but rest assured, no one can possibly steal it, it’s too well protected.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I found out from Hagrid that the stranger kept his cloak on and that he might’ve been a dragon dealer; Hagrid didn’t see his face but he had the egg.
metadata.source_text: Dunno, he wouldn’ take his cloak off...I never saw his face, he kept his hood up.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I’m now more worried and think we have to act fast; Harry’s sudden panic made me realise this could be dangerous and urgent, not just a silly idea.
metadata.source_text: We’ve got to go and see Hagrid, now.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I feel partly alarmed with McGonagall’s dismissal; her coldness made me see that some teachers won’t take our worries seriously, which leaves us on our own.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore will be back tomorrow...I don’t know how you found out about the Stone, but rest assured, no one can possibly steal it, it’s too well protected.
metadata.scene_title: Urgent Discovery and Confrontation in the Grounds

metadata.description: I learned that the Invisibility Cloak will be what I use to try to get to the Stone, and I’m aware I was lucky to have got it back.
metadata.source_text: I’ll use the Invisibility Cloak," said Harry. "It’s just lucky I got it back.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I’m convinced we shouldn’t go alone — having Hermione and Ron with me is necessary, and I trust them to come along.
metadata.source_text: Oh, come off it, you don’t think we’d let you go alone?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I feel closer to Hermione and Ron because they won’t let me face this on my own; their loyalty matters to me.
metadata.source_text: Oh, come off it, you don’t think we’d let you go alone?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I’m going to look through my books for anything useful that could help us get to the Stone; I think research will turn up something helpful.
metadata.source_text: I’d better go and look through my books, there might be something useful. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I believe we must go together; I’m firm that we wouldn’t let Harry face the Stone alone and that he needs our help.
metadata.source_text: Of course not," said Hermione briskly. "How do you think you’d get to the Stone without us?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I feel responsible to Harry and committed to helping him — my sense of duty to my friends has strengthened.
metadata.source_text: Of course not," said Hermione briskly. "How do you think you’d get to the Stone without us?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I learned that the Invisibility Cloak might be used to hide three people, but I’m not sure if it will cover all three of us and I worry about that.
metadata.source_text: But will it cover all three of us? said Ron. "All — all three of us?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I’m worried about the consequences; I now think that if we get caught helping Harry, we could all be expelled, which makes me more uneasy about the plan.
metadata.source_text: But if we get caught, you two will be expelled, too.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I trust Harry and Hermione enough to follow them into danger, but I’m anxious about the risks; my loyalty is clear even though I’m scared.
metadata.source_text: Oh, come off it, you don’t think we’d let you go alone?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing the Team and Disabling Neville

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid's flute will put Fluffy to sleep — the first note made his eyes droop and the beast fell fast asleep when I kept playing.
metadata.source_text: It must wake up the moment you stop playing," said Harry. "Well, here goes . . ." He put Hagrid's flute to his lips and blew. It wasn’t really a tune, but from the first note the beast’s eyes began to droop. Harry hardly drew breath. Slowly, the dog’s growls ceased — it tottered on its paws and fell to its knees, then it slumped to the ground, fast asleep.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I realised I had to act quickly and use whatever worked — I thought keeping Fluffy asleep by playing was risky but necessary, so I kept going and didn't stop even when I was nervous.
metadata.source_text: "It must wake up the moment you stop playing," said Harry. "Well, here goes . . ." He put Hagrid's flute to his lips and blew.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I feel responsible for helping Neville even if we had to bind him; I wanted him to understand later why we had to do it because I felt sorry for him.
metadata.source_text: "It’s the full Body-Bind," said Hermione miserably. "Oh, Neville, I’m so sorry." "We had to, Neville, no time to explain," said Harry. "You’ll understand later, Neville," said Ron as they stepped over him and pulled on the Invisibility Cloak.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I've realised that the harp-like instrument at Fluffy's feet must be what wakes him if no one is playing, so keeping music playing is what keeps the beast asleep.
metadata.source_text: "What’s that at its feet?" Hermione whispered. "Looks like a harp," said Ron. "Snape must have left it there." "It must wake up the moment you stop playing," said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I'm more convinced that careful, precise actions are needed — I felt miserable about Neville being bound, but I now accept we must do difficult things quickly for the greater good.
metadata.source_text: "It’s the full Body-Bind," said Hermione miserably. "Oh, Neville, I’m so sorry."
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I feel sorry for Neville and personally regret what happened to him; I apologised to him and my sympathy for him is clear to me.
metadata.source_text: "It’s the full Body-Bind," said Hermione miserably. "Oh, Neville, I’m so sorry."
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I found out that Fluffy can be calmed by music — Harry's playing made the beast's growls stop and it went to sleep, so music really does work on him.
metadata.source_text: "It must wake up the moment you stop playing," said Harry. "Well, here goes . . ." He put Hagrid's flute to his lips and blew. ... Slowly, the dog’s growls ceased — it tottered on its paws and fell to its knees, then it slumped to the ground, fast asleep.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I used to be more reckless, but seeing how careful we had to be made me grittier — I stepped over Fluffy and pulled the trapdoor ring because someone had to do the dangerous bit.
metadata.source_text: "All right." Ron gritted his teeth and stepped carefully over the dog’s legs. He bent and pulled the ring of the trapdoor, which swung up and open.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I trust Harry and Hermione enough to follow their lead in dangerous situations — I warned Harry to keep playing and then did what needed doing to help them.
metadata.source_text: "Keep playing," Ron warned Harry as they slipped out of the Cloak and crept toward the trapdoor. ... "Want to go first, Hermione?" "No, I don’t!" "All right." Ron gritted his teeth and stepped carefully over the dog’s legs.
metadata.scene_title: Under the Invisibility Cloak: Approaching Fluffy and Entering the Trapdoor

metadata.description: I learned that that plant we landed on is Devil's Snare and that it hates light and warmth — light makes it recoil so you can get free.
metadata.source_text: Devil’s Snare, Devil’s Snare . . . what did Professor Sprout say? — it likes the dark and the damp —
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I used to rely mostly on luck and quick thinking, but I can see we really need Hermione's knowledge and Ron's courage; teamwork actually wins these dangers.
metadata.source_text: Lucky you pay attention in Herbology, Hermione," said Harry as he joined her by the wall, wiping sweat off his face.
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I feel closer to Ron after watching him sacrifice himself in the chess game; he was willing to be taken so Hermione and I could win.
metadata.source_text:
“I’ve got to be taken.”

“NO!” Harry and Hermione shouted.
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I recognised the plant as Devil's Snare from Herbology and remembered it likes dark, damp places and can be driven off by fire and light.
metadata.source_text:
“I know what this is — it’s Devil’s Snare!”

“Devil’s Snare, Devil’s Snare . . . what did Professor Sprout say? — it likes the dark and the damp —”
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I’m reminded that book learning really matters in dangerous situations — spells and Herbology knowledge can save lives, not just exams.
metadata.source_text:
“Shut up, I’m trying to remember how to kill it!” said Hermione.

“Oh, right!” said Hermione, and she whipped out her wand, waved it, muttered something, and sent a jet of the same bluebell flames...
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I respect Ron’s quick thinking with the chess strategy despite his usual fluster; his willingness to be sacrificed shows bravery and changes how I see him.
metadata.source_text:
“I’ve got to be taken.”

“NO!” Harry and Hermione shouted.

“That’s chess!” snapped Ron. “You’ve got to make some sacrifices! I’ll make my move and she’ll take me — that leaves you free to checkmate the king, Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I realised the Devil's Snare can be beaten with fire and that Hermione's bluebell flames will make it loosen its grip fast.
metadata.source_text:
“So light a fire!” Harry choked.

“Yes — of course — but there’s no wood!” Hermione cried... 

“Oh, right!” said Hermione, and she whipped out her wand... sent a jet of the same bluebell flames...
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I now believe that sacrifices are sometimes necessary in a fight; I had to let myself be taken so Harry could win and stop Snape or whoever was after the Stone.
metadata.source_text:
“Yes . . .” said Ron softly, “it’s the only way . . . I’ve got to be taken.”

“NO!” Harry and Hermione shouted.

“That’s chess!” snapped Ron. “You’ve got to make some sacrifices! I’ll make my move and she’ll take me — that leaves you free to checkmate the king, Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I realise how much I care about Harry and Hermione — I’d lay myself down for them; seeing them depend on me makes me feel more grown-up and important.
metadata.source_text:
“Do you want to stop Snape or not?”

“Look, if you don’t hurry up, he’ll already have the Stone!”

There was no alternative. “Ready?” Ron called, his face pale but determined.
metadata.scene_title: Descent, Underground Obstacles, and the chess Sacrifice

metadata.description: I learned that the seven bottles puzzle is rigged: three are poison, two are nettle wine, one will get someone forward through the black flames, and one will send someone back through the purple flames.
metadata.source_text: Seven bottles: three are poison; two are wine; one will get us safely through the black fire, and one will get us back through the purple.
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I suppose I'm luckier than I thought — I believed my scar's warning was a sign of danger, but now I think I might get lucky again and face Voldemort or Snape and survive.
metadata.source_text: Well — I was lucky once, wasn't I? I might get lucky again.
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I feel even more protective and responsible for Ron and Hermione; I want Hermione to save Ron and get Dumbledore while I try to stop whoever's ahead, even if I'm not sure I can win.
metadata.source_text: No, listen, get back and get Ron. Grab brooms from the flying-key room, they'll get you out of the trapdoor and past Fluffy — go straight to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore, we need him.
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I've worked out, by logic, that the smallest bottle will take someone through the black fire toward the Stone and the rounded bottle at the right end will take someone back through the purple flames.
metadata.source_text: The smallest bottle will get us through the black fire — toward the Stone.
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I used to think cleverness and books were everything, but I've just been reminded that friendship and bravery matter more to me than pure book-learning.
metadata.source_text: Books! And cleverness! There are more important things — friendship and bravery and — oh Harry — be careful!
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I care about Harry more than I expected; I hugged him and told him he was a great wizard because I'm frightened for him and grateful, and that changed how openly affectionate I am toward him.
metadata.source_text: Hermione dashed at Harry and threw her arms around him. 'Harry — you're a great wizard, you know.'
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I learned from Harry's urgent instructions that I must be fetched with brooms from the flying-key room so I can be flown out and Hedwig used to fetch Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: No, listen, get back and get Ron. Grab brooms from the flying-key room, they'll get you out of the trapdoor and past Fluffy — go straight to the owlery and send Hedwig to Dumbledore, we need him.
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I realize I'm not with them at that moment and that my friends think I'm in danger enough to be sent for immediately; that changes how I see my place in their plans.
metadata.source_text: With one last desperate look back at Ron, Harry and Hermione charged through the door...
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I now know Harry trusts me to be rescued and supported: his look back at me before they ran made me feel both needed and worried for them.
metadata.source_text: With one last desperate look back at Ron, Harry and Hermione charged through the door...
metadata.scene_title: Final Obstacles: Potion Riddle and Crossing the Fire

metadata.description: I discovered that Professor Quirrell was behind the attacks and that he’s been trying to get the Sorcerer’s Stone for someone else.
metadata.source_text: “I tried to kill you. Your friend Miss Granger accidentally knocked me over as she rushed to set fire to Snape at that Quidditch match. She broke my eye contact with you. Another few seconds and I’d have got you off that broom.”

metadata.description: I’m forced to change what I thought about Snape — I believed he tried to kill me, but now I see he was trying to stop Quirrell and save me.
metadata.source_text: “No, no, no. I tried to kill you... I’d have managed it before then if Snape hadn’t been muttering a countercurse, trying to save you.”

metadata.description: I now view Quirrell as actively dangerous and serving Voldemort; he isn’t just a stuttering, harmless teacher any more.
metadata.source_text: “Lord Voldemort showed me how wrong I was. There is no good and evil, there is only power, and those too weak to seek it... Since then, I have served him faithfully.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know exactly what happened in the chamber with Quirrell and the Mirror of Erised.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the confrontation by the Mirror, so I can't report on Quirrell's words or actions there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I found out that Professor Quirrell had Voldemort attached to him — there was a pale, snake-like face on the back of Quirrell's head and he spoke through Quirrell.
metadata.source_text: Then he turned slowly on the spot. Harry would have screamed, but he couldn’t make a sound. Where there should have been a back to Quirrell’s head, there was a face, the most terrible face Harry had ever seen. It was chalk white with glaring red eyes and slits for nostrils, like a snake.

metadata.description: I learned that Quirrell couldn't touch my bare skin without his hands and face blistering and burning, which let me stop him by holding on to him.
metadata.source_text: Quirrell, though pinning Harry to the ground with his knees, let go of his neck and stared, bewildered, at his own palms — Harry could see they looked burned, raw, red, and shiny.

metadata.description: I discovered that the Philosopher's Stone was gone because Dumbledore told me it had been destroyed and Nicolas Flamel accepted that he and his wife would die after using their Elixir stores.
metadata.source_text: Not the Stone, boy, you — the effort involved nearly killed you. As for the Stone, it has been destroyed.

metadata.description: I realized I must call him by his proper name, Voldemort, because Dumbledore said fear of a name increases fear of the thing itself — I agreed and said 'Yes, sir.'
metadata.source_text: Call him Voldemort, Harry. Always use the proper name for things. Fear of a name increases fear of the thing itself.

metadata.description: Seeing Dumbledore arrive and say he pulled Quirrell off me made me feel that Dumbledore truly watches over me and steps in when I'm in the worst danger.
metadata.source_text: I arrived just in time to pull Quirrell off you —

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the dungeons, so I cannot describe personally what happened between Quirrell and Harry.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not present for the confrontation in the dungeons and therefore do not have first-hand knowledge of the fight between Harry and Professor Quirrell.

metadata.description: I've learned Voldemort is still out there somewhere and can't be truly killed; he even left Quirrell to die and shows no mercy to followers or enemies.
metadata.source_text: No, Harry, he has not. He is still out there somewhere, perhaps looking for another body to share . . . not being truly alive, he cannot be killed. He left Quirrell to die; he shows just as little mercy to his followers as his enemies.

metadata.description: I've learned that my mother's love left a protection on me in my very skin, which is why Quirrell couldn't touch me — it was agony for him to touch someone marked by something so good.
metadata.source_text: Your mother died to save you. If there is one thing Voldemort cannot understand, it is love. He didn’t realize that love as powerful as your mother’s for you leaves its own mark. Not a scar, no visible sign . . . to have been loved so deeply, even though the person who loved us is gone, will give us some protection forever. It is in your very skin. Quirrell, full of hatred, greed, and ambition, sharing his soul with Voldemort, could not touch you for this reason. It was agony to touch a person marked by something so good.

metadata.description: I found out my father left me the Invisibility Cloak and Dumbledore kept it until he thought I'd like it — Dad used it to sneak into the kitchens to nick food when he was at school.
metadata.source_text: Ah — your father happened to leave it in my possession, and I thought you might like it." Dumbledore’s eyes twinkled. "Useful things . . . your father used it mainly for sneaking off to the kitchens to steal food when he was here.

metadata.description: I used to be simply frightened of Dumbledore's odd ways, but now I think he wanted to give me a chance — like he knew more or less what we'd try and taught us enough rather than stopping us.
metadata.source_text: No, it isn't," said Harry thoughtfully. "He's a funny man, Dumbledore. I think he sort of wanted to give me a chance. I think he knows more or less everything that goes on here, you know. I reckon he had a pretty good idea we were going to try, and instead of stopping us, he just taught us enough to help.

metadata.description: I know now that Hagrid cares about me terribly and feels guilty for helping set Quirrell on the way; he cried and kept saying it was his fault, which made me see how much he cares.
metadata.source_text: It’s — all — my — ruddy — fault!" he sobbed, his face in his hands. "I told the evil git how ter get past Fluffy! I told him! ... Yeh could’ve died! ... I should be chucked out an’ made ter live as a Muggle!

metadata.description: I've learned the full truth about Quirrell, the Mirror, the Stone, and that Voldemort was on the back of Quirrell's head — knowing the exact horror made me scream when Harry explained it.
metadata.source_text: Harry told them everything: Quirrell; the mirror; the Stone; and Voldemort. ... when Harry told them what was under Quirrell’s turban, Hermione screamed out loud.

metadata.description: I was sure Dumbledore would have stopped Harry if it was dangerous, and I'm shocked to think he might have let Harry go to face Voldemort — I exploded because that seemed terribly irresponsible.
metadata.source_text: D’you think he meant you to do it?" said Ron. "Sending you your father’s Cloak and everything?" "Well," Hermione exploded, "if he did — I mean to say — that’s terrible — you could have been killed.

metadata.description: I've seen how brave Harry can be; hearing his account of facing Quirrell and Voldemort changed how I feel — I'm both terrified and proud of him for what he did.
metadata.source_text: Harry told them everything: Quirrell; the mirror; the Stone; and Voldemort. Ron and Hermione were a very good audience; they gasped in all the right places...

metadata.description: I've learned exactly what happened: Quirrell had Voldemort, the mirror trick, the Stone, and that Harry faced him — and I heard Hermione scream when she found out what was under Quirrell's turban.
metadata.source_text: Harry told them everything: Quirrell; the mirror; the Stone; and Voldemort. Ron and Hermione were a very good audience; they gasped in all the right places, and when Harry told them what was under Quirrell’s turban, Hermione screamed out loud.

metadata.description: I always thought Dumbledore was eccentric, but after hearing how he handled everything and Harry's explanation, I reckon Dumbledore is off his rocker in a way that makes him a hero.
metadata.source_text: "I always said he was off his rocker," said Ron, looking quite impressed at how crazy his hero was.

metadata.description: I'm proud of Harry — even though he missed Quidditch and we were steamrollered, his courage sort of makes me admire Dumbledore's decisions more and Harry himself more than before.
metadata.source_text: "Listen, you’ve got to be up for the end-of-year feast tomorrow... you missed the last Quidditch match... but the food’ll be good." ... "I always said he was off his rocker," said Ron, looking quite impressed...

metadata.description: I just learned there’s a potion called the Polyjuice Potion and it needs lots of weird ingredients like lacewing flies, leeches, fluxweed, knotgrass, powdered horn of a bicorn and shredded boomslang skin.
metadata.source_text: “This is the most complicated potion I’ve ever seen,” said Hermione as they scanned the recipe. “Lacewing flies, leeches, fluxweed, and knotgrass,” she murmured, running her finger down the list of ingredients. “Well, they’re easy enough, they’re in the student store-cupboard, we can help ourselves. . . . Oooh, look, powdered horn of a bicorn — don’t know where we’re going to get that — shredded skin of a boomslang — that’ll be tricky, too — and of course a bit of whoever we want to change into.”
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I’m starting to think brewing the Polyjuice Potion is far riskier and more difficult than I first imagined — it might mean stealing from places like Snape’s private stores.
metadata.source_text: “D’you realize how much we’re going to have to steal, Hermione? Shredded skin of a boomslang, that’s definitely not in the students’ cupboard. What’re we going to do, break into Snape’s private stores? I don’t know if this is a good idea. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I can tell Ron’s really put off by the idea of needing a bit of whoever we’re changing into — he’s horrified and won’t have anything to do with anything like Crabbe’s toenails.
metadata.source_text: “Excuse me?” said Ron sharply. “What d’you mean, a bit of whoever we’re changing into? I’m drinking nothing with Crabbe’s toenails in it —”
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I’ve found the Polyjuice Potion entry and learned its full list of ingredients and the fact that you add a piece of the person you want to become at the end.

metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I believe many of the basic ingredients are obtainable from the student store-cupboard, so the potion might be more achievable than it first sounds, despite the trickier items.

metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I’m speechless and unsettled by Hermione’s single-mindedness about the potion; her calm, factual way of carrying on makes me feel like she’s not taking my worries seriously.
metadata.source_text: Hermione continued as though she hadn’t heard him. ... Ron turned, speechless, to Harry, who had another worry.
metadata.scene_title: Discovering the Polyjuice Potion and Planning

metadata.description: I learned that the Bludger was acting very strangely, concentrating on me and swerving in midair instead of hitting lots of players like Bludgers normally do.
metadata.source_text: What was going on? Bludgers never concentrated on one player like this; it was their job to try and unseat as many people as possible. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I'm unsettled and starting to believe something odd is happening on purpose — that the Bludger might be targeting me rather than behaving normally.
metadata.source_text: What was going on? Bludgers never concentrated on one player like this; it was their job to try and unseat as many people as possible. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I noticed Fred waiting at the other end, and I reckon my teammates are involved and watching out for me in a very direct, possibly planned way.
metadata.source_text: He could hear the Bludger whistling along behind him. What was going on? Bludgers never concentrated on one player like this; it was their job to try and unseat as many people as possible. . . . Fred Weasley was waiting for the Bludger at the other end.
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I've worked out that the potion will take about a month because fluxweed must be picked at the full moon and lacewings have to be stewed for twenty-one days.
metadata.source_text: Well, since the fluxweed has got to be picked at the full moon and the lacewings have got to be stewed for twenty-one days . . . I’d say it’d be ready in about a month, if we can get all the ingredients.
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I'm more determined now; even though a month seems long, I think it's the best plan we've got and we need to be careful and thorough about getting ingredients.
metadata.source_text: But it's the best plan we've got, so full steam ahead, I say.
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I can tell Ron and Harry are worried and ready to help, but they panic more easily than I do; I feel responsible for steering the plan and checking we leave safely.
metadata.source_text: However, while Hermione was checking that the coast was clear for them to leave the bathroom, Ron muttered to Harry, “It’ll be a lot less hassle if you can just knock Malfoy off his broom tomorrow.”
metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I've learned that the potion Hermione is reading about will take about a month to be ready because of the timing for fluxweed and the lacewing stewing.
