metadata.description: I'm worried now and think Malfoy could cause a lot of trouble before the potion is ready — I'm more convinced we should act quickly rather than wait a month.

metadata.scene_title: Resolving to Brew and Quizzical Reactions

metadata.description: I reckon Harry could take Malfoy down in the air; I muttered that it would be much easier if Harry just knocked Malfoy off his broom tomorrow.

metadata.source_text: "Someone’s fixed it — it won’t leave Harry alone. It hasn’t gone for anyone else all game."
metadata.scene_title: Timeout, Resumption, and Pursuit of the Snitch

metadata.description: I believe we can’t stop now; if we do we’ll have to forfeit and I’m not going to let Slytherin win just because of a crazy Bludger.
metadata.source_text: "If we stop now, we’ll have to forfeit the match! And we’re not losing to Slytherin just because of a crazy Bludger!"
metadata.scene_title: Timeout, Resumption, and Pursuit of the Snitch

metadata.description: I trust Fred and George to look after other Bludger threats, but I don’t want them circling me — I told them to go back to the team and let me deal with the rogue one myself.
metadata.source_text: "with you two flying around me all the time the only way I’m going to catch the Snitch is if it flies up my sleeve. Go back to the rest of the team and let me deal with the rogue one."
metadata.scene_title: Timeout, Resumption, and Pursuit of the Snitch

metadata.description: I wasn’t present during the Quidditch match scene, so I don’t know what happened firsthand.

metadata.description: I saw the Golden Snitch hovering inches above Malfoy’s left ear while Malfoy was laughing and hadn’t noticed it, so the Snitch can hover very close to someone without being seen.
metadata.source_text: he saw it — the Golden Snitch. It was hovering inches above Malfoy’s left ear — and Malfoy, busy laughing at Harry, hadn’t seen it.
metadata.scene_title: The Bludger Fixes on Harry and He Is Injured

metadata.description: I believed I could get the Snitch even while dodging the Bludger, but after the Bludger smashed my arm I realise I can be seriously hurt mid-play and that hesitation can cost me.
metadata.source_text: For an agonizing moment, Harry hung in midair, not daring to speed toward Malfoy in case he looked up and saw the Snitch. WHAM. He had stayed still a second too long. The Bludger had hit him at last, smashed into his elbow, and Harry felt his arm break.
metadata.scene_title: The Bludger Fixes on Harry and He Is Injured

metadata.description: I hate Malfoy even more now — when he mocked me while I was being driven crazy by that Bludger and the Snitch was right above his head, I felt furious and betrayed by his mocking laughter.
metadata.source_text: “Training for the ballet, Potter?” yelled Malfoy as Harry was forced to do a stupid kind of twirl in midair to dodge the Bludger, and he fled, the Bludger trailing a few feet behind him; and then, glaring back at Malfoy in hatred, he saw it — the Golden Snitch.
metadata.scene_title: The Bludger Fixes on Harry and He Is Injured

metadata.description: I found out that Dobby stopped the barrier at the station and watched me miss the train — he sealed the gateway so I couldn't get through.
metadata.source_text: Dobby hid and watched for Harry Potter and sealed the gateway and Dobby had to iron his hands afterward

metadata.description: I learned that Dobby somehow caused the malicious Bludger that attacked me; Dobby admits the Bludger was meant to hurt me so I'd be sent home.
metadata.source_text: Dobby thought his Bludger would be enough to make —" "Your Bludger?" said Harry, anger rising once more. "What d’you mean, your Bludger? You made that Bludger try and kill me?" "Not kill you, sir, never kill you!" said Dobby, shocked. "Dobby wants to save Harry Potter’s life! Better sent home, grievously injured, than remain here, sir! Dobby only wanted Harry Potter hurt enough to be sent home!"

metadata.description: I went from furious to worried; at first I wanted Dobby gone and even threatened him, but when I saw how pathetic and frightened he is I couldn't stay angry — his tears made my anger ebb away.
metadata.source_text: Dobby smiled weakly. "Dobby is used to death threats, sir. Dobby gets them five times a day at home." He blew his nose on a corner of the filthy pillowcase he wore, looking so pathetic that Harry felt his anger ebb away in spite of himself.

metadata.description: I now believe there is a real danger at Hogwarts: the Chamber of Secrets has been opened before and might be open again, which could put Muggle-born students at risk.
metadata.source_text: "But I’m not Muggle-born — how can I be in danger from the Chamber?" "Ah, sir, ask no more, ask no more of poor Dobby," stammered the elf, his eyes huge in the dark. "Dark deeds are planned in this place, but Harry Potter must not be here when they happen — go home, Harry Potter, go home. Harry Potter must not meddle in this, sir, ’tis too dangerous —"

metadata.description: I realize Dobby isn't simply malicious — he's terrified for me and other students; he thinks I'm a symbol of hope and so he acted out of panic and loyalty to protect me.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby remembers how it was when He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named was at the height of his powers, sir! We house-elves were treated like vermin, sir!... Harry Potter survived, and the Dark Lord’s power was broken, and it was a new dawn, sir, and Harry Potter shone like a beacon of hope for those of us who thought the dark days would never end, sir."

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the hospital wing with Harry and Dobby, so I do not know what happened there firsthand.

metadata.source_text: Marge’ll be here for a week," Uncle Vernon snarled, "and while we’re on the subject" — he pointed a fat finger threateningly at Harry — "we need to get a few things straight before I go and collect her."

metadata.description: I'm furious and can't believe Vernon thinks he can force me to stick to his lie about where I go to school; I'm starting to feel I must stand up to him more.
metadata.source_text: "And you’ll be sticking to that story, boy, or there’ll be trouble," spat Uncle Vernon.

metadata.description: I see Aunt Marge as a dreadful guest who delights in tormenting me; Vernon backs her visits and treats me worse because of her presence.
metadata.source_text: Aunt Marge lived in the country, in a house with a large garden, where she bred bulldogs...Ripper had chased Harry out into the garden and up a tree, and Aunt Marge had refused to call him off until past midnight.

I wasn't present for the Dursleys' breakfast scene and didn't witness the conversation about Aunt Marge or Vernon's threats.

metadata.source_text: I shall monitor your behavior carefully during Marge’s visit. If, at the end of it, you’ve toed the line and kept to the story, I’ll sign your ruddy form.

metadata.description: I learned they send me to St. Brutus's school and that corporal punishment — the cane — is used there, because Aunt Marge asked and Uncle Vernon confirmed it.
metadata.source_text: Do they use the cane at St. Brutus’s, boy?" she barked across the table. "Er —" Uncle Vernon nodded curtly behind Aunt Marge’s back. "Yes," said Harry.

metadata.description: I’m convinced I must pretend more strongly to be ordinary; if I want that Hogsmeade trip I have to act like a real Muggle and hide anything that gives me away.
metadata.source_text: If he was going to act like a real Muggle, he’d better start now.

metadata.description: I feel Ron will look after Hedwig while I’m forced to keep away — I trust Ron enough to mind her for a week.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig, you’re going to have to clear off for a week. Go with Errol. Ron’ll look after you. I’ll write him a note, explaining.

I've learned that Aunt Marge can insult me and my parents without shame, and that she drinks a lot and brags about cruelty toward animals.
metadata.source_text: Aunt Marge had already had quite a lot of wine. Her huge face was very red. "Just a small one, then," she chuckled. "A bit more than that . . . and a bit more . . . that's the ticket."

metadata.description: I felt a reckless rage come over me and realised I'm not going to stand there and take those lies about my parents — I'm done letting them bully me.
metadata.source_text: "A reckless rage had come over Harry. He kicked his trunk open, pulled out his wand, and pointed it at Uncle Vernon."

metadata.description: I think Uncle Vernon and Aunt Petunia will never really protect me; Vernon snarled at me and Petunia looked tense while Marge attacked me, so I don't trust them to care for me properly.
metadata.source_text: Uncle Vernon and Aunt Petunia were looking extremely tense. Dudley had even looked up from his pie to gape at his parents.

I learned who the conductor was and what the Knight Bus does: it's emergency transport for stranded witches or wizards and the conductor's name is Stan Shunpike.
metadata.source_text: "Welcome to the Knight Bus, emergency transport for the stranded witch or wizard. Just stick out your wand hand, step on board, and we can take you anywhere you want to go. My name is Stan Shunpike, and I will be your conductor this eve —"

metadata.description: I felt a bit annoyed and defensive when that bloke sneered at me for falling over; I don't like being laughed at, and I didn't want anyone thinking I fell on purpose.
metadata.source_text: "What were you doin' down there?" said Stan, dropping his professional manner. "Fell over," said Harry. "'Choo fall over for?" sniggered Stan. "I didn't do it on purpose," said Harry, annoyed.

metadata.description: Seeing Stan close up, I noticed he's only a few years older than me with big ears and pimples, and his teasing manner makes me see him as a young, disrespectful conductor rather than a proper, professional one.
metadata.source_text: "Close up, he saw that Stan Shunpike was only a few years older than he was, eighteen or nineteen at most, with large, protruding ears and quite a few pimples."

metadata.source_text: "There was a big black thing," said Harry, pointing uncertainly into the gap. "Like a dog . . . but massive . . ."

metadata.description: I decided I can't let anyone see my scar or recognize me; if the Ministry is watching, I must lie and hide what I am to make things harder for them.
metadata.source_text: "Woss that on your ’ead?" said Stan abruptly. "Nothing," said Harry quickly, flattening his hair over his scar.

metadata.description: I gave Stan a false name — I said I was Neville Longbottom — because I don't trust strangers on the bus with my real identity right now.
metadata.source_text: "Woss your name?" Stan persisted. "Neville Longbottom," said Harry, saying the first name that came into his head.

metadata.description: I've learned the Minister of Magic, Cornelius Fudge, was waiting for me at the Leaky Cauldron and has arranged a room for me at the inn. He told me to keep to Diagon Alley and be back before dark.
metadata.source_text: Room eleven’s free, Harry," said Fudge. "I think you’ll be very comfortable. Just one thing, and I’m sure you’ll understand . . . I don’t want you wandering off into Muggle London, all right? Keep to Diagon Alley. And you’re to be back here before dark each night. Sure you’ll understand. Tom will be keeping an eye on you for me.

metadata.description: I'm starting to doubt the Ministry's consistency; I used to expect strict punishment from them, but Fudge acted as if my breaking the Decree was nothing and even awkwardly avoided the issue.

metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Leaky Cauldron and Meeting Cornelius Fudge

metadata.description: I feel uncertain about Cornelius Fudge now; he seemed pleasant but also awkward and evasive, so I can't tell if he's genuinely looking out for me or has some other motive.
metadata.source_text: Well, I’ll be off, plenty to do, you know. . . ." "Have you had any luck with Black yet?" Harry asked. Fudge’s finger slipped on the silver fastenings of his cloak.

metadata.source_text: THE FIREBOLT This state-of-the-art racing broom sports a streamlined, superfine handle of ash, treated with a diamond-hard polish and hand-numbered with its own registration number. Each individually selected birch twig in the broomtail has been honed to aerodynamic perfection, giving the Firebolt unsurpassable balance and pinpoint precision. The Firebolt has an acceleration of 150 miles an hour in ten seconds and incorporates an unbreakable Braking Charm.

metadata.source_text: So's Scabbers's rat tonic," said Ron, throwing things out of his trunk to look. "I'll get Scabbers's stuff, I'm packed," Harry said to Ron, and he went downstairs.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Announces Percy’s Badge and Farewells

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Weasley kitchen where Percy's Head Boy badge went missing, so I don't know what happened there.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the whole family exchange about Percy's badge and the immediate arguments afterward, so I can't provide an eyewitness account of everyone’s reactions.

metadata.description: I've learned that Sirius Black escaped from Azkaban — Mr. Weasley warned me about him before I left.
metadata.source_text: "There’s something I’ve got to tell you before you leave —" said Mr. Weasley, in a tense voice.

metadata.description: I honestly don’t feel as frightened as people expect; I don’t think Sirius Black can be worse than Voldemort, so I’m not going to panic.
metadata.source_text: "I’m not. Really," he added, because Mr. Weasley was looking disbelieving. "I’m not trying to be a hero, but seriously, Sirius Black can’t be worse than Voldemort, can he?"

metadata.description: I know Mr. and Mrs. Weasley care enough to argue about my safety and to warn me privately; Arthur feels anxious but trusts I can handle myself.
metadata.source_text: "That’s not the way I’d have chosen for you to find out," said Mr. Weasley, looking anxious.

metadata.description: I've read that Hogsmeade is the only entirely non-Muggle settlement in Britain and that its inn was the goblin rebellion headquarters in 1612.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve read it’s the only entirely non-Muggle settlement in Britain —" "In Sites of Historical Sorcery it says the inn was the headquarters for the 1612 goblin rebellion,"

metadata.description: I’m much more worried about Harry now that I know Sirius Black escaped; I think Harry will have to be extremely careful and not look for trouble.
metadata.source_text: "Sirius Black escaped to come after you? Oh, Harry . . . you’ll have to be really, really careful. Don’t go looking for trouble, Harry —"

metadata.description: I don’t trust the idea of sneaking Harry out with Ron’s reckless suggestions; I think protecting Harry means following rules, not risking him for adventure.
metadata.source_text: "I don’t think Harry should be sneaking out of school with Black on the loose —"

metadata.description: I found out that Sirius Black escaped from Azkaban and that nobody knows how he did it; everyone’s saying it’s unheard of.
metadata.source_text: "No one knows how he got out of Azkaban," said Ron uncomfortably. "No one’s ever done it before. And he was a top-security prisoner too."

metadata.description: I’m terrified at the idea that Black might come after Harry; I’d never have expected to be so shaken by the news.
metadata.source_text: "How thick would Harry have to be, to go looking for a nutter who wants to kill him?" said Ron shakily.

metadata.description: I’d do anything to help Harry get to Hogsmeade — I even think being with him would make Black less likely to attack, so I’m ready to stand by him.
metadata.source_text: "But if we’re with him," said Ron spiritedly to Hermione, "Black wouldn’t dare —"

metadata.description: I saw a cloaked figure with a gray, slimy, scabbed hand slip briefly into view before it drew the hand back into its cloak.
metadata.source_text: There was a hand protruding from the cloak and it was glistening, grayish, slimy-looking, and scabbed, like something dead that had decayed in water. . . .

metadata.description: I felt an intense cold sweep over us and my breath caught when the creature drew that long, slow, rattling breath.
metadata.source_text: And then the thing beneath the hood, whatever it was, drew a long, slow, rattling breath, as though it were trying to suck something more than air from its surroundings. An intense cold swept over them all. Harry felt his own breath catch in his chest.

metadata.description: Seeing Lupin wake and act made me trust him more as someone who can protect us in a crisis.
metadata.source_text: Professor Lupin appeared to have woken up at last. Harry could hear movements in his corner. None of them spoke.

metadata.description: I noticed Professor Lupin was fast asleep and that he looked like he could do with some food when the trolley passed.
metadata.source_text: Er — Professor?" she said. "Excuse me — Professor?" He didn’t move. "Don’t worry, dear," said the witch as she handed Harry a large stack of Cauldron Cakes.

metadata.description: I became more cautious about provoking a scene because Professor Lupin was asleep and I wanted to avoid embarrassing or endangering him.
metadata.source_text: Ron," hissed Hermione, pointing at Professor Lupin, "be careful . . ." But Professor Lupin was still fast asleep.

metadata.description: I saw the lamps go out and people stumble; then I watched Lupin produce a small fire in his hand to light the compartment.
metadata.source_text: There was a soft, crackling noise, and a shivering light filled the compartment. Professor Lupin appeared to be holding a handful of flames.

metadata.description: I decided I wasn't going to take any more of Malfoy's rude comments about my family and meant to stand up for myself.
metadata.source_text: I’m not going to take any crap from Malfoy this year," he said angrily. "I mean it. If he makes one more crack about my family, I’m going to get hold of his head and —

metadata.description: I learned that Lupin was sleeping in the compartment, and that he was breathing so I shouldn't panic about him.
metadata.source_text: "I suppose he is asleep?" said Ron quietly as the witch slid the compartment door closed. "I mean — he hasn’t died, has he?" "No, no, he’s breathing," whispered Hermione

metadata.description: I noticed something moving outside the window and thought people might be coming aboard when the train slowed and lights went out.
metadata.source_text: "There’s something moving out there," Ron said. "I think people are coming aboard. . . ."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.

I learned that the dementors were on the train earlier and frightened people — they make prisoners go weak and mad in Azkaban, and they really do suck the happiness out of a place.
metadata.source_text: They’re horrible things, those dementors. . . . They suck the happiness out of a place, dementors. Most of the prisoners go mad in there.

metadata.description: I feel a bit better about Malfoy now; hearing he nearly wet himself when the dementors came makes me less intimidated by him.
metadata.source_text: Nearly wet himself," said Fred, with a contemptuous glance at Malfoy.

metadata.description: I know I can count on the Weasleys — George and Fred are on my side, sharing schedules and sticking up for me, which makes me feel supported.
metadata.source_text: New third-year course schedules," said George, passing them over.

metadata.description: I've noticed that we're starting new subjects today from my timetable — new classes begin this morning and I’m quite pleased about that.
metadata.source_text: Ooh, good, we’re starting some new subjects today," she said happily.

metadata.description: I’m not going to be overwhelmed by a heavy timetable because I’ve already fixed the clashes with Professor McGonagall; I believe I can manage the workload.
metadata.source_text: I’ll manage. I’ve fixed it all with Professor McGonagall.

metadata.description: When Ron questions my schedule I snap because I don’t like being patronised about my abilities — I expect him to trust I’ve sorted it properly.
metadata.source_text: Oh, Ron, what’s it to you if my schedule’s a bit full?" Hermione snapped. "I told you, I’ve fixed it all with Professor McGonagall.

metadata.description: I learned that Malfoy was terrified of the dementors on the train — he ran into our compartment and nearly fainted, which shows he’s not so brave.
metadata.source_text: He wasn’t so cocky last night when the dementors were down at our end of the train. Came running into our compartment, didn’t he, Fred?

metadata.description: I’m more convinced now that dementors are awful things that sap you of happiness and strength; Dad’s story about Azkaban made me realise how dreadful they must be.
metadata.source_text: Dad had to go out to Azkaban one time, remember, Fred? And he said it was the worst place he’d ever been, he came back all weak and shaking. . . .

metadata.description: I’m protective of Hermione when I see her schedule — I question it because I care and don’t want her to be overwhelmed, even if she’s annoyed by my worrying.
metadata.source_text: Hermione," said Ron, frowning as he looked over her shoulder, "they’ve messed up your schedule.

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid is giving his very first lesson right after lunch and he’s been up since five getting everything ready.
metadata.source_text: Yer in my firs’ ever lesson! Right after lunch! Bin up since five gettin’ everythin’ ready. . . . Hope it’s okay. . . . Me, a teacher . . . hones’ly. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I’m surprised to hear books won’t help much in Divination; I didn’t expect Hermione to be shortchanged by books in any subject.
metadata.source_text: Books can take you only so far in this field. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I noticed Ron and I both glanced at Hermione when Professor Trelawney said books won’t take you far; I’m more aware of Hermione’s reliance on books now.
metadata.source_text: At these words, both Harry and Ron glanced, grinning, at Hermione, who looked startled at the news that books wouldn’t be much help in this subject.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I discovered from Professor Trelawney that Divination is thought to be the most difficult of all magical arts and requires the Sight more than book learning.
metadata.source_text: So you have chosen to study Divination, the most difficult of all magical arts. I must warn you at the outset that if you do not have the Sight, there is very little I will be able to teach you. Books can take you only so far in this field. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I’m taken aback and a little unsettled to learn that books won’t be much help in Divination; that clashes with how I usually trust written knowledge.
metadata.source_text: At these words, both Harry and Ron glanced, grinning, at Hermione, who looked startled at the news that books wouldn’t be much help in this subject.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I noticed Harry and Ron glanced at me when Divination was criticized as unsuited to books; I realise they expect me to be the book expert even in subjects where books aren’t enough.
metadata.source_text: At these words, both Harry and Ron glanced, grinning, at Hermione, who looked startled at the news that books wouldn’t be much help in this subject.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I found out that Divination is at the top of the North Tower and it’ll take us ten minutes to get there.
metadata.source_text: We’d better go, look, Divination’s at the top of North Tower. It’ll take us ten minutes to get there. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I’m anxious about being on time for Divination after Hagrid’s announcement; Hagrid being a teacher makes me worry about what sort of lesson he’ll give.
metadata.source_text: Wonder what he’s been getting ready?” said Ron, a note of anxiety in his voice.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I noticed Harry and I both looked at Hermione when Professor Trelawney said books won’t help much; I’m reminded that Hermione’s our go-to for book knowledge even when books might fail.
metadata.source_text: At these words, both Harry and Ron glanced, grinning, at Hermione, who looked startled at the news that books wouldn’t be much help in this subject.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Announcement and Divination Class Begins

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Trelawney reads tea leaves and sees ominous symbols; she told us the tea-leaf method is the first-term Divination lesson and that she can interpret shapes like falcons and skulls.
metadata.source_text: We will be covering the basic methods of Divination this year. The first term will be devoted to reading the tea leaves.

metadata.description: I started off thinking Divination was a daft, bookish subject, but when Trelawney screamed and said I had the Grim I actually felt shaken — suddenly it felt real and frightening to me.
metadata.source_text: Everyone went quiet to watch. Professor Trelawney was staring into the teacup... gasped, and then screamed.

metadata.description: I noticed people looked at me differently after Trelawney named the Grim; even Ron and others seemed to avoid my eyes, so I feel more alone and aware that classmates see me as marked.
metadata.source_text: Now nobody seemed to want to look at him. 'I think we will leave the lesson here for today,' said Professor Trelawney...

metadata.description: I've learned that tea-leaf reading is done by swilling the dregs three times with the left hand, turning the cup upside down on its saucer, and interpreting the patterns using Unfogging the Future pages five and six.
metadata.source_text: Swill these around the cup three times with the left hand, then turn the cup upside down on its saucer... You will interpret the patterns using pages five and six of Unfogging the Future.

metadata.description: I was surprised to find that books won't teach everything in Divination; Trelawney said books can take you only so far in this field, which made me realise there's a limit to textbook learning here.
metadata.source_text: Books can take you only so far in this field...

metadata.description: When I flatly said I don't think Harry's cup looked like a Grim, I realised I could challenge a teacher's dramatic reading; I perceive that I can speak up even if others are shocked.
metadata.source_text: I don't think it looks like a Grim,' she said flatly.

metadata.description: I found out how the tea-leaf guide works — you look for shapes and check Unfogging the Future; for example, an acorn can mean 'a windfall, unexpected gold', according to the book.
metadata.source_text: 'A windfall, unexpected gold.' Excellent, you can lend me some... 'A windfall, unexpected gold.'

metadata.description: I was joking about the readings and thought they were daft, but when Professor Trelawney started declaring dark omens for Harry I stopped laughing; the whole thing felt serious and a bit scary.
metadata.source_text: Professor Trelawney whirled around as Harry let out a snort of laughter... Professor Trelawney was staring at her.

metadata.description: I noticed Hermione spoke back to the teacher and everyone stared at her; I admiringly realised Hermione can be blunt and bold, and that surprised me because I hadn't heard her speak to a teacher like that before.
metadata.source_text: They had never heard Hermione speak to a teacher like that before.

metadata.description: I've learned you have to stroke those Care of Magical Creatures textbooks to calm them down; they try to bite if you don't.
metadata.source_text: Yeh’ve got ter stroke ’em,
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I want Hagrid's first lesson to go well; I feel protective of him and annoyed at Malfoy's sneering.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid was looking downcast and Harry wanted Hagrid’s first lesson to be a success.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I still don't like Malfoy and I tell him to shut up when he mocks Hagrid; Malfoy makes me defensive toward Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: “Shut up, Malfoy,” said Harry quietly.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I've seen Hagrid rip the Spellotape off my book and calm it by running a finger down the spine; stroking the book makes it stop trying to bite.
metadata.source_text: He took Hermione’s copy and ripped off the Spellotape that bound it. The book tried to bite, but Hagrid ran a giant forefinger down its spine, and the book shivered, and then fell open and lay quiet in his hand.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I feel a bit uncertain because Hagrid seemed unsure when he spoke to me, but the books do behave as he said they would when stroked.
metadata.source_text: “I — I thought they were funny,” Hagrid said uncertainly to Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: Hagrid treated my book gently and helped it settle; that makes me see him as caring and capable despite his awkwardness.
metadata.source_text: The book tried to bite, but Hagrid ran a giant forefinger down its spine, and the book shivered, and then fell open and lay quiet in his hand.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I've learned the Care of Magical Creatures books need stroking to be opened safely; otherwise they'll try to rip your hands off.
metadata.source_text: Yeh’ve got ter stroke ’em,
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I think Hagrid's lesson might be odd but it's supposed to work; despite the embarrassment, the method does calm the books.
metadata.source_text: He took Hermione’s copy and ripped off the Spellotape that bound it. The book tried to bite, but Hagrid ran a giant forefinger down its spine, and the book shivered, and then fell open and lay quiet in his hand.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I don't like Malfoy mocking Hagrid; hearing Malfoy sneer makes me side with Hagrid more, even if Hagrid seems a bit lost.
metadata.source_text: “God, this place is going to the dogs,” said Malfoy loudly. “That oaf teaching classes, my father’ll have a fit when I tell him —”
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care of Magical Creatures — Book Mishap and Hippogriffs Introduced

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid can get very drunk and he'll hug us so hard it feels like my ribs might break.
metadata.source_text: He grabbed both Harry and Ron and pulled them into a bone-breaking hug.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I feel more worried about wandering around after dark now because Hagrid got really angry when he found out I had been out late.
metadata.source_text: WHAT D’YEH THINK YOU’RE DOIN’, EH? ... YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY!
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I know Hagrid cares an awful lot about me — he bursts into tears, hugs me, and then gets protective and furious when he thinks I've been out late.
metadata.source_text: Tears leaked out of the crinkled corners of Hagrid’s beetle-black eyes. He grabbed both Harry and Ron and pulled them into a bone-breaking hug.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I've noticed Hagrid had been drinking enough that someone needed to take his tankard away and empty it out to stop him from drinking more.
metadata.source_text: “I think you’ve had enough to drink, Hagrid,” said Hermione firmly. She took the tankard from the table and went outside to empty it.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I feel more certain that being practical and firm helps when Hagrid's upset or drunk; taking action calms things down quicker than letting him continue.
metadata.source_text: “I think you’ve had enough to drink, Hagrid,” said Hermione firmly. She took the tankard from the table and went outside to empty it.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I see myself as someone Hagrid and the others rely on to be sensible — I can interrupt and manage a difficult moment to keep everyone safe.
metadata.source_text: She took the tankard from the table and went outside to empty it.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid can get emotional and grab you in a huge hug when he's pleased or upset, and it can actually hurt a bit.
metadata.source_text: He grabbed both Harry and Ron and pulled them into a bone-breaking hug.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that we shouldn't be wandering about after dark — Hagrid shouted at us proper, and that frightened me.
metadata.source_text: “YEH’RE NOT TO GO WANDERIN’ AROUND AFTER DARK, HARRY! AN’ YOU TWO! LETTIN’ HIM!”
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I feel protective and a bit guilty toward Hagrid; he's clearly fond of us and gets upset when he thinks we've been careless or put him in a bad way.
metadata.source_text: “Listen, it was good of yeh ter come an’ see me, I really —” Hagrid stopped dead, staring at Harry as though he’d only just realized he was there.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Drunk, Comforted, and Scolded by Dumbledore's Rule Reminder

metadata.description: I've heard him say he's takin' us back up to school — he intends to return us there himself.
metadata.source_text: I’m takin’ yer all back up ter school

metadata.description: I reckon he really doesn't want us comin' down to see him after dark no more; he's proper worried about our safety.
metadata.source_text: don’ let me catch yeh walkin’ down ter see me after dark again

metadata.description: I can tell he cares but thinks he's not worth us riskin' danger for — makes me feel guilty and protective toward him.
metadata.source_text: I’m not worth that!

metadata.description: He's sayin' he'll take us all back up to school himself — that's his plan for us.
metadata.source_text: I’m takin’ yer all back up ter school

metadata.description: I've come to believe he's serious about us not visitin' him after dark; he's dead set on keepin' us away for our own good.
metadata.source_text: don’ let me catch yeh walkin’ down ter see me after dark again

metadata.description: He says he's not worth us riskin' trouble for, and that makes me feel protective — I don't want him puttin' himself down like that.
metadata.source_text: I’m not worth that!

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the speaker's warning, so I don't have direct knowledge of what was said or how it was said.
I saw Snape favor Malfoy in class — he let Malfoy get away with demands while he would have punished me or Ron if we'd been late.
metadata.source_text: Snape wouldn’t have said “settle down” if they’d walked in late, he’d have given them detention. But Malfoy had always been able to get away with anything in Snape’s classes; Snape was head of Slytherin House, and generally favored his own students above all others.
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I’m more convinced than before that Snape really dislikes me — he gave me that look of loathing when he told me to skin Malfoy’s shrivelfig.
metadata.source_text: “Potter, you can skin Malfoy’s shrivelfig,” said Snape, giving Harry the look of loathing he always reserved just for him.
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I notice Malfoy’s smugness toward Ron and me — he knows how to use Snape and enjoys winding us up, winked at Crabbe and Goyle when Pansy looked away.
metadata.source_text: But Harry saw him wink at Crabbe and Goyle when Pansy had looked away.
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I found out Snape will obey Malfoy’s complaints — Snape told me to cut Malfoy’s roots and then to swap roots with him when Malfoy lied about his arm.
metadata.source_text: “Weasley, cut up Malfoy’s roots for him,” said Snape without looking up. ... “Change roots with Malfoy, Weasley.”
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I’m angrier and more humiliated than before — Snape’s favouritism and Malfoy’s cheek made me go brick red and I felt wrongly punished.
metadata.source_text: Ron went brick red. ... Ron shoved his own beautifully cut roots across the table at Malfoy, then took up the knife again.
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I think Malfoy is a proper bully and a sneak — he pretended to be hurt and then accused me of mutilating his roots while smirking at me.
metadata.source_text: “There’s nothing wrong with your arm,” he hissed at Malfoy. Malfoy smirked across the table. “Professor,” drawled Malfoy, “Weasley’s mutilating my roots, sir.”
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I was not present during the potions class with Snape, Malfoy, Harry, and Ron, so I do not know the details of how the ingredients were handled.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was not present in the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Potions Class: Malfoy’s Taunts and Snape’s Favoritism

metadata.description: I heard from Seamus that the Daily Prophet says a Muggle spotted Sirius Black not too far from Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Daily Prophet this morning — they reckon Sirius Black’s been sighted.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: Malfoy winding me up about Hagrid made me angry enough to start shaking — I feel even more sure Malfoy tries to get people into trouble.
metadata.source_text: So that’s why you’re putting it on,” said Harry, accidentally beheading a dead caterpillar because his hand was shaking in anger. “To try to get Hagrid fired.”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I’m convinced Malfoy enjoys provoking people and using petty cruelty to get at others; I don't trust his motives when he speaks to me.
metadata.source_text: “So that’s why you’re putting it on,” said Harry, accidentally beheading a dead caterpillar because his hand was shaking in anger. “To try to get Hagrid fired.”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I know Neville's potion was meant to be bright acid green but turned orange because he added too much rat spleen and failed to use the correct dash of leech juice.
metadata.source_text: His potion, which was supposed to be a bright, acid green, had turned — “Orange, Longbottom,” said Snape, ladling some up and allowing it to splash back into the cauldron, so that everyone could see. “Orange. Tell me, boy, does anything penetrate that thick skull of yours? Didn’t you hear me say, quite clearly, that only one rat spleen was needed? Didn’t I state plainly that a dash of leech juice would suffice?
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I thought offering help would be sensible and practical, but Snape's cold rebuke made me feel embarrassed and taught me that showing willingness to assist can be punished in front of the class.
metadata.source_text: “Please, sir,” said Hermione, “please, I could help Neville put it right —” “I don’t remember asking you to show off, Miss Granger,” said Snape coldly, and Hermione went as pink as Neville.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I feel more wary of Professor Snape after he publicly shamed Neville and dismissed my offer to help; I see him as harsher and less fair than I had hoped.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t remember asking you to show off, Miss Granger,” said Snape coldly, and Hermione went as pink as Neville.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I heard Seamus telling Harry that a Muggle believed they saw Sirius Black close by, so news of Black's possible sighting is spreading fast among the students.
metadata.source_text: “Hey, Harry,” said Seamus Finnigan, leaning over to borrow Harry’s brass scales, “have you heard? Daily Prophet this morning — they reckon Sirius Black’s been sighted.”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: After Malfoy’s sneer about Hagrid, I’m more inclined to believe Malfoy will use any excuse to try and get Hagrid into trouble; I feel irritated with him.
metadata.source_text: “So that’s why you’re putting it on,” said Harry, accidentally beheading a dead caterpillar because his hand was shaking in anger. “To try to get Hagrid fired.”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy’s Provocations and News of Sirius Black

metadata.description: I trust Harry and want to be alert with him about Sirius Black's sighting; when Harry and I both ask where Black was seen, it shows how we stick together over worrying news.

I learned that a boggart hides in dark, enclosed places like wardrobes or under beds and that our wardrobe bumped the wall because the boggart is inside.
metadata.source_text: Wardrobes, the gap beneath beds, the cupboards under sinks — I once met one that had lodged itself in a grandfather clock. This one moved in yesterday afternoon, and I asked the headmaster if the staff would leave it to give my third years some practice.

metadata.source_text: His first thought was Lord Voldemort — a Voldemort returned to full strength. But before he had even started to plan a possible counterattack on a boggart-Voldemort, a horrible image came floating to the surface of his mind. . . . A rotting, glistening hand, slithering back beneath a black cloak . . . a long, rattling breath from an unseen mouth . . . then a cold so penetrating it felt like drowning. . . .

metadata.description: I used to doubt I'd be able to face a boggart, but Lupin being impressed made me realise I can do it — I feel a lot happier about it now.
metadata.source_text: Well, well . . . I’m impressed.” He smiled slightly at the look of surprise on Harry’s face. “That suggests that what you fear most of all is — fear. Very wise, Harry." ... "So you’ve been thinking that I didn’t believe you capable of fighting the boggart?” said Lupin shrewdly. “Well . . . yeah,” said Harry. He was suddenly feeling a lot happier.

I am very lucky to be working alongside Professor Snape; there aren’t many wizards who are up to making it.”

Dervish and Banges, the wizarding equipment shop, Zonko’s Joke Shop, into the Three Broomsticks for foaming mugs of hot butterbeer, and many places besides. “The post office, Harry! About two hundred owls, all sitting on shelves, all color-coded depending on how fast you want your letter to get there!” “Honeydukes has got a new kind of fudge; they were giving out free samples, there’s a bit, look —”

metadata.description: Seeing Snape humiliate Hermione and give Ron detention made me feel more convinced that Snape is unfair and likes to belittle people in front of the class.
metadata.source_text: "That is the second time you have spoken out of turn, Miss Granger," said Snape coolly. "Five more points from Gryffindor for being an insufferable know-it-all."
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I'm more protective of Hermione and angrier at Snape now; after he called her an insufferable know-it-all and took points, my sympathies and loyalty to my friends feel stronger.
metadata.source_text: Hermione went very red, put down her hand, and stared at the floor with her eyes full of tears.
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I've discovered that Snape will take control of the lesson and order the class to page 394, even if Professor Lupin hasn't taught that subject yet.
metadata.source_text: "— werewolves," said Snape. "But, sir," said Hermione, seemingly unable to restrain herself, "we're not supposed to do werewolves yet, we're due to start hinkypunks —"
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I feel shocked and deeply upset that answering a question to help the class resulted in public humiliation and lost house points; I didn't expect Snape to be so deliberately cruel.
metadata.source_text: "That is the second time you have spoken out of turn, Miss Granger," said Snape coolly. "Five more points from Gryffindor for being an insufferable know-it-all."
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I now see Snape as openly hostile toward me; his reaction to my wanting to answer shows he resents my eagerness and will punish me for speaking up.
metadata.source_text: Hermione went very red, put down her hand, and stared at the floor with her eyes full of tears.
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I learned that if I defend Hermione openly against Snape's bullying, Snape will punish me with detention and threats about criticizing his teaching.
metadata.source_text: "You asked us a question and she knows the answer! Why ask if you don't want to be told?" ... "Detention, Weasley," Snape said silkily, his face very close to Ron's.
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: After seeing Hermione go red and nearly cry because of Snape, I'm angrier at him and more willing to stand up for my friends even if I get in trouble.
metadata.source_text: Hermione went very red, put down her hand, and stared at the floor with her eyes full of tears. ... "You asked us a question and she knows the answer!"
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hermione and annoyed with Snape; his treatment of her makes me see him as someone who enjoys trampling on people, especially Gryffindors.
metadata.source_text: It was a mark of how much the class loathed Snape that they were all glaring at him, because every one of them had called Hermione a know-it-all at least once, and Ron ... said loudly, "You asked us a question and she knows the answer!"
metadata.scene_title: Snape's Belittling Lesson and Detention Orders

metadata.description: I learned that Snape made everyone write an essay on how to recognize and kill werewolves — two rolls of parchment, due Monday morning.
metadata.source_text: “You will each write an essay, to be handed in to me, on the ways you recognize and kill werewolves. I want two rolls of parchment on the subject, and I want them by Monday morning.”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I'm starting to think there's something personal between Snape and Lupin — Snape's gone out of his way to embarrass him in class.
metadata.source_text: “Why’s he got it in for Lupin? D’you think this is all because of the boggart?”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I feel closer to Hermione after we both complain about Snape — she listens and worries about Lupin the way I do.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Hermione left the room with the rest of the class, who waited until they were well out of earshot, then burst into a furious tirade about Snape.
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I've learned that Snape marked Lupin's answer scarcely, and that he ordered a hard essay assignment on werewolves for the whole class.
metadata.source_text: “You will each write an essay, to be handed in to me, on the ways you recognize and kill werewolves. I want two rolls of parchment on the subject, and I want them by Monday morning.”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I really hope Professor Lupin gets better soon; after what happened, I'm more worried about his condition than before.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t know,” said Hermione pensively. “But I really hope Professor Lupin gets better soon. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I find myself agreeing with Harry's indignation about Snape, which makes me feel more aligned with him on this matter.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Hermione left the room with the rest of the class, who waited until they were well out of earshot, then burst into a furious tirade about Snape.
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I've been told I have to do detention scrubbing bedpans in the hospital wing and I can't use magic to get out of it.
metadata.source_text: “I’ve got to scrub out the bedpans in the hospital wing. Without magic!”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I'm convinced Snape's a complete — well, he's made me furious enough to wish someone would finish him off for us.
metadata.source_text: “D’you know what that” — (he called Snape something that made Hermione say “Ron!”) — “is making me do? I’ve got to scrub out the bedpans in the hospital wing. Without magic!”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I feel even more hostile toward Snape and wish Sirius Black had been in Snape's office so Black could have 'finished him off' for us.
metadata.source_text: “Why couldn’t Black have hidden in Snape’s office, eh? He could have finished him off for us!”
metadata.scene_title: Students Leave After Snape's Assignment; Harry and Friends Talk

metadata.description: I learned that my glasses were useless in a downpour — the rain on the lenses can blind me mid-Quidditch and make me miss Bludgers and other players.
metadata.source_text: his vision was so clouded by the rain on his glasses he hadn’t seen them coming.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I felt more determined once I could see; when Hermione fixed my glasses I believed we still had a real chance to catch the Snitch before nightfall.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s spell had done the trick. Harry was still numb with cold, still wetter than he’d ever been in his life, but he could see. Full of fresh determination, he urged his broom...
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I owe Hermione one — she saved the game for me with that spell, and I noticed how amazed everyone was. She really pulled us out of a bad spot.
metadata.source_text: He handed them to her, and as the team watched in amazement, Hermione tapped them with her wand and said, “Impervius!”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I've learned that Impervius will repel water from glass surfaces — it keeps rain off spectacles well enough for a Seeker to see in a storm.
metadata.source_text: She tapped them with her wand and said, “Impervius!” “There!” she said, handing them back to Harry. “They’ll repel water!”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I felt pleased and confident that a quick, correct spell could make a real difference in an urgent situation; seeing Harry's relief changed how I felt about acting in the crowd.
metadata.source_text: Hermione appeared at his shoulder; she was holding her cloak over her head and was, inexplicably, beaming. “I’ve had an idea, Harry! Give me your glasses, quick!”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I realised the team values practical help as much as playing skill — when I fixed Harry's glasses, Wood and the others were astonished and grateful, which made me feel useful to them.
metadata.source_text: Wood looked as though he could have kissed her. “Brilliant!” he called hoarsely after her as she disappeared into the crowd.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Quidditch match in the storm, so I don't know what happened on the pitch.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match: Storm, Hermione's Spell, and the Dementor Attack

metadata.description: I realised there were at least a hundred dementors standing beneath me, and their presence made the stadium go eerily quiet and filled me with freezing, drowning sensations.
metadata.source_text: At least a hundred dementors, their hidden faces pointing up at him, were standing beneath him.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I suddenly believed I couldn't trust my senses when dementors were near — the silence, the cold and the screaming inside my head showed me they can overwhelm everything I know.
metadata.source_text: An eerie silence was falling across the stadium. The wind, though as strong as ever, was forgetting to roar. It was as though someone had turned off the sound, as though Harry had gone suddenly deaf
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I felt terrified and helpless in a way that made me cling to life and others more; after feeling that woman's screaming inside my head, I can't pretend the dementors are only a distant danger anymore.
metadata.source_text: Someone was screaming, screaming inside his head . . . a woman . . . “Not Harry, not Harry, please not Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I noticed that the presence of dementors causes an immediate, overwhelming silence and cold that affects people's minds and bodies very quickly.
metadata.source_text: An eerie silence was falling across the stadium. The wind, though as strong as ever, was forgetting to roar.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I now think dementors can do more than just suck happiness; they can invade minds with vivid, traumatic impressions and voices, making their victims lose control.
metadata.source_text: It was as though freezing water were rising in his chest, cutting at his insides. And then he heard it again. . . . Someone was screaming, screaming inside his head
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I'm more worried about Harry's vulnerability to dark influences after seeing how deeply the dementors affected him; I feel I must be closer and more protective of him.
metadata.source_text: With a jolt of panic, Harry threw himself flat to the broom-handle and zoomed toward the Snitch.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I realised something awful was happening when the crowd's noise dropped and Harry's flying suddenly looked wrong — like the air itself had been choked by those dark creatures.
metadata.source_text: An eerie silence was falling across the stadium. The wind, though as strong as ever, was forgetting to roar.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I started to believe dementors are terrifyingly dangerous up close; hearing that horrible screaming in Harry's head would convince me they're not things you can face lightly.
metadata.source_text: Someone was screaming, screaming inside his head . . . a woman . . . “Not Harry, not Harry, please not Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: Seeing Harry fall under that horror made me feel more protective and scared for him; I don't want him to have to face those creatures on his own.
metadata.source_text: With a jolt of panic, Harry threw himself flat to the broom-handle and zoomed toward the Snitch.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Mental Agony and Fainting; Recovery in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I woke up in the hospital wing with my body aching and flashes in my head — lightning, a Grim, the Snitch, dementors — and I learned I’d fallen during the match.
metadata.source_text: The lightning — the Grim — the Snitch — and the dementors . . . “What happened?” he said, sitting up so suddenly they all gasped.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: I thought I might be dead when I fell; after waking up I had to accept that I hadn’t died but I wasn’t safe either — something terrifying had happened to me.
metadata.source_text: We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: Being surrounded by the Gryffindor team, with Ron and Hermione there and everyone upset, made me feel how much they care — I noticed their worry and mud-splattered relief firsthand.
metadata.source_text: The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed. Ron and Hermione were also there, looking as though they’d just climbed out of a swimming pool.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: I saw Harry awake in the hospital wing and noticed his memory jumping from scary images to questions about the match; I learned he’d been through something awful and was confused.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s eyes snapped open. He was lying in the hospital wing. The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: I was shaken and my eyes were bloodshot; seeing Harry brought home to me how frightened I am about whatever caused him to fall — I feel more frightened now than before.
metadata.source_text: Hermione made a small, squeaky noise. Her eyes were extremely bloodshot.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: Being at Harry’s bedside and hearing the others’ reactions reminded me that we stand together — I care deeply about him and we’re tied by this terrifying experience.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione were also there, looking as though they’d just climbed out of a swimming pool.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: I learned that Harry had fallen during the match and that the team feared he was dead — they thought the fall was fatal until we found out otherwise.
metadata.source_text: We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: Seeing Harry alive but battered changed how terrified I feel — I genuinely thought we’d lost him and now I’m shaken to realize how close we came to losing a friend.
metadata.source_text: How’re you feeling?" said Fred. "We thought you’d died," said Alicia, who was shaking.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: Watching everyone crowd around Harry and hearing them talk about him made me feel how important he is to us; my worry for him just deepened my loyalty.
metadata.source_text: The Gryffindor Quidditch team, spattered with mud from head to foot, was gathered around his bed.
metadata.scene_title: Explaining the Aftermath: Match Result and Dumbledore's Intervention

metadata.description: I lost a Quidditch match for the first time ever; I've never failed to catch the Snitch before and this is the first time I've come off second-best.
metadata.source_text: They had lost . . . for the first time ever, he had lost a Quidditch match.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I'm shaken — the dementors did something to me that left me haunted; I can't just shrug this off like a bad fall, their presence really terrifies me now.
metadata.source_text: He was thinking about what the dementors had done to him . . . about the screaming voice.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I know people care about me — Fred and George tried to cheer me up and said I'm still the best Seeker, and Madam Pomfrey told everyone to leave me in peace, so I feel supported even when I'm at my lowest.
metadata.source_text:
“Don’t beat yourself up, Harry, you’re still the best Seeker we’ve ever had.”
Madam Pomfrey came over to tell the team to leave him in peace.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I've seen what Dumbledore did on the field: he slowed Harry's fall with his wand, shot silver at the dementors to drive them away, and then had Harry carried on a levitating stretcher.
metadata.source_text: “He ran onto the field as you fell, waved his wand, and you sort of slowed down before you hit the ground. Then he whirled his wand at the dementors. Shot silver stuff at them. They left the stadium right away. . . . He was furious they’d come onto the grounds. We heard him —”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I'm shaken by how angry Dumbledore was — I've never seen him like that before, and his fury at the dementors made me realise this was far worse than a normal interruption.
metadata.source_text: “Dumbledore was really angry,” Hermione said in a quaking voice. “I’ve never seen him like that before."
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I feel protective and anxious for Harry — seeing him hurt and watching Dumbledore's reaction made me more worried about his safety than I was before.
metadata.source_text: “Dumbledore was really angry,” Hermione said in a quaking voice. “I’ve never seen him like that before. He ran onto the field as you fell..."
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the showers and I wasn't part of the conversations that happened elsewhere; I don't have direct knowledge of those moments.
metadata.source_text: Absent from scene
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Finishes the Story: The Whomping Willow and Flitwick's Help

metadata.description: I've just learned that a bit of ragged parchment called the Marauder's Map can show every corridor and hidden passage of Hogwarts and the real-time positions of people as moving ink dots.
metadata.source_text: It was a map showing every detail of the Hogwarts castle and grounds. But the truly remarkable thing were the tiny ink dots moving around it, each labeled with a name in minuscule writing.

metadata.description: I saw that the map can be made to reveal itself by tapping it with a wand and saying, 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good,' and that it can be cleared by tapping it and saying, 'Mischief managed!'
metadata.source_text: He took out his wand, touched the parchment lightly, and said, 'I solemnly swear that I am up to no good.' ... 'Don't forget to wipe it after you've used it —' '— or anyone can read it,' Fred said warningly. 'Just tap it again and say, 'Mischief managed!' And it'll go blank.'

metadata.description: I've found out that there are several secret passages from the castle to Hogsmeade, including one that opens under the hump of the one-eyed witch statue right outside the classroom and another that leads into Honeydukes' cellar.
metadata.source_text: This map showed a set of passages he had never entered. ... 'Right into Hogsmeade,' said Fred, tracing one of them with his finger. 'There are seven in all.' ... 'But this one here, this one leads right into the cellar of Honeydukes. We've used it loads of times. And as you might've noticed, the entrance is right outside this room, through that one-eyed old crone's hump.'

metadata.description: I'm amazed and a bit stunned; I used to think Hogwarts was mostly mapped out, but now I believe there are secret routes and a magical map that knows where everyone is, which changes how I see moving round the school.
metadata.source_text: It was a map showing every detail of the Hogwarts castle and grounds. But the truly remarkable thing were the tiny ink dots moving around it, each labeled with a name in minuscule writing.

metadata.description: I feel grateful to Fred and George for trusting me with something so dangerous and clever; they treated me like someone who needs this more than they do and gave it to me as an early present.
metadata.source_text: 'Early Christmas present for you, Harry,' he said. Fred pulled something from inside his cloak with a flourish and laid it on one of the desks. 'It's a wrench, giving it to you,' said Fred, 'but we decided last night, your need's greater than ours.'

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the third-floor corridor and classroom, so I don't know the details of what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the third floor where Fred and George showed Harry the Marauder's Map, so I can't report what happened firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I found that tapping the statue while the map shows the word 'Dissendium' opens a hidden entrance through the statue's hump.
metadata.source_text: The tiniest speech bubble had appeared next to his figure. The word inside said, “Dissendium.”

metadata.description: I discovered that saying 'Dissendium' and tapping the statue makes the hump open just enough for a fairly thin person to get through.
metadata.source_text: “Dissendium!” Harry whispered, tapping the stone witch again. At once, the statue’s hump opened wide enough to admit a fairly thin person.

metadata.description: I learned the passage beyond the statue is a long, narrow, earthy tunnel, almost like a giant rabbit's burrow, which eventually slopes up to a hidden cellar.
metadata.source_text: He slid a considerable way down what felt like a stone slide, then landed on cold, damp earth... He was in a very narrow, low, earthy passageway... The passage twisted and turned, more like the burrow of a giant rabbit than anything else.

metadata.description: I found that the Marauder's Map can show words in a speech bubble next to my figure and that the word 'Dissendium' indicated the secret entrance.
metadata.source_text: The tiniest speech bubble had appeared next to his figure. The word inside said, “Dissendium.”

metadata.description: I wasn't sure the statue would actually open, but seeing the hump give way when I whispered 'Dissendium' changed my mind — I trusted the map's clue.
metadata.source_text: “Dissendium!” Harry whispered, tapping the stone witch again. At once, the statue’s hump opened wide enough to admit a fairly thin person.

metadata.description: I'm more reliant on the map now; it doesn't just show people, it gives clues and feels like a guide I can trust in tight spots.
metadata.source_text: He raised the map, tapped it with the tip of his wand, and muttered, “Mischief managed!” The map went blank at once.

metadata.description: I was not present during these events, so I did not witness Harry using the map or entering the secret passage.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not present during these events, so I did not see Harry find or use the Dissendium entrance or explore the cellar.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I've learned that the map shows seven secret tunnels, and that one is caved in, one is blocked by the Whomping Willow and another is hard to see in the cellar — the one I used.
metadata.source_text: There are seven secret tunnels on the map, right? Fred and George reckon Filch already knows about four of them. And of the other three — one of them’s caved in, so no one can get through it. One of them’s got the Whomping Willow planted over the entrance, so you can’t get out of it. And the one I just came through — well — it’s really hard to see the entrance to it down in the cellar, so unless he knew it was there . . .

metadata.description: I'm not about to hand the map in — no way I'd give something that good to the teachers, I'd have to say where I got it and Filch would twig Fred and George nicked it.
metadata.source_text: But Harry isn’t going to keep it!" said Hermione... "No, I’m not!" said Harry. "Are you mad?" said Ron... "If I hand it in, I’ll have to say where I got it! Filch would know Fred and George had nicked it!"

metadata.description: I feel annoyed that Fred and George never gave me the Map earlier — I'm properly outraged because I'm their brother and missed out on something brilliant.
metadata.source_text: "How come Fred and George never gave it to me!" said Ron, outraged. "I’m their brother!"

metadata.description: I've learned from the notice that Dementors will be patrolling Hogsmeade every night after sundown until Sirius Black is recaptured, so shops warn customers to finish shopping well before nightfall.
metadata.source_text: ——— BY ORDER OF ——— THE MINISTRY OF MAGIC Customers are reminded that until further notice, dementors will be patrolling the streets of Hogsmeade every night after sundown. This measure has been put in place for the safety of Hogsmeade residents and will be lifted upon the recapture of Sirius Black. It is therefore advisable that you complete your shopping well before nightfall. Merry Christmas!

metadata.description: I'm more convinced that Harry shouldn't be in Hogsmeade without a signed form; if anyone finds out he'll be in so much trouble and the risk of Black turning up right now worries me.
metadata.source_text: Look, Harry still shouldn’t be coming into Hogsmeade. He hasn’t got a signed form! If anyone finds out, he’ll be in so much trouble! And it’s not nightfall yet — what if Sirius Black turns up today? Now?

metadata.description: I'm shocked and relieved when Harry appears; I clearly care about his safety and I'm upset that he would put himself at risk by sneaking into Hogsmeade.
metadata.source_text: "Harry!" squealed Hermione. "What are you doing here? How — how did you — ?"

metadata.description: I've noticed the Ministry warning about Dementors patrolling Hogsmeade at night and I reckon that would make it hard for Sirius Black to break into Honeydukes while Dementors swarm the village.
metadata.source_text: See?" said Ron quietly. "I’d like to see Black try and break into Honeydukes with dementors swarming all over the village.

metadata.description: I think Harry deserves a break — it's Christmas, and with the snow and the crowds Black wouldn't spot Harry easily, so I'm willing to take the risk of him being here.
metadata.source_text: Come on, Hermione, it’s Christmas. Harry deserves a break." "He’d have a job spotting Harry in this," said Ron, nodding through the mullioned windows at the thick, swirling snow.

metadata.description: I'm impressed and jealous when Harry appears because at first I think he's Apparated; I keep seeing Harry as one of us who should be included in Fred and George's jokes and pranks.
metadata.source_text: "Wow!" said Ron, looking very impressed, "you’ve learned to Apparate!" and later "Reckon Fred’d take a bit of Cockroach Cluster if I told him they were peanuts?"

metadata.description: I found an old leather-bound photo album Hagrid gave me with wizard pictures of Mum and Dad, and I stopped on a wedding photo that showed Sirius Black smiling and laughing with them.
metadata.source_text: He pushed his books aside and quickly found what he was looking for — the leather-bound photo album Hagrid had given him two years ago, which was full of wizard pictures of his mother and father.

metadata.description: I can't think of Sirius Black as the same man from that photograph; seeing him laughing in the picture makes me wonder if he was already working for Voldemort and if he could be capable of betraying my parents.
metadata.source_text: If he hadn’t known it was the same person, he would never have guessed it was Black in this old photograph. His face wasn’t sunken and waxy, but handsome, full of laughter. Had he already been working for Voldemort when this picture had been taken?

metadata.description: I feel a new, poisonous hatred for Black; I see him as the one who betrayed my parents and caused me never to have spoken to them, and that changes how I think of him completely.
metadata.source_text: A hatred such as he had never known before was coursing through Harry like poison.

metadata.description: I know Harry heard something upsetting about Black and I realise he’s deeply distressed; I read his face and homework spread shows I'm worried and trying to be sensible about danger.
metadata.source_text: “You really don’t look well, you know,” Hermione said, peering anxiously into his face.

metadata.description: I'm convinced that Harry must not go doing anything stupid after what we heard; I'm more adamant than before that he should stay safe because Black wants him to act rashly.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, listen,” said Hermione, exchanging a look with Ron, “you must be really upset about what we heard yesterday. But the thing is, you mustn’t go doing anything stupid.”

metadata.description: I feel protective toward Harry and more emotional about his safety than before; I truly believe his parents wouldn't want him risking himself to hunt down Black.
metadata.source_text: “Oh, Harry, you’d be playing right into Black’s hands if you went looking for him. Your mum and dad wouldn’t want you to get hurt, would they? They’d never want you to go looking for Black!”

metadata.description: I heard from Dad about Pettigrew’s fate — the Order of Merlin, First Class, and Pettigrew’s finger in a box — and I remember how horrific that was when Harry mentions it.
metadata.source_text: “Dad told me — the Order of Merlin, First Class, and Pettigrew’s finger in a box. That was the biggest bit of him they could find.”

metadata.description: I'm more worried than pleased about Harry wanting revenge; I believe Black is mad and dangerous and that Harry going after him would be daft and could get him killed.
metadata.source_text: “Black’s a madman, Harry, and he’s dangerous —”

metadata.description: I suspect Malfoy gloats about hoping Harry will get himself killed; I don't trust Malfoy’s sympathy and think his comments are intended to stir trouble for Harry.
metadata.source_text: “Get a grip. Malfoy’s just hoping you’ll get yourself killed before he has to play you at Quidditch.”

metadata.description: I learned that the school governors accepted Dumbledore's assurance that Hagrid bore no responsibility for the hippogriff's attack, but the case will still be sent to the Committee for the Disposal of Dangerous Creatures.
metadata.source_text: Further to our inquiry into the attack by a hippogriff on a student in your class, we have accepted the assurances of Professor Dumbledore that you bear no responsibility for the regrettable incident.

metadata.description: Seeing Hagrid so terrified and upset makes me feel I can't blame him for not telling me everything about Sirius Black right now; I won't berate him while he's like that.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione looked quickly at Harry, as though expecting him to start berating Hagrid for not telling him the truth about Black. But Harry couldn't bring himself to do it, not now that he saw Hagrid so miserable and scared.

metadata.description: I'm ready to stand up for Hagrid — I offered to be a witness and promised to help, showing I trust and support him when he's in trouble.
metadata.source_text: Listen, Hagrid, you can't give up. Hermione's right, you just need a good defense. You can call us as witnesses —

metadata.description: I've found in records that there was at least one historical case of a hippogriff being tried (1722) though in that case the hippogriff was convicted; I promised to look up cases to help Hagrid's defense.
metadata.source_text: Here’s something . . . there was a case in 1722 . . . but the hippogriff was convicted — ugh, look what they did to it, that’s disgusting —

metadata.description: I believe that careful research and precedent might help Hagrid — I'm sure we can prove Buckbeak is safe if we find the right case history and argue it properly.
metadata.source_text: You’ll have to put up a good strong defense, Hagrid," said Hermione, sitting down and laying a hand on Hagrid’s massive forearm. "I’m sure you can prove Buckbeak is safe.

metadata.description: I don't like how the Committee and people like Malfoy treat Hagrid and his creatures; I'm prepared to help him because I care about fairness and Hagrid's classes.
metadata.source_text: "Yeh don' know them gargoyles at the Committee fer the Disposal o’ Dangerous Creatures!" choked Hagrid, wiping his eyes on his sleeve. "They've got it in fer interestin' creatures!"

metadata.description: I learned from the letter that Hagrid must present himself and the hippogriff to the Committee in London on April twentieth and that Buckbeak must be kept tethered in the meantime.
