metadata.source_text: The hearing will take place on April 20th, and we ask you to present yourself and your hippogriff at the Committee’s offices in London on that date. In the meantime, the hippogriff should be kept tethered and isolated.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced Hagrid's creatures are good — I told him Buckbeak isn't a bad hippogriff and tried to cheer him up, even though I know the Committee might be nasty.
metadata.source_text: "Oh," said Ron. "But you said Buckbeak isn’t a bad hippogriff, Hagrid. I bet he’ll get off —"

metadata.description: I want to help Hagrid, even if I sound daft — I made tea and lied that we all liked his lessons to comfort him; I care about him enough to try and lift his spirits.
metadata.source_text: Er — shall I make a cup of tea?" said Ron. "It’s what my mum does whenever someone’s upset," Ron muttered, shrugging. "We do like them!" lied Hermione at once. "Yeah, they’re great!" said Ron, crossing his fingers under the table.

metadata.description: I've found an anonymous Firebolt broom waiting for me and there was no card or message with it — I really don't know who sent it.
metadata.source_text: No idea," said Harry. "There wasn't a card or anything with it."

metadata.description: I was excited about the broom, but when McGonagall took it away to check for jinxes I felt unsettled; I thought it was fine, but I can't argue with having it checked.
metadata.source_text: "There's nothing wrong with it!" said Harry, his voice shaking slightly. "Honestly, Professor —"

metadata.description: Hermione's behaviour surprised me — she wasn't thrilled about the broom and then told McGonagall she thought Sirius Black sent it; I'm starting to see her as someone who acts on strong, cautious instincts.
metadata.source_text: "Because I thought — and Professor McGonagall agrees with me — that that broom was probably sent to Harry by Sirius Black!"

metadata.description: I've noticed the Firebolt is an exceptionally good broom and likely very expensive, and I don't like that someone sent Harry such an expensive present without identifying themselves.
metadata.source_text: "Well . . . who'd send Harry something as expensive as that, and not even tell him they'd sent it?" said Hermione.

metadata.description: I felt less excited than the others when I first saw the broom; my worries about its origin grew and I decided to speak to Professor McGonagall about it.
metadata.source_text: To his great surprise, Hermione did not appear either excited or intrigued by the news. On the contrary, her face fell, and she bit her lip.

metadata.description: I now believe Sirius Black might be involved; I went to McGonagall because I thought the broom was probably sent by Sirius Black and I told Harry and Ron so directly.
metadata.source_text: "Because I thought — and Professor McGonagall agrees with me — that that broom was probably sent to Harry by Sirius Black!"

metadata.description: I've seen the Firebolt and I know it's the best broom there is — I reckoned it must have cost more than all the Slytherins' brooms put together.
metadata.source_text: "It's the best broom there is, Hermione," he said. "So it must've been really expensive. . . ." "Probably cost more than all the Slytherins' brooms put together," said Ron happily.

metadata.description: At first I suspected Lupin could have sent it because he likes Harry, but when Harry said Lupin was ill I thought Lupin couldn't afford something like that — my mind swung from hopeful to doubtful.
metadata.source_text: "I know who it could've been — Lupin!" "Lupin? Listen, if he had this much gold, he'd be able to buy himself some new robes."

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione run to McGonagall and accuse Sirius Black made me annoyed with her at first, but it also made me realise she can act very decisively when she thinks someone's at risk.
metadata.source_text: "What did you go running to McGonagall for?" Hermione threw her book aside... "Because I thought ... that broom was probably sent to Harry by Sirius Black!"

metadata.description: I've just learned that my Firebolt broomstick was confiscated so Professor McGonagall can check it for jinxes.
metadata.source_text: I haven’t got it anymore. It was confiscated.

metadata.description: I’m convinced now that McGonagall thinks Sirius Black could have sent the Firebolt, so she wants it stripped down to check for jinxes.
metadata.source_text: Sirius Black," Harry said wearily. "He’s supposed to be after me. So McGonagall reckons he might have sent it.

metadata.description: I feel a bit resigned and unsupported when Wood gushes about having a Firebolt on the team while I’m stuck worrying about it being taken away because of Black—it’s like my problems are background noise to Quidditch talk.
metadata.source_text: "But Black couldn’t have bought a Firebolt! He’s on the run! The whole country’s on the lookout for him! How could he just walk into Quality Quidditch Supplies and buy a broomstick?"

metadata.description: I heard that Harry got a Firebolt for Christmas—a real Firebolt—and I’m dead impressed by that news.
metadata.source_text: "He got a Firebolt for Christmas," said Ron.

metadata.description: I’m annoyed and defensive when Hermione ‘tuts’ at us; I reckon she’s just trying to get attention because she wants us to talk to her again.
metadata.source_text: "She doesn’t know," said Ron, staring resentfully after Hermione. "She’s just trying to get us to talk to her again."

metadata.description: I’m sceptical about Professor Lupin’s health; seeing him look ill makes me wonder aloud what’s wrong with him and worry about him being fit enough for class.
metadata.source_text: "Still looks ill, doesn’t he?" said Ron as they walked down the corridor, heading to dinner. "What d’you reckon’s the matter with him?"

metadata.description: I was not present for the Quidditch and Firebolt conversation between Harry, Ron, and Wood, so I don’t have direct knowledge of those exchanges.
I've learned that Professor Lupin plans to teach us an anti-dementor method called the Patronus Charm and that it needs me to concentrate on a single, very happy memory while saying an incantation.
metadata.source_text: The spell I am going to try and teach you is highly advanced magic, Harry — well beyond Ordinary Wizarding Level. It is called the Patronus Charm.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I feel a bit more hopeful now because I actually made something happen with the charm — a silvery wisp came out of my wand when I concentrated on flying and said 'Expecto Patronum.'
metadata.source_text: Something whooshed suddenly out of the end of his wand; it looked like a wisp of silvery gas.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I trust Professor Lupin to help me prepare against dementors; he found a boggart to act as a dementor substitute and talked me through the Patronus calmly and sensibly.
metadata.source_text: The boggart will turn into a dementor when he sees you, so we’ll be able to practice on him.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I've noticed that Professor Trelawney has started teaching palmistry and that she told Harry he has the shortest life line she has ever seen.
metadata.source_text: Professor Trelawney was now teaching them palmistry, and she lost no time in informing Harry that he had the shortest life line she had ever seen.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I think Lupin is looking ill and that it's obvious something is wrong with him, even if others don't want to talk about it.
metadata.source_text: Well, isn’t it obvious?
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I want Ron and Harry to include me when they talk about school matters; I get annoyed and tut when they exclude me and try to make them carry on the conversation.
metadata.source_text: There was a loud and impatient “tuh” from behind them.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I've learned from Wood and Harry that a Firebolt might be jinxed and that people think Sirius Black could be linked to strange happenings around Harry.
metadata.source_text: But Black couldn’t have bought a Firebolt! He’s on the run! The whole country’s on the lookout for him!
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I feel suspicious and annoyed about Hermione's sudden interest; I reckon she's only trying to get our attention again, not because she really knows what's wrong with Lupin.
metadata.source_text: She’s just trying to get us to talk to her again.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I'm resentful that Hermione tries to involve herself in our conversations; I stare after her and feel irritated when she acts superior and marches off.
metadata.source_text: She marched off.
metadata.scene_title: First Days Back: Lessons and Preparations

metadata.description: I learned that when a dementor gets close I feel a wave of piercing cold and horrible memories — it makes me fall through thick white fog and hear voices from my past.
metadata.source_text: A wave of piercing cold broke over him — “Expecto Patronum!” Harry yelled. ... Harry was falling again through thick white fog, and his mother’s voice was louder than ever, echoing inside his head — “Not Harry! Not Harry! Please — I’ll do anything —”
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I used to think I might manage a Patronus quickly, but I'm starting to believe it's harder than I expected — that the memories the dementor brings up can stop me from doing it properly.
metadata.source_text: I didn’t expect you to do it your first time; in fact, I would have been astounded if you had.” “It’s getting worse,” Harry muttered, biting off the Frog’s head. “I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —”
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: Hearing my father's voice made me feel closer to him; for the first time I realized he tried to fight Voldemort to give Mum and me time to run, and that changed how I think about him.
metadata.source_text: “I heard my dad,” Harry mumbled. “That’s the first time I’ve ever heard him — he tried to take on Voldemort himself, to give my mum time to run for it. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I noticed that dementors can force someone to relive powerful, private memories and that a Patronus is needed to repel them — the presence of a dementor brings icy darkness and memory-fog.
metadata.source_text: The lamps around the classroom flickered and went out. The dementor stepped from the box and started to sweep silently toward Harry, drawing a deep, rattling breath. A wave of piercing cold broke over him
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I believe now that attempting a Patronus can be much more traumatic than I thought and that concentrating on a genuinely happy memory is crucial for success.
metadata.source_text: “You might want to select another memory, a happy memory, I mean, to concentrate on. . . . That one doesn’t seem to have been strong enough. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: Watching Harry struggle made me feel more concerned for him; I think of him as braver but also more vulnerable than I had fully realised before.
metadata.source_text: “Are you all right?” said Lupin. “Yes . . .” Harry pulled himself up on one of the desks and leaned against it. “Here —” Lupin handed him a Chocolate Frog.
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I see that facing dementors is terrifying and that even trying a Patronus can leave someone exhausted and crying — it's not just a simple classroom spell.
metadata.source_text: Harry jerked back to life. He was lying flat on his back on the floor. The classroom lamps were alight again. He didn’t have to ask what had happened. “Sorry,” he muttered, sitting up and feeling cold sweat trickling down behind his glasses.
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I'm starting to believe that Harry's connection to his past and to Voldemort is deeper and more painful than I realised; hearing his parents in his head clearly affects him badly.
metadata.source_text: “I could hear her louder that time — and him — Voldemort —”
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: Seeing Harry's tears makes me feel more protective of him; I think of him less as 'just Harry' and more like someone who needs our support because of what he's been through.
metadata.source_text: Harry suddenly realized that there were tears on his face mingling with the sweat.
metadata.scene_title: Gathering for Dementor Practice and the Boggart

metadata.description: I learned that thinking about the happiest moment I can remember helps me produce a Patronus — for me, the moment I found out I was a wizard and leaving Privet Drive was the memory I used.
metadata.source_text: Concentrating very hard on how he had felt when he’d realized he’d be leaving Privet Drive, Harry got to his feet and faced the packing case once more.
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Patronus: First Trials and Failures

metadata.description: I believed I could do better with the Patronus; after that attempt I feel encouraged because a huge silver shadow came bursting out of my wand, so I think I'm on the right track even if I can't hold it yet.
metadata.source_text: and then a huge, silver shadow came bursting out of the end of Harry’s wand, to hover between him and the dementor, and though Harry’s legs felt like water, he was still on his feet
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Patronus: First Trials and Failures

metadata.description: I realised Professor Lupin actually knew my father and knew Sirius Black too, which makes Lupin feel more connected to my past and not just some teacher I see in class.
metadata.source_text: If you knew my dad, you must’ve known Sirius Black as well." Lupin turned very quickly. "What gives you that idea?" he said sharply. "Nothing— I mean, I just knew they were friends at Hogwarts too. . . ." Lupin’s face relaxed. "Yes, I knew him," he said shortly. "Or I thought I did.
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Patronus: First Trials and Failures

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the Patronus practice scene with Harry and Professor Lupin, so I don't know exactly how Harry's Patronus attempt went that night.
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Patronus: First Trials and Failures

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room during Harry's Patronus lesson with Professor Lupin, so I didn't witness the dementor or Harry's Patronus being produced.
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Patronus: First Trials and Failures

metadata.description: I've learned from McGonagall and the professors that my broom is being inspected for curses and might be carrying a Hurling Hex, so I can't have it back yet.
metadata.source_text: No, Potter, you can’t have it back yet," Professor McGonagall told him the twelfth time this happened, before he’d even opened his mouth. "We’ve checked for most of the usual curses, but Professor Flitwick believes the broom might be carrying a Hurling Hex.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I've learned that my Patronus practice only makes an indistinct, silvery shadow so far and that it drains me when I force it to hold against a boggart-dementor.
metadata.source_text: Several sessions on, he was able to produce an indistinct, silvery shadow every time the boggart-dementor approached him, but his Patronus was too feeble to drive the dementor away. All it did was hover, like a semi-transparent cloud, draining Harry of energy as he fought to keep it there.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I thought a Patronus would charge the dementors down and make them disappear, but Lupin explained that the true Patronus does that and mine isn't there yet, so I have to lower my expectations.
metadata.source_text: I thought a Patronus would — charge the dementors down or something," said Harry dispiritedly. "Make them disappear —" "The true Patronus does do that," said Lupin.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I feel reassured by Lupin; he treats me kindly, believes I'm making fast progress, and even gives me butterbeer — I trust his judgement more now about my magical progress.
metadata.source_text: "You have complete confidence in you," said Lupin, smiling. "Here — you’ve earned a drink — something from the Three Broomsticks. You won’t have tried it before —" He pulled two bottles out of his briefcase.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: When I heard the Ministry will let dementors give Sirius the Dementor's Kiss, I felt shock and then thought Sirius deserves it; Lupin questioned that, making me realise my feelings about justice might be more complicated.
metadata.source_text: "It’s the fate that awaits Sirius Black. It was in the Daily Prophet this morning. The Ministry have given the dementors permission to perform it if they find him." ... "He deserves it," he said suddenly. "You think so?" said Lupin lightly.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the scene, so I don't know what Hermione said or did here.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the scene, so I don't know what Ron said or did here.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Attempts: Visions, Patronus, and Exhaustion

metadata.description: I can tell the Firebolt is faster and more precise than other brooms — it climbs and turns like nothing I've flown before.
metadata.source_text: the Firebolt zoomed higher and faster than any other broom; he soared around the stadium and began squinting around for the Snitch

metadata.description: Diving and sudden changes of pace are my speciality when I'm trying to catch the Snitch; I rely on quick, low dives and explosive climbs.
metadata.source_text: dives were his speciality, he was ten feet away

metadata.description: I realise that being chased by a good opponent like Cho can ruin my chances — if someone marks me closely, I can't just rely on raw speed.
metadata.source_text: She was undoubtedly a very good flier — she kept cutting across him, forcing him to change direction.

metadata.description: Cho Chang is clearly a skilled and determined rival in the air; she's prepared to tail me and grin while doing it.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught sight of Cho; she was grinning. She’d decided to mark him rather than search for the Snitch herself.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the Quidditch match, so I cannot say what I saw during the aerial plays or the Dementor appearance.
I wasn't present at the match itself, so I didn't witness the Firebolt flying or Cho's tailing of Harry or the dementors arriving.
I grabbed the Snitch just in time while still on my broom; I actually closed my fingers around the small, struggling Snitch as Madam Hooch blew her whistle.
metadata.source_text: he looked ahead — he was nearly there. He stretched out the hand still grasping his wand and just managed to close his fingers over the small, struggling Snitch. Madam Hooch’s whistle sounded.

metadata.description: I thought dementors were attacking, but Lupin told me they weren't dementors, so I realise the danger wasn’t what I believed at first.
metadata.source_text: The dementors didn’t affect me at all!” Harry said excitedly. “I didn’t feel a thing!” “That would be because they — er — weren’t dementors,” said Professor Lupin.

metadata.description: I felt an enormous surge of friendship and admiration from my teammates and the Gryffindor crowd — everyone was hugging me, kissing me, and shouting; I know they care a great deal.
metadata.source_text: Harry turned around in midair and saw six scarlet blurs bearing down on him; next moment, the whole team was hugging him so hard he was nearly pulled off his broom. Down below he could hear the roars of the Gryffindors in the crowd. “That’s my boy!” Wood kept yelling. Alicia, Angelina, and Katie had all kissed Harry;

metadata.description: I was not present for the events on the Quidditch pitch during this match, so I did not witness what happened there.
metadata.source_text: I was not present for the events on the Quidditch pitch during this match, so I did not witness what happened there.

metadata.description: I was not present for the events on the Quidditch pitch during this match, so I did not witness what happened there.
metadata.source_text: I was not present for the events on the Quidditch pitch during this match, so I did not witness what happened there.

metadata.description: I know Fred and George came back with loads of sweets and drinks — they disappeared for a couple of hours and returned with bottles of butterbeer, pumpkin fizz, and bags of Honeydukes sweets.
metadata.source_text: Fred and George Weasley disappeared for a couple of hours and returned with armfuls of bottles of butterbeer, pumpkin fizz, and several bags full of Honeydukes sweets.

metadata.description: I heard Fred say they got help from Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs — so someone used those nicknames to explain how they managed to get the provisions.
metadata.source_text: “With a little help from Moony, Wormtail, Padfoot, and Prongs,” Fred muttered in Harry’s ear.

metadata.description: I felt a pull to try and bury the hatchet with Ron after the match; I wondered if I was in a good enough mood to sort things out between us.
metadata.source_text: “I can’t, Harry. I’ve still got four hundred and twenty-two pages to read!” said Hermione... “Come on, Hermione, come and have some food,” Harry said, looking over at Ron and wondering whether he was in a good enough mood to bury the hatchet.

metadata.description: I've learned I still have exactly four hundred and twenty-two pages to read and that I must finish them by Monday — I can't be distracted even after the match.
metadata.source_text: “I can’t, Harry. I’ve still got four hundred and twenty-two pages to read!” said Hermione, now sounding slightly hysterical.

metadata.description: I feel furious and hurt enough about Scabbers that I burst into tears; I'm convinced Ron is dismissive of the loss and won't admit any fault or show proper sympathy.
metadata.source_text: “He doesn’t want me to join in.” ... “If Scabbers hadn’t just been eaten, he could have had some of those Fudge Flies. He used to really like them —” Hermione burst into tears.

metadata.description: I now see Ron as unsympathetic and stubborn; his flippant comment about Scabbers being 'on vacation' convinced me he isn't taking things seriously, so I ran off upset.
metadata.source_text: “He’s still acting like Scabbers has gone on vacation or something.”

metadata.description: I know I woke up convinced that Sirius Black was in our dormitory holding a knife and that the curtains had been slashed — I remember shouting that Black had been standing over me.
metadata.source_text: “Black! Sirius Black! With a knife!” “Here! Just now! Slashed the curtains! Woke me up!”

metadata.description: I'm certain it wasn't a nightmare — I genuinely believe Sirius Black entered Gryffindor Tower and stood over my bed with a knife, and I'm upset to be dismissed.
metadata.source_text: “IT WASN’T A NIGHTMARE!” Ron yelled. “PROFESSOR, I WOKE UP, AND SIRIUS BLACK WAS STANDING OVER ME, HOLDING A KNIFE!”

metadata.description: I feel betrayed by people brushing off my experience as a mere nightmare, and I point at Sir Cadogan because I think he should be asked whether someone entered through the portrait hole.
metadata.source_text: “Ask him!” said Ron, pointing a shaking finger at the back of Sir Cadogan’s picture.

metadata.description: I was not present when Aftermath in the Great Hall and Neville's Howler occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Great Hall and Neville's Howler

metadata.description: I learned Hagrid invited Ron and me to tea this afternoon and told us to wait in the entrance hall; Hedwig made sure I noticed my letter.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry and Ron, How about having tea with me this afternoon ’round six? I’ll come and collect you from the castle. WAIT FOR ME IN THE ENTRANCE HALL; YOU’RE NOT ALLOWED OUT ON YOUR OWN. Cheers, Hagrid
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I found out Buckbeak has a hearing this Friday — it’s Buckbeak’s case against the Committee for the Disposal o’ Dangerous Creatures, and Hagrid’s going down to London with him.
metadata.source_text: Buckbeak’s case against the Committee fer the Disposal o’ Dangerous Creatures,” said Hagrid. “This Friday. Him an’ me’ll be goin’ down ter London together.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I feel guilty because I’d completely forgotten Buckbeak’s trial and that Hagrid wanted our help; I realize the Firebolt distracted us and we let Hagrid down a bit.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt a nasty pang of guilt. He had completely forgotten that Buckbeak’s trial was so near, and judging by the uneasy look on Ron’s face, he had too.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I see Hermione as someone who’s been having a rough time — she’s been crying and visiting Hagrid a lot; I understand she’s been trying too hard and still helped with Buckbeak’s case.
metadata.source_text: She’s bin comin’ down ter visit me a lot since Chris’mas. Bin feelin’ lonely. ... She’s cried a fair few times, yeh know. Goin’ through a rough time at the moment.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I’ve been helping Hagrid with Buckbeak’s case and have found useful research that makes me think Buckbeak will stand a good chance at the hearing.
metadata.source_text: Still found time ter help me with Buckbeak’s case, mind. . . . She’s found some really good stuff fer me . . . reckon he’ll stand a good chance now. . . .
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I feel worn out and upset because I’ve been trying to do too much schoolwork and other things; I’ve cried and felt lonely but kept helping Hagrid anyway.
metadata.source_text: She’s cried a fair few times, yeh know. Goin’ through a rough time at the moment. Bitten off more’n she can chew, if yeh ask me, all the work she’s tryin’ ter do.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I know Hagrid thinks I’m a good friend for helping him, and he’s noticed I’ve been visiting and feeling lonely; this makes me aware that others see my efforts and struggles.
metadata.source_text: She’s bin comin’ down ter visit me a lot since Chris’mas. Bin feelin’ lonely. ... Still found time ter help me with Buckbeak’s case, mind.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I learned Hagrid’s invited me and Harry for tea at six and that he’s booked two beds on the Knight Bus because he and Buckbeak have to go to London for the hearing.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry and Ron, How about having tea with me this afternoon ’round six? ... Buckbeak’s case against the Committee fer the Disposal o’ Dangerous Creatures,” said Hagrid. “This Friday. Him an’ me’ll be goin’ down ter London together. I’ve booked two beds on the Knight Bus. . . .
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I feel bad because I forgot Buckbeak’s hearing too and we’d promised Hagrid help preparing the defense; I hadn’t realized how close the trial was.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt a nasty pang of guilt. He had completely forgotten that Buckbeak’s trial was so near, and judging by the uneasy look on Ron’s face, he had too.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I’m annoyed with Hermione about her cat and Scabbers, but Hagrid’s defending her, saying cats are just cats; I’m reminded to consider other explanations before blaming her.
metadata.source_text: “— ate Scabbers!” Ron interjected angrily. “Because her cat acted like all cats do,” Hagrid continued doggedly.
metadata.scene_title: The Invitation from Hagrid and the Bit About Buckbeak

metadata.description: I learned Hermione was very upset when Black nearly stabbed Ron; she cared enough to be genuinely worried about what happened.
metadata.source_text: Really upset, she was, when Black nearly stabbed yeh, Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I feel a bit guilty about not talking to Hermione; Hagrid made me see she has her heart in the right place and deserves better from us.
metadata.source_text: She’s got her heart in the right place, Hermione has, an’ you two not talkin’ to her —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I now see Hermione as someone who cares deeply for us; Hagrid’s words remind me she’s a good friend even if we’re annoyed at her pet choices.
metadata.source_text: She’s got her heart in the right place, Hermione has, an’ you two not talkin’ to her —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I know I was very upset when Sirius Black nearly stabbed Ron; my feelings were obvious to Hagrid and mattered to the others.
metadata.source_text: Really upset, she was, when Black nearly stabbed yeh, Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I’m aware Hagrid thinks my heart is in the right place; hearing that makes me feel my concern for my friends is recognized even if they’re sulking.
metadata.source_text: She’s got her heart in the right place, Hermione has, an’ you two not talkin’ to her —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I understand Harry and Ron are currently not talking to me because of my cat, and that has strained our friendship — I can feel the distance between us.
metadata.source_text: you two not talkin’ to her —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I heard Hagrid say Hermione was really upset when Black nearly stabbed me; I know she was worried about what happened to me.
metadata.source_text: Really upset, she was, when Black nearly stabbed yeh, Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I’ve become more furious about Hermione sticking up for that cat; I don’t care what Hagrid says about her heart, I still think that animal’s dangerous.
metadata.source_text: But she’s still sticking up for it! It’s a maniac, and she won’t hear a word against it!
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I’m not willing to speak to Hermione while she keeps that cat; my opinion of her choices about that pet has soured and put a wedge in our friendship.
metadata.source_text: If she’d just get rid of that cat, I’d speak to her again!
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Rebuke About Hermione and Quidditch Talk

metadata.description: I've learned Filch hasn't done anything about the secret passage into Honeydukes yet, so there may still be a way in from Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Well, Filch hasn’t done anything about the passage into Honeydukes. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I'm willing to risk going into Hogsmeade again as long as I can take the Invisibility Cloak; I'm more careful now but I still want to go and see what's there.
metadata.source_text: Okay," he said. "But I’m taking the Invisibility Cloak this time.
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I think Ron's my mate for sticking up for me and for laughing at Malfoy — I trust him to back me and enjoy our daft adventures together.
metadata.source_text: Harry seized the back of Ron’s robes to stop him from leaping on Malfoy.
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I've learned that Harry might go into Hogsmeade again, and I know about the Map he uses; I can use that knowledge to warn McGonagall if I have to.
metadata.source_text: Harry, if you go into Hogsmeade again . . . I’ll tell Professor McGonagall about that map!
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I'm genuinely more frightened for Harry after what Sirius Black nearly did to him; I'm determined to stop him doing anything reckless because I worry he could be hurt.
metadata.source_text: Ron, how can you let him go with you? After what Sirius Black nearly did to you! I mean it, I’ll tell —
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I feel exasperated with Ron — I think he's been unfair to Harry and has been needlessly harsh; I won't stand by if I think he's being stupid or mean.
metadata.source_text: So now you’re trying to get Harry expelled!" said Ron furiously. "Haven’t you done enough damage this year?
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I've heard Hogsmeade is on next weekend and that Fred and George tried to get into that ruined house but all entrances are sealed, and even the ghosts avoid it.
metadata.source_text: Even the Hogwarts ghosts avoid it," said Ron ... "Fred and George tried, obviously, but all the entrances are sealed shut. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I'm dead set on going to Hogsmeade again; after hearing there are shops like Zonko's and seeing Malfoy, I'm even more determined to go and have a laugh.
metadata.source_text: So how about it?" Ron said to Harry as though there had been no interruption. "Come on, last time we went you didn’t see anything. You haven’t even been inside Zonko’s yet!
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: I still feel fiercely protective of Harry and ready to stand up to people like Malfoy — I laughed when Malfoy got hit and made a joke about the place being haunted.
metadata.source_text: Very haunted up here, isn’t it?" said Ron, with the air of one commenting on the weather.
metadata.scene_title: Return to the Castle: Hogsmeade Rumors and the Invisibility Cloak

metadata.description: My Invisibility Cloak can slip off if someone trips over it, because Crabbe’s foot caught the hem and the Cloak slid off my face for a split second.
metadata.source_text: Crabbe stumbled — and his huge, flat foot caught the hem of Harry’s Cloak. Harry felt a great tug, then the Cloak slid off his face.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I reckon I’m not as safe as everyone says; even a quick glimpse of my head in Hogsmeade could get me in real trouble with teachers and make people think I ignore rules.
metadata.source_text: If your head was in Hogsmeade, so was the rest of you.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I know Ron worries about me and thinks I should run back to the castle fast if Malfoy tells anyone; his panic shows he looks out for my safety even when I don’t want to admit it.
metadata.source_text: Harry! you’d better run for it! If Malfoy tells anyone — you’d better get back to the castle, quick —
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I saw Harry’s Cloak slip and I saw where Harry had gone; I know Malfoy could tell someone he saw Harry in Hogsmeade, which would be trouble.
metadata.source_text: Harry! you’d better run for it! If Malfoy tells anyone — you’d better get back to the castle, quick —
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I’m convinced that Malfoy seeing Harry in Hogsmeade would be serious, so I believe Harry must get away quickly or face consequences from teachers and headmasters.
metadata.source_text: Harry! you’d better run for it! If Malfoy tells anyone — you’d better get back to the castle, quick —
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I care about Harry and react in a flustered, hopeless way when he vanishes; I’m protective and panicked because I don’t want him to get blamed or caught.
metadata.source_text: Harry! you’d better run for it! If Malfoy tells anyone — you’d better get back to the castle, quick —
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I was not present for the events on the hill or the later questioning by Snape, so I do not know firsthand what happened during those moments.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation on the Hill, Cloak Revealed, and Flight to Hogsmeade

metadata.description: I learned that Snape says my father saved his life, because Dumbledore told me that much and Snape reacted bitterly when I mentioned it.
metadata.source_text: I know the truth, all right? He saved your life! Dumbledore told me!
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I'm shaken by what Snape suggested about Dad — I hadn't known the full circumstances and I suddenly don't want to assume Dad's rescue was purely heroic.
metadata.source_text: And did the headmaster tell you the circumstances in which your father saved my life?
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: My opinion of Snape is confirmed as hostile and vindictive; he tries to humiliate me by attacking my father and threatens me when I stand up to him.
metadata.source_text: Turn out your pockets, Potter! ... Turn out your pockets, or we go straight to the headmaster!
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I didn't speak in this scene, so I didn't learn anything aloud here myself.
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I'm not present in the dialogue and therefore don't record any changed beliefs from this exchange.
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I wasn't an active participant in this moment, so I don't have a direct change in how I view Snape or Harry from the lines given.
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know exactly what was said or done in this confrontation between Harry and Snape.
metadata.scene_title: Snape’s Interrogation and the Map Revealed

metadata.description: I found a map that speaks and insults people — it literally wrote that Professor Snape is an ugly git and other rude things; the Marauder's Map can show writing about people.
metadata.source_text: “Mr. Prongs agrees with Mr. Moony, and would like to add that Professor Snape is an ugly git.”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I thought the map might be dangerous at first, but Lupin's calm look and suggestion that it's a Zonko product made me realise it might not be Dark Magic after all, just a joke map.
metadata.source_text: “Full of Dark Magic?” he repeated mildly. “Do you really think so, Severus? It looks to me as though it is merely a piece of parchment that insults anybody who reads it. Childish, but surely not dangerous? I imagine Harry got it from a joke shop —”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I felt anxious and exposed with Snape demanding I empty my pockets, and Lupin's protective warning not to interrupt made me realise Lupin was quietly on my side compared to Snape's fury.
metadata.source_text: “You called, Severus?” said Lupin mildly. “I certainly did,” said Snape, his face contorted with fury as he strode back to his desk. “I have just asked Potter to empty his pockets. He was carrying this.”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I remembered I gave Harry that map ages ago because I bought it in Zonko's — I realised straight away where he got it from when we were accused.
metadata.source_text: “I — gave — Harry — that — stuff,” he choked. “Bought — it . . . in Zonko’s . . . ages — ago . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I felt relieved when Lupin accepted it as a Zonko item; I no longer thought the map would get Harry into deadly trouble once someone sensible called it a joke product.
metadata.source_text: “Well!” said Lupin, clapping his hands together and looking around cheerfully. “That seems to clear that up! Severus, I’ll take this back, shall I?”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I felt like I had to step in and confess for Harry — telling Snape I bought the map for Harry showed I'm willing to protect him and take blame to sort things out.
metadata.source_text: “I — gave — Harry — that — stuff,” he choked. “Bought — it . . . in Zonko’s . . . ages — ago . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in the entrance hall with Snape, Lupin, Harry, and Ron, so I don't know what happened during that confrontation.
metadata.scene_title: Lupin Arrives, the Map’s Insults, and Confiscation

metadata.description: I was not present when Lupin’s Warning and Harry’s Guilt occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I realized the Invisibility Cloak was still down there, but I didn't dare go and get it.
metadata.source_text: As Harry passed the one-eyed witch, he remembered the Invisibility Cloak — it was still down there, but he didn’t dare go and get it.
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I felt my heart plummet because I suddenly thought Hermione must have told Professor McGonagall; my fear about consequences just got worse.
metadata.source_text: One look at her face convinced Harry that she had heard what had happened. His heart plummeted — had she told Professor McGonagall?
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione's face made me realize she already knows what went wrong and I worry our actions have lost her sympathy; I feel exposed to her judgment.
metadata.source_text: One look at her face convinced Harry that she had heard what had happened.
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I've learned and must tell them that Hagrid lost his case and Buckbeak is going to be executed.
metadata.source_text: I just thought you ought to know . . . Hagrid lost his case. Buckbeak is going to be executed.
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I'm upset and trembling while I tell them the news, so I now feel this is urgent and terrible and that they need to know straight away rather than gloat or scold.
metadata.source_text: She was holding a letter in her hands and her lip was trembling.
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: By bringing this awful news to them, I show I'm on Hagrid's side and expect them to take the situation seriously rather than mock or boast.
metadata.source_text: I just thought you ought to know . . . Hagrid lost his case. Buckbeak is going to be executed.
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I admitted it was my fault because I persuaded Harry to go; I recognise that I encouraged something I'd now call stupid.
metadata.source_text: “It’s my fault,” said Ron abruptly. “I persuaded you to go. Lupin’s right, it was stupid, we shouldn’t’ve done it —”
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I suddenly feel guilty and agree with Lupin that what we did was stupid; I'm not defending our choice any more.
metadata.source_text: “Lupin’s right, it was stupid, we shouldn’t’ve done it —”
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: When Hermione appears I react savagely, which shows I fear being judged or told on; my anger towards her is really just a front for shame.
metadata.source_text: “Come to have a good gloat?” said Ron savagely as she stopped in front of them. “Or have you just been to tell on us?”
metadata.scene_title: Meeting Hermione with Bad News — Buckbeak’s Fate Revealed

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Trelawney plans to start crystal-ball lessons earlier than scheduled because she says the exam in June will be about the Orb.
metadata.source_text: I have decided to introduce the crystal ball a little earlier than I had planned
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I'm a bit relieved we've finished palmistry; I was getting sick of her flinching every time she looked at my hands, so I actually prefer crystal balls to more awkward palm readings.
metadata.source_text: Don’t complain, this means we’ve finished palmistry," Harry muttered back. "I was getting sick of her flinching every time she looked at my hands.
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I see Hermione's not afraid to mock teachers loudly when she thinks they're ridiculous; she snorted at Trelawney's claim and made Ron and me choke back laughs with her bluntness.
metadata.source_text: Hermione snorted. "Well, honestly . . . ‘the fates have informed her’ . . . who sets the exam? She does! What an amazing prediction!"
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I've understood from Trelawney's announcement that the June examination will concern the Orb and so crystal-ball work will be examined.
metadata.source_text: "The fates have informed me that your examination in June will concern the Orb, and I am anxious to give you sufficient practice."
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I no longer accept Trelawney's pronouncements at face value; I'm openly skeptical and think she probably arranges or influences the exam content herself rather than being guided by mystical 'fates'.
metadata.source_text: Hermione snorted. "Well, honestly . . . ‘the fates have informed her’ . . . who sets the exam? She does! What an amazing prediction!"
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I feel comfortable voicing my disbelief in front of Harry and Ron; my blunt reaction made them laugh and showed I'm willing to call out what I see as absurdity, even in a teacher.
metadata.source_text: Hermione snorted. "Well, honestly . . . ‘the fates have informed her’ . . . who sets the exam? She does! What an amazing prediction!"
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I realized we're being started on crystal balls earlier than we expected; I thought crystal-ball lessons weren't supposed to start until next term.
metadata.source_text: "I thought we weren’t starting crystal balls until next term," Ron muttered
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I'm wary and a bit put out by the sudden change to the timetable; I muttered casting a wary eye around for Trelawney in case she was lurking nearby, showing I'm uncomfortable with surprises.
metadata.source_text: "I thought we weren’t starting crystal balls until next term," Ron muttered, casting a wary eye around for Professor Trelawney, in case she was lurking nearby.
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I find Hermione's bluntness funny and supportive; when she mocked Trelawney, Harry and I choked back laughs, which makes me feel more camaraderie with them in class moments like this.
metadata.source_text: Hermione snorted. "Well, honestly . . . ‘the fates have informed her’ . . . who sets the exam? She does! What an amazing prediction!"
metadata.scene_title: Divination Lesson Begins with Crystal Gazing

metadata.description: I learned that crystal gazing involves staring into an Orb while trying to empty your mind so the "Inner Eye" or superconscious might show you visions.
metadata.source_text: We shall start by practicing relaxing the conscious mind and external eyes so as to clear the Inner Eye and the superconscious.

metadata.description: I felt even more convinced that this exercise is silly and makes me feel foolish when I can't stop thinking "This is stupid" while trying to look blank.
metadata.source_text: Harry, at least, felt extremely foolish, staring blankly at the crystal ball, trying to keep his mind empty when thoughts such as "This is stupid" kept drifting across it.

metadata.description: I found myself laughing with Hermione at Ron's joke about the burn and fog, which reminded me how easily we bounce off each other during daft moments in class.
metadata.source_text: "Both Harry and Hermione burst out laughing."

metadata.description: I've learned that Professor Trelawney thinks crystal gazing is a refined art that requires clearing the conscious mind and the "Inner Eye" to See within the Orb.
metadata.source_text: Crystal gazing is a particularly refined art," she said dreamily. "I do not expect any of you to See when first you peer into the Orb's infinite depths. We shall start by practicing relaxing the conscious mind and external eyes so as to clear the Inner Eye and the superconscious.

metadata.description: I'm more certain that this lesson is a waste of time and that my time would be better spent practicing useful spells like Cheering Charms instead of staring at a crystal ball.
metadata.source_text: "This is such a waste of time," Hermione hissed. "I could be practicing something useful. I could be catching up on Cheering Charms —"

metadata.description: I was annoyed by the class's silliness and by Ron's giggling; my tutting at Ron shows I'm easily exasperated when people undermine learning with childish behaviour.
metadata.source_text: It didn't help that Ron kept breaking into silent giggles and Hermione kept tutting.

metadata.description: I noticed an actual burn mark on the table after peering at the Orb and guessed someone had spilled a candle, which I thought counted as seeing something from the gazing.
metadata.source_text: "Yeah, there's a burn on this table," said Ron, pointing. "Someone's spilled their candle."

metadata.description: I reckon the whole crystal-gazing bit isn't as solemn as Trelawney makes out; I'm more inclined to mock it and make jokes, like predicting fog from a shadowy shape.
metadata.source_text: "I don't need help," Ron whispered. "It's obvious what this means. There's going to be loads of fog tonight."

metadata.description: I laughed and joked with Harry and Hermione during the lesson, which shows I'm comfortable ribbing my mates even when a teacher is being serious, though it gets us told off.
metadata.source_text: Both Harry and Hermione burst out laughing.

metadata.description: I think Trelawney saw something moving in the crystal ball that was ominous and coming toward me—her words made me certain it wasn't good.
metadata.source_text: There is something here! ... Something moving . . . but what is it?
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: I was convinced from the way she spoke that whatever Trelawney meant wasn't good news; I bet everything I owned it wouldn't be good.
metadata.source_text: Harry was prepared to bet everything he owned, including his Firebolt, that it wasn’t good news, whatever it was.
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: Trelawney singled me out when she breathed, 'my dear, stalking toward you,' so I now feel like her prophecies can include me directly and make me uneasy.
metadata.source_text: My dear . . . ," Professor Trelawney breathed, gazing up at Harry. "It is here, plainer than ever before . . . my dear, stalking toward you, growing ever closer . . . the Gr —
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: I've learned that Professor Trelawney repeatedly interprets the crystal ball as showing a Grim, and I find that interpretation ridiculous enough to say so aloud.
metadata.source_text: Not that ridiculous Grim again!
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: I gave up on tolerating the class because I truly believe Divination in this form is nonsense; I'm fed up and decided to leave rather than keep pretending.
metadata.source_text: Fine! ... I give up! I'm leaving!
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: Because Trelawney angrily told me my mind is 'hopelessly mundane,' I now see that she regards me as unsuited to Divination and that our relationship is strained by her contempt.
metadata.source_text: I am sorry to say that from the moment you have arrived in this class, my dear, it has been apparent that you do not have what the noble art of Divination requires. Indeed, I don’t remember ever meeting a student whose mind was so hopelessly mundane.
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: I realised that Trelawney had supposedly seen something called the Grim moving toward Harry, and Hermione thought that idea was ridiculous.
metadata.source_text: There is something here! ... Something moving . . . but what is it?
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: Hermione's sudden anger and decision to leave showed me she's more impatient with Trelawney's theatrics than I might have guessed; I felt surprised by how quickly she stormed out.
metadata.source_text: Fine! ... I give up! I'm leaving!
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: When Hermione nearly knocked me off my chair as she grabbed her bag and left, I realised her frustration can be explosive and that her actions affect those sitting beside her.
metadata.source_text: Fine! she repeated, swinging the bag over her shoulder and almost knocking Ron off his chair.
metadata.scene_title: Trelawney's Grim Prediction Redirected to Hermione

metadata.description: I've heard Professor Trelawney say she thought Hermione would be leaving around Easter; Lavender loudly reminded her of that prediction and Trelawney answered as if she had foreseen it.
metadata.source_text: ‘Around Easter, one of our number will leave us forever!’ You said it ages ago, Professor!” Professor Trelawney gave her a dewy smile. “Yes, my dear, I did indeed know that Miss Granger would be leaving us.

metadata.description: I'm starting to feel uneasy about the whole Trelawney thing — Lavender's excitement and the way Trelawney spoke makes the idea of Hermione leaving seem disturbingly possible.
metadata.source_text: ‘Around Easter, one of our number will leave us forever!’ You said it ages ago, Professor!” Professor Trelawney gave her a dewy smile. “Yes, my dear, I did indeed know that Miss Granger would be leaving us.

metadata.description: I notice Hermione is under terrible pressure and exhausted; seeing her like that has made me more concerned for her wellbeing and made me view her as someone who needs help, not just a brilliant student.
metadata.source_text: She was usually last to leave the common room at night, first to arrive at the library the next morning; she had shadows like Lupin’s under her eyes, and seemed constantly close to tears.

metadata.description: I've learned that Professor Trelawney believed I would be leaving around Easter; Lavender reminded her of the prophecy and Trelawney said she did indeed know I would be leaving.
metadata.source_text: ‘Around Easter, one of our number will leave us forever!’ You said it ages ago, Professor!” Professor Trelawney gave her a dewy smile. “Yes, my dear, I did indeed know that Miss Granger would be leaving us.

metadata.description: I'm beginning to feel crushed by my workload; taking more subjects than anyone and skipping Divination hasn't made things easier, and I'm convinced I can't keep going at this pace without breaking down.
metadata.source_text: But nobody had as much to do as Hermione. Even without Divination, she was taking more subjects than anybody else. She was usually last to leave the common room at night, first to arrive at the library the next morning; she had shadows like Lupin’s under her eyes, and seemed constantly close to tears.

metadata.description: I can tell others have noticed my state; people like Lavender and Trelawney talk about me and speculate, which makes me feel exposed and aware that my struggle is visible to my peers.
metadata.source_text: ‘Around Easter, one of our number will leave us forever!’ ... “Yes, my dear, I did indeed know that Miss Granger would be leaving us.

metadata.description: I've found out Professor Trelawney said she thought Hermione would be leaving around Easter when Lavender piped up, and Trelawney answered as though she'd foreseen Hermione's departure.
metadata.source_text: ‘Around Easter, one of our number will leave us forever!’ You said it ages ago, Professor!” Professor Trelawney gave her a dewy smile. “Yes, my dear, I did indeed know that Miss Granger would be leaving us.

metadata.description: I'm worried about Hermione more than I was; seeing her exhausted and near tears while doing far too many subjects has made me think she needs support, not just study time.
metadata.source_text: She was usually last to leave the common room at night, first to arrive at the library the next morning; she had shadows like Lupin’s under her eyes, and seemed constantly close to tears.

metadata.source_text: The taunt about his father rang in Harry’s ears as though Black had bellowed it. A boiling hate erupted in Harry’s chest, leaving no place for fear.

metadata.source_text: His eyes were fixed on Harry. “I thought you’d come and help your friend,” he said hoarsely. “Your father would have done the same for me. Brave of you, not to run for a teacher. I’m grateful . . . it will make everything much easier. . . .”

metadata.source_text: “Expelliarmus!” he croaked, pointing Ron’s wand at them.

metadata.source_text: HE KILLED MY MUM AND DAD!” Harry roared, and with a huge effort he broke free of Hermione’s and Ron’s restraint and lunged forward —

metadata.source_text: “You’ll have to kill all three of us!”

metadata.source_text: If Black wanted to save it, that only proved he cared more for Crookshanks than for Harry’s parents.

metadata.source_text: He was going to kill Black. He had to kill Black.

metadata.source_text: Now was the moment to do it. Now was the moment to avenge his mother and father.

metadata.description: I feel deep sorrow and fear for Harry — his grief has pushed him to a dangerous place, and I see him differently now: as someone dangerously close to doing something irreversible.
metadata.source_text: To his right, Hermione gave a dry sob.

metadata.description: I noticed Harry was absolutely fixed on killing Black — he raised his wand and seemed certain that this was the moment to act.
metadata.source_text: Harry raised the wand. Now was the moment to do it.

metadata.description: Seeing Harry so determined to kill Black makes me rethink how dangerous the situation is; I now believe immediate action or intervention is necessary to stop him.
metadata.source_text: He was going to kill Black. He had to kill Black.

metadata.description: Harry's obsession with vengeance makes me feel alarmed and worried about him — our friendship is strained by how ready he seems to be to harm others in the name of revenge.
metadata.source_text: So what if he had to kill the cat too? It was in league with Black.

metadata.source_text: Muffled footsteps were echoing up through the floor — someone was moving downstairs.

metadata.description: I felt suddenly empty; I realised I hadn't acted when I should have and that changes how I see my own nerve under pressure.
metadata.source_text: Harry stood there, feeling suddenly empty.

metadata.description: I held my wand over Sirius Black and saw him crumpled and bleeding at my feet — I know now how closely his fate was tied to my hesitation in that moment.
metadata.source_text: His eyes flickered ... to Harry, standing there with his wand covering Black, and then to Black himself, crumpled and bleeding at Harry’s feet.

metadata.source_text: “WE’RE UP HERE!” Hermione screamed suddenly.

metadata.source_text: Lupin caught them all deftly, then moved into the room, staring at Black,

metadata.source_text: He hadn’t done it. His nerve had failed him.

metadata.source_text: He hadn’t done it. His nerve had failed him.

metadata.description: I've noticed Lupin speaking in an odd, trembling voice that shows he's holding back strong feelings; that tells me something important is upsetting him.
metadata.source_text: Then Lupin spoke in an odd voice, a voice that shook with some suppressed emotion.

metadata.source_text: Then Lupin spoke in an odd voice, a voice that shook with some suppressed emotion.

metadata.description: I've seen Lupin look and speak in a new, troubled way, so I now feel there's more to his connection with Sirius than I appreciated before.
metadata.source_text: Then Lupin spoke in an odd voice, a voice that shook with some suppressed emotion. “Where is he, Sirius?”

metadata.description: I found out that Sirius Black pointed straight at me with a slow, empty hand; I learned that I've been singled out in a way I didn't expect.
metadata.source_text: Then, very slowly, he raised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron.

metadata.source_text: Then, very slowly, he raised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron.

metadata.source_text: Then, very slowly, he raised his empty hand and pointed straight at Ron.

metadata.scene_title: Explanation Begins — The Map and the Dots

metadata.description: I've known that Lupin is a werewolf for ages after doing Professor Snape's essay and recognising his symptoms from what I read for that assignment.

metadata.scene_title: Explanation Begins — The Map and the Dots

metadata.scene_title: Explanation Begins — The Map and the Dots

metadata.description: I feel betrayed and furious with Lupin for hiding his condition and for relying on me to cover for him; our relationship is damaged because I was protecting him without his telling others.

metadata.scene_title: Explanation Begins — The Map and the Dots

metadata.source_text: The map," said Lupin. "The Marauder's Map. I was in my office examining it —" "You know how to work it?" Harry said suspiciously. "Of course I know how to work it," said Lupin, waving his hand impatiently. "I helped write it. I'm Moony — that was my friends' nickname for me at school."

metadata.description: I used to think Lupin might have been helping Sirius Black, but after he swears he hasn't and asks to explain, I'm thrown into confusion and not sure what to believe.

metadata.scene_title: Lupin's Role Revealed and Scabbers Thrashed Out

metadata.source_text: He was pointing at Black, who suddenly crossed to the four-poster bed and sank onto it, his face hidden in one shaking hand. Crookshanks leapt up beside him and stepped onto his lap, purring. Ron edged away from both of them, dragging his leg.
metadata.scene_title: Lupin's Role Revealed and Scabbers Thrashed Out
