metadata.source_text: How could Scabbers be Peter Pettigrew? Azkaban must have unhinged Black after all — but why was Lupin playing along with him?

metadata.description: I've found out from the register that the Ministry keeps records of Animagi and that Pettigrew's name isn't on the list, so officially he wasn't known as an Animagus.
metadata.source_text: Because . . . because people would know if Peter Pettigrew had been an Animagus. We did Animagi in class with Professor McGonagall. And I looked them up when I did my homework — the Ministry of Magic keeps tabs on witches and wizards who can become animals; there's a register showing what animal they become, and their markings and things . . . and I went and looked Professor McGonagall up on the register, and there have been only seven Animagi this century, and Pettigrew's name wasn't on the list —

metadata.description: I believed Pettigrew couldn't be Scabbers because official records said so, but Professor Lupin's calm correction about unregistered Animagi has made me realise official records can be incomplete.
metadata.source_text: But the Ministry never knew that there used to be three unregistered Animagi running around Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I'm surprised that Professor Lupin, whom I usually respect, is the one revealing such personal and shocking history here; I feel both respect and a new curiosity about him.
metadata.source_text: The Shrieking Shack was never haunted. . . . The screams and howls the villagers used to hear were made by me." He pushed his graying hair out of his eyes, thought for a moment, then said, "That's where all of this starts — with my becoming a werewolf.

metadata.description: I've been forced to see Scabbers as more than a pet because people are saying he's actually Peter Pettigrew — I can feel how badly everyone wants me to understand, even if I can't accept it yet.
metadata.source_text: HE'S NOT PETER, HE'S SCABBERS!" Ron yelled, trying to force the rat back into his front pocket, but Scabbers was fighting too hard; Ron swayed and overbalanced, and Harry caught him and pushed him back down to the bed.

metadata.description: I'm starting to doubt what I thought I knew about Scabbers because Sirius and Lupin insist on this story so angrily; I'm frightened and confused and thinking of leaving.
metadata.source_text: "You're nutters, both of you," said Ron shakily, looking round at Harry and Hermione for support. "I've had enough of this. I'm off."

metadata.description: I feel attacked and desperate when Sirius lunges for Scabbers and Professor Lupin restrains him; I don't like how they treat me and my pet, even if they claim to be telling the truth.
metadata.source_text: And Crookshanks was thrown to the floor as Black lunged at Scabbers; Ron yelled with pain as Black's weight fell on his broken leg.

metadata.description: I learned that before the Wolfsbane Potion existed, Lupin became a full monster each month and was smuggled out of Hogwarts so he wouldn't hurt anyone.
metadata.source_text: Before the Wolfsbane Potion was discovered, however, I became a fully fledged monster once a month.

metadata.description: I learned that the Whomping Willow and the tunnel and that house were put there specifically because Lupin came to Hogwarts, to hide him when he transformed.
metadata.source_text: I told you, months ago, that the Whomping Willow was planted the year I came to Hogwarts. The truth is that it was planted because I came to Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I've realized that James Potter, Sirius Black and Peter Pettigrew were not only Lupin's friends but risk-taking allies who became Animagi to keep him company during his changes.
metadata.source_text: For the first time ever, I had friends, three great friends. Sirius Black . . . Peter Pettigrew . . . and, of course, your father, Harry — James Potter.

metadata.description: I'm surprised and moved to discover that my dad and his friends could and did become Animagi, working for years to manage Lupin's transformations.
metadata.source_text: They became Animagi.

metadata.description: I've learned that Lupin's friends sneaked out under James's Invisibility Cloak and turned into animals to join him during his transformations.
metadata.source_text: They sneaked out of the castle every month under James’s Invisibility Cloak. They transformed . . .

metadata.description: I am astonished to accept that students like James and Sirius managed such a dangerous magical transformation at school after years of work.
metadata.source_text: It took them the best part of three years to work out how to do it.

metadata.description: I now understand that Lupin's relationship with James, Sirius and Peter was deeply loyal and practical; they risked Ministry rules to protect him.
metadata.source_text: Instead, they did something for me that would make my transformations not only bearable, but the best times of my life. They became Animagi.

metadata.description: I learned that Peter Pettigrew was small enough to slip beneath the Whomping Willow's branches to touch the knot that freezes it so they could get into the tunnel.
metadata.source_text: Peter, as the smallest, could slip beneath the Willow’s attacking branches and touch the knot that freezes it.

metadata.description: I'm impressed and a bit stunned that my mate's father and his friends risked illegal Animagus work and sneaking about to help Lupin every month.
metadata.source_text: They sneaked out of the castle every month under James’s Invisibility Cloak.

metadata.description: I now see James Potter, Sirius Black and Peter Pettigrew as incredibly loyal to Lupin; they didn't desert him when they learned he was a werewolf.
metadata.source_text: And they didn’t desert me at all. Instead, they did something for me...

metadata.description: I learned that Sirius is called Padfoot, Peter is Wormtail, and James was Prongs, and that they made the Marauder’s Map together when they became Animagi to keep Remus company.
metadata.source_text: And that’s how we came to write the Marauder’s Map, and sign it with our nicknames. Sirius is Padfoot. Peter is Wormtail. James was Prongs.

metadata.description: I’m beginning to understand how dangerous their nights were and why people like Snape would have distrusted them; it makes me rethink how reckless their adventures really were.
metadata.source_text: That was still really dangerous! Running around in the dark with a werewolf! What if you’d given the others the slip, and bitten somebody?

metadata.description: I’ve learned more about Sirius and Lupin’s past and how close they were at school, which changes my view of them from just adults at Hogwarts to young people who took huge risks together.
metadata.source_text: Soon we were leaving the Shrieking Shack and roaming the school grounds and the village by night. Sirius and James transformed into such large animals, they were able to keep a werewolf in check.

metadata.description: I realised how dangerous it was to run about at night with a werewolf and that being an Animagus was used so the others could keep Remus under control during transformations.
metadata.source_text: That was still really dangerous! Running around in the dark with a werewolf! What if you’d given the others the slip, and bitten somebody?

metadata.description: I feel more convinced that rules exist for good reasons; hearing Lupin admit guilt about breaking Dumbledore’s trust reinforces my faith in authority and safety regulations at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: I sometimes felt guilty about betraying Dumbledore’s trust, of course . . . he had admitted me to Hogwarts when no other headmaster would have done so, and he had no idea I was breaking the rules he had set down for my own and others’ safety.

metadata.description: My opinion of Lupin has shifted: I see both his vulnerability and his remorse, so I view him less as merely a dangerous creature and more as someone who is deeply conflicted and repentant.
metadata.source_text: Lupin’s face had hardened, and there was self-disgust in his voice. “All this year, I have been battling with myself, wondering whether I should tell Dumbledore that Sirius was an Animagus.

metadata.description: I found out the nicknames the marauders used — Padfoot, Wormtail and Prongs — and that they made the Marauder’s Map when they were all Animagi running about with Lupin.
metadata.source_text: And that’s how we came to write the Marauder’s Map, and sign it with our nicknames. Sirius is Padfoot. Peter is Wormtail. James was Prongs.

metadata.description: I’m more worried about Scabbers now, given how hungry Sirius looked and what Lupin said about near misses; I’m starting to feel uneasy about how safe our rat actually is.
metadata.source_text: Hurry up, Remus,” snarled Black, who was still watching Scabbers with a horrible sort of hunger on his face.

metadata.description: Hearing that Snape saw Lupin transforming and then spent the year trying to undermine him makes me think Snape’s bitterness at school had deeper reasons than simple bullying.
metadata.source_text: Severus was very interested in where I went every month,” Lupin told Harry, Ron, and Hermione. “We were in the same year, you know, and we — er — didn’t like each other very much.

metadata.description: I've been alone with Professor Lupin many times for defense against the Dementors; he could have killed me on those occasions if he'd wanted to.
metadata.source_text: Professor Lupin could have killed me about a hundred times this year," Harry said. "I've been alone with him loads of times, having defense lessons against the dementors.

metadata.description: I'm questioning the idea that Lupin would be helping Black because I can't see why he wouldn't have finished me if he really was on Black's side.
metadata.source_text: "If he was helping Black, why didn't he just finish me off then?"

metadata.description: I'm furious with Snape; I think he's pathetic and won't listen because of being made a fool at school, and I don't trust his motives toward me.
metadata.source_text: "YOU'RE PATHETIC!" Harry yelled. "JUST BECAUSE THEY MADE A FOOL OF YOU AT SCHOOL YOU WON'T EVEN LISTEN —"

metadata.description: I learned that Ron and I can Disarm Snape together at exactly the same moment as Harry casts a spell; our simultaneous shout knocked Snape out and sent his wand flying.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I now see that acting together with Ron and Harry can produce powerful results quickly in dangerous situations; coordinated spells can incapacitate even a skilled wizard like Snape.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I feel more aligned with Ron and Harry in urgent moments; our teamwork mattered here and I recognize that we can protect each other when needed.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I found out that I can perform a Disarming spell at the same instant as Hermione and Harry and that combined we can knock Snape out and send his wand skittering across the bed.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that joining forces with my friends has real power; I don't want to hang back when Harry and Hermione act in dangerous situations.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I feel closer to Harry and Hermione because we reacted together; we've proven we can back each other up when things get violent with adults like Snape.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around. Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment.

metadata.description: I learned that Snape's wand flew from him when we all tried to Disarm him at exactly the same moment; the wand landed on the bed next to Crookshanks.
metadata.source_text: Both Ron and Hermione had tried to Disarm Snape at exactly the same moment. Snape’s wand soared in a high arc and landed on the bed next to Crookshanks.

metadata.description: I'm not sure I did the right thing by attacking a teacher; even now I avoid Sirius's eyes because I keep thinking maybe I shouldn't have intervened.
metadata.source_text: You shouldn’t have done that," said Black, looking at Harry. "You should have left him to me. . . ." Harry avoided Black’s eyes. He wasn’t sure, even now, that he’d done the right thing.

metadata.description: Sirius blames me for not leaving the matter to him, and although he then helps prove my point, I feel the tension between us — he's willing to press me but still thanks me through action.
metadata.source_text: "You shouldn’t have done that," said Black, looking at Harry. "You should have left him to me. . . ." ... "Thank you, Harry," he said.

metadata.description: I've realised we just attacked a teacher; seeing Snape lifeless makes me understand the gravity of what we've done and that serious trouble is likely.
metadata.source_text: We attacked a teacher. . . . We attacked a teacher . . . ," Hermione whimpered, staring at the lifeless Snape with frightened eyes. "Oh, we’re going to be in so much trouble —

metadata.description: I'm frightened and now believe that our impulsive action has put us in deep trouble; my confidence has shifted to fear about consequences.
metadata.source_text: "We attacked a teacher. . . . We attacked a teacher . . . ," Hermione whimpered, staring at the lifeless Snape with frightened eyes. "Oh, we’re going to be in so much trouble —

metadata.description: Seeing Harry avoid Sirius and hearing Lupin thank Harry makes me see Harry's position as complicated: he acted bravely but now faces distrust and blame from others.
metadata.source_text: Harry avoided Black’s eyes. He wasn’t sure, even now, that he’d done the right thing. ... "Thank you, Harry," he said. "I’m still not saying I believe you," Harry retorted.

metadata.description: I've learned that someone must have seen Scabbers in a photograph — there's actually a Daily Prophet picture showing Scabbers on my shoulder from last summer.
metadata.source_text: It was the photograph of Ron and his family that had appeared in the Daily Prophet the previous summer, and there, on Ron’s shoulder, was Scabbers.

metadata.description: I was sceptical that Pettigrew would have escaped Azkaban just to find Scabbers, but seeing the photograph and hearing Black's explanation makes me realise there's a way Pettigrew could have been traced to Scabbers.
metadata.source_text: Are you trying to say he broke out of Azkaban just to get his hands on Scabbers? ... "Okay, say Pettigrew could turn into a rat — there are millions of rats — how’s he supposed to know which one he’s after if he was locked up in Azkaban?"

metadata.description: I'm clinging to Scabbers because I distrust anyone who threatens him; but Black producing the photo makes me see that Sirius had external help (Fudge) to track Scabbers, which shifts how I view the threat.
metadata.source_text: Ron clutched Scabbers closer to his chest. ... "Fudge," said Black. "When he came to inspect Azkaban last year, he gave me his paper.

metadata.description: I've just seen Peter in a photograph on the front page and I recognized him at once — the rat on that boy's shoulder is the same man I've been thinking about.
metadata.source_text: And there was Peter, on the front page . . . on this boy’s shoulder. . . . I knew him at once . . . how many times had I seen him transform?

metadata.description: I used to believe Sirius was the one who betrayed my parents, but I'm suddenly not so sure; Lupin says we've got it the wrong way round, and that changes everything for me.
metadata.source_text: All this time we’ve thought Sirius betrayed your parents, and Peter tracked him down — but it was the other way around, don’t you see?

metadata.description: I'm furious with Black, thinking he came to finish Pettigrew just like he finished my parents' enemies, and I want to confront him for what I think he planned to do.
metadata.source_text: And now you’ve come to finish him off! "Yes, I have," said Black, with an evil look at Scabbers. "Then I should’ve let Snape take you!" Harry shouted.

metadata.description: I've learned from what Black says that Crookshanks recognized Peter straight away and even stole the Gryffindor Tower passwords from a boy's bedside table to help expose him.
metadata.source_text: He tried to bring Peter to me, but couldn’t . . . so he stole the passwords into Gryffindor Tower for me. . . . As I understand it, he took them from a boy’s bedside table.

metadata.description: I believed Scabbers was just an ordinary pet, but hearing that the biggest piece of Peter found was his finger and seeing the missing toe makes me reconsider that simple explanation.
metadata.source_text: The biggest bit of Peter they found was his finger." "His front paw . . ." "He’s got a toe missing," said Black.

metadata.description: I'm surprised at Crookshanks' cleverness and at how Crookshanks allied with Black to try to reveal Peter; my opinion of the cat's intelligence has definitely risen.
metadata.source_text: He’s the most intelligent of his kind I’ve ever met. He recognized Peter for what he was right away. ... Finally, I managed to communicate to him what I was after, and he’s been helping me.

metadata.description: I've been told that Scabbers has lived in my family twelve years and that he might've been losing weight since Sirius was on the loose, which suggests my rat's age and condition are suspicious.
metadata.source_text: We — we’ve been taking good care of him! ... "Twelve years, in fact," said Lupin. "Didn’t you ever wonder why he was living so long?" ... "I’d guess he’s been losing weight ever since he heard Sirius was on the loose again. . . ."

metadata.description: I wanted to believe Scabbers is just a normal rat and that Crookshanks is a mad cat, but now I'm shaken — people say Scabbers might be Peter and that changes how I feel about him.
metadata.source_text: Look, Scabbers probably had a fight with another rat or something! He’s been in my family for ages, right —" ... "This cat isn't mad," said Black hoarsely.

metadata.description: I feel defensive and protective about Scabbers because he's been in my family, but I'm beginning to doubt him after hearing Lupin and Black's accusations and the newspaper evidence.
metadata.source_text: Look, Scabbers probably had a fight with another rat or something! He’s been in my family for ages, right —" ... "And the caption said the boy would be going back to Hogwarts . . . to where Harry was. . . .

metadata.description: I just found out that Peter was their Secret-Keeper and that he said he killed my mum and dad.
metadata.source_text: HE WAS THEIR SECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU TURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I used to think Sirius was the one who betrayed and killed them, but hearing that Peter was the Secret-Keeper and claimed responsibility has shaken what I believed about who did it.
metadata.source_text: HE WAS THEIR SECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU TURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I'm furious and accusing at Sirius now; I can't accept his explanation without confronting him — I'm pointing at him and demanding the truth.
metadata.source_text: He was pointing at Black, who shook his head slowly; the sunken eyes were suddenly overbright.
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I recognize that Peter was named Secret-Keeper for the Potters and that Peter claimed responsibility for killing them.
metadata.source_text: HE WAS THEIR SECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU TURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: Hearing Sirius admit he persuaded the Potters to change Secret-Keeper makes me reconsider how choices and persuasion affected the outcome — I see the gravity of that decision more clearly.
metadata.source_text: I as good as killed them," he croaked. "I persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the last moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-Keeper instead of me.
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I'm aware that my view of Sirius will be complicated now; his admission that he influenced James and Lily shifts how I regard him — from simply an accused man to someone confessing regret.
metadata.source_text: Harry . . . I as good as killed them," he croaked. "I persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the last moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-Keeper instead of me.
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I've learned that Peter was the Potters' Secret-Keeper and that he claimed he killed James and Lily.
metadata.source_text: HE WAS THEIR SECRET-KEEPER! HE SAID SO BEFORE YOU TURNED UP. HE SAID HE KILLED THEM!
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I'm taken aback by the idea that Sirius might not have been the killer — hearing that Peter said he did it and that Sirius admits persuading the change makes me doubt what I thought.
metadata.source_text: I as good as killed them," he croaked. "I persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the last moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-Keeper instead of me.
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: My attitude toward Sirius is conflicted now: I'm shocked and don't know whether to blame him outright, since he's admitting a role in the decision that led to the Potters' deaths.
metadata.source_text: Harry . . . I as good as killed them," he croaked. "I persuaded Lily and James to change to Peter at the last moment, persuaded them to use him as Secret-Keeper instead of me.
metadata.scene_title: Confession and Quarreling over the Past

metadata.description: I saw Lupin insistently demand proof and make Ron hand over Scabbers so they could force him to show himself — it was a deliberate test to reveal truth by magic.
metadata.source_text: There’s one certain way to prove what really happened. Ron, give me that rat.

metadata.description: I couldn't help feeling that something serious was about to happen when Lupin's voice went steely and Sirius's wet eyes seemed to burn — I started to think this wasn't just a petty argument anymore.
metadata.source_text: “Enough of this,” said Lupin, and there was a steely note in his voice Harry had never heard before.

metadata.description: Watching Lupin take control and Sirius cooperate made me see Lupin as someone who can act decisively, and Sirius as willing to risk showing emotion to help the truth come out.
metadata.source_text: “Together?” he said quietly. “I think so,” said Lupin, holding Scabbers tightly in one hand and his wand in the other.

metadata.description: I've observed that forcing a creature to reveal its true form can be done by simultaneous wandwork from two skilled wizards, producing a very bright, blue-white light and a rapid transformation.
metadata.source_text: A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair, his small gray form twisting madly

metadata.description: I felt more certain that a properly executed magical test will produce undeniable evidence; the way Lupin and Sirius acted together convinced me that the method would force the truth out.
metadata.source_text: “If he really is a rat, it won’t hurt him.”

metadata.description: Seeing Lupin take charge and Sirius participate quietly made me respect Lupin's authority in an emergency and understand Sirius's readiness to help reveal facts, even when he's upset.
metadata.source_text: “Together?” he said quietly. “I think so,” said Lupin, holding Scabbers tightly in one hand and his wand in the other.

metadata.description: I learned that showing me the rat wouldn't hurt him if he really was a rat — Lupin said he'd force him to show himself and that it wouldn't harm Scabbers if he were just a rat.
metadata.source_text: “Force him to show himself,” said Lupin. “If he really is a rat, it won’t hurt him.”

metadata.description: At first I hesitated and felt tense about giving Scabbers up, but when I finally handed him over I realized I trusted Lupin enough to try to prove what was true.
metadata.source_text: Ron hesitated. Then at long last, he held out Scabbers and Lupin took him.

metadata.description: Giving Scabbers to Lupin and seeing Sirius step forward made me see Lupin and Sirius as people prepared to confront whatever the truth was; I felt more reliant on their judgment than I did before.
metadata.source_text: “Ready, Sirius?” said Lupin. Black had already retrieved Snape’s wand from the bed.

metadata.description: I saw a rat turn into a man right before my eyes when Lupin and Black cast the spell together; the rat really transformed into a short man in an instant.
metadata.source_text: A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair... There was another blinding flash of light and then — It was like watching a speeded-up film of a growing tree. A head was shooting upward from the ground; limbs were sprouting; a moment later, a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I can't think of Scabbers as just a harmless rat any more; seeing him become a man changes everything I believed about him being an ordinary pet.
metadata.source_text: A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair... a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I'm suddenly more alert to Lupin and Black's involvement — Lupin was calm and certain about forcing the rat to show himself, and Black helped by casting with him, so I see them as working together decisively.
metadata.source_text: Force him to show himself," said Lupin. "If he really is a rat, it won't hurt him." ... "Together?" he said quietly. "I think so," said Lupin

metadata.description: I watched Lupin and Black cast a joint spell that revealed an Animagus or transformed creature; the small grey rat became a man after two bright flashes from their wands.
metadata.source_text: A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair... There was another blinding flash of light and then... a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I no longer believe Scabbers is simply a rat; the transformation proves there's more to him than I thought and my understanding of his identity has changed.
metadata.source_text: Scabbers began to squeak without stopping... There was another blinding flash of light and then... a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I see Lupin as someone who knows how to reveal hidden magical forms; his calm control when taking Scabbers and casting suggests competence I respect.
metadata.source_text: Force him to show himself," said Lupin. "If he really is a rat, it won't hurt him." ... "I think so," said Lupin, holding Scabbers tightly in one hand and his wand in the other

metadata.description: I watched Scabbers change — after I handed him over, he squeaked and then the rat became a man when Lupin and Black cast the spell together.
metadata.source_text: Then at long last, he held out Scabbers and Lupin took him... A flash of blue-white light erupted from both wands; for a moment, Scabbers was frozen in midair... a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I can't believe my rat was actually a man; I was tense giving Scabbers up, but seeing him transform has totally changed how I feel about him and about everything.
metadata.source_text: Ron hesitated. Then at long last, he held out Scabbers... Scabbers began to squeak without stopping... a man was standing where Scabbers had been

metadata.description: I'm shaken and confused about Scabbers and by extension about people connected to him; I feel betrayed and unsure who to trust after he turns into a man.
metadata.source_text: Ron hesitated. Then at long last, he held out Scabbers and Lupin took him... a man was standing where Scabbers had been, cringing and wringing his hands

metadata.description: I noticed Peter Pettigrew looks awful — thin, grubby skin, a bald patch and ratlike features. He’s sweating, squeaking, and his index finger is missing.
metadata.source_text: His thin, colorless hair was unkempt and there was a large bald patch on top. He had the shrunken appearance of a plump man who has lost a lot of weight in a short time. His skin looked grubby, almost like Scabbers’s fur, and something of the rat lingered around his pointed nose and his very small, watery eyes.
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I’m beginning to think Pettigrew really is terrified and hiding something — he keeps darting his eyes to the door and squeaks that Black tried to kill him.
metadata.source_text: Harry saw his eyes dart to the door and back again.
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I realise I can’t take Pettigrew at face value anymore; he’s not just a harmless creature — he’s panicked, possibly guilty, and certainly not trustworthy.
metadata.source_text: “He killed Lily and James and now he’s going to kill me too. . . . You’ve got to help me, Remus. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I can see Peter Pettigrew’s appearance and behaviour clearly: he’s shrunken, sweating, missing his index finger, and sounds squeaky when he speaks.
metadata.source_text: Even Pettigrew’s voice was squeaky. Again, his eyes darted toward the door.
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I no longer feel sympathetic in a naive way toward Pettigrew; his frantic claims and ratlike looks make me suspect something darker happened that night.
metadata.source_text: “He’s come to try and kill me again!” Pettigrew squeaked suddenly, pointing at Black, and Harry saw that he used his middle finger, because his index was missing.
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I believe Lupin and Black are united against Pettigrew on the question of what happened the night Lily and James died; Lupin’s coldness shows he’s convinced there are matters to clear up with Peter.
metadata.source_text: “We’ve been having a little chat, Peter, about what happened the night Lily and James died... I’d like to clear up one or two little matters with you, Peter, if you’d be so —”
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I can see Pettigrew is terrified and pointing fingers — literally — he says Black tried to kill him and even uses his middle finger because his index is missing.
metadata.source_text: “He’s come to try and kill me again!” Pettigrew squeaked suddenly, pointing at Black, and Harry saw that he used his middle finger, because his index was missing.
metadata.scene_title: Pettigrew’s Pleas and Black’s Accusation of Treachery

metadata.description: I’m less inclined to believe Pettigrew’s frantic pleas; his behaviour looks like the panic of someone hiding something rather than an honest victim.
metadata.source_text: “He killed Lily and James and now he’s going to kill me too. . . . You’ve got to help me, Remus. . . .”

metadata.source_text: Harry lay listening with his eyes tight shut. He felt very groggy. The words he was hearing seemed to be traveling very slowly from his ears to his brain, so that it was difficult to understand. . . . His limbs felt like lead; his eyelids too heavy to lift. . . . He wanted to lie here, on this comfortable bed, forever.

metadata.description: I can see Ron and Hermione here in the hospital wing with me; Ron’s red hair is under Madam Pomfrey’s arm and Hermione is in the bed to my right looking petrified.
metadata.source_text: At the very end of the ward, he could make out Madam Pomfrey with her back to him, bending over a bed. Harry squinted. Ron’s red hair was visible beneath Madam Pomfrey’s arm. Harry moved his head over on the pillow. In the bed to his right lay Hermione. Moonlight was falling across her bed. Her eyes were open too. She looked petrified...

metadata.description: I heard Fudge and Snape talking outside and learned from their voices that Black was bound and gagged and that the dementors retreated for an odd reason.
metadata.source_text: “No, Minister . . . by the time I had come ’round they were heading back to their positions at the entrances. . . .” “Extraordinary. And yet Black, and Harry, and the girl —” “All unconscious by the time I reached them. I bound and gagged Black, naturally, conjured stretchers, and brought them all straight back to the castle.”

metadata.description: I’m more certain now that I was somewhere near trouble and that adults are debating whether we were at fault or bewitched — I feel accused and aware they think I acted foolishly.
metadata.source_text: “On the other hand, their interference might have permitted Black to escape. . . . They obviously thought they were going to catch Black single-handed. They’ve got away with a great deal before now. . . . I’m afraid it’s given them a rather high opinion of themselves . . . and of course Potter has always been allowed an extraordinary amount of license by the headmaster —”

metadata.description: I realise the Ministry and Snape view me with suspicion and think I get special treatment from the headmaster; whatever they think, I want to see Dumbledore about what happened.
metadata.source_text: “And yet — is it good for him to be given so much special treatment? Personally, I try and treat him like any other student. And any other student would be suspended — at the very least — for leading his friends into such danger. Consider, Minister — against all school rules — after all the precautions put in place for his protection — out-of-bounds, at night, consorting with a werewolf and a murderer — and I have reason to believe he has been visiting Hogsmeade illegally too —”

metadata.description: I woke up in the hospital wing and was beside Harry, very frightened and aware that adults were talking outside the door.
metadata.source_text: In the bed to his right lay Hermione. Moonlight was falling across her bed. Her eyes were open too. She looked petrified, and when she saw that Harry was awake, pressed a finger to her lips, then pointed to the hospital wing door.

metadata.description: I feel alarmed and cautious now; seeing Fudge and Snape whispering makes me realise the situation is serious and that we may be blamed despite being unconscious.
metadata.source_text: She pressed a finger to her lips, then pointed to the hospital wing door. It was ajar, and the voices of Cornelius Fudge and Snape were coming through it from the corridor outside.

metadata.description: I know Harry is determined to see Dumbledore and concerned about what adults think; I’m unnerved but supportive, signalling him to be quiet because of the conversation outside.
metadata.source_text: When she saw that Harry was awake, pressed a finger to her lips, then pointed to the hospital wing door... “How’s Ron?” said Harry and Hermione together.

metadata.description: I was unconscious but I’m alive; Madam Pomfrey says I’ll live, and my red hair was visible under Madam Pomfrey’s arm when Harry woke up.

metadata.description: I feel dependent on Madam Pomfrey’s care now; the fact she’s breaking chocolate with a hammer for us shows she’s taking charge and we’re in her hands.

metadata.description: I realized that Dumbledore wants us to change something from three hours ago and that the window of Flitwick’s office is where Sirius is locked up — we could fly Buckbeak to that window and get Sirius out.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore just said — just said we could save more than one innocent life. . . . "Dumbledore said — he just told us where the window is — the window of Flitwick’s office! metadata.description: I suddenly believed we could actually save Buckbeak and Sirius if we acted carefully; what felt impossible before started to feel like something we had to try.
metadata.source_text: Harry stared at her shadowy face. “There must be something that happened around now he wants us to change,” he said slowly. “What happened? We were walking down to Hagrid’s three hours ago. . . .”

metadata.description: I feel more reliant on Hermione’s planning and quick thinking — she’s the one who explained the Time-Turner and kept us focused and cautious when I wanted to act rashly.

metadata.description: I got a Time-Turner from Professor McGonagall at the start of term and I’ve been using it all year to attend multiple lessons by turning it back so I could do hours over again.

metadata.description: I’m terrified of messing with time now; even though the Time-Turner helps with lessons, Dumbledore’s instructions and McGonagall’s warnings make me convinced we must be extremely careful or awful things could happen.
metadata.source_text: “Don’t you see? Professor McGonagall told me what awful things have happened when wizards have meddled with time. . . .”

metadata.description: I trust Dumbledore’s judgment enough to follow his odd instructions even when I don’t fully understand them, which makes me willing to cooperate with Harry on a dangerous plan rather than act alone.
metadata.source_text: Harry, I don’t understand what Dumbledore wants us to do. Why did he tell us to go back three hours? How’s that going to help Sirius?”

metadata.description: I see Uncle Vernon as someone who hates having me around and who treats wizarding things like filthy words; he's angry and frightened by anything to do with my world.

metadata.description: I believe saying Sirius might think something’s wrong is a good way to make Vernon worry and back off; I can use the idea that Sirius would suspect mistreatment to influence Vernon.

metadata.source_text: "Incendio!" said Mr Weasley, pointing his wand at the hole in the wall behind him. Flames rose at once in the fireplace, crackling merrily as though they had been burning for hours. Mr Weasley took a small drawstring bag from his pocket, untied it, took a pinch of the powder inside, and threw it onto the flames, which turned emerald green and roared higher than ever.

metadata.description: I realise the Weasleys think Dudley is a bully and that giving him a Ton-Tongue Toffee was more about punishing a bully than targeting a Muggle.

metadata.description: I feel warmer about the Weasleys: Bill and Charlie greeted me properly and the family laugh made me feel included and less alone.

The tiny kitchen exploded with laughter; Harry looked around and saw that Ron and George were sitting at the scrubbed wooden table with two red-haired people... Bill got to his feet, smiling, and also shook Harry’s hand.

metadata.description: Ginny clearly likes me; when I grinned at her she went scarlet and I've noticed she's been very taken with me since my first visit to the Burrow.
metadata.source_text: Both of them smiled at Harry, who grinned back, which made Ginny go scarlet — she had been very taken with Harry ever since his first visit to the Burrow.

metadata.description: I expect Crookshanks to be out in the garden chasing gnomes; he likes chasing gnomes and he's never seen any before.

metadata.description: I think the arguing between Mr and Mrs Weasley has stopped now, so I'm trying to cover the awkward moment by suggesting they go and help with dinner.

metadata.description: I’m closely involved with helping Sirius escape and I'm as concerned about him as Ron is, so I listen carefully when the subject comes up.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione had been so deeply involved in helping Sirius escape from the Ministry of Magic that they were almost as concerned about Harry’s godfather as he was.

metadata.description: Pigwidgeon won't answer to anything else now because Ginny named him and she thinks the name is sweet, so I've taken to calling him Pig.
metadata.source_text: Ginny named him, he explained to Harry. She reckons it’s sweet. And I tried to change it, but it was too late, he won’t answer to anything else. So now he’s Pig.

metadata.description: Fred and George are up here in our room because Bill and Charlie are in their room, Percy has his room to himself because of work, and I'm sharing beds squeezed into the room.

metadata.description: I learned that Apparating means disappearing from one place and reappearing almost instantly in another — it's difficult and you need to pass a test to do it.
metadata.source_text: Harry knew that Apparating meant disappearing from one place and reappearing almost instantly in another, but had never known any Hogwarts student to do it, and understood that it was very difficult.

metadata.description: I used to think magic like Apparition might be something kids at Hogwarts could do easily, but hearing about Splinching and licences has made me realise it's dangerous and strictly controlled.
metadata.source_text: The Department of Magical Transportation had to fine a couple of people the other day for Apparating without a license. It’s not easy, Apparition, and when it’s not done properly it can lead to nasty complications.
metadata.scene_title: Apparition Risks and Weasley Morning Fuss

metadata.description: I learned that when a Portkey goes off it feels like a hook behind my navel jerking me forward and then everything becomes a howl of wind and colour before I slam down.
metadata.source_text: It happened immediately: Harry felt as though a hook just behind his navel had been suddenly jerked irresistibly forward. metadata.description: I felt even more awkward about being stared at; people still look straight at my scar and talk about me as if I’m some spectacle, and I can't think of anything to say back.
metadata.source_text: Harry was used to people looking curiously at him when they met him, used to the way their eyes moved at once to the lightning scar on his forehead, but it always made him feel uncomfortable.

metadata.description: I noticed Cedric seemed embarrassed and tried to defend me to his father by saying I fell off my broom and it was an accident, so I see that Cedric isn’t as boastful as his dad wants him to be.

metadata.description: I noticed Harry feeling uncomfortable under attention and understood again that other people’s gawking affects him; I feel protective and aware of how the world treats him differently.

metadata.source_text: "Hello there, Arthur," said Basil wearily. "Not on duty, eh? It’s all right for some. . . . We’ve been here all night. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I found out there's a big party coming from the Black Forest at five-fifteen, because Basil warned Mr Weasley to get out of the way for them.
metadata.source_text: "You’d better get out of the way, we’ve got a big party coming in from the Black Forest at five-fifteen."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I learned my family's campsite is about a quarter of a mile's walk in the first field you come to and that the site manager is called Mr Roberts, from Basil's parchment list.
metadata.source_text: "Hang on, I’ll find your campsite. . . . Weasley . . . Weasley . . ." He consulted his parchment list. "About a quarter of a mile’s walk over there, first field you come to. Site manager’s called Mr Roberts."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I suppose I started thinking the Muggle-like rubbish in the Portkey box means wizards toss things in casually; it makes our world feel messier and more ordinary than I thought.
metadata.source_text: "...threw it into a large box of used Portkeys beside him; Harry could see an old newspaper, an empty drinks can, and a punctured football."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I noticed Mr Weasley and Basil talk in a friendly, practical way, so I reckon Mr Weasley is treated like a regular by campsite people and not above asking directions.
metadata.source_text: "Morning, Basil," said Mr Weasley, picking up the boot and handing it to the kilted wizard... "Hello there, Arthur," said Basil wearily.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the exchange between Mr Weasley and Basil at the campsite, so I don't know what Hermione did or said there.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the conversation between Mr Weasley and Basil by the Portkey box, so I can't report anything Ron did during that moment.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Campsite and Directions from Basil

metadata.description: I noticed there were hundreds of tents stretching up the slope toward a dark wood, and I realised the campsite is huge from where we stood by the cottage.
metadata.source_text: Beyond it, Harry could just make out the ghostly shapes of hundreds and hundreds of tents, rising up the gentle slope of a large field toward a dark wood on the horizon.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Correct Field and Heading Across the Moor

metadata.description: I realised the man in the doorway was the only real Muggle for several acres; I don't expect many Muggles around here after seeing him stand alone.
metadata.source_text: Harry knew at a glance that this was the only real Muggle for several acres.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Correct Field and Heading Across the Moor

metadata.description: I watched Mr Weasley speak cheerfully to the Muggle and I felt more certain Mr Weasley knows how to deal with Muggles calmly and politely.
metadata.source_text: “Morning!” said Mr Weasley brightly.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Correct Field and Heading Across the Moor

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the walk across the moor and the meeting at the cottage, so I don't know the moment-to-moment details of those events.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Correct Field and Heading Across the Moor

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the exchange with Mr Roberts at the cottage, so I can't say what I heard or saw there.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Correct Field and Heading Across the Moor

metadata.description: I saw hundreds of pale tents rising up the slope toward a dark wood; the campsite was huge and ghostly through the mist.
metadata.source_text: Harry could just make out the ghostly shapes of hundreds and hundreds of tents, rising up the gentle slope of a large field toward a dark wood on the horizon.
metadata.scene_title: Approach to the Campsite Cottage and Booking

metadata.description: I realised Mr. Weasley is fussy but easily flustered around Muggles — he tries to be bright but he gets muddled with Muggle money.
metadata.source_text: “Ah — right — certainly —” said Mr. Weasley. He retreated a short distance from the cottage and beckoned Harry toward him. “Help me, Harry,” he muttered, pulling a roll of Muggle money from his pocket and starting to peel the notes apart.
metadata.scene_title: Approach to the Campsite Cottage and Booking

metadata.description: I feel a bit protective and useful toward Mr. Weasley in these Muggle dealings; I slip in quietly to correct him when he needs help with notes.
metadata.source_text: “A twenty,” Harry corrected him in an undertone, uncomfortably aware of Mr. Roberts trying to catch every word.
metadata.scene_title: Approach to the Campsite Cottage and Booking

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at the campsite cottage, so I don't have direct observations of the booking or the exchange with Mr. Roberts.
metadata.scene_title: Approach to the Campsite Cottage and Booking

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at the campsite cottage, so I don't have direct observations of the booking or the exchange with Mr. Roberts.
metadata.scene_title: Approach to the Campsite Cottage and Booking

metadata.description: I noticed a man at a stall saying people had tried to pay with huge gold coins the size of hubcaps; that's odd and shows some folks use the wrong kind of money here.
metadata.source_text: I had two try and pay me with great gold coins the size of hubcaps ten minutes ago.
metadata.scene_title: Payment Confusion and Mr Roberts' Observations

metadata.description: I'm thinking now that this place is much busier than usual and a bit chaotic; Mr. Roberts saying "Never been this crowded" makes me believe the crowd explains the confusion over money.
metadata.source_text: Never been this crowded," he said suddenly, looking out over the misty field again. "Hundreds of pre-bookings.
metadata.scene_title: Payment Confusion and Mr Roberts' Observations

metadata.description: I can tell Mr. Roberts sizes people up quickly and he might be a bit suspicious of strangers; his question "You foreign?" shows he's ready to judge someone who struggles with our currency.
metadata.source_text: "You foreign?" said Mr. Roberts as Mr. Weasley returned with the correct notes.
metadata.scene_title: Payment Confusion and Mr Roberts' Observations

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the misty field, so I don't know the exact details of the payment confusion or the exchange between Mr. Weasley and Mr. Roberts.
metadata.scene_title: Payment Confusion and Mr Roberts' Observations

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the busy stall when Mr. Roberts commented about people paying with large gold coins, so I don't have direct knowledge of how the payment was resolved.
metadata.scene_title: Payment Confusion and Mr Roberts' Observations

metadata.description: Blimey, I've learned that Ludo Bagman talks loudly about Bludgers and Quaffles near Muggles, which is really careless for someone in charge of Magical Games and Sports.
metadata.source_text: Trotting around talking about Bludgers and Quaffles at the top of his voice, not a worry about anti-Muggle security.
metadata.scene_title: Memory Charm on Mr Roberts and Gate Escort

metadata.description: Blimey, I reckon Ludo's not as responsible as you'd expect from the Head of the sports department; I'm more worried about security because of how lax he is.
metadata.source_text: I thought Mr Bagman was Head of Magical Games and Sports," said Ginny, looking surprised. "He should know better than to talk about Bludgers near Muggles, shouldn’t he?" "He should," said Mr Weasley, smiling, and leading them through the gates into the campsite, "but Ludo’s always been a bit . . . well . . . lax about security.
metadata.scene_title: Memory Charm on Mr Roberts and Gate Escort

metadata.description: I've updated how I see Mr Weasley: he's worn out and worried, the kind of bloke who mutters about Memory Charms and security — he seems protective and fed up rather than relaxed.
metadata.source_text: He looked exhausted: His chin was blue with stubble and there were deep purple shadows under his eyes. Once out of earshot of Mr Roberts, he muttered to Mr Weasley, “Been having a lot of trouble with him. Needs a Memory Charm ten times a day to keep him happy.
metadata.scene_title: Memory Charm on Mr Roberts and Gate Escort

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the campsite and didn't hear the conversation about Bagman, Memory Charms, or anti-Muggle security.
metadata.scene_title: Memory Charm on Mr Roberts and Gate Escort

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the campsite discussion, so I didn't witness Mr Weasley's complaints about Bagman or the comments about Memory Charms and security.
metadata.scene_title: Memory Charm on Mr Roberts and Gate Escort

metadata.description: I was not present when Whispered Complaints about Bagman and Departure occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Whispered Complaints about Bagman and Departure

metadata.description: I heard snatches of conversation in strange languages coming from the tents, and although I couldn't understand any of the words, I noticed every single voice sounded excited.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught snatches of conversation in strange languages from the inside of tents they passed, and though he couldn’t understand a word, the tone of every single voice was excited.

metadata.description: I realised the campsite was much more decorated and lively than I'd expected; the shamrock-covered tents made the place look like little hillocks and gave a very festive, full-of-color feeling.
metadata.source_text: They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.

metadata.description: I heard Seamus calling our names and saw him sitting with his mother and Dean; it made me feel more connected to the other Gryffindors here, seeing friends relaxing with their families in the campsite.
metadata.source_text: Then, from behind them, they heard their names. "Harry! Ron! Hermione!" It was Seamus Finnigan, their fellow Gryffindor fourth year. He was sitting in front of his own shamrock-covered tent, with a sandy-haired woman who had to be his mother, and his best friend, Dean Thomas, also of Gryffindor.

metadata.description: I've noticed the tents are covered in thick shamrocks so that they resemble small hillocks, and the people inside are speaking different languages with excited tones, even if the words are unintelligible to me.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught snatches of conversation in strange languages from the inside of tents they passed, and though he couldn’t understand a word, the tone of every single voice was excited. ... They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.

metadata.description: I think the campsite decorations are a deliberate display of national pride now; the shamrocks and other national decorations clearly show people want to announce where they're from, despite any Ministry disapproval.
metadata.source_text: "Like the decorations?" said Seamus, grinning. "The Ministry’s not too happy." "Ah, why shouldn’t we show our colors?" said Mrs Finnigan.

metadata.description: Seeing Seamus with his mother and Dean here makes me realise the tournament campsite brings families and friends together, and I feel more aware of the personal side of other students beyond school.
metadata.source_text: It was Seamus Finnigan, their fellow Gryffindor fourth year. He was sitting in front of his own shamrock-covered tent, with a sandy-haired woman who had to be his mother, and his best friend, Dean Thomas, also of Gryffindor.

metadata.description: Blimey, everything really had gone green — the tents were covered in thick shamrocks so much that the ground looked like little hills, not just my eyes playing tricks on me.
metadata.source_text: "Er — is it my eyes, or has everything gone green?" said Ron. ... They had walked into a patch of tents that were all covered with a thick growth of shamrocks, so that it looked as though small, oddly shaped hillocks had sprouted out of the earth.

metadata.description: I reckon the Ministry might be grumpy about the decorations, but I don't see why we shouldn't show our colors — it's grand to be proud and make a right show of where we come from.
metadata.source_text: "Like the decorations?" said Seamus, grinning. "The Ministry’s not too happy." "Ah, why shouldn’t we show our colors?" said Mrs Finnigan.

metadata.description: Seeing Seamus and Dean with Seamus's mum and them calling us over made me feel proper chummy with the other Gryffindors; it's nice to be welcomed so openly at the campsite.
metadata.source_text: "Harry! Ron! Hermione!" It was Seamus Finnigan, their fellow Gryffindor fourth year. He was sitting in front of his own shamrock-covered tent, with a sandy-haired woman who had to be his mother, and his best friend, Dean Thomas, also of Gryffindor.

metadata.description: I spotted a whole patch of Bulgarian tents upfield flying a white, green and red flag and noticed each tent had the same moving poster of a surly face.
metadata.source_text: pointing to a large patch of tents upfield, where the Bulgarian flag — white, green, and red — was fluttering in the breeze. The tents here had not been bedecked with plant life, but each and every one of them had the same poster attached to it, a poster of a very surly face with heavy black eyebrows.

metadata.description: Seeing all those Krums staring out from every tent made me properly realise how big a presence Viktor Krum is; I’m expecting him to be brilliant tonight.
metadata.source_text: He’s unbelievable. He’s really young too. Only just eighteen or something. He’s a genius, you wait until tonight, you’ll see.

metadata.description: I know now that Ron admires Krum a lot and genuinely thinks he’s a genius, which changes how I hear Ron when he talks about top players.
metadata.source_text: “He’s unbelievable. He’s really young too. Only just eighteen or something. He’s a genius, you wait until tonight, you’ll see.”

metadata.description: I noticed that the Bulgarian tents weren’t decorated with plants but all had identical moving posters of a surly face with heavy black eyebrows.
metadata.source_text: The tents here had not been bedecked with plant life, but each and every one of them had the same poster attached to it, a poster of a very surly face with heavy black eyebrows.

metadata.description: When I saw all those Krums blinking and scowling I couldn’t help thinking he really does look grumpy; my opinion shifted from neutral to amused curiosity about his expression.
metadata.source_text: “He looks really grumpy,” said Hermione, looking around at the many Krums blinking and scowling at them.

metadata.description: I reacted with giggles at old Archie’s refusal to wear Muggle trousers, which shows me I’m more easily embarrassed and amused by crude comments than I usually admit.
metadata.source_text: “I’m not putting them on,” said old Archie in indignation. “I like a healthy breeze ’round my privates, thanks.” Hermione was overcome with such a strong fit of the giggles at this point that she had to duck out of the queue and only returned when Archie had collected his water and moved away.

metadata.description: I recognised the picture straight away and said Krum’s name — Viktor Krum, the Bulgarian Seeker — because I know who he is and what he does.
metadata.source_text: “Krum,” said Ron quietly... “Viktor Krum, the Bulgarian Seeker!”

metadata.description: I’m even more convinced than before that Krum is unbelievable and a genius; hearing and seeing those posters just made me prouder to back someone like him.
metadata.source_text: “He’s unbelievable. He’s really young too. Only just eighteen or something. He’s a genius, you wait until tonight, you’ll see.”

metadata.description: I feel that supporting Ireland in public is obvious when we’re surrounded by other fans, and I expect Harry and Hermione to play along — we don’t blurt out anything different when folk are watching.
metadata.source_text: When they had assured her that they were indeed supporting Ireland, they set off again, though, as Ron said, “Like we’d say anything else surrounded by that lot.”

metadata.description: I noticed a large group of teenagers I didn't recognise and realised they probably aren't from Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Who d’you reckon they are? They don’t go to Hogwarts, do they?
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I was a bit embarrassed when Cho waved and I splashed water down my front — I felt awkward and wanted to cover it up so Ron wouldn't smirk.
metadata.source_text: She waved and smiled at Harry, who slopped quite a lot of water down his front as he waved back. More to stop Ron from smirking than anything, Harry hurriedly pointed out a large group of teenagers whom he had never seen before.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I know Oliver Wood well enough for him to drag me over to introduce me to my parents' tent; he's enthusiastic about my Quidditch future and keeps in touch.
metadata.source_text: Oliver Wood... dragged Harry over to his parents’ tent to introduce him, and told him excitedly that he had just been signed to the Puddlemere United reserve team.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I observed that many Hogwarts students were at the campsite with their families and that other schools' students might also be present among the groups.
metadata.source_text: Here and there, they saw more familiar faces: other Hogwarts students with their families.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I realised we're not the only ones around; there are likely pupils from foreign schools visiting too, so the gathering is more international than I first thought.
metadata.source_text: Who d’you reckon they are? They don’t go to Hogwarts, do they?
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I can see Harry's a bit shy or self-conscious when girls like Cho wave at him, which makes me notice how much Ron teases him and how Harry tries to dodge the teasing.
metadata.source_text: She waved and smiled at Harry, who slopped quite a lot of water down his front as he waved back. More to stop Ron from smirking than anything, Harry hurriedly pointed out a large group of teenagers whom he had never seen before.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I reckon those kids belong to some foreign school; I've heard there are pupils from other schools, though I've never met any before.
metadata.source_text: ’Spect they go to some foreign school," said Ron. "I know there are others. Never met anyone who went to one, though.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I remembered my brother Bill once had a penfriend at a school in Brazil and wanted an exchange trip, so I think exchanges are possible even if our folks couldn't afford them.
metadata.source_text: Bill had a penfriend at a school in Brazil . . . this was years and years ago . . . and he wanted to go on an exchange trip but Mum and Dad couldn’t afford it.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I tease Harry when girls like Cho pay attention to him, and his splashing water made me smirk — it shows I can rile him, but it's just friendly ribbing.
metadata.source_text: She waved and smiled at Harry, who slopped quite a lot of water down his front as he waved back. More to stop Ron from smirking than anything, Harry hurriedly pointed out a large group of teenagers whom he had never seen before.
metadata.scene_title: Wandering Among National Tents and Souvenir Shopping

metadata.description: I've just learned what Omnioculars do — you can replay action, slow everything down, and get a play-by-play breakdown while watching matches.
metadata.source_text: "You can replay action . . . slow everything down . . . and they flash up a play-by-play breakdown if you need it."
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I decided I ought to be generous with Ron and Hermione, so I bought three pairs of Omnioculars and gave them to them despite how much they cost.
metadata.source_text: "Three pairs," said Harry firmly to the wizard.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I know Ron gets touchy about money compared to me, so I expect him to feel awkward when I buy expensive things for us all.
metadata.source_text: "No — don't bother," said Ron, going red. He was always touchy about the fact that Harry, who had inherited a small fortune from his parents, had much more money than he did.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I've found out that Harry bought Omnioculars and is giving us one each, and I understand they're useful for watching play-by-play action.
metadata.source_text: "You can replay action . . . slow everything down . . . and they flash up a play-by-play breakdown if you need it."
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I'm grateful to Harry for buying the Omnioculars for us — I feel appreciative and eager to use them, so I thanked him properly.
metadata.source_text: "Oooh, thanks, Harry," said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I see that Harry is generous and willing to spend his money on friends; that makes me feel closer to him and appreciative of his kindness.
metadata.source_text: "You won't be getting anything for Christmas," Harry told him, thrusting Omnioculars into his and Hermione's hands.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I've learned that a penfriend once sent me a cursed hat that made my ears shrivel up — and that left me annoyed and embarrassed.
metadata.source_text: "His penfriend got all offended when he said he wasn’t going and sent him a cursed hat. It made his ears shrivel up."
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I felt sour about my purchases when I saw the Omnioculars and realised I couldn't afford them; I'm jealous of how much Harry can spend.
metadata.source_text: "Wish I hadn’t bought this now," said Ron, gesturing at his dancing shamrock hat and gazing longingly at the Omnioculars.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I know I'm touchy about money compared with Harry, and his buying expensive gifts for us only makes me go red and feel awkward, even if I'm pleased inside.
metadata.source_text: "No — don't bother," said Ron, going red. He was always touchy about the fact that Harry, who had inherited a small fortune from his parents, had much more money than he did.
metadata.scene_title: The Signal to Proceed to the Field

metadata.description: I noticed the Bulgarian minister spotted my scar and started gabbling and pointing at it, so I learned that my scar still draws loud attention from foreign wizards.
metadata.source_text: The Bulgarian wizard suddenly spotted Harry’s scar and started gabbling loudly and excitedly, pointing at it.

metadata.description: I’m reminded again that people will always treat me differently because I’m 'the boy who survived You-Know-Who' — it’s tiring but it’s how they see me.
metadata.source_text: “Harry Potter . . . oh come on now, you know who he is . . . the boy who survived You-Know-Who . . . you do know who he is —”

metadata.description: Seeing Lucius and Draco Malfoy seated near us makes me feel the old hostility all over; I know Draco and I have been enemies since we first went to Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Draco Malfoy had been enemies ever since their very first journey to Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the top box arrival during the Quidditch World Cup, so I don't have direct observations from that moment.
I wasn't present at the top box arrival during the Quidditch World Cup, so I didn't witness the introductions and the tension with the Malfoys firsthand.
I noticed the scoreboard had been wiped clean and now read BULGARIA: 0, IRELAND: 0, so the match was officially starting and the teams were about to be announced.
metadata.source_text: The huge blackboard opposite them was wiped clear of its last message (Bertie Bott’s Every Flavor Beans — A Risk with Every Mouthful!) and now showed BULGARIA: 0, IRELAND: 0.

metadata.description: I found myself completely distracted and mesmerized by the veela; I stopped worrying about anything because their dancing made my mind go blissfully blank.
metadata.source_text: The veela had started to dance, and Harry’s mind had gone completely and blissfully blank.

metadata.description: I know the Malfoys look down on people like Hermione because they're proud of being purebloods; Malfoy's sneer made it clear he thinks Muggle-borns are second-class.
metadata.source_text: The Malfoys prided themselves on being purebloods; in other words, they considered anyone of Muggle descent, like Hermione, second-class.

metadata.description: I saw Mr. Malfoy staring at me and making his lip curl; I know exactly why he behaves like that because he and his family pride themselves on pureblood status.
metadata.source_text: Mr Malfoy’s eyes had returned to Hermione, who went slightly pink, but stared determinedly back at him.

metadata.description: I felt embarrassed and self-conscious when Mr. Malfoy stared at me and I went slightly pink, but I kept staring back determinedly rather than shrinking away.
metadata.source_text: Mr Malfoy’s eyes had returned to Hermione, who went slightly pink, but stared determinedly back at him.

metadata.description: I realized the Malfoys' attitude toward me is openly hostile; their pride in being purebloods makes them treat Muggle-borns like me as inferior.
metadata.source_text: The Malfoys prided themselves on being purebloods; in other words, they considered anyone of Muggle descent, like Hermione, second-class.

metadata.description: I noticed Ludo Bagman burst into the box all excited and shout for everyone to be ready before announcing the Quidditch World Cup final over a Sonorus charm.
metadata.source_text: Next moment, Ludo Bagman charged into the box. 'Everyone ready?' he said... Ludo whipped out his wand, directed it at his own throat, and said 'Sonorus!'

metadata.description: I muttered that Malfoy and his family were 'slimy gits' because I felt angry and disgusted at their sneering, especially when Draco gave us that contemptuous look.
metadata.source_text: Draco shot Harry, Ron, and Hermione one contemptuous look... 'Slimy gits,' Ron muttered as he, Harry, and Hermione turned to face the field again.

metadata.description: I now think worse of Draco and the Malfoys after seeing their sneering behaviour and Draco's contemptuous look at me and my friends; they're arrogant and nasty.
metadata.source_text: Draco shot Harry, Ron, and Hermione one contemptuous look, then settled himself between his mother and father.

metadata.description: I learned that when the veela dance faster I get completely dazed and start having wild, half-formed thoughts — I can even imagine jumping into the stadium without thinking it through.
metadata.source_text: All that mattered in the world was that he kept watching the veela, because if they stopped dancing, terrible things would happen. . . . And as the veela danced faster and faster, wild, half-formed thoughts started chasing through Harry’s dazed mind. He wanted to do something very impressive, right now. Jumping from the box into the stadium seemed a good idea . . . but would it be good enough?
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I suddenly felt like I was with the crowd supporting Bulgaria — I even wondered why I had a large green shamrock pinned to my chest, as if I'd adopted their side without thinking.
metadata.source_text: The crowd didn’t want the veela to go. Harry was with them; he would, of course, be supporting Bulgaria, and he wondered vaguely why he had a large green shamrock pinned to his chest.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I noticed Hermione pulling me back and tutting; she's willing to step in and stop me doing something reckless, which reminded me she keeps me out of trouble even when I'm dazed.
metadata.source_text: Hermione made a loud tutting noise. She reached up and pulled Harry back into his seat. “Honestly!” she said.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I've seen that Harry can be swept up by excitement and nearly act on dazed impulses when captivated — I know to intervene quickly because he might actually try something dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Hermione made a loud tutting noise. She reached up and pulled Harry back into his seat. “Honestly!” she said.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I felt exasperated enough to tut and pull Harry back, which changed how I saw his behavior in that moment — not as daring but as thoughtless and in need of restraint.
metadata.source_text: Hermione made a loud tutting noise. She reached up and pulled Harry back into his seat. “Honestly!” she said.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I acted on the instinct to stop Harry, which confirms for me that I'm responsible enough to check him when he gets carried away, strengthening my role as his sensible friend.
metadata.source_text: Hermione made a loud tutting noise. She reached up and pulled Harry back into his seat. “Honestly!” she said.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I found myself frozen and dazed like I might dive from a springboard, which taught me that the veela's dancing can leave you oddly stunned and off-balance.
metadata.source_text: Next to him, Ron was frozen in an attitude that looked as though he were about to dive from a springboard.
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I started absentmindedly shredding the shamrocks on my hat, and Mr Weasley taking the hat made me realise I might prefer keeping an eye on my things during the spectacle rather than messing about.
metadata.source_text: Ron, meanwhile, was absentmindedly shredding the shamrocks on his hat. Mr Weasley, smiling slightly, leaned over to Ron and tugged the hat out of his hands. “You’ll be wanting that,” he said, “once Ireland have had their say.”
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: Mr Weasley's gentle tugging of my hat showed me he looks out for me in a fatherly way even amid the excitement, which makes me more aware of how he cares for us in public situations.
metadata.source_text: Mr Weasley, smiling slightly, leaned over to Ron and tugged the hat out of his hands. “You’ll be wanting that,” he said, “once Ireland have had their say.”
metadata.scene_title: Veela Enchantment and Harry's Near Leap

metadata.description: I saw a giant shamrock made of thousands of tiny bearded men with red vests, each carrying a tiny lamp, and gold coins started raining down over the crowd.

metadata.source_text: And within ten minutes, Ireland had scored twice more, bringing their lead to thirty–zero ... The match became still faster, but more brutal.

metadata.description: Watching Troy, Mullet and Moran work together made me admire them hugely — they move so as if they can read each other's minds; I respect the Irish Chasers' teamwork and skill now more than before.

metadata.source_text: Wronski Defensive Feint — dangerous Seeker diversion read the shining purple lettering across his lenses.

metadata.source_text: Krum hadn’t seen the Snitch at all, he was just making Lynch copy him.

metadata.description: Seeing Krum’s face so concentrated and deliberate in the replay made me view him as a cunning, tactical player rather than just a fearless diver — I respect his gamesmanship more now.
metadata.source_text: He saw Krum’s face contorted with concentration as he pulled out of the dive just in time, while Lynch was flattened, and he understood — Krum hadn’t seen the Snitch at all, he was just making Lynch copy him.

metadata.description: Using my Omnioculars, I saw Krum circling high above Lynch and noticed his dark eyes darting all over the ground a hundred feet below, looking for the Snitch while Lynch was being revived.

Harry, focusing still more closely upon Krum’s face, saw his dark eyes darting all over the ground a hundred feet below. He was using the time while Lynch was revived to look for the Snitch without interference.

metadata.description: Seeing Lynch get revived and fly off gave me the impression that his recovery could swing the whole match; I felt Ireland’s spirit lift and knew the momentum had changed against Bulgaria.
metadata.source_text: Lynch got to his feet at last, to loud cheers from the green-clad supporters, mounted his Firebolt, and kicked back off into the air. His revival seemed to give Ireland new heart.
metadata.scene_title: Crowd Movement to the Stadium and Stadium Description

metadata.description: After watching fifteen more furious minutes of play, I realised the game had become much rougher and dirtier as Ireland pulled further ahead by ten more goals.

metadata.scene_title: Crowd Movement to the Stadium and Stadium Description

metadata.description: Hearing the crowd scream and the whistle blow when a foul was committed made me see how fiercely the fans backed their team; I felt more aware of how the Irish supporters react to rough play.

metadata.description: Walking through the wood with Mr Weasley and the others, I noticed the atmosphere of feverish excitement — thousands moving, singing, shouting — and I couldn't stop grinning at how infectious it was.
metadata.source_text: Clutching their purchases, Mr Weasley in the lead, they all hurried into the wood, following the lantern-lit trail. They could hear the sounds of thousands of people moving around them, shouts and laughter, snatches of singing. The atmosphere of feverish excitement was highly infectious; Harry couldn’t stop grinning.

metadata.source_text: The rain sounded even louder at the top of the house, accompanied by loud whistlings and moans from the wind, not to mention sporadic howls from the ghoul who lived in the attic.

metadata.description: I told someone to bung Pigwidgeon some Owl Treats, which shows I feel comfortable ordering about a bit when it comes to looking after the owl — he's our responsibility and I expect us to deal with him.
metadata.source_text: “Bung him some Owl Treats,”
