metadata.description: I've seen Hedwig's cage sitting empty and it's been over a week since she's used her perch.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig’s cage stood next to it, still empty. “It’s been over a week,” Harry said, looking at Hedwig’s deserted perch.

metadata.description: I've been given school things from Mum: The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4, new quills, parchment, and potion refills because I was low on spine of lionfish and essence of belladonna.
metadata.source_text: Apart from The Standard Book of Spells, Grade 4, by Miranda Goshawk, he had a handful of new quills, a dozen rolls of parchment, and refills for his potion-making kit — he had been running low on spine of lionfish and essence of belladonna.

metadata.description: I'm a bit reassured that if Sirius had been caught it would have been in the Daily Prophet, so maybe he hasn't been caught after all.

metadata.description: I've noticed Ron and his family's normal, teasing domestic way of treating me like one of their own — Mum packed me things and even washed my socks.
metadata.source_text: “Look, here’s the stuff Mum got for you in Diagon Alley. And she’s got some gold out of your vault for you . . . and she’s washed all your socks.” He heaved a pile of parcels onto Harry’s camp bed and dropped the money bag and a load of socks next to it.

metadata.description: I reckon if Sirius had been caught the Prophet would have printed it — the Ministry would want the credit.

metadata.description: I don't want to wear those dress robes — I'm dead certain I'd rather go starkers than put that on.
metadata.source_text: “I’ll go starkers before I put that on,” said Ron stubbornly.

metadata.description: I'm embarrassed by Mum's notion of clothes for me, and I feel like she doesn't get how awful some things are to wear — I react strongly when she hands me what I think is Ginny's dress.
metadata.source_text: “Mum, you’ve given me Ginny’s new dress,” said Ron, handing it out to her. “Of course I haven’t,” said Mrs. Weasley. “That’s for you. Dress robes.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Burrow bedroom and so I don't know what happened there.

metadata.description: I'm never going to wear those things; I keep saying I will never do it.

metadata.description: I've decided firmly that humiliating clothing is worth refusing no matter what, and I'm not swayed by anyone telling me otherwise.

metadata.description: I reckon Mum will mock me and demand a picture if I refuse, which makes me more determined to resist her orders.

metadata.source_text: There was a funny spluttering noise from behind them. Pigwidgeon was choking on an overlarge Owl Treat.

metadata.description: I feel like everything I own is rubbish right now — I'm properly furious about how useless my things seem to be.
metadata.source_text: “Why is everything I own rubbish?” said Ron furiously, striding

metadata.description: I care enough about Pigwidgeon to react when he chokes, but I'm also so fed up with bad luck that I lump my owl in with all my rubbish possessions.

I heard that Mad-Eye Moody said someone tried to break into his house last night — apparently that's what Mrs. Weasley said.
metadata.source_text: He says someone tried to break into his house last night," said Mrs. Weasley.

metadata.description: I realise Mad-Eye Moody is known as a proper Dark wizard catcher, someone who put half the cells in Azkaban full; that's more serious than I thought.
metadata.source_text: Half the cells in Azkaban are full because of him. He made himself loads of enemies, though . . . the families of people he caught, mainly . . . and I heard he’s been getting really paranoid in his old age.

metadata.description: I now see that the Weasleys, like Bill and Charlie, respect Moody and think highly of him, even if Fred and George joke about him.
metadata.source_text: Your father thinks very highly of Mad-Eye Moody," said Mrs. Weasley sternly."Moody was a great wizard in his time," said Bill.

metadata.description: I learned that Moody used to be an Auror and was a top Dark wizard catcher; Charlie told me he put loads of people in Azkaban.
metadata.source_text: He’s retired, used to work at the Ministry," said Charlie. "I met him once when Dad took me in to work with him. He was an Auror — one of the best . . . a Dark wizard catcher," he added, seeing Harry’s blank look.

metadata.description: I'm starting to think Moody really is a bit mad and paranoid, seeing Dark wizards everywhere, like Charlie said, rather than just being a scary legend.
metadata.source_text: and I heard he’s been getting really paranoid in his old age. Doesn’t trust anyone anymore. Sees Dark wizards everywhere.

metadata.description: I can tell the family take Moody seriously; Mum and Bill treat him with respect even when Fred and George mock him, so I reckon he's important to them.
metadata.source_text: Your father thinks very highly of Mad-Eye Moody," said Mrs. Weasley sternly. "Moody was a great wizard in his time," said Bill.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Weasley conversation about Mad-Eye Moody and the departures; I boarded the train and was talking to Mrs. Weasley as we left.
metadata.source_text: Thanks for having us to stay, Mrs. Weasley," said Hermione as they climbed on board, closed the door, and leaned out of the window to talk to her.

metadata.description: I heard Fred shouting about what’s happening at Hogwarts and asking which rules are changing, so I know people on the train are clamoring for news about Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts!" Fred bellowed out of the window

metadata.description: I got the feeling that folks are more worried or nosy than usual about Hogwarts — everyone’s shouting for details and even asking about rule changes, so things must be stirring up trouble.
metadata.source_text: Tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts!" Fred bellowed out of the window

metadata.description: I noticed Fred’s loudness and impatience; I’m a bit more aware of how loudly he demands news and how that pulls attention, so I see him as someone who’ll shout to get answers.
metadata.source_text: Tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts!" Fred bellowed out of the window

metadata.description: I heard Fred asking what rules are changing at Hogwarts, which tells me people think there are rule changes happening and are eager for specifics.
metadata.source_text: "What rules are they changing?"

metadata.description: I suddenly became convinced we should be quiet and listen carefully rather than join the shouting; someone nearby might have useful information and we could overhear it.
metadata.source_text: "Shh!" Hermione whispered suddenly, pressing her finger to her lips and pointing toward the compartment next to theirs.

metadata.description: I realise I have to be the sensible, quiet one in moments like this — I’ll step in to hush others so we can catch anything important from the neighbouring compartment.
metadata.source_text: "Shh!" Hermione whispered suddenly, pressing her finger to her lips and pointing toward the compartment next to theirs.

metadata.description: I heard Fred bellowing out the window asking what’s happening at Hogwarts and about rule changes, so I know people are desperate for news about the school.
metadata.source_text: Tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts!" Fred bellowed out of the window

metadata.description: I got the impression that Bagman was supposed to tell them something important at the World Cup but didn’t, and that makes me think there’s some gossip or information being kept back — it’s odd.
metadata.source_text: "Bagman wanted to tell us what’s happening at Hogwarts," he said grumpily, sitting down next to Harry. "At the World Cup, remember?"

metadata.description: I’m a bit more suspicious of whoever’s holding back information — if Bagman was meant to tell us and someone’s keeping quiet, I don’t like that secrecy and I’ll notice who’s not talking.
metadata.source_text: "But my own mother won’t say. Wonder what —"

metadata.description: I've learned that Durmstrang is another wizarding school with a reputation for emphasizing the Dark Arts more than Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Durmstrang’s another Wizarding school?
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I think Durmstrang might be way up north because of the fur capes; I wasn't sure where other schools were before, but that sounds likely now.
metadata.source_text: But I think Durmstrang must be somewhere in the far north
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: Hearing Malfoy’s father say he prefers Durmstrang makes me more aware that Malfoy’s family look down on Dumbledore and Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Father actually considered sending me to Durmstrang rather than Hogwarts, you know. He knows the headmaster, you see. Well, you know his opinion of Dumbledore — the man’s such a Mudblood-lover
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I've read that Durmstrang has a horrible reputation and places a lot of emphasis on the Dark Arts, according to An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe.
metadata.source_text: According to An Appraisal of Magical Education in Europe, it puts a lot of emphasis on the Dark Arts.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I now believe Durmstrang is probably hidden the way other schools are — with Unplottable enchantments or Muggle-repelling charms — because magical schools try to conceal their locations.
metadata.source_text: Durmstrang and Beauxbatons like to conceal their whereabouts so nobody can steal their secrets... they’ll have made it Unplottable
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I feel angry about Malfoy and his family’s attitude; I wish Malfoy had gone to Durmstrang so we wouldn’t have to put up with him.
metadata.source_text: So he thinks Durmstrang would have suited him, does he? ... I wish he had gone, then we wouldn’t have to put up with him.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I've picked up that Durmstrang might be hidden like Hogwarts, although I’m not sure how you hide a big castle — it sounds daft but I’m following the idea.
metadata.source_text: Durmstrang’s got to be about the same size as Hogwarts — how are you going to hide a great big castle?
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I'm thinking Durmstrang being in the far north makes sense with those fur capes, so I’m more convinced of Hermione’s guess than I was at first.
metadata.source_text: But I think Durmstrang must be somewhere in the far north
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: Hearing Malfoy’s family talk like that makes me want to do something nasty to Malfoy — I joked about pushing him off a glacier, which shows how much I dislike him.
metadata.source_text: It would’ve been so easy to push Malfoy off a glacier and make it look like an accident. . . . Shame his mother likes him. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy boasts about Durmstrang and Malfoy’s taunts

metadata.description: I heard Malfoy tell us that there’s some contest connected to the Ministry and that people like his father and Cornelius Fudge know about it.
metadata.source_text: My God, my father told me about it ages ago . . . heard it from Cornelius Fudge.

metadata.description: I’m annoyed by Malfoy’s needling — I don’t like him barging in and showing off as if he knows everything; I’m more ready to tell him to go away than before.
metadata.source_text: Don’t remember asking you to join us, Malfoy,

metadata.description: I feel even more distrustful of Malfoy after he came in to mock Ron and parade his connections; he’s the sort who wants to make us feel small.
metadata.source_text: Weasley . . . what is that?

metadata.description: I learned from Malfoy’s words that there is gossip about a Ministry-linked competition and that some people at the Ministry, like Cornelius Fudge, are talking about it.
metadata.source_text: heard it from Cornelius Fudge.

metadata.description: I’m more convinced that Malfoy deliberately tries to wound people by flaunting supposed connections; I think his comments are meant to upset Ron and provoke a reaction.
metadata.source_text: My God, my father told me about it ages ago . . . heard it from Cornelius Fudge. But then, Father’s always associated with the top people at the Ministry.

metadata.description: I’m protective of Ron when he gets angry — I don’t approve of Malfoy attacking him, and I’ll step in to repair the immediate damage, like the broken glass.
metadata.source_text: Ron! said Hermione reproachfully, and she pulled out her wand, muttered “Reparo!”

metadata.description: I found out from Malfoy that there’s supposedly money and glory to be won in a contest the Ministry knows about and that winning could buy decent robes.
metadata.source_text: So . . . going to enter, Weasley? Going to try and bring a bit of glory to the family name? There’s money involved as well, you know . . . you’d be able to afford some decent robes if you won. . . .

metadata.description: I’m angrier and more sensitive about Dad’s position after Malfoy’s sneer — I keep insisting Dad likes his job and wouldn’t want a promotion, because I’m defensive about our family.
metadata.source_text: 'Father’s always associated with the top people at the Ministry.' . . . 'Dad could've got a promotion any time . . . he just likes it where he is.'

metadata.description: I feel humiliated and hostile toward Malfoy for mocking my family and our robes; I’m ready to answer him with anger and even smash things when I’m pushed.
metadata.source_text: Eat dung, Malfoy! said Ron, the same color as the dress robes as he snatched them back out of Malfoy’s grip.

metadata.description: I saw Hagrid’s huge silhouette on the platform and heard him call out to me, so I learned he was waiting for us when the train stopped.
metadata.source_text: Hi, Hagrid!" Harry yelled, seeing a gigantic silhouette at the far end of the platform.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I felt even gloomier about the trip because I was still glowering as the Express slowed and the weather was awful; the storm made everything feel worse.
metadata.source_text: He didn’t talk much as they changed into their school robes, and was still glowering when the Hogwarts Express slowed down at last and finally stopped in the pitch-darkness of Hogsmeade station.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I feel reassured by Hagrid’s presence; hearing him bellow back and wave made me glad he was there to meet us at the station.
metadata.source_text: “All righ’, Harry?” Hagrid bellowed back, waving.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I bundled Crookshanks up in my cloak to keep him dry, so I learned that protecting him from the rain was necessary right away.
metadata.source_text: Hermione bundled up Crookshanks in her cloak
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I don’t think crossing the lake would be sensible tonight; after feeling the cold and seeing the storm I became convinced we shouldn’t cross in that weather.
metadata.source_text: “Oooh, I wouldn’t fancy crossing the lake in this weather,” said Hermione fervently, shivering
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I rely on my friends during upsetting situations; moving along the platform together and getting into a carriage with Harry and Ron made me feel we’re a team in bad weather.
metadata.source_text: the dark platform with the rest of the crowd. A hundred horseless carriages stood waiting for them outside the station. Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Neville climbed gratefully into one of them
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I put my dress robes over Pigwidgeon to stop him from getting soaked, so I learned that the bird needed covering in this downpour.
metadata.source_text: Ron left his dress robes over Pigwidgeon as they left the train
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I reckon the weather’s bad enough to make Hagrid joke about us drowning; after hearing him I believed the storm was really severe and not to be taken lightly.
metadata.source_text: “See yeh at the feast if we don’ drown!”
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I feel comfortable joking and bantering with Hagrid and the others in awkward situations; sharing the carriage and watching out for each other made me feel closer to them.
metadata.source_text: Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Neville climbed gratefully into one of them, the door shut with a snap
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogsmeade in a storm and carriage to Hogwarts

metadata.description: I'm looking forward to seeing the Sorting again because I haven't been to one since my own; I'm expecting the new first years to be divided into Houses at the start-of-term feast.
metadata.source_text: The Sorting of the new students into Houses took place at the start of every school year, but by an unlucky combination of circumstances, Harry hadn’t been present at one since his own. He was quite looking forward to it.

metadata.description: I've noticed there are more empty seats at the staff table than normal and that there doesn't seem to be a new face for Defense Against the Dark Arts.
metadata.source_text: There seemed to be rather more empty seats there than usual... There was definitely no new face there.

metadata.description: I supposed brothers and sisters usually go in the same Houses because of the Weasleys, but Hermione pointed out that's not always true, so I'm less sure siblings end up together.
metadata.source_text: Brothers and sisters usually go in the same Houses, don’t they?... “Oh no, not necessarily,” said Hermione. “Parvati Patil’s twin’s in Ravenclaw, and they’re identical.

metadata.description: I still dislike Snape a lot; my feeling about him hasn't improved — in fact, last year's events made his hatred of me feel stronger and more personal.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s loathing of Snape was matched only by Snape’s hatred of him, a hatred which had, if possible, intensified last year, when Harry had helped Sirius escape right under Snape’s overlarge nose

metadata.description: I know that siblings don't always get sorted into the same House; Parvati Patil's twin is in Ravenclaw despite being identical.
metadata.source_text: “Oh no, not necessarily,” said Hermione. “Parvati Patil’s twin’s in Ravenclaw, and they’re identical.

metadata.description: I'm worried there might not be a new Defence Against the Dark Arts teacher this year, because we've never had one last more than three terms and I can't see a new face at the staff table.
metadata.source_text: Where’s the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher?” said Hermione... “There was definitely no new face there.

metadata.description: I'm more anxious about staff coverage for Defence Against the Dark Arts; the absence of a new teacher made me think they might not have found anyone.
metadata.source_text: “Maybe they couldn’t get anyone!” said Hermione, looking anxious.

metadata.description: I remain observant about Hogwarts' staff and seating; noticing who is missing or present helps me understand where people are and what's happening.
metadata.source_text: They had never yet had a Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher who had lasted more than three terms.

metadata.description: I'm starving and can't wait for the food at the feast — I even joked I could eat a hippogriff because I'm that hungry.
metadata.source_text: “Oh hurry up,” Ron moaned, beside Harry, “I could eat a hippogriff.”

metadata.description: I'm annoyed at being drenched and mutter under my breath while wiping sopping hair from my face after Peeves' water bombs soaked us in the entrance hall.
metadata.source_text: Ron muttering furiously under his breath as he pushed his sopping hair off his face.

metadata.description: Seeing the soaked first years coming in made me feel a bit sympathetic and reminded me how frightening the start at Hogwarts can be for the littler pupils.
metadata.source_text: If Harry, Ron, and Hermione were wet, it was nothing to how these first years looked. They appeared to have swum across the lake rather than sailed.

metadata.description: I'm friendly with people like Colin Creevey and share the excitement around new students arriving; the scene makes me feel part of the Gryffindor crowd gathered for the Feast.
metadata.source_text: Just then, a highly excited, breathless voice called down the table. “Hiya, Harry!” It was Colin Creevey

metadata.description: I saw the Sorting Hat shout out which House each new student belonged to and watched Stewart Ackerley go to Ravenclaw and Malcolm Baddock go to Slytherin.
metadata.source_text: “RAVENCLAW!” shouted the hat. Stewart Ackerley took off the hat and hurried into a seat at the Ravenclaw table, where everyone was applauding him. ... “SLYTHERIN!” The table on the other side of the hall erupted with cheers; Harry could see Malfoy clapping as Baddock joined the Slytherins.

metadata.description: I noticed Dennis Creevey got sorted into Gryffindor after tumbling forward, and he was thrilled about being thrown into the lake and tossed back by something in the water.
metadata.source_text: The rip at the brim opened wide — “GRYFFINDOR!” the hat shouted. ... “Colin, I fell in!” he said shrilly, throwing himself into an empty seat. “It was brilliant! And something in the water grabbed me and pushed me back in the boat!”

metadata.description: For a fleeting second, I wanted to join the Ravenclaw table too; I actually felt tempted by their side for a moment, which surprised me.
metadata.source_text: Harry caught a glimpse of Cho, the Ravenclaw Seeker, cheering Stewart Ackerley as he sat down. For a fleeting second, Harry had a strange desire to join the Ravenclaw table too.

metadata.description: I noticed Hagrid wink at us and I remembered he looks alarming but is really kind; it made me feel more comfortable seeing him sit with the staff.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid ... looked slightly alarming — a misleading impression, for Harry, Ron, and Hermione knew Hagrid to possess a very kind nature. He winked at them as he sat down at the end of the staff table

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events of this scene and did not witness the conversation or actions described.
I've just learned that Hogwarts has a large number of house-elves working in the kitchens—over a hundred, apparently—and they usually stay out of sight by day.
metadata.source_text: “The largest number in any dwelling in Britain, I believe. Over a hundred.”

metadata.description: I am shocked to discover house-elves are at Hogwarts because I had never seen one before; I didn't expect so many to be employed here.
metadata.source_text: “I’ve never seen one!” said Hermione. “Well, they hardly ever leave the kitchen by day, do they?” said Nearly Headless Nick.

metadata.description: Hearing Nearly Headless Nick describe the ghosts' council about Peeves made me realize even the staff and ghosts try to manage troublesome school elements; I respect their efforts more.
metadata.source_text: “We held a ghost’s council — the Fat Friar was all for giving him the chance — but most wisely, in my opinion, the Bloody Baron put his foot down.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events of this scene and did not witness the conversation or actions described.
I learned that the Sorting takes ages and that Gryffindor's been winning the Inter-House Championship for the last three years, so there's pressure on the new lot to be good.
metadata.source_text: “I do hope this year’s batch of Gryffindors are up to scratch,” said Nearly Headless Nick, applauding as “McDonald, Natalie!” joined the Gryffindor table. “We don’t want to break our winning streak, do we?” Gryffindor had won the Inter-House Championship for the last three years in a row.

metadata.description: I was annoyed and hungry and thought the Sorting was taking too long—I care more about getting my food at that moment than the ceremony, apparently.
metadata.source_text: “Oh hurry up,” Ron moaned, massaging his stomach. ... “About time,” said Ron, seizing his knife and fork and looking expectantly at his golden plate.

metadata.description: Hearing the ghosts argue about Peeves and the Bloody Baron's influence made me think the ghostly residents take their rules seriously; I trust their judgment a bit more now.
metadata.source_text: “The Fat Friar was all for giving him the chance — but most wisely, in my opinion, the Bloody Baron put his foot down.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events of this scene and did not witness the conversation or actions described.
I heard Dumbledore say Hogwarts will host the Triwizard Tournament and that champions from three schools will be chosen to compete in dangerous tasks.
metadata.source_text: It is my very great pleasure to inform you that the Triwizard Tournament will be taking place at Hogwarts this year.

metadata.description: I was surprised and more excited than worried about the Tournament; hearing about the tasks made me interested rather than frightened by the old deaths.
metadata.source_text: Harry himself was far more interested in hearing about the tournament than in worrying about deaths that had happened hundreds of years ago.

metadata.description: Seeing Fred and George so determined and scheming about entering even though they aren’t of age showed me how reckless and thrill-seeking they are.
metadata.source_text: “I’m going for it!” Fred Weasley hissed down the table, his face lit with enthusiasm at the prospect of such glory and riches.

metadata.description: I've learned from Dumbledore that only students aged seventeen or older may put their names forward for the Triwizard Tournament this year.
metadata.source_text: Only students who are of age — that is to say, seventeen years or older — will be allowed to put forward their names for consideration.

metadata.description: I feel worried about the Tournament’s danger because Dumbledore mentioned a high death toll in the past; that made me anxious despite other students’ excitement.
metadata.source_text: “Death toll?” Hermione whispered, looking alarmed.

metadata.description: Watching Fred and George joke about fooling the judge and taking risks makes me think they don't take safety seriously, which worries me about their influence.
metadata.source_text: “I reckon a couple of drops of Aging Potion might do it, George. . . .”

metadata.description: I learned that only seventh-year-aged students can enter the Triwizard Tournament and that an impartial judge will select the champions at Halloween.
metadata.source_text: The selection of the three champions will take place at Halloween. An impartial judge will decide which students are most worthy to compete for the Triwizard Cup...

metadata.description: Hearing about the thousand Galleons and the glory made me daydream about entering even though I know we might not be ready and might be stopped for being underage.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah,” said Ron, a faraway look on his face. “Yeah, a thousand Galleons . . .”

metadata.description: Seeing Fred and George so fired up about cheating Dumbledore to enter makes me feel tempted and excited by the idea, even though I'm not fully sure it's sensible.
metadata.source_text: “Dumbledore knows you’re not of age, though,” said Ron. “Yeah, but he’s not the one who decides who the champion is, is he?” said Fred shrewdly.

metadata.description: I found that my astrological chart as we worked on it seemed wrong — I can see "two Neptunes" on my parchment and that doesn't make sense to me.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve got two Neptunes here," said Harry after a while, frowning down at his piece of parchment, "that can’t be right, can it?"

metadata.description: I still reckon Professor Trelawney is mostly an old fraud with spooky mannerisms, though I can't shake that once she gave a genuine trance about Voldemort which Dumbledore thought was real.
metadata.source_text: Hermione was right, Harry thought irritably, Professor Trelawney really was an old fraud. ... Except, of course, for that time at the end of last term, when she had made the prediction about Voldemort rising again . . . and Dumbledore himself had said that he thought that trance had been genuine, when Harry had described it to him.

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and a bit mocked when Ron rolls his eyes at me after Trelawney's doom-laden line; Ron's teasing makes me look stonily back at him.
metadata.source_text: Her voice dropped almost to a whisper. Ron rolled his eyes at Harry, who looked stonily back.

metadata.description: I said that Professor Trelawney is likely a fraud and dismiss her methods, because I know better than to be carried away by spooky mannerisms and lucky guesses.
metadata.source_text: But Hermione was right, Harry thought irritably, Professor Trelawney really was an old fraud.

metadata.description: I might accept that Trelawney can be a fraud in general, yet I'm aware there was an exception when her trance about Voldemort seemed genuine, as Dumbledore confirmed.
metadata.source_text: Except, of course, for that time at the end of last term, when she had made the prediction about Voldemort rising again . . . and Dumbledore himself had said that he thought that trance had been genuine, when Harry had described it to him.

metadata.description: I feel skeptical of Trelawney's authority and style, which distances me from taking her proclamations at face value.
metadata.source_text: But Hermione was right, Harry thought irritably, Professor Trelawney really was an old fraud.

metadata.description: I mocked Trelawney in a daft whisper about two Neptunes meaning a midget in glasses will be born — I was teasing Harry and the whole mystical mood.
metadata.source_text: "Aaaaah," said Ron, imitating Professor Trelawney’s mystical whisper, "when two Neptunes appear in the sky, it is a sure sign that a midget in glasses is being born, Harry. . . ."

metadata.description: I clearly don't take Divination seriously and I enjoy poking fun at Trelawney's dramatic predictions, which shows I'm dismissive of her methods.
metadata.source_text: Ron rolled his eyes at Harry, who looked stonily back.

metadata.description: I feel comfortable ribbing Harry in front of the class; my eye-rolling and mockery show I'm relaxed about his reactions and not especially sympathetic.
metadata.source_text: Her voice dropped almost to a whisper. Ron rolled his eyes at Harry, who looked stonily back.

metadata.description: I heard Malfoy reading that Arnold Weasley had been involved in a public tussle with Muggle policemen and had to modify memories before escaping.
metadata.source_text: Arnold Weasley, who was charged with possession of a flying car two years ago, was yesterday involved in a tussle with several Muggle law-keepers ("policemen") over a number of highly aggressive dustbins. Mr. Weasley was forced to modify several memories before he could escape from the policemen

metadata.description: Hearing Malfoy sneer about Ron's parents made me more protective and angrier at Malfoy than before — I won't stand by while he humiliates my mate.
metadata.source_text: Get stuffed, Malfoy," said Harry. "C’mon, Ron. . . .

metadata.description: I came to feel even closer to Ron and Hermione in that instant; I grabbed Ron's robes with Hermione to stop him attacking Malfoy because mates stick together.
metadata.source_text: both he and Hermione had grabbed the back of Ron’s robes to stop him from launching himself at Malfoy

metadata.description: I've learned from Ron that Professor Trelawney heard him asking to see Uranus, and as a result she set a big homework assignment on planetary movements.
metadata.source_text: Can I have a look at Uranus too, Lavender? ... Most unfortunately, Professor Trelawney heard him, and it was this ... that made her give them so much homework

metadata.description: Seeing Malfoy openly mock the Weasleys made me more annoyed with him; his behaviour is deliberately cruel and designed to humiliate people publicly.
metadata.source_text: Your dad’s in the paper, Weasley! ... "And there’s a picture, Weasley!" said Malfoy, flipping the paper over and holding it up. "A picture of your parents outside their house — if you can call it a house! Your mother could do with losing a bit of weight, couldn’t she?"

metadata.description: I reflexively reached for Ron and helped hold him back when Malfoy taunted his family; I'm willing to physically back up my friends when they're being attacked.
metadata.source_text: both he and Hermione had grabbed the back of Ron’s robes to stop him from launching himself at Malfoy

metadata.description: I found out my dad gets written up in the Daily Prophet for making a fuss at Mad-Eye Moody's and getting in trouble with Muggle policemen — and they even printed our picture.
metadata.source_text: Your dad’s in the paper, Weasley!... Arnold Weasley, who was charged with possession of a flying car two years ago, was yesterday involved in a tussle with several Muggle law-keepers ... "And there’s a picture, Weasley!" said Malfoy, flipping the paper over and holding it up.

metadata.description: After Malfoy's nasty taunts about Mum and Dad I felt furious and humiliated; I don't see why they'd mock my family in front of everyone.
metadata.source_text: "Your mother could do with losing a bit of weight, couldn’t she?" ... Ron was shaking with fury.

metadata.description: Malfoy showed himself to be a proper bully by making fun of my parents publicly; I dislike him even more and feel more defensive of my family now.
metadata.source_text: Imagine them not even getting his name right, Weasley. It’s almost as though he’s a complete nonentity, isn’t it?" he crowed.

metadata.description: I saw Professor Moody yank a wand on a white ferret and bounce it around because someone attacked when their opponent's back was turned.
metadata.source_text: I don’t think so!" roared Moody, pointing his wand at the ferret again — it flew ten feet into the air, fell with a smack to the floor, and then bounced upward once more. "I don’t like people who attack when their opponent’s back’s turned," growled Moody as the ferret bounced higher and higher, squealing in pain.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that Moody is dangerous but effective — he won't tolerate cowardly attacks and watches closely for trouble.
metadata.source_text: Well, I know your father of old, boy. . . . You tell him Moody’s keeping a close eye on his son . . . you tell him that from me. . . . Now, your Head of House’ll be Snape, will it?

metadata.description: I feel a new respect and a bit of wariness toward Moody; he clearly means business and isn't above rough methods.
metadata.source_text: "He knows, man," said Lee. "Knows what it's like to be out there doing it," said George impressively.

metadata.description: I noticed that Professor McGonagall stopped Moody before he could do more harm and that Transfiguration was used on Draco as punishment.
metadata.source_text: "Moody, we never use Transfiguration as a punishment!" said Professor McGonagall weakly.

metadata.description: I'm disturbed by how dangerous Moody's methods looked; even if Malfoy deserved punishment, that ferret could have been seriously hurt.
metadata.source_text: "He could have really hurt Malfoy, though," she said. "It was good, really, that Professor McGonagall stopped it —"

metadata.description: I trust Professor McGonagall to intervene and do what's appropriate; she acted quickly to restore Malfoy and object to Moody's punishment.
metadata.source_text: "No!" cried Professor McGonagall, running down the stairs and pulling out her wand; a moment later, with a loud snapping noise, Draco Malfoy had reappeared, lying in a heap on the floor...

metadata.description: I will remember Draco Malfoy forever as the amazing bouncing ferret — that picture is fixed in my memory.
metadata.source_text: "Because I want to fix that in my memory forever," said Ron, his eyes closed and an uplifted expression on his face. "Draco Malfoy, the amazing bouncing ferret . . ."

metadata.description: I'm adamant that that moment should stay brilliant and untouched — I don't want anyone spoiling the joke by being sensible about it.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione!" said Ron furiously, his eyes snapping open again, "you're ruining the best moment of my life!"

metadata.description: I think Moody is completely awesome now — someone who's been out fighting knows his stuff and is totally cool in my book.
metadata.source_text: "Moody!" he said. "How cool is he?" "Beyond cool," said George.

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Moody says we've been taught about boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves already.
metadata.source_text: Seems you’ve had a pretty thorough grounding in tackling Dark creatures — you’ve covered boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves, is that right?
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I didn't expect to be taught illegal Dark curses now, but Moody says Dumbledore thinks I can cope and that we'll be shown more than the Ministry usually allows, so I'm more prepared for hard stuff sooner.
metadata.source_text: I’m not supposed to show you what illegal Dark curses look like until you’re in the sixth year. You’re not supposed to be old enough to deal with it till then. But Professor Dumbledore’s got a higher opinion of your nerves, he reckons you can cope, and I say, the sooner you know what you’re up against, the better.
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I noticed Moody can smile and that, even when his face looks worse for it, he can be friendly — that made me feel a bit safer about him teaching us.
metadata.source_text: Moody’s magical eye spun around to stare at Ron; Ron looked extremely apprehensive, but after a moment Moody smiled — the first time Harry had seen him do so.
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I've learned from Moody that the class has already covered a list of Dark creatures: boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves.
metadata.source_text: Seems you’ve had a pretty thorough grounding in tackling Dark creatures — you’ve covered boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves, is that right?
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I previously assumed we wouldn't be shown illegal Dark curses until the sixth year, but Moody says Dumbledore believes our nerves can manage earlier instruction, so I accept we'll be taught more advanced material now.
metadata.source_text: I’m not supposed to show you what illegal Dark curses look like until you’re in the sixth year. You’re not supposed to be old enough to deal with it till then. But Professor Dumbledore’s got a higher opinion of your nerves, he reckons you can cope, and I say, the sooner you know what you’re up against, the better.
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I observed Moody address Ron as Arthur Weasley’s son and saw Moody smile; that changes my view of him slightly — he isn't just menace and severity, he can be civil and has loyalties to others like Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: You’ll be Arthur Weasley’s son, eh? ... Yeah, I’m staying just the one year. Special favor to Dumbledore. . . . One year, and then back to my quiet retirement.
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I heard Moody say we’ve covered creatures like boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves already.
metadata.source_text: Seems you’ve had a pretty thorough grounding in tackling Dark creatures — you’ve covered boggarts, Red Caps, hinkypunks, grindylows, Kappas, and werewolves, is that right?
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I blurted out asking if Moody was staying because I was worried; when he said he was staying one year as a favor to Dumbledore, I felt a huge relief and less terrified about his lessons.
metadata.source_text: What, aren’t you staying? ... Yeah, I’m staying just the one year. Special favor to Dumbledore. . . . One year, and then back to my quiet retirement.
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I realized Moody knows my dad, Arthur Weasley, and because Moody said Dad got him out of a tight corner, I feel better about Moody — he’s not just scary, he owes Dad a favor.
metadata.source_text: You’ll be Arthur Weasley’s son, eh? Your father got me out of a very tight corner a few days ago. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Moody Addresses the Class and Declares His Curriculum

metadata.description: I've learned that the Imperius Curse can make a victim move and act entirely under another's control, even forcing them to do humiliating or dangerous things.
metadata.source_text: I could make it jump out of the window, drown itself, throw itself down one of your throats . . .

metadata.description: I now believe being watchful and prepared is vital because a wizard about to curse you won't warn you; you have to expect attacks and be constantly vigilant.
metadata.source_text: How are you supposed to defend yourself against something you’ve never seen? ... You need to be prepared. You need to be alert and watchful.

metadata.description: Seeing Moody's methods and how he shows the curses makes me realize I respect his seriousness and ability to teach us harsh realities, even if his style is frightening.
metadata.source_text: CONSTANT VIGILANCE!

metadata.description: I've learned that the Cruciatus Curse causes unbearable pain and visible convulsions even in an animal; it can be used to torture and is one of the most serious illegal spells.
metadata.source_text: The Cruciatus Curse ... 'Crucio!' ... the spider’s legs bent in upon its body; it rolled over and began to twitch horribly

metadata.description: I now feel that some demonstrations, though educational, can cross a line; seeing real effects on a creature made me shout to stop it because the pain was unacceptable.
metadata.source_text: Stop it!" Hermione said shrilly.

metadata.description: Watching Neville's reaction and the class responses makes me see how much fear and sensitivity some classmates have; I feel more protective toward them in lessons like this.
metadata.source_text: She was looking, not at the spider, but at Neville, and ... Neville’s hands were clenched upon the desk ... his eyes wide and horrified.

metadata.description: My dad told me about the Imperius Curse, and now I see exactly how it can control someone; it's dangerous and was a big problem for the Ministry back when Voldemort was powerful.
metadata.source_text: Er, my dad told me about one. . . . Is it called the Imperius Curse, or something?" ... "Gave the Ministry a lot of trouble at one time, the Imperius Curse.

metadata.description: I feel properly creeped out and worried now—seeing a spider forced to do things makes me shudder and want to keep as far away as possible from those curses.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt Ron recoil slightly next to him — Ron hated spiders.

metadata.description: Watching Moody treat the class so severely makes me think he isn't like other teachers; he commands fear and respect, and I reckon he's someone to listen to when it comes to dark magic.
metadata.source_text: CONSTANT VIGILANCE!

metadata.description: I learned what Avada Kedavra actually does: a flash of green light and an instant, unmarked death — no bruise, no wound, just life ended immediately.
metadata.source_text: "Avada Kedavra!" Moody roared. There was a flash of blinding green light and a rushing sound, as though a vast, invisible something was soaring through the air — instantaneously the spider rolled over onto its back, unmarked, but unmistakably dead.

metadata.description: I keep thinking about my parents’ deaths differently now — seeing the green flash and the rushing sound makes me picture their last moments exactly like the spider, and that fills me with a new, colder certainty about how they died.
metadata.source_text: So that was how his parents had died . . . exactly like that spider. Had they been unblemished and unmarked too? Had they simply seen the flash of green light and heard the rush of speeding death, before life was wiped from their bodies?

metadata.description: I felt exposed when Moody said only one person survived the curse and then looked directly at me — it made me aware that everyone else was looking at me too, and I suddenly felt very singled out in front of my classmates.
metadata.source_text: "Only one known person has ever survived it, and he’s sitting right in front of me." Harry felt his face redden as Moody’s eyes (both of them) looked into his own. He could feel everyone else looking around at him too.

metadata.description: I've learned the name and nature of the worst Unforgivable Curse: Avada Kedavra is the Killing Curse — it kills instantly and there is no countercurse.
metadata.source_text: "Avada Kedavra," Hermione whispered. ... "Ah," said Moody, another slight smile twisting his lopsided mouth. "Yes, the last and worst. Avada Kedavra . . . the Killing Curse."

metadata.description: I was shaken when I raised my hand and said the words quietly — I realise saying the name of such a thing makes it feel horribly real and frightening, even though I thought knowing it was necessary.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s hand shook slightly as, for the third time, she raised it into the air. "Yes?" said Moody, looking at her. "Avada Kedavra," Hermione whispered.

metadata.description: I noticed others looked uneasy when I whispered Avada Kedavra — I can tell my classmates reacted to me saying the name; it made me aware that my straightforwardness can make people uncomfortable.
metadata.source_text: Several people looked uneasily around at her, including Ron. "Ah," said Moody, another slight smile twisting his lopsided mouth.

metadata.description: I saw what Avada Kedavra does: the curse produces a blinding green light and a rushing sound, and kills instantly — the spider was dead without a mark.
metadata.source_text: Moody raised his wand, and Harry felt a sudden thrill of foreboding. "Avada Kedavra!" Moody roared. There was a flash of blinding green light and a rushing sound... the spider rolled over onto its back, unmarked, but unmistakably dead.

metadata.description: Seeing the Killing Curse in action changed how frightened I am of those curses — after the spider, I realise how terrifying they are and how dangerous people who use them must be.
metadata.source_text: "Not nice," he said calmly. "Not pleasant. And there’s no countercurse. There’s no blocking it."

metadata.description: I felt startled and protective during the demonstration — I nearly toppled out of my seat when the spider slid toward me, which made me realise how close danger feels even in class.
metadata.source_text: Several of the students stifled cries; Ron had thrown himself backward and almost toppled off his seat as the spider skidded toward him.

metadata.description: I've just learned from a hurried letter that Dumbledore is flying north and keeping an eye on strange rumors about my scar; if the scar hurts again I must go straight to Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: Harry — I’m flying north immediately. This news about your scar is the latest in a series of strange rumors that have reached me here. If it hurts again, go straight to Dumbledore — they’re saying he’s got Mad-Eye out of retirement, which means he’s reading the signs, even if no one else is.
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I reckon telling Dumbledore something might make him think he has to come back; I feel guilty because I think I made him decide to return even though there’s nothing actually wrong with me.
metadata.source_text: I shouldn’t’ve told him! ... It’s made him think he’s got to come back!
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I see Fred and George acting oddly secretive and serious about a parchment now; they're not just jokers tonight — they’re careful and worried about wording, which makes me think they’re handling something delicate.
metadata.source_text: There was something secretive about the way they were working on the piece of parchment... George shook his head at Fred, scratched out something with his quill, and said, in a very quiet voice... 'No — that sounds like we’re accusing him. Got to be careful . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I've noticed Neville is in a very distressed, babbling state after the lesson; he’s speaking in an unnaturally high voice and seems terrified where he previously reacted badly to the Cruciatus demonstration.
metadata.source_text: Neville was standing alone, halfway up the passage, staring at the stone wall... 'Neville?' Hermione said gently. Neville looked around. 'Oh hello,' he said, his voice much higher than usual.
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I feel more convinced that Professor Moody takes a rough, immediate approach and yet can be gentle when needed; he soothed Neville with tea and books despite his frightening demonstrations.
metadata.source_text: It’s all right, sonny,' he said to Neville. 'Why don’t you come up to my office? Come on . . . we can have a cup of tea. . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I’m concerned for Neville and feel a protective, sympathetic pull toward him; seeing him terrified makes me want to help him even if he’s embarrassed.
metadata.source_text: Neville looked pleadingly at Harry, Ron, and Hermione, but they didn’t say anything, so Neville had no choice but to allow himself to be steered away...
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I worked out that making up dire Divination predictions is an easy trick — you just pile on unlucky planets and misery and people will lap it up, so I started writing awful forecasts for the week.
metadata.source_text: I think it’s back to the old Divination standby... 'Next Monday,' he said as he scribbled, 'I am likely to develop a cough, owing to the unlucky conjunction of Mars and Jupiter.'
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I reckon Moody and Dumbledore probably would be in trouble with the Ministry if they’d shown the curses, but I’ve also decided Dumbledore does things his way and Moody’s always been a bit lawless, so I’m not that worried.
metadata.source_text: Wouldn’t Moody and Dumbledore be in trouble with the Ministry if they knew we’d seen the curses?... 'But Dumbledore’s always done things his way, hasn’t he, and Moody’s been getting in trouble for years, I reckon.'
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I noticed Neville acting weird and I’m worried for him, but I also trust Moody to handle him; seeing Moody speak gently made me think Moody isn't just about roughness — he can look after pupils too.
metadata.source_text: All four of them fell silent, watching him apprehensively, but when he spoke, it was in a much lower and gentler growl than they had yet heard. 'It’s all right, sonny,' he said to Neville.
metadata.scene_title: Hallway Talk, Neville’s Distress, and Return to Gryffindor Common Room

metadata.description: I learned what the Imperius Curse actually feels like when Moody put it on me — a floating, empty sort of happiness where every worry and thought just goes away.
metadata.source_text: It was the most wonderful feeling. Harry felt a floating sensation as every thought and worry in his head was wiped gently away, leaving nothing but a vague, untraceable happiness.

metadata.description: I realised I'm not completely helpless under the Imperius Curse — another voice in my head could argue back and I could partly resist the command even while the curse made me obedient.
metadata.source_text: No, I don’t think I will, thanks, said the other voice, a little more firmly . . . no, I don’t really want to. . . .

metadata.description: I see Moody as a harsh but effective teacher — he deliberately subjects us to real danger to make a point, and he doesn't flinch when it causes harm to teach us.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore wants you taught what it feels like,” said Moody, his magical eye swiveling onto Hermione... “If you’d rather learn the hard way — when someone’s putting it on you so they can control you completely — fine by me.

metadata.description: I've learned that Moody is prepared to use the Imperius Curse on students in class because Dumbledore wants them to be taught what it feels like, even though I know using it on humans is illegal.
metadata.source_text: “Dumbledore wants you taught what it feels like,” said Moody, his magical eye swiveling onto Hermione and fixing her with an eerie, unblinking stare.

metadata.description: I felt conflicted and uneasy — I still think using the Imperius Curse on another person is wrong and illegal, but I understand that Dumbledore believes there's value in learning its effects firsthand.
metadata.source_text: “But — but you said it’s illegal, Professor,” said Hermione uncertainly... “Dumbledore wants you taught what it feels like,” said Moody...

metadata.description: I sense Moody is unlike typical professors; his methods are alarming and morally troubling to me, which makes me more cautious of his approach even as I grudgingly accept the lesson's purpose.
metadata.source_text: “If you’d rather learn the hard way — when someone’s putting it on you so they can control you completely — fine by me. You’re excused. Off you go.” He pointed one gnarled finger toward the door.

metadata.description: I saw Moody put people under the Imperius Curse and make them do daft things — Dean hopping and singing, Lavender acting like a squirrel, Neville doing unbelievable gymnastics — and none could break free.
metadata.source_text: Harry watched as, one by one, his classmates did the most extraordinary things under its influence. Dean Thomas hopped three times around the room, singing the national anthem. Lavender Brown imitated a squirrel. Neville performed a series of quite astonishing gymnastics...

metadata.description: I'm now convinced the Imperius Curse is terrifyingly powerful and that learning about it in class is necessary, even if Moody's methods are extreme — you can't rely on everyone to resist it.
metadata.source_text: Not one of them seemed to be able to fight off the curse, and each of them recovered only when Moody had removed it.

metadata.description: I trust Moody to be blunt and no-nonsense as a teacher; he doesn't sugarcoat dangers and expects us to learn by facing them, which makes me see him as more of a tough guardian than a gentle instructor.
metadata.source_text: “Potter,” Moody growled, “you next.” ... Moody raised his wand, pointed it at Harry, and said, “Imperio!”

metadata.description: I learned that Moody thinks watching someone's eyes will show when they're affected; he kept telling everyone to watch my eyes to see the curse.
metadata.source_text: watch his eyes, that’s where you see it
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I used to just take lessons as lessons, but after Moody put me through it four times, I believe he really will push you until you can shake something off completely.
metadata.source_text: Moody had insisted on putting Harry through his paces four times in a row, until Harry could throw off the curse entirely
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I feel like Moody is watching me closely and praising me in front of everyone, which makes me the focus of the class and shows he thinks I can handle more than the others.
metadata.source_text: Look at that, you lot . . . Potter fought! He fought it, and he damn near beat it! ... very good, Potter, very good indeed!
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I've noticed that Moody teaches by forcing repeat practice until the effect is gone; he made Harry repeat the exercise four times to throw off the curse.
metadata.source_text: Moody had insisted on putting Harry through his paces four times in a row, until Harry could throw off the curse entirely
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I think Moody's methods are extreme and alarmist; seeing him shout and insist we watch Harry's eyes made me more convinced he's over-the-top in demonstrating danger.
metadata.source_text: you'd think we were all going to be attacked any second.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I feel that Moody singles out students for demonstration, especially Harry, which changes how I view his role: less like a calm teacher, more like a showman testing people.
metadata.source_text: Look at that, you lot . . . Potter fought! ... very good, Potter, very good indeed!
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I found out the curse hit me harder than Harry; Moody said the effects would wear off by lunchtime, so I know it's temporary.
metadata.source_text: He had had much more difficulty with the curse than Harry, though Moody assured him the effects would wear off by lunchtime.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I used to think teachers just taught calmly, but after Moody kept us on edge and acted paranoid, I believe he's excessively alarmed and theatrical.
metadata.source_text: Talk about paranoid . . .
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I reckon the Ministry were glad to get rid of Moody; from how he behaves, I can see why folks at the Ministry were glad he left.
metadata.source_text: No wonder they were glad to get shot of him at the Ministry.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Lesson and Students' Reactions

metadata.description: I've found out that Heads of the participating schools always sit on the judging panel for the Tournament — and that a cockatrice rampaged in the Tournament of 1792.
metadata.source_text: Well, the Heads of the participating schools are always on the panel," said Hermione, and everyone looked around at her, rather surprised, "because all three of them were injured during the Tournament of 1792, when a cockatrice the champions were supposed to be catching went on the rampage.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I suppose Hermione's really serious about the house-elf thing; buying a S.P.E.W. badge didn't mean much to me, but I can see she's not going to drop it, and it's starting to press on me.
metadata.source_text: True, both of them had paid two Sickles for a S.P.E.W. badge, but they had only done it to keep her quiet.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I've noticed Hermione's persistence — she keeps badgering Ron and me, rattling the collecting tin and cornering people; I reckon she's more determined than she's ever been about causes.
metadata.source_text: Their Sickles had been wasted, however; if anything, they seemed to have made Hermione more vociferous. She had been badgering Harry and Ron ever since, first to wear the badges, then to persuade others to do the same, and she had also taken to rattling around the Gryffindor common room every evening, cornering people and shaking the collecting tin under their noses.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I've read in Hogwarts: A History that the Heads of the participating schools are always on the judging panel and that in 1792 a cockatrice attack injured three Heads during the Tournament.
metadata.source_text: Well, the Heads of the participating schools are always on the panel," said Hermione, and everyone looked around at her, rather surprised, "because all three of them were injured during the Tournament of 1792, when a cockatrice the champions were supposed to be catching went on the rampage.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that Hogwarts: A History is biased and incomplete — it glosses over nasty aspects, so we need to question what it leaves out about the school.
metadata.source_text: It’s all in Hogwarts: A History. Though, of course, that book’s not entirely reliable. A Revised History of Hogwarts would be a more accurate title. Or A Highly Biased and Selective History of Hogwarts, Which Glosses Over the Nastier Aspects of the School.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I feel furious about the way everyone treats house-elves — I see it as collusion in the oppression of slaves, and I can't stand that many students laugh or ignore the issue.
metadata.source_text: Not once, in over a thousand pages, does Hogwarts: A History mention that we are all colluding in the oppression of a hundred slaves!
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I heard that Heads of the schools are always judges for the Tournament and that once, back in 1792, a cockatrice caused real trouble — sounds like proper dangerous stuff to me.
metadata.source_text: Well, the Heads of the participating schools are always on the panel," said Hermione, and everyone looked around at her, rather surprised, "because all three of them were injured during the Tournament of 1792, when a cockatrice the champions were supposed to be catching went on the rampage.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I rolled my eyes at Hermione's S.P.E.W. campaign and thought most people see it as a joke, but I did pay my Sickles just to stop her glaring at me, so I suppose I'm slightly more involved than before.
metadata.source_text: Some people, like Neville, had paid up just to stop Hermione from glowering at them. A few seemed mildly interested in what she had to say, but were reluctant to take a more active role in campaigning. Many regarded the whole thing as a joke.
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: Hermione keeps going on about house-elves and I've noticed George actually listens a bit when people defend the house-elves; I reckon opinions among friends are split and people that normally shrug can be persuaded.
metadata.source_text: George, however, leaned in toward Hermione. "Listen, have you ever been down in the kitchens, Hermione?" "No, of course not," said Hermione curtly, "I hardly think students are supposed to —" "Well, we have," said George, indicating Fred, "loads of times, to nick food. And we’ve met them, and they’re happy."
metadata.scene_title: School Chatter: Tournament, S.P.E.W., and Hedwig's Letter

metadata.description: I learned that Hedwig draws attention if she keeps returning to me — a snowy owl that keeps appearing could give me away.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig’ll attract too much attention," said Hermione at once. "She stands out. A snowy owl that keeps returning to wherever he’s hiding . . . I mean, they’re not native birds, are they?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I'm a bit reassured knowing Sirius might be nearer; if he's managing to get back without being caught, I won't have to wait ages for his replies.
metadata.source_text: He supposed that Sirius managing to get back without being caught was something. He couldn’t deny either that the idea that Sirius was much nearer was reassuring; at least he wouldn’t have to wait so long for a response every time he wrote.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I noticed Madame Maxime and her students right away; I watched her arrive and realized those Beauxbatons kids looked cold and uneasy compared to us.
metadata.source_text: Harry, whose attention had been focused completely upon Madame Maxime, now noticed that about a dozen boys and girls... were shivering... they were staring up at Hogwarts with apprehensive looks on their faces.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I've figured out that Hedwig standing out as a snowy owl could attract too much attention and isn't a good idea if someone is hiding.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig’ll attract too much attention," said Hermione at once. "She stands out. A snowy owl that keeps returning to wherever he’s hiding . . . I mean, they’re not native birds, are they?
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I’m more insistent now that Apparition rules at Hogwarts matter — I don't think you can Apparate inside the grounds, and I felt the need to tell them off about it.
metadata.source_text: "You can’t Apparate inside the Hogwarts grounds, how often do I have to tell you?" said Hermione impatiently.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: Seeing the Beauxbatons students shivering made me more aware of the differences between them and our students; I judged them as poorly clothed for the cold.
metadata.source_text: From what Harry could see of them (they were standing in Madame Maxime’s enormous shadow), they were staring up at Hogwarts with apprehensive looks on their faces.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I learned to keep an eye on the time and the drive — I was checking my watch and wondering how the foreign kids were turning up, whether by train or brooms or Portkey.
metadata.source_text: "Nearly six," said Ron, checking his watch and then staring down the drive that led to the front gates. "How d’you reckon they’re coming? The train?"
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I reckon it's possible something dramatic will happen with their arrival — I kept saying maybe they'd use a Portkey or broomsticks, showing I'm expecting a bit of showmanship.
metadata.source_text: "A Portkey?" Ron suggested. "Or they could Apparate — maybe you’re allowed to do it under seventeen wherever they come from?"
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: Watching Madame Maxime talk and her big students made me grin and imagine how Hagrid will handle enormous horses or escaped creatures; I think Hagrid's up to a laughable challenge.
metadata.source_text: "My steeds require — er — forceful ’andling," said Madame Maxime... "I assure you that Hagrid will be well up to the job," said Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Greet the Visiting Delegations

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in the Great Hall during the Triwizard announcement, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Announcement of the Triwizard Tournament and the Goblet

metadata.description: I was not present for the Triwizard announcement in the Great Hall and therefore cannot describe the scene from personal observation.
metadata.scene_title: Announcement of the Triwizard Tournament and the Goblet

metadata.description: I wasn't at the Great Hall when the Triwizard Tournament was announced, so I didn't see the casket or hear Dumbledore's explanation myself.
metadata.scene_title: Announcement of the Triwizard Tournament and the Goblet

metadata.description: I wasn't present for this announcement and the Goblet's appearance, so I don't have first-hand knowledge of Dumbledore's exact words or the Age Line details from the Hall.
metadata.scene_title: The Goblet Revealed and Rules Explained

metadata.description: I wasn't at the announcement when Dumbledore revealed the Goblet of Fire and explained the rules of the Triwizard Tournament, so I can't quote what was said directly.
metadata.scene_title: The Goblet Revealed and Rules Explained

metadata.description: I wasn't present for Dumbledore opening the casket or for his explanation about writing names into the Goblet of Fire, so I don't know how the students reacted.
metadata.scene_title: The Goblet Revealed and Rules Explained

metadata.description: I've learned that Fred and George tried an Aging Potion and were hurled out of the Goblet's line and came away with long white beards.
metadata.source_text: There was a loud sizzling sound, and both twins were hurled out of the golden circle as though they had been thrown by an invisible shot-putter. They landed painfully, ten feet away on the cold stone floor, and to add insult to injury, there was a loud popping noise, and both of them sprouted identical long white beards.
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I reckon someone at Hogwarts might have put their name in secretly the night before; I wouldn't have wanted everyone watching me either.
metadata.source_text: Bet some of them put it in last night after we’d all gone to bed,” said Harry. “I would’ve if it had been me . . . wouldn’t have wanted everyone watching.
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I feel chummy and protective around Ron and Hermione — we keep trading worries and jokes about the Tournament and Hagrid, and I include them when Hagrid gets excited about the tasks.
metadata.source_text: Harry watched, fascinated, as Fred pulled a slip of parchment out of his pocket bearing the words Fred Weasley — Hogwarts... “Go on, Hagrid!” Harry, Ron, and Hermione urged him, but he just shook his head, grinning.
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I've noticed that several students from other schools and houses have entered names into the Goblet, and Angelina Johnson has definitely put her name in.
metadata.source_text: All the Durmstrang lot,” she replied. “But I haven’t seen anyone from Hogwarts yet... Angelina Johnson coming into the Hall, grinning in an embarrassed sort of way. ... “Well, I’ve done it! Just put my name in!”
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I'm worried that clever tricks like Ageing Potions might defeat the Tournament's rules; I think Dumbledore will have thought of precautions, so I doubt simple cheating will work.
metadata.source_text: “I’m not sure this is going to work, you know,” said Hermione warningly. “I’m sure Dumbledore will have thought of this.”
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I genuinely want someone from Gryffindor to do well — I'm pleased Angelina entered and I hope she wins; I showed her support straight away.
metadata.source_text: “Well, I’m glad someone from Gryffindor’s entering,” said Hermione. “I really hope you get it, Angelina!”
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I found out that Fred and George took an Aging Potion, tried to enter, got thrown out and grew beards — it was hilarious even if nasty for them.
metadata.source_text: “The Aging Potion, dung brains,” said Fred. “One drop each,” said George... there was a loud sizzling sound, and both twins were hurled out of the golden circle... and both of them sprouted identical long white beards.
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that the Tournament can't have a Slytherin as champion — I don't want a Slytherin like Warrington winning for Gryffindor's sake.
metadata.source_text: “We can’t have a Slytherin champion!”
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I feel impressed and a bit more respectful toward Angelina for putting her name in; I even joke about her age because I reckon she looks old enough.
metadata.source_text: “You’re kidding!” said Ron, looking impressed. “Are you seventeen, then?” asked Harry. “’Course she is, can’t see a beard, can you?” said Ron. “I had my birthday last week,” said Angelina.
metadata.scene_title: Feast Ends; Students Discuss the Goblet and Attempts to Enter

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid won't join S.P.E.W. and that he thinks most house-elves prefer serving humans rather than being freed.
metadata.source_text: for he flatly refused to join S.P.E.W. when she showed him her badges.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I've heard Hermione say Dobby was over the moon when freed and now asks for wages, which makes me see freeing elves can make them happy rather than just upsetting them.
metadata.source_text: But Harry set Dobby free, and he was over the moon about it! ... And we heard he’s asking for wages now!
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I notice Hagrid and Hermione argue on house-elves but it's friendly; Hagrid's steady, stubborn ways make me appreciate his simple, earnest view even when I don't fully agree.
metadata.source_text: It’d be doin’ ’em an unkindness, Hermione," he said gravely, threading a massive bone needle with thick yellow yarn.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I've found out Hagrid refuses to join S.P.E.W. even when I showed him my badges, and he explained his belief that house-elves like serving humans.
metadata.source_text: for he flatly refused to join S.P.E.W. when she showed him her badges.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I am surprised to hear Hagrid say most house-elves wouldn't want freedom; that makes me rethink how complicated convincing them might be, though I still believe freedom is right.
metadata.source_text: It’d be doin’ ’em an unkindness, Hermione," he said gravely, "... Yeh’d be makin’ ’em unhappy ter take away their work, an’ insultin’ ’em if yeh tried ter pay ’em.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I realise Hagrid's loyalty to creatures and his earnest way of speaking means he can't be easily persuaded on S.P.E.W.; I respect him even when we disagree.
metadata.source_text: I’ll come with yeh," said Hagrid, putting away his darning.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I heard Hermione saying Dobby was thrilled about being set free and even asking for wages, so I know freeing an elf can make them very happy.
metadata.source_text: But Harry set Dobby free, and he was over the moon about it! ... And we heard he’s asking for wages now!
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I'm taking Hagrid's side a bit here — he says most house-elves wouldn't want freedom and are happy serving, so I'm less sure that freeing them is always the right thing.
metadata.source_text: It’d be doin’ ’em an unkindness, Hermione," he said gravely, "... Yeh’d be makin’ ’em unhappy ter take away their work, an’ insultin’ ’em if yeh tried ter pay ’em.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I can see Hagrid's stubborn, gentle nature in this argument; he nags a bit but I like him for being so protective of creatures, even when he annoys Hermione.
metadata.source_text: for he flatly refused to join S.P.E.W. when she showed him her badges.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid’s Tales and Entrance Hall Antics with the Age Line

metadata.description: I saw Hagrid go off with Madame Maxime — he wasn't waiting for us; he actually walked up the grounds with her and the Beauxbatons students.
metadata.source_text: Without so much as a backward glance at his cabin, Hagrid was trudging off up the grounds with Madame Maxime, the Beauxbatons students following in their wake, jogging to keep up with their enormous strides.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I think Hagrid fancies Madame Maxime now; seeing him misty-eyed and leaving with her made me realise he's smitten in a way I hadn't expected.
metadata.source_text: He was talking to Madame Maxime with a rapt, misty-eyed expression Harry had only ever seen him wear once before — when he had been looking at the baby dragon, Norbert.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I feel a bit more distant from Hagrid in that moment because he left without waiting for us — I noticed he didn't look back at his cabin or at us.
metadata.source_text: Without so much as a backward glance at his cabin, Hagrid was trudging off up the grounds with Madame Maxime...
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I recognised Hagrid's scent as 'eau de cologne' when he asked 'Don' yeh like it?' and I heard myself ask if it was aftershave; I know exactly what it smelled like and that he was blushing about it.
metadata.source_text: Coughing, Ron said, 'Hagrid, what's that?' 'Eh?' said Hagrid, turning around with a large bottle in his hand. 'Don' yeh like it?' 'Is that aftershave?' said Hermione in a slightly choked voice. 'Er — eau de cologne,' Hagrid muttered. He was blushing.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I thought Hagrid would wait for us, but now I don't — he went off with Madame Maxime straightaway; I'm annoyed and a bit surprised he didn't stick around.
