metadata.source_text: 'He’s going up to the castle with her!' said Hermione indignantly. 'I thought he was waiting for us!'
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: Seeing Hagrid so infatuated and going with Madame Maxime has altered how I view his priorities right now — he cares about her enough to leave without a backward glance.
metadata.source_text: Without so much as a backward glance at his cabin, Hagrid was trudging off up the grounds with Madame Maxime...
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I smelt that horrible stuff and asked Hagrid 'what's that?' — I know now he was wearing an awful lot of 'eau de cologne' and then went to wash it off.
metadata.source_text: Coughing, Ron said, 'Hagrid, what's that?' 'Eh?' said Hagrid... 'Er — eau de cologne,' Hagrid muttered. He was blushing. 'Maybe it's a bit much,' he said gruffly. 'I'll go take it off, hang on . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid fancies Madame Maxime — seeing him all googly-eyed and walking off with her made me certain he's taken with her.
metadata.source_text: 'He fancies her!' said Ron incredulously.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I feel Hagrid's a bit unpredictable now — one moment he's with us, the next he's off with a Beauxbatons headmistress; makes him seem more grown-up and oddly secretive.
metadata.source_text: Without so much as a backward glance at his cabin, Hagrid was trudging off up the grounds with Madame Maxime...
metadata.scene_title: Arrival of Guests, Goblet’s Selection and the Three Champions Announced

metadata.description: I learned that my name actually came out of the Goblet of Fire and that people are treating me as a legitimate Triwizard champion whether I feel ready or not.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s name just came out of the Goblet of Fire!

metadata.description: I didn’t expect to be named; I’m suddenly certain I can’t just explain away what happened — everyone believes the goblet chose me so I must face what comes.
metadata.source_text: I don’t think there can be any ducking out at this stage. . . . It’s down in the rules, you’re obliged . . . Harry will just have to do the best he —

metadata.description: I noticed how the other champions looked at me — Krum’s face went darker, Cedric seemed politely bewildered, and Fleur treated me with contempt — so I’ve realised their impressions of me have shifted immediately.
metadata.source_text: Viktor Krum straightened up. His surly face darkened as he surveyed Harry. Cedric looked nonplussed. Fleur Delacour, however, tossed her hair, smiling, and said, “Oh, vairy funny joke, Meester Bagman.”

metadata.description: I wasn’t present during the announcement by Ludo Bagman and didn’t witness the Goblet of Fire producing Harry’s name, so I don’t have first-hand knowledge of that moment.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t present during the announcement by Ludo Bagman and didn’t witness the Goblet of Fire producing Harry’s name, so I don’t have first-hand knowledge of that moment.

metadata.description: I wasn’t in the room when Harry’s name was announced from the Goblet of Fire and therefore didn’t see the champions’ reactions or Bagman’s presentation.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t in the room when Harry’s name was announced from the Goblet of Fire and therefore didn’t see the champions’ reactions or Bagman’s presentation.

metadata.description: I learned that the Goblet of Fire has chosen me as a champion and that everyone is watching me and questioning how my name got into the Goblet.
metadata.source_text: "Did you put your name into the Goblet of Fire, Harry?"

metadata.description: I feel outraged and numb — I never put my name into the Goblet and I'm furious at being called a 'little boy' when people don't believe me.
metadata.source_text: "Zey are saying zat zis little boy is to compete also!"

metadata.description: I now view Professor Snape as openly hostile toward me; his sneering accusations make me realize he is willing to blame me publicly.
metadata.source_text: "It’s no one’s fault but Potter’s, Karkaroff," said Snape softly. "Don’t go blaming Dumbledore for Potter’s determination to break rules."

metadata.description: I was not present during the Goblet of Fire controversy and therefore did not witness the debate about the champions.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the room, so I don't know what happened firsthand.

metadata.description: I was not there when the schools argued about the Goblet of Fire and Harry being named a champion; I did not observe the accusations or Moody's arrival.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the argument after the Goblet selection, so I didn't see the confrontation.

metadata.description: I was not present when Determination to Enforce the Tournament occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Determination to Enforce the Tournament occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I've been told — by Dumbledore in front of everyone — that both Cedric and I have been chosen to compete in the tournament, and that is final even though nobody knows how that happened.
metadata.source_text: Both Cedric and Harry have been chosen to compete in the tournament. This, therefore, they will do. . . .

metadata.description: I feel unsettled and confused; my head's in complete disarray and I can't think straight after hearing we're both champions — I didn't expect this and it's rattled me.
metadata.source_text: He really couldn’t think of anything to say. The inside of his head seemed to be in complete disarray, as though his brain had been ransacked.

metadata.description: Cedric and I are set to play against each other again in the tournament; he spoke to me with a slight smile, and I recognize we're officially opponents now even if we're awkward about it.
metadata.source_text: “So,” said Cedric, with a slight smile. “We’re playing against each other again!”

metadata.description: I wasn't present at this meeting or the announcement about the tournament champions, so I don't know firsthand what was said or how people reacted.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t the only one either. Snape looked furious; Karkaroff livid; Bagman, however, looked rather excited.

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room when Dumbledore announced that Cedric and Harry were chosen for the tournament, so I don't have any direct observations about the discussion or the reactions.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore waited, but Madame Maxime did not speak, she merely glared.

metadata.description: I keep having to say I didn’t put my name in the Goblet; I learned that everyone assumes I entered the tournament even though I’m certain I didn’t.
metadata.source_text: I didn’t," he said, over and over again, "I don’t know how it happened.

metadata.description: I’ve started to believe that telling people the truth won’t change their minds — no matter how often I say it, they simply don’t listen and treat me like a hero instead.
metadata.source_text: I didn’t," he said, over and over again, "I don’t know how it happened. But for all the notice anyone took, he might just as well not have answered at all.

metadata.description: I feel a bit distant from my fellow Gryffindors right now; although they’re cheering and stuffing food at me, I don’t feel like celebrating with them and their excitement feels suffocating.
metadata.source_text: Nobody wanted to hear that he wasn’t hungry; nobody wanted to hear that he hadn’t put his name in the goblet; not one single person seemed to have noticed that he wasn’t at all in the mood to celebrate.

metadata.description: I was not present at the celebration in the common room, so I do not know how the crowd reacted to Harry’s explanation.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events in the common room.

metadata.description: I wasn’t there for the moment when Harry was swamped by the Gryffindors after the Goblet announcement, so I can’t say what he said to them.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t present during the crowd’s celebration around Harry in the common room.

metadata.description: I found out Hermione accepted my story about what happened after I left the Gryffindor table; she believed I hadn't put my own name into the Goblet.
metadata.source_text: To his immense relief, Hermione accepted his story without question.
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I'm relieved and a bit stunned that Hermione doesn't doubt me at all; I thought there might be suspicion, but she's completely on my side.
metadata.source_text: To his immense relief, Hermione accepted his story without question.
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I think there's a gap between Ron and me now — Hermione says Ron might be jealous of the attention I get, which makes me feel bitter and a bit exasperated with him.
metadata.source_text: Oh Harry, isn’t it obvious? ... He’s jealous!
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I know that Harry didn’t enter himself; I could tell from the look on his face when Dumbledore read out his name.
metadata.source_text: Well, of course I knew you hadn’t entered yourself," she said when he’d finished telling her about the scene in the chamber off the Hall. "The look on your face when Dumbledore read out your name!
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I'm now more convinced that no student could have put Harry’s name into the Goblet or fooled the Goblet, because Moody is right and the protections are too strong for a pupil to bypass.
metadata.source_text: But the question is, who did put it in? Because Moody’s right, Harry . . . I don’t think any student could have done it . . . they’d never be able to fool the goblet, or get over Dumbledore’s —
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I feel sympathetic toward Ron and understand why he might be upset; I think he's jealous of Harry because Harry always gets the attention and Ron is pushed aside, which explains his awkwardness.
metadata.source_text: Oh Harry, isn’t it obvious? ... He’s jealous! ... it’s always you who gets all the attention, you know it is. ... he’s always shunted to one side whenever people see you, and he puts up with it, and he never mentions it, but I suppose this is just one time too many.
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I was not present for the walk to the lake or for the detailed conversation between Harry and Hermione, so I do not know everything they discussed.
metadata.source_text: Erm . . . yes . . . he was at breakfast," she said.
metadata.scene_title: Breakfast and Walk to the Lake — Harry Confides in Hermione

metadata.description: I learned that Sirius wanted me to keep him posted about everything at Hogwarts, so I have to write and tell him what’s happened with the Tournament.
metadata.source_text: Write to Sirius. You’ve got to tell him what’s happened. He asked you to keep him posted on everything that’s going on at Hogwarts. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Plans — Writing to Sirius and the Toast Tossed to the Lake

metadata.description: I’ve changed my mind about writing to Sirius — I’ll do it even if I think he’ll burst into the castle the moment he hears my scar twinged.
metadata.source_text: Okay, okay, I’ll write to him.
metadata.scene_title: Plans — Writing to Sirius and the Toast Tossed to the Lake

metadata.description: I’m fed up with Ron and I’m not going to ask him for anything after how he’s acted; I won’t be running around trying to make him grow up.
metadata.source_text: I’m not running around after him trying to make him grow up!
metadata.scene_title: Plans — Writing to Sirius and the Toast Tossed to the Lake

metadata.description: I know that the Triwizard Tournament won’t stay secret and that the Daily Prophet will probably mention Harry competing because the tournament is famous and Harry is famous.
metadata.source_text: Harry, this isn’t going to be kept quiet. This tournament’s famous, and you’re famous. I’ll be really surprised if there isn’t anything in the Daily Prophet about you competing. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Plans — Writing to Sirius and the Toast Tossed to the Lake

metadata.source_text: “That doesn’t matter,” said Hermione firmly. “Just as long as you’re concentrating really, really hard on it, it’ll come. Harry, we’d better get some sleep . . . you’re going to need it.”
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Summoning Charm — Practice and Tension

metadata.description: I was not present during these events in the greenhouse, classroom practice, and Divination; I do not know what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Learning the Summoning Charm — Practice and Tension

metadata.description: I've learned that the champions must go down onto the grounds now and get ready for the first task; we're to wait in a tent where Mr. Bagman will tell us the procedure.
metadata.source_text: You’re to go in here with the other champions," said Professor McGonagall, in a rather shaky sort of voice, "and wait for your turn, Potter. Mr. Bagman is in there . . . he’ll be telling you the — the procedure. . . . Good luck.
metadata.scene_title: March to the Enclosure — The Champions Prepare

metadata.description: I feel more alone and on edge than I expected; people’s looks and comments make me think I really am singled out and that I might lose control if pushed too far.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt oddly separate from everyone around him, whether they were wishing him good luck or hissing “We’ll have a box of tissues ready, Potter” as he passed. It was a state of nervousness so advanced that he wondered whether he mightn’t just lose his head when they tried to lead him out to his dragon, and start trying to curse everyone in sight.
metadata.scene_title: March to the Enclosure — The Champions Prepare

metadata.description: I've noticed Professor McGonagall is anxious too; she isn't just stern — she actually seems worried for me and is trying to steady me, which makes me feel a bit less alone.
metadata.source_text: She didn’t seem herself either; in fact, she looked nearly as anxious as Hermione. As she walked him down the stone steps and out into the cold November afternoon, she put her hand on his shoulder. "Now, don’t panic," she said, "just keep a cool head. . . . We’ve got wizards standing by to control the situation if it gets out of hand. . . . The main thing is just to do your best, and nobody will think any the worse of you. . . . Are you all right?"
metadata.scene_title: March to the Enclosure — The Champions Prepare

metadata.description: I was not present during these moments at the dragons’ enclosure and so I don't have direct knowledge of what occurred there.
metadata.scene_title: March to the Enclosure — The Champions Prepare

metadata.description: I was not present during these events at the dragons’ enclosure and therefore cannot report on what happened during the champions' preparations.
metadata.scene_title: March to the Enclosure — The Champions Prepare

metadata.description: I learned that the first task requires us to collect a golden egg, and Bagman actually hands out tiny models of the dragons so we know which breed we'll face.
metadata.source_text: ‘When the audience has assembled, I’m going to be offering each of you this bag ... from which you will each select a small model of the thing you are about to face! ... your task is to collect the golden egg!’
metadata.scene_title: Drawing the Dragons — Bagman's Reveal and the Order

metadata.description: I feel more alone and separate from everyone else than I expected; hearing Bagman cheer and seeing the others so pale made me realise how scared I actually am and how different my feelings are from the crowd.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt as separate from the crowd as though they were a different species.
metadata.scene_title: Drawing the Dragons — Bagman's Reveal and the Order

metadata.description: I noticed that Cedric tried to be friendly — he gave me a small smile — which made me realise he’s polite and steady even when he’s nervous; I feel I can return that politeness to him.
metadata.source_text: When Harry entered, Cedric gave him a small smile, which Harry returned...
metadata.scene_title: Drawing the Dragons — Bagman's Reveal and the Order

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the tent, so I don't know what was said or how the draw went.
metadata.source_text: She left him at the entrance of the tent. Harry went inside.
metadata.scene_title: Drawing the Dragons — Bagman's Reveal and the Order

metadata.description: I wasn't at the tent when Bagman revealed the dragon models and the order of the draw, so I can't describe the champions' reactions firsthand.
metadata.source_text: She left him at the entrance of the tent. Harry went inside.
metadata.scene_title: Drawing the Dragons — Bagman's Reveal and the Order

metadata.description: I learned that the dragons are drawn for each champion and the numbers decide the order we face them; Bagman told us the numbers refer to who goes when.
metadata.source_text: You have each pulled out the dragon you will face, and the numbers refer to the order in which you are to take on the dragons, do you see?
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I felt suddenly calmer once I was on the Firebolt; flying made the fear lift and I realised this was like Quidditch, which steadied me more than anything else could.
metadata.source_text: As he soared upward... he realized that he had left not only the ground behind, but also his fear. ... This was just another Quidditch match, that was all ... just another Quidditch match
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I found Bagman’s commentary infuriating and intrusive — he kept making everything worse with his running mouth, even when I was trying to concentrate.
metadata.source_text: And Bagman’s commentary made everything much, much worse. . . . Horrible pictures formed in Harry’s mind as he heard: 'Oooh, narrow miss there, very narrow' ... 'Clever move — pity it didn't work!'
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I learned that shouting Accio Firebolt will bring my Firebolt to me even across the arena — it hurtled in around the edge of the woods and stopped dead beside me.
metadata.source_text: “Accio Firebolt!” he shouted. ... he turned and saw his Firebolt hurtling toward him around the edge of the woods, soaring into the enclosure, and stopping dead in midair beside him, waiting for him to mount.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I discovered that flying like in a Quidditch match helps me lose my fear — when I was up on the broom I felt like I belonged and my fear left me.
metadata.source_text: And a second later, something miraculous happened. . . . As he soared upward, ... he realized that he had left not only the ground behind, but also his fear. . . . He was back where he belonged. . . . This was just another Quidditch match, that was all . . .
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I found that a dragon guarding eggs will move reluctantly; if I kept close enough to threaten but not provoke, I could draw her away from the clutch and grab the golden egg.
metadata.source_text: The Horntail didn’t seem to want to take off, she was too protective of her eggs. ... The trick was to do it carefully, gradually. ... He flew higher. The Horntail’s head rose with him, ... He dived. ... he had seized the golden egg
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I used to be terrified at the thought of facing a dragon, but after grabbing the egg I felt braver and more confident — flying made it feel like another Quidditch match.
metadata.source_text: As he soared upward, ... he realized that he had left not only the ground behind, but also his fear. . . . This was just another Quidditch match, that was all . . .
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I now believe quick thinking and Quidditch reflexes can get me out of life-or-death tasks; dodging fire and spikes felt like dodging Bludgers and it worked.
metadata.source_text: a jet of fire had been released exactly where he would have been had he not swerved away . . . but Harry didn’t care . . . that was no more than dodging a Bludger.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I feel grateful to Hagrid for his help and proud that he’s so pleased; his hoarse 'Yeh did it, Harry!' made me know he’s on my side.
metadata.source_text: “Yeh did it, Harry!” said Hagrid hoarsely. “Yeh did it! An’ agains’ the Horntail an’ all, an’ yeh know Charlie said that was the wors’ —”
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I learned I could distract a Horntail long enough to dive under it, snatch the golden egg, and get away on my Firebolt even after letting go to grab the egg.
metadata.source_text: “Come on,” Harry hissed, swerving tantalizingly above her, “come on, come and get me . . . up you get now . . .” And then she reared, spreading her great, black, leathery wings at last, as wide as those of a small airplane — and Harry dived. Before the dragon knew what he had done, or where he had disappeared to, he was speeding toward the ground as fast as he could go, toward the eggs now unprotected by her clawed front legs — he had taken his hands off his Firebolt — he had seized the golden egg — And with a huge spurt of speed, he was off, he was soaring out over the stands, the heavy egg safely under his uninjured arm
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I feel braver now — I believed I might not manage a dragon, but pulling that off made me realise I can handle far scarier things than I thought.
metadata.source_text: And with a huge spurt of speed, he was off, he was soaring out over the stands, the heavy egg safely under his uninjured arm, and it was as though somebody had just turned the volume back up
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I know Hagrid cares about me and wants to celebrate my success, but I also know he nearly gave away that he showed me dragons, so I need to be careful around him when crowd excitement is high.
metadata.source_text: “Yeh did it, Harry!” said Hagrid hoarsely. “Yeh did it! An’ agains’ the Horntail an’ all, an’ yeh know Charlie said that was the wors’ —” “Thanks, Hagrid,” said Harry loudly, so that Hagrid wouldn’t blunder on and reveal that he had shown Harry the dragons beforehand.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I've heard the order and that each champion drew a dragon and the numbers show who goes when, the procedure for the First Task is clearly laid out by Bagman.
metadata.source_text: You have each pulled out the dragon you will face, and the numbers refer to the order in which you are to take on the dragons, do you see?
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: Hearing Bagman’s loud commentary and watching the champions made me feel more anxious for Harry; the whole thing seemed less dignified and more sensational than it should be.
metadata.source_text: And Bagman’s commentary made everything much, much worse. . . . Horrible pictures formed in Harry’s mind as he heard: 'Oooh, narrow miss there, very narrow' ... 'Clever move — pity it didn't work!'
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: Seeing Harry step up and then summon his Firebolt reminded me that he handles pressure like a player in a match; I respect his ability to turn fear into focus.
metadata.source_text: As he soared upward... he realized that he had left not only the ground behind, but also his fear. ... This was just another Quidditch match, that was all ... just another Quidditch match
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I noticed that Professor McGonagall thought Harry needed medical attention immediately after the task — she told him to see Madam Pomfrey before the judges gave out his score.
metadata.source_text: “You’ll need to see Madam Pomfrey before the judges give out your score. . . . Over there, she’s had to mop up Diggory already. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I realized that even brilliant, brave actions can leave students hurt and in need of care; victory in a task doesn’t mean you’re untouched.
metadata.source_text: He noticed that her hand shook as she pointed at his shoulder. “You’ll need to see Madam Pomfrey before the judges give out your score.”
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I understand more clearly that the professors look out for the students’ safety; McGonagall’s concern for Harry showed she’ll protect us even when impressed.
metadata.source_text: “You’ll need to see Madam Pomfrey before the judges give out your score. . . .” said Professor McGonagall.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I've seen Harry get the egg from a Horntail; he really did dive in, grab the egg, and get away on his broom—he was brilliant under pressure.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, you were brilliant!” Hermione said squeakily. ... “You were amazing! You really were!”
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I feel even more certain now that Harry is capable of extraordinary things when he's focused; my worry turned into admiration the moment he held that egg.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, you were brilliant!” Hermione said squeakily. There were fingernail marks on her face where she had been clutching it in fear.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I know I care for Harry more than just as a friend in danger — seeing him risk himself made my feelings of concern and loyalty stronger and more urgent.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, you were brilliant!” Hermione said squeakily. There were fingernail marks on her face where she had been clutching it in fear.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I know now that Bagman explains the draw and the numbers show who goes first, second, third and fourth; that's how the order was decided for the dragons.
metadata.source_text: You have each pulled out the dragon you will face, and the numbers refer to the order in which you are to take on the dragons, do you see?
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: Watching from the stands and hearing Bagman made me more worried for Harry; Bagman’s shouty commentary only made the whole contest seem more dangerous and showy.
metadata.source_text: And Bagman’s commentary made everything much, much worse. . . . Horrible pictures formed in Harry’s mind as he heard: 'Oooh, narrow miss there, very narrow' ... 'Clever move — pity it didn't work!'
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: Seeing Harry call his Firebolt and then ride it steady into the sky made me proud — he can take a hit and still act like a Quidditch player when it counts.
metadata.source_text: Accio Firebolt! ... he turned and saw his Firebolt hurtling through the air ... he swung his leg over the broom and kicked off from the ground. ... As he soared upward... he realized that he had left not only the ground behind, but also his fear.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I realized watching Harry that his Quidditch skill transfers into tasks outside school — his flying made the dragon seem like an opposing team and he grabbed the egg quick.
metadata.source_text: He was back where he belonged. . . . This was just another Quidditch match, that was all . . . he had seized the golden egg
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I feel more impressed and a bit stunned by Harry now — seeing him dive and snatch the egg made me think he’s braver and more capable than I maybe admitted before.
metadata.source_text: “That was excellent, Potter!” cried Professor McGonagall as he got off the Firebolt — which from her was extravagant praise.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I’m proud of Harry and feel closer to him because he succeeded; hearing the crowd and Hagrid cheering made me see how important he is to others as well as to me.
metadata.source_text: “Yeh did it, Harry!” said Hagrid hoarsely. “Yeh did it! An’ agains’ the Horntail an’ all...”
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I've learned that Harry managed to get the golden egg from the Horntail and survived — he really did dive under the dragon and escape with the egg.
metadata.source_text: And with a huge spurt of speed, he was off, he was soaring out over the stands, the heavy egg safely under his uninjured arm
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: Seeing Harry come back alive and holding the egg changed me — I went from terrified he might die to stunned and speechless; I can't pretend I'm not shaken by what he did.
metadata.source_text: But Harry was looking at Ron, who was very white and staring at Harry as though he were a ghost.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I realise Harry is more than just 'one of us' in danger; after watching him risk himself for the egg I'm more aware of how extraordinary he is, and it makes me feel small and astonished.
metadata.source_text: But Harry was looking at Ron, who was very white and staring at Harry as though he were a ghost.
metadata.scene_title: The First Task — Harry vs. the Horntail

metadata.description: I learned how the other champions handled the dragon: Cedric Transfigured a rock into a dog to distract the dragon, Fleur tried a sleep charm that went wrong and set her skirt alight, and Krum struck the dragon in the eye but caused extra damage.
metadata.source_text: You were the best, you know, no competition. Cedric did this weird thing where he Transfigured a rock on the ground . . . turned it into a dog . . . he was trying to make the dragon go for the dog instead of him. Well, it was a pretty cool bit of Transfiguration, and it sort of worked, because he did get the egg, but he got burned as well — the dragon changed its mind halfway through and decided it would rather have him than the Labrador; he only just got away. And that Fleur girl tried this sort of charm, I think she was trying to put it into a trance — well, that kind of worked too, it went all sleepy, but then it snored, and this great jet of flame shot out, and her skirt caught fire — she put it out with a bit of water out of her wand. And Krum — you won’t believe this, but he didn’t even think of flying! He was probably the best after you, though. Hit it with some sort of spell right in the eye. Only thing is, it went trampling around in agony and squashed half the real eggs — they took marks off for that, he wasn’t supposed to do any damage to them.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I felt odd about getting a ten because I knew I was hurt; I started to believe the judges might reward bravery or the outcome more than the injury itself, since Bagman gave me a ten despite my wound.
metadata.source_text: Ludo Bagman — ten. “Ten?” said Harry in disbelief. “But . . . I got hurt. . . . What’s he playing at?”
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I felt really grateful to Ron — his indignation on my behalf made me feel lighter than air and worth a hundred points to me; his defence mattered more than the exact scores from the judges.
metadata.source_text: But Harry didn’t care, he wouldn’t have cared if Karkaroff had given him zero; Ron’s indignation on his behalf was worth about a hundred points to him.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I've learned how the scoring works: five judges each give marks out of ten and they put their scores up in the air with their wands so everyone can see them.
metadata.source_text: It’s marks out of ten from each one," Ron said, and Harry, squinting up the field, saw the first judge — Madame Maxime — raise her wand in the air.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I got angrier about Karkaroff’s bias when he gave Harry only a four whereas he gave Krum ten — I actually think Karkaroff’s a lousy, biased scumbag for that.
metadata.source_text: “Four? You lousy, biased scumbag, you gave Krum ten!”
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I feel fiercely protective and proud of Harry — I can’t help shouting and thumping him on the back when the scores look good; I want him to know I’m on his side.
metadata.source_text: “Looking good!” Ron yelled, thumping Harry on the back.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the arena, so I don't have direct knowledge of the scores or what happened with the other champions.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath and Scoring — Relief and Recognition

metadata.description: I've learned we've been put level on points with Krum — we're tied in first place after the first task.
metadata.source_text: “You’re tied in first place, Harry! You and Krum!”
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I don't care what the Slytherins think anymore; most of the school was on our side and I can stand whatever they throw at me now.
metadata.source_text: He didn’t care about the Slytherins, he could stand whatever they threw at him now.
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I've got more of the school behind me than I expected — people cheered for me as well as Cedric, which makes me feel supported.
metadata.source_text: those weren’t only Gryffindors cheering in the crowd. When it had come to it, when they had seen what he was facing, most of the school had been on his side as well as Cedric’s.
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I've been told by Charlie that Harry and Krum are tied in first place after the task.
metadata.source_text: “You’re tied in first place, Harry! You and Krum!” said Charlie Weasley, hurrying to meet them
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I’ll wait around as asked — I'm prepared to hang about for Bagman to have a word with Harry in the champions' tent.
metadata.source_text: They told me to tell you you’ve got to hang around for a few more minutes. . . . Bagman wants a word, back in the champions’ tent.” Ron said he would wait
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I'm sticking by Harry now — I'll wait for him and talk things over; we're together on this after the task.
metadata.source_text: Ron said he would wait, so Harry reentered the tent, which somehow looked quite different now: friendly and welcoming.
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events of the first task or the conversation in the champions' tent, so I don't know the specifics of what happened.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Instructions for the Second Task and Rita Skeeter's Interview

metadata.description: Blimey, I found the golden egg is hollow and empty inside, but when I opened it a horrible, screechy wail came out — like the ghost orchestra playing a musical saw.
metadata.source_text: It was hollow and completely empty — but the moment Harry opened it, the most horrible noise, a loud and screechy wailing, filled the room. The nearest thing to it Harry had ever heard was the ghost orchestra at Nearly Headless Nick’s deathday party, who had all been playing the musical saw.
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I thought the tournament clues would be straightforward, but hearing that ear-splitting wail made me realise the tasks can be terrifying and not just puzzles to solve.
metadata.source_text: It was hollow and completely empty — but the moment Harry opened it, the most horrible noise, a loud and screechy wailing, filled the room.
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I feel a bit guilty but fond when Hermione covers for the rules and grins at me quietly — she’s looking out for me, and I notice she cares about fairness.
metadata.source_text: “He’s supposed to work out the clue on his own,” Hermione said swiftly. “It’s in the tournament rules. . . .” “I was supposed to work out how to get past the dragon on my own too,” Harry muttered, so only Hermione could hear him, and she grinned rather guiltily.
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I've learned that the tournament rules state champions must work out their own clues, so I know Harry is supposed to decipher the egg by himself.
metadata.source_text: “He’s supposed to work out the clue on his own,” Hermione said swiftly. “It’s in the tournament rules. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I felt uneasy when Rita Skeeter showed up with Hagrid’s skrewts — I’m beginning to think Rita’s interest could cause trouble and we shouldn’t trust her harmless smile.
metadata.source_text: Rita acted as though she hadn’t heard what Hagrid had said. “What are these fascinating creatures called?” she asked, beaming still more widely.
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I see Hagrid as earnest and proud of his creatures; when he beamed at Harry and agreed to Rita’s interview, I realised Hagrid trusts people too readily and I worry for him.
metadata.source_text: “Ah, you’re here, Harry!” said Rita Skeeter as she looked around. “So you like Care of Magical Creatures, do you? One of your favorite lessons?” “Yes,” said Harry stoutly. Hagrid beamed at him. “Lovely,” said Rita.
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I was not present during these events in the common room and thus did not witness the golden egg being opened or Hagrid speaking with Rita Skeeter.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: The Golden Egg and Hogsmeade Students’ Banter

metadata.description: I know that Rita Skeeter is the sort of person who'll twist whatever Hagrid says, so anything she asks him will probably come out wrong in print.
metadata.source_text: She’ll twist everything he says,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I’m more certain now that I can’t trust Rita Skeeter to report fairly about Hagrid; my opinion of her journalism has gone down because she'll twist his words.
metadata.source_text: She’ll twist everything he says,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hagrid — I don't want him to be misrepresented and I'm ready to stand by him when people like Rita poke around.
metadata.source_text: She’ll twist everything he says,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I'm worried that Hagrid might have imported skrewts illegally — that's something I genuinely think could have happened and would be serious.
metadata.source_text: Just as long as he didn’t import those skrewts illegally or anything,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I'm feeling desperate about the possibility that Hagrid broke rules; my concern for legalities and consequences has increased because the idea seems plausible.
metadata.source_text: Just as long as he didn’t import those skrewts illegally or anything,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I still care about Hagrid, but I'm worried now in a more practical way — I might judge him for rule-breaking if there's evidence he imported skrewts unlawfully.
metadata.source_text: Just as long as he didn’t import those skrewts illegally or anything,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I've reminded everyone that Hagrid's been in trouble before and Dumbledore never sacked him, so I know Hagrid's past troubles haven't cost him his job.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid’s been in loads of trouble before, and Dumbledore’s never sacked him,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I'm more confident now that things probably won't be that bad for Hagrid — my worry has eased because Dumbledore seems likely to stand by him.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid’s been in loads of trouble before, and Dumbledore’s never sacked him,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I feel even more protective and sympathetic towards Hagrid; I want to console him and believe he'll be okay even if he's in trouble again.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid’s been in loads of trouble before, and Dumbledore’s never sacked him,
metadata.scene_title: Lesson Ends and Rita’s Questions; Hagrid’s Troubles Speculated

metadata.description: I learned that Dobby has been freed by Professor Dumbledore and that Dobby is getting a Galleon a week and one day off a month.
metadata.source_text: And so Dobby is a free elf, sir, and Dobby gets a Galleon a week and one day off a month!
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I reckon freed house-elves can be happy working where they want; Dobby seems proud and pleased to be free rather than miserable.
metadata.source_text: Dobby likes freedom, miss, but he isn't wanting too much, miss, he likes work better.
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I feel closer to Dobby now — he trusts me enough to ask if he can visit me sometime and I promised he can come.
metadata.source_text: Harry Potter . . . can Dobby come and see you sometimes, sir?
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I've learned that Professor Dumbledore offered Dobby ten Galleons a week and weekends off, though Dobby refused the larger offer.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore offered Dobby ten Galleons a week, and weekends off,
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that freeing Dobby and letting him work at Hogwarts is the best thing for him and may influence other house-elves to desire freedom too.
metadata.source_text: I think this is the best thing that could have happened to those elves, you know,... The other elves will see how happy he is, being free, and slowly it'll dawn on them that they want that too!
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I feel protective toward Winky; I tried to tell her Mr Crouch was wrong and that she didn't do anything wrong, even though she refused to hear it.
metadata.source_text: But — Winky, come on! It's Mr Crouch who should be ashamed, not you! You didn't do anything wrong, he was really horrible to you —
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I found out Dobby is planning to spend his wages on a sweater next, because Dobby pointed to his bare chest and said so.
metadata.source_text: Dobby is going to buy a sweater next, Harry Potter!
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I'm impressed that nicking food from the kitchens isn't hard — the elves are too keen to give stuff away, which makes me see Fred and George's antics differently.
metadata.source_text: All these years I've been really impressed with Fred and George, nicking food from the kitchens — well, it's not exactly difficult, is it? They can't wait to give it away!
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I've warmed to Dobby; I like him and even offered him one of my mum's Christmas jumpers to wear, which felt like doing him a proper favor.
metadata.source_text: I'll give you the one my mum knits me this Christmas, I always get one from her. You don't mind maroon, do you?
metadata.scene_title: Dobby’s Return and Revelation in the Kitchens

metadata.description: I noticed that Viktor Krum was quite good-looking and a foot taller than me; I can imagine how odd I'd look dancing with someone that tall.
metadata.source_text: “She was quite good-looking,” said Ron fairly, after he’d stopped laughing. “She was a foot taller than me,” said Harry, still unnerved. “Imagine what I’d look like trying to dance with her.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I began to doubt that girls ask champions to the ball for any reason other than fame; I really think some would only want to go because we're school champions.
metadata.source_text: “They only like him because he’s famous!” Harry doubted very much if any of the girls who had asked to be his partner so far would have wanted to go to the ball with him if he hadn’t been a school champion.
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I felt relieved that Hagrid defended me to Rita Skeeter and wasn't willing to bad-mouth me; Hagrid sticking up for me makes me appreciate him more.
metadata.source_text: “She jus’ wanted me ter talk about you, Harry,” Hagrid continued in a low voice. “Well, I told her we’d been friends since I went ter fetch yeh from the Dursleys. ‘Never had to tell him off in four years?’ she said. ‘Never played you up in lessons, has he?’ I told her no, an’ she didn’ seem happy at all. Yeh’d think she wanted me to say yeh were horrible, Harry.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I've realised the golden egg might take weeks to work out, and that I need to press Harry to open it sooner so he knows what the next task will be.
metadata.source_text: “But it might take weeks to work it out!” said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I think Harry shouldn't just relax over Christmas; I'm more convinced he ought to be doing something constructive and preparing for the tasks instead of leaving the egg unopened.
metadata.source_text: “I’d have thought you’d be doing something constructive, Harry, even if you don’t want to learn your antidotes!”
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I'm frustrated with Ron and Harry's lax attitude about studying; I'm more determined to nag them into taking the competition seriously because I care about their chances.
metadata.source_text: “You’re not exactly straining yourself, though, are you?” said Hermione, looking at him over the top of her Potions notes.
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I learned that Rita Skeeter wanted Hagrid to say Harry was bad, that she was after scandal rather than skrewts, and I can see she asked Hagrid to talk about Harry more than the creatures.
metadata.source_text: “She didn’ seem very int’rested in magical creatures, ter tell yeh the truth,” Hagrid said... “She jus’ wanted me ter talk about you, Harry,” Hagrid continued in a low voice.
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I'm bitter about the professor springing a test on us on the last day; I now think the teacher was evil for ruining term-end celebrations with extra studying.
metadata.source_text: “Evil, he is,” Ron said bitterly that night in the Gryffindor common room. “Springing a test on us on the last day. Ruining the last bit of term with a whole load of studying.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I reckon Hagrid's defence of Harry shows Hagrid's loyalty; I feel glad that Hagrid wouldn't say nasty things about Harry to please Rita Skeeter.
metadata.source_text: “Well, yeh might’ve bent a few rules, Harry, bu’ yeh’re all righ’ really, aren’ you?”
metadata.scene_title: Hogwarts bustle and Christmas decorations; Harry's unease about the ball

metadata.description: I've learned that Hogwarts is all decked out for Christmas — icicles on the banisters, twelve trees in the Great Hall, and suits of armor bewitched to sing carols.
metadata.source_text: Everlasting icicles had been attached to the banisters of the marble staircase; the usual twelve Christmas trees in the Great Hall were bedecked with everything from luminous holly berries to real, hooting, golden owls, and the suits of armor had all been bewitched to sing carols whenever anyone passed them.
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I'm starting to believe I'm hopeless at asking Cho out — I'm getting more nervous by the hour and even thought, gloomily, that there's always Moaning Myrtle as a joke option.
metadata.source_text: And still, Harry hadn’t asked Cho to the ball. ... “I suppose there’s always Moaning Myrtle,” he said gloomily, referring to the ghost who haunted the girls’ toilets on the second floor.
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I feel Cho is always surrounded by friends and hard to get to; my view of her is that she's rarely alone, so I worry someone else will ask her before I do.
metadata.source_text: But every time he glimpsed Cho that day — during break, and then lunchtime, and once on the way to History of Magic — she was surrounded by friends. Didn’t she ever go anywhere alone?
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I've noticed how the school is decorated for Christmas with icicles, lots of trees, and bewitched armor singing carols — it's quite a spectacle.
metadata.source_text: Everlasting icicles had been attached to the banisters of the marble staircase; the usual twelve Christmas trees in the Great Hall were bedecked with everything from luminous holly berries to real, hooting, golden owls, and the suits of armor had all been bewitched to sing carols whenever anyone passed them.
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I'm aware that Harry is anxious about asking Cho and that he hasn't done it yet; I now believe his nerves are affecting him more than I first thought.
metadata.source_text: And still, Harry hadn’t asked Cho to the ball. He and Ron were getting very nervous now...
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I recognise Harry's preoccupation with Cho is serious — he keeps failing to concentrate because of it, which changes how I see his state of mind at the moment.
metadata.source_text: He found it hard to concentrate on Snape’s Potions test, and consequently forgot to add the key ingredient — a bezoar — meaning that he received bottom marks.
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I've learned that Harry still hasn't asked Cho to the ball and that we're both getting very nervous about turning up without partners.
metadata.source_text: And still, Harry hadn’t asked Cho to the ball. He and Ron were getting very nervous now...
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I now believe we have to be bold about getting partners — I've told Harry we must grit our teeth and act like we're storming an impregnable fortress.
metadata.source_text: “Harry — we’ve just got to grit our teeth and do it,” said Ron on Friday morning, in a tone that suggested they were planning the storming of an impregnable fortress.
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I feel protective and determined about Harry — I'm trying to encourage him and promised we'll both have partners when we get back to the common room.
metadata.source_text: “When we get back to the common room tonight, we’ll both have partners — agreed?”
metadata.scene_title: Festive atmosphere and Harry's failed attempt to ask Cho

metadata.description: I asked Cho Chang to the ball and found out she had already agreed to go with someone else.
metadata.source_text:
D’you — d’you want to go to the ball with me?" said Harry.

"Oh Harry, I’m really sorry," and she truly looked it. "I’ve already said I’ll go with someone else."
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I thought I might have a chance with Cho, but being turned down so plainly made me feel strangely hollow and a bit numb inside.
metadata.source_text: "Oh," said Harry. It was odd; a moment before his insides had been writhing like snakes, but suddenly he didn’t seem to have any insides at all.
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I now know Cho is going with Cedric Diggory, so she’s not available to me and that shifts how I see her in relation to me.
metadata.source_text: "Who’re you going with?" "Oh — Cedric," she said. "Cedric Diggory."
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I asked Fleur Delacour to the ball and she didn’t even answer properly — she just looked at me as if I were a sea slug.
metadata.source_text: "I asked her to go with me just now," Ron gasped. "She looked at me like I was a sea slug or something. Didn’t even answer."
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I keep thinking I’ve gone mad for asking Fleur — I’m convinced I behaved like a fool in front of everyone and that I’ll look stupid if I don’t find a partner.
metadata.source_text: "Why did I do it?" he said wildly. "I don’t know what made me do it!" ... "I’ve gone mad — everyone watching!"
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: When Hermione snapped that she’s already going with someone, I still can’t accept it and I’m suddenly seeing Hermione in a different light, like she’s clearly a girl I hadn’t noticed properly before.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione, Neville’s right — you are a girl. . . ." ... "Just because it’s taken you three years to notice, Ron, doesn’t mean no one else has spotted I’m a girl!"
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I wasn’t present for most of the conversation about the ball partners that happened before I arrived at the portrait hole, so I didn’t witness the earlier rejections and arrangements.
metadata.source_text: Hermione climbed in through the portrait hole. "Why weren’t you two at dinner?"
metadata.scene_title: Harry asks Cho and is turned down; friends scramble for partners

metadata.description: I've been warned someone put my name into the Goblet and they might be trying to hurt me; I'm supposed to keep my eyes open and stay out of trouble.
metadata.source_text: Whoever put your name in that goblet shouldn’t be feeling too happy right now! ... Keep your eyes open — particularly when the person we discussed is around — and concentrate on keeping yourself out of trouble.

metadata.description: I'm more uneasy now; even after beating the dragon I can't relax because whoever entered me in the tournament could try other things.
metadata.source_text: Don’t get complacent, though, Harry. You’ve only done one task; whoever put you in for the tournament’s got plenty more opportunity if they’re trying to hurt you.

metadata.description: Dobby's proper happy about socks and thinks I'm a great friend; I feel a soft spot for him when he cries with gratitude over simple gifts.
metadata.source_text: Dobby knew sir must be a great wizard, for he is Harry Potter’s greatest friend, but Dobby did not know that he was also as generous of spirit, as noble, as selfless —

metadata.description: I've realized that Harry still has two tasks left and he really ought to examine that golden egg to figure out what it means.
metadata.source_text: But he’s right, Harry, you have still got two tasks to do. You really ought to have a look at that egg, you know, and start working out what it means. . . .

metadata.description: I'm nervous but trying to be encouraging; even though I'm anxious about exams and appearances, I still think preparation is important for Harry.
metadata.source_text: But he’s right, Harry, you have still got two tasks to do. You really ought to have a look at that egg, you know, and start working out what it means. . . .

metadata.description: I came to the ball looking very different and I noticed people stared and reacted; I can tell Harry saw me as changed, which makes me aware of how others perceive me.
metadata.source_text: Hi, Harry! ... She was wearing robes made of a floaty, periwinkle-blue material... She was also smiling — rather nervously, it was true...

metadata.description: I've seen that Harry's survived the dragon and people are fussing over presents, and Dobby loves socks more than anything else — apparently they're his favourite clothes.
metadata.source_text: Socks are Dobby’s favorite, favorite clothes, sir!

metadata.description: I still think Harry's lucky with girls, but I'm embarrassed about my dress robes and tried to make them less dainty with a Severing Charm.
metadata.source_text: I still can’t work out how you two got the best-looking girls in the year," muttered Dean. "Animal magnetism," said Ron gloomily... he used a Severing Charm on the ruff and cuffs.

metadata.description: I gave Dobby socks and Mrs. Weasley's sweater; seeing him so grateful made me proud and a bit awkward about being praised as kind.
metadata.source_text: Sir is very kind!" he squeaked, his eyes brimming with tears again, bowing deeply to Ron.

metadata.description: I noticed Percy telling everyone he was Mr. Crouch’s personal assistant and that Crouch wasn’t well since the World Cup; Percy made a big point of representing him at the Ball.
metadata.source_text: I’m now Mr. Crouch’s personal assistant, and I’m here representing him.

metadata.description: I saw Dumbledore deliberately speak to his plate to call pork chops and make jokes about hidden rooms in Hogwarts — he’s playful and teasing even at dinner.
metadata.source_text: Pork chops!

metadata.description: I’m more aware that the Champions’ schools are different: Fleur brags about Beauxbatons’ glamour while Krum and Karkaroff hint at Durmstrang’s secrecy, which makes the contest feel bigger than just Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Ve have just four floors, and the fires are lit only for magical purposes... in summer ve are flying every day, over the lakes and the mountains —

metadata.description: I felt a bit awkward being paraded around the dance floor with Parvati, but the moment made me more conscious of how others watch me; I’m reminded people notice the champions and their partners.
metadata.source_text: Parvati had seized his hands, placed one around her waist, and was holding the other tightly in hers.

metadata.description: I taught Viktor to say my name slowly and clearly — I said it exactly: 'Her-my-oh-nee' to help him pronounce it properly.
metadata.source_text: “Her-my-oh-nee,” she said slowly and clearly.

metadata.description: I’m a bit embarrassed but not ashamed that I danced with Viktor; his attempts to speak to me in the library show he was shy and sincere, which changes my opinion of him slightly.
metadata.source_text: he — he said he’d been coming up to the library every day to try and talk to me, but he hadn’t been able to pluck up the courage!

metadata.description: I feel frustrated at Ron’s jealousy and his rude accusations about fraternizing with the enemy; it makes me see Ron as petulant and unfair in this moment.
metadata.source_text: He’s from Durmstrang! He’s competing against Harry! Against Hogwarts! You — you’re — fraternizing with the enemy, that’s what you’re doing!

metadata.description: I know that Viktor Krum is dancing with Hermione and that she’s been spending time with him in the library, which I find irritating and worrying.
metadata.source_text: He’s from Durmstrang! He’s competing against Harry! Against Hogwarts! You — you’re — fraternizing with the enemy, that’s what you’re doing!

metadata.description: I’ve become convinced that Hermione is somehow betraying Hogwarts by being friendly with Krum; I feel resentful and jealous, and my mind jumps to worst-case ideas.
metadata.source_text: He’s from Durmstrang! He’s competing against Harry! Against Hogwarts!

metadata.description: I’m sulking and giving Hermione the cold shoulder; our relationship feels strained because I’m angry and won’t explain why, which will probably push her away.
metadata.source_text: If you don’t know," said Ron scathingly, "I’m not going to tell you.

metadata.description: I heard Hagrid tell Madame Maxime that his mother was a giantess and that she left when he was very small — he said she was one of the last ones in Britain.
metadata.source_text: "It was my mother," said Hagrid quietly. "She was one o' the las' ones in Britain. 'Course, I can' remember her too well . . . she left, see. When I was abou' three."

metadata.description: I learned Hagrid's dad raised him but died just after Hagrid started at Hogwarts, and that Dumbledore helped him out when he was growing up.
metadata.source_text: "Dad raised me . . . but he died, o' course, jus' after I started school. Sorta had ter make me own way after that. Dumbledore was a real help, mind. Very kind ter me, he was. . . ."

metadata.description: I didn't know Hagrid was half-giant before — now I see a private, painful side of him; hearing his story makes me feel more protective and sorry for him.
metadata.source_text: "I jus' knew . . . knew you were like me. . . ."

metadata.description: I am furious that Ron would even suggest I would help Krum find out about Harry's egg — I want Harry to win and I resent being accused like that.
metadata.source_text: "For your information, he hasn't asked me one single thing about Harry, not one —"

metadata.description: I believe the whole point of the tournament is about getting to know other wizards and making friends — I said so hotly when Ron sneered at me.
metadata.source_text: "This whole tournament's supposed to be about getting to know foreign wizards and making friends with them!"

metadata.description: I feel deeply insulted by Ron's tone and his refusal to treat me with respect; his comment about asking me only as a last resort makes me determined to demand better from him in future.
metadata.source_text: "Next time there's a ball, ask me before someone else does, and not as a last resort!"

metadata.description: I reckon the Tournament is about winning, not making friends — I shouted that when Hermione argued it was about friendship.
metadata.source_text: "No it isn't!" shouted Ron. "It's about winning!"

metadata.description: I now know Hagrid is half-giant and that people will probably be uneasy about him because giants are supposed to be vicious; I think that's why Hagrid kept it secret.
metadata.source_text: "Did you know?" he whispered. "About Hagrid being half-giant?"

metadata.description: I'm angry and jealous about Hermione dancing with Krum and I said she'd better ask me before the next ball — my feelings toward her got more complicated and cross.
metadata.source_text: "Next time there's a ball, ask me before someone else does, and not as a last resort!"

metadata.description: I read that Rita Skeeter's article in the Daily Prophet claims Hagrid has been breeding dangerous creatures like "Blast-Ended Skrewts" and that he might be part-giant because his mother is the giantess Fridwulfa.
metadata.source_text: In a bizarre twist, Hagrid is reputed to have developed a close friendship with the boy who brought around You-Know-Who’s fall from power — thereby driving Hagrid’s own mother, like the rest of You-Know-Who’s supporters, into hiding.
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I'm shocked and unsettled — I hadn't thought Hagrid could be dangerous or part-giant, and Rita Skeeter's accusations make me question how others see him now.
metadata.source_text: DUMBLEDORE’S GIANT MISTAKE ... As if this were not enough, the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard. He is not, in fact, even pure human.
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I feel defensive of Hagrid and worried about what this article will do to his reputation and how people like Malfoy will use it to hurt him and me.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Harry Potter is unaware of the unpleasant truth about his large friend — but Albus Dumbledore surely has a duty to ensure that Harry Potter, along with his fellow students, is warned about the dangers of associating with part-giants.
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I've just learned from the paper that Hagrid has been accused of breeding illegal creatures called "Blast-Ended Skrewts" and that a reporter claims his mother is the giantess Fridwulfa.
metadata.source_text: the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard. He is not, in fact, even pure human. His mother, we can exclusively reveal, is none other than the giantess Fridwulfa
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I'm disturbed by how readily a sensational article like Rita Skeeter's can present half-truths and damage someone's reputation; I think we should check facts before believing everything printed.
metadata.source_text: DUMBLEDORE’S GIANT MISTAKE ... Rubeus Hagrid, who admits to being expelled from Hogwarts in his third year, has enjoyed the position of gamekeeper at the school ever since
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I still care about Hagrid and feel more protective; hearing such awful claims makes me more determined to defend him and question those who spread rumours.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Harry Potter is unaware of the unpleasant truth about his large friend — but Albus Dumbledore surely has a duty to ensure that Harry Potter, along with his fellow students, is warned about the dangers of associating with part-giants.
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I found out from the paper that Hagrid is being accused of terrifying the students with dangerous beasts and that a reporter says his mother was a giantess called Fridwulfa.
metadata.source_text: In a bizarre twist, Hagrid is reputed to have developed a close friendship with the boy who brought around You-Know-Who’s fall from power ... the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard.
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I'm gobsmacked and can't quite believe Rita Skeeter's story — it makes me more suspicious of how the Prophet portrays people and more worried about Hagrid being treated badly.
metadata.source_text: DUMBLEDORE’S GIANT MISTAKE ... Hagrid has maimed several pupils during a series of lessons that many admit to being 'very frightening.'
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I feel upset for Hagrid; he's our friend, and seeing his picture and those nasty claims makes me want to stick up for him, not believe the muck being printed.
metadata.source_text: There you go," he said. "Hate to break it to you, Potter. . . ." He smirked as Harry snatched the page, unfolded it, and read it
metadata.scene_title: Care of Magical Creatures Class Arrival and Daily Prophet Discovery

metadata.description: I learned from the Prophet that Hagrid’s mother is claimed to be the giantess Fridwulfa and that the paper says giants joined You-Know-Who and committed terrible attacks on Muggles.
metadata.source_text: As if this were not enough, the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard. He is not, in fact, even pure human. His mother, we can exclusively reveal, is none other than the giantess Fridwulfa, whose whereabouts are currently unknown.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I feel furious and unsettled — I can’t accept people saying Hagrid is brutal or dangerous just because of his mother. My trust in those rumours has collapsed; I don’t believe those claims about him.
metadata.source_text: But that wasn’t what was bothering Harry. “What d’you mean, ‘we all hate Hagrid’?” Harry spat at Malfoy.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m determined to stand by Hagrid. Hearing Malfoy mock him and suggest firing him makes me defend Hagrid even more; I see Malfoy as cruel and someone who’ll turn people against my friend.
metadata.source_text: “What d’you mean, ‘we all hate Hagrid’?” Harry spat at Malfoy.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’ve learned from the article that Fridwulfa is said to have been brutal and that giants allegedly fought among themselves and aided You-Know-Who, causing mass Muggle killings according to the Prophet.
metadata.source_text: Bloodthirsty and brutal, the giants brought themselves to the point of extinction by warring amongst themselves during the last century. The handful that remained joined the ranks of He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named, and were responsible for some of the worst mass Muggle killings of his reign of terror.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m disturbed by how quickly the press repeats accusations; I’m less inclined to accept everything printed as fact without checking evidence myself.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Harry Potter is unaware of the unpleasant truth about his large friend — but Albus Dumbledore surely has a duty to ensure that Harry Potter, along with his fellow students, is warned about the dangers of associating with part-giants.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m concerned for Hagrid and worried about how others will treat him because of this story; I feel the need to help protect him and to correct false impressions among students.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Harry Potter is unaware of the unpleasant truth about his large friend — but Albus Dumbledore surely has a duty to ensure that Harry Potter, along with his fellow students, is warned about the dangers of associating with part-giants.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I found out from what Harry read that the Prophet says Hagrid’s mother is a giantess named Fridwulfa and that giants supposedly fought for You-Know-Who and did terrible things.
metadata.source_text: As if this were not enough, the Daily Prophet has now unearthed evidence that Hagrid is not — as he has always pretended — a pure-blood wizard. He is not, in fact, even pure human. His mother, we can exclusively reveal, is none other than the giantess Fridwulfa, whose whereabouts are currently unknown.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m shocked and can’t quite believe how people are saying Hagrid is dangerous just because of his blood; I’m less willing to trust the Prophet’s nonsense after reading that.
metadata.source_text: Harry finished reading and looked up at Ron, whose mouth was hanging open.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m worried for Hagrid and feel like I need to stick up for him; seeing Malfoy laugh and Crabbe snigger makes me dislike how they treat my mates.
metadata.source_text: Crabbe was sniggering, apparently very pleased with himself.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Malfoy and Plans to Find Hagrid

metadata.description: I learned that when we went to Hagrid’s cabin at night, Fang answered and Hagrid didn’t — he didn’t open up or come to the door despite our shouting and pounding.
metadata.source_text: They knocked, and Fang’s booming barks answered. “Hagrid, it’s us!” Harry shouted, pounding on the door. “Open up!” Hagrid didn’t answer.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I’m starting to worry that Hagrid is avoiding us or is in trouble, because even after banging and shouting for ages he still didn’t answer and we saw no sign of him all week.
metadata.source_text: They hammered on it for ten more minutes; Ron even went and banged on one of the windows, but there was no response.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I feel more concerned about Hagrid now; he’s someone I want to check up on, and his silence makes me feel abandoned and anxious about his safety.
metadata.source_text: They didn’t see a sign of him all week.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I realised Hagrid didn’t answer when we knocked and that Fang was the only one making noise at the door while Hagrid stayed silent.
metadata.source_text: They knocked, and Fang’s booming barks answered. “Hagrid, it’s us!” Harry shouted, pounding on the door. “Open up!” Hagrid didn’t answer. They could hear Fang scratching at the door, whining, but it didn’t open.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I’ve changed my mind about what Hagrid might feel — I didn’t expect him to care about being thought of as half-giant, and his not answering makes me think he does worry about how others see him.
metadata.source_text: “What’s he avoiding us for?” Hermione said when they had finally given up and were walking back to the school. “He surely doesn’t think we’d care about him being half-giant?”
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I feel protective and puzzled about Hagrid; his silence suggests he’s more sensitive than I assumed, and I’m more inclined to defend or check on him now.
metadata.source_text: They didn’t see a sign of him all week.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I found out Hagrid didn’t answer the door even after we banged on it for ages and I even knocked on a window — only Fang made a fuss.
metadata.source_text: They hammered on it for ten more minutes; Ron even went and banged on one of the windows, but there was no response.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I’m bothered now — I didn’t expect Hagrid to be missing or to avoid us; his silence has made me think he might be upset or hiding for some reason.
metadata.source_text: They didn’t see a sign of him all week.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I’ve grown more worried about Hagrid and feel we should look out for him; he’s important to us, and his not being around all week makes me feel uneasy.
metadata.source_text: They didn’t see a sign of him all week.
metadata.scene_title: Deciding to Visit Hagrid and Finding Him Absent

metadata.description: I learned that Viktor Krum dives into the freezing lake straight from the Durmstrang ship in just swimming trunks — he really went and jumped in despite the January cold.
metadata.source_text: Viktor Krum emerge onto the deck, dressed in nothing but swimming trunks. He ... dived, right into the lake.
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I found out that Ludo Bagman was in the Three Broomsticks with a group of goblins and that the goblins were looking for Barty Crouch, who has apparently been absent from the Ministry.
metadata.source_text: She pointed into the mirror behind the bar, and Harry saw Ludo Bagman reflected there, sitting in a shadowy corner with a bunch of goblins... “They . . . er . . . they’re looking for Barty Crouch.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I’m more suspicious of Bagman now — he kept looking strained, slipped into a whisper about helping me with the egg, and seemed to be hiding things about Crouch and the goblins.
metadata.source_text: He was looking strained again... “Wonder if I could have a quick, private word, Harry?” ... “I feel very bad about all this . . . you were thrown into this tournament... if I can help at all . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation
