metadata.description: I feel less trusting of Bagman — even though he praised me for the dragon, his offer to help with the egg made me refuse him; I prefer help from people I actually trust.
metadata.source_text: “Listen, Harry,” he said... “if I can help at all . . . a prod in the right direction . . . I’ve taken a liking to you” ... “Well, thanks,” said Harry, “but I think I’m nearly there with the egg . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I’m angrier at Rita Skeeter than I was before; when she tried to chatter about Hagrid I couldn’t stand it and shouted that there’s nothing wrong with him, which shut the pub up.
metadata.source_text: Rita Skeeter... “Harry!” she said, beaming. “How lovely! Why don’t you come and join — ?” “I wouldn’t come near you with a ten-foot broomstick,” said Harry furiously. “What did you do that to Hagrid for, eh?” ... “Who cares if he’s half-giant?” Harry shouted. “There’s nothing wrong with him!”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I noticed that Viktor Krum probably finds the lake warmer than he would at home; I said it’s a lot colder here but it might feel quite warm to him.
metadata.source_text: “It’s a lot colder where he comes from,” said Hermione. “I suppose it feels quite warm to him.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I saw Ludo Bagman in the Three Broomsticks with goblins and heard from Harry that the goblins were looking for Barty Crouch, who hasn’t been coming into work and is supposedly ill.
metadata.source_text: She pointed into the mirror behind the bar, and Harry saw Ludo Bagman reflected there, sitting in a shadowy corner with a bunch of goblins... “They . . . er . . . they’re looking for Barty Crouch.” “He’s sort of . . . stopped coming to work. Been absent for a couple of weeks now.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I’m shocked and disapproving that Bagman would offer Harry help with the egg since he’s a judge; I think Dumbledore wouldn’t like that and it looks like cheating.
metadata.source_text: “He shouldn’t be doing that!” said Hermione, looking very shocked. “He’s one of the judges! And anyway, you’ve already worked it out — haven’t you?”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I feel protective of proper procedure and fairness; Bagman’s behaviour has lowered my opinion of him as someone who should act impartially in the Tournament.
metadata.source_text: “Well, I don’t think Dumbledore would like it if he knew Bagman was trying to persuade you to cheat!” said Hermione, still looking deeply disapproving.
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I’m aware that goblins are clever and capable of dealing with wizards; I compared them to house-elves and reminded Ron they don’t need protection like house-elves might.
metadata.source_text: “They’re very clever. They’re not like house-elves, who never stick up for themselves.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I noticed Viktor Krum dived into the freezing lake and I said there’s still the giant squid, mostly in a hopeful voice rather than worried about Krum’s safety.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah, but there’s still the giant squid,” said Ron. He didn’t sound anxious — if anything, he sounded hopeful.
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I heard Bagman say the goblins were looking for Barty Crouch and that Crouch has not been coming to the office for weeks and is supposedly ill.
metadata.source_text: “They . . . er . . . they’re looking for Barty Crouch.” “He’s sort of . . . stopped coming to work. Been absent for a couple of weeks now. Young Percy, his assistant, says he’s ill.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I joked that Percy might want Crouch out so he could get a promotion, which shows I’m suspicious about motives at the Ministry and think family might try to benefit.
metadata.source_text: “Maybe Percy’s poisoning him,” said Ron. “Probably thinks if Crouch snuffs it he’ll be made Head of the Department of International Magical Cooperation.”
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I don’t much care if Cedric gets help from Bagman — I said who cares if Diggory’s getting help, showing I’m more concerned with fairness only when it affects us directly.
metadata.source_text: “Who cares if Diggory’s getting help?” said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I saw Rita Skeeter enter wearing banana-yellow robes with shocking pink nails and a photographer, and I noticed she seemed pleased and ready to dig for a story.
metadata.source_text: Rita Skeeter had just entered. She was wearing banana-yellow robes today; her long nails were painted shocking pink, and she was accompanied by her paunchy photographer.
metadata.scene_title: Hogsmeade Visit, Bagman, and Rita Skeeter's Provocation

metadata.description: I saw Rita Skeeter pull out her Quick-Quotes Quill and start writing immediately after she started asking about Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: Rita Skeeter’s Quick-Quotes Quill was out; it was zooming backward and forward over a piece of parchment on the table.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I'm beginning to realise Rita Skeeter will target anyone connected to a story, even my friends; she isn't someone to be trusted and she'll use anything for a piece.
metadata.source_text: How about giving me an interview about the Hagrid you know, Harry? The man behind the muscles? Your unlikely friendship and the reasons behind it.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I feel protective about Hagrid and annoyed at Rita Skeeter for trying to make a story out of him and our friendship.
metadata.source_text: How about giving me an interview about the Hagrid you know, Harry? The man behind the muscles? Your unlikely friendship and the reasons behind it.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I've learned Rita Skeeter literally carries a Quick-Quotes Quill and uses it without hesitation to record sensational stories.
metadata.source_text: she snapped open her crocodile-skin handbag, pulled out her Quick-Quotes Quill, and said, “How about giving me an interview about the Hagrid you know, Harry?
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I'm furious and convinced Rita Skeeter cares only about a story and will hurt people to get one; I'm no longer prepared to tolerate her behaviour calmly.
metadata.source_text: You horrible woman, you don’t care, do you, anything for a story, and anyone will do, won’t they?
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I am more determined than ever to defend Hagrid; I won't let Rita upset him and I will go after her for what she did to him and to Harry.
metadata.source_text: And Hagrid isn’t hiding anymore! He should never have let that excuse for a human being upset him! Come on!
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I noticed Rita Skeeter was writing fast with her Quick-Quotes Quill after she started pestering Harry about Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: Rita Skeeter’s Quick-Quotes Quill was out; it was zooming backward and forward over a piece of parchment on the table.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I'm worried now that Rita Skeeter will dig up something on Hermione or anyone she can to get a story; she's dangerous in that way.
metadata.source_text: She’ll be after you next, Hermione ... I’m serious, Hermione, she’ll dig up something on you —
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hermione and uneasy about her wanting to confront Rita, because I think Rita could cause real trouble for her.
metadata.source_text: You don’t want to go upsetting Rita Skeeter ... I’m serious, Hermione, she’ll dig up something on you —
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Fury and Return to Hagrid's Cabin

metadata.description: I saw Dumbledore standing at Hagrid's doorway and know he invited us in and magicked tea and cakes onto the table.
metadata.source_text: “Good afternoon,” he said pleasantly, smiling down at them. “We — er — we wanted to see Hagrid,” said Hermione in a rather small voice. “Yes, I surmised as much,” said Dumbledore, his eyes twinkling. “Why don’t you come in?”
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I really don't care what Rita Skeeter writes; I won't let her words make me think less of Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: “You don’t think anything that Skeeter cow — sorry, Professor,” he added quickly, looking at Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hagrid and more determined to stand by him; seeing him upset made me furious and ready to defend him.
metadata.source_text: “Of course we still want to know you!” Harry said, staring at Hagrid.
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I realised Dumbledore was at the hut and that he invited us inside where he produced tea and cakes by magic.
metadata.source_text: “Good afternoon,” he said pleasantly, smiling down at them. “We — er — we wanted to see Hagrid,” said Hermione in a rather small voice.
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I felt how much Hagrid is missed; seeing him broken made me want him back teaching more than before.
metadata.source_text: “Come back and teach, Hagrid,” said Hermione quietly, “please come back, we really miss you.”
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I care deeply for Hagrid and am willing to speak up for him; he matters to me and I want him to stay.
metadata.source_text: “Er — right,” said Harry sheepishly. “I just meant — Hagrid, how could you think we’d care what that — woman — wrote about you?”
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore can produce a revolving tea tray and cakes with a flick of his wand.
metadata.source_text: “More tea, I think,” said Dumbledore, closing the door behind Harry, Ron, and Hermione, drawing out his wand, and twiddling it; a revolving tea tray appeared in midair along with a plate of cakes.
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I feel, as Hagrid hinted, that not everyone will always support you; I understand popularity isn't guaranteed even for good people.
metadata.source_text: “Not all of ’em,” said Hagrid hoarsely. “Not all of ’em wan’ me ter stay.”
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I'm on Hagrid's side and want him back; seeing him cry made me feel sorry and more loyal to him.
metadata.source_text: Two fat tears leaked out of Hagrid’s beetle-black eyes and fell slowly into his tangled beard.
metadata.scene_title: Revelation: Dumbledore, Hagrid Inside Cabin, and Reassurances

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid's father died in Hagrid's second year at school and that there is a photograph of Hagrid's young, beardless father sitting on Hagrid's shoulder.
metadata.source_text: Died, see, in me second year. . . . Hagrid got up, went over to his dresser, opened a drawer, and pulled out a picture of a short wizard with Hagrid’s crinkled black eyes, beaming as he sat on top of Hagrid’s shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I felt differently about Hagrid hearing him say he's been stupid and promising not to bother with her any more — it makes me see he's ashamed but determined to stand up for himself.
metadata.source_text: I’ve bin an idiot. I’m not botherin’ with her no more, I promise yeh that.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I realise Hagrid sees me as someone like him when he first arrived at Hogwarts — someone who felt like they wouldn't fit — and that he really wants me to win to prove a point about acceptance.
metadata.source_text: Yeh know wha’, Harry? ... when I firs’ met you, you reminded me o’ me a bit. Mum an’ Dad gone, an’ you was feelin’ like yeh wouldn’ fit in at Hogwarts, remember? ... Yeh know what I’d love, Harry? I’d love yeh ter win, I really would.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I noticed Hagrid was extremely upset and that my comforting — patting his arm — helped him steady enough to show us a photograph and talk about his past.
metadata.source_text: When the door had shut behind him, Hagrid began to sob into his dustbin-lid-sized hands. Hermione kept patting his arm, and at last, Hagrid looked up...
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I feel more sympathetic toward Hagrid now that I've seen him break down and talk about his father and Dumbledore's support; he isn't just a towering figure, he's vulnerable and grateful.
metadata.source_text: Tha’ was taken jus’ after I got inter Hogwarts... Dumbledore was the one who stuck up for me after Dad went. Got me the gamekeeper job...
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I've come to appreciate that Hagrid trusts Dumbledore deeply and that he respects Dumbledore for giving people second chances, which changes how I understand Hagrid's loyalty.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore was the one who stuck up for me after Dad went. Got me the gamekeeper job... Gives ’em second chances ... tha’s what sets him apar’ from other Heads...
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid's dad would have been ashamed of Hagrid's recent behaviour and that Hagrid's dad died in Hagrid's second year at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: ‘Ar, he’s righ’, o’ course — yeh’re all righ’ . . . I bin stupid . . . my ol’ dad woulda bin ashamed o’ the way I’ve bin behavin’. . . . Died, see, in me second year. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I feel sorry for Hagrid and I believe more strongly that Dumbledore does the right thing in trusting people and giving them second chances after hearing Hagrid praise him.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore was the one who stuck up for me after Dad went. Got me the gamekeeper job . . . trusts people, he does. Gives ’em second chances...
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I'm reminded that Hagrid sees Harry as someone like himself and wants Harry to win to prove that being not pureblood doesn't matter, which makes me respect Hagrid's faith in Dumbledore and Harry.
metadata.source_text: Yeh know wha’, Harry?... when I firs’ met you, you reminded me o’ me a bit... Yeh know what I’d love, Harry? I’d love yeh ter win, I really would. It’d show ’em all ... yeh don’ have ter be pureblood ter do it.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid Breaks Down, Dumbledore Refuses Resignation, and Encouragement

metadata.description: I'm saying I'm doing fine with the egg; I tell Hagrid, "Great," even if I'm not exactly shouting about it.
metadata.source_text: "Great," said Harry. "Really great."
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Hope for Harry and Closing Encouragement

metadata.description: Saying I'm "great" makes Hagrid light up, so I can see that my words can lift him; I guess I notice my answers affect how he feels.
metadata.source_text: "Great," said Harry. "Really great."
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Hope for Harry and Closing Encouragement

metadata.description: Hagrid looks at me with pride when I say I'm doing fine — he calls me "my boy" and cheers me on, so I know he believes in me and wants me to beat the others.
metadata.source_text: Tha’s my boy . . . you show ’em, Harry, you show ’em. Beat ’em all.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Hope for Harry and Closing Encouragement

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the exchange between Hagrid and Harry, so I don't know what was said or how they acted.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Hope for Harry and Closing Encouragement

metadata.description: I wasn't present for Hagrid's talk with Harry about the egg, so I can't report what happened or what was said.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Hope for Harry and Closing Encouragement

metadata.description: I learned the Triwizard egg sings underwater and its song said: "Come seek us where our voices sound," which made me realise the second task would involve creatures whose voices are heard below water.
metadata.source_text: “Come seek us where our voices sound, We cannot sing above the ground, And while you’re searching, ponder this: We’ve taken what you’ll sorely miss, An hour long you’ll have to look, And to recover what we took, But past an hour — the prospect’s black, Too late, it’s gone, it won’t come back.”

metadata.description: At first I was hoping for an easier clue, but after hearing the egg I started to think the task is underwater and realised I'm not a confident swimmer, which worries me a lot.
metadata.source_text:
Well, does anything in there have a human voice? Hang on —
...
“Underwater . . .” Harry said slowly.
...
“I’m not a very good swimmer; I’d never had much practice.

metadata.description: Moaning Myrtle annoyed me, but her help made me feel grudgingly grateful; she bossed me about and I thanked her even though I don't plan on visiting her bathroom often.
metadata.source_text:
“I’d try putting it in the water, if I were you.”
...
“See you, Myrtle . . . thanks for your help.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the prefects' bathroom or when Harry opened the Triwizard egg, so I don't know the details of the egg's song or the conversation with Moaning Myrtle.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there when Harry opened the egg underwater or when Filch found the egg near the stairs; I only waited at the portrait hole to give the Fat Lady the password and then went to bed.
metadata.source_text: This time it was Ron who waited outside to give the Fat Lady the password (“banana fritters”).

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the hallway disturbance involving Moody, Filch, Peeves, and Snape, so I don't have firsthand knowledge of the noises or the break-in.
I wasn't present for the incident where Moody, Filch, and Snape discussed Peeves and a possible break-in, so I cannot report direct observations from that moment.
I wasn't there when Moody, Filch, and Snape were arguing about Peeves throwing things and someone breaking into Snape's office, so I didn't see or hear what happened.
I wasn't present during these events; I did not witness the scene firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events; I did not witness the scene firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events; I did not witness the scene firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I've learned that Moody and others have been searching Snape's office; Moody mentioned Dumbledore only lets Snape stay because he's been given a second chance.
metadata.source_text: Moody said Dumbledore only lets Snape stay here because he’s giving him a second chance or something. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I'm more suspicious now — I don't trust Snape the way Hermione suggests; even if he saved me once, I still think he loathes me and targets me when he can.
metadata.source_text: Snape loved taking points from Harry, and had certainly never missed an opportunity to give him punishments, or even to suggest that he should be suspended from the school.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I feel less sure about Snape being on our side; my opinion shifted from confusion to distrust because of his past hostility and the fact everyone is searching him.
metadata.source_text: He, Ron, and Hermione were sitting at the very back of the Charms class... 'Moody said Dumbledore only lets Snape stay here because he’s giving him a second chance or something. . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I've noticed that Professor Flitwick gave cushions to everyone for Banishing practice to prevent accidents, but the plan isn't working because students are still sending things flying.
metadata.source_text: Owing to the potential for nasty accidents when objects kept flying across the room, Professor Flitwick had given each student a stack of cushions on which to practice, the theory being that these wouldn’t hurt anyone if they went off target.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I'm less willing to accept wild accusations against Snape just because people suspect him; remembering he once saved Harry makes me question quick judgments.
metadata.source_text: Oh Ron, we thought Snape was trying to kill Harry before, and it turned out he was saving Harry’s life, remember?
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I've reaffirmed trust in Dumbledore's judgement — I think Dumbledore was right to trust people like Hagrid and Lupin, so I give him the benefit of the doubt about Snape too.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore’s not stupid. He was right to trust Hagrid and Professor Lupin, even though loads of people wouldn’t have given them jobs, so why shouldn’t he be right about Snape, even if Snape is a bit —
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I've learned that Moody has been searching around and that people are suspicious enough to be asking if Snape put Harry's name in the Goblet of Fire.
metadata.source_text: Snape said Moody’s searched his office as well?... 'Harry . . . maybe Moody thinks Snape put your name in the Goblet of Fire!'
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I'm leaning toward thinking Snape might be guilty of something nasty — frankly, I think he might be up to something because loads of Dark-wizard catchers are searching his stuff.
metadata.source_text: Come on, Hermione, why are all these Dark wizard catchers searching his office, then?
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I still don't like Mr Crouch because of what happened with Winky, and that colours how I view these odd behaviours around the school.
metadata.source_text: You just don’t like Crouch because of that elf, Winky.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Class and Despair Over the Egg

metadata.description: I learned that Sirius only sent a very short message asking for the date of the next Hogsmeade weekend — nothing about the egg or how to survive underwater.
metadata.source_text: Send date of next Hogsmeade weekend by return owl.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I felt a quick spike of hope when the owl returned, but that hope died when I realised Sirius hadn't given any advice on the egg; I started to feel more alone and desperate about the clue.
metadata.source_text: The momentary happiness that had flared inside him at the sight of the owl had died.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I realise Sirius is reachable but not always helpful about the tasks I need him for; he can send a quick message, but I can't depend on him for detailed guidance right now.
metadata.source_text: Send date of next Hogsmeade weekend by return owl.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I've read the note over Harry's shoulder and learned that Sirius wants the date of the next Hogsmeade weekend sent back immediately.
metadata.source_text: Weekend after next," whispered Hermione, who had read the note over Harry’s shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I felt it necessary to help straight away — when Harry looked stuck, I offered my quill and urged him to send the reply without delay, showing I'm inclined to be practical and proactive.
metadata.source_text: Here — take my quill and send this owl back straight away.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I think of Harry as someone I must support closely; when he is down or preoccupied I step in to help with small practical things, like lending a quill so he can respond to Sirius.
metadata.source_text: Here — take my quill and send this owl back straight away.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I learned that Sirius's message only asked for the date of the next Hogsmeade weekend — I asked Harry why Sirius would want that information.
metadata.source_text: What's he want to know about the next Hogsmeade weekend for?" said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: Seeing Harry's downcast mood after the owl's arrival made me realise that a quick reply from Sirius wasn't enough to cheer him; I noticed Harry had expected more help.
metadata.source_text: The momentary happiness that had flared inside him at the sight of the owl had died.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I view Harry as someone who's bearing a heavy burden right now; even though I asked a simple question, I became aware he's distracted and not himself.
metadata.source_text: Dunno," said Harry dully.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Obsession with the Underwater Clue

metadata.description: I learned that the second task starts at ten past nine and the champions have exactly an hour to recover what was taken from them; I saw Bagman count down and announce the hour limit.
metadata.source_text: "They have precisely an hour to recover what has been taken from them."
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Sleepless Research, and Dobby's Warning

metadata.description: I was hopeless at first, thinking I couldn't do the task because I didn't know what to do, but when Dobby told me about gillyweed and that Ron had been taken, my doubts vanished and I decided I had to try.
metadata.source_text: "It’s too late, Dobby," Harry said hopelessly. "I’m not doing the task, I don’t know how —" ... "Dobby is quite sure, sir!" ... "Harry’s doubts vanished."
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Sleepless Research, and Dobby's Warning

metadata.description: Dobby helped me when I needed it; I feel grateful and trust him enough to take his gillyweed even though he has messed things up before.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby knew Harry had not found the right book, so Dobby did it for him!" and "Dobby is quite sure, sir!"
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Sleepless Research, and Dobby's Warning

metadata.description: I was not present with Hermione during these events at the lake and in the library, so I don't know what she did or thought here.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Sleepless Research, and Dobby's Warning

metadata.description: I was not with Ron during these events; I wasn't present when he was mentioned as being taken by the merpeople near the lake.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Sleepless Research, and Dobby's Warning

metadata.description: I found out my wand can blast out hot, scalding water underwater — it practically choked the grindylows and left them with angry red patches where it hit them.
metadata.source_text: A large bubble issued from his mouth, and his wand, instead of sending sparks at the grindylows, pelted them with what seemed to be a jet of boiling water, for where it struck them, angry red patches appeared on their green skin.
metadata.scene_title: Rushed Preparation and Arrival at the Task

metadata.description: I felt panic like I might be having a heart attack when something startled me, but seeing Myrtle calmed me enough to get moving again — I realised I could keep control if I stayed focused.
metadata.source_text: “How are you getting on?” Harry thought he was having a heart attack. He whipped around and saw Moaning Myrtle...
metadata.scene_title: Rushed Preparation and Arrival at the Task

metadata.description: I gave Myrtle a thumbs-up and felt grateful she helped by pointing the way, so I'm more willing to rely on odd allies like her in a pinch.
metadata.source_text: Harry gave her the thumbs-up to show his thanks and set off once more, careful to swim a bit higher over the weed to avoid any more grindylows...
metadata.scene_title: Rushed Preparation and Arrival at the Task

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Black Lake, so I don't know exactly what happened down there.
metadata.scene_title: Rushed Preparation and Arrival at the Task

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Black Lake, so I don't have firsthand knowledge of the underwater encounter.
metadata.scene_title: Rushed Preparation and Arrival at the Task

metadata.description: I saw a merpeople village with houses, weed gardens, and even a pet grindylow tied outside a door; the merpeople were watching me and pointing at my webbed hands and gills.
metadata.source_text: There were gardens of weed around some of them, and he even saw a pet grindylow tied to a stake outside one door. Merpeople were emerging on all sides now, watching him eagerly, pointing at his webbed hands and gills, talking behind their hands to one another.

metadata.description: I found a crude stone merperson statue in a village square with four people bound to its tail, all apparently asleep with bubbles issuing from their mouths.
metadata.source_text: A whole crowd of merpeople was floating in front of the houses that lined what looked like a mer-version of a village square. A choir of merpeople was singing in the middle, calling the champions toward them, and behind them rose a crude sort of statue; a gigantic merperson hewn from a boulder. Four people were bound tightly to the tail of the stone merperson.

metadata.description: I recognised Ron tied between Hermione and Cho Chang, and a small girl with silvery hair who looked like Fleur Delacour's sister; all four were in a deep sleep with streams of bubbles from their mouths.
metadata.source_text: Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang. There was also a girl who looked no older than eight, whose clouds of silvery hair made Harry feel sure that she was Fleur Delacour’s sister. All four of them appeared to be in a very deep sleep. Their heads were lolling onto their shoulders, and fine streams of bubbles kept issuing from their mouths.

metadata.description: I half-expected the merpeople to attack me the moment I swam up, but I realised they weren't lowering their spears or charging; that changed how dangerous and unpredictable I thought they were in this moment.
metadata.source_text: Harry sped toward the hostages, half expecting the merpeople to lower their spears and charge at him, but they did nothing.

metadata.description: Seeing Ron tied up between Hermione and Cho made me feel a sharper, more urgent need to get them free — Ron's presence there made this personal and immediate for me.
metadata.source_text: Ron was tied between Hermione and Cho Chang.

metadata.description: The ropes tying the hostages were made of thick, slimy weed and were very strong; I knew I didn't have the knife Sirius gave me because it was locked away in my trunk at the castle.
metadata.source_text: The ropes of weed tying the hostages to the statue were thick, slimy, and very strong. For a fleeting second he thought of the knife Sirius had bought him for Christmas — locked in his trunk in the castle a quarter of a mile away, no use to him whatsoever.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the underwater encounter at the merpeople village, so I don't know the details of what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the underwater encounter at the merpeople village, so I don't know the details of what happened there firsthand.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the underwater events in the merpeople village, so I can't describe what I saw there myself.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the underwater events in the merpeople village, so I can't describe what I saw there myself.

metadata.description: I learned that the merpeople refuse to help champions and will not lend their weapons — they make that clear: "We do not help."
metadata.source_text: “We do not help,” he said in a harsh, croaky voice.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I felt furious and more determined than ever that I shouldn't follow the merpeople's rules about only rescuing my own friend; I don't want anyone to die, not just Ron.
metadata.source_text: “No way!” said Harry furiously — but only two large bubbles came out.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I realised Hermione is as much my friend as Ron is — I shouted that she's my friend too, so I can't abandon her.
metadata.source_text: “She’s my friend too!” Harry yelled, gesturing toward Hermione, an enormous silver bubble emerging soundlessly from his lips.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I've discovered that the merpeople enforce a strict rule: each champion must retrieve only their own friend; they won't help with others.
metadata.source_text: “Your task is to retrieve your own friend . . . leave the others . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: Seeing the merpeople pull Harry away and laugh has made me realise their rules are heartless and they won't be persuaded by pleas — they stick to their own ways.
metadata.source_text: At once, several pairs of strong gray hands seized him. Half a dozen mermen were pulling him away from Hermione, shaking their green-haired heads, and laughing.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I sense that Harry cares for me strongly — he risked and fought to try to cut me free and shouted that I'm his friend as he was held back.
metadata.source_text: “She’s my friend too!” Harry yelled, gesturing toward Hermione, an enormous silver bubble emerging soundlessly from his lips.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I realised I was unconscious and floating just above the lake bottom after Harry hacked my bindings free; he managed to break the ropes and save me from being tied to the statue.
metadata.source_text: He began to hack at the ropes binding Ron, and after several minutes’ hard work, they broke apart. Ron floated, unconscious, a few inches above the lake bottom, drifting a little in the ebb of the water.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: Although I was out cold, the scene makes it clear to me that the merpeople won't help champions who try to free anyone but their own — their priority is odd and strict.
metadata.source_text: “Your task is to retrieve your own friend . . . leave the others . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: Even while unconscious, I am shown that Harry will risk fighting the merpeople for me and for Hermione; he struggled and shouted that he didn't want anyone to die.
metadata.source_text: “And I don’t want them to die either!” Cho’s head was on Hermione’s shoulder; the small silver-haired girl was ghostly green and pale.
metadata.scene_title: Merpeople Village, Hostages, and Rescue Attempts

metadata.description: I saw Cedric come swimming toward us inside a huge air bubble around his head, and he mouthed that he got lost and that Fleur and Krum were coming.
metadata.source_text: “Got lost!” he mouthed, looking panic-stricken. “Fleur and Krum’re coming now!”
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I was terrified about the time limit because my watch had stopped and the song said the hostages would be lost after an hour, so I believed we could actually lose people if rescue didn’t happen fast.
metadata.source_text: Time was getting short, and according to the song, the hostages would be lost after an hour. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I felt enormously relieved and grateful when Cedric appeared and freed Cho, which made me trust that other champions might still manage to help despite the chaos.
metadata.source_text: Feeling enormously relieved, Harry watched Cedric pull a knife out of his pocket and cut Cho free.
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I noticed Cedric come up with a big bubble around his head and mouth that he got lost, and I observed him cut Cho free and pull her upward out of sight.
metadata.source_text: “Got lost!” he mouthed, looking panic-stricken. “Fleur and Krum’re coming now!”
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I realised the situation was more urgent than I first thought when Harry’s watch stopped and the song warned hostages would be lost after an hour, so I believed we had to act very quickly.
metadata.source_text: He looked down at his watch to see how much time was left — it had stopped working. ... Time was getting short, and according to the song, the hostages would be lost after an hour. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: Seeing Cedric rescue Cho made me acknowledge that the other champions, like Cedric, Fleur, and Krum, were doing their best under pressure and could be relied on to try to save people.
metadata.source_text: Feeling enormously relieved, Harry watched Cedric pull a knife out of his pocket and cut Cho free. He pulled her upward and out of sight.
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I saw Cedric come up inside a huge bubble and mouth that he got lost and said Fleur and Krum were coming, and I saw Cedric cut Cho free and carry her away.
metadata.source_text: “Got lost!” he mouthed, looking panic-stricken. “Fleur and Krum’re coming now!”
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: Seeing Harry’s watch stopped and hearing the song’s warning that hostages would be lost after an hour made me believe we were running out of time and that panic was justified.
metadata.source_text: He looked down at his watch to see how much time was left — it had stopped working. ... Time was getting short, and according to the song, the hostages would be lost after an hour. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: Watching Cedric rescue Cho and the merpeople react, I realised the other champions might be more capable and resourceful than I had assumed, which changed how I felt about their chances.
metadata.source_text: Feeling enormously relieved, Harry watched Cedric pull a knife out of his pocket and cut Cho free. He pulled her upward and out of sight.
metadata.scene_title: Capture and Aid; Arrival of Cedric and Krum

metadata.description: I found out that mermen understand some basic commands or gestures even when I can only make bubbles, because when I shouted "Get out of the way!" they stopped laughing and fixed their eyes on my wand.
metadata.source_text: "Get out of the way!"
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I began to believe the mermen weren't particularly skilled with magic — they looked scared of my wand and I could tell they knew no more magic than the giant squid did.
metadata.source_text: because they suddenly stopped laughing. Their yellowish eyes were fixed upon Harry's wand, and they looked scared. There might be a lot more of them than there were of him, but Harry could tell, by the looks on their faces, that they knew no more magic than the giant squid did.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I feel increasingly responsible for Ron and Hermione; I rushed to help Hermione when Krum was about to hurt her, and I held off the mermen to protect Ron and the little girl as we struggled upward.
metadata.source_text: Darting forward, Harry hit Krum hard on the shoulder and held up the jagged stone. Krum seized it and began to cut Hermione free.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I learned that Krum's partial transfiguration into a shark made his teeth awkward for delicate biting — they were really meant for something bigger than a human.
metadata.source_text: The shark-man swam straight to Hermione and began snapping and biting at her ropes; the trouble was that Krum’s new teeth were positioned very awkwardly for biting anything smaller than a dolphin
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I realized that in this situation I needed others to act quickly to save me; Krum started to cut me free but only Harry's intervention ensured I was taken up toward the surface.
metadata.source_text: Within seconds, he had done it; he grabbed Hermione around the waist, and without a backward glance, began to rise rapidly with her toward the surface.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I now see Krum as dangerous and unpredictable when transformed; although he freed me, his shark-like teeth could have torn me apart if Harry hadn't acted.
metadata.source_text: The shark-man swam straight to Hermione and began snapping and biting at her ropes; the trouble was that Krum’s new teeth were positioned very awkwardly for biting anything smaller than a dolphin, and Harry was quite sure that if Krum wasn’t careful, he was going to rip Hermione in half.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I learned that the mermen will antagonize those they deem weaker or more vulnerable — they closed in around me and the little girl and were shaking their heads at Harry.
metadata.source_text: but the mermen now closed in around Ron and the little girl, shaking their heads at him.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I started to think that brute numbers don't always mean control — even though there were more mermen than Harry, they reacted to his wand with fear and hesitation.
metadata.source_text: There might be a lot more of them than there were of him, but Harry could tell, by the looks on their faces, that they knew no more magic than the giant squid did.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I feel more reliant on Harry's quick thinking; he threatened a countdown and held up fingers to control the mermen while we were still trapped underwater.
metadata.source_text: “You’ve got until three!” Harry shouted; a great stream of bubbles burst from him, but he held up three fingers to make sure they got the message.
metadata.scene_title: Final Rescues and Struggle to Surface

metadata.description: I learned I can force myself to surface even when my legs and shoulders are seizing and I can hardly breathe — I made it to the light and hauled Ron and the girl up with me.
metadata.source_text: And then he felt his head break the surface of the lake; wonderful, cold, clear air was making his wet face sting; he gulped it down, feeling as though he had never breathed properly before, and, panting, pulled Ron and the little girl up with him.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I felt stupid and annoyed afterwards — I thought I was doing the right thing, but I had to admit I’d acted like a prat for risking myself when the song was only to make sure we got back in time.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt both stupid and annoyed. It was all very well for Ron; he’d been asleep, he hadn’t felt how eerie it was down in the lake, surrounded by spear-carrying merpeople who’d looked more than capable of murder.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I couldn't leave Fleur’s sister because Fleur didn’t turn up; that made me feel responsible for Gabrielle, and I acted to bring her back even though I was terrified.
metadata.source_text: “Fleur didn’t turn up, I couldn’t leave her,” Harry panted.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I saw that Harry was utterly exhausted and nearly drowned before he reached the surface; he was forced into Madam Pomfrey’s care and given a very hot potion to recover.
metadata.source_text: Madam Pomfrey. She seized Harry and pulled him over to Hermione and the others, wrapped him so tightly in a blanket that he felt as though he were in a straitjacket, and forced a measure of very hot potion down his throat.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I now realise the task under the lake was more dangerous than I’d thought — the merpeople and grindylows were genuinely threatening, not just theatrics to worry us.
metadata.source_text: he hadn’t felt how eerie it was down in the lake, surrounded by spear-carrying merpeople who’d looked more than capable of murder.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I feel closer to Harry in the sense that I saw him risk himself for someone else; his exhaustion and determination made me recognise how committed he can be.
metadata.source_text: “C’mon,” Harry said shortly, “help me with her, I don’t think she can swim very well.”
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I learned Harry dragged me up and the little girl to the surface because he wouldn’t leave her; he really did go through the water to bring us back even though I’d been asleep.
metadata.source_text: Then he spotted Fleur’s sister. “What did you bring her for?” “Fleur didn’t turn up, I couldn’t leave her,” Harry panted.
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I changed how I see Harry’s actions — at first I mocked him for taking the song seriously, but seeing him panting and exhausted made me realise he’d risked himself for someone else.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, you prat,” said Ron, “you didn’t take that song thing seriously, did you? Dumbledore wouldn’t have let any of us drown!”
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I feel a sort of sheepish admiration for Harry now; he saved us and the girl, even if I complain about him being a prat about the instructions.
metadata.source_text: Ron merely expelled a great spout of water, blinked in the bright light, turned to Harry, and said, “Wet, this, isn’t it?”
metadata.scene_title: Rising with the Merpeople and Reaching Surface

metadata.description: I realised Dumbledore can speak Mermish — he was crouched at the water's edge making the same screechy noises as the merpeople and talking to their chief.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore was crouching at the water’s edge, deep in conversation with what seemed to be the chief merperson, a particularly wild and ferocious-looking female. He was making the same sort of screechy noises that the merpeople made when they were above water; clearly, Dumbledore could speak Mermish.

metadata.description: I started thinking Dumbledore's precautions must've meant no hostage could die just because a champion was late — so I felt stupid for not grabbing Ron and coming back quicker.
metadata.source_text: Now he was out of the water, it seemed perfectly clear that Dumbledore’s safety precautions wouldn’t have permitted the death of a hostage just because their champion hadn’t turned up. Why hadn’t he just grabbed Ron and gone? He would have been first back. . . .

metadata.description: I noticed Karkaroff watching me — he was the only judge not pleased — and I became aware that some judges, like him, might hold a poor opinion of me or be openly unfriendly.
metadata.source_text: He was the only judge who had not left the table; the only judge not showing signs of pleasure and relief that Harry, Ron, and Fleur’s sister had got back safely.

metadata.description: I know Harry found out how to rescue the hostages by himself — I told him so, cheering that he did it all on his own.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, well done!” Hermione cried. “You did it, you found out how all by yourself!”

metadata.description: I became annoyed with trifles in the moment — I brushed away the water beetle and focused on the timing, reminding Harry he was outside the time limit.
metadata.source_text: Harry had the impression that Krum was drawing her attention back onto himself; perhaps to remind her that he had just rescued her from the lake, but Hermione brushed away the beetle impatiently and said, “You’re well outside the time limit, though, Harry. . . . Did it take you ages to find us?”

metadata.description: I showed gratitude and relief that Harry had rescued us, and I spoke to him directly and warmly in the aftermath, acknowledging his success despite my practical concerns.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, well done!” Hermione cried. “You did it, you found out how all by yourself!”

metadata.description: I had to be rescued and Madam Pomfrey gave me a blanket and Pepperup Potion when she fetched me from Percy’s clutches — I was cold and needed fixing up.
metadata.source_text: Madam Pomfrey had gone to rescue Ron from Percy’s clutches; she led him over to Harry and the others, gave him a blanket and some Pepperup Potion, then went to fetch Fleur and her sister.

metadata.description: I felt a bit proud and hopeful about helping — I said I helped 'a bit' and looked really hopeful when Fleur kissed Harry and thanked him.
metadata.source_text: “And you too — you ’elped —” “Yeah,” said Ron, looking extremely hopeful, “yeah, a bit —”

metadata.description: I recognised Harry's role in saving Fleur’s sister and felt closer to him for what he did, even if I only helped a little.
metadata.source_text: “You saved ’er,” she said breathlessly. “Even though she was not your ’ostage.” “Yeah,” said Harry, who was now heartily wishing he’d left all three girls tied to the statue. Fleur bent down, kissed Harry twice on each cheek... “And you too — you ’elped —” “Yeah,” said Ron, looking extremely hopeful, “yeah, a bit —”

metadata.description: I've learned that Snape thinks things have been taken from his private stores — boomslang skin and gillyweed — and he believes I was near his office the night it was broken into.
metadata.source_text: "Boomslang skin. Gillyweed. Both come from my private stores, and I know who stole them."

metadata.description: I feel even more convinced now that Snape hates me and will seize any excuse to punish me; his threats and the way he read the article made me angrier and more certain he's out to get me.
metadata.source_text: "To me, Potter, you are nothing but a nasty little boy who considers rules to be beneath him."

metadata.description: I'm aware Sirius still looks out for me; he turned up in the cave, ate the food I brought, and acts like my godfather who wants to protect me from whatever's brewing in the papers.
metadata.source_text: "Fulfilling my duty as godfather," said Sirius, gnawing on the chicken bone in a very doglike way.

metadata.description: I've learned that Viktor Krum asked me to visit him in Bulgaria over the summer right after he pulled me out of the lake and after Madam Pomfrey gave us blankets.
metadata.source_text: "He asked me right after he’d pulled me out of the lake," Hermione muttered. "After he’d got rid of his shark’s head. Madam Pomfrey gave us both blankets and then he sort of pulled me away from the judges so they wouldn’t hear, and he said, if I wasn’t doing anything over the summer, would I like to —"

metadata.description: I'm worried and puzzled now because Rita Skeeter seems to know private things — I didn't tell anyone about Viktor's invitation, so I suspect someone overheard or spied on us at the second task.
metadata.source_text: "How could Rita Skeeter have known . . . ?"

metadata.description: I feel unfairly attacked and annoyed by Rita Skeeter; her article makes me look scandalous and ridiculous, and it angers me that others, like Pansy, are speculating nastily about me.
metadata.source_text: "If that’s the best Rita can do, she’s losing her touch," said Hermione, still giggling, as she threw Witch Weekly onto the empty chair beside her. "What a pile of old rubbish."

metadata.description: I've learned that Viktor Krum asked Hermione to visit him over the summer and that he said he'd never felt this way about any other girl, and Hermione blushed when she explained it.
metadata.source_text: "He asked me right after he’d pulled me out of the lake," Hermione muttered ... "and he did say he’d never felt the same way about anyone else," Hermione went on, going so red now that Harry could almost feel the heat coming from her,

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more protective about Hermione because Rita Skeeter has made her out to be a 'scarlet woman' in the paper, and I keep thinking I told her not to annoy Rita.
metadata.source_text: "I told you!" Ron hissed at Hermione as she stared down at the article. "I told you not to annoy Rita Skeeter! She’s made you out to be some sort of — of scarlet woman!"

metadata.description: I still care about Hermione a lot and feel embarrassed and defensive when others mock her; seeing her upset and blushing made me react strongly and lose my temper a bit.
metadata.source_text: "If that’s the best Rita can do, she’s losing her touch," said Hermione, still giggling ... "I told you!" Ron hissed at Hermione as she stared down at the article.

metadata.description: I read that Barty Crouch hasn’t been seen in public since November, his house looks deserted, and the Ministry refuses to confirm rumors of his critical illness — it’s all in the paper I was reading.
metadata.source_text: hasn’t been seen in public since November . . . house appears deserted . . . St. Mungo’s Hospital for Magical Maladies and Injuries decline comment . . . Ministry refuses to confirm rumors of critical illness.

metadata.description: I noticed Winky the house-elf was in the Top Box saving Crouch a seat at the World Cup and she was later found holding my wand after the Dark Mark appeared.
metadata.source_text: You first saw the elf in the Top Box. She was saving Crouch a seat, right? ... Winky being found with Harry’s wand clutched in her hand

metadata.description: I’m starting to think my wand might have been taken in the Top Box — the idea that whoever conjured the Dark Mark stole my wand there actually makes sense now.
metadata.source_text: Are you saying whoever conjured the Mark stole my wand in the Top Box? ... It’s possible

metadata.description: I’m more suspicious of people who sat near us at the Cup — names like the Malfoys and Ludo Bagman stick in my head as possible leads.
metadata.source_text: The Malfoys! ... I don’t know anything about Bagman ... We saw him in the forest just before the Dark Mark appeared

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the conversation Sirius had about Barty Crouch and his son, so I didn't witness the full exchange or hear all the details firsthand.
I’ve learned that Barty Crouch sacked his house-elf Winky after the Quidditch World Cup, apparently because she hadn’t stayed in her tent and got trampled.
metadata.source_text: Crouch sacked his house-elf? ... He sacked her, just because she hadn’t stayed in her tent and let herself get trampled

metadata.description: I don’t believe Winky could have conjured the Dark Mark or stolen Harry’s wand — it’s more likely someone else there did it, like Ludo Bagman.
metadata.source_text: Winky didn’t steal that wand! ... It’s more likely he did it than Winky

metadata.description: I feel even more strongly that house-elves matter and that Crouch treated Winky badly — his treatment of his servant shows a lot about him.
metadata.source_text: I bet he wishes he hadn’t done it now — bet he feels the difference now she’s not there to look after him. ... If you want to know what a man’s like, take a good look at how he treats his inferiors

metadata.description: I wasn't in the scene where Sirius described Barty Crouch's actions and his son's fate, so I can't recount those events from being present there.
My brother said Crouch’s personal assistant told him Crouch is suffering from overwork, so people are saying he’s ill or worn out.
metadata.source_text: My brother’s Crouch’s personal assistant ... He says Crouch is suffering from overwork.

metadata.description: I suddenly reckon Lucius Malfoy might be involved — when I thought about who was near us in the Top Box, Malfoy jumped out at me as a likely suspect.
metadata.source_text: The Malfoys! ... I bet it was Lucius Malfoy!

metadata.description: I’m annoyed at Hermione for going on about house-elves all the time — I called her obsessed and gave her a dark look when she kept pushing the point.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s obsessed with house-elves ... Hermione’s obsessed with house-elves, Ron muttered to Sirius, casting Hermione a dark look.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during Sirius's account of Barty Crouch sending his son to Azkaban, so I didn't directly witness the events he described.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I learned Winky has been drinking a lot of butterbeer and is now so unhappy she’s collapsed from it.
metadata.source_text: Winky is getting through six bottles a day now," Dobby whispered to Harry.

metadata.description: I found out Winky still thinks Mr. Crouch is her master and won’t accept Professor Dumbledore as master.
metadata.source_text: Winky wants to go home. Winky still thinks Mr. Crouch is her master, sir, and nothing Dobby says will persuade her that Professor Dumbledore is her master now.

metadata.description: I’m thinking maybe asking Winky about Mr. Crouch could help — I wondered aloud if she knew where Mr. Crouch was because he’d stopped turning up to judge the Tournament.
metadata.source_text: you don’t know what Mr. Crouch might be up to, do you? Because he’s stopped turning up to judge the Triwizard Tournament.

metadata.description: I feel Dobby is loyal and grateful to me; he called out my name and thanked me for the socks while standing by Winky.
metadata.source_text: Thank you for the socks, Harry Potter!" Dobby called miserably from the hearth

metadata.description: I learned that nifflers love sparkly stuff and will dig up buried treasure if you set them loose — they really go for gold coins when you let them into fresh earth.

metadata.description: I've learned that Rita Skeeter wrote an article calling me "disturbed and dangerous" and claiming I collapsed at school and that my scar still hurts.
metadata.source_text: HARRY POTTER “DISTURBED AND DANGEROUS” The boy who defeated He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named is unstable and possibly dangerous, writes Rita Skeeter, Special Correspondent. Alarming evidence has recently come to light about Harry Potter’s strange behavior, which casts doubts upon his suitability to compete in a demanding competition like the Triwizard Tournament, or even to attend Hogwarts School. Potter, the Daily Prophet can exclusively reveal, regularly collapses at school, and is often heard to complain of pain in the scar on his forehead (relic of the curse with which You-Know-Who attempted to kill him).

metadata.description: I found out the article accused me of speaking Parseltongue and hinted I'm connected to werewolves and giants, which makes people suspect me of Dark Arts sympathies.
metadata.source_text: “Potter can speak Parseltongue,” reveals Draco Malfoy, a Hogwarts fourth year. “There were a lot of attacks on students a couple of years ago, and most people thought Potter was behind them after they saw him lose his temper at a dueling club and set a snake on another boy.... Parseltongue, the ability to converse with snakes, has long been considered a Dark Art.... Similarly, “anyone who seeks out the company of such vicious creatures as werewolves and giants would appear to have a fondness for violence.”

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that people like Malfoy will use anything to humiliate me — even twisting what I do or what happens to me into stories to make me look dangerous.
metadata.source_text: “Gone off me a bit, hasn’t she?” said Harry lightly, folding up the paper.

A twenty-foot-high hedge ran all the way around the edge of it. There was a gap right in front of them: the entrance to the vast maze.”

metadata.source_text: “Surprise!” Mrs. Weasley said excitedly as he smiled broadly and walked over to them. “Thought we’d come and watch you, Harry!”

metadata.description: I've realised Rita Skeeter might have been able to listen at Harry’s open window and report his scar hurting, which suggests she used some secret listening method.
metadata.source_text: “How did she know your scar hurt in Divination?” Ron said.... “The window was open,” said Harry. “I opened it to breathe.” “You were at the top of North Tower!” Hermione said. “Your voice couldn’t have carried all the way down to the grounds!” ... “I’ve had an idea,” Hermione said, gazing into space.

metadata.description: I'm angrier about Rita Skeeter now; I think she goes out of her way to cause trouble and may be using underhand methods to get stories.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter goes out of her way to cause trouble, Amos!” Mrs. Weasley said angrily.

metadata.description: I knew the article would damage people like Ludo Bagman and that Rita’s stories could twist trials and statements into scandalous gossip.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter,” she muttered finally. “How can you be worrying about her now?” said Ron.... “This is what she meant, isn’t it? She reported his trial, she knew he’d passed information to the Death Eaters. And Winky too, remember . . . ‘Ludo Bagman’s a bad wizard.’

metadata.description: I'm convinced prejudice from people like Fudge can make them jump to conclusions about giants and treat innocent people unfairly.
metadata.source_text: “Look what happened to Hagrid when Rita found out about his mother. Look at Fudge, jumping to conclusions about her, just because she’s part giant. Who needs that sort of prejudice?”

metadata.description: I care enough about Harry and the others to risk missing an exam to check the library for evidence against Rita — that shows how strongly I want to help them.
metadata.source_text: “Just give me two seconds in the library — just to make sure!” With that, Hermione seized her school bag and dashed out of the Great Hall.

metadata.description: I've learned that Dumbledore reckons You-Know-Who’s getting stronger again — and we talked over nearly everything Harry saw in the Pensieve.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore reckons You-Know-Who’s getting stronger again as well?” Ron whispered. Everything Harry had seen in the Pensieve... he had now shared with Ron and Hermione

metadata.description: I'm beginning to take Rita Skeeter seriously as a nuisance; her stories upset people and have caused arguments like the one about the Triwizard champions.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter goes out of her way to cause trouble, Amos!” Mrs. Weasley said angrily. “I would have thought you’d know that, working at the Ministry!”

metadata.description: I felt protective of Harry when Malfoy mocked him with the paper — I don't like seeing my mate humiliated in front of everyone.
metadata.source_text: “Hey, Potter! Potter! How’s your head? You feeling all right? Sure you’re not going to go berserk on us?” Malfoy was holding a copy of the Daily Prophet too. Slytherins up and down the table were sniggering

metadata.description: I saw Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle acting suspiciously by a tree and heard Malfoy speaking into his hand like a walkie-talkie, which looked really dodgy.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle were standing in the shadow of a tree below. Crabbe and Goyle seemed to be keeping a lookout; both were smirking. Malfoy was holding his hand up to his mouth and speaking into it.

metadata.description: I'm more annoyed with reporters like Rita and with people who jump to conclusions about giants after what happened with Hagrid and Madame Maxime.
metadata.source_text: “Of course she doesn’t,” said Hermione sharply... “Look what happened to Hagrid when Rita found out about his mother. Look at Fudge, jumping to conclusions about her, just because she’s part giant.”

metadata.description: I learned that the Four-Point Spell can tell me rough cardinal directions in the maze, though it can mislead me when paths force me off-course.
metadata.source_text: “Point Me,” he whispered to his wand, holding it flat in his palm. The wand spun around once and pointed toward his right, into solid hedge.

metadata.description: I found out that a Patronus works on dementors even here in the maze — a silver stag burst out of my wand and drove the creature back.
metadata.source_text: He summoned the happiest thought he could... raised his wand, and cried, “Expecto Patronum!” A silver stag erupted from the end of Harry’s wand and galloped toward the dementor, which fell back

metadata.description: I discovered that things that look like dementors might be boggarts in disguise, because after the stag attacked I shouted Riddikulus and the thing exploded into smoke.
metadata.source_text: “Hang on!” he shouted... “You’re a boggart! Riddikulus!” There was a loud crack, and the shape-shifter exploded in a wisp of smoke.

metadata.description: I learned the golden mist can invert gravity — when I ran through it the world flipped and I was hanging from the ground, so it's more than a visual enchantment.
metadata.source_text: He took a deep breath and ran through the enchanted mist. The world turned upside down. Harry was hanging from the ground, with his hair on end

metadata.description: I learned Blast-Ended Skrewts are huge and dangerous — Stupefy bounces off their armor but hitting the soft underside can stop one, at least for a short time.
metadata.source_text: He rounded another corner and found himself facing a Blast-Ended Skrewt... “Stupefy!” The spell hit the skrewt’s armor and rebounded... “IMPEDIMENTA!” The skrewt was inches from him when it froze — he had managed to hit it on its fleshy, shell-less underside.

metadata.description: I felt the maze was trying to lull me into a false sense of safety — after too much empty path I started to think it was deliberately making me let my guard down.
metadata.source_text: The path ahead was empty too... the lack of obstacles was unnerving him. Surely he should have met something by now? It felt as though the maze were luring him into a false sense of security.

metadata.description: I realized Cedric trusts me enough for me to try and rescue him — after I stunned Krum he recovered and we spoke; he was grateful and shaken, and I grabbed his arm to help him up.
metadata.source_text: Harry dashed over to Cedric... “Are you all right?” Harry said roughly, grabbing Cedric’s arm. “Yeah,” panted Cedric.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the maze events, so I don't know the specifics of what happened inside the maze.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the tasks in the maze and can't report on the encounters or rescues that took place.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 (Part 1) occurred.
I found out that saying 'Point Me' makes my wand physically point me along the maze — it spun and sent me down the right-hand path toward the light.
metadata.source_text: "Point Me!" he whispered again to his wand, and it spun around and pointed him to the right-hand one.

metadata.description: I learned that the Disarming Spell 'Expelliarmus' can make a huge magical creature drop someone it's holding, because when I shouted it, the spider dropped me.
metadata.source_text: "Expelliarmus!" It worked — the Disarming Spell made the spider drop him

metadata.description: I thought winning would be about getting to the Cup first and the glory that comes with it, but after Cedric's refusal to take the Cup alone I changed my mind and agreed we should both take it.
metadata.source_text: "You take it. You should win. That’s twice you’ve saved my neck in here." ... "Both of us," Harry said.

metadata.description: I'm seeing Cedric as fair and honorable — he won't accept the Cup even though he's closer; he keeps saying I should take it because I helped him, and that changes how I feel about him.
metadata.source_text: "You take it. You should win. That’s twice you’ve saved my neck in here."

metadata.description: I've learned I've got a sprained ankle and I'm bleeding after the spider attack; my leg shakes when I put weight on it and I'm struggling to stand properly.
metadata.source_text: it shook violently as he put weight on it; he had sprained his ankle when the spider had dropped him.

metadata.description: For a moment I pictured myself coming out of the maze holding the Cup and hearing the crowd and Cho's admiration, but then I changed my mind and decided we should share it instead.
metadata.source_text: For one shining moment, he saw himself emerging from the maze, holding it. He saw himself holding the Triwizard Cup aloft, heard the roar of the crowd, saw Cho’s face shining with admiration, more clearly than he had ever seen it before . . . and then the picture faded

metadata.description: I've realised Cedric's decent and stubborn in a way that makes me want to respect him; after everything we've done for each other I felt we should take the Cup together.
metadata.source_text: You — you sure? "Yeah," said Harry. "Yeah . . . we’ve helped each other out, haven’t we? We both got here. Let’s just take it together."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 (Part 1) occurred.
I wasn't present during the events in the maze, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
I wasn't present during the events in the maze or at the Triwizard Cup, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
I was not present when Part 3 (Part 1) occurred.
I wasn't present during the events in the maze, so I wasn't there to witness the confrontation with the spider or Cedric's actions.
I wasn't present during the moments when Harry and Cedric reached the Cup, so I didn't witness their decision to take it together.
