I was not present when Arrival in the Graveyard occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I noticed someone was coming; I could tell from the way they were walking and holding their arms that they were carrying something, maybe a baby or just a bundle of robes.
metadata.source_text: Someone’s coming," he said suddenly. ... from the way it was walking and holding its arms, he could tell that it was carrying something. ... Harry saw that the thing in the person’s arms looked like a baby . . . or was it merely a bundle of robes?

metadata.description: I kept feeling we were being watched — that uneasy feeling got stronger and made me announce the approach; I'm more convinced now that we weren't alone out there.
metadata.source_text: He had, yet again, the strange feeling that they were being watched. "Someone’s coming," he said suddenly.

metadata.description: I glanced at Cedric when I lowered my wand and he looked back at me quizzically; I realised we're both sharing the same uncertainty and watching the same strange thing together.
metadata.source_text: Harry lowered his wand slightly and glanced sideways at Cedric. Cedric shot him a quizzical look.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard scene, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard scene, so I can't report any direct observations from that moment.
My scar exploded with pain and I learned that the pain is a signal tied to something dangerous: it was agony like I'd never felt before and it coincided with a voice saying, "Kill the spare."
metadata.source_text: And then, without warning, Harry’s scar exploded with pain.

metadata.description: I believed I was fighting in a contest, but that belief changed in an instant when Cedric was hit by a killing curse; I can't think of the Triwizard tasks the same way after seeing him dead.
metadata.source_text: Cedric was lying spread-eagled on the ground beside him. He was dead.

metadata.description: Seeing Cedric's dead, surprised face has made everything about him feel immediate and horribly personal to me; I can't see him as just a fellow champion anymore — he's been killed beside me.
metadata.source_text: For a second that contained an eternity, Harry stared into Cedric’s face, at his open gray eyes, blank and expressionless as the windows of a deserted house, at his half-open mouth, which looked slightly surprised.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there from personal observation.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there from personal observation.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there from personal observation.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there from personal observation.

metadata.description: I saw the name TOM RIDDLE on the headstone flickering in my wandlight before I was forced around and slammed against it.
metadata.source_text: Harry saw the name upon it flickering in the wandlight before he was forced around and slammed against it.

metadata.description: I realized who was under the hood — Wormtail — and that changed everything for me in that instant; I gasped, 'You!' when I knew who had bound me.
metadata.source_text: And Harry realized who was under the hood. It was Wormtail. “You!” he gasped.

metadata.description: I now see Wormtail as my captor and betrayer up close: he has a missing finger, he breathes shallow and fast, and he tied me so tightly I couldn’t move an inch — I can't trust him at all.
metadata.source_text: The cloaked man was now conjuring tight cords around Harry, tying him from neck to ankles to the headstone. Harry could hear shallow, fast breathing from the depths of the hood; he struggled, and the man hit him — hit him with a hand that had a finger missing.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the headstone, so I don't know what happened first-hand.
I wasn't present at the moment when Harry was bound to the headstone, so I can't report any direct observations.
I can see Cedric's body lying about twenty feet away and the Triwizard Cup glinting in the starlight beyond him; my wand is on the ground at Cedric's feet.
metadata.source_text: Cedric’s body was lying some twenty feet away. Some way beyond him, glinting in the starlight, lay the Triwizard Cup. Harry’s wand was on the ground at Cedric’s feet.

metadata.description: I noticed a bundle of robes at the foot of the grave that I first thought was a baby, and it's stirring fretfully while something inside struggles to free itself.
metadata.source_text: The bundle of robes that Harry had thought was a baby was close by, at the foot of the grave. It seemed to be stirring fretfully.

metadata.description: I heard noises and then saw a gigantic snake slithering through the grass, circling the headstone where I was tied.
metadata.source_text: He looked down and saw a gigantic snake slithering through the grass, circling the headstone where he was tied.

metadata.description: I saw Wormtail pushing a huge stone cauldron to the foot of the grave, full of sloshing liquid and big enough for a full-grown man to sit in.
metadata.source_text: Then he came back within Harry’s range of vision, and Harry saw him pushing a stone cauldron to the foot of the grave. It was full of what seemed to be water — Harry could hear it slopping around — and it was larger than any cauldron Harry had ever used; a great stone belly large enough for a full-grown man to sit in.

metadata.description: My scar sears again and I'm terrified; I suddenly know I don't want the bundle opened — I don't want to see what's in those robes.
metadata.source_text: Harry watched it, and his scar seared with pain again . . . and he suddenly knew that he didn’t want to see what was in those robes . . . he didn’t want that bundle opened. . . .

metadata.description: Wormtail's wheezy breathing and his actions make him seem more threatening to me; I can tell he's up to something cruel by the way he forces the heavy cauldron along.
metadata.source_text: Wormtail’s fast, wheezy breathing was growing louder again. It sounded as though he was forcing something heavy across the ground. Then he came back within Harry’s range of vision, and Harry saw him pushing a stone cauldron to the foot of the grave.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Harry couldn’t make a sound, nor could he see where Wormtail had gone; he couldn’t turn his head to see beyond the headstone; he could see only what was right in front of him.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the graveyard, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Harry couldn’t make a sound, nor could he see where Wormtail had gone; he couldn’t turn his head to see beyond the headstone; he could see only what was right in front of him.

metadata.description: I saw Wormtail working at the bottom of the cauldron with a wand while the liquid in the cauldron heated unbelievably fast and began to send out fiery sparks.
metadata.source_text: Now Wormtail was busying himself at the bottom of the cauldron with a wand. The liquid in the cauldron seemed to heat very fast. The surface began not only to bubble, but to send out fiery sparks, as though it were on fire.

metadata.description: Hearing that high, cold voice made me feel more certain that something dangerous and urgent was happening; the voice changed the scene from odd to outright threatening.
metadata.source_text: And Harry heard the high, cold voice again. “Hurry!”

metadata.description: Seeing Wormtail so frantic and hidden under robes, and hearing the cold voice command him, I feel more wary of Wormtail and the people he serves — I don’t trust the situation around him.
metadata.source_text: Steam was thickening, blurring the outline of Wormtail tending the fire. The movements beneath the robes became more agitated.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the cauldron scene, so I don't have direct knowledge of what Wormtail did or said.
metadata.source_text: Now Wormtail was busying himself at the bottom of the cauldron with a wand.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the cauldron and the sudden flames, so I can't say I witnessed the potion heating or the high, cold voice.
metadata.source_text: The surface began not only to bubble, but to send out fiery sparks, as though it were on fire.

metadata.description: I saw Wormtail reveal something that looked like a crouched human child but was hideous — hairless, scaly, dark reddish-black, with thin limbs and a flat, snakelike face with gleaming red eyes.
metadata.source_text: Wormtail pulled open the robes on the ground, revealing what was inside them, and Harry let out a yell that was strangled in the wad of material blocking his mouth.

metadata.description: I believed there were terrible things, but seeing that creature made me know how utterly monstrous some dark magics can be; it's worse than anything I imagined and it terrified me.
metadata.source_text: It was hairless and scaly-looking, a dark, raw, reddish black. Its arms and legs were thin and feeble, and its face — no child alive ever had a face like that — flat and snakelike, with gleaming red eyes.

metadata.description: Seeing Wormtail lift that thing and the look of revulsion on his face made me realise Wormtail isn't proud of what he's doing; he seems weak and sickened, not a willing, happy servant.
metadata.source_text: As he did so, his hood fell back, and Harry saw the look of revulsion on Wormtail’s weak, pale face in the firelight as he carried the creature to the rim of the cauldron.

metadata.description: I was not present during these events and cannot describe them firsthand.
I was not present during these events and cannot describe them firsthand.
I learned that Wormtail can perform a dark ritual using bone, flesh and blood to renew someone; he spoke the words aloud while he put those things into a cauldron.
metadata.source_text: Bone of the father, unknowingly given, you will renew your son!
metadata.scene_title: The Ritual: Bone, Flesh, and Blood

metadata.description: I no longer think I can stop everything; tied up and forced to watch, I felt utterly helpless and that my attempts to intervene were useless in the face of that ritual.
metadata.source_text: Harry could do nothing to prevent it, he was tied too tightly.
metadata.scene_title: The Ritual: Bone, Flesh, and Blood

metadata.description: I've seen Wormtail's true, pathetic role — he's terrified and degrading himself to revive his master; I now see him as a frightened, desperate lackey rather than just an enemy's follower.
metadata.source_text: Wormtail was whimpering. He pulled a long, thin, shining silver dagger... His voice broke into petrified sobs.
metadata.scene_title: The Ritual: Bone, Flesh, and Blood

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the forest, so I don't know what happened at the ritual.
metadata.scene_title: The Ritual: Bone, Flesh, and Blood

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the forest, so I don't know what happened at the ritual.
metadata.scene_title: The Ritual: Bone, Flesh, and Blood

metadata.description: I saw the liquid inside the cauldron turn instantly blinding white and send diamond sparks everywhere, so bright they turned everything else to velvety blackness.
metadata.source_text: The liquid within turned, instantly, a blinding white. ... The cauldron was simmering, sending its diamond sparks in all directions, so blindingly bright that it turned all else to velvety blackness.

metadata.description: I found myself wishing the whole thing had failed — I really wanted it to have gone wrong rather than see whatever came next.
metadata.source_text: Nothing happened. . . . Let it have drowned, Harry thought, let it have gone wrong. . . .

metadata.description: I watched Wormtail drop to his knees and then slump, cradling his bleeding stump, and seeing him like that makes me view him as desperate and pathetic rather than simply obedient.
metadata.source_text: Wormtail, his job done, dropped to his knees beside the cauldron, then slumped sideways and lay on the ground, cradling the bleeding stump of his arm, gasping and sobbing.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know what happened in that moment.
I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't have direct knowledge of the steam and what followed the cauldron's reaction.
I thought whatever was in the water might be dead — I really believed it had drowned.
metadata.source_text: it’s drowned . . . please . . . please let it be dead. . . .

metadata.description: I went from hoping it was dead to being terrified when I saw a tall dark man in the mist — my fear jumped straight up into icy terror.
metadata.source_text: But then, through the mist in front of him, he saw, with an icy surge of terror, the dark outline of a man, tall and

metadata.description: I no longer feel safe or uncertain about what I faced; seeing a man's outline made me feel directly threatened by a person, not just by some drowned thing.
metadata.source_text: But then, through the mist in front of him, he saw, with an icy surge of terror, the dark outline of a man, tall and

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the mist and water, so I don't know what happened there.
I wasn't present at the scene by the misty water, so I don't have any firsthand account of the moment.
I learned that Voldemort will force me to perform submissive acts — he demanded I bow and used magic to bend my spine, just to humiliate me.
metadata.source_text: “We bow to each other, Harry,” said Voldemort, bending a little, but keeping his snakelike face upturned to Harry. “Come, the niceties must be observed. . . . Dumbledore would like you to show manners. . . . Bow to death, Harry. . . .”

metadata.description: I found out how vicious the Cruciatus Curse is — it feels like white-hot knives and makes you scream as though your head will burst.
metadata.source_text: The pain was so intense, so all-consuming, that he no longer knew where he was. . . . White-hot knives were piercing every inch of his skin, his head was surely going to burst with pain, he was screaming more loudly than he’d ever screamed in his life

metadata.description: I believed for a moment I was going to die like Cedric; those pitiless red eyes of Voldemort made me feel utterly hopeless, but I also resolved not to beg or obey him.
metadata.source_text: He was going to die like Cedric, those pitiless red eyes were telling him so . . . he was going to die, and there was nothing he could do about it . . . but he wasn’t going to play along. He wasn’t going to obey Voldemort . . . he wasn’t going to beg. . . .

metadata.description: I now see Voldemort as someone who revels in my suffering and uses obedience as punishment; he delights in torturing me while the Death Eaters laugh.
metadata.source_text: The Death Eaters were laughing again. Voldemort’s lipless mouth was smiling. ... "That hurt, didn’t it, Harry? You don’t want me to do that again, do you?"

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the graveyard confrontation, so I do not know the moment-to-moment details of Voldemort's taunts or the Cruciatus effects firsthand.
I wasn't present at the graveyard duel; I didn't witness Voldemort forcing Harry to bow, the Cruciatus pain, or Harry's shouted defiance.
I learned that when my and Voldemort's spells collided the connection between our wands formed a golden, webbed cage of light that lifted us both and played a phoenix song.
metadata.source_text: A jet of green light issued from Voldemort’s wand just as a jet of red light blasted from Harry’s — they met in midair — and suddenly Harry’s wand was vibrating as though an electric charge were surging through it; ... a narrow beam of light connected the two wands, neither red nor green, but bright, deep gold.

metadata.description: I realized I wouldn't simply crouch and wait to die; I must stand and try to defend myself even against impossible odds, following my father's example.
metadata.source_text: he was not going to die crouching here like a child playing hide-and-seek; he was not going to die kneeling at Voldemort’s feet . . . he was going to die upright like his father, and he was going to die trying to defend himself, even if no defense was possible.

metadata.description: I felt something like a friend inside the music of the golden web—the phoenix song made me think of Dumbledore and gave me hope and strength when Voldemort tried to force the connection.
metadata.source_text: It was a sound Harry recognized, though he had heard it only once before in his life: phoenix song. It was the sound of hope to Harry . . . He felt as though the song were inside him instead of just around him. . . . It was the sound he connected with Dumbledore, and it was almost as though a friend were speaking in his ear.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the graveyard, so I don't know the specifics of what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the graveyard, so I don't have firsthand knowledge of the confrontation between Harry and Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I learned that forcing a bead of light back along a golden thread can reconnect my wand to Voldemort's and make his wand expel those he's killed — they came out like solid smoke.
metadata.source_text: one of the beads of light was quivering, inches from the tip of Voldemort’s wand. Harry didn’t understand why he was doing it, didn’t know what it might achieve . . . but he now concentrated as he had never done in his life on forcing that bead of light right back into Voldemort’s wand . . . and slowly . . . very slowly . . . it moved along the golden thread . . . and then it connected. . . . At once, Voldemort’s wand began to emit echoing screams of pain . . . then — Voldemort’s red eyes widened with shock — a dense, smoky hand flew out of the tip of it and vanished . . . the ghost of the hand he had made Wormtail . . . more shouts of pain . . . and then something much larger began to blossom from Voldemort’s wand-tip

metadata.description: I learned that the shades of Voldemort’s victims can speak to me through that connection, giving me information and urging actions while they circle the duel.
metadata.source_text: Voldemort’s dead victims whispered as they circled the duelers, whispered words of encouragement to Harry, and hissed words Harry couldn’t hear to Voldemort.

metadata.description: I never expected the people Voldemort killed to come out of his wand; seeing Cedric, my parents, and others made me believe there was still some way to get help from them in the fight.
metadata.source_text: the thick gray ghost of Cedric Diggory ... emerged in its entirety from the end of Voldemort’s wand ... the smoky shadow of a young woman with long hair ... the smoky, shadowy form of James Potter blossomed from the end of Voldemort’s wand

metadata.description: Seeing my parents appear and speak to me changed things — I felt them close and protective in a way I hadn't before; my father's quiet command to run felt like a direct trust in me.
metadata.source_text: Your father’s coming. . . . Hold on for your father. . . . When the connection is broken, we will linger for only moments . . . but we will give you time . . . you must get to the Portkey, it will return you to Hogwarts . . . do you understand, Harry?

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the graveyard, so I do not know the details of what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I was not present at the duel in the graveyard and therefore did not witness Voldemort's wand expelling his victims or Harry's retrieval actions.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present

metadata.description: I found out that the Triwizard Cup was a Portkey and it transported Cedric and me to a graveyard where Lord Voldemort was waiting.
metadata.source_text: Cup was a Portkey," said Harry as they crossed the entrance hall. "Took me and Cedric to a graveyard . . . and Voldemort was there . . . Lord Voldemort . . .

metadata.description: I saw Voldemort take things from his father's grave, from Wormtail, and from me to get his body back.
metadata.source_text: "He took stuff from his father’s grave, and from Wormtail, and me," said Harry.

metadata.description: I learned that Cedric Diggory was killed there; he's dead and I couldn't save him despite holding him.
metadata.source_text: "Killed Cedric . . . they killed Cedric. . . ."

metadata.description: I saw Death Eaters alongside Voldemort when he returned — there were loads of them.
metadata.source_text: "And the Death Eaters came . . . and then we dueled. . ." "Yes," said Harry. "Loads of them . . ."

metadata.description: I believe Voldemort has truly returned — he's not just a story anymore; he's come back with a body and followers.
metadata.source_text: "The Dark Lord got his body back? He’s returned?" "And the Death Eaters came . . . and then we dueled. . ."

metadata.description: I now feel that someone at Hogwarts must have helped the plot against me — there's a Death Eater here who put my name in the Goblet of Fire.
metadata.source_text: "There’s a Death Eater at Hogwarts! There’s a Death Eater here — they put my name in the Goblet of Fire, they made sure I got through to the end —"

metadata.description: I've just learned that the man I thought was Moody handed me over to Voldemort and used tricks so I would reach the Cup and be delivered to him.
metadata.source_text: I gave you to him — the thing he needed above all to regenerate — and then I killed you for him.

metadata.description: I believed Alastor Moody was a protector; now I can't trust that person at all — I realise the Moody I knew wasn't Moody at all.
metadata.source_text: This is not Alastor Moody.

metadata.description: My view of supposed allies is shaken: Dobby and others were used as pawns, and someone I trusted betrayed me, so I feel more wary of who is really loyal.
metadata.source_text: I called the elf to the staffroom to collect some robes for cleaning. I staged a loud conversation... and your little elf friend ran straight to Snape’s office and then hurried to find you.

metadata.description: I feel that Dumbledore is taking charge and looking after everyone; I now believe adults are acting quickly and responsibly to get help for Moody and to deal with Crouch.
metadata.source_text: please tell Madam Pomfrey to come down here; we need to get Alastor Moody into the hospital wing.

metadata.description: I sense Dumbledore cares about me — he spoke my name gently and is personally taking me upstairs, which makes me feel he is protective and attentive toward me.

metadata.description: I noticed the pain in my leg had come back in full; I hadn't felt it while listening to Crouch, but now it's there and I can feel myself swaying.
metadata.source_text: the pain in his leg, which he had not noticed all the time he had been listening to Crouch, now returned in full measure.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Brought to the Office — Dazed, Phoenix Comforts Him

metadata.description: I'm feeling numb and unreal, and strangely I'm glad of that numbness because it keeps me from facing everything properly right now.
metadata.source_text: A kind of numbness and a sense of complete unreality were upon him, but he did not care; he was even glad of it.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Brought to the Office — Dazed, Phoenix Comforts Him

metadata.description: Dumbledore steadied me and took my arm to help me out; I see him as someone who looks after me in moments when I can't manage alone.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore gripped his arm and helped him out into the dark corridor.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Brought to the Office — Dazed, Phoenix Comforts Him

metadata.description: I saw Voldemort rise again from the steaming cauldron and watched Wormtail slumped on the ground with his arm ruined; I also found Cedric dead and he begged to be returned to his parents.
metadata.source_text: Mad-Eye Moody, inside the trunk. Wormtail, slumped on the ground, cradling his stump of an arm. Voldemort, rising from the steaming cauldron. Cedric . . . dead . . . Cedric, asking to be returned to his parents. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry Reluctant to Remember — Dumbledore Requests the Truth

metadata.description: I don't want to pretend everything is fine anymore; the things I've seen have left me exhausted and I want to stop thinking, but I know I can't avoid telling what happened.
metadata.source_text: He didn’t want to have to think about anything that had happened since he had first touched the Triwizard Cup. He didn’t want to have to examine the memories, fresh and sharp as photographs, which kept flashing across his mind.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Reluctant to Remember — Dumbledore Requests the Truth

metadata.description: I felt deep gratitude toward Sirius when he put a hand on my shoulder and tried to make Dumbledore leave me to sleep; his concern comforts me when I'm shattered.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt a rush of gratitude toward Sirius, but Dumbledore took no notice of Sirius’s words. He leaned forward toward Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Reluctant to Remember — Dumbledore Requests the Truth

metadata.scene_title: Harry Reluctant to Remember — Dumbledore Requests the Truth

metadata.description: I saw the potion that brought Voldemort back; I can picture its sparkling surface and I remember Cedric's body lying beside the cup.
metadata.source_text: he saw the sparkling surface of the potion that had revived Voldemort; he saw the Death Eaters Apparating between the graves around them; he saw Cedric’s body, lying on the ground beside the cup.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Relates Priori Incantatem and Echoes

metadata.description: I feel like telling everything is helping me; once I started I felt as if something poisonous was being extracted from me, and I believe I'll feel better when I've finished.
metadata.source_text: It was even a relief; he felt almost as though something poisonous were being extracted from him. It was costing him every bit of determination he had to keep talking, yet he sensed that once he had finished, he would feel better.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Relates Priori Incantatem and Echoes

metadata.description: Sirius's reaction shows he cares fiercely — his hand was tight on my shoulder and he let out a vehement exclamation when I said Wormtail pierced my arm.
metadata.source_text: Once or twice, Sirius made a noise as though about to say something, his hand still tight on Harry’s shoulder... When Harry told of Wormtail piercing his arm with the dagger, however, Sirius let out a vehement exclamation
metadata.scene_title: Harry Relates Priori Incantatem and Echoes

metadata.description: I learned that Voldemort said my blood would make him stronger and that he could touch me because of my mother’s protection inside me.
metadata.source_text: “He said my blood would make him stronger than if he’d used someone else’s,” Harry told Dumbledore. “He said the protection my — my mother left in me — he’d have it too. And he was right — he could touch me without hurting himself, he touched my face.”
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: I discovered the name of the strange magical effect when our wands connected: Priori Incantatem — the Reverse Spell effect made echoes of people Voldemort had killed appear.
metadata.source_text: “Priori Incantatem,” he muttered. His eyes gazed into Harry’s and it was almost as though an invisible beam of understanding shot between them. “The Reverse Spell effect?” said Sirius sharply. “Exactly,” said Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: I found out that my wand and Voldemort’s share cores: feathers from the same phoenix — Fawkes — and that explains why the wands produced those reverse echoes.
metadata.source_text: “Harry’s wand and Voldemort’s wand share cores. Each of them contains a feather from the tail of the same phoenix. This phoenix, in fact,” he added, and he pointed at the scarlet-and-gold bird, perching peacefully on Harry’s knee. “My wand’s feather came from Fawkes?” Harry said, amazed. “Yes,” said Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: I learned that the echoes showed the last spells Voldemort’s wand performed in reverse order, so Cedric’s echo and then older shadows came out while our wands were linked.
metadata.source_text: “They will not work properly against each other,” said Dumbledore. “If, however, the owners of the wands force the wands to do battle . . . a very rare effect will take place. One of the wands will force the other to regurgitate spells it has performed — in reverse. The most recent first . . . and then those which preceded it. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: I learned the echoes included Cedric, Bertha Jorkins, and my parents; Cedric’s echo even spoke to me and made a final request.
metadata.source_text: “An old man,” Harry said, his throat still constricted. “Bertha Jorkins. And . . .” “Your parents?” said Dumbledore quietly. “Yes,” said Harry. ... Harry described how the figures that had emerged from the wand had prowled the edges of the golden web, how Voldemort had seemed to fear them, how the shadow of Harry’s father had told him what to do, how Cedric’s had made its final request.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: I had to accept that Voldemort is back — I saw him return and I know he’s regained a body; I can’t just let people pretend otherwise.
metadata.source_text: “I saw Voldemort come back!” Harry shouted. He tried to get out of bed again, but Mrs. Weasley forced him back. “I saw the Death Eaters! I can give you their names! Lucius Malfoy —”
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.description: Sirius is someone I want near me, but Dumbledore sent him away to warn others; I know Sirius cares and will act for the fight, even if he must leave now.
metadata.source_text: “You’ll see me very soon, Harry,” said Sirius, turning to him. “I promise you. But I must do what I can, you understand, don’t you?” “Yeah,” said Harry. “Yeah . . . of course I do.”
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Heals Harry — Minister Arrives, Confrontation Ensues

metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events in the hospital wing and the Triwizard aftermath, so I do not have an eyewitness account of what happened there.

metadata.description: I was given one thousand Galleons as prize money; Dumbledore or Fudge left a large bag of gold on my bedside table as my winnings.
metadata.source_text: “Your winnings,” he said shortly, taking a large bag of gold out of his pocket and dropping it onto Harry’s bedside table. “One thousand Galleons.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I feel that I shouldn't have kept the prize; I believe the gold belongs to Cedric because he ought to have won instead of me.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t want that gold,” said Harry in an expressionless voice. “You have it. Anyone can have it. I shouldn’t have won it. It should’ve been Cedric’s.”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I trust Sirius and want him near me; when he promises to see me soon I feel some comfort even though he has to leave at once.
metadata.source_text: “You’ll see me very soon, Harry,” said Sirius, turning to him. “I promise you. But I must do what I can, you understand, don’t you?”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I've seen Dumbledore insist that enemies like Sirius and Snape at least pretend to cooperate, because the situation needs everyone who knows the truth to act together.
metadata.source_text: “Time is short, and unless the few of us who know the truth stand united, there is no hope for any of us.”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I am now more convinced that unity is necessary even between people who loathe one another; Dumbledore's demand that Sirius and Snape shake hands shows how serious things are.
metadata.source_text: “I trust you both. It is time for you to lay aside your old differences and trust each other.”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I recognize that Sirius is being treated as an ally by Dumbledore and that opinions of him among adults have shifted enough that he's invited and given tasks.
metadata.source_text: “He is here at my invitation,” said Dumbledore, looking between them, “as are you, Severus.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I saw Sirius turn from a big black dog into a man right in front of us; Mrs Weasley screamed when she recognized him as Sirius Black.
metadata.source_text: “Sirius . . . if you could resume your usual form.” The great black dog looked up at Dumbledore, then, in an instant, turned back into a man. Mrs Weasley screamed and leapt back from the bed. “Sirius Black!” she shrieked, pointing at him.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I feel defensive of my mum and startled by Sirius's return; hearing Mum scream made me tell her to shut up, but I also tried to calm things by saying it's okay.
metadata.source_text: “Mum, shut up!” Ron yelled. “It’s okay!”
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: Sirius's presence has shifted how I see him — he's not just a wanted man in stories anymore but someone Dumbledore trusts and who says he'll look out for Harry.
metadata.source_text: “You’ll see me very soon, Harry,” said Sirius, turning to him. “I promise you.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Consolation — Mrs Weasley Comforts Him

metadata.description: I learned that Cedric died after winning the tournament and someone said he suffered very little at the end.
metadata.source_text: “He suffered very little then,” she said, when Harry had told her how Cedric had died.

metadata.description: I feel colder about going home — even a beautiful summer’s day doesn’t cheer me up; Privet Drive won’t be any comfort to me right now.
metadata.source_text: It was another beautiful summer’s day. He supposed that Privet Drive would be hot and leafy, its flower beds a riot of color, when he arrived there that evening. The thought gave him no pleasure at all.

metadata.description: I felt Hagrid’s support — his hug and words made me feel like he truly sees what I did and thinks I acted like my father would have.
metadata.source_text: “Yeh did as much as yer father would’ve done, an’ I can’ give yeh no higher praise than that.”

metadata.description: I've seen Dumbledore speak to the school and urge everyone to remember Cedric Diggory and what happens when someone crosses Lord Voldemort’s path.
metadata.source_text: “Remember Cedric. Remember, if the time should come when you have to make a choice between what is right and what is easy, remember what happened to a boy who was good, and kind, and brave, because he strayed across the path of Lord Voldemort. Remember Cedric Diggory.”

metadata.description: I'm more aware now that darker and more difficult times are coming and that many families have been torn apart — I hoped I was wrong, but Dumbledore says we face real danger.
metadata.source_text: “It is my belief — and never have I so hoped that I am mistaken — that we are all facing dark and difficult times. Some of you in this Hall have already suffered directly at the hands of Lord Voldemort. Many of your families have been torn asunder.”

metadata.description: I recognize Harry’s burden more clearly after hearing Dumbledore and seeing Hagrid’s pride in him; Harry’s actions are being openly valued by adults like Hagrid and Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: “Yeh did as much as yer father would’ve done, an’ I can’ give yeh no higher praise than that.”

metadata.description: I learned Madame Maxime was at Hagrid’s earlier because Hagrid said he’d been having a cuppa with Olympe and she’d just left.
metadata.source_text: “Bin havin’ a cuppa with Olympe,” Hagrid said. “She’s jus’ left.”

metadata.description: Hagrid’s certainty that Voldemort would return and that they must fight makes me take the threat more seriously — it’s not just talk anymore.
metadata.source_text: “Knew he was goin’ ter come back,” said Hagrid, and Harry, Ron, and Hermione looked up at him, shocked. “Known it fer years, Harry. Knew he was out there, bidin’ his time. It had ter happen. Well, now it has, an’ we’ll jus’ have ter get on with it. We’ll fight.”

metadata.description: Seeing Hagrid so proud of Harry and hearing Dumbledore’s speech made me respect Harry’s role more; he’s carrying something big and people notice.
metadata.source_text: “Remember Cedric. Remember ... Remember Cedric Diggory.”

metadata.description: I've seen Fleur hurry back to Madame Maxime and heard her say she's hoping to get a job here to improve her English.
metadata.source_text: “I am ’oping to get a job ’ere, to improve my Eenglish.”

metadata.description: I learned that Krum said Diggory was always polite to him, which makes me remember how people treated Cedric.
metadata.source_text: “I liked Diggory,” said Krum abruptly to Harry. “He vos alvays polite to me. Alvays.”

metadata.description: I found out from Hermione that Rita Skeeter is an unregistered Animagus who can turn into a beetle and has been spying to get stories.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter isn’t going to be writing anything at all for a while. Not unless she wants me to spill the beans on her.”

metadata.description: I’m more certain now that the Daily Prophet isn’t telling the whole truth about the tournament and Cedric’s death — I suspect official pressure is keeping things quiet.
metadata.source_text: “If you ask me, Fudge is forcing them to keep quiet.”

metadata.description: Seeing Krum shake my hand made me feel he respects me; he spoke about Cedric kindly and was polite when he left.
metadata.source_text: He held out his hand as Fleur had done, shook Harry’s hand, and then Ron’s.

metadata.description: I've discovered that Rita Skeeter is an unregistered Animagus who transforms into a beetle, and I actually caught her on the hospital-wing windowsill.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter isn’t going to be writing anything at all for a while. Not unless she wants me to spill the beans on her.”

metadata.description: I've confirmed that the beetle markings match Rita’s glasses, and that beetles have been present at several important moments this year.
metadata.source_text: “Look very closely, and you’ll notice the markings around her antennae are exactly like those foul glasses she wears.”

metadata.description: I've put an Unbreakable Charm on the jar so Rita can’t transform, and I intend to keep her from writing for a year to stop her spreading lies.
metadata.source_text: “I’ve put an Unbreakable Charm on the jar, you see, so she can’t transform. And I’ve told her she’s to keep her quill to herself for a whole year.”

metadata.description: I believe the Daily Prophet is being silenced by the Ministry, and it’s unacceptable that they’ve barely mentioned Cedric after the third task.
metadata.source_text: “There’s nothing in there. You can look for yourself, but there’s nothing at all. I’ve been checking every day. Just a small piece the day after the third task saying you won the tournament. They didn’t even mention Cedric.”

metadata.description: I now see Malfoy and certain Slytherins as willing accomplices to Rita, giving her gossip and lies without caring about legality.
metadata.source_text: “He knew, of course. That’s how she’s been getting all those nice little interviews with the Slytherins.”

metadata.description: I noticed Fleur hoped to find a job in England to improve her English — she was polite when she said goodbye to Harry.
metadata.source_text: “I am ’oping to get a job ’ere, to improve my Eenglish.”

metadata.description: Krum said he liked Cedric and that Cedric was always polite to him, which made me think about how decent Cedric was.
metadata.source_text: “I liked Diggory,” said Krum abruptly to Harry. “He vos alvays polite to me. Alvays.”

metadata.description: Hermione caught Rita Skeeter as a beetle; she’s unregistered and’s been buzzing around listening to private stuff for stories.
metadata.source_text: “Rita Skeeter isn’t going to be writing anything at all for a while. Not unless she wants me to spill the beans on her.”

metadata.description: I’m more convinced now that the Daily Prophet isn’t reporting properly about the tournament, and that people like Fudge might be controlling the press.
metadata.source_text: “If you ask me, Fudge is forcing them to keep quiet.”

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione calmly reveal and control Rita made me respect her cleverness and determination more than before.
metadata.source_text: Hermione took the glass jar back from Ron and smiled at the beetle, which buzzed angrily against the glass.

metadata.description: I just found out Bagman put a big bet on me to win the tournament outright, trying to pay off his debts.
metadata.source_text: He put a bet on you, mate," said Fred. "Put a big bet on you to win the tournament.

metadata.description: I'm surprised and a bit furious to learn Bagman was betting on me; I didn't realize anyone would gamble on my performance like that.
metadata.source_text: So that's why he kept trying to help me win!" said Harry.

metadata.description: I'm uneasy about Bagman now — he sounds dishonest and desperate, using me to cover his debts to goblins.
metadata.source_text: He put a bet on you, mate," said Fred. "Put a big bet on you to win the tournament. Bet against the goblins.

metadata.description: I've learned that the leprechaun gold the twins were paid vanished by the next morning and that they believed Bagman was responsible.
metadata.source_text: So, the git paid us in leprechaun gold he’d caught from the Irish mascots." "So?" "So," said Fred impatiently, "it vanished, didn’t it? By next morning, it had gone!

metadata.description: I thought the disappearance might have been an accident at first, but the twins' story makes me see Bagman could have been deliberately avoiding them.
metadata.source_text: "But — it must’ve been an accident, mustn’t it?" said Hermione.

metadata.description: I now regard Bagman as unreliable and possibly culpable in the twins' loss; he avoided them and made excuses instead of settling the matter.
metadata.source_text: Ignored our letter. We kept trying to talk to him about it at Hogwarts, but he was always making some excuse to get away from us.

metadata.description: I learned that the twins were paid in leprechaun gold and that the gold disappeared by morning, leaving them out of their savings.
metadata.source_text: Well, the git paid us in leprechaun gold he’d caught from the Irish mascots." "So?" "So," said Fred impatiently, "it vanished, didn’t it? By next morning, it had gone!

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and worried for the twins because that money was their savings — I didn't expect Bagman to treat them like that.
metadata.source_text: "But that was all your savings!" said Ron.

metadata.description: My opinion of Bagman has dropped; I see him as a bit of an idiot and a liar for not paying and for getting into trouble with goblins.
metadata.source_text: "Nah," said George gloomily. "Nothing like that. Stupid git. He wouldn’t have the brains."

metadata.description: I learned that Mrs Figg is a Squib who’s been keeping an eye on me for Dumbledore, and she was nearby when dementors attacked Dudley.
metadata.source_text: I’m a Squib, as Mundungus knows full well, so how on earth was I supposed to help you fight off dementors?
metadata.scene_title: Arrival in Alley and Mrs Figg's Intervention

metadata.description: I’m more worried now that the Ministry will detect my use of magic because dementors were nearby and I had to use spells to get rid of them.
metadata.source_text: the Ministry have their own ways of detecting underage magic, they’ll know already, you mark my words
metadata.scene_title: Arrival in Alley and Mrs Figg's Intervention

metadata.description: I see Mrs Figg differently — she’s been acting under Dumbledore’s orders to watch me, so I realise she wasn’t just being nosey; she had a reason to be around my house.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore’s orders. I was to keep an eye on you but not say anything, you were too young.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival in Alley and Mrs Figg's Intervention

metadata.description: I was not present during the events on Wisteria Walk and did not witness the Dementor attack or the confrontation with Mundungus.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events on Wisteria Walk and did not witness the Dementor attack or the confrontation with Mundungus.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival in Alley and Mrs Figg's Intervention

metadata.description: I was not present at the alley when the Dementors attacked and so I cannot report any first-hand observations of what happened to Dudley or who was on duty.
metadata.source_text: I was not present at the alley when the Dementors attacked and so I cannot report any first-hand observations of what happened to Dudley or who was on duty.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival in Alley and Mrs Figg's Intervention

metadata.description: I learned that Dementors make people relive their worst memories — Dudley went all dark and cold and heard horrible things inside his head.
metadata.source_text: Dementors caused a person to relive the worst moments of their life. . . . What would spoiled, pampered, bullying Dudley have been forced to hear?
metadata.scene_title: Getting Dudley Home — Struggling Down the Street

metadata.description: I believe Dumbledore has been having me followed since June; I didn’t expect to be left wandering on my own after what happened before.
metadata.source_text: So, Dumbledore’s . . . been having . . . me followed? "Of course he has," said Mrs Figg impatiently. "Did you expect him to let you wander around on your own after what happened in June?
metadata.scene_title: Getting Dudley Home — Struggling Down the Street

metadata.description: I'm angrier than usual with the Dursleys — I’m prepared to threaten Uncle Vernon with a jinx to protect Dudley when push comes to shove.
metadata.source_text: "If you don’t get out of the way I’m going to jinx you," said Harry, raising the wand.
metadata.scene_title: Getting Dudley Home — Struggling Down the Street

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on Privet Drive with Mrs. Figg, Mundungus, Dudley, and Uncle Vernon, so I don't know the details firsthand.
