metadata.scene_title: Getting Dudley Home — Struggling Down the Street

metadata.description: I learned what dementors are and what they do: they guard Azkaban, they suck all the happiness out of you and they "kiss" by sucking a soul out of your mouth.
metadata.source_text: They guard the wizard prison, Azkaban," said Aunt Petunia. ... "They suck all the happiness out of you," said Harry, "and if they get the chance, they kiss you —"
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I used the Patronus Charm to drive the dementors away — it's the only thing that works against them and that's why Dudley wasn't emptied of his soul.
metadata.source_text: "Because I used the Patronus —"
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I'm starting to feel that people I expect to support me, like Sirius and Mr Weasley, are treating me like I've done something wrong instead of praising me for fighting off two dementors.
metadata.source_text: Harry found this such an inadequate response to everything that had happened tonight that he turned the piece of parchment over... Wasn’t anybody going to say “well done” for fighting off two dementors single-handedly?
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I feel more isolated from the Dursleys than ever; Uncle Vernon's quickness to blame me makes me realise they see me as the cause of danger rather than as family.
metadata.source_text: "It’s you," said Uncle Vernon forcefully. "It’s got something to do with you, boy, I know it. Why else would they turn up here?..."
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Number Four, so I don't know what happened in the kitchen or the alleyway.
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I wasn't at Number Four when the dementors appeared and when Harry confronted the Dursleys, so I don't have direct knowledge of those moments.
metadata.scene_title: At Number Four — Explanations and Panic

metadata.description: I used the Patronus Charm to drive off the dementors; it's the only thing that works against them.
metadata.source_text: I did the Patronus Charm to get rid of the dementors," he said, forcing himself to remain calm. "It's the only thing that works against them.

metadata.description: I'm starting to think the dementors weren't just wandering — they might have been sent. The idea that they'd come to Little Whinging because of me has lodged in my head.
metadata.source_text: Had they been sent? Had the Ministry of Magic lost control of the dementors, had they deserted Azkaban and joined Voldemort, as Dumbledore had predicted they would?

metadata.description: Aunt Petunia looked at me with fear and understanding for the first time; I realized she's actually my mother's sister and she now seems to grasp what Voldemort's return could mean.
metadata.source_text: "Back?" whispered Aunt Petunia. She was looking at Harry as she had never looked at him before...All he knew was that he was not the only person in the room who had an inkling of what Lord Voldemort being back might mean.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the kitchen confrontation in Little Whinging, so I don't know what was said or done there.
I wasn't in the Dursleys' kitchen for the incident with the dementors and the Dursley questioning, so I can't report on those events firsthand.
I know that voice — I recognised it straight away, even before I was told who it was.
metadata.source_text: He knew that voice, but he did not lower his wand.

metadata.description: I'm suspicious and I won't let my guard down even when someone I think I know speaks to me; I had very good reason to be cautious.
metadata.source_text: He had very good reason to be suspicious.

metadata.description: I called him 'Professor Moody?' uncertainly, because I think I know him but I'm not sure I trust him enough to be casual.
metadata.source_text: "Professor Moody?" he said uncertainly.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the confrontation on the staircase, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
I wasn't present at the moment Harry faced the growling voice on the staircase, so I can't report any details from personal observation.
I've learned that the people who turned up at Privet Drive include Remus Lupin, Mad-Eye Moody and others who know me well enough to test me — they want proof I'm the real Harry.
metadata.source_text: We’ve come to take you away.

metadata.description: I’d been suspicious after the Moody business, and now I’m even more wary — I can hardly believe anyone would just appear, but Lupin asking about my Patronus convinced me a bit.
metadata.source_text: He had very good reason to be suspicious. He had recently spent nine months in what he had thought was Mad-Eye Moody’s company only to find out that it wasn’t Moody at all, but an impostor; an impostor, moreover, who had tried to kill Harry before being unmasked.

metadata.description: Seeing Lupin smile and shake my hand made me feel a strange relief — I can tell Remus still cares about me despite everything that's happened.
metadata.source_text: Lupin held out his hand and shook Harry’s. “How are you?” he asked, looking at Harry closely.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Privet Drive in this scene, so I didn't witness the arrival of Lupin, Moody, or the others.
I wasn't at Privet Drive for this particular visit; I have no direct knowledge of the group's questioning or Harry's leaving.
I've learned we're not going to the Burrow because it's too risky and they've set up headquarters somewhere undetectable instead.
metadata.source_text: Not the Burrow, no," said Lupin, motioning Harry toward the kitchen; the little knot of wizards followed, all still eyeing Harry curiously. "Too risky. We\'ve set up headquarters somewhere undetectable. It\'s taken a while . . ."

metadata.description: I feel strange about all these people watching me; I used to think grown-ups would be reassuring, but right now I feel like I'm being put onstage and it's uncomfortable.
metadata.source_text: He inclined his head awkwardly at each of them as they were introduced. He wished they would look at something other than him; it was as though he had suddenly been ushered onstage.

metadata.description: I know Mad-Eye Moody as the man with the magical eye now; I thought I knew him for a year, but being introduced properly feels odd and makes me see him more clearly as one of my guards.
metadata.source_text: "This is Alastor Moody, Harry," Lupin continued, pointing toward Moody. "Yeah, I know," said Harry uncomfortably; it felt odd to be introduced to somebody he'd thought he'd known for a year.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Dursleys' kitchen, so I don't know what was said or done there.
I wasn't present during the events in the Dursleys' kitchen, so I don't know what happened with the Order members and Harry.
I learned we have to fly on brooms to get away because Apparition isn’t an option for me, the Floo is watched, and making an unauthorized Portkey is too dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Brooms," said Lupin. "Only way. You're too young to Apparate, they'll be watching the Floo Network, and it's more than our life's worth to set up an unauthorized Portkey.
metadata.scene_title: Planning the Escape — Packing and Preparation

metadata.description: I now believe that flying is our only safe option for the trip; I can’t Apparate and the other magical routes are watched or too risky, so broom travel is the real plan.
metadata.source_text: Brooms," said Lupin. "Only way. You're too young to Apparate, they'll be watching the Floo Network, and it's more than our life's worth to set up an unauthorized Portkey.
metadata.scene_title: Planning the Escape — Packing and Preparation

metadata.description: I've heard Remus defend me to Kingsley and others; Remus says I'm a good flier, which makes me feel trusted and backed by him in front of the group.
metadata.source_text: "Remus says you're a good flier," said Kingsley Shacklebolt in his deep voice. "He's excellent," said Lupin, who was checking his watch.
metadata.scene_title: Planning the Escape — Packing and Preparation

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the planning and packing for the broom flight, so I didn't witness the discussion about Apparition, the Floo Network, or the Portkey risks.
metadata.scene_title: Planning the Escape — Packing and Preparation

metadata.description: I wasn't there for the conversation about travel arrangements and packing; I didn't hear Moody's eyeball check or Lupin's explanation about why brooms are necessary.
metadata.scene_title: Planning the Escape — Packing and Preparation

metadata.description: I learned Tonks can change her appearance at will because she told me she was a Metamorphmagus and showed me by turning her hair bubble-gum pink right in front of me.
metadata.source_text: "I’m a Metamorphmagus," she said, looking back at her reflection and turning her head so that she could see her hair from all directions.

metadata.description: I’m impressed that being an Auror is possible right out of training; Tonks saying she’s an Auror and that Kingsley is higher up made me feel more certain that catching Dark wizards is a proper job I could respect.
metadata.source_text: "You’re an Auror?" said Harry, impressed. "Yeah," said Tonks, looking proud. "Kingsley is as well; he’s a bit higher up than I am, though."

metadata.description: I noticed Tonks cares enough to help me pack and tidy Hedwig’s cage; she’s friendly and a practical ally — I can trust her to help get me out safely and to treat me kindly.
metadata.source_text: "Don’t be stupid, it’ll be much quicker if I — pack!" cried Tonks, waving her wand... "Scourgify —" She pointed her wand at Hedwig’s cage; a few feathers and droppings vanished.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events described in the scene, so I don't have direct knowledge of what Tonks, Moody, Lupin, and Harry did that night.
I wasn't present during the events described in the scene, so I don't have direct knowledge of the packing, the Disillusionment Charm, or the trip to the square.
I learned that Grimmauld Place is between numbers eleven and thirteen — it only showed up when I remembered the line about number twelve.
metadata.source_text: Think about what you’ve just memorized," said Lupin quietly. Harry thought, and no sooner had he reached the part about number twelve, Grimmauld Place, than a battered door emerged out of nowhere between numbers eleven and thirteen

metadata.description: I didn't expect houses to appear and disappear like that; seeing Grimmauld Place materialize made me realise the magical world can hide whole houses from Muggles very easily.
metadata.source_text: Grimmauld Place, than a battered door emerged out of nowhere between numbers eleven and thirteen, followed swiftly by dirty walls and grimy windows.

metadata.description: Mrs Weasley fusses over me like I'm one of her own; she hugged me and told me I looked peaky and that I'd have to wait for dinner, so I feel cared for and protected by her.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, Harry, it’s lovely to see you!" she whispered, pulling him into a rib-cracking hug before holding him at arm’s length and examining him critically. "You’re looking peaky; you need feeding up, but you’ll have to wait a bit for dinner, I’m afraid . . ."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Grimmauld Place, so I don't know what happened inside while the meeting took place.
I wasn't present during the arrival at Grimmauld Place and the Order meeting; I was upstairs and didn't witness the main doorway appearing.
I've seen a house that looks like it belongs to the Darkest of wizards, and I felt more and more bewildered as I walked through it.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s bewilderment deepened with every step he took. What on earth were they doing in a house that looked as though it belonged to the Darkest of wizards?
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I realise people around me are trying to protect me and keep things secret on Dumbledore's orders, so maybe I shouldn't be furious with them for not telling me everything.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione will explain everything, dear, I’ve really got to dash," Mrs Weasley whispered distractedly. "there — they had reached the second landing — "you’re the door on the right. I’ll call you when it’s over.
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I know Ron and Hermione are frantic and caring about me — Hermione is desperate to tell me things and Ron is relaxedly protective, closing the door behind me like he always does.
metadata.source_text: "HARRY! Ron, he’s here, Harry’s here! We didn’t hear you arrive! Oh, how are you? Are you all right? ... "Let him breathe, Hermione," said Ron, grinning, closing the door behind Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I've looked up the Ministry rules and learned that the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Sorcery contains a provision allowing magic in life-threatening situations, which means they can't simply expel someone for using needed magic.
metadata.source_text: I’ve looked it all up, they can’t expel you, they just can’t, there’s provision in the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for the use of magic in life-threatening situations —
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I'm convinced now that Harry shouldn't have been expelled and that the law supports him, so my worry has shifted into determination to tell him the facts straight away.
metadata.source_text: I’ve looked it all up, they can’t expel you, they just can’t, there’s provision in the Decree for the Restriction of Underage Sorcery for the use of magic in life-threatening situations —
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I feel desperate to explain things to Harry and to fix whatever he thinks of us; Dumbledore made us swear, but I still want him to know we care and that we've been loyal to him.
metadata.source_text: "We didn’t hear you arrive! Oh, how are you? Are you all right? Have you been furious with us? I bet you have, I know our letters were useless — but we couldn’t tell you anything, Dumbledore made us swear we wouldn’t, oh, we’ve got so much to tell you, and you’ve got to tell us — the dementors!"
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I know where Harry's supposed to go — we're at the second landing and he's the door on the right; I closed the door behind him to give him a moment with Hermione.
metadata.source_text: "There" — they had reached the second landing — "you’re the door on the right. I’ll call you when it’s over." ... "Let him breathe, Hermione," said Ron, grinning, closing the door behind Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I reckon Hermione will rattle Harry with questions and worries, and I believe it's best to calm things down a bit so Harry can actually answer without being overwhelmed.
metadata.source_text: "Let him breathe, Hermione," said Ron, grinning, closing the door behind Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I feel protective and fond of Harry; I grin and shut the door for him, showing I side with him and want him to have space after his arrival.
metadata.source_text: "Let him breathe, Hermione," said Ron, grinning, closing the door behind Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Entering Grimmauld Place and House Interior

metadata.description: I found out that people from the Order of the Phoenix had been tailing me all the time over the summer without my knowledge.
metadata.source_text: that’s why he’s had people from the Order of the Phoenix tailing you all the time —

metadata.description: I used to want to see Ron and Hermione desperately after a month apart, but now I feel I would rather be left alone; seeing them made me feel cold and betrayed.
metadata.source_text: All of a sudden — after yearning to see them for a solid month — he felt he would rather Ron and Hermione left him alone.

metadata.description: I'm angry with Dumbledore for keeping things from me; if Dumbledore hadn't left, I wouldn't have done magic and I might have been stuck at Privet Drive all summer — I'm resentful now.
metadata.source_text: If he hadn’t, I wouldn’t have done magic and Dumbledore would probably have left me at Privet Drive all summer.

metadata.description: I know that Dumbledore made us swear not to tell Harry things about his summer and that the Order had been watching him because of the dementors.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore made us — "— swear not to tell me," said Harry. "Yeah, Hermione’s already said."

metadata.description: I was convinced that keeping Harry in the dark was best for his safety with the Muggles, but seeing his reaction now makes me question whether that was the right decision.
metadata.source_text: I think he thought you were safest with the Muggles —" Ron began. "Yeah?" said Harry, raising his eyebrows.

metadata.description: I feel guilty and worried because I was 'going spare' about him being alone and I pushed to help, and now I realise my intentions may have hurt Harry despite wanting to protect him.
metadata.source_text: Hermione was going spare, she kept saying you’d do something stupid if you were stuck all on your own without news, but Dumbledore made us —

metadata.description: I saw Hedwig pecking at Harry's letters and I even got a deep cut on my finger from her when she brought the last letters.
metadata.source_text: Pecked us half to death when she brought your last letters, look at this —" He showed Harry the index finger of his right hand, which sported a half-healed but clearly deep cut.

metadata.description: I thought tailing Harry was the right move to keep him safe, but hearing him say he had to look after himself makes me realise our precautions might not have worked as we hoped.
metadata.source_text: Had to look after myself after all, didn’t I?" "He was so angry," said Hermione in an almost awestruck voice.

metadata.description: I feel protective and apologetic toward Harry because we tried to follow orders and kept things from him to protect him, yet he feels betrayed and hurt by our silence.
metadata.source_text: "We wanted to give them to you, mate," said Ron. "Hermione was going spare, she kept saying you’d do something stupid if you were stuck all on your own without news, but Dumbledore made us —"

metadata.description: I’ve learned that Dumbledore has been deliberately keeping me uninformed about what’s been happening here, even when I asked Ron and Hermione why I’m being kept in the dark.
metadata.source_text: So why’s Dumbledore been so keen to keep me in the dark?

metadata.description: I’m starting to believe Dumbledore doesn’t trust me or doesn’t think I can be trusted with important news, and that makes me furious and hurt.
metadata.source_text: Maybe he thinks I can’t be trusted,

metadata.description: I feel betrayed and left out by Ron and Hermione because they’ve been here together while I was stuck at the Dursleys’, even if they say they weren’t in the meetings.
metadata.source_text: How come you two are allowed to know everything that’s going on — ?

metadata.description: I know Dumbledore didn’t want Harry to know what’s been going on; he told us not to tell him important stuff because the owls might be intercepted.
metadata.source_text: We did, mate. But he’s really busy now, we’ve only seen him twice since we came here and he didn’t have much time, he just made us swear not to tell you important stuff when we wrote, he said the owls might be intercepted —

metadata.description: I thought Dumbledore might have ways to send messages without owls, but I’ve come to accept that he simply didn’t want Harry to know anything right now.
metadata.source_text: I thought that too. But he didn’t want you to know anything.

metadata.description: I’m anxious because Harry’s lashing out shows he feels excluded, and I worry our not telling him has damaged our friendship even if we were trying to follow Dumbledore’s instructions.
metadata.source_text: Of course he doesn’t think that!

metadata.description: I know Dumbledore was too busy to talk properly to us and that he made us swear not to tell Harry important things because of the risk to owl mail.
metadata.source_text: We did, mate. But he’s really busy now, we’ve only seen him twice since we came here and he didn’t have much time, he just made us swear not to tell you important stuff when we wrote, he said the owls might be intercepted —

metadata.description: I don’t think Dumbledore believes Harry can’t take care of himself; I’m upset Harry thinks that, and I don’t want him to be thick about it.
metadata.source_text: Don’t be thick,

metadata.description: I feel bad that Mum won’t let us near the meetings and that Harry thinks we excluded him, but I’m also defensive because we were following rules and not trying to shut him out.
metadata.source_text: Mum won’t let us near the meetings, she says we’re too young —

metadata.description: I found out that this place is the headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix — that’s what Ron called it straight away when I asked what the place was.
metadata.source_text: "Headquarters of the Order of the Phoenix," said Ron at once.

metadata.description: I’m furious and I feel betrayed because nobody thought to tell me what’s been going on while I’ve been stuck at Privet Drive — I really believed they should have told me.
metadata.source_text: "BUT WHY SHOULD I KNOW WHAT’S GOING ON? WHY SHOULD ANYONE BOTHER TO TELL ME WHAT’S BEEN HAPPENING?"

metadata.description: I’m less trusting of my friends right now; even though they plead they tried, I’m glaring at them and pacing because I feel they excluded me from important things.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, we wanted to tell you, we really did —" Hermione began. "CAN’T’VE WANTED TO THAT MUCH, CAN YOU, OR YOU’D HAVE SENT ME AN OWL, BUT DUMBLEDORE MADE YOU SWEAR —"

metadata.description: I know that the Order of the Phoenix is a secret society founded by Dumbledore and that it’s made up of the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time.
metadata.source_text: "It’s a secret society," said Hermione quickly. "Dumbledore’s in charge, he founded it. It’s the people who fought against You-Know-Who last time."

metadata.description: I feel terrible and genuinely sorry — I’ve changed from wanting to explain calmly to being desperate and tearful because Harry is so hurt and angry at not being told.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, we’re really sorry!" said Hermione desperately, her eyes now sparkling with tears.

metadata.description: I believe Harry is right to be furious; I’d be furious if I were in his place, and I now see our silence has damaged how he sees us.
metadata.source_text: "You’re absolutely right, Harry — I’d be furious if it was me!"

metadata.description: I can tell you that Fred and George invented Extendable Ears and we’ve been using them to try to find out what’s happening, though we’ve had to stop because Mum found out.
metadata.source_text: "Fred and George have invented Extendable Ears, see," said Ron. "They’re really useful."

metadata.description: I feel guilty and a bit stunned; I hadn’t expected Harry’s reaction and I’m at a loss for words, realising how badly our secrecy looks to him.
metadata.source_text: "Er," said Ron."

metadata.description: I now see that Harry feels abandoned by us; even though we’ve been together, his anger shows our attempts to protect him haven’t been enough.
metadata.source_text: "I SUPPOSE YOU’VE BEEN HAVING A REAL LAUGH, HAVEN’T YOU, ALL HOLED UP HERE TOGETHER —"

metadata.description: I know some of the Order are following known Death Eaters, keeping tabs on them and doing guard duty and recruitment work.
metadata.source_text: We know some of the Order are following known Death Eaters, keeping tabs on them, you know —

metadata.description: I felt ashamed when I saw Ron and Hermione looking so nervous; I’m less convinced now that I should be hostile with them after everything they’ve been trying to do.
metadata.source_text: Both of them were watching him apprehensively, as though they feared that he would start shouting again now that everyone else had gone. The sight of them looking so nervous made him feel slightly ashamed.

metadata.description: I grudgingly accept that Hermione and Ron really did try to persuade Dumbledore, so I’m a bit more understanding of their choices.
metadata.source_text: Look . . .” he muttered, but Ron shook his head, and Hermione said quietly, “We knew you’d be angry, Harry, we really don’t blame you, but you’ve got to understand, we did try and persuade Dumbledore —” “Yeah, I know,” said Harry grudgingly.

metadata.description: We’ve been decontaminating this house; I’ve managed to clean out the kitchen and most of the bedrooms and I think we’re doing the drawing room tomorrow.
metadata.source_text: We have,” said Hermione quickly. “We’ve been decontaminating this house, it’s been empty for ages and stuff’s been breeding in here. We’ve managed to clean out the kitchen, most of the bedrooms, and I think we’re doing the drawing room tomo

metadata.description: I know you’d be angry, Harry, but I don’t blame you; I’ve changed how I expect you to react and now approach you more quietly and carefully.
metadata.source_text: We knew you’d be angry, Harry, we really don’t blame you, but you’ve got to understand, we did try and persuade Dumbledore —

metadata.description: I’m worried about how upset I’ve made Harry, and I’m more careful around him now because I can see how nervous and ashamed he feels.
metadata.source_text: Both of them were watching him apprehensively, as though they feared that he would start shouting again now that everyone else had gone. The sight of them looking so nervous made him feel slightly ashamed.

metadata.description: They’re always talking about guard duty; some of the Order are guarding things and keeping tabs on known Death Eaters.
metadata.source_text: “They’re always talking about guard duty.”

metadata.description: Oh yeah, I suddenly realised what Harry meant about guard duty — I’m starting to see how tangled all this Order business is and how Harry might be upset.
metadata.source_text: “Oh yeah,” said Ron, with a look of dawning comprehension.

metadata.description: I can tell Harry feels bad when we look nervous; I’m more sympathetic towards him now and don’t want to make him feel worse by arguing.
metadata.source_text: Both of them were watching him apprehensively, as though they feared that he would start shouting again now that everyone else had gone. The sight of them looking so nervous made him feel slightly ashamed.

metadata.description: I learned that Kreacher is the house-elf who lives here. I hadn’t known who he was until I asked and Ron told me straight out.
metadata.source_text: “Who’s Kreacher?” he asked. “The house-elf who lives here,” said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I’m angrier than I expected whenever Dumbledore’s name comes up; the very thought makes my insides burn with anger again, so I can’t talk about him calmly.
metadata.source_text: He cast around for a topic to change the subject from Dumbledore — the very thought of him made Harry’s insides burn with anger again.
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I noticed Professor Snape in the middle of the Order’s group below and I really don’t like him — seeing his greasy hair and prominent nose makes him my least favorite teacher all over again.
metadata.source_text: In the very center of the group Harry saw the dark, greasy-haired head and prominent nose of his least favorite teacher at Hogwarts, Professor Snape.
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I know that SPEW stands for the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare and I believe people should be kind to Kreacher, as Dumbledore says we should.
metadata.source_text: “It’s not ‘spew’!” said Hermione heatedly. “It’s the Society for the Promotion of Elfish Welfare, and it’s not just me, Dumbledore says we should be kind to Kreacher too —”
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I still think campaigning for house-elf welfare is right even if others mock it; I haven’t given up on SPEW despite Ron’s eyes and jibes.
metadata.source_text: Ron rolled his eyes at Harry. “Hermione still hasn’t given up on spew —” “It’s not ‘spew’!” said Hermione heatedly.
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I defended Kreacher against Ron’s insult, so I feel protective toward him and bothered when others call him a nutter; I don’t accept that it’s his fault if he’s odd.
metadata.source_text: Hermione frowned at Ron. “He’s not a nutter, Ron —” “His life’s ambition is to have his head cut off and stuck up on a plaque just like his mother,” said Ron irritably. “Is that normal, Hermione?” “Well — well, if he is a bit strange, it’s not his fault —”
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I found out that Kreacher is the house-elf who lives here, and I’m honestly a bit grossed out by him — never met one like him.
metadata.source_text: “Who’s Kreacher?” he asked. “The house-elf who lives here,” said Ron. “Nutter. Never met one like him.”
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I’m still not interested in SPEW or being kind to house-elves; I rolled my eyes at Hermione and I haven’t changed my opinion despite her arguing for it.
metadata.source_text: Ron rolled his eyes at Harry. “Hermione still hasn’t given up on spew —”
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I’m relieved that Snape never eats in the hall — I’m glad he’s not at the tables with us, so I don’t have to deal with him while eating.
metadata.source_text: “Snape never eats here,” Ron told Harry quietly. “Thank God. C’mon.”
metadata.scene_title: Reminder to Keep Quiet and Move to Dinner

metadata.description: I learned that Grimmauld Place used to be my parents' house and that Sirius has offered it to Dumbledore to use as headquarters for the Order.
metadata.source_text: This was my parents’ house," said Sirius. "But I’m the last Black left, so it’s mine now. I offered it to Dumbledore for headquarters — about the only useful thing I’ve been able to do.

metadata.description: I'm disappointed by Sirius's rough welcome because his voice sounded hard and bitter; I had expected a warmer greeting from my godfather.
metadata.source_text: Harry, who had expected a better welcome, noted how hard and bitter Sirius’s voice sounded.

metadata.description: I feel a sudden upsurge of affection for Sirius when I hear him moan about being stuck inside and unfairly judged by Dumbledore and Snape.
metadata.source_text: There was something about the slightly flattened tone of voice in which Sirius uttered Dumbledore’s name that told Harry that Sirius was not very happy with the headmaster either. Harry felt a sudden upsurge of affection for his godfather.

metadata.description: I haven’t seen anyone from the Order or "old Figgy" — I really haven't seen anyone at all.
metadata.source_text: No," said Harry, "I haven’t seen anyone."

metadata.description: I feel a sudden surge of affection for Sirius — he’s been stuck inside and miserable, and knowing that makes me appreciate him more.
metadata.source_text: There was something about the slightly flattened tone of voice in which Sirius uttered Dumbledore’s name that told Harry that Sirius was not very happy with the headmaster either. Harry felt a sudden upsurge of affection for his godfather.

metadata.description: I laughed with Sirius when the twins nearly sliced his hand off — we were both finding the joke in the chaos together.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Sirius were both laughing.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the meeting at Grimmauld Place, so I don't know the exact exchanges that happened in the kitchen.
metadata.source_text: Harry, who had expected a better welcome, noted how hard and bitter Sirius’s voice sounded.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Weasley kitchen, so I don't know what happened there.
I wasn't in the basement kitchen at Grimmauld Place; I didn't see the meeting, Mrs. Weasley's fussing, or Mundungus's awkward greeting to Harry.
metadata.source_text: Mr. Weasley said, hurrying forward to greet him and shaking his hand vigorously.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the kitchen incident with Fred and George or the conversation between Harry, Sirius, and Mundungus.
I've heard Sirius say that Mundungus is useful to the Order because he 'knows all the crooks' and that Dumbledore helped him out once, so Dung is kept around despite being unreliable.
metadata.source_text: He’s useful," Sirius muttered. "Knows all the crooks — well, he would, seeing as he’s one himself. But he’s also very loyal to Dumbledore, who helped him out of a tight spot once.

metadata.description: I heard Sirius argue that because I saw Voldemort return I have more right than most to be told things by the Order — that seeing him makes my claim to information stronger.
metadata.source_text: "but as he was the one who saw Voldemort come back"

metadata.description: I'm feeling that adults around me are divided: some want me to know what's going on and some want to protect me from details; I now think I should be allowed more say in what I learn.
metadata.source_text: "I think Harry ought to be allowed a say in this," Lupin continued.

metadata.description: Molly Weasley cares fiercely for me but treats me like a child; I sense her love is real yet smothering — she nearly breaks down defending her position on my ignorance.
metadata.source_text: "Speaking as someone who has got Harry’s best interests at heart —"

metadata.description: I noticed Tonks entertaining us by changing her nose into all sorts of shapes during dinner, which kept Ginny and me asking for favorites; it lightened the mood before the argument began.
metadata.source_text: Tonks was entertaining Hermione and Ginny by transforming her nose between mouthfuls.

metadata.description: I feel that being kept from Order discussions is right in some ways — we're not members — but the scene made me realise adults disagree about how much we should know.
metadata.source_text: "I asked Ron and Hermione but they said we’re not allowed in the Order, so —"

metadata.description: I see Mrs Weasley as fiercely protective and strict; her authority makes the younger ones fall quiet and even the grown men hesitate to push her when she is upset.
metadata.source_text: "I absolutely forbid —"

metadata.description: I heard Mum forbid the younger ones from staying in the kitchen to hear about what the Order knows, and that she thinks some things are too dangerous or grown-up for us.
metadata.source_text: "Ginny — Ron — Hermione — Fred — George — I want you out of this kitchen, now."

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and put out that I'm being treated as too young to hear about Voldemort-related things, especially when others at the table argue I'm old enough.
metadata.source_text: "If Harry’s allowed, why can’t I?"

metadata.description: I suspect Sirius is protective of Harry and pushes for his involvement; that makes me see Sirius as a rebel but someone who cares — though Mum sees him as reckless.
metadata.source_text: "Meaning you’ve been known to act rashly, Sirius, which is why Dumbledore keeps reminding you to stay at home and —"

metadata.description: I learned that You-Know-Who is hiding and not killing openly because he doesn't want attention right now; his comeback didn't go as planned and he's being cautious.
metadata.source_text: Because he doesn’t want to draw attention to himself at the moment," said Sirius. "It would be dangerous for him. His comeback didn’t come off quite the way he wanted it to, you see. He messed it up.

metadata.description: I've been told that Dumbledore was warned immediately about Voldemort's return and that helped the Order reconvene fast to try to stop him rebuilding his forces.
metadata.source_text: Thanks to you, Dumbledore was able to recall the Order of the Phoenix about an hour after Voldemort returned," said Sirius.

metadata.description: I was told that Voldemort is trying to gain followers and recruit dangerous allies like giants, and that he's likely planning other secret schemes besides recruiting.
metadata.source_text: Well, firstly, he wants to build up his army again," said Sirius. "In the old days he had huge numbers at his command... You heard him planning to recruit the giants; well, they’ll be just one group he’s after.

metadata.description: I've been told the Ministry, especially Fudge, is refusing to admit Voldemort's back because they're frightened of Dumbledore and would rather discredit him than face the truth.
metadata.source_text: Fudge is frightened of him, you see," said Tonks sadly... "Fudge just can’t bring himself to face it. It’s so much more comfortable to convince himself Dumbledore’s lying to destabilize him.

metadata.description: I heard that the Daily Prophet and the Ministry are suppressing news of Voldemort's return, and that Dumbledore has been publicly undermined and demoted by Ministry wizards.
metadata.source_text: Didn’t you see the Daily Prophet last week? ... They reported that he’d been voted out of the Chairmanship of the International Confederation of Wizards ... They’ve demoted him from Chief Warlock on the Wizengamot... and they’re talking about taking away his Order of Merlin, First Class, too.

metadata.description: I was told Voldemort is likely seeking some hidden weapon or item he couldn't get before — something he can acquire by stealth rather than open battle.
metadata.source_text: "Like a weapon. Something he didn’t have last time." "When he was powerful before?" "Yes." "Like what kind of weapon?" said Harry. "Something worse than the Avada Kedavra — ?"

metadata.description: I used to hope the Ministry would act, but now I see they're denying facts because of politics and fear of Dumbledore, and that makes me worry the public won't be protected.
metadata.source_text: Because accepting that Voldemort’s back would mean trouble like the Ministry hasn’t had to cope with for nearly fourteen years," said Sirius bitterly. "Fudge just can’t bring himself to face it.

metadata.description: I feel closer to Ron and Hermione when Ron asks me to tell them everything; promising him made Ron and Hermione beam and made me realise how much they rely on me.
metadata.source_text: "Harry’ll tell me and Hermione everything you say anyway!" said Ron hotly... "’Course I will," Harry said. Ron and Hermione beamed.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the discussion in the Burrow kitchen about Voldemort's return, so I don't have direct recollection of who said what there.
metadata.source_text: Absent

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the adult conversation about Voldemort and the Ministry at the kitchen table, so I can't recount those specific details firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Absent

metadata.description: I've learned that the Order were warning people against joining Voldemort again and that they mentioned some sort of weapon — something to be worried about.
metadata.source_text: All right, Ron, Harry," said Mrs Weasley on the second landing, pointing them into their bedroom. "Off to bed with you." ... "The weapon Sirius mentioned?" said Harry.

metadata.description: I reckon I'm more worried now than before; hearing about a weapon that could be worse than curses makes me think the danger's bigger than I guessed.
metadata.source_text: So, got there yet?" said George eagerly. "The weapon Sirius mentioned?" said Harry.

metadata.description: I feel closer to Ron in this — we talk things over quietly in the dark and he looks out for odd things like bolting the door because of Kreacher; he isn't just a mate, he's protective.
metadata.source_text: What d’you reckon?" Harry didn’t need to ask what Ron meant. ... "Kreacher," said Ron as he turned off the light.

metadata.description: I learned we're not supposed to let owls hunt every night because Dumbledore worries too many owls around the square will look suspicious.
metadata.source_text: We can’t let them out to hunt every night," Ron explained as he pulled on his maroon pajamas. "Dumbledore doesn’t want too many owls swooping around the square, thinks it’ll look suspicious.

metadata.description: I'm more jumpy about things after tonight; hearing about some weapon and worrying it might be at Hogwarts makes me think even school isn't safe.
metadata.source_text: "If it is, Dumbledore’s probably keeping it," said Fred. "Where?" said Ron quickly. "Hogwarts?" "Bet it is!" said George.

metadata.description: I trust Fred and George to be daft but useful for news — they use the Extendable Ears and pass on gossip; they make me feel better when they joke, even about scary stuff.
metadata.source_text: "We already knew nearly everything they told us, from using the Extendable Ears. The only new bit was —" Crack. "OUCH!"

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the bedroom at the Burrow that night, so I don't have first-hand knowledge of the late-night conversation about the weapon or the twins' Apparating.
metadata.source_text: I expect Ginny’s asleep," she added to Hermione, "so try not to wake her up."

metadata.description: I know the Order's been trying to stop people joining Voldemort — that was the main thing they told us downstairs.
metadata.source_text: I mean, all they’ve really said is that the Order’s trying to stop people joining Vol —

metadata.description: I want Ron to stop messing about and say his name properly; I reckon using his name is important and stopping the avoidance shows we aren't cowed.
metadata.source_text: When are you going to start using his name? Sirius and Lupin do.

metadata.description: I noticed Fred and George barging in and acting like mad things, but their eagerness about the weapon makes me see them as both a nuisance and oddly useful for gathering gossip.
metadata.source_text: So, got there yet? ... The weapon Sirius mentioned? ... We didn’t hear about that on the old Extendables, did we?

metadata.description: I learned that pretty much nothing new was said downstairs that we hadn't guessed already — the Extendable Ears gave us most of it.
metadata.source_text: We already knew nearly everything they told us, from using the Extendable Ears.

metadata.description: I suppose I feel frightened at the idea there could be something worse than the Killing Curse; thinking about more painful or mass-killing weapons makes me nervous.
metadata.source_text: But there can’t be anything worse than the Avada Kedavra curse, can there? ... Maybe it’s something that can kill loads of people at once ... Maybe it’s some particularly painful way of killing people.

metadata.description: I hope it's our side that has the weapon; if Dumbledore's got it, I feel safer and more trusting of him keeping it secure at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: I hope it’s our side ... If it is, Dumbledore’s probably keeping it.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the conversation in the boys' dormitory, so I don't know the exact details they discussed about the Order or the weapon.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the conversation in the boys' dormitory, so I don't know the exact details they discussed about the Order or the weapon.

metadata.description: I heard footsteps coming up the stairs and felt the weight vanish from the end of my bed when George signalled — so someone used a quick trick to move whatever was there.
metadata.source_text: “Mum,” said George, and without further ado there was a loud crack and Harry felt the weight vanish from the end of his bed.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I realise the house is in more chaos than I thought — portraits can be silenced and people are hiding things; hearing Mrs. Black scream makes me think some domestic troubles are worse than they sound.
metadata.source_text: They heard him thundering down the stairs as Mrs. Black’s screeches echoed up through the house once more: “Stains of dishonor, filthy half-breeds, blood traitors, children of filth . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I can tell Sirius and Mrs. Weasley are still prickly with each other after last night — their polite voices mean they're pretending everything's fine, but I notice the tension between them.
metadata.source_text: They were both speaking in carefully light, polite voices that told Harry quite plainly that neither had forgotten their disagreement of the night before.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: She told us to cover our faces and take a spray of Doxycide because there’s a dreadful infestation — so I know those bottles are for killing Doxies and we must use them.
metadata.source_text: “Cover your faces and take a spray,” Mrs. Weasley said to Harry and Ron the moment she saw them, pointing to two more bottles of black liquid standing on a spindle-legged table. “It’s Doxycide.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I feel a bit annoyed that Mum doesn’t trust us at all — I thought she’d believe us more, but she’s obviously watching and doubting what we do.
metadata.source_text: “She doesn’t trust us at all, you know,” said Ron regretfully.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I’ve noticed Mrs. Weasley and Sirius are still not on good terms after yesterday — they’re being careful with words around each other, so I reckon their argument isn’t over.
metadata.source_text: They were both speaking in carefully light, polite voices that told Harry quite plainly that neither had forgotten their disagreement of the night before.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the drawing room described here, so I don't have a firsthand account of what happened in that room.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s face was half concealed by a tea towel but Harry distinctly saw her throw a reproachful look at Mrs. Weasley at these words.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Patrols While Curtains Scream

metadata.description: I learned that doxies have poisonous teeth and that Doxycide will paralyze them with one good squirt so you can pick them up and throw them in a bucket.
metadata.source_text: you need to be careful, because doxies bite and their teeth are poisonous. I’ve got a bottle of antidote here, but I’d rather nobody needed it.

metadata.description: I found out what Fred and George’s Skiving Snackboxes are: sweets made to make you ill enough to leave class, with a second sweet to restore you afterward.
metadata.source_text: Range of sweets to make you ill," George whispered, keeping a wary eye on Mrs. Weasley’s back. "Not seriously ill, mind, just ill enough to get you out of a class when you feel like it.

metadata.description: I’m glad I helped the twins with money; I feel better knowing my thousand-Galleon prize actually helped their plans even though Mum wouldn’t approve of a joke shop.
metadata.source_text: He had forced the Weasley twins to take the thousand-Galleon prize money he had won in the Triwizard Tournament to help them realize their ambition to open a joke shop

metadata.description: I’ve got a bit of pride in Fred and George’s cunning and inventiveness; they keep me in on their schemes quietly and they trust me enough to whisper about their tests.
metadata.source_text: We want to experiment with doxy venom for our Skiving Snackboxes," George told Harry under his breath.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the drawing room, so I didn't see the de-doxying or the twins' discussion about Skiving Snackboxes.
I wasn't in the room for the de-doxying at the curtains and I missed Fred and George explaining their Skiving Snackboxes and pocketing doxies.
I heard Mrs. Weasley shouting that they are not running a hideout for stolen goods — she thinks Mundungus brought stolen cauldrons into the house.
metadata.source_text: WE ARE NOT RUNNING A HIDEOUT FOR STOLEN GOODS!
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I realised Kreacher recognises me by my scar; he muttered that I must be the boy who stopped the Dark Lord, so people in the house know who I am and what I did.
metadata.source_text: Is it true? Is it Harry Potter? Kreacher can see the scar, it must be true, that’s that boy who stopped the Dark Lord, Kreacher wonders how he did it —
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I can tell Kreacher hates the people he calls blood traitors and Mudbloods but is oddly loyal to the Black family history; he spoke of serving the noble house of Black and muttered about saving the tapestry.
metadata.source_text:
Kreacher lives to serve the noble house of Black —

...Mistress would never forgive Kreacher if the tapestry was thrown out, seven centuries it’s been in the family, Kreacher must save it, Kreacher will not let Master and the blood traitors and the brats destroy it —
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I've learned there's a huge Black family tapestry in the house that shows generations of Blacks and that the top reads 'THE NOBLE AND MOST ANCIENT HOUSE OF BLACK' with the motto 'TOUJOURS PUR'.
metadata.source_text: The tapestry looked immensely old; it was faded ... Large words at the very top of the tapestry read: THE NOBLE AND MOST ANCIENT HOUSE OF BLACK "TOUJOURS PUR"
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I found out I'm not on the Black family tree — my name used to be there but there's a small, round, charred hole where it was, like a cigarette burn.
metadata.source_text: "You’re not on here!" said Harry, after scanning the bottom of the tree. "I used to be there," said Sirius, pointing at a small, round, charred hole in the tapestry, rather like a cigarette burn.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I didn't realize Sirius had run away from home as a teenager and was welcomed by my parents; that changed how I see him — he's not just reckless, he was rejected and found real friends with my family.
metadata.source_text: "When I was about sixteen," said Sirius. "I’d had enough." ... "Your dad’s place," said Sirius. "Your grandparents were really good about it; they sort of adopted me as a second son."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I feel closer to Sirius now that I know he stayed with my parents and was treated like a second son; I see him more as part of my family's circle than I did before.
metadata.source_text: "Your dad’s place," said Sirius. "Your grandparents were really good about it; they sort of adopted me as a second son. Yeah, I camped out at your dad’s during the school holidays... I was always welcome at Mr. and Mrs. Potter’s for Sunday lunch, though."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I learned that Regulus Black joined the Death Eaters and was murdered — likely on Voldemort's orders — after trying to back out when he realized what they were doing.
metadata.source_text: "He was younger than me," said Sirius. "He joined the Death Eaters." ... "From what I found out after he died, he got in so far, then panicked about what he was being asked to do and tried to back out... he was murdered by Voldemort. Or on Voldemort’s orders, more likely."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I've learned that Regulus Black joined the Death Eaters and later died because of Voldemort or Voldemort's orders — he didn't die in battle against Aurors.
metadata.source_text: He was younger than me," said Sirius, "and a much better son, as I was constantly reminded." "But he died," said Harry. "Yeah," said Sirius. "Stupid idiot . . . he joined the Death Eaters." "You're kidding!" "Come on, Harry, haven't you seen enough of this house to tell what kind of wizards my family were?" said Sirius testily. ... "Was he killed by an Auror?" Harry asked tentatively. "Oh no," said Sirius. "No, he was murdered by Voldemort. Or on Voldemort's orders, more likely, I doubt Regulus was ever important enough to be killed by Voldemort in person.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I feel differently about the Black family now — I'm seeing how nasty their pure-blood beliefs were and how dangerous following Voldemort could be for someone like Regulus.
metadata.source_text: Because I hated the whole lot of them: my parents, with their pure-blood mania, convinced that to be a Black made you practically royal ... "He was younger than me," said Sirius, "and a much better son, as I was constantly reminded." "But he died," said Harry. "Yeah," said Sirius. "Stupid idiot . . . he joined the Death Eaters."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I'm reconsidering how I thought of Regulus; hearing Sirius describe him as someone who panicked and tried to back out makes me see Regulus as tragic and not a simple villain.
metadata.source_text: "From what I found out after he died, he got in so far, then panicked about what he was being asked to do and tried to back out. Well, you don't just hand in your resignation to Voldemort. It's a lifetime of service or death."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Burrow when Mundungus, Kreacher and Sirius argued about the tapestry and stolen cauldrons, so I don't know exactly what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Black family sitting room, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I was not present for this conversation about the Black family, Regulus, or Sirius's explanations, so I do not have firsthand knowledge of what was said.
metadata.source_text: He was younger than me," said Sirius, "and a much better son, as I was constantly reminded." "But he died," said Harry. "Yeah," said Sirius. "Stupid idiot . . . he joined the Death Eaters."
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room for the argument about stolen cauldrons and Kreacher's muttering, so I didn't witness the whole exchange with Sirius and the house-elf personally.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room for the encounter with Kreacher and the Black family tapestry, so I can't report on those conversations firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room when Sirius told Harry about Regulus joining the Death Eaters and being murdered on Voldemort's orders, so I can't report witnessing that exchange.
metadata.source_text: "Was he killed by an Auror?" Harry asked tentatively. "Oh no," said Sirius. "No, he was murdered by Voldemort. Or on Voldemort's orders, more likely...
metadata.scene_title: Mundungus, Kreacher and the Black Family Tapestry

metadata.description: I learned that Tonks’s hair was blonde and curly this morning — she looked different when she arrived for breakfast.
metadata.source_text: Her hair was blonde and curly this morning.

metadata.description: I feel oddly grateful that I don’t have to join the grown-ups’ conversation; I’m glad to be able to sit quiet while they talk about Scrimgeour.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt vaguely grateful that he was not required to join in the conversation.

metadata.description: I notice Tonks as a bit frazzled and nervous this morning — she’s stuttering and yawning, which makes her seem more flustered than usual to me.
metadata.source_text: “M-m-morning, Harry,” yawned Tonks. ... “I’ve b-b-been up all night,” she said, with another shuddering yawn.

metadata.description: I wasn't present at this breakfast scene in the Burrow, so I don't have any direct observations about the conversation or actions there.
I wasn't present at this breakfast scene in the Burrow, so I don't know what Ron might have said or done during this conversation.
I've learned that my hearing will be held in Amelia Bones's office and that she's Head of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement — she'll be the one asking me questions.
metadata.source_text: The hearing’s on my floor, in Amelia Bones’s office. She’s Head of the Department of Magical Law Enforcement and she’s the one who’ll be questioning you.

metadata.description: I'm starting to believe the law might actually be on my side; Lupin says underage wizards can use magic in life-threatening situations, which makes me feel a little less terrified.
metadata.source_text: The law’s on your side," said Lupin quietly. "Even underage wizards are allowed to use magic in life-threatening situations.

metadata.description: Sirius sounds like he'll protect me no matter what — his straight warning about Amelia Bones convinces me he means it and I feel a weak sort of comfort from him.
metadata.source_text: "And if it’s not," said Sirius grimly, "I’ll see to Amelia Bones for you . . ."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at the Burrow so I don't have first-hand knowledge of what happened at breakfast or who said what.
I wasn't present during these events at the Burrow so I don't know the details of Harry's hearing discussion or the family's reactions in person.
I learned that the Ministry of Magic can be entered through a shabby Muggle telephone box that hides an enchanted visitor system which dispenses visitor badges from the coin chute.
metadata.source_text: There was a click and a rattle, and Harry saw something slide out of the metal chute where returned coins usually appeared.
metadata.scene_title: Entering the Ministry via Telephone Box

metadata.description: I had thought the Ministry would be grand and imposing, but now I see I was wrong — the entrance can look like an ordinary, battered Muggle phone box.
metadata.source_text: Harry had expected a rather more impressive location for the Ministry of Magic.
metadata.scene_title: Entering the Ministry via Telephone Box

metadata.description: Mr Weasley is kind and eager to help me, even though he’s a bit flustered with Muggle things; I trust him to escort me despite his nervousness about using the visitor entrance.
metadata.source_text: ‘Ah yes . . . this way, Harry,’ and led him down a side road. 'After you, Harry.' He opened the telephone box door. Harry stepped inside, wondering what on earth this was about.
metadata.scene_title: Entering the Ministry via Telephone Box

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what happened in the telephone box or at the Ministry entrance.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger is absent from the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Entering the Ministry via Telephone Box

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know how Mr Weasley and Harry entered the Ministry or what the visitor voice said.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley is absent from the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Entering the Ministry via Telephone Box

metadata.description: I learned that visitors to the Ministry have to wear a badge that shows why they're there — mine even says "Harry Potter, Disciplinary Hearing" and I had to pin it to my T-shirt.
metadata.source_text: He picked it up: It was a square silver badge with Harry Potter, Disciplinary Hearing on it. He pinned it to the front of his T-shirt

metadata.description: I discovered that the Ministry requires visitors to submit to a search and present their wand at the security desk, which they said was located at the far end of the Atrium.
metadata.source_text: “Visitor to the Ministry, you are required to submit to a search and present your wand for registration at the security desk, which is located at the far end of the Atrium.”

metadata.description: I felt even more nervous about being at the Ministry and the hearing — seeing the badge and the security checks made the situation feel very real and worrying, like I might actually be expelled.
metadata.source_text: If I’m not expelled from Hogwarts, I’ll put in ten Galleons, Harry found himself thinking desperately.

metadata.description: I trusted Mr Weasley to guide me through the Ministry; he kept directing me and looked out for me while we moved toward security, so I relied on him to handle the formalities.
metadata.source_text: “This way,” said Mr Weasley. ... “Over here, Harry,” said Mr Weasley, and they stepped out of the stream of Ministry employees heading for the golden gates, toward a desk on the left, over which hung a sign saying SECURITY.

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Atrium at the Ministry, so I have no direct knowledge of what happened there.
I was not present during the events in the Atrium at the Ministry, so I did not witness the security checks or the badge registration.
I learned that my wand is eleven inches long, has a phoenix-feather core, and has been in use for four years when the wizard read that slip aloud.
metadata.source_text: Eleven inches, phoenix-feather core, been in use four years. That correct?
metadata.scene_title: Wand Check and Into the Gates

metadata.description: I felt nervous when the wizard read my wand's details and checked my badge and forehead, so I'm more aware that officials might scrutinize me more closely than other visitors.
metadata.source_text: Yes," said Harry nervously. "I keep this," said the wizard, impaling the slip of parchment on a small brass spike.
metadata.scene_title: Wand Check and Into the Gates

metadata.description: I felt reassured when Mr Weasley took my shoulder and steered me away; he acted firmly and protectively, so I trust him to look out for me in crowded, official places.
metadata.source_text: Thank you, Eric," said Mr Weasley firmly, and grasping Harry by the shoulder, he steered him away from the desk and back into the stream of wizards and witches walking through the golden gates.
metadata.scene_title: Wand Check and Into the Gates

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the wand inspection and movement through the gates, so I can't say what I would have noticed about the brass instrument or the lifts.
metadata.scene_title: Wand Check and Into the Gates

metadata.description: I wasn't there for the wand-check scene at the desk or the trip through the gates, so I don't have any direct observations about the parchment slip or the lifts.
metadata.scene_title: Wand Check and Into the Gates

metadata.description: I learned that a curious creature in a cardboard box was thought to be a chicken until it started breathing fire, and that someone suspects a serious breach of the Ban on Experimental Breeding.
metadata.source_text: We thought it was a bog-standard chicken until it started breathing fire. Looks like a serious breach of the Ban on Experimental Breeding to me.

metadata.description: I felt more on edge in the lift than I expected; being jammed against the back wall with people staring made me want to hide my face and flatten my fringe so no one would notice me.
metadata.source_text: Harry found himself jammed against the back wall of the lift. Several witches and wizards were looking at him curiously; he stared at his feet to avoid catching anyone’s eye, flattening his fringe as he did so.

metadata.description: I stood with Mr Weasley and listened to him talk with the bearded wizard about the box; being with Arthur made me feel like I belonged with the adults handling the situation, even if I was nervous.
metadata.source_text: Harry and Mr Weasley joined the crowd around one of them. 'All right, Arthur?' said the wizard, nodding at Mr Weasley. 'What’ve you got there, Bob?' asked Mr Weasley, looking at the box.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Ministry lift and so I don't know the details of the cardboard box, the fire-breathing creature, or the announcements heard on the way up.
I wasn't present in the lift with Harry and Mr Weasley, so I didn't witness the bearded wizard's box, the creature's rasping, or the Ministry level announcements.
I learned that the Ministry uses enchanted interdepartmental memos — pale violet papers stamped MINISTRY OF MAGIC — that fly about instead of owls because owls made a terrible mess.
metadata.source_text: they were a pale violet color and he could see MINISTRY OF MAGIC stamped along the edges of their wings. “Just Interdepartmental memos,” Mr Weasley muttered to him. “We used to use owls, but the mess was unbelievable . . . droppings all over the desks . . .”

metadata.description: I learned the lift announces floors and the Ministry is split into many departments — International Magical Cooperation, Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures, Magical Accidents and Catastrophes, and Magical Law Enforcement, among others.
metadata.source_text: “Level five, Department of International Magical Cooperation, incorporating the International Magical Trading Standards Body, the International Magical Office of Law, and the International Confederation of Wizards, British Seats.” ... “Level four, Department for the Regulation and Control of Magical Creatures, incorporating Beast, Being, and Spirit Divisions, Goblin Liaison Office, and Pest Advisory Bureau.” ... “Level three, Department of Magical Accidents and Catastrophes, including the Accidental Magic Reversal Squad, Obliviator Headquarters, and Muggle-Worthy Excuse Committee.” ... “Level two, Department of Magical Law Enforcement, including the Improper Use of Magic Office, Auror Headquarters, and Wizengamot Administration Services.”

metadata.description: Seeing those enchanted windows and hearing Mr Weasley makes me realise the Ministry is much stranger and more organised than I thought — they even control weather underground with Magical Maintenance.
metadata.source_text: “Mr Weasley,” said Harry, as they passed a window through which sunlight was streaming, “aren’t we underground?” “Yes, we are,” said Mr Weasley, “those are enchanted windows; Magical Maintenance decide what weather we’re getting every day. We had two months of hurricanes last time they were angling for a pay raise. . . .

metadata.description: I feel more comfortable following Mr Weasley around; he explains things kindly and points out where his office is, so I trust him to guide me through the Ministry’s oddities.
metadata.source_text: “This is us, Harry,” said Mr Weasley, and they followed the witch out of the lift into a corridor lined with doors. “My office is on the other side of the floor.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what Hermione did or said here.
I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what Ron did or said here.
I saw Sirius Black’s face all over an Auror cubicle — photographs and newspaper cuttings even showed him as best man at my parents’ wedding, so the Aurors clearly have a lot on file about him.
metadata.source_text: Sirius’s face was blinking down at him from every direction. Newspaper cuttings and old photographs — even the one of Sirius being best man at the Potters’ wedding — papered the walls.

metadata.description: Seeing Sirius plastered everywhere made me realise how central he is to the Aurors’ investigations; I no longer think of him as just a distant name, he’s very much a focus for them now.
metadata.source_text: Sirius’s face was blinking down at him from every direction. Newspaper cuttings and old photographs — even the one of Sirius being best man at the Potters’ wedding — papered the walls.

metadata.description: I noticed Kingsley treating Mr Weasley brusquely but with familiarity — Kingsley even winked at me — so I feel a bit more comfortable that Kingsley sees me and can be casual around me.
metadata.source_text: Kingsley tipped Harry an enormous wink and added, in a whisper, “Give him the magazine, he might find it interesting.”

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Auror offices, so I do not know the details of the conversations or what the Aurors discussed.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger

metadata.description: I was not present during the Auror office visit; I can't report on Mr Weasley’s exchange with Kingsley or on the wall covered with Sirius’s photographs.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I learned that my hearing time and venue were changed at the last minute — it now starts at eight o'clock and is down in old Courtroom Ten.
metadata.source_text: "No, no, it’s not the toilet, it’s the Potter boy’s hearing — they’ve changed the time and venue — it starts at eight o’clock now and it’s down in old Courtroom Ten —"

metadata.description: I'm convinced now that last-minute changes at the Ministry can happen and I can't rely on being told in time unless someone is actually there to fetch me.
metadata.source_text: "I only hope we can catch whoever’s doing it." "Ah, Arthur, this is Perkins." "No, no, it’s not the toilet, it’s the Potter boy’s hearing — they’ve changed the time and venue — it starts at eight o’clock now and it’s down in old Courtroom Ten —"

metadata.description: Arthur Weasley really looks out for me; he fusses, he rushes, and he gets me moving when the Ministry messes up — I feel he genuinely cares about not letting me miss the hearing.
metadata.source_text: "Quick, Harry, we should have been there five minutes ago!" "Come ON!"

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at the Ministry and therefore have no direct knowledge of what happened there.
I wasn't present during these events at the Ministry and therefore have no direct knowledge of what happened there.
I learned that my arrival was considered late and that an owl had been sent to tell me about the time — I didn't know the time had changed, and apparently a message was delivered.
metadata.source_text: I-I didn't know the time had changed.

metadata.description: I felt worse about the whole situation once I realized missing the time wasn't the Wizengamot's fault; I shouldn't blame them because they say an owl was sent to me.
metadata.source_text: That is not the Wizengamot’s fault,

metadata.description: I now see the Wizengamot as more severe and formal than I might have expected; their voice is strict and unmoved by my nervous excuse, so I feel more intimidated by them.
metadata.source_text: That is not the Wizengamot’s fault,

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the hearing scene, so I don't have firsthand details about the exchange or the chained chair.
I wasn't present at the Wizengamot hearing; I do not know what was said beyond secondhand reports and can't describe the room myself.
I felt the chains spring to life when I sat down, and I learned that the chains can activate and clink threateningly even if they don't bind you.
metadata.source_text: He had seen those chains spring to life and bind whoever sat between them.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Faces the Bench; Dumbledore Arrives

metadata.description: I got more nervous and rather sick seeing all those people in plum robes staring down at me; I no longer feel calm about facing the Ministry officials.
metadata.source_text: Feeling rather sick he looked up at the people seated at the bench above.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Faces the Bench; Dumbledore Arrives

metadata.description: I noticed Percy sitting at the front bench taking notes and I expected him to recognise me, but he didn't — I feel a colder distance from him now because he ignored me.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked at Percy, expecting some sign of recognition from him, but none came.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Faces the Bench; Dumbledore Arrives

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the disciplinary hearing at the Ministry and so I don't know the details I would have heard or seen there.

metadata.description: I wasn't at the hearing; I don't know what happened in the courtroom because I wasn't there to witness it.

metadata.scene_title: Harry Faces the Bench; Dumbledore Arrives

metadata.description: I did conjure a Patronus on August the second at twenty-three minutes past nine, and it was a fully fledged stag — always a stag when it appears.
metadata.source_text: Yes, but — "A corporeal Patronus?" "A — what?" said Harry. "Your Patronus had a clearly defined form? I mean to say, it was more than vapor or smoke?" "Yes," said Harry, feeling both impatient and slightly desperate, "it's a stag, it's always a stag."

metadata.description: I know now I have to argue why I used magic — I used a Patronus because dementors attacked me and Dudley; I won't let them say I made it up.
metadata.source_text: "I did it because of the dementors!" he said loudly, before anyone could interrupt him again.

metadata.description: Percy's sanctimonious nod really got to me; I feel more irritated with him and the way the Ministry men are ready to believe the worst about me.
metadata.source_text: Those who had been frowning now murmured in agreement, but it was the sight of Percy’s sanctimonious little nod that goaded Harry into speech.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Wizengamot hearing and so I don't know what happened at the proceedings firsthand.
I wasn't at the Ministry or the Wizengamot hearing, so I didn't witness the exchange about the Patronus or the dementors.
I heard Mrs. Figg say she saw dementors gliding toward two boys in the alley between Magnolia Crescent and Wisteria Walk shortly after nine on the evening of the second of August.
metadata.source_text: "I had gone out to buy cat food from the corner shop at the end of Wisteria Walk, shortly after nine on the evening of the second of August," gabbled Mrs. Figg at once, "when I heard a disturbance down the alleyway between Magnolia Crescent and Wisteria Walk. On approaching the mouth of the alleyway I saw dementors running —"

metadata.description: I'm more certain now that people around Privet Drive are aware of magical dangers; Mrs. Figg's testimony and the Ministry's questions show they've been monitoring the area because of past events.
metadata.source_text: "We have no record of any witch or wizard living in Little Whinging other than Harry Potter," said Madam Bones at once. "That situation has always been closely monitored, given . . . given past events."

metadata.description: I feel uneasy about Mrs. Figg: she seems frightened and batty, but she actually knew enough to recognize and report dementors, so I'm seeing her as a frightened witness rather than just a harmless oddball.
metadata.source_text: Percy returned, followed by Mrs. Figg. She looked scared and more batty than ever. ... "Yes, we can!" said Mrs. Figg indignantly.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the courtroom, so I don't know what was said or witnessed firsthand.
I wasn't in the courtroom for this testimony and therefore didn't observe Mrs. Figg's account or the Ministry's questioning.
I spoke up to correct them; I said that the Hover Charm three years ago wasn’t my doing, it was a house-elf.
metadata.source_text: That wasn’t me, it was a house-elf!
metadata.scene_title: Details of the Attack and Debate Over Authority

metadata.description: I feel even more aware that people in authority like Fudge might be determined to punish me no matter what I say or how it’s explained.
metadata.source_text: Have you ever bothered to tot up the number of cock-and-bull stories this boy has come out with, Dumbledore, while trying to cover up his flagrant misuse of magic out of school? I suppose you’ve forgotten the Hover Charm he used three years ago —
metadata.scene_title: Details of the Attack and Debate Over Authority

metadata.description: I notice Dumbledore defending me calmly and backing me up; he offers to call witnesses and stands between me and the Ministry’s attacks.
metadata.source_text: I can summon him here in an instant to give evidence if you wish.
metadata.scene_title: Details of the Attack and Debate Over Authority

metadata.description: I've learned that the Wizengamot can vote to clear me of all charges; many benches raised their hands for my acquittal when Madam Bones asked for a vote.
metadata.source_text: “Those in favor of clearing the accused of all charges?” said Madam Bones’s booming voice. Harry’s head jerked upward. There were hands in the air, many of them . . . more than half!

metadata.description: I was starting to doubt Dumbledore's decision to tell the Wizengamot it was time to decide; I wasn't at all sure he was right to push them like that.
metadata.source_text: Harry glanced sideways at Dumbledore, seeking reassurance; he was not at all sure that Dumbledore was right in telling the Wizengamot, in effect, that it was about time they made a decision.

metadata.description: Fudge looked furious and embarrassed at the same time; I can tell he was choking on his anger before he lowered his hand and gave in — I saw his restraint and suppressed rage.
metadata.source_text: Fudge glanced around at them all, looking as though there was something large stuck in his throat, then lowered his own hand. He took two deep breaths and then said, in a voice distorted by suppressed rage, “Very well, very well . . . cleared of all charges.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Wizengamot deliberation and verdict, so I didn't witness the voting or Dumbledore's actions.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the trial proceedings at the Wizengamot; I did not see the hands go up or hear Madam Bones call the vote.

metadata.description: I've been cleared of all charges by the Wizengamot — they found me not guilty and I'm allowed to go back to Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: “Cleared,” Harry said, pulling the door closed behind him, “of all charges!”

metadata.description: I saw Lucius Malfoy in the Ministry talking to Fudge in a way that looked too friendly; he actually went up to Fudge's office with the Minister.
