metadata.source_text: “The Minister was just telling me about your lucky escape, Potter,” drawled Mr Malfoy. ... “Shall we go up to your office, then, Minister?” “Certainly,” said Fudge, turning his back on Harry and Mr Weasley.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that Malfoy is dangerous and properly connected; seeing him cosying up to Fudge made me worry they're working together in ways that could harm people like Dumbledore and me.
metadata.source_text: “Why wasn’t he waiting outside Fudge’s office if they’ve got business to do together?” Harry burst out furiously. “What was he doing down here?”

metadata.description: I feel oddly let down by Fudge — I told him about Malfoy being a Death Eater and now he seems chummy with him; I don't trust the Minister the way I used to.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t think private matters between myself and the Minister are any concern of yours, Potter,” said Malfoy... “Certainly,” said Fudge, turning his back on Harry and Mr Weasley.

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the Wizengamot hearing in the Ministry, so I didn't see Harry's trial or the encounter with Lucius Malfoy there.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present at the Wizengamot hearing in the Ministry, so I didn't see Harry's trial or the encounter with Lucius Malfoy there.

metadata.description: I wasn't at the Wizengamot courtroom during Harry's hearing; I only found out afterward and celebrated with everyone back at Grimmauld Place.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't at the Wizengamot courtroom during Harry's hearing; I only found out afterward and celebrated with everyone back at Grimmauld Place.

metadata.description: I found out Ron got made a prefect even though I’d been too wrapped up in worrying about being expelled to think about badges arriving.
metadata.source_text: He had forgotten completely about prefects being chosen in the fifth year. He had been too anxious about the possibility of being expelled to spare a thought for the fact that badges must be winging their way toward certain people.
metadata.scene_title: Weasley Family Return to Grimmauld Place — Relief and Gossip

metadata.description: I realised I’d been a bit arrogant to expect the prefect badge for myself — I’d assumed I deserved it because of what I’d been through, but maybe Dumbledore looks for other things.
metadata.source_text: But if he had remembered . . . if he had thought about it . . . what would he have expected? Not this, said a small and truthful voice inside his head.... Maybe Dumbledore doesn’t choose prefects because they’ve got themselves into a load of dangerous situations. . . . Maybe he chooses them for other reasons.
metadata.scene_title: Weasley Family Return to Grimmauld Place — Relief and Gossip

metadata.description: I know I almost sulked and felt jealous, but I don’t want to ruin Ron’s moment — I’m his friend and I’ll try to be happy for him even though I’m jealous inside.
metadata.source_text: Was he, Harry, Ron’s best friend in the world, going to sulk because he didn’t have a badge, laugh with the twins behind Ron’s back, ruin this for Ron when, for the first time, he had beaten Harry at something?
metadata.scene_title: Weasley Family Return to Grimmauld Place — Relief and Gossip

metadata.description: I wasn't present during some parts of the scene described and so I don't have direct knowledge of events I wasn't in the room for.
metadata.source_text: Hermione and Hedwig had gone.
metadata.scene_title: Weasley Family Return to Grimmauld Place — Relief and Gossip

metadata.description: I wasn't present for parts of the scene after I left the room to fetch my broom with Mum, so I don't know everything that happened afterwards.
metadata.source_text: He dashed from the room, leaving Harry and Hermione alone.
metadata.scene_title: Weasley Family Return to Grimmauld Place — Relief and Gossip

metadata.description: I found Mrs. Weasley in the drawing-room pointing her wand at a corpse; I learned that what she was fighting was a boggart taking the form of dead people she feared.
metadata.source_text: Someone was cowering against the dark wall, her wand in her hand, her whole body shaking with sobs.
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: I felt I was falling through the floor when I saw Ron — then Bill — then my own body; I realized how quickly fear can make everything seem real and how wrong first impressions can be.
metadata.source_text: All the air seemed to vanish from Harry’s lungs; he felt as though he were falling through the floor; his brain turned icy cold — Ron dead, no, it couldn’t be — But wait a moment, it couldn’t be — Ron was downstairs —
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: Seeing Mrs. Weasley so broken up and begging made me feel for her more — I saw how terrified she is for her family and how deeply she loves them, even when she loses control.
metadata.source_text: “I see them d-d-dead all the time!” Mrs. Weasley moaned into his shoulder. “All the t-t-time! I d-d-dream about it . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: I learned that Mrs. Weasley’s worst fear is seeing her family dead; even I was briefly pictured among those deaths by the boggart.
metadata.source_text: Sprawled on the dusty old carpet in a patch of moonlight, clearly dead, was Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: I must admit I felt raw and shaken seeing my own body appear among the dead figures; it made me realise how frightening my mother’s fear can be for all of us.
metadata.source_text: Crack. Dead Harry . . . “Mrs. Weasley, just get out of here!” shouted Harry, staring down at his own dead body on the floor.
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: Mrs. Weasley’s sobs and desperate commands showed me how protective and panicked she becomes; I understand more clearly how much she dreads losing any of us.
metadata.source_text: “D-d-don’t tell Arthur,” Mrs. Weasley was gulping now, mopping her eyes frantically with her cuffs. “I d-d-don’t want him to know. . . . Being silly . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the drawing-room and so I do not know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know what happened.
metadata.scene_title: Boggart in the Drawing Room — Mrs Weasley’s Fears

metadata.description: I learned Moody says we have to go to King’s Cross with a guard — apparently someone like Sturgis Podmore matters for head count, according to what Hermione told me.
metadata.source_text: We have to go to King’s Cross with a guard
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I thought Voldemort was supposed to be lying low, and I still reckon that, but hearing about a guard being necessary made me realise people are taking threats more seriously than I expected.
metadata.source_text: I thought Voldemort was supposed to be lying low, or are you telling me he’s going to jump out from behind a dustbin to try and do me in?
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I felt oddly lost without Ron at my side on the Express; I hadn’t realised how much I relied on him for company until he and Hermione had to go to the prefect carriage.
metadata.source_text: He had never traveled on the Hogwarts Express without Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: Mad-Eye says we can’t leave unless Sturgis Podmore is present because otherwise the guard will be one short; that’s what I was checking on my watch and telling Harry.
metadata.source_text: Mad-Eye’s complaining that we can’t leave unless Sturgis Podmore’s here, otherwise the guard will be one short.
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I was worried about missing the train and, listening to Mad-Eye’s orders, I’m convinced it’s safer to follow strict protection rules even if it’s inconvenient.
metadata.source_text: But if we don’t leave soon we’re definitely going to miss the train . . .
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I was uncomfortable about leaving Harry alone, but I accepted that Ron and I must go to the prefect carriage and do our duty; I still care about Harry getting on fine.
metadata.source_text: We’re — well — Ron and I are supposed to go into the prefect carriage
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I wasn’t absent; however, for the purposes of this scene extract, I am noted as absent from the requested present-character analysis so I acknowledge I am not the primary POV here.
metadata.source_text: We’re — well — Ron and I are supposed to go into the prefect carriage
metadata.scene_title: Chaotic Departure from the Weasley Home and Station Arrival

metadata.description: I learned that Luna Lovegood is in my year at Hogwarts but in Ravenclaw, and she reads The Quibbler upside-down while wearing odd things like a butterbeer-cap necklace.
metadata.source_text: Luna’s in my year, but in Ravenclaw." "Wit beyond measure is man’s greatest treasure," said Luna in a singsong voice.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I hadn't expected to find someone as odd as Luna on the train; seeing her stare without blinking and behave so dreamily made me think she really is a bit dotty.
metadata.source_text: She did not seem to need to blink as much as normal humans. She stared and stared at Harry, who had taken the seat opposite her and now wished he had not.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I now know Neville better as someone who really loves Herbology — he proudly shows off a rare Mimbulus mimbletonia and wants to breed it and show Professor Sprout.
metadata.source_text: “Mimbulus mimbletonia,” he said proudly. "It’s really, really rare," said Neville, beaming. "I can’t wait to show it to Professor Sprout."
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I noticed that Luna Lovegood is in Ravenclaw and behaves oddly, reading The Quibbler upside-down and wearing peculiar things like a butterbeer-cap necklace.
metadata.source_text: Luna’s in my year, but in Ravenclaw." "Wit beyond measure is man’s greatest treasure," said Luna in a singsong voice.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: Seeing Neville’s pride in the Mimbulus mimbletonia makes me change my estimate of how devoted he is to Herbology; he truly values rare plants despite his awkwardness.
metadata.source_text: “It’s really, really rare,” said Neville, beaming. “I don’t know if there’s one in the greenhouse at Hogwarts, even. I can’t wait to show it to Professor Sprout.”
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I now view Neville more sympathetically — he’s earnest and passionate about plants, even if he’s clumsy and embarrassed when the plant sprays Stinksap.
metadata.source_text: He shook his head to get the worst out of his eyes. “S-sorry,” he gasped. “I haven’t tried that before. . . . Didn’t realize it would be quite so . . . Don’t worry, though, Stinksap’s not poisonous,” he added nervously.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I noticed that Luna Lovegood is an odd sort who reads The Quibbler upside-down and wears strange things like a butterbeer-cap necklace; she’s in Ravenclaw and sings their motto.
metadata.source_text: She had straggly, waist-length, dirty-blond hair, very pale eyebrows, and protuberant eyes that gave her a permanently surprised look... The girl called Luna watched them over her upside-down magazine, which was called The Quibbler.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: Watching Neville show off his Mimbulus mimbletonia and then get drenched makes me think Neville’s interest in Herbology is serious but also that he’s accident-prone when he tries experimental things.
metadata.source_text: “It’s got an amazing defensive mechanism — hold Trevor for me . . .” He dug the hand that was not keeping a firm grip on Trevor into his schoolbag... Liquid squirted from every boil on the plant...
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I feel a bit more protective of Neville after seeing him embarrassed and apologetic when the plant sprayed Stinksap; he’s trying his best even when things go wrong.
metadata.source_text: “S-sorry,” he gasped. “I haven’t tried that before. . . . Didn’t realize it would be quite so . . . Don’t worry, though, Stinksap’s not poisonous,” he added nervously.
metadata.scene_title: Final Goodbyes, Boarding and Early Train Conversation

metadata.description: I saw Cho Chang at the compartment door and she said hello to me in a nervous, embarrassed way.
metadata.source_text: “Oh . . . hello, Harry,” said a nervous voice. “Um . . . bad time?”
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I was upset because I realized I'd looked far less impressive than I'd hoped when Cho came by; I wanted her to see me with cooler friends, not Neville and Luna.
metadata.source_text: He would have liked Cho to discover him sitting with a group of very cool people laughing their heads off at a joke he had just told; he would not have chosen to be sitting with Neville and Loony Lovegood, clutching a toad and dripping in Stinksap.
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I learned that Luna keeps a copy of The Quibbler and that the magazine contained a sensational article about Sirius Black; this made me eager to read more and changed how I see sources people keep.
metadata.source_text: Harry, glancing at the magazine on the floor, noticed something that made him dive for it... Harry opened the magazine and scanned the index; until this moment he had completely forgotten the magazine Kingsley had handed Mr Weasley to give to Sirius, but it must have been this edition of The Quibbler.
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I've learned that the fifth-year prefects are two from each House: a boy and a girl, and I can name several pairs.
metadata.source_text: “Well, there are two fifth-year prefects from each House,” said Hermione, looking thoroughly disgruntled as she took her seat. “Boy and girl from each.”
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and think Pansy Parkinson is unfit to be a prefect; I can't understand how someone so slow-witted would be given responsibility.
metadata.source_text: “And that complete cow Pansy Parkinson,” said Hermione viciously. “How she got to be a prefect when she’s thicker than a concussed troll . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I now regard Ron's idea of misusing prefect powers skeptically and feel compelled to warn him against it, since I believe prefecting shouldn't be abused.
metadata.source_text: “You’re not supposed to abuse your position, Ron!” said Hermione sharply.
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I'm aware that as a prefect I'll have to patrol corridors and we can give punishments when people misbehave; I was looking forward to using that on Crabbe and Goyle.
metadata.source_text: “We’re supposed to patrol the corridors every so often,” he told Harry and Neville, “and we can give out punishments if people are misbehaving. I can’t wait to get Crabbe and Goyle for something . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I feel bitter about Malfoy being a Slytherin prefect and I'm determined to get his mates before he gets mine; I see prefecting as a chance for a bit of revenge.
metadata.source_text: “And guess who’s a Slytherin prefect?” said Ron, still with his eyes closed. “Malfoy,” replied Harry at once, his worst fear confirmed. “’Course,” said Ron bitterly...
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I learned Padma Patil didn't enjoy going to the Yule Ball with me because I refused to dance, and that surprises me and makes me a bit awkward about how I treated her.
metadata.source_text: “She didn’t enjoy it very much,” Luna informed him. “She doesn’t think you treated her very well, because you wouldn’t dance with her.”
metadata.scene_title: Carriage Conversations — Finding a Compartment and The Quibbler

metadata.description: I read that The Quibbler printed a ridiculous claim — that Sirius Black might actually be Stubby Boardman, lead singer of The Hobgoblins, which made me stare at the page in disbelief.
metadata.source_text: Harry finished reading and stared at the page in disbelief.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I'm starting to worry that having Sirius come with me to the station was reckless; I used to think it was funny, but now I fear it could be dangerous.
metadata.source_text: He had thought Sirius coming with him to the station was a bit of a laugh, but suddenly it seemed reckless, if not downright dangerous.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: Malfoy feels more threatening to me now — his remark about "dogging my footsteps" put me on edge and made me suspect he might discover where Sirius is hiding.
metadata.source_text: Well, just watch yourself, Potter, because I’ll be dogging your footsteps in case you step out of line.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I've noted that The Quibbler is full of nonsense and that most people regard it as rubbish; I said so fairly scathingly when Harry closed the magazine.
metadata.source_text: Of course not," said Hermione scathingly, before Harry could answer, "The Quibbler's rubbish, everyone knows that.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I felt embarrassed when Luna mentioned her father edits The Quibbler; I realised I was too quick to dismiss the magazine without thinking of who wrote it.
metadata.source_text: "Excuse me," said Luna; her voice had suddenly lost its dreamy quality. "My father's the editor." "I — oh," said Hermione, looking embarrassed.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: Malfoy's sneer and threatening tone made me just as unnerved as Harry; I recognised immediately that his words were worrying and potentially dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Hermione slammed the compartment door behind them and turned to look at Harry, who knew at once that she, like him, had registered what Malfoy had said and been just as unnerved by it.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I noticed there was nothing good in The Quibbler when Harry closed it, and I asked Harry if there was anything worth reading because I like having a bit of a laugh.
metadata.source_text: "Anything good in there?" asked Ron as Harry closed the magazine.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I didn't pick up on Malfoy's remark at all — I still found things fairly normal and carried on joking and asking for a Chocolate Frog.
metadata.source_text: "Chuck us another Frog," said Ron, who had clearly noticed nothing.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I laughed along with Ginny and Neville at Harry's comment and felt part of the group, showing I'm still close and easygoing around them.
metadata.source_text: Ron, Hermione, Ginny, and Neville laughed.
metadata.scene_title: Reading The Quibbler, Tension over Sirius, and Changing Weather

metadata.description: I saw the coaches being pulled by horrible, bat-winged, almost skeletal horses with white staring eyes; they looked reptilian and dragonish and weren’t just regular horses.
metadata.source_text: There were creatures standing between the carriage shafts; if he had had to give them a name, he supposed he would have called them horses, though there was something reptilian about them, too.
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I realised I wasn’t imagining the creatures when Luna said she could see them too, so my worry that I might be going mad eased a bit.
metadata.source_text: “You’re not going mad or anything. I can see them too.”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: Luna seems oddly calm and sure about strange things; I feel more relieved and a bit closer to her because she confirmed she sees the same creepy horses I do.
metadata.source_text: “Oh yes,” said Luna, “I’ve been able to see them ever since my first day here. They’ve always pulled the carriages. Don’t worry. You’re just as sane as I am.”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I noticed Malfoy being rude and bullying a first year as soon as we got off the train, and I intend to report that behaviour because it’s unacceptable.
metadata.source_text: “Malfoy was being absolutely foul to a first year back there, I swear I’m going to report him, he’s only had his badge three minutes and he’s using it to bully people worse than ever. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: Seeing Malfoy shove a younger student confirmed for me that his behaviour is escalating; I feel more determined that his actions need addressing.
metadata.source_text: “Malfoy was being absolutely foul to a first year back there, I swear I’m going to report him, he’s only had his badge three minutes and he’s using it to bully people worse than ever. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I appreciate Ginny helping with Crookshanks and wanted us to stick together to get a carriage; I feel cooperative toward my friends when they help out.
metadata.source_text: “Thanks,” said Hermione, relieving Ginny of the cat. “Come on, let’s get a carriage together before they all fill up . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I realised I hadn’t got Pigwidgeon yet and felt rattled about not having my owl while everyone else was getting sorted for the carriages.
metadata.source_text: “I haven’t got Pig yet!” Ron said, but Hermione was already heading off toward the nearest unoccupied coach.
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: When Harry kept saying there were strange horses, I thought he might be unwell; I became worried about him rather than the horses themselves.
metadata.source_text: “Are you feeling all right, Harry?”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I trusted Hermione to lead us to a carriage quickly and felt reliant on her to sort things out when there was a crowd and chaos.
metadata.source_text: “Come on, let’s get a carriage together before they all fill up . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Prefects, First Years and the Horrible Horses at the Station

metadata.description: I noticed Hagrid isn't sitting at the staff table — he's not there where he'd be obvious because of his size.
metadata.source_text: “He’s not there.”

metadata.description: I tried not to panic and told myself Hagrid can't be hurt; then I let myself consider he might still be away on that mission for Dumbledore — it's possible he's simply not back yet.
metadata.source_text: “No,” said Harry at once. “But where is he, then?” ... “Maybe he’s not back yet. You know — from his mission — the thing he was doing over the summer for Dumbledore.”

metadata.description: Seeing Dolores Umbridge up at the staff table made me react sharply — I recognized her from the hearing and now I regard her as someone worrying and uncomfortable to have near Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: “It’s that Umbridge woman!”

metadata.description: I clocked that Hagrid isn't visible on the staff table and I said he can't have left, so I learnt he's missing from his usual place.
metadata.source_text: “He can’t have left,” said Ron, sounding slightly anxious.

metadata.description: I sounded reassured when Harry suggested Hagrid might still be away on Dumbledore’s mission — I bought into that as the likeliest explanation.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah . . . yeah, that’ll be it,” said Ron, sounding reassured

metadata.description: When I spotted Umbridge I made a joke about her cardigan and reacted to her presence at the staff table — she's someone I notice and sneer at rather than trust.
metadata.source_text: “Nice cardigan,” said Ron, smirking.

metadata.description: I noticed Dumbledore standing before everyone as headmaster at the start-of-term feast, which looked exactly how it should be — him rising to greet us all.
metadata.source_text: their headmaster rising to greet them all before the start-of-term feast.

metadata.description: Even though I've been bitter with him recently, seeing Dumbledore there soothed me and changed how I felt a bit — it reminded me that some things at Hogwarts are meant to be comforting.
metadata.source_text: Harry was somehow soothed to see Dumbledore standing before them all, whatever his recent bitter feelings toward his headmaster.

metadata.description: I feel a little more reconciled with Dumbledore now; his presence and smile made me calmer and more willing to accept him as headmaster again, at least for the moment.
metadata.source_text: Harry was somehow soothed to see Dumbledore standing before them all, whatever his recent bitter feelings toward his headmaster.

metadata.description: I saw Dumbledore step forward to welcome newcomers and returning students before the feast started, making clear this moment was meant for greeting rather than speaking at length.
metadata.source_text: To our newcomers," said Dumbledore in a ringing voice, his arms stretched wide and a beaming smile on his lips, "welcome! To our old hands — welcome back! There is a time for speech making, but this is not it.

metadata.description: Noticing Dumbledore's familiar ritual of greeting the school made me think that, despite odd changes like Hagrid's absence and dragonish horses, Hogwarts traditions still hold firm.
metadata.source_text: Between the absence of Hagrid and the presence of those dragonish horses, he had felt that his return to Hogwarts, so long anticipated, was full of unexpected surprises like jarring notes in a familiar song. But this, at least, was how it was supposed to be

metadata.description: Seeing Dumbledore smile and call everyone to tuck in reminded me that I respect his role as headmaster and value the steadiness he provides, even when things around us seem strange.
metadata.source_text: their headmaster rising to greet them all before the start-of-term feast. "To our newcomers," said Dumbledore... "Tuck in!"

metadata.description: I heard Dumbledore welcome everyone and tell us to tuck in, and took that as my cue to get stuck into the food straight away.
metadata.source_text: "There is a time for speech making, but this is not it. Tuck in!" "Excellent," said Ron, with a kind of groan of longing, and he seized the nearest plate of chops

metadata.description: Seeing Dumbledore's call to eat made me forget any oddness about the return; I'm reminded that good food and feasts are what I care about most at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: "Tuck in!" "Excellent," said Ron, with a kind of groan of longing, and he seized the nearest plate of chops

metadata.description: When Dumbledore cheerfully welcomed us back, it made me feel more at home with the school again — and I suppose I'm grateful to him for keeping things bright enough for a proper feast.
metadata.source_text: "To our newcomers," said Dumbledore... "welcome back!" "Tuck in!" "Excellent," said Ron

metadata.description: I've heard the Sorting Hat's advice is always to stand together and be strong from within — it's a constant message about unity.
metadata.source_text: And always, of course, its advice is the same: Stand together, be strong from within.
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I feel revolted by Ron's rude chewing; I'm more inclined to think people should show better manners at the table.
metadata.source_text: His mouth was so full Harry thought it was quite an achievement for him to make any noise at all.
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I'm put off by the casual, sloppy behavior at meals — it makes me less impressed with whoever behaves like that.
metadata.source_text: His mouth was so full Harry thought it was quite an achievement for him to make any noise at all.
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: How's a hat supposed to know when the school's in danger? I learned I don't understand how a hat could pick up warnings about danger.
metadata.source_text: How can it know if the school’s in danger if it’s a hat?
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I reckon the Sorting Hat being a hat makes its warnings seem daft to me; I'm less inclined to take its advice seriously if it's just an object.
metadata.source_text: How can it know if the school’s in danger if it’s a hat?
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I think Sir Nicholas (Nearly Headless Nick) is only avoiding the Bloody Baron because he's scared — I see him as someone who knows his limits around scarier ghosts.
metadata.source_text: Only because you’re terrified of him,
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I wasn't present in this scene, so I don't have first-hand knowledge of the conversation about the Sorting Hat, Nick, Ron's chewing, or the Slytherin table.
metadata.source_text: Absent
metadata.scene_title: Ghostly Etiquette and House Rivalry Banter

metadata.description: I was not present when Nick Offended; First Years Shown Out occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Nick Offended; First Years Shown Out

metadata.description: I noticed the first years looked tiny and younger than I remember feeling when I arrived here.
metadata.source_text: They did indeed seem very small; Harry was sure he had not appeared that young when he had arrived here.
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: My grin slid off like Stinksap when Euan and the blond boy looked horrified at me; I felt suddenly self-conscious and uneasy being stared at.
metadata.source_text: Euan Abercrombie looked equally frightened and stole a horrified look at Harry, who felt the grin slide off his face like Stinksap.
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: I told Ron and Hermione 'See you later' and left alone; I felt I needed distance from them and the crowd at that moment.
metadata.source_text: “See you later,” he said to Ron and Hermione and he made his way out of the Great Hall alone,
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: I've called the first years forward and directed them along the table — I can organise them calmly and commandingly when needed.
metadata.source_text: First years!” Hermione called commandingly along the table. “This way, please!”
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: Seeing the new students shy and trying not to lead made me think more about how small and nervous they are, and that they need clear guidance.
metadata.source_text: A group of new students walked shyly up the gap between the Gryffindor and Hufflepuff tables, all of them trying hard not to lead the group.
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: By calling the first years along, I reinforced to Harry and Ron that I take responsibility in these situations — I expect them to notice how I step in.
metadata.source_text: First years!” Hermione called commandingly along the table. “This way, please!”
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: I heard Hermione call the first years forward and watched them come; they're shy and very small compared with what we remember.
metadata.source_text: First years!” Hermione called commandingly along the table. “This way, please!” A group of new students walked shyly up the gap between the Gryffindor and Hufflepuff tables, all of them trying hard not to lead the group.
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: When Harry said 'See you later' and left alone, I realised he wanted to get away from the attention; he wasn't up for sticking around.
metadata.source_text: “See you later,” he said to Ron and Hermione and he made his way out of the Great Hall alone,
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: Harry leaving by himself made me feel a bit concerned for him; I recognised he was bothered by whispers and pointing and needed space.
metadata.source_text: doing everything he could to ignore more whispering, staring, and pointing as he passed.
metadata.scene_title: Guiding the First Years; Harry's Unease

metadata.description: I realised everyone is staring at me because I came out of the Triwizard maze clutching a dead student and said I'd seen Voldemort back — that's why I'm being watched and whispered about.
metadata.source_text: He had emerged from the Triwizard maze two months ago clutching the dead body of a fellow student and claiming to have seen Lord Voldemort return to power.
metadata.scene_title: Coronation of Stares; Harry Withdraws to Common Room

metadata.description: I'm angrier with myself for not expecting people's reaction and for not having explained what happened in the graveyard before term ended; I feel cut off and misunderstood by everyone at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: He had been stupid not to expect this, he thought angrily, as he walked through much emptier upstairs corridors.
metadata.scene_title: Coronation of Stares; Harry Withdraws to Common Room

metadata.description: Neville helped me get in by remembering the password and shouting it out, so I see him as useful and steady in small ways right now — he actually jogged up and saved me the trouble.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, I know it!” someone panted from behind him, and he turned to see Neville jogging toward him. “Guess what it is? I’m actually going to be able to remember it for once —” He waved the stunted little cactus he had shown them on the train. “Mimbulus mimbletonia!”
metadata.scene_title: Coronation of Stares; Harry Withdraws to Common Room

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events described in this scene, so I don't know firsthand what happened during Harry's walk to the common room or the password exchange at the portrait.
metadata.scene_title: Coronation of Stares; Harry Withdraws to Common Room

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the corridor walk and the moment at the Fat Lady's portrait; I don't have direct knowledge of Harry's mood or Neville shouting the password.
metadata.scene_title: Coronation of Stares; Harry Withdraws to Common Room

metadata.description: I've just learned that Seamus's mum didn't want him to come back to Hogwarts; she blamed me and thought Dumbledore was an old fool, probably because of the Daily Prophet.
metadata.source_text: She didn’t want me to come back to Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I'm getting sick of always being stared at and talked about; I feel more isolated and angrier because people like Mrs. Finnigan believe the papers rather than me.
metadata.source_text: He was sick of it; sick of being the person who was stared at and talked about all the time.

metadata.description: I snapped at Seamus and defended myself fiercely; I won't accept being called a liar by friends or their family, so my relationship with Seamus is strained now.
metadata.source_text: I’ll have a go at anyone who calls me a liar," said Harry. "Don’t talk to me like that!

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the dormitory conversation between Harry, Seamus, Dean, and Neville, so I don't know what was said or how people reacted.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during this scene.

metadata.description: I wasn't in the dormitory when Harry argued with Seamus and the others, so I can't report the exact exchange or the feelings in the room.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during this scene.

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Snape expects precise ingredient order and timing for the Draught of Peace — miss one thing and the potion is ruined.
metadata.source_text: "Today we will be mixing a potion that often comes up at Ordinary Wizarding Level: the Draught of Peace, a potion to calm anxiety and soothe agitation. Be warned: If you are too heavy-handed with the ingredients you will put the drinker into a heavy and sometimes irreversible sleep, so you will need to pay close attention to what you are doing."

metadata.description: I feel more certain that Potions with Snape are brutal and that one slip — like forgetting an ingredient — will get you singled out and humiliated.
metadata.source_text: "Potter, what is this supposed to be?"

metadata.description: I'm aware that Cho being alone still makes me nervy and awkward; between Neville and Ron I doubt I'll get a decent moment with her without feeling like running away.
metadata.source_text: "At least you’re not covered in Stinksap this time, he told himself."

metadata.description: I've learned that the Draught of Peace must show a light silver vapor and that precise stirring, timing and ingredient order are essential for a correct brew.
metadata.source_text: "A light silver vapor should now be rising from your potion," called Snape, with ten minutes left to go.

metadata.description: I now believe I must guard my notes and effort more closely; if Ron and Harry won't pay attention, they risk failing their O.W.L.s and I might resent being relied upon.
metadata.source_text: "How would it be," she asked them coldly as they left the classroom for break, "if I refused to lend you my notes this year?"

metadata.description: I think Ron is tactless and careless about other people's feelings when he butts in — I expect more consideration from my friends.
metadata.source_text: "You are so tactless!"

metadata.description: I've realised O.W.L.s are massive — they affect job options and we get career advice; they really matter for deciding which N.E.W.T.s to take next year.
metadata.source_text: "O.W.L.s are really important, affect the jobs you can apply for and everything. We get career advice too, later this year, Bill told me."

metadata.description: I reckon being an Auror would be brilliant and worthwhile, even if it's tough and you have to be top-notch.
metadata.source_text: "Well, it’d be cool to be an Auror," said Ron in an offhand voice.

metadata.description: I'm suspicious and curious about Fred and George's sudden money; I can't help wondering where they got gold to buy things like dress robes.
metadata.source_text: "They bought me a new set of dress robes this summer, and I couldn’t understand where they got the Galleons . . ."

metadata.description: My potion disappeared when someone used the spell "Evanesco" — I ended up standing there like an idiot beside an empty cauldron.
metadata.source_text: Evanesco.” The contents of Harry’s potion vanished; he was left standing foolishly beside an empty cauldron.

metadata.description: I don't think Snape has ever been fair to me; his treatment hasn't improved even though he's in the Order now — I still expect him to be hostile.
metadata.source_text: since when has Snape ever been fair to me?

metadata.description: I'm fed up with Hermione and Ron bickering; I told them to give it a rest because their arguing was driving me mad, and I walked out on them.
metadata.source_text: Can’t you give it a rest? ... You’re always having a go at each other, it’s driving me mad.

metadata.description: I'm bored rigid by Umbridge's lesson — the book and her instruction are dull and make my concentration slip; reading Defensive Magical Theory is about as soporific as listening to Professor Binns.
metadata.source_text: It was desperately dull, quite as bad as listening to Professor Binns. He felt his concentration sliding away from him; he had soon read the same line half a dozen times without taking in more than the first few words.

metadata.description: I'm increasingly worried that Umbridge's theory-only course will leave us badly prepared for practical defense; her insistence on Ministry-approved, theory-centered teaching makes me think we're below standard for O.W.L. year.
metadata.source_text: The constant changing of teachers, many of whom do not seem to have followed any Ministry-approved curriculum, has unfortunately resulted in your being far below the standard we would expect to see in your O.W.L. year.

metadata.description: I notice Hermione behaving oddly — she hasn't even opened her book and is staring at Umbridge, which surprises me because Hermione never neglects to read when told to; I'm struck by how focused she is on challenging Umbridge.
metadata.source_text: Hermione had not even opened her copy of Defensive Magical Theory. She was staring fixedly at Professor Umbridge with her hand in the air. Harry could not remember Hermione ever neglecting to read when instructed to.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 3) occurred.
I know that Goyle made a much worse mess with his potion — it shattered and set his robes on fire, which is why I tried to console Harry about his mistake.
metadata.source_text: Your potion wasn’t nearly as bad as Goyle’s, when he put it in his flagon the whole thing shattered and set his robes on fire.

metadata.description: I had hoped Snape might be better this year because he's in the Order now, but I'm disappointed — I don't think his behaviour toward Harry has improved.
metadata.source_text: I did think he might be a bit better this year ... Now he’s in the Order and everything.

metadata.description: I defended Dumbledore's judgment quietly when Ron doubted it; I think Dumbledore must have reasons for trusting Snape even if he doesn't tell everyone.
metadata.source_text: I think Dumbledore’s probably got plenty of evidence, even if he doesn’t share it with you, Ron,

metadata.description: I've read Umbridge's course aims and I can see plainly there's nothing mentioned about actually teaching defensive spells; the aims are theory-focused, not practical.
metadata.source_text: There’s nothing written up there about using defensive spells.

metadata.description: I don't accept that simply reading theory is sufficient for Defense Against the Dark Arts; I'm convinced practical instruction in spells is essential and must be questioned.
metadata.source_text: There’s nothing written up there about using defensive spells.

metadata.description: I'm immediately critical of Professor Umbridge's approach; I see her as someone whose teaching priorities are wrong and who needs to be challenged so students learn real defensive magic.
metadata.source_text: I’ve got a query about your course aims," said Hermione.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 3) occurred.
I remember that Snape is the sort who never changes — I said "Poisonous toadstools don’t change their spots" about him because I still don't trust Snape.
metadata.source_text: Poisonous toadstools don’t change their spots,

metadata.description: I still reckon Dumbledore might be cracked for trusting Snape; I asked where the evidence was that Snape stopped working for You-Know-Who, showing I remain suspicious.
metadata.source_text: Anyway, I’ve always thought Dumbledore was cracked trusting Snape, where’s the evidence he ever really stopped working for You-Know-Who?

metadata.description: I'm annoyed about how much homework we have and complained loudly about Binns, Snape, and Trelawney piling on work — I told Harry Fred and George weren’t wrong about O.W.L. year.
metadata.source_text: D’you realize how much homework we’ve got already? Binns set us a foot-and-a-half-long essay on giant wars, Snape wants a foot on the use of moonstones, and now we’ve got a month’s dream diary from Trelawney!

metadata.description: I've got loads of homework already and adding a month’s dream diary is just more than we need; the O.W.L. year is shaping up to be heavy on pointless assignments.
metadata.source_text: D’you realize how much homework we’ve got already? Binns set us a foot-and-a-half-long essay on giant wars, Snape wants a foot on the use of moonstones, and now we’ve got a month’s dream diary from Trelawney!

metadata.description: I'm starting to think Fred and George were right about O.W.L. year being a nightmare — the workload just keeps piling up and it's grim.
metadata.source_text: Fred and George weren’t wrong about O.W.L. year, were they?

metadata.description: I share Harry’s annoyance at Umbridge's rule of 'wands away' and the tedious reading; I feel camaraderie with Harry in grumbling about how dull and pointless the lesson is.
metadata.source_text: When the bell went, he and Ron led the way back down the ladder, Ron grumbling loudly.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 3) occurred.
I found out Umbridge will only teach theoretical Defence Against the Dark Arts and refuses practical lessons, even though practical practice is how you learn to protect people.
metadata.source_text: It is the view of the Ministry that a theoretical knowledge will be more than sufficient to get you through your examination, which, after all, is what school is all about.

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more convinced than ever that the Ministry and Umbridge are lying about Voldemort; I know he's back and I won't shut up about it even when they try to silence me.
metadata.source_text: It is NOT a lie! I saw him, I fought him!

metadata.description: I'm frustrated and hostile toward Dolores Umbridge; I no longer see her as a harmless bureaucrat but as someone actively dangerous and obstructive, and I openly clashed with her in front of the class.
metadata.source_text: Ten points from Gryffindor, Mr. Potter.

metadata.description: I've learned that Umbridge insists on theory-only teaching for Defence Against the Dark Arts, claiming theory alone will be enough for examinations despite students asking about practicals.
metadata.source_text: It is the view of the Ministry that a theoretical knowledge will be more than sufficient to get you through your examination, which, after all, is what school is all about.

metadata.description: I'm worried and displeased at how Umbridge silences sensible questions; I believe we must be careful how we challenge her because she has real authority and will punish us.
metadata.source_text: Misbehavior in Dolores Umbridge’s class could cost you much more than House points and a detention.

metadata.description: I respect and rely on Professor McGonagall's support; she quietly defends students and warns Harry to be cautious, so I feel McGonagall is an ally even if she must be restrained.
metadata.source_text: Have another biscuit," she said irritably, thrusting the tin at him.

metadata.description: I heard that Umbridge will give detentions and that she enforces Ministry policy in class, taking points and giving punishments for speaking out.
metadata.source_text: Detention, Mr. Potter!

metadata.description: I'm shocked and unsettled by Umbridge's refusal to accept that Voldemort is back; events at Hogwarts are more dangerous and complicated than I'd hoped.
metadata.source_text: Who do you imagine wants to attack children like yourselves?

metadata.description: I'm alarmed for Harry when he speaks out; I care about him and react strongly when Umbridge attacks him, showing I'm on his side even if I'm frightened.
metadata.source_text: Ron gasped;

metadata.description: I've worked out that bowtruckles are small tree-guardians that come from wand-quality trees and can be studied and sketched in class.
metadata.source_text: “Bowtruckles,” said Hermione. “They’re tree-guardians, usually live in wand-trees.”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I'm more suspicious than before about Malfoy; his sneer and what he implied about Hagrid made me think he might know things the Order doesn't.
metadata.source_text: “Maybe,” said Malfoy in an undertone, so that only Harry could hear him, “the stupid great oaf’s got himself badly injured.”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I feel more protective and closer to Ron and Hermione when Hagrid's whereabouts are uncertain; I trust them to help and to be with me while we worry.
metadata.source_text: He hurried back around the table to Ron and Hermione, who were squatting on the grass some distance away and attempting to persuade a bowtruckle to remain still long enough to draw it.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I know that leaving a gift of wood lice will distract a bowtruckle when you need leaves or wood from its tree, because they eat wood lice and fairy eggs.
metadata.source_text: “So whenever you need leaves or wood from a tree in which a bowtruckle lodges, it is wise to have a gift of wood lice ready to distract or placate it.”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I’m convinced the house-elves want freedom and I’ll keep trying to free them even if others don’t agree; I get fiercely defensive about their rights.
metadata.source_text: “Of course they want to be free!” said Hermione at once, though her face was turning pink.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and unfairly treated when Ron interferes with my efforts for the elves; I don’t want him to touch the hats because I care about the plan.
metadata.source_text: “Don’t you dare touch those hats, Ron!”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I learned that hiding hats under rubbish to make house-elves pick them up is Hermione’s method for freeing them, though I think that’s not right.
metadata.source_text: “You’re leaving out hats for the house-elves?” said Ron slowly. “And you’re covering them up with rubbish first?”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I now strongly believe that tricking house-elves into picking up hidden hats is wrong because they might be forced into freedom they don't want.
metadata.source_text: “You’re trying to trick them into picking up the hats. You’re setting them free when they might not want to be free.”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I feel protective and responsible toward Hermione’s things in a clumsy sort of way; I cleaned the rubbish off her hats because I thought the elves should see what they pick up.
metadata.source_text: Ron waited until she had disappeared through the door to the girls’ dormitories, then cleared the rubbish off the woolly hats. “They should at least see what they’re picking up,” he said firmly.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Confronts the Twins; Homework and Dormitory

metadata.description: I learned that Malfoy told people his father said the Ministry wants to crack down on substandard teaching and that Hagrid might be sent away because of it.
metadata.source_text: “Father was talking to the Minister just a couple of days ago, you know, and it sounds as though the Ministry’s really determined to crack down on substandard teaching in this place. So even if that overgrown moron does show up again, he’ll probably be sent packing straight away.”
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I feel even more protective of Hagrid now; I don't want people laughing about him and I don't accept Malfoy calling him a moron.
metadata.source_text: “If he calls Hagrid a moron one more time . . .” snarled Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I noticed Hermione is reliably sensible and supportive—she patched my hand with her handkerchief and told me not to pick a fight, which makes me trust her judgment in tense moments.
metadata.source_text: When the bell echoed distantly over the grounds Harry rolled up his bloodstained bowtruckle picture and marched off to Herbology with his hand wrapped in a handkerchief of Hermione’s and Malfoy’s derisive laughter still ringing in his ears.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I've decided that drawing worried attention plays into Malfoy's hands and that Dumbledore would be the person to know if anything had happened to Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: “Dumbledore would know if something had happened to Hagrid,” said Hermione at once. “It’s just playing into Malfoy’s hands to look worried, it tells him we don’t know exactly what’s going on. We’ve got to ignore him, Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that Grubbly-Plank cannot match Hagrid's teaching; I wouldn't accept her as better simply because Hagrid gave an exemplary lesson.
metadata.source_text: “Because she’ll never be as good as Hagrid,” said Harry firmly, fully aware that he had just experienced an exemplary Care of Magical Creatures lesson and was thoroughly annoyed about it.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I find myself correcting and protecting Harry calmly—I'm prepared to step in and help him, like when I gave him my handkerchief and told him not to start a row with Malfoy.
metadata.source_text: Harry rolled up his bloodstained bowtruckle picture and marched off to Herbology with his hand wrapped in a handkerchief of Hermione’s and Malfoy’s derisive laughter still ringing in his ears. “Harry, don’t go picking a row with Malfoy, don’t forget, he’s a prefect now, he could make life difficult for you . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I heard Malfoy boasting that the Ministry wants to crack down on poor teaching and that Hagrid might be sent away because of it.
metadata.source_text: “Father was talking to the Minister just a couple of days ago, you know, and it sounds as though the Ministry’s really determined to crack down on substandard teaching in this place. So even if that overgrown moron does show up again, he’ll probably be sent packing straight away.”
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I'm more amused than worried about Malfoy's threats; I laughed after Harry's sarcastic remark and don't seem to take Malfoy's prefect status too seriously.
metadata.source_text: “Wow, I wonder what it’d be like to have a difficult life?” said Harry sarcastically. Ron laughed, but Hermione frowned.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I back Harry without thinking too hard—I'm loyal and ready to laugh with him, and I trust him when he says Hagrid is a better teacher than the replacement.
metadata.source_text: “Because she’ll never be as good as Hagrid,” said Harry firmly, fully aware that he had just experienced an exemplary Care of Magical Creatures lesson and was thoroughly annoyed about it.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Elf Freedom, Homework, and Care of Magical Creatures Class

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Umbridge has a special black quill that writes on the page and scars the skin at the same time — it doesn't need ink and the words appear in shining red.
metadata.source_text: You’re going to be using a rather special one of mine. Here you are." She handed him a long, thin black quill with an unusually sharp point. "You won’t need ink," said Professor Umbridge with the merest suggestion of a laugh in her voice. Harry placed the point of the quill on the paper and wrote: I must not tell lies. He let out a gasp of pain. The words had appeared on the parchment in what appeared to be shining red ink. At the same time, the words had appeared on the back of Harry’s right hand, cut into his skin as though traced there by a scalpel
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I felt the lesson she said she was teaching me was actually meant to hurt and humiliate me — I no longer think her punishments are fair or about teaching, they're about control.
metadata.source_text: No, you will come here at five o’clock tomorrow, and the next day, and on Friday too, and you will do your detentions as planned. I think it rather a good thing that you are missing something you really want to do. It ought to reinforce the lesson I am trying to teach you.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I see Professor Umbridge as smug and malicious — she watches me with that sweet, wide smile while knowing she can make me suffer, and I can't trust her to be fair.
metadata.source_text: She was watching him with her head slightly to one side, still smiling widely, as though she knew exactly what he was thinking and was waiting to see whether he would start shouting again.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I observed that Harry was given a special black quill by Professor Umbridge which caused writing to appear on skin as well as parchment and did not require ink.
metadata.source_text: You’re going to be using a rather special one of mine. Here you are." She handed him a long, thin black quill with an unusually sharp point. "You won’t need ink," said Professor Umbridge with the merest suggestion of a laugh in her voice. Harry placed the point of the quill on the paper and wrote: I must not tell lies. He let out a gasp of pain. The words had appeared on the parchment in what appeared to be shining red ink. At the same time, the words had appeared on the back of Harry’s right hand, cut into his skin as though traced there by a scalpel
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I've come to believe that Umbridge's punishments are intentionally punitive rather than corrective; her delight in making a student miss something important shows she's cruel, not reasonable.
metadata.source_text: No, you will come here at five o’clock tomorrow, and the next day, and on Friday too, and you will do your detentions as planned. I think it rather a good thing that you are missing something you really want to do. It ought to reinforce the lesson I am trying to teach you.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I now regard Professor Umbridge as openly hostile toward students like Harry; she disguises her cruelty with a syrupy smile and I don't trust her motives.
metadata.source_text: Oh no, no, no. This is your punishment for spreading evil, nasty, attention-seeking stories, Mr Potter, and punishments certainly cannot be adjusted to suit the guilty one’s convenience.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I noticed that Harry tried to ask to miss a Quidditch tryout for detention and that Umbridge refused flatly, insisting punishments couldn't be changed and that missing something he wanted would teach him a lesson.
metadata.source_text: Well I’m . . . I’m on the Gryffindor Quidditch team. And I was supposed to be at the tryouts for the new Keeper at five o’clock on Friday and I was — was wondering whether I could skip detention that night and do it — do it another night . . . instead . . ." "Oh no," said Umbridge, smiling so widely that she looked as though she had just swallowed a particularly juicy fly.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I felt more certain that Umbridge is petty and unreasonable; refusing Harry a single night for tryouts proves she's out to make him suffer rather than be fair.
metadata.source_text: I think it rather a good thing that you are missing something you really want to do. It ought to reinforce the lesson I am trying to teach you.
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I trust Harry's judgment about how awful Umbridge is; seeing him hurt like that with the special quill makes me feel angrier at her and more protective of him.
metadata.source_text: Harry placed the point of the quill on the paper and wrote: I must not tell lies. He let out a gasp of pain. The words had appeared on the parchment in what appeared to be shining red ink. At the same time, the words had appeared on the back of Harry’s right hand, cut into his skin as though traced there by a scalpel
metadata.scene_title: After Class Walk, Luna’s Announcement, and Support from Ernie

metadata.description: I've learned that Umbridge's quill makes me write with my own blood; every time I put the quill to the parchment the words "I must not tell lies" are cut into the back of my hand and then heal only to be cut again.
metadata.source_text: Again and again Harry wrote the words on the parchment in what he soon came to realize was not ink, but his own blood.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I won't show Umbridge any sign of weakness; even if I have to sit all night cutting my hand, I'm not going to give her the satisfaction of seeing me falter.
metadata.source_text: He knew she was watching him for signs of weakness and he was not going to show any, not even if he had to sit here all night, cutting open his own hand with this quill.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: Umbridge is someone I must resist; she watches me with a smile while causing me pain, and I now see her as deliberately cruel and manipulative rather than merely officious.
metadata.source_text: She was watching him, her wide, toadlike mouth stretched in a smile.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I observed Harry being forced to write painful lines with a quill that cut his hand; the practice caused his skin to be red raw even after the cuts healed.
metadata.source_text: Again and again the words were cut into the back of his hand, healed, and then reappeared the next time he set quill to parchment.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I feel more alarmed about Umbridge's methods now that I've seen the physical cost to Harry; the severity of her punishment is worse than I might have expected from someone so 'proper'.
metadata.source_text: He looked down at it he saw that the cut had healed, but that the skin there was red raw.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: My view of Umbridge has shifted to seeing her as actively harmful; her smiling inspection while causing injury shows she cannot be trusted to be fair or kind.
metadata.source_text: Tut, tut, I don’t seem to have made much of an impression yet," she said, smiling.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I learned that Harry had detention with Umbridge and that she made him write lines; when I asked he just said "Lines" like it wasn't too bad, though he clearly suffered.
metadata.source_text: "How was detention with Umbridge, anyway? What did she make you do?" Harry hesitated for a fraction of a second, then said, "Lines."
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I reckon dodging Umbridge properly is worth a fib; I told a quick story about dreaming I bought shoes so she can't make anything weird of it, showing I prefer a cheeky shortcut to getting into trouble.
metadata.source_text: Ron, who had been fast asleep when Harry got back to the dormitory, muttered something about “doing other stuff,” bent low over his parchment, and scrawled a few words.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I'm more sympathetic to Harry now because I can tell he's been hurt by the detention, even if he plays it down; I groan when I hear he wasn't let off for Friday, sharing the annoyance.
metadata.source_text: "No," said Harry. Ron groaned sympathetically.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Tryouts Fuss and Harry’s Departure to Umbridge

metadata.description: I found out I'm one of the worst in Transfiguration because I haven't practiced Vanishing Spells at all, and I've been given extra work like finishing a bowtruckle picture.
metadata.source_text: he was one of the worst in Transfiguration, not having practiced Vanishing Spells at all. He had to give up his lunch hour to complete the picture of the bowtruckle
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I learned that Umbridge uses a cruel quill in detention that writes on your skin — my hand became red and inflamed and the words stayed scratched there.
metadata.source_text: The skin on the back of Harry’s hand became irritated more quickly now, red and inflamed; ... The second detention was just as bad as the previous one.
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I feel like this is a private battle between me and Umbridge now; I don't want to tell Ron and Hermione because their horror would make it worse and give her satisfaction.
metadata.source_text: He only knew that he did not want to see their looks of horror; that would make the whole thing seem worse and therefore more difficult to face. He also felt dimly that this was between himself and Umbridge, a private battle of wills
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I get that Angelina expects players to put Quidditch first and she's annoyed with me — she tracked me down and told me she wasn't impressed by my attitude about the tryouts.
metadata.source_text: Angelina Johnson tracked him down at dinner again and, on learning that he would not be able to attend Friday’s Keeper tryouts, told him she was not at all impressed by his attitude
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I wasn't present during Umbridge's detentions, so I don't have direct experience of the punishments she gave in her office.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I wasn't in Umbridge's office for the detentions and I didn't see the quill carve words into anyone's hand, so I can't report on the specifics of those punishments.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge’s Office — The Quill and First Detention

metadata.description: I've learned I’m being made to come back to Umbridge’s office again tomorrow and she intends to etch the writing deeper into my hand.
metadata.source_text: Oh yes," said Professor Umbridge, smiling widely as before. "Yes, I think we can etch the message a little deeper with another evening’s work.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I've started thinking there might be a teacher worse than Snape — Umbridge makes me hate her in a new way; she’s evil and twisted, and I can’t stand her.
metadata.source_text: He had never before considered the possibility that there might be another teacher in the world he hated more than Snape, but as he walked back toward Gryffindor Tower he had to admit he had found a contender. She’s evil, he thought, as he climbed a staircase to the seventh floor, she’s an evil, twisted, mad, old —
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I’m not going to go to Dumbledore for help about Umbridge because he hasn’t spoken to me since last June, and I don’t want to give Umbridge the satisfaction of knowing she’s hurt me.
metadata.source_text: I’m not giving her the satisfaction of knowing she’s got to me." "Got to you? You can’t let her get away with this!" "I don’t know how much power McGonagall’s got over her," said Harry. "Dumbledore, then, tell Dumbledore!" "No," said Harry flatly. "Why not?" "He’s got enough on his mind," said Harry, but that was not the true reason. He was not going to go to Dumbledore for help when Dumbledore had not spoken to him once since last June.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I know Hermione is sitting by the fire in the common room — Fred pointed her out in an armchair, so she’s present with the others.
metadata.source_text: "She’s there," said Fred, who was also swigging butterbeer, and pointed to an armchair by the fire.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I reckon Hermione’s presence in the common room means things are calmer there now — she’s keeping watch and preventing Fred and George from causing mischief inside.
metadata.source_text: They just went past with a bunch of first years, I bet they’re testing stuff on them again, I mean, they can’t do it in the common room now, can they, not with Hermione there.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I feel confident Hermione is someone who keeps order enough that even Fred and George won’t carry on in the common room — she matters to how the juniors are treated.
metadata.source_text: they can’t do it in the common room now, can they, not with Hermione there.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I’ve been practising every evening since Tuesday on my broom because I want to try out to be Gryffindor Keeper now I’ve got a decent Cleansweep Eleven.
metadata.source_text: I — I thought I’d try out for Gryffindor Keeper now I’ve got a decent broom. "There. Go on. Laugh." "I’m not bad," said Ron. "Charlie, Fred, and George always made me Keep for them when they were training during the holidays." "Every evening since Tuesday . . . just on my own, though, I’ve been trying to bewitch Quaffles to fly at me, but it hasn’t been easy and I don’t know how much use it’ll be."
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I feel nervous and worried that Fred and George will laugh at me for trying out as Keeper, especially since they’ve been taking the mickey out of me since I became a prefect.
metadata.source_text: Fred and George are going to laugh themselves stupid when I turn up for the tryouts. They haven’t stopped taking the mickey out of me since I got made a prefect.
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I’m relieved and chuffed that Harry didn’t laugh at my Keeper idea — his support means a lot to me after all the teasing.
metadata.source_text: "I’m not laughing," said Harry. Ron blinked. "It’s a brilliant idea! It’d be really cool if you got on the team!"
metadata.scene_title: Nightfall, Pain, and Concealment of Detentions

metadata.description: I've been told to avoid the corridor by Nearly Headless Nick because Peeves is planning a joke at the bust of Paracelsus; sounds like someone might get squashed by a falling bust.
metadata.source_text: “I would not go that way if I were you,” said Nearly Headless Nick, drifting disconcertingly through a wall just ahead of him as he walked down the passage. “Peeves is planning an amusing joke on the next person to pass the bust of Paracelsus halfway down the corridor.”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I reckon we should ignore the Slytherins' jeers and concentrate on the game; getting rattled by their taunts won't help us win.
metadata.source_text: “Ignore them,” he said, accelerating to catch up with Ron. “We’ll see who’s laughing after we play them . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I feel I need to back Ron up and keep his spirits up when Malfoy and the Slytherins mock him — I'm sticking by him on the pitch.
metadata.source_text: “Ignore them,” he said, accelerating to catch up with Ron. “We’ll see who’s laughing after we play them . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I've put on Oliver Wood's old team robes and I'm going out to play Quidditch in them; they fit me okay though they were broader in the shoulder.
metadata.source_text: “Shut up,” said Ron, stony-faced, pulling on his own team robes for the first time. They fitted him well considering they had been Oliver Wood’s, who was rather broader in the shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I'm getting quieter and more serious about this match; the jeering from Slytherin is getting to me but I want to show them I'm not to be laughed at.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah,” said Ron, who had become quieter and quieter all the way down to the pitch.
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I know Harry's got my back on the pitch — he tells me to ignore the Slytherins and seems determined we'll prove them wrong.
metadata.source_text: “Ignore them,” he said, accelerating to catch up with Ron. “We’ll see who’s laughing after we play them . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I was not present for the Quidditch warm-up and the corridor warning by Nearly Headless Nick, so I do not know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Absent
metadata.scene_title: Quidditch Match Begins and Early Play

metadata.description: I was not present when Quaffle Drop, Taunts, and Bludger Play occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Quaffle Drop, Taunts, and Bludger Play

metadata.description: I know my job is to catch the Snitch — that tiny golden ball is worth a hundred and fifty points and I have to accelerate, roll and swerve to recapture it.
metadata.source_text: it was his job to recapture the tiny fluttering golden ball that was worth a hundred and fifty points to the Seeker’s team and doing so required enormous speed and skill.
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I felt that once the Bludger was let fly and the Snitch released, everything else blurred out — I became barely aware of what the others were doing because I had to be totally focused.
metadata.source_text: from that moment on, Harry was barely aware of what the others were doing.
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I noticed Ron drifting off his post and felt a bit annoyed and unsettled by it; I look to Ron to hold his position and when he doesn't it affects how I see his reliability on the pitch.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around at Ron, who was hovering in front of the left-hand hoop, leaving the other two completely unprotected.
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I learned that I'm supposed to stay in center position until I have to move to defend a hoop, or else circle the hoops — drifting off leaves them unprotected.
metadata.source_text: Either stay in center position until you have to move to defend a hoop, or else circle the hoops, but don’t drift vaguely off to one side, that’s how you let in the last three goals!
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I felt embarrassed and guilty after Angelina shouted at me; I really believed I messed up because my red face was shining and I kept apologising.
metadata.source_text: “Oh . . . sorry . . .” “You keep shifting around while you’re watching the Chasers!” said Angelina. “Either stay in center position..." “Sorry . . .” Ron repeated, his red face shining like a beacon
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I realised Angelina expects discipline and will call me out loudly if I don't hold my post properly; that makes me more aware that she won't let mistakes slide.
metadata.source_text: “Stop — stop — STOP!” screamed Angelina. “Ron — you’re not covering your middle post!”
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these Quidditch events, so I don't know the on-the-spot details of the practice, whistles, or Katie's nosebleed.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Strategy, Snitch Release, and Seeker Focus

metadata.description: I saw Angelina, Fred and George zooming toward Katie and learned Katie was chalk-white and covered in blood — she needed the hospital wing right away.
metadata.source_text: She needs the hospital wing," said Angelina.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play
