metadata.description: I still reckon Ron wasn't rubbish at practice; I think he could've played better but the first session wasn't the whole picture, so I'm more forgiving of him now.
metadata.source_text: Well, I suppose he could’ve played better," Harry muttered, "but it was only the first training session, like you said . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I defended Ron to Hermione when she sounded cool — I'm loyal to Ron and willing to stand by him even when Hermione questions how practice went.
metadata.source_text: Was he lousy?" "No," said Harry loyally.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I found out Katie was badly hurt and that Angelina thought she needed the hospital wing; Fred said she might have swallowed a Blood Blisterpod by mistake.
metadata.source_text: "She needs the hospital wing," said Angelina. "We’ll take her," said Fred. "She — er — might have swallowed a Blood Blisterpod by mistake —"
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I felt completely lousy about practice and I really believe the session was awful — I'm convinced right then that things went badly and I'm fed up with it.
metadata.source_text: "Completely lousy," said Ron in a hollow voice, sinking into a chair beside Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I was annoyed with Hermione's correction and snapped at her; I'm more prickly with her when I'm stressed, so my patience with her is thinner than before.
metadata.source_text: "Who said it was me who made it lousy?" snapped Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Quidditch rush to help Katie at the pitch; I only encountered Harry and Ron later in the common room.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Chases the Snitch, Whistle Stops Play

metadata.description: I saw that the letter was addressed To Ronald Weasley, Gryffindor House, Hogwarts, so I know Percy sent Ron official-looking mail about his prefectship.
metadata.source_text: To Ronald Weasley, Gryffindor House, Hogwarts.
metadata.scene_title: Concern Over Katie, Pause in Game

metadata.description: I reckon Percy is poking his nose into Ron's business more than usual; I feel a bit wary about how involved Percy and the Ministry seem to be in school affairs.
metadata.source_text: I have only just heard (from no less a person than the Minister of Magic himself, who has it from your new teacher, Professor Umbridge) that you have become a Hogwarts prefect.
metadata.scene_title: Concern Over Katie, Pause in Game

metadata.description: Seeing Ron disgusted at Percy's tone makes me realise I'm more on Ron's side than Percy's; I feel closer to Ron against that kind of lecturing brotherly tone.
metadata.source_text: When he had finished reading, he looked disgusted. He thrust the letter at Harry and Hermione, who leaned toward each other to read it together:
metadata.scene_title: Concern Over Katie, Pause in Game

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in this scene, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Concern Over Katie, Pause in Game

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in this scene, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Concern Over Katie, Pause in Game

metadata.description: I've learned that people close to power think I'm likely to lose influence at Hogwarts and that many folk are speaking against me in the newspapers after my hearing.
metadata.source_text: I must tell you, Ron, that nothing could put you in danger of losing your badge more than continued fraternization with that boy. Yes, I am sure you are surprised to hear this — no doubt you will say that Potter has always been Dumbledore’s favorite — but I feel bound to tell you that Dumbledore may not be in charge at Hogwarts much longer and the people who count have a very different — and probably more accurate — view of Potter’s behavior.

metadata.description: I now believe that public opinion and powerful people think badly of me after that Wizengamot hearing; it seems my escape was called a mere technicality by some and that has damaged how they see me.
metadata.source_text: As you must be aware, given that our father escorted him to court, Potter had a disciplinary hearing this summer in front of the whole Wizengamot and he did not come out of it looking too good. He got off on a mere technicality if you ask me and many of the people I’ve spoken to remain convinced of his guilt.

metadata.description: I realize now that my association with certain friends could harm their prospects; whoever wrote this thinks anyone seen with me, like Ron, might be tarred by association, which changes how I see people's willingness to stand by me.
metadata.source_text: Seriously, Ron, you do not want to be tarred with the same brush as Potter, it could be very damaging to your future prospects, and I am talking here about life after school too.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the writing or reading of this letter and so I don't know what happened in the exchange between the writer and Ron.
metadata.source_text: Hopefully you will be able to read this away from prying eyes and avoid awkward questions.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the conversation that produced this warning about my friendships with Harry, so I can't report on Ron's response or actions in reaction to these accusations.
metadata.source_text: From something the Minister let slip when telling me you are now a prefect, I gather that you are still seeing a lot of Harry Potter.

metadata.description: I've been told that Professor Umbridge is trying to change how things are run at Hogwarts and that so far very few staff are helping her with those changes.
metadata.source_text: Professor Umbridge is encountering very little cooperation from staff as she strives to make those necessary changes within Hogwarts that the Ministry so ardently desires
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I'm being encouraged to think that loyalty to Dumbledore might be misplaced and that my loyalty should be to the school and the Ministry instead.
metadata.source_text: Your loyalty, Ron, should be not to him, but to the school and the Ministry.
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I'm being told to view certain adults close to Dumbledore—like Sturgis Podmore—as criminals and to distance myself from my parents if they stay mixed up with those people.
metadata.source_text: a certain Sturgis Podmore, who is a great friend of Dumbledore’s, has recently been sent to Azkaban for trespass at the Ministry. Perhaps that will open their eyes to the kind of petty criminals with whom they are currently rubbing shoulders
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I've been told that Professor Umbridge is meeting very little cooperation from staff while she tries to make changes at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Professor Umbridge is encountering very little cooperation from staff as she strives to make those necessary changes within Hogwarts that the Ministry so ardently desires
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I'm being urged to shift my loyalty away from Dumbledore and towards the school and the Ministry; I'm supposed to consider that my parents might be mistaken for backing Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: Your loyalty, Ron, should be not to him, but to the school and the Ministry. I do hope, Ron, that you will not allow family ties to blind you to the misguided nature of our parents’ beliefs and actions either.
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I'm being encouraged to see my parents as mixed up with dangerous people around Dumbledore and to judge them harshly until they apologise.
metadata.source_text: it pains me to criticize our parents, but I am afraid I can no longer live under their roof while they remain mixed up with the dangerous crowd around Dumbledore
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this exchange and so I don't know what was said or done in the room.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was not present
metadata.scene_title: Katie Collapses; Team Races to Help

metadata.description: I found out Percy told Ron to 'sever ties' with me; seeing the words written in Percy's letter made Percy advising Ron to drop me painfully real.
metadata.source_text: "— ‘sever ties’ with me, I swear I won’t get violent."

metadata.description: I know more clearly now that a lot of people at Hogwarts and beyond really do think I'm strange or mad; reading Percy's advice made the idea feel true in a way nothing else had.
metadata.source_text: He knew that half the people inside Hogwarts thought him strange, even mad; he knew that the Daily Prophet had been making snide allusions to him for months, but there was something about seeing it written down like that in Percy’s writing...

metadata.description: I feel let down by Percy — someone I knew well and spent summers with — because Percy thinks I'm unbalanced and possibly violent; that changes how I see him.
metadata.source_text: He had known Percy for four years, had stayed in his house during the summers... yet now, Percy thought him unbalanced and possibly violent.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events described in the scene, so I don't have firsthand knowledge of what happened there.
I wasn't present during the events described in the scene, so I can't report direct observations about them.
I learned Dumbledore said the pain in my scar happens whenever Voldemort is feeling a powerful emotion; it linked that night of detention and later flare-ups to Voldemort's feelings.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore said it happened whenever Voldemort was feeling a powerful emotion,
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I used to just think the scar hurt randomly, but now I believe the pain increases when Voldemort is stronger or angry and that his return will make it hurt more often.
metadata.source_text: Well, now he’s back it’s bound to hurt more often,
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I'm starting to doubt Umbridge and dislike her more after hearing Sirius and remembering her comments about part-humans; I feel she's foul and dangerous to people like Lupin.
metadata.source_text: She’s foul enough to be one,
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I've learned that Umbridge drafted anti-werewolf legislation that makes it almost impossible for Lupin to get a job, which explains why he looks worse and is struggling.
metadata.source_text: she drafted a bit of anti-werewolf legislation two years ago that makes it almost impossible for him to get a job.
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I used to assume the Ministry would train us properly, but now I believe Fudge is deliberately preventing practical Defense Against the Dark Arts lessons because he's paranoid about Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: So we’re being prevented from learning Defense Against the Dark Arts because Fudge is scared we’ll use spells against the Ministry?
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I feel more protective of creatures like Kreacher and offended by Sirius's joke; I think he should try to get on with Kreacher because Dumbledore said family matters.
metadata.source_text: Honestly, if you made a bit of an effort with Kreacher I’m sure he’d respond, after all, you are the only member of his family he’s got left, and Professor Dumbledore said —
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I've learned from Sirius that the Ministry, especially Fudge, thinks Dumbledore might be trying to build an army and so stops us from getting combat training in class.
metadata.source_text: Our information from inside the Ministry is that Fudge doesn’t want you trained in combat.
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I used to shrug off the Ministry's decisions, but hearing Sirius I now believe Fudge is dangerously paranoid and could try to have Dumbledore arrested on false charges.
metadata.source_text: He’s getting more paranoid about Dumbledore by the day. It’s a matter of time before he has Dumbledore arrested on some trumped-up charge.
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I'm annoyed by the idea of Sirius coming to Hogsmeade after Malfoy might have seen him; I agree with Harry and Hermione that Sirius shouldn't risk being recognized again.
metadata.source_text: So don’t come up here, whatever you do, if Malfoy recognizes you again —
metadata.scene_title: Reading Percy's Letter and Fire-Conversation with Sirius

metadata.description: I saw Umbridge put in as some Ministry inspector called a High Inquisitor and she sat in on Trelawney’s class taking notes and telling students to put their wands away.
metadata.source_text: MINISTRY SEEKS EDUCATIONAL REFORM DOLORES UMBRIDGE APPOINTED FIRST-EVER “HIGH INQUISITOR”

metadata.description: I already thought Trelawney was a bit of a fraud, but watching Umbridge bully her made me feel oddly on Trelawney’s side — until Umbridge snapped at us and took points from Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: They both knew that Professor Trelawney was an old fraud, but on the other hand, they loathed Umbridge so much that they felt very much on Trelawney’s side

metadata.description: Umbridge’s behavior convinces me she’s someone to resist; she’s not a teacher I can respect — she’s petty and vindictive, especially when she takes points and gives detention.
metadata.source_text: Miss Granger, I am going to take five points from Gryffindor House.

metadata.description: I already read the whole Slinkhard book, so I know what he says about counterjinxes and I can quote his argument that 'counterjinx' is just a name people give their jinxes.
metadata.source_text: I’ve read the whole book.

metadata.description: I disagree with Slinkhard that jinxes are useless — I think jinxes can be very useful defensively, and I’ll say so even if the class is meant to follow the Ministry line.
metadata.source_text: But I think they can be very useful when they’re used defensively.

metadata.description: When Umbridge punished me by taking points for speaking up, I felt the Ministry’s methods were stifling proper learning and that Umbridge is an enemy to meaningful education at Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Miss Granger, I am going to take five points from Gryffindor House.

metadata.description: I had to help Harry work out the Dream Oracle details — like adding his age and the number of letters in the dream subject — because I’d done it last time and it’s my turn to assist.
metadata.source_text: Okay, we’ve got to add your age to the date you had the dream, the number of letters in the subject . . .

metadata.description: I was annoyed when Harry tried to dump the dreaming on me after I’d done it before, but I still laugh and make light of his wild dream about drowning Snape — typical of how I try to keep things joking.
metadata.source_text: I did it last time, it’s your turn, you tell me one.

metadata.description: Seeing Umbridge take control made me feel more protective of Harry and our group — we’re all under pressure now, and I don’t like how easily she swats at people like Hermione.
metadata.source_text: Well, if that’s really the best you can do . . .

metadata.description: I'm in detention with Umbridge and she slices my hand open every night; I'm being punished by her and still had points docked from Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: From Professor Umbridge," muttered Harry, not meeting Professor McGonagall’s beady, square-framed eyes.

metadata.description: I feel it's unfair that McGonagall took house points from Gryffindor when I'm already punished by Umbridge; I'm furious at the injustice but my anger cools when McGonagall warns me.
metadata.source_text: But — what? Professor, no!" Harry said, furious at this injustice. "I’m already being punished by her, why do you have to take points as well?

metadata.description: I like McGonagall a bit more after she defends her class against Umbridge and even caught what seemed like a faint smile from her when she swept us along.
metadata.source_text: Harry could not help giving her a faint smile and could have sworn he received one in return.

metadata.description: I've seen that McGonagall warns Harry not to lose his temper with Umbridge and I explained, calmly, that she is right to warn him.
metadata.source_text: "I wish she hadn’t taken points from you, but I think she’s right to warn you not to lose your temper with Umbridge," said Hermione’s voice

metadata.description: I'm less openly reactive in this moment; I keep reading the Prophet and speak properly about tempering anger rather than matching Harry's fury.
metadata.source_text: Hermione, however, merely rustled the pages of her Daily Prophet and said nothing.

metadata.description: I still stand with Harry and Ron practically, following McGonagall out and listening in, but I maintain a more measured, admonishing tone toward reckless anger.
metadata.source_text: Hurry up, you three," she added, sweeping Harry, Ron, and Hermione before her.

metadata.description: I know Umbridge has given Harry detention and McGonagall took points off Gryffindor; I pointed out to Harry that Umbridge's behavior is 'bang out of order.'
metadata.source_text: I know, mate," said Ron sympathetically, tipping bacon onto Harry’s plate, "she’s bang out of order.

metadata.description: I'm angrier at Umbridge for treating Harry unfairly and more determined that she should get what she deserves; I whisper approval at the chance of her being exposed.
metadata.source_text: "Excellent," whispered Ron, as they sat down in their usual seats. "Let’s see Umbridge get what she deserves."

metadata.description: I stand by Harry—feeding him, sympathizing, and intentionally eavesdropping with him and Hermione when Umbridge questions McGonagall and Grubbly-Plank.
metadata.source_text: "Hurry up, you three," she added, sweeping Harry, Ron, and Hermione before her.

metadata.description: I've learned that a solution of strained and pickled murtlap tentacles helps soothe and stop bleeding when I soak my hand in it.
metadata.source_text: "soak your hand in that, it’s a solution of strained and pickled murtlap tentacles, it should help."

metadata.description: I can use Reparo to mend broken china well enough to make the bowl whole again, even if the contents are lost.
metadata.source_text: "Reparo," Harry muttered, pointing his wand at the broken pieces of china. They flew back together, good as new

metadata.description: I felt ashamed after shouting and then, quiet-like, I nodded because I think I’ll consider Hermione’s idea about teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts myself.
metadata.source_text: He nodded, hardly aware of what he was agreeing to.

metadata.description: I realised Hermione and Ron truly want to help and trust me enough to suggest I teach them how to defend themselves against real danger.
metadata.source_text: "I’m talking about you, Harry."

metadata.description: I know that a bowl of strained and pickled murtlap tentacles eases bleeding and aching when soaked in; I gave it to Harry to help his injured hand.
metadata.source_text: "Here," she said anxiously, pushing a small bowl of yellow liquid toward him, "soak your hand in that, it’s a solution of strained and pickled murtlap tentacles, it should help."

metadata.description: I’ve changed from hoping teachers would teach Defence properly to believing we must learn it ourselves; I now think Harry should teach us because experience matters more than class tests.
metadata.source_text: "We need a teacher, a proper one, who can show us how to use the spells and correct us if we’re going wrong."

metadata.description: I feel that Harry’s firsthand experience facing Voldemort makes him someone we should learn from; saying his name aloud shows how serious I am about this.
metadata.source_text: "We need to know what it’s r-really like . . . facing him . . . facing V-Voldemort."

metadata.description: I reckon Umbridge is the sort of woman who’d make life impossible and even pass decrees to silence complaints, so complaining won’t help much.
metadata.source_text: "And how long d’you reckon it’d take Umbridge to pass another Decree saying anyone who complains about the High Inquisitor gets sacked immediately?"

metadata.description: I went from thinking Hermione’s schemes were daft to warming to the idea that Harry might teach us Defence; after thinking, I said, "That’s an idea."
metadata.source_text: "That’s an idea."

metadata.description: I realised I want Harry teaching us because I trust his experience and, after considering everything, I supported Hermione’s suggestion instead of mocking it.
metadata.source_text: "You," said Ron. "Teaching us to do it."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I noticed folk in the Hog's Head hide their faces; there's a man wrapped in dirty gray bandages drinking a smoking, fiery drink and hooded figures talking in Yorkshire accents.
metadata.source_text: There was a man at the bar whose whole head was wrapped in dirty gray bandages, though he was still managing to gulp endless glasses of some smoking, fiery substance through a slit over his mouth. Two figures shrouded in hoods sat at a table in one of the windows; Harry might have thought them dementors if they had not been talking in strong Yorkshire accents;

metadata.description: I realised a lot more people turned up because they wanted to hear my side; I can't waste time convincing anyone who doesn't believe me after Dumbledore told the school.
metadata.source_text: It had just dawned upon him why there were so many people there. He felt that Hermione should have seen this coming... "I saw him. But Dumbledore told the whole school what happened last year, and if you didn’t believe him, you don’t believe me, and I’m not wasting an afternoon trying to convince anyone."

metadata.description: I felt frustrated with Hermione for not predicting how many would come, even though she organised it; she meant well but I wanted to be kept warned about expectations.
metadata.source_text: He could not imagine what all these people had turned up for until the horrible thought occurred to him that they might be expecting some kind of speech, at which he rounded on Hermione. "What have you been telling people?" he said in a low voice.

metadata.description: I've checked the school rules and Professor Flitwick said students can come to the Hog's Head, though he advised we bring our own glasses.
metadata.source_text: I specifically asked Professor Flitwick whether students were allowed to come in the Hog’s Head, and he said yes, but he advised me strongly to bring our own glasses.

metadata.description: I decided we must teach practical Defense Against the Dark Arts ourselves because Umbridge's lessons are useless; I want more than just O.W.L. theory.
metadata.source_text: Well, I thought it would be good if we, well, took matters into our own hands... learning how to defend ourselves properly, not just theory but the real spells... 'Of course I do,' said Hermione at once. 'But I want more than that, I want to be properly trained in Defense because... because... Because Lord Voldemort's back.'

metadata.description: I felt responsible and protective; I promised Harry I'd speak first so he wouldn't be forced into explaining everything straight away.
metadata.source_text: You don't have to do anything yet, I'll speak to them first.

metadata.description: I realised the barman wouldn't care what we ordered; I thought we could get away with trying things like firewhisky though I remembered I'm a prefect.
metadata.source_text: We could order anything we liked in here, I bet that bloke would sell us anything, he wouldn’t care. I’ve always wanted to try firewhisky —" "You — are — a — prefect," snarled Hermione. "Oh," said Ron, the smile fading from his face. "Yeah . . ."

metadata.description: Seeing so many people turn up made me suddenly aware this wasn't just a small group; I understood Hermione's plan was more popular than I expected.
metadata.source_text: He watched numbly as the large chattering group took their beers from Fred and rummaged in their robes to find coins. He could not imagine what all these people had turned up for until the horrible thought occurred to him...

metadata.description: I felt awkward when Cho sat next to me; I noticed she smiled at Harry and not at me, which made me uneasy but I tried to carry on.
metadata.source_text: Cho had just smiled at him and sat down on Ron’s right.

metadata.description: I can produce a corporeal Patronus—a stag—and people know about it now.
metadata.source_text: “Er — you don’t know Madam Bones, do you?” he asked. The girl smiled. “She’s my auntie,” she said. “I’m Susan Bones. She told me about your hearing. So — is it really true? You make a stag Patronus?” “Yes,” said Harry.

metadata.description: I killed a basilisk with a sword in Dumbledore’s office, and folks are impressed by that.
metadata.source_text: “And did you kill a basilisk with that sword in Dumbledore’s office?” demanded Terry Boot. “That’s what one of the portraits on the wall told me when I was in there last year . . .” “Er — yeah, I did, yeah,” said Harry.

metadata.description: I don’t want to talk about Cedric Diggory; I’m not going to relive how he died for people’s curiosity.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t want to talk about Cedric Diggory, all right? So if that’s what you’re here for, you might as well clear out.”

metadata.description: I blame Hermione a bit for putting me on display—she made me feel like a freak in front of everyone.
metadata.source_text: He cast an angry look in Hermione’s direction. This was, he felt, all her fault; she had decided to display him like some sort of freak and of course they had all turned up to see just how wild his story was.

metadata.description: If we want to learn Defence properly, we need to work out how often and where to meet; once a week seems the minimum sensible plan.
metadata.source_text: “So . . . like I was saying . . . if you want to learn some defense, then we need to work out how we’re going to do it, how often we’re going to meet, and where we’re going to —”

metadata.description: I think Umbridge doesn’t want students trained because she suspects Dumbledore might turn us into a private army for the school.
metadata.source_text: “We think the reason Umbridge doesn’t want us trained in Defense Against the Dark Arts,” said Hermione, “is that she’s got some . . . some mad idea that Dumbledore could use the students in the school as a kind of private army. She thinks he’d mobilize us against the Ministry.”

metadata.description: I’m taking responsibility to organize the group, collect names, and keep things secret from Umbridge; I’ll hold the list safely in my bag.
metadata.source_text: “I-I think everybody should write their name down, just so we know who was here. But I also think,” she took a deep breath, “that we all ought to agree not to shout about what we’re doing. So if you sign, you’re agreeing not to tell Umbridge — or anybody else — what we’re up to.”

metadata.description: I’m not having Zacharias keep on about Harry—he deserved to be told to shut his mouth.
metadata.source_text: “Are you trying to weasel out of showing us any of this stuff?” said Zacharias Smith. “Here’s an idea,” said Ron loudly, before Harry could speak, “why don’t you shut your mouth?”

metadata.description: I’m protective of Harry and get ready to defend him physically when someone insults him.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps the word “weasel” had affected Ron particularly strongly; in any case, he was now looking at Zacharias as though he would like nothing better than to thump him.

metadata.description: I side with Harry and the others who want practical Defence lessons; I’ll back him up against critics.
metadata.source_text: “Here’s an idea,” said Ron loudly, before Harry could speak, “why don’t you shut your mouth?”

metadata.description: I found a notice that clearly means Umbridge might know about our group, and that discovery wiped away the happiness I felt and made me furious.
metadata.source_text: The happiness that had filled him since Saturday was gone. His insides were pulsing with rage. "This isn’t a coincidence," he said, his hands forming fists. "She knows."

metadata.description: I used to think we might be lucky and safe, but after reading that notice I don't believe it's a coincidence anymore; I now believe someone told Umbridge and I feel betrayed.
metadata.source_text: "This isn’t a coincidence," he said, his hands forming fists. "She knows."

metadata.description: I noticed Hedwig arrived late with a letter and, worse, that her feathers were ruffled and one wing looked injured, so she's hurt and won't fly properly without care.
metadata.source_text: "Hedwig’s feathers were oddly ruffled; some were bent the wrong way, and she was holding one of her wings at an odd angle. 'She’s hurt!' Harry whispered, bending his head low over her."

metadata.description: I still trust Hermione and Ron to act — I want to tell Hermione first and go to her, and I rely on them to help me deal with the notice and the danger it means.
metadata.source_text: "I wonder if Hermione’s seen this yet?" Harry said, looking around at the door to the girls’ dormitories. "Let’s go and tell her," said Ron.

metadata.description: I found Hedwig at the window with a letter and realised something was wrong with her wing when her feathers were ruffled and she was holding one wing oddly.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig’s feathers were oddly ruffled; some were bent the wrong way, and she was holding one of her wings at an odd angle.

metadata.description: I believed at first Hedwig would just hand me the letter and fly off, but then I learned she was hurt and needed help instead.
metadata.source_text: He had expected Hedwig to hold out her leg so that he could remove the letter and then fly off to the Owlery, but the moment the window was open wide enough she hopped inside, hooting dolefully.

metadata.description: I felt guilty leaving Hedwig with Professor Grubbly-Plank because she stared at me as if she couldn't believe I'd give her away like that.
metadata.source_text: Hedwig, who was staring at Harry as though unable to believe he would give her away like this.

metadata.description: I've got a letter from Sirius that says "Today, same time, same place."
metadata.source_text: Today, same time, same place.

metadata.description: McGonagall warned me that channels of communication in and out of Hogwarts may be being watched, so I'm suddenly more careful about how messages get in and out.
metadata.source_text: Bear in mind, that channels of communication in and out of Hogwarts may be being watched, won’t you?

metadata.description: I handed Hedwig to Professor Grubbly-Plank because she said she could look after her; I feel a bit guilty for giving Hedwig away like that, but I trusted Grubbly-Plank to help.
metadata.source_text: She shouldn’t be flying long distances for a few days, in any case.

metadata.description: I've put a jinx on the parchment we signed, so if anyone runs off and tells Umbridge we'll be able to find out who betrayed us.
metadata.source_text: "No, they can’t have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed," said Hermione grimly.

metadata.description: I no longer think that secrecy alone will protect us; I believe we need defensive measures like jinxes and caution, and I'm prepared to act to expose a traitor.
metadata.source_text: "No, they can’t have done because I put a jinx on that piece of parchment we all signed," said Hermione grimly. "Believe me, if anyone’s run off and told Umbridge, we’ll know exactly who they are and they will really regret it."

metadata.description: I think the situation makes some classmates look suspicious and untrustworthy around us, and I'm anxious that obvious guests at the Hufflepuff table would draw attention, so I told them to sit down.
metadata.source_text: "Never mind spots, the idiots can’t come over here now, it’ll look really suspicious — sit down!" she mouthed to Ernie and Hannah, gesturing frantically to them to rejoin the Hufflepuff table.

metadata.description: I noticed Hedwig was quivering and that there was something wrong with her wing when I put my quill down and leaned in to look more closely.
metadata.source_text: Hermione and Ron leaned in closer; Hermione even put down her quill. 'Look — there’s something wrong with her wing —'

metadata.description: I briefly stopped being focused on the lesson because Hedwig's condition made the whole class pay attention to something other than Professor Binns.
metadata.source_text: Professor Binns who continued to read his notes, serenely unaware that the class’s attention was even less focused upon him than usual.

metadata.description: I joined Harry and Ron at once to help with Hedwig, showing I'm ready to support Harry when his owl is hurt.
metadata.source_text: Hermione and Ron leaned in closer; Hermione even put down her quill.

metadata.description: I asked Harry if Hedwig was okay and where he had taken her, because Hedwig being looked after matters and I wanted to know immediately.
metadata.source_text: Is Hedwig okay?

metadata.description: Hearing McGonagall’s warning about communications being watched makes me more alert to the possibility that messages could be intercepted.
metadata.source_text: Bear in mind, that channels of communication in and out of Hogwarts may be being watched, won’t you?

metadata.description: I stood with Ron and watched Harry come over; I'm clearly concerned for Harry and Hedwig and ready to listen when he explains what happened.
metadata.source_text: Is Hedwig okay? asked Hermione anxiously

metadata.description: I reckon someone in the crowd could have run off and told Umbridge, and that thought makes me angry enough to start naming people I don't trust.
metadata.source_text: "And let’s face it, we don’t know how many of the people who turned up we can trust. . . . Any of them could have run off and told Umbridge . . ."

metadata.description: I used to think some people admired us and believed us, but now I feel betrayed and suspect classmates like Zacharias Smith and Michael Corner might be the sort to grass us to Umbridge.
metadata.source_text: "Zacharias Smith!" said Ron at once, punching a fist into his hand. "Or — I thought that Michael Corner had a really shifty look too —"

metadata.description: I'm furious and less trusting of certain classmates; I openly blame specific people and I'm ready to confront them or lash out if I have to.
metadata.source_text: "Zacharias Smith!" said Ron at once, punching a fist into his hand. "Or — I thought that Michael Corner had a really shifty look too —"

metadata.description: I leaned in to see Hedwig and noticed something seemed wrong with her wing alongside Harry and Hermione.
metadata.source_text: Hermione and Ron leaned in closer; Hermione even put down her quill. 'Look — there’s something wrong with her wing —'

metadata.description: I realised the lesson was boring and that our attention was caught by Hedwig instead, showing how quickly we can be distracted from Binns's lecture.
metadata.source_text: Professor Binns who continued to read his notes, serenely unaware that the class’s attention was even less focused upon him than usual.

metadata.description: I stayed with Harry and Hermione in the courtyard after break, keeping close as we looked at Harry’s letter together.
metadata.source_text: Here he spotted Ron and Hermione already standing in a sheltered corner, their cloak collars turned up against the wind.

metadata.description: I asked Harry who the letter was from when he handed it to me, wanting to know straight away who'd sent it.
metadata.source_text: Who’s the letter from anyway?

metadata.description: When Harry told me the note was from 'Snuffles' I understood who had sent it and that we might need to be careful about meeting as instructed.
metadata.source_text: 'Snuffles,' said Harry quietly.

metadata.description: I was standing with Hermione in the courtyard and went straight to ask Harry about Hedwig and the letter; I'm clearly ready to support Harry and quick to question odd circumstances.
metadata.source_text: Where did you take her?

metadata.description: I found out Malfoy said the Ministry might have me sent to St. Mungo's — they supposedly have a special ward for people whose brains have been addled by magic.
metadata.source_text: My father says it’s a matter of time before the Ministry has him carted off to St. Mungo’s. . . . apparently they’ve got a special ward for people whose brains have been addled by magic . . .

metadata.description: I felt even more threatened by how much the Ministry and people like Malfoy are willing to smear us; it made me believe our safety at Hogwarts is more precarious than I thought.
metadata.source_text: My father says it’s a matter of time before the Ministry has him carted off to St. Mungo’s. . . . apparently they’ve got a special ward for people whose brains have been addled by magic . . .

metadata.description: I know now Snape will use any chance to humiliate me — he emptied my cauldron and gave me an essay, like he was waiting to punish me the moment I slipped up.
metadata.source_text: No marks again, then, Potter," said Snape maliciously, emptying Harry’s cauldron with a wave of his wand. "You will write me an essay..."

metadata.description: I worried that a scroll could easily be resealed by magic and that communications over the Floo Network might be watched, so messages can be intercepted unless precautions are taken.
metadata.source_text: It wouldn’t be exactly difficult to reseal the scroll by magic. . . . And if anyone’s watching the Floo Network . . . but I don’t really see how we can warn him not to come without that being intercepted too!

metadata.description: I grew more anxious about our security after reading the note; I no longer feel that a sealed scroll is necessarily safe from prying eyes or tampering.
metadata.source_text: I just hope nobody else has read this . . ." "But it was still sealed and everything," said Harry, trying to convince himself as much as her.

metadata.description: I disapprove of Umbridge's involvement in lessons and suspect the Ministry's interference in school matters is inappropriate; her presence in Snape's class confirms my concerns.
metadata.source_text: She gestured toward the dim corner of the dungeon, and Harry saw Professor Umbridge sitting there, clipboard on her knee.

metadata.description: I learned from Malfoy's bragging that Umbridge allowed the Slytherin Quidditch team to carry on because of connections with the Ministry — his father pops into the Ministry all the time.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, Umbridge gave the Slytherin Quidditch team permission to continue playing straightaway, I went to ask her first thing this morning. Well, it was pretty much automatic, I mean, she knows my father really well, he’s always popping in and out of the Ministry. . . .

metadata.description: I felt angrier about how unfair things are — Malfoy gloating about influence made me believe Gryffindor might be treated worse and that the Ministry favours certain families.
metadata.source_text: It’ll be interesting to see whether Gryffindor are allowed to keep playing, won’t it?” “Don’t rise," Hermione whispered...

metadata.description: When Neville charged Malfoy I realised I and Harry have to protect our mates; grabbing Neville with Harry was necessary because Crabbe and Goyle would have torn him apart.
metadata.source_text: Crabbe and Goyle would’ve torn you apart." "Neville, no!" Harry leapt forward and seized the back of Neville’s robes; Neville struggled frantically...

metadata.description: I've learned that Umbridge has put Trelawney on probation and that the Ministry are enforcing decrees like banning Quidditch practice and restricting our activities.
metadata.source_text: Looks like she\'s put her on probation." "No Quidditch practice," said Angelina in hollow tones

metadata.description: I reckon sitting safely at school without learning how to defend ourselves is worse than being expelled for trying — I'd rather be expelled and able to fight than clueless.
metadata.source_text: Well, better expelled and able to defend yourselves than sitting safely in school without a clue," said Sirius.

metadata.description: Sirius feels proud of me for wanting to form an illegal Defense group — I can tell he backs us and that makes me trust him more and want his support.
metadata.source_text: He looked neither angry nor worried; on the contrary, he was looking at Harry with distinct pride.

metadata.description: I've realised that the blocked Fourth-Floor mirror passage and the cramped Shrieking Shack make organising a twenty-eight-person Defense group tricky; we need a much larger, private space.
metadata.source_text: "Well, Sirius, it\'s just that there were only four of you meeting in the Shrieking Shack when you were at school... But there are twenty-eight of us and none of us is an Animagus"

metadata.description: I still think following rules matters, but I can see that learning to defend ourselves now might be necessary even if it risks expulsion; I\'m worried yet pragmatic about consequences.
metadata.source_text: "And if we do get expelled?" "Well, better expelled and able to defend yourselves than sitting safely in school without a clue," said Sirius.

metadata.description: Fred and George are clearly clever at making money and entertaining, but I regard their tricks as flashy and not academically useful, even if everyone else adores them.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, they only know flashy stuff that\'s no real use to anyone," said Hermione disparagingly.

metadata.description: Mum doesn\'t want me anywhere near an illegal Defense group; she thinks I\'ll be expelled and my future ruined, and Sirius passed her message on to make sure I knew.
metadata.source_text: "She says on no account whatsoever are you to take part in an illegal secret Defense Against the Dark Arts group... She says you\'ll be expelled for sure and your future will be ruined."

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and resentful about Umbridge cutting Quidditch and using it as a threat; I think she\'s enjoying holding power over us and it makes me angry.
metadata.source_text: "She\'s given the Slytherins permission, why not us?"

metadata.description: Hearing Sirius back the idea of the Defense group makes me more willing to join — I trust his support and it lifts my spirits even though Mum warned me off.
metadata.source_text: "I think it\'s an excellent idea!" said Sirius.

metadata.description: I heard Professor Flitwick praise Hermione after she silenced the raven; he said, "Very good, Miss Granger!", so I know she performed the Silencio successfully.
metadata.source_text: "Very good, Miss Granger!" said Professor Flitwick’s squeaky little voice and Harry, Ron, and Hermione all jumped.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I'm a bit more convinced that Hermione's good at precise charms than I thought; seeing her swap in her frog and silence that raven made me trust her skill more.
metadata.source_text: "Fine, let’s swap," said Hermione, seizing Ron’s raven and replacing it with her own fat bullfrog. "Silencio!" The raven continued to open and close its sharp beak, but no sound came out.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I feel closer to Angelina and Ron over Quidditch plans now that Angelina’s got permission; hearing Ron and I say "Excellent!" together made it a proper team moment.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve got permission!" she said. "To re-form the Quidditch team!" "Excellent!" said Ron and Harry together.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I've learned that the Silencio charm needs a sharp jab of the wand rather than a waving motion; moving the wand correctly silenced the raven when I tried it.
metadata.source_text: "It’s the way you’re moving your wand," said Hermione, watching Ron critically. "You don’t want to wave it, it’s more a sharp jab."
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I’m wondering now whether we are doing the right thing about Sirius and Snuffles; looking at the rain and thinking about him has made me uncertain instead of certain.
metadata.source_text: "Just thinking . . ." she said. "About Siri . . . Snuffles?" said Harry. "No . . . not exactly . . ." said Hermione slowly. "More . . . wondering . . . I suppose we’re doing the right thing . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I feel a protective, practical closeness to Ron and Harry when I help in class and when we plan things; swapping the raven for my frog and coaching Ron shows I trust them to learn.
metadata.source_text: "Fine, let’s swap," said Hermione, seizing Ron’s raven and replacing it with her own fat bullfrog. "Silencio!"
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I learnt that some creatures are trickier to silence than others because I said, "Ravens are harder than frogs," after struggling with the charm on the raven.
metadata.source_text: "Ravens are harder than frogs," said Ron testily.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I felt flustered by Flitwick’s attention when he asked to see me; after Hermione showed how it was done I realised I need to pay more attention to wand movement.
metadata.source_text: "Now, let me see you try, Mr Weasley!" "Wha — ? Oh — oh, right," said Ron, very flustered. "Er — Silencio!"
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I feel excited and united with Harry and Angelina about Quidditch again; when Angelina told us she’d got permission I joined Harry saying "Excellent!" because I want the team back.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve got permission!" she said. "To re-form the Quidditch team!" "Excellent!" said Ron and Harry together.
metadata.scene_title: Charms Lesson Continues; Permission and Pitch Plans

metadata.description: I've learned that Hermione put an Impervius charm on my glasses to stop rain fogging them, because she did it when we played Hufflepuff in a storm.
metadata.source_text: Hermione did it," said Harry. He pulled out his wand, tapped his glasses and said, "Impervius!
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I still trust Sirius's advice completely; I believe he's given us good guidance before and I don't think he's lost his judgment despite being confined.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I do!" said Harry at once. "He’s always given us great advice!
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I see Sirius as someone whose advice matters to me and who supports our plans; talking to him has made me more confident about starting the Defense group.
metadata.source_text: Sirius agrees with us, so you don't think we should do it anymore?" Hermione looked tense ... "Do you honestly trust his judgment?" "Yes, I do!" said Harry at once. "He’s always given us great advice!
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I've learnt that the Silencio charm works better with a sharp jab of the wand rather than a waving motion; precise movement matters for the spell to silence animals properly.
metadata.source_text: You don’t want to wave it, it’s more a sharp jab."
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I've started to doubt whether forming a secret Defense Against the Dark Arts group is the right thing to do after talking to Snuffles; what seemed right at first now worries me.
metadata.source_text: But after talking to Snuffles . . ." "But he’s all for it!" said Harry. "Yes," said Hermione, staring at the window again. "Yes, that’s what made me think maybe it wasn’t a good idea after all . . .
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I'm concerned that Sirius might be becoming reckless while he's stuck in Grimmauld Place and could be encouraging us because he’s frustrated and wants to act through us.
metadata.source_text: You don’t think he has become . . . sort of . . . reckless . . . since he’s been cooped up in Grimmauld Place? You don’t think he’s . . . kind of . . . living through us?
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: Ravens are trickier to silence than frogs, or at least I found them harder than frogs when I tried the Silencio charm on that ugly raven.
metadata.source_text: Ravens are harder than frogs," said Ron testily.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I still reckon Sirius knows what he's doing and I trust him; when Hermione worries I defend him and say he’s right, though I get confused by her doubts.
metadata.source_text: "Sirius is right," he said, "you do sound just like my mother.""Yes, I do!" said Harry at once. "He’s always given us great advice!"
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I see Hermione as suddenly uneasy and worrying more than usual; she’s acting more tense and miserable when she brings up doubts about Sirius and our plans.
metadata.source_text: Hermione looked tense and rather miserable. Now staring at her own hands she said, "Do you honestly trust his judgment?"
metadata.scene_title: Hermione's Doubts About Sirius; Rain and Impervius

metadata.description: I've learned that Dobby volunteered to return Hedwig and that Professor Grubbly-Plank said Hedwig is all well now.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby volunteered to return Harry Potter’s owl!" said the elf squeakily, with a look of positive adoration on his face. "Professor Grubbly-Plank says she is all well now, sir!"
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I feel a bit unsettled by my dream about the door; it's been very vivid and I keep trying to shake the image off.
metadata.source_text: "Thanks, Dobby!" said Harry, stroking Hedwig’s head and blinking hard, trying to rid himself of the image of the door in his dream. . . . It had been very vivid. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: Dobby clearly adores me and is grateful because I set him free; I appreciate his loyalty even if I can't accept his offers to help.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby wishes he could help Harry Potter, for Harry Potter set Dobby free and Dobby is much, much happier now . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I've left many knitted hats and clothes out in the common room; they are being taken by house-elves like Dobby and used by them or others.
metadata.source_text: Dobby the house-elf was standing beside the table on which Hermione had left her half a dozen knitted hats.
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I might need to think about how leaving clothes out affects house-elves, because hiding hats and socks makes some elves find it insulting and stop cleaning.
metadata.source_text: Nor do the other house-elves. None of them will clean Gryffindor Tower anymore, not with the hats and socks hidden everywhere, they finds them insulting, sir.
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: My knitting and gifts are appreciated by Dobby and used by house-elves like Winky, but they also cause complicated feelings among elves I didn't intend to upset.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby has been taking some for Winky too, sir."
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I found out that Winky, another house-elf, has been drinking a lot and won't take clothes, so Dobby has been collecting some of Hermione's things for her.
metadata.source_text: "Yeah, how is Winky?" asked Harry. Dobby’s ears drooped slightly. "Winky is still drinking lots, sir," he said sadly...
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I think house-elves' reactions to clothes are more serious than I realised; hiding socks and hats can make them stop doing tasks like cleaning.
metadata.source_text: "Nor do the other house-elves. None of them will clean Gryffindor Tower anymore, not with the hats and socks hidden everywhere, they finds them insulting, sir."
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: Dobby seems devoted to Harry and even sacrifices his own comfort to bring news and help other elves; I respect his loyalty more now.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby wishes he could help Harry Potter, for Harry Potter set Dobby free and Dobby is much, much happier now . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Retreat to Common Room; Dobby Appears with News of Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I've learned that the Room of Requirement can provide almost anything someone needs — furniture, antidotes, even chamber pots if a bathroom is required.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby has used it, sir," said the elf, dropping his voice and looking guilty, "when Winky has been very drunk. He has hidden her in the Room of Requirement and he has found antidotes to butterbeer there, and a nice elf-sized bed to settle her on while she sleeps it off, sir. . . . And Dobby knows Mr. Filch has found extra cleaning materials there when he has run short, sir, and —" "— and if you really needed a bathroom," said Harry, suddenly remembering something Dumbledore had said at the Yule Ball the previous Christmas, "would it fill itself with chamber pots?" "Dobby expects so, sir," said Dobby, nodding earnestly.
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I feel convinced the Room of Requirement is perfect for secret meetings now; what seemed like a handy rumor actually looks like a reliable place we can use.
metadata.source_text: "It sounds brilliant," said Harry, his heart racing. "It sounds perfect, Dobby. When can you show me where it is?"
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: Dobby's been really helpful and honest with me; I trust him to show us the room and I value what he tells me about Hogwarts secrets.
metadata.source_text: "Anytime, Harry Potter, sir," said Dobby, looking delighted at Harry's enthusiasm. "We could go now, if you like!"
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I've observed that most people stumble across the Room of Requirement by chance and often cannot find it again because they don't realise it's always there to be called into service.
metadata.source_text: "Very few, sir. Mostly people stumbles across it when they needs it, sir, but often they never finds it again, for they do not know that it is always there waiting to be called into service, sir."
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I'm more cautious about rushing off at odd hours now; even exciting opportunities like seeing the Room need proper planning rather than reckless haste.
metadata.source_text: For a moment Harry was tempted to go now; he was halfway out of his seat, intending to hurry upstairs for his Invisibility Cloak when, not for the first time, a voice very much like Hermione's whispered in his ear: reckless.
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I think Harry listens to reason when I caution him; my warning about recklessness seems to influence his decision to postpone immediate action.
metadata.source_text: Not tonight, Dobby," said Harry reluctantly, sinking back into his chair. "This is really important. . . . I don't want to blow it, it'll need proper planning. . . . Listen, can you just tell me exactly where this Room of Requirement is and how to get in there?"
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I've realised from the talk that the Room of Requirement is very secretive and only a few people find it, usually by accident when they desperately need something.
metadata.source_text: "Very few, sir. Mostly people stumbles across it when they needs it, sir, but often they never finds it again, for they do not know that it is always there waiting to be called into service, sir."
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I'm more impressed by the Room's usefulness than I expected; the idea of a place that supplies everything you need changes how useful I think Hogwarts can be.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby expects so, sir," said Dobby, nodding earnestly. "It is a most amazing room, sir."
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I trust Dobby's information about the castle a bit more now; he seems to know hidden things and he was straightforward when he told us about the Room.
metadata.source_text: "Anytime, Harry Potter, sir," said Dobby, looking delighted at Harry's enthusiasm. "We could go now, if you like!"
metadata.scene_title: Dobby Describes Uses of the Room; Plans for D.A. Meeting

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore at least mentioned the room to me at the Yule Ball, so Dumbledore is aware of the place alongside Dobby's involvement.
metadata.source_text: “This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball.”
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: Well, when Hermione reminded me about Dobby’s past recklessness I felt a bit concerned, but when I remembered Dumbledore had mentioned it I was reassured and relaxed a bit.
metadata.source_text: “This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball.”
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I noticed Hermione watching me closely and questioning things, and when I explained Dumbledore knew, she trusted my word and stopped objecting to my plans — that showed me she listens and will back down when satisfied.
metadata.source_text: “What?” he said thickly. “Well . . . it’s just that Dobby’s plans aren’t always that safe. Don’t you remember when he lost you all the bones in your arm?” “This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball.” Hermione’s expression cleared. “Dumbledore told you about it?” “Just in passing,” said Harry, shrugging. “Oh well, that’s all right then,” said Hermione briskly and she raised no more objections.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I remembered that Dobby has a history of unsafe plans — like when he caused Harry to lose the bones in his arm — so Dobby’s schemes can be risky.
metadata.source_text: “Well . . . it’s just that Dobby’s plans aren’t always that safe. Don’t you remember when he lost you all the bones in your arm?”
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I was worried about the safety of the room at first, but when Harry told me Dumbledore had mentioned it at the Yule Ball, I changed my mind and decided it was all right.
metadata.source_text: “This room isn’t just some mad idea of Dobby’s; Dumbledore knows about it too, he mentioned it to me at the Yule Ball.” “Dumbledore told you about it?” “Just in passing,” said Harry, shrugging. “Oh well, that’s all right then,” said Hermione briskly and she raised no more objections.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I showed my concern for Harry by questioning the plan, and when he reassured me I stepped back quickly — it reminded me that Harry can get reliable information from his teachers and I trust him when he says so.
metadata.source_text: When he looked up to take a drink of pumpkin juice, he found Hermione watching him. “What?” he said thickly. “Well . . . it’s just that Dobby’s plans aren’t always that safe...”“Oh well, that’s all right then,” said Hermione briskly and she raised no more objections.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I helped Harry and Hermione spend most of the day finding people who signed the list in the Hog’s Head, so I know we tracked down nearly everyone who agreed to meet that evening.
metadata.source_text: Together with Ron they had spent most of the day seeking out those people who had signed their names to the list in the Hog’s Head and telling them where to meet that evening.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I felt a bit nervous walking the corridors, but being with Harry and Hermione and knowing we’d told all twenty-five people made me more confident that the plan would go ahead.
metadata.source_text: Somewhat to Harry’s disappointment, it was Ginny who managed to find Cho Chang and her friend first; however, by the end of dinner he was confident that the news had been passed to every one of the twenty-five people who had turned up in the Hog’s Head.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: Going out around the castle with Harry and Hermione reminded me that we act as a team — I back them and help with the practical work of getting people together for what we decide to do.
metadata.source_text: Together with Ron they had spent most of the day seeking out those people who had signed their names to the list in the Hog’s Head and telling them where to meet that evening.
metadata.scene_title: Spreading the Word and Setting Out with the Marauder’s Map

metadata.description: I found a polished door that suddenly appeared in the wall and I opened it — there’s a spacious room inside with flickering torches, bookcases, and big silk cushions instead of chairs.
metadata.source_text: A highly polished door had appeared in the wall. ... Harry reached out, seized the brass handle, pulled open the door, and led the way into a spacious room lit with flickering torches like those that illuminated the dungeons eight floors below. The walls were lined with wooden bookcases, and instead of chairs there were large silk cushions on the floor.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I think we might actually have somewhere to practice without being found now — that door led to a hidden room that feels private enough for training.
metadata.source_text: We need somewhere to learn to fight. . . . he thought. Just give us a place to practice . . . somewhere they can’t find us . . .
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I trust Hermione to spot things or to call us back when we’ve missed something — she caught us as we wheeled around, and that sharpness matters when we’re hunting out secret places.
metadata.source_text: “Harry,” said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I noticed and named the moment Harry should stop — I sharply called to him as they wheeled around and then observed the polished door appearing in the wall.
metadata.source_text: “Harry,” said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past. A highly polished door had appeared in the wall.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I’m convinced that careful observation pays off — my sharpness made them stop and see the door, so being attentive actually uncovers useful things.
metadata.source_text: “Harry,” said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I feel responsible for keeping Harry and Ron focused and aware; my voice can redirect them when they miss important details, and they rely on that from me.
metadata.source_text: “Harry,” said Hermione sharply, as they wheeled around after their third walk past.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I stared at the polished door and felt wary — that door appearing out of nowhere made me uneasy even as Harry reached for the handle.
metadata.source_text: A highly polished door had appeared in the wall. Ron was staring at it, looking slightly wary.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I’m a bit more cautious now about strange magical things appearing suddenly — that door made me uneasy and I don’t want to rush into unknown places without thinking.
metadata.source_text: Ron was staring at it, looking slightly wary.
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I rely on Harry to take the lead when something surprising appears; he grabbed the handle and went in, and I followed but I still felt wary about the situation.
metadata.source_text: Harry reached out, seized the brass handle, pulled open the door, and led the way into a spacious room ...
metadata.scene_title: Finding the Room of Requirement and Discovering Its Contents

metadata.description: I recognised a cracked Foe-Glass that I was sure had been hanging in Moody’s fake office the previous year.
metadata.source_text: a large, cracked Foe-Glass that Harry was sure had hung, the previous year, in the fake Moody’s office.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: Seeing all those books and instruments here makes me think this room will actually help us practice Stunning and other defensive spells properly.
metadata.source_text: “These will be good when we’re practicing Stunning,” said Ron enthusiastically, prodding one of the cushions with his foot.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: I noticed Hermione so happy and convinced by the books that I can tell she's fully behind what we're doing now; her excitement reassures me about our plan.
metadata.source_text: She looked around at Harry, her face glowing, and he saw that the presence of hundreds of books had finally convinced Hermione that what they were doing was right.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: I've found a whole range of relevant books — a Compendium of Common Curses and Their Counter-Actions, The Dark Arts Outsmarted, Self-Defensive Spellwork — which should help with defensive magic study.
metadata.source_text: “A Compendium of Common Curses and Their Counter-Actions . . . The Dark Arts Outsmarted . . . Self-Defensive Spellwork . . . wow . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: Seeing hundreds of books here has convinced me that what we're doing is right; I'm really certain now that studying here is the correct thing to do.
metadata.source_text: She looked around at Harry, her face glowing, and he saw that the presence of hundreds of books had finally convinced Hermione that what they were doing was right.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: I feel closer to Harry about this because he’s here and involved; sharing this discovery with him makes me more confident we'll succeed together.
metadata.source_text: She looked around at Harry, her face glowing, and he saw that the presence of hundreds of books had finally convinced Hermione that what they were doing was right.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the room, so I do not know what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Exploring the Room's Arsenal and Students Arrive

metadata.description: I was not present when Closing the Door, Choosing Leadership, and Planning Lessons occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Closing the Door, Choosing Leadership, and Planning Lessons

metadata.description: I've learned that Expelliarmus can save your life — I used it against him and it saved me last June.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve used it against him," said Harry quietly. "It saved my life last June."
metadata.scene_title: Training Begins; Mixed Results and Discipline

metadata.description: I'm a bit surprised at myself — I felt odd issuing instructions, but seeing everyone follow made me reckon I'm capable of leading practice.
metadata.source_text: "It felt very odd to be issuing instructions, but not nearly as odd as seeing them followed."
metadata.scene_title: Training Begins; Mixed Results and Discipline

metadata.description: I think Neville's braver and more competent than I thought — he actually managed to disarm me and was thrilled, so I want to encourage him.
metadata.source_text: "I DID IT!" said Neville gleefully. "I’ve never done it before — I DID IT!"
metadata.scene_title: Training Begins; Mixed Results and Discipline

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the training practice, so I don't know the specifics of what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was absent from the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Training Begins; Mixed Results and Discipline

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the training practice, so I don't know the specifics of what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley was absent from the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Training Begins; Mixed Results and Discipline

metadata.description: I've learned the practice is running late — it's already ten past nine and we risk being caught and punished by Filch if we don't leave straight away.
metadata.source_text: have you checked the time?" He looked down at his watch and received a shock — it was already ten past nine, which meant they needed to get back to their common rooms immediately or risk being caught and punished by Filch for being out-of-bounds.
metadata.scene_title: Session Wraps Up; Plans for Next Meeting and Safe Return

metadata.description: I reckon the group's getting better; slowly the general performance improved as I moved around and made suggestions, so I feel more confident about leading further meetings.
metadata.source_text: Slowly the general performance improved. He moved off around the room again, stopping here and there to make suggestions.
metadata.scene_title: Session Wraps Up; Plans for Next Meeting and Safe Return

metadata.description: I felt awkward with Cho and Marietta — I tried not to go near them at first, then when Cho misfired and Marietta glared I had to smooth things over and tell Cho not to mind her friend.
metadata.source_text: He avoided going near Cho and her friend for a while... "You made me nervous, I was doing all right before then!" Cho told Harry ruefully. "Don't mind her," Cho muttered.
metadata.scene_title: Session Wraps Up; Plans for Next Meeting and Safe Return

metadata.description: I wasn't present during most of the events; I called about the time from the other end of the room but otherwise I'm not a primary witness to the other conversations.
metadata.source_text: Hermione called from the other end of the room, "have you checked the time?"
metadata.scene_title: Session Wraps Up; Plans for Next Meeting and Safe Return

metadata.description: I wasn't in the scene; Ron isn't here and I don't know what he would have seen or said during the practice session.
metadata.scene_title: Session Wraps Up; Plans for Next Meeting and Safe Return

metadata.description: I noticed that Hermione’s fake Galleons change their numerals to show the next meeting’s date when Harry sets his coin and that they grow hot when the date changes.
metadata.source_text: On these fake coins, though, the numbers will change to reflect the time and date of the next meeting. The coins will grow hot when the date changes, so if you’re carrying them in a pocket you’ll be able to feel them.

metadata.description: I reckon Hermione’s method is far better than branding anyone; engraving the date on metal is clever and less horrible than marking people’s skin.
metadata.source_text: That is where I got the idea . . . but you’ll notice I decided to engrave the date on bits of metal rather than on our members’ skin . . .

metadata.description: I’m proud of Hermione for that idea and I trust her skills — I slid my Galleon into my pocket gladly because I like the plan and what she’s done.
metadata.source_text: Yeah . . . I prefer your way," said Harry, grinning, as he slipped his Galleon into his pocket.

metadata.description: I’ve worked out that on real Galleons the numerals are serial numbers for the goblin who cast the coin, and that I can mimic that system with an enchanted Protean Charm so the coins will all change together.
metadata.source_text: On real Galleons that’s just a serial number referring to the goblin who cast the coin. On these fake coins, though, the numbers will change to reflect the time and date of the next meeting. ... because I’ve put a Protean Charm on them, they’ll all change to mimic his.

metadata.description: I think carrying a Galleon is innocuous enough to avoid suspicion even if Umbridge made us empty pockets; I believed the coin idea would be practical and discreet.
metadata.source_text: I mean, even if Umbridge asked us to turn out our pockets, there’s nothing fishy about carrying a Galleon, is there?

metadata.description: I felt slightly uncertain when the room went quiet, but I stood my ground and answered Terry Boot — I realised I get noticed for being clever, and people regard my skill with some surprise.
metadata.source_text: A blank silence greeted Hermione’s words. She looked around at all the faces upturned to her, rather disconcerted. “Well — I thought it was a good idea,” she said uncertainly, ... “You can do a Protean Charm?” said Terry Boot. “Yes,” said Hermione.

metadata.description: I learned that I’ve got no real Galleons to confuse Hermione’s fake ones with — I stared at my fake Galleon feeling a bit mournful about it.
metadata.source_text: Fat chance," said Ron, who was examining his own fake Galleon with a slightly mournful air. "I haven’t got any real Galleons to confuse it with.

metadata.description: I’m convinced the Slytherin taunts are getting to me more than usual; I’m starting to lose confidence and my hands shake when Malfoy imitates me.
metadata.source_text: When Draco Malfoy imitated Ron dropping the Quaffle ... Ron’s ears glowed red and his hands shook so badly that he was likely to drop whatever he was holding at the time too.

metadata.description: I can see how the Slytherins’ relentless insults make me panic on the pitch; I feel isolated when they sing about me and I don’t laugh it off like Harry does.
metadata.source_text: When Slytherins, some of them seventh years and considerably larger than he was, muttered as they passed in the corridors, 'Got your bed booked in the hospital wing, Weasley?' he did not laugh, but turned a delicate shade of green.

metadata.description: I caught the Snitch in a mad two-second scramble right after diving low; my fingers actually closed around the Snitch while Malfoy tried to grab it.
metadata.source_text: It was over in two breathless, desperate, windswept seconds — Harry’s fingers closed around the tiny, struggling ball — Malfoy’s fingernails scrabbled the back of Harry’s hand hopelessly — Harry pulled his broom upward, holding the struggling ball in his hand and the Gryffindor spectators screamed their approval.

metadata.description: I felt that winning the match made everything okay for a moment — that a Snitch grab would blot out Ron letting in goals — but the Bludger and the row afterwards showed things weren't that simple.
metadata.source_text: They were saved, it did not matter that Ron had let in those goals, nobody would remember as long as Gryffindor had won — WHAM! A Bludger hit Harry squarely in the small of the back

metadata.description: I know now exactly how nasty Malfoy can be; his jibes about my mother and the Weasleys pushed me over the edge and made me attack him — I won't forget his insults.
metadata.source_text: Or perhaps," said Malfoy, leering as he backed away, "you can remember what your mother’s house stank like, Potter, and Weasley’s pigsty reminds you of it —

metadata.description: I've learned that Professor Umbridge has the backing of the Minister — she brandishes a parchment called Educational Decree Number Twenty-five giving the High Inquisitor supreme authority over student punishments.
metadata.source_text: 'Educational Decree Number Twenty-five . . .'

metadata.description: I feel that the rules and authority at Hogwarts can be used unfairly against me; suddenly I don't expect impartial treatment when people like Umbridge are empowered.
metadata.source_text: I do not care what provocation Malfoy offered you, I do not care if he insulted every family member you possess, your behavior was disgusting and I am giving each of you a week’s worth of detention!

metadata.description: I'm seeing Umbridge as someone openly hostile to me and my teammates — she smiled as she said we should be banned for life, and I now view her as an enemy who enjoys hurting us.
