metadata.source_text: I really think I will have to ban these two from playing Quidditch ever again," she said, looking from Harry to George and back again.

metadata.description: I've learned that Educational Decree Number Twenty-five exists and that it gives the High Inquisitor power to override other staff's punishments and remove pupils' privileges.
metadata.source_text: 'The High Inquisitor will henceforth have supreme authority over all punishments, sanctions, and removal of privileges pertaining to the students of Hogwarts, and the power to alter such punishments, sanctions, and removals of privileges as may have been ordered by other staff members.'

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that Hogwarts is being controlled from above in an unfair way; authority can be shifted to people like Umbridge who misuse it, and that worries me greatly.
metadata.source_text: Well, actually, Minerva," simpered Umbridge, "I think you’ll find that what I think does count.

metadata.description: I think Minerva is being undermined by Umbridge and the Ministry; despite Minerva's anger, Umbridge's official support makes me feel the staff cannot always protect us.
metadata.source_text: "You thought wrong," she said, turning her back on Umbridge. "Now, you two had better listen closely."

metadata.description: I've learned that I've been given a lifetime Quidditch ban along with Fred and George, and that Umbridge intends to confiscate our broomsticks to enforce it.
metadata.source_text: "Yes, Mr. Potter, I think a lifelong ban ought to do the trick," said Umbridge... "I will want their broomsticks confiscated, of course; I shall keep them safely in my office."

metadata.description: I feel utterly useless at Quidditch and convinced I should quit the team; after being banned and feeling I can't play properly, I'm ready to resign tomorrow.
metadata.source_text: "I'm going to resign first thing tomorrow."

metadata.description: I'm ashamed and blaming myself in front of Harry and Hermione; I'm distancing myself because I think my poor playing contributed to the disaster and letting the team down.
metadata.source_text: "For thinking I can play Quidditch," said Ron. "I'm going to resign first thing tomorrow."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 1 (Part 1) occurred.
I wasn't present during Hagrid's trip to find the giants, so I don't know the exact route or what he saw up close.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 1 (Part 1) occurred.
I wasn't there when Hagrid and Madame Maxime traveled to the giants, so I can't speak from firsthand experience about their journey.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 1 (Part 1) occurred.
I wasn't present on Hagrid's mission to the giants, therefore I don't have direct knowledge of the trekking or the giants themselves.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events Hagrid describes; I didn't see the giants, the gifts, or the fight in the valley.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there for Hagrid's meeting with the giants; I didn't witness the presentation of the Gubraithian fire or the subsequent fighting firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the giants' camp; I didn't watch Hagrid give gifts or see Karkus killed or Golgomath take over.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid and Madame Olympe tried to persuade some giants to listen to Dumbledore and that a few wounded giants understood their message.
metadata.source_text: Me an’ Olympe talked it over an’ we agreed, jus’ ’cause the Gurg looked like favorin’ You-Know-Who didn’ mean all of ’em would.

metadata.description: I’m more worried about the Death Eaters being bold enough to visit Golgomath and bring gifts — that makes them a bigger, more dangerous presence than I thought.
metadata.source_text: Couple of ’em were visitin’ him ev’ry day, bringin’ gifts ter the Gurg, an’ he wasn’ dangling them upside down.

metadata.description: I see Hagrid as stubbornly loyal and reckless in a good way — he still won’t stop trying to help creatures even when it’s dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Look, don’ you go worryin’ abou’ me, I promise yeh I’ve got really good stuff planned fer yer lessons now I’m back.

metadata.description: I found out that Macnair was visiting Golgomath and that Hagrid recognized him — that ties Death Eater activity directly to the giants.
metadata.source_text: Because I recognized one of ’em," Hagrid growled. "Macnair, remember him?

metadata.description: I'm increasingly convinced that we must be careful about what Hagrid teaches if Umbridge is inspecting — she’ll use any excuse to remove teachers close to Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: Umbridge is looking for any excuse to get rid of teachers she thinks are too close to Dumbledore. Please, Hagrid, teach us something dull that’s bound to come up in our O.W.L

metadata.description: I feel sorry and awkward about asking Hagrid about his mother, and I realise Hagrid doesn’t remember her fondly — it changes how tenderly I treat him.
metadata.source_text: Did you . . . was there any sign of . . . did you hear anything about your . . . your . . . mother while you were there?" "Dead," Hagrid grunted.

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid and Olympe managed to convince six or seven giants at one point, though they didn’t stick around after Golgomath’s raid.
metadata.source_text: I reckon we had abou’ six or seven o’ them convinced at one poin’." "Six or seven?" said Ron eagerly.

metadata.description: I’m disappointed that there aren’t giants coming to fight You-Know-Who with us now — I actually hoped they’d join our side.
metadata.source_text: So . . . so there aren’t any giants coming?" said Ron, looking disappointed.

metadata.description: I’ve got a lot of respect for Hagrid’s courage — sneaking around dark caves to talk to giants sounds proper brave to me.
metadata.source_text: You went poking around dark caves looking for giants?" said Ron with awed respect in his voice.

metadata.description: I saw a great black winged horse come out of the trees and tear flesh from the dead cow — they're real, not something I've imagined.
metadata.source_text: A pair of blank, white, shining eyes were growing larger through the gloom and a moment later the dragonish face, neck, and then skeletal body of a great, black, winged horse emerged from the darkness. ... and began to tear flesh from the dead cow with its pointed fangs.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I felt a big wave of relief because now I believe Hagrid truly knows about these creatures — I hadn't made them up in my head.
metadata.source_text: A great wave of relief broke over Harry. Here at last was proof that he had not imagined these creatures, that they were real: Hagrid knew about them too.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I'm looking at Hagrid with more trust now — if he can call beasts like that, I reckon he really understands them more than most people give him credit for.
metadata.source_text: Here at last was proof that he had not imagined these creatures, that they were real: Hagrid knew about them too.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I tried to plan Hagrid's lessons and found he wasn't there when I arrived — he came stumping out of the forest and refuses to tell me what he's keeping there.
metadata.source_text: He wasn’t even there when I arrived, I was knocking for at least half an hour. And then he came stumping out of the forest —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I'm worried and a bit hopeless about getting Hagrid to listen; I told him Umbridge is a problem and suggested following Grubbly-Plank's plan, but I don't think he took half of it in.
metadata.source_text: I tried to explain about Umbridge, but he just doesn’t get it. I tried to explain about Umbridge... I don’t think he listened to half of what I said.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I feel frustrated with Hagrid's stubbornness — even though I respect him, I don't think he always takes sensible advice, especially about safety and planning.
metadata.source_text: I don’t think he listened to half of what I said. He’s in a bit of a funny mood, you know.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: She said Hagrid wasn't there when she knocked and that he came stumping out of the forest — so Hagrid goes into the forest and brings strange things back.
metadata.source_text: He wasn’t even there when I arrived, I was knocking for at least half an hour. And then he came stumping out of the forest —
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I'm confused and jumpy — even when a huge black horse is eating right there, I still keep looking around and wondering why Hagrid didn't call again.
metadata.source_text: Why doesn’t Hagrid call again? ... Most of the rest of the class were wearing expressions as confused and nervously expectant as Ron’s and were still gazing everywhere but at the horse standing feet from them.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I guess Hagrid must know what he's doing with these creatures, though I still worry about him — he seems odd but he's also capable of handling dangerous beasts.
metadata.source_text: A great wave of relief broke over Harry. Here at last was proof that he had not imagined these creatures, that they were real: Hagrid knew about them too.
metadata.scene_title: Hagrid's Care and the Forbidden Forest Lesson Begins

metadata.description: I saw thestrals — weird winged, skeletal horses that pull the school carriages and strip flesh from carcasses as they feed.
metadata.source_text: Thestrals," said Hagrid proudly and Hermione gave a soft "oh!" of comprehension at Harry's shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I realized that the thestrals aren't just frightening omens; they're real creatures used at Hogwarts and useful for transport when needed.
metadata.source_text: Thestrals aren' unlucky, they' re dead clever an' useful! 'Course, this lot don' get a lot o' work, it’s mainly jus' pullin' the school carriages
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: Seeing Hagrid handle the thestrals and stand up to Umbridge made me respect him more — he knows his creatures and tries to calm everyone down.
metadata.source_text: “Don’ worry, it won’ hurt yeh,” said Hagrid patiently.
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I've learned that only people who have seen death can see thestrals — that's the reason some students can see them and others can't.
metadata.source_text: “The only people who can see thestrals,” she said, “are people who have seen death.”
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I'm angrier than I expected at Umbridge's condescension; hearing her mock Hagrid makes me feel furious and determined to call her out in my own way.
metadata.source_text: “You hag, you evil hag!” she whispered, as Umbridge walked toward Pansy Parkinson.
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: Watching Umbridge treat Hagrid like he's stupid has changed how I see her — I now view her as spiteful and untrustworthy, someone who enjoys humiliating others.
metadata.source_text: “'has . . . to . . . resort . . . to . . . crude . . . sign . . . language . . .'”
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I learned that thestrals can be tamed to find directions and won't lose you if you tell them where to go — they have amazing senses of direction.
metadata.source_text: “Well, once they’re tamed, like this lot, yeh’ll never be lost again. ’Mazin’ senses o’ direction, jus’ tell ’em where yeh want ter go —”
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I used to think thestrals were just creepy omens, but Hagrid's explanation made me change my mind a bit — they're not out to harm people unless provoked.
metadata.source_text: “Thestrals aren’ dangerous! All righ’, they might take a bite outta you if yeh really annoy them —”
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: Seeing Umbridge make fun of Hagrid and have the class laugh with Malfoy makes me feel protective of Hagrid and annoyed at the others who encourage her.
metadata.source_text: “Assuming they can understand you, of course,” said Malfoy loudly, and Pansy Parkinson collapsed in a fit of renewed giggles.
metadata.scene_title: The Thestrals Appear and Umbridge Intervenes

metadata.description: I was not present when Umbridge's Inspection and Questioning about Seeing Death occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge's Inspection and Questioning about Seeing Death

metadata.description: I was not present when Umbridge's Inspection and Questioning about Seeing Death occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Umbridge's Inspection and Questioning about Seeing Death

metadata.description: I found out that Cho kissed me after the meeting and she started crying all over me — she really did just sort of come at me and sob into my shoulder.
metadata.source_text: She — I wouldn’t’ve — she just sort of came at me — and next thing she’s crying all over me — I didn’t know what to do —
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I’d liked Cho for ages, but seeing her sobbing on my shoulder makes me suddenly unsure about how I feel and whether I want to be the one she’s with right now.
metadata.source_text: Don’t be silly," said Hermione vaguely, "Harry’s liked her for ages, haven’t you, Harry?" He did not answer. Yes, he had liked Cho for ages, but whenever he had imagined a scene involving the two of them it had always featured a Cho who was enjoying herself, as opposed to a Cho who was sobbing uncontrollably into his shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I know now that my relationship with Cho is complicated because she’s grieving Cedric — I feel awkward because she kissed me while crying and I’m worried about what that means between us.
metadata.source_text: Because she was crying," Harry continued heavily.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I know Cho has been crying all over the place — at mealtimes, in the loos, everywhere — so I can see she's grieving and upset pretty constantly.
metadata.source_text: Because Cho spends half her time crying these days," said Hermione vaguely. "She does it at mealtimes, in the loos, all over the place.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I’ve realized that Cho’s feelings are tangled: sad about Cedric, confused about who she likes, guilty about kissing, frightened of gossip, and worried about Quidditch — all at once.
metadata.source_text: Well, obviously, she’s feeling very sad, because of Cedric dying. Then I expect she’s feeling confused because she liked Cedric and now she likes Harry, and she can’t work out who she likes best. Then she’ll be feeling guilty, thinking it’s an insult to Cedric’s memory to be kissing Harry at all, and she’ll be worrying about what everyone else might say about her if she starts going out with Harry. And she probably can’t work out what her feelings toward Harry are anyway, because he was the one who was with Cedric when Cedric died, so that’s all very mixed up and painful. Oh, and she’s afraid she’s going to be thrown off the Ravenclaw Quidditch team because she’s been flying so badly.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I think Ron is being horribly insensitive about Cho’s situation — he’ll tease and laugh when he shouldn’t, and I’m not having any of his wartish attitudes now.
metadata.source_text: Ron," said Hermione in a dignified voice, dipping the point of her quill into her ink pot, "you are the most insensitive wart I have ever had the misfortune to meet.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I learned that Cho kissed Harry and even cried during it — he nodded and said she cried, and I saw him looking embarrassed about the whole thing.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked from Ron’s expression of mingled curiosity and hilarity to Hermione’s slight frown, and nodded. "HA!" Ron made a triumphant gesture...
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I’m beginning to feel a bit less gleeful about Harry and Cho because when Harry said she was crying I suddenly worried about how awkward that must’ve been for him.
metadata.source_text: "Because she was crying," Harry continued heavily. "Oh," said Ron, his smile fading slightly.
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I still tease Harry mercilessly, but I’d defend him if anyone said he was a coward — hearing he patted her on the back made me think he did what he could and that’s mate behavior.
metadata.source_text: "Don’t blame you, mate," said Ron, looking alarmed at the very thought. "You just had to be nice to her," said Hermione, looking up anxiously. "You were, weren’t you?" "Well," said Harry, an unpleasant heat creeping up his face, "I sort of — patted her on the back a bit."
metadata.scene_title: Returning to the Castle — Reactions and Personal Matters

metadata.description: I saw Ron’s dad being bitten and badly wounded — there was blood everywhere and the attack looked serious.
metadata.source_text: Your dad! He’s . . . been attacked . . .

metadata.description: I was there in the vision, not just dreaming in the usual way; I actually experienced the attack as though I’d done it.
metadata.source_text: No! It wasn’t a dream . . . not an ordinary dream. . . . I was there, I saw it. . . . I did it . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I’m convinced now that some dreams of mine can be more than dreams — they can show real events or make me present where something awful is happening.
metadata.source_text: No! It wasn’t a dream . . . not an ordinary dream. . . . I was there, I saw it. . . . I did it . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I need Ron to understand and trust me about his dad’s danger even if he thinks I’m imagining things; I feel urgent responsibility toward him.
metadata.source_text: No! It wasn’t a dream . . . not an ordinary dream. . . . I was there, I saw it. . . . I did it . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I was told that my dad’s been attacked and bitten and that there was serious bleeding.
metadata.source_text: Your dad! He’s . . . been attacked . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I’m shaken — at first I thought Harry was only dreaming, but hearing him and seeing him like that makes me fear something really has happened to my dad.
metadata.source_text: Harry, you’re not well," he said shakily. "Neville’s gone for help . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I feel frightened and helpless for Harry and for my family; Harry’s frantic insistence makes me worry for him and also for my dad’s safety.
metadata.source_text: Harry, mate," said Ron uncertainly, "you . . . you were just dreaming . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I wasn’t present during the events in the Gryffindor dormitory, so I don’t know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Dream, Waking in Pain, and Confession of Vision

metadata.description: I saw Mr. Weasley being attacked by a giant snake — I know he was badly hurt because I could tell how much someone bleeds when fangs that long pierce their side.
metadata.source_text: Ron’s dad — Mr. Weasley — has been attacked by a giant snake.

metadata.description: I know my vision wasn't an ordinary dream; it felt real, like I watched it happen rather than dreamed it.
metadata.source_text: But it wasn’t an ordinary dream . . . it was real. . . . I saw it happen . . .

metadata.description: I discovered that I experienced the attack from the snake's point of view — I was actually the snake when I saw it.
metadata.source_text: I was the snake,

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more impatient than usual because adults seem slow to react to what I told them; I expect quicker understanding when something serious happens.
metadata.source_text: Well . . . I don’t know," said Harry, rather angrily — what did it matter?

metadata.description: I feel awkward around Ron and the others now; when they stare at me after I tell them, I think they might blame me for seeing the attack.
metadata.source_text: Fred, George, and Ginny continued to stare at him for a moment. Harry did not know whether he was imagining it or not, but he fancied there was something accusatory in their looks.

metadata.description: I've learned that Mr. Weasley was attacked and that his family got news quickly — Mum says Dad is still alive and she's going to St. Mungo's right away.
metadata.source_text: Dad is still alive. I am setting out for St. Mungo’s now. Stay where you are. I will send news as soon as I can. Mum.

metadata.description: I'm shaken and guilty: I feel responsible somehow because I was the reason their alarm was raised, and I keep thinking maybe I was the one attacking people when I had those strange urges.
metadata.source_text: They would not be here if it were not for him; they would all still be asleep in bed. And it was no good telling himself that by raising the alarm he had ensured that Mr. Weasley was found, because there was also the inescapable business of it being he who had attacked Mr. Weasley in the first place.

metadata.description: I still care about them all a lot; even though I feel awful and confused, I'm trying to help — I hurry to the stove to help with breakfast because they're my family and friends and I want to do something useful.
metadata.source_text: Harry hurried over to the stove to help.

metadata.description: I wasn't at the kitchen when this happened, so I don't have any new direct information from the scene to report.
I wasn't present during these events and therefore can't say my opinions changed based on this scene.
I wasn't there to update any relationships from the events in the kitchen.
I wasn't in the room to speak or act in this scene, so I don't have a direct statement from myself about what happened here.
I wasn't present at the kitchen argument, so I have no change of belief recorded from that moment.
I wasn't there to change how I see anyone during this scene; I was absent from these interactions.
I saw every detail of the vision and I know I was the snake that attacked Mr Weasley — I remember being the snake and feeling like I’d struck him.
metadata.source_text: Without preamble Harry told his godfather every detail of the vision he had had, including the fact that he himself had been the snake who had attacked Mr Weasley.

metadata.description: I remember a moment in Dumbledore’s office when my scar hurt and I felt like a snake; for a couple of seconds I thought I was a snake and I wanted to attack him.
metadata.source_text: Back in Dumbledore’s office, just before we took the Portkey . . . for a couple of seconds there I thought I was a snake, I felt like one — my scar really hurt when I was looking at Dumbledore — Sirius, I wanted to attack him —

metadata.description: I think I’m going mad — I feel like there’s a snake inside me, not just remembering the dream but something rising up inside me that’s dangerous.
metadata.source_text: But that’s not all," said Harry in a voice only a little above a whisper. "Sirius, I . . . I think I’m going mad. . . . Back in Dumbledore’s office, just before we took the Portkey . . . for a couple of seconds there I thought I was a snake, I felt like one —

metadata.description: I’m frustrated with Dumbledore because he didn’t tell me what the vision meant; I feel like he doesn’t tell me anything anymore and that upsets me.
metadata.source_text: "Did you tell Dumbledore this?" "Yes," said Harry impatiently, "but he didn’t tell me what it meant. Well, he doesn’t tell me anything anymore . . ."

metadata.description: I was not present during the events described in this scene and therefore did not witness the Weasley breakfast, Harry’s confession to Sirius, or the St Mungo’s visit.
I was not present for the private conversation Harry had with Sirius in the pantry and did not observe Harry recounting his vision or feelings there.
I've learned Dumbledore told someone to tell me to 'stay where you are' rather than explain what happened to me.
metadata.source_text: I have a message for you from Albus Dumbledore." "Stay where you are."

metadata.description: I'm starting to feel that grown-ups withhold things from me and that makes me furious and more alone than before.
metadata.source_text: So that’s it, is it? he said loudly. "Stay there? That’s all anyone could tell me after I got attacked by those dementors too!

metadata.description: I realise Ginny understands being possessed in a way others don't, and that makes me feel less isolated with what happened to me.
metadata.source_text: Well, you have!" she said. "And you won’t look at any of us!" ... "Then You-Know-Who hasn’t ever possessed you," said Ginny simply.

metadata.description: Dumbledore told me what happened to Harry the morning after, and I learned Umbridge is furious because Harry and the others vanished despite given permission to visit Mr. Weasley in St. Mungo's.
metadata.source_text: "Dumbledore told me what had happened first thing yesterday morning, but I had to wait for term to end officially before setting off. Umbridge is already livid that you lot disappeared right under her nose, even though Dumbledore told her Mr. Weasley was in St. Mungo’s, and he’d given you all permission to visit."

metadata.description: I believe Harry is trying to hide from everyone and that’s why we need to press him to say how he truly feels.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, don’t lie, Harry," she said impatiently. "Ron and Ginny say you’ve been hiding from everyone since you got back from St. Mungo’s."

metadata.description: I want to help Harry and I feel responsible enough to confront him gently when he shuts people out.
metadata.source_text: "We wanted to talk to you, Harry," said Ginny, "but as you’ve been hiding ever since we got back —"

metadata.description: Mum says dinner’s ready and she’ll save me something if I want to stay in bed, which I tell Harry because I still care about him even when he’s upset.
metadata.source_text: "Harry," said Ron’s voice, from far, far away, "Mum says dinner’s ready, but she’ll save you something if you want to stay in bed . . ."

metadata.description: I feel awkward and guilty about how Harry’s been avoiding everyone, and I know telling Hermione and the others was right even if I felt embarrassed.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, don’t lie, Harry," she said impatiently. "Ron and Ginny say you’ve been hiding from everyone since you got back from St. Mungo’s."

metadata.description: I still regard Harry as my mate and want to help him, even if he’s snappy and shutting us out.
metadata.source_text: "They do, do they?" said Harry, glaring at Ron and Ginny. Ron looked down at his feet...

metadata.description: I've learned you can't Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts — not even Voldemort could just make someone fly out of their dormitory.
metadata.source_text: you’ll read Hogwarts: A History, and perhaps that will remind you that you can’t Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts. Even Voldemort couldn’t just make you fly out of your dormitory, Harry.

metadata.description: I thought I might be some kind of weapon, but after hearing them and calming down I realised I'm not the weapon after all — I felt huge relief.
metadata.source_text: I’m not the weapon after all, thought Harry. His heart swelled with happiness and relief, and he felt like joining in...

metadata.description: I can hear the way everyone cares — Sirius and Lupin gave me books, the Weasleys fuss over family matters — it makes me feel part of a real, messy family.
metadata.source_text: Sirius and Lupin had given Harry a set of excellent books... Mr. and Mrs. Weasley the usual hand-knitted jumper... Fred and George Apparated... "Mum’s crying again," said Fred heavily.

metadata.description: I saw Kreacher's bedroom under the boiler — a nest of rags with stale food and some coins, and he had kept damaged silver family photos, Bellatrix's picture placed to the front.
metadata.source_text: Most of the cupboard was taken up with a very large and old-fashioned boiler, but in the foot’s space underneath the pipes Kreacher had made himself something that looked like a nest. ... In a far corner glinted small objects and coins ... and he had also managed to retrieve the silver-framed family photographs ... including ... the dark, heavy-lidded woman ... Bellatrix Lestrange. By the looks of it, hers was Kreacher’s favorite photograph; he had placed it to the fore of all the others and had mended the glass clumsily with Spellotape.

metadata.description: I used to think house-elves couldn't leave their families at all, but remembering Dobby, I now believe a house-elf can leave if they find a way, even if it means punishing themselves afterward.
metadata.source_text: No, no, house-elves can’t leave unless they’re given clothes, they’re tied to their family’s house," said Sirius. "They can leave the house if they really want to," Harry contradicted him. "Dobby did, he left the Malfoys’ to give me warnings three years ago. He had to punish himself afterward, but he still managed it.

metadata.description: Seeing Kreacher's careful keeping of Bellatrix's picture made me feel uneasy about how much the house-elf revered certain Black family members; it tightened my sense that the Black/Lestrange influence lingers here.
metadata.source_text: including — he felt a little jolt in his stomach — the dark, heavy-lidded woman whose trial he had witnessed in Dumbledore’s Pensieve: Bellatrix Lestrange. By the looks of it, hers was Kreacher’s favorite photograph; he had placed it to the fore of all the others and had mended the glass clumsily with Spellotape.

metadata.description: Blimey, I remembered the tearoom is on the fifth floor so I could get out of that mess quickly.
metadata.source_text: I wonder where the tearoom is? "Fifth floor," said Harry, remembering the sign over the Welcome Witch’s desk.

metadata.description: I’m not terribly sympathetic to Lockhart now; after what happened with his memory and us he doesn’t get much of my pity.
metadata.source_text: It had been Ron’s malfunctioning wand that had damaged Professor Lockhart’s memory so badly that he had landed here in the first place, though, as Lockhart had been attempting to permanently wipe Harry and Ron’s memories at the time, Harry’s sympathy was limited.

metadata.description: I’m glad Ginny and I can share a private snort at Lockhart’s daftness; she grinned when I muttered that he hadn’t changed much.
metadata.source_text: "Hasn’t changed much, has he?" Harry muttered to Ginny, who grinned.

metadata.description: I've read in Hogwarts: A History that one cannot Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts, so I reminded them of that fact when they worried about being taken to London.
metadata.source_text: One day," said Hermione, sounding thoroughly exasperated, "you’ll read Hogwarts: A History, and perhaps that will remind you that you can’t Apparate or Disapparate inside Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I wanted to help Kreacher be more comfortable, so I chose a patchwork quilt thinking it would brighten his bedroom; I feel sure leaving it quietly is kinder than forcing myself on him.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher," said Hermione brightly... "No, it’s a patchwork quilt, I thought it would brighten up his bedroom."

metadata.description: I know that Kreacher lives under the boiler and keeps family photographs, and I feel a bit uneasy seeing Bellatrix Lestrange among them — it shows Kreacher's loyalties and connections are complicated.
metadata.source_text: Apparently he sleeps under the boiler in that cupboard off the kitchen... including ... Bellatrix Lestrange.

metadata.description: I found Kreacher's bedroom under the boiler; it's basically a pile of rags, stale food and a few salvaged treasures including damaged family photographs, which shows how he hoards bits of the house.
metadata.source_text: Most of the cupboard was taken up with a very large and old-fashioned boiler, but in the foot’s space underneath the pipes Kreacher had made himself something that looked like a nest. A jumble of assorted rags and smelly old blankets were piled on the floor ... Here and there among the material were stale bread crusts and moldy old bits of cheese. In a far corner glinted small objects and coins ... and he had also managed to retrieve the silver-framed family photographs...

metadata.description: I thought leaving a present out might be rude, but I decided quietly that leaving Kreacher's gift in his bedding is better; he'll find it later and I needn't disturb him more now.
metadata.source_text: “I think I’ll just leave his present here,” said Hermione, laying the package neatly in the middle of the depression in the rags and blankets and closing the door quietly. “He’ll find it later, that’ll be fine . . .”

metadata.description: Seeing Kreacher's devotion to certain family portraits, especially Bellatrix's, made me more aware that house-elves can form unsettling loyalties tied to old family prejudices.
metadata.source_text: including ... Bellatrix Lestrange. By the looks of it, hers was Kreacher’s favorite photograph; he had placed it to the fore of all the others and had mended the glass clumsily with Spellotape.

metadata.source_text: "I wonder where the tearoom is?" "Fifth floor," said Harry, remembering the sign over the Welcome Witch’s desk. "What floor's this?" "I think it's the fifth," said Hermione.

metadata.description: Hearing Mr Weasley’s explanation, I think some Muggle remedies can be effective on non-magical wounds; it’s sensible, not silly, to consider scientific reasons.
metadata.source_text: "Well, you know, they do work well on non-magical wounds," said Hermione fairly. "I suppose something in that snake's venom dissolves them or something..."

metadata.description: Seeing Lockhart here makes me feel oddly breathless and surprised; I still associate him with class theatrics rather than a hospital bed.
metadata.source_text: "Blimey!" said Ron, also staring at the man. "Oh my goodness," said Hermione suddenly, sounding breathless. "Professor Lockhart!"

metadata.description: I saw Harry thrashing in his sleep about a minute before we woke him — that's how I know he didn't get out of bed during whatever happened.
metadata.source_text: You didn’t leave your bed, mate," said Ron. "I saw you thrashing around in your sleep about a minute before we could wake you up . . .

metadata.description: Hearing Mum crying because Percy sent back his jumper without a note made me angrier about Percy's behaviour; I keep thinking Percy’s being a humongous pile of rat droppings.
metadata.source_text: "Mum’s crying again," said Fred heavily. "Percy sent back his Christmas jumper." ... "Told her Percy’s nothing more than a humongous pile of rat droppings —"

metadata.description: Seeing Kreacher’s 'bedroom' made me think less kindly about how house-elves live; I call out what it is and feel uneasy about how he’s kept and treated.
metadata.source_text: So, this is Kreacher’s bedroom?" said Ron... "Urgh." Harry peered inside. ... A jumble of assorted rags and smelly old blankets...

metadata.description: I opened Kreacher's door and saw his little nest under the boiler — loads of rags, old food and a bunch of bits and bobs he'd nicked back, including smashed family photos.
metadata.source_text: “He must be sneaking around upstairs,” he said, and without further ado pulled open the door. “Urgh.” ...
