metadata.description: I guessed Kreacher might be hiding upstairs after Sirius sent him out, but seeing his bedroom made me think he's been staying put and clinging to those old family things instead of leaving.
metadata.source_text: “He must be sneaking around upstairs,” he said, and without further ado pulled open the door. ... In a far corner glinted small objects and coins ... and he had also managed to retrieve the silver-framed family photographs...

metadata.description: Finding Kreacher's hoard of the Black family's items, including that Lestrange picture, reminded me how tied house-elves are to old pure-blood families — it makes me feel wary of what loyalties they have.
metadata.source_text: In a far corner glinted small objects and coins ... and he had also managed to retrieve the silver-framed family photographs ... including ... Bellatrix Lestrange. By the looks of it, hers was Kreacher’s favorite photograph;

metadata.description: I learned that people confuse freckles for something worse when some daft Healer suggests ridiculous cures; I was furious to be called anything other than freckles.
metadata.source_text: "They're freckles!" said Ron furiously. "Now get back in your own picture and leave me alone!"

metadata.description: I’m annoyed with the Healer’s mockery and more defensive about my appearance than I expected; being called gruesome makes my ears go red and I snap back.
metadata.source_text: "Watch who you're calling gruesome!" said Ron, his ears turning red.

metadata.description: I still feel awkward about Lockhart because my wand malfunctioned and caused his mess; I’m guilty and uneasy when I see him wandering about.
metadata.source_text: It had been Ron's malfunctioning wand that had damaged Professor Lockhart's memory so badly that he had landed here in the first place...

metadata.description: I saw that Gilderoy Lockhart is being kept in a closed ward because he wanders off and seems to have memory problems; he signs photos like mad and keeps many pictures of himself up by his bed.
metadata.source_text: He was in a closed ward, you know, he must have slipped out while I was bringing in the Christmas presents, the door’s usually kept locked . . . not that he’s dangerous! But, bit of a danger to himself, bless him. . . . Doesn’t know who he is, you see, wanders off and can’t remember how to get back.

metadata.description: I realised that some patients in the long-term ward have permanent spell damage and personal effects around their beds, and that people like Mr. Bode and others show varying levels of recovery or lasting harm.
metadata.source_text: This is our long-term resident ward," she informed Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Ginny in a low voice. "For permanent spell damage, you know. Of course, with intensive remedial potions and charms and a bit of luck, we can produce some improvement. . . . Gilderoy does seem to be getting back some sense of himself, and we’ve seen a real improvement in Mr. Bode, he seems to be regaining the power of speech very well...

metadata.description: Seeing Neville with his grandmother and his parents in that state made me feel almost unbearably sorry for him; I can't look at Neville the same way after seeing how ashamed and miserable he was in front of them.
metadata.source_text: Neville jumped and cowered as though a bullet had narrowly missed him.... Neville looked as though he would rather be anywhere in the world but here.

metadata.description: I thought Lockhart was a ridiculous show-off before, but seeing him like this—autographing himself, lost and fragile—made me realise his fame was a sad, hollow thing rather than something admirable.
metadata.source_text: He had autographed many of them to himself in disjointed, childish writing. The moment he had been deposited in his chair by the Healer, Gilderoy pulled a fresh stack of photographs toward him, seized a quill, and started signing them all feverishly.

metadata.description: I've observed that the Janus Thickey ward cares for people with permanent spell damage and that remedial potions and charms sometimes produce improvement, though recovery is uncertain.
metadata.source_text: This is our long-term resident ward," she informed Harry, Ron, Hermione, and Ginny in a low voice. "For permanent spell damage, you know. Of course, with intensive remedial potions and charms and a bit of luck, we can produce some improvement...

metadata.description: Seeing Neville's parents in St Mungo's made me understand more about Neville; I feel more sympathetic toward him now that I know his parents were tortured into insanity and he struggles with that.
metadata.source_text: My son and his wife," she said, turning haughtily... "were tortured into insanity by You-Know-Who’s followers.

metadata.description: I used to treat Lockhart as vain and ridiculous, and seeing the reality of his condition—signing photos obsessively—makes me think his fame hides real harm and delusion.
metadata.source_text: He had autographed many of them to himself in disjointed, childish writing. The moment he had been deposited in his chair by the Healer, Gilderoy pulled a fresh stack of photographs toward him, seized a quill, and started signing them all feverishly.

metadata.description: Blimey, I saw that Lockhart's memory's gone a bit — he's in a closed ward 'cause he wanders off and can't remember who he is, yet he still wants to sign loads of photos.
metadata.source_text: He was in a closed ward, you know, he must have slipped out while I was bringing in the Christmas presents, the door’s usually kept locked . . . not that he’s dangerous! But, bit of a danger to himself, bless him. . . . Doesn’t know who he is, you see, wanders off and can’t remember how to get back.

metadata.description: Seeing Neville flinch at us and go red made me feel awkward and sorry — I don't think I'd realised how bad things were for him until I saw his Nan and his parents in that state.
metadata.source_text: Neville jumped and cowered as though a bullet had narrowly missed him.... Neville looked as though he would rather be anywhere in the world but here.

metadata.description: I used to find Lockhart laughable for his boasting, but watching him sign pictures like a kid made me think his fame is pathetic rather than impressive.
metadata.source_text: He had autographed many of them to himself in disjointed, childish writing. The moment he had been deposited in his chair by the Healer, Gilderoy pulled a fresh stack of photographs toward him, seized a quill, and started signing them all feverishly.

metadata.description: I've been told I must study Occlumency this term — it's the magical defence of the mind against external penetration and I'll have private lessons once a week.
metadata.source_text: The headmaster has sent me to tell you, Potter, that it is his wish for you to study Occlumency this term.

metadata.description: I feel horrified and uneasy about the idea of having extra lessons with Snape — the idea that he will teach me makes my stomach turn.
metadata.source_text: I am in rather a hurry, Black . . . unlike you, I do not have unlimited leisure time . . . "I will expect you at six o'clock on Monday evening, Potter. My office.

metadata.description: I notice Sirius is ready to defend me fiercely; he told Snape he would have him to answer to if Snape used the lessons to give me a hard time.
metadata.source_text: If I hear you’re using these Occlumency lessons to give Harry a hard time, you’ll have me to answer to.

metadata.description: I've observed Harry being told he must study Occlumency with Snape and that the lessons are to be kept secret from others, including Dolores Umbridge.
metadata.source_text: You will receive private lessons once a week, but you will not tell anybody what you are doing, least of all Dolores Umbridge. You understand?

metadata.description: I worry about Harry—I think he should learn Occlumency to protect himself, even if it means he has to have lessons with Snape.
metadata.source_text: Harry, I know you don’t like Snape, but he is a superb Occlumens and we all — Sirius included — want you to learn to protect yourself, so work hard, all right?

metadata.description: I see that despite her usual composure, Ginny and I are both concerned and staring at Harry when Mrs Weasley interrupts his game to summon him for Snape's visit.
metadata.source_text: "Harry dear," said Mrs Weasley, poking her head into his and Ron’s bedroom ... where the pair of them were playing wizard chess watched by Hermione, Ginny, and Crookshanks,

metadata.description: I heard Mrs Weasley tell Harry that Professor Snape wants a word in the kitchen and saw Harry go down to meet him with Sirius already there.
metadata.source_text: "Professor Snape, dear. In the kitchen. He’d like a word."

metadata.description: I felt unnerved and worried when Mrs Weasley asked Harry to come down; I asked him nervously if he'd done anything to make Snape pursue him.
metadata.source_text: "What’s he want with you?" said Ron, looking unnerved as Mrs Weasley withdrew from the room. "You haven’t done anything, have you?"

metadata.description: I can tell Sirius is protective of Harry and ready to argue with Snape; it makes me more trusting of Sirius’s loyalty to Harry.
metadata.source_text: If I hear you’re using these Occlumency lessons to give Harry a hard time, you’ll have me to answer to.

metadata.description: I found out Professor Snape told me Dumbledore wants me to learn Occlumency so I can shut my mind against the Dark Lord.
metadata.source_text: The headmaster has asked me to teach you Occlumency. I can only hope that you prove more adept at it than Potions.

metadata.description: I learned that Legilimency is not simple 'mind-reading' but an ability to extract feelings and memories from someone else's mind.
metadata.source_text: It is the ability to extract feelings and memories from another person’s mind —

metadata.description: I’m suddenly worried and confused: I used to think the link with the Dark Lord might be useful, but now I see Dumbledore wants it stopped and that scares me.
metadata.source_text: But why does Professor Dumbledore want to stop it? ... I don’t like it much, but it’s been useful, hasn’t it?

metadata.description: I feel oddly pleased and relieved that Cho agreed to go into Hogsmeade with me on Valentine’s Day — it’s made the day feel less bleak.
metadata.source_text: Er — d’you want to come into Hogsmeade with me on Valentine’s Day?" "Oooh, yes!"

metadata.description: I noticed Ron wants to defend me — he glares after Smith and even tries to jinx him; Ron’s loyalty is obvious even when I’m down.
metadata.source_text: As Smith strode away in an annoyingly buoyant fashion, Ron glared after him. "Shall I jinx him? I can still get him from here," he said, raising his wand

metadata.description: I learned that Legilimency is a skill that lets people delve into others' minds and that Occlumency is what one must learn to shut those intrusions down.
metadata.source_text: It is true, however, that those who have mastered Legilimency are able, under certain conditions, to delve into the minds of their victims and to interpret their findings correctly. ... Only those skilled at Occlumency are able to shut down those feelings and memories that contradict the lie, and so utter falsehoods in his presence without detection.

metadata.description: I found out that the failed curse that almost killed me seems to have forged some kind of connection between me and the Dark Lord, letting me share his thoughts at times.
metadata.source_text: The curse that failed to kill you seems to have forged some kind of connection between you and the Dark Lord.

metadata.description: I discovered that when I'm relaxed or asleep I sometimes share Voldemort's thoughts and emotions, which is why I dreamed inside the snake when he was possessing it.
metadata.source_text: The evidence suggests that at times, when your mind is most relaxed and vulnerable — when you are asleep, for instance — you are sharing the Dark Lord’s thoughts and emotions. ... You seem to have visited the snake’s mind because that was where the Dark Lord was at that particular moment. He was possessing the snake at the time and so you dreamed you were inside it too . . .

metadata.description: I used to think those visions could be useful, like when I saw the snake attack Bill Weasley, but now I'm told that the most recent powerful vision alerted Voldemort to me and that's worrying.
metadata.source_text: I don’t like it much, but it’s been useful, hasn’t it? I mean . . . I saw that snake attack Mr. Weasley and if I hadn’t, Professor Dumbledore wouldn’t have been able to save him, would he? Sir? ... the vision you had shortly before Christmas represented such a powerful incursion upon the Dark Lord’s thoughts —

metadata.description: I'm beginning to see Dumbledore as someone who insists on protecting me by ordering Occlumency lessons, even if I don't fully understand why he wants the link stopped.
metadata.source_text: The headmaster thinks it inadvisable for this to continue. He wishes me to teach you how to close your mind to the Dark Lord.

metadata.description: I've learned that Voldemort knows I can get into his thoughts and that he might try to get into mine as well, which could let him make me do things against my will.
metadata.source_text: The important point is that the Dark Lord is now aware that you are gaining access to his thoughts and feelings. He has also deduced that the process is likely to work in reverse; that is to say, he has realized that he might be able to access your thoughts and feelings in return —

metadata.description: I had thought I was only sneaking into his mind; now I realize that this is a two-way danger and that I need to defend my own mind properly.
metadata.source_text: The important point is that the Dark Lord is now aware that you are gaining access to his thoughts and feelings. He has also deduced that the process is likely to work in reverse; that is to say, he has realized that he might be able to access your thoughts and feelings in return —

metadata.description: I've seen how a skilled wizard can extract memories from his own head with a wand and drop them into a Pensieve as a silvery strand of memory substance.
metadata.source_text: Snape pulled out his wand from an inside pocket of his robes... he raised the wand to his temple and placed its tip into the greasy roots of his hair... some silvery substance came away, stretching from temple to wand like a thick gossamer strand... fell gracefully into the Pensieve, where it swirled silvery white

metadata.description: I feel more vulnerable now — when Snape strikes into my mind with Legilimens I couldn't brace myself in time and my worst memories and fears were flooded out.
metadata.source_text: Snape had struck before Harry was ready... the office swam in front of his eyes and vanished, image after image was racing through his mind like a flickering film

metadata.description: Snape is cold and demanding, and though I want help I find his manner intimidating; he forces me into a test of mind-defence without much sympathy.
metadata.source_text: “I told you,” said Snape, rigid in his chair, his eyes slits, “to call me ‘sir.’” ... “He might,” said Snape, sounding cold and unconcerned. “Which brings us back to Occlumency.”

metadata.description: I told Ron and Harry we’d be in the library and took charge of getting them moving toward lessons, showing I expect us to focus on study as usual.
metadata.source_text: "We’ll be in the library, Harry," said Hermione firmly, and she seized Ron above the elbow and dragged him off toward the marble staircase.

metadata.description: I remain convinced that routines and study are important; seeing Harry distracted by other things only strengthens my belief we must keep to our academic responsibilities.
metadata.source_text: "We’ll be in the library, Harry," said Hermione firmly

metadata.description: I pulled Ron away from sulking and tried to keep our group focused, which shows I still see us as a unit who need to look out for each other.
metadata.source_text: "We’ll be in the library, Harry," said Hermione firmly, and she seized Ron above the elbow and dragged him off

metadata.description: I wasn't present during Severus Snape's lesson about Legilimency and Occlumency, so I did not witness the conversation or the Pensieve demonstration.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in Snape's office where Snape explained Voldemort's awareness and tested Harry with Legilimency, so I don't know the exact details.
I attempted to jinx Zacharias Smith when he mocked Harry, showing I can be quick to anger and protective of my mates.
metadata.source_text: "Shall I jinx him? I can still get him from here," he said, raising his wand and taking aim between Smith’s shoulder blades.

metadata.description: I felt annoyed and defensive when Smith mocked Harry for taking Remedial Potions; it reinforced how much I dislike people sneering at Harry.
metadata.source_text: "You take Remedial Potions?" asked Zacharias Smith superciliously ... As Smith strode away ... Ron glared after him.

metadata.description: I stayed close to Harry and let Hermione pull me away to the library, which underlines that I’m still part of their circle even when tensions are high.
metadata.source_text: "We’ll be in the library, Harry," said Hermione firmly, and she seized Ron above the elbow and dragged him off

metadata.description: I wasn't present in Snape's office when he explained Legilimency and Occlumency or when Harry described seeing the snake attack Bill Weasley.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the encounter between Snape and Harry in the office involving the Pensieve and the Legilimens attack, so I can't report what happened firsthand.
I've realised the thing You-Know-Who is after has to be in the Department of Mysteries at the Ministry of Magic; I saw that same plain black door when Mr Weasley took me down to the courtrooms.
metadata.source_text: I saw that door when your dad took me down to the courtrooms for my hearing and it’s definitely the same one he was guarding when the snake bit him.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that I must learn to protect my mind — being unable to empty myself of feeling makes me an easy target for Voldemort, and I can't stand that idea.
metadata.source_text: Let go of all emotion . . . "You’re not doing it, Potter. . . . You will need more discipline than this. . . . Focus, now . . ."

metadata.description: I hate Snape even more after those lessons; his way of teaching and his accusations feel cruel, and I don't trust him to be fair with me.
metadata.source_text: No," said Harry bitterly, getting up from the floor. "I thought not," said Snape contemptuously. "You let me get in too far. You lost control."

metadata.description: I've worked out that if Sturgis Podmore tried to get through a Ministry door and Harry saw the same plain black door, then whatever Harry saw is probably in the Department of Mysteries.
metadata.source_text: Sturgis Podmore was trying to get through a door at the Ministry of Magic. . . . It must have been that one, it’s too much of a coincidence!

metadata.description: I'm more certain now that extra lessons with Snape are serious business and that repeated mental attacks would leave anyone shaken; I expect Harry will feel the after-effects of Occlumency.
metadata.source_text: I expect anyone would feel shaky if they’d had their mind attacked over and over again,

metadata.description: I feel protective and concerned about Harry; hearing what he's been through makes me more worried for his wellbeing and more determined to help him when I can.
metadata.source_text: Are you all right, Harry? ... "I expect anyone would feel shaky if they’d had their mind attacked over and over again," said Hermione sympathetically.

metadata.description: I know the people who work in the Department of Mysteries are called Unspeakables because no one really seems to know what they do, so it's a weird place for a weapon, but Harry thinks that's where it is.
metadata.source_text: I know they call the people who work in there ‘Unspeakables,’" said Ron, frowning. "Because no one really seems to know what they do in there. . . .

metadata.description: I'm uneasy about the idea of extra lessons with Snape — I said I'd rather have nightmares than more of those lessons, so my gut tells me it's a bad idea for Harry.
metadata.source_text: "Extra lessons with Snape?" said Ron, sounding aghast. "I'd rather have the nightmares!"

metadata.description: I'm puzzled that Sturgis Podmore, who should be on our side, was trying to break into the Ministry; it makes me more suspicious about who is doing what and why.
metadata.source_text: "How come Sturgis was trying to break in when he’s on our side?" said Ron.

metadata.description: I saw Bellatrix Lestrange's photograph in the Prophet and I recognized her face even though Azkaban has made her look worse.
metadata.source_text: Bellatrix Lestrange, convicted of the torture and permanent incapacitation of Frank and Alice Longbottom.

metadata.description: I learned from the front page that ten high-security prisoners escaped from Azkaban and the Ministry is saying Sirius Black may have helped them.
metadata.source_text: The Ministry of Magic announced late last night that there has been a mass breakout from Azkaban.

metadata.description: I read that Broderick Bode, a Ministry worker we saw at the Department of Mysteries, was found dead strangled by a potted plant at St. Mungo's.
metadata.source_text: TRAGIC DEMISE OF MINISTRY OF MAGIC WORKER... Broderick Bode, 49, was discovered dead in his bed, strangled by a potted-plant.

metadata.description: I'm furious that the Ministry is blaming Sirius for the Azkaban breakout; I don't believe Fudge's version and I don't think that's the whole truth.
metadata.source_text: “I don't believe this,” snarled Harry, “Fudge is blaming the breakout on Sirius?”

metadata.description: I feel more certain that Dumbledore and I are not being listened to by the Ministry, and that people who trust Dumbledore are now quietly doubting the official story.
metadata.source_text: They sounded curious rather than hostile now, and once or twice he was sure he overheard snatches of conversation that suggested that the speakers were not satisfied with the Prophet’s version

metadata.description: I've read the Prophet's report that ten high-security prisoners escaped from Azkaban and the Ministry thinks Black is the rallying point for the old Death Eaters.
metadata.source_text: MASS BREAKOUT FROM AZKABAN MINISTRY FEARS BLACK IS RALLYING POINT FOR OLD DEATH EATERS

metadata.description: I learned that Broderick Bode was strangled by a potted Devil's Snare at St. Mungo's and that a healer has been suspended pending inquiry.
metadata.source_text: TRAGIC DEMISE OF MINISTRY OF MAGIC WORKER... Broderick Bode, 49, was discovered dead in his bed, strangled by a potted-plant.

metadata.description: I'm convinced this was murder and a clever disguise; I feel we can't dismiss the Devil's Snare death as an accident any more.
metadata.source_text: I don't think anyone could put Devil's Snare in a pot and not realize it tries to kill whoever touches it? This — this was murder. . . . A clever murder, as well.

metadata.description: I distrust the Ministry's narrative and feel Dumbledore's warnings were more credible than Fudge's statements; the Ministry has been refusing to admit certain facts.
metadata.source_text: He can hardly say, 'Sorry everyone, Dumbledore warned me this might happen, the Azkaban guards have joined Lord Voldemort'

metadata.description: I read the newspaper and heard that ten prisoners escaped from Azkaban and that the Ministry is blaming Sirius Black for leading them.
metadata.source_text: The Ministry of Magic announced late last night that there has been a mass breakout from Azkaban.

metadata.description: I recognized the name Broderick Bode when Harry mentioned him because Dad has talked about Bode being an Unspeakable at the Department of Mysteries.
metadata.source_text: “I met Bode,” he said slowly... “I’ve heard Dad talk about him at home! He was an Unspeakable — he worked in the Department of Mysteries!”

metadata.description: I'm shocked and a bit shaken by Bode's death, but I also want to say it's not our fault about the Devil's Snare — whoever sent it is to blame.
metadata.source_text: Who expects Devil's Snare to turn up in a hospital disguised as a potted plant?... It's not our fault, whoever sent it to the bloke is to blame!

metadata.description: I'm impressed and annoyed by Hermione's sudden decisions; she bolts off to act without telling us and I don't like being left behind.
metadata.source_text: “Where are you going?” said Ron, startled. “To send a letter,” said Hermione... “I hate it when she does that,” grumbled Ron

metadata.description: I can feel Umbridge turning everything at Hogwarts into her business; she sits in lessons with a clipboard and interrupts teachers, even making Trelawney perform tricks and predict students’ answers.
metadata.source_text: Every single Divination and Care of Magical Creatures lesson was now conducted in the presence of Umbridge and her clipboard. She lurked by the fire in the heavily perfumed tower room, interrupting Professor Trelawney’s increasingly hysterical talks with difficult questions about Ornithomancy and Heptomology, insisting that she predict students’ answers before they gave them and demanding that she demonstrate her skill at the crystal ball, the tea leaves, and the rune stones in turn.

metadata.description: I’ve noticed Hagrid is off his game — distracted in class, answering wrongly, and forbidding us to visit after dark because he’s scared Umbridge will get him fired.
metadata.source_text: He was oddly distracted and jumpy in lessons, losing the thread of what he was saying while talking to the class, answering questions wrongly and glancing anxiously at Umbridge all the time. He was also more distant with Harry, Ron, and Hermione than he had ever been before, expressly forbidding them to visit him after dark. 'If she catches yeh, it’ll be all of our necks on the line,' he told them flatly

metadata.description: I’m increasingly convinced the Ministry’s mess means real danger — ten Death Eaters are loose and there are no dementors searching Hogsmeade, which makes me think the Ministry’s grip is slipping.
metadata.source_text: The poster ('By Order of the Ministry of Magic') offered a thousand-Galleon reward... 'Remember when that Sirius Black escaped, and there were dementors all over Hogsmeade looking for him? And now ten Death Eaters are on the loose and there aren’t dementors anywhere . . .'

metadata.description: Snape’s Occlumency lessons seem to be making me worse — my scar prickles more, I feel tuned into Voldemort’s moods, and I keep dreaming of the Department of Mysteries door.
metadata.source_text: Nowadays, however, his scar hardly ever stopped prickling... he often felt lurches of annoyance or cheerfulness... always accompanied by a particularly painful twinge from his scar... he was now dreaming about walking down the corridor toward the entrance to the Department of Mysteries almost every night

metadata.description: I’ve pulled away from Hagrid a bit because he’s scared for his job and told us not to visit; I understand why, but it still hurts because I miss him and his place.
metadata.source_text: He was also more distant with Harry, Ron, and Hermione than he had ever been before, expressly forbidding them to visit him after dark... 'If she catches yeh, it’ll be all of our necks on the line,' he told them flatly

metadata.description: Dumbledore asked Snape to teach Harry Occlumency because those dreams about the Department of Mysteries are dangerous; Harry mustn't be having them, so he needs to work harder in lessons.
metadata.source_text: 'Dumbledore doesn’t want you to have dreams about that corridor at all, or he wouldn’t have asked Snape to teach you Occlumency. You’re just going to have to work a bit harder in your lessons.'

metadata.description: I really believe we have to trust Dumbledore’s judgment about Snape despite suspicion; if we can't trust Dumbledore, we can't trust anyone.
metadata.source_text: 'Dumbledore trusts him,' Hermione repeated. 'And if we can’t trust Dumbledore, we can’t trust anyone.'

metadata.description: I pushed Harry to keep working on Occlumency because I'm concerned for him; I’m blunt about it because he's in danger and Dumbledore chose Snape for a reason.
metadata.source_text: 'Dumbledore doesn’t want you to have dreams about that corridor at all... You’re just going to have to work a bit harder in your lessons.'

metadata.description: I know Harry's scar is hurting him more since Snape started the lessons and he's been dreaming about the Department of Mysteries; it's making him miserable and jumpy.
metadata.source_text: Before he had started studying Occlumency, his scar had prickled occasionally... Nowadays, however, his scar hardly ever stopped prickling... he was now dreaming about walking down the corridor toward the entrance to the Department of Mysteries almost every night

metadata.description: I'm starting to suspect Snape might not be purely helping Harry — I said maybe Snape is actually trying to open Harry's mind wider for You-Know-Who.
metadata.source_text: 'Maybe Snape isn’t really trying to help Harry ... Maybe he’s actually trying to open Harry’s mind a bit wider ... make it easier for You-Know —' 'Shut up, Ron,' said Hermione angrily.

metadata.description: I'm grumpy about Quidditch practice and Angelina making me train when the team's awful, and I felt distant from Harry at breakfast because I was miserable about it.
metadata.source_text: 'I can’t come into Hogsmeade at all, Angelina wants a full day’s training... I dunno why Angelina won’t just let me resign ...' He heaved a great sigh.

metadata.description: I learned Cho asked me point-blank whether Cedric had mentioned her before he died, and that talk about Cedric makes her cry, which makes things horribly awkward between us.
metadata.source_text: Did Cedric — did he m-m-mention me at all before he died?

metadata.description: I felt that Cho thought I preferred talking to Hermione over her, and that idea suddenly made me realise our little outing could look like I was meeting other girls straight after asking her out.
metadata.source_text: You’re meeting Hermione Granger? Today?

metadata.description: Cho exploded and stormed off; I now see she's easily hurt and quick to assume the worst about my intentions, which makes me feel distant and confused about us.
metadata.source_text: I’ll see you around, Harry

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these tea shop events, so I don't know what happened there or how people reacted in the room.
I wasn't present at the tea shop when Harry and Cho argued; I can't describe the scene or the conversation from direct experience.
I learned that my interview with Rita's paper, The Quibbler, is out and printed with my picture and the headline about He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named — people have actually written to me about it.
metadata.source_text: HARRY POTTER SPEAKS OUT AT LAST: THE TRUTH ABOUT HE-WHO-MUST-NOT-BE-NAMED AND THE NIGHT I SAW HIM RETURN

metadata.description: I reckon I have to tell people what Voldemort is capable of even if loads of them think I'm mad; the breakout of Death Eaters made me desperate to do something, whether it helps or not.
metadata.source_text: But the breakout of Bellatrix Lestrange and her fellow Death Eaters had given Harry a burning desire to do something, whether it worked or not. . . .

metadata.description: I noticed Ron sulking and feeling crushed about Quidditch; I like that Angelina believes in him, but I think it might be kinder if he could leave the team until he feels better.
metadata.source_text: Harry liked Angelina for the faith she was showing in Ron, but at the same time thought it would really be kinder to let him leave the team.

metadata.description: I've seen that people have written to Harry after his Quibbler interview; some letters defend him and say the Daily Prophet was unfair.
metadata.source_text: 'Having read your side of the story I am forced to the conclusion that the Daily Prophet has treated you very unfairly. . . . Little though I want to think that He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named has returned, I am forced to accept that you are telling the truth . . .' Oh this is wonderful!

metadata.description: I realise Harry was tactless on his date with Cho and that she tried to make him jealous; I feel sorry but I still think explaining feelings would have helped more.
metadata.source_text: Look — you upset Cho when you said you were going to meet me, so she tried to make you jealous. It was her way of trying to find out how much you liked her.

metadata.description: I think Harry's worse than Ron for not thinking things through at times, but I still care and try to explain things patiently so he understands people's feelings.
metadata.source_text: Harry, you’re worse than Ron. . . . Well, no, you’re not,

metadata.description: I've seen loads of letters for Harry after his Quibbler interview, some calling him barking and some saying he's a hero; the mail made me say some were mad and some converted.
metadata.source_text: This one’s from a bloke who thinks you’re off your rocker," said Ron... "Another one who thinks you’re barking," said Ron, throwing a crumpled letter over his shoulder, "but this one says you’ve got her converted, and she now thinks you’re a real hero

metadata.description: I'm feeling pretty down about my Quidditch; getting mocked and having 'Weasley Is Our King' shouted by Slytherins has left me crumpled and embarrassed.
metadata.source_text: Ron had left the pitch to another booming chorus of “Weasley Is Our King” sung with great gusto by the Slytherins, who were now favorites to win the Quidditch Cup.

metadata.description: Watching Harry go public makes me realise he wants people to know the truth even if it causes trouble; I'm not sure what to think but I'm embarrassed and protective in my own way.
metadata.source_text: People have written to me because I gave an interview," said Harry. "About what happened to me last June.

metadata.description: I saw Rookwood tell me that Bode couldn't have removed whatever was taken — Bode would have known he couldn't, and he fought Malfoy's Imperius because of it.
metadata.source_text: "Bode could never have taken it, Master. . . . Bode would have known he could not. . . . Undoubtedly that is why he fought so hard against Malfoy’s Imperius Curse . . ."

metadata.description: I realized I actually became You-Know-Who in that vision — I was him, looking at Rookwood and interrogating him about the mistake and the weapon.
metadata.source_text: "I was You-Know-Who," said Harry, and he stretched out his hands in the darkness and held them up to his face to check that they were no longer deathly white and long-fingered.

metadata.description: I'm convinced now that the escaped Death Eaters are actively working to recover whatever was removed and that Rookwood and Avery are involved again — this isn't just rumor, it's dangerous and immediate.
metadata.source_text: "You have done well to tell me this," said Harry. "Very well . . . I have wasted months on fruitless schemes, it seems. . . . But no matter . . . We begin again, from now. You have Lord Voldemort’s gratitude, Rookwood . . ."

metadata.description: I understand that Rookwood and the Death Eaters like Avery are important, active pawns for Voldemort again — I now see them as direct threats rather than distant names.
metadata.source_text: "Send Avery to me." Rookwood scurried backward, bowing, and disappeared through a door.

metadata.description: I've realized that Umbridge's ban actually guaranteed more people would read Harry's interview — banning it made everyone eager to read it, and students hid copies with clever enchantments.
metadata.source_text: "Oh Harry, don’t you see?" Hermione breathed. "If she could have done one thing to make absolutely sure that every single person in this school will read your interview, it was banning it!"

metadata.description: I now believe more strongly that the school is beginning to accept Harry's version of events — people are quoting the interview and Hermione says she thinks they've finally got them convinced.
metadata.source_text: "and Harry, I think they believe you, I really do, I think you’ve finally got them convinced!"

metadata.description: I've noticed students and some teachers are quietly on Harry's side — Professors Sprout, Flitwick, and Trelawney showed supportive acts that make me trust there are allies within the staff.
metadata.source_text: "Professor Sprout awarded Gryffindor twenty points when Harry passed her a watering can; a beaming Professor Flitwick pressed a box of squeaking sugar mice on him at the end of Charms..."

metadata.description: I heard Harry say he was You-Know-Who in the vision, and that Rookwood told him Bode couldn't have removed the object — meaning Bode was bewitched and Malfoy's father might be involved.
metadata.source_text: "I was You-Know-Who," said Harry... "Bode could never have taken it, Master. . . . Bode would have known he could not. . . . Undoubtedly that is why he fought so hard against Malfoy’s Imperius Curse . . ."

metadata.description: I'm frightened and shaken by what Harry saw; I believed he was exaggerating before, but seeing him panic and hurt from his scar makes me think these visions are real and dangerous.
metadata.source_text: "Has someone been attacked again?" asked Ron, pulling Harry roughly to his feet... "D'you mean . . . did you just see You-Know-Who?"

metadata.description: I feel more protective of Harry now — when he woke screaming and writhing, I rushed to help and kept asking him to tell others because I don't want him carrying this alone.
metadata.source_text: "Will you stop acting like a maniac, and I can get you out of here!" Ron wrenched the hangings apart, and Harry stared up at him...

metadata.description: I realised Sturgis Podmore was seen in the Department of Mysteries corridor the day of my hearing and that he might have been involved with Moody’s Invisibility Cloak.
metadata.source_text: He was in the Department of Mysteries corridor that day! Your dad said he was probably trying to sneak down and find out what happened in my hearing, but what if —

metadata.description: I think now that people I assumed were merely officials could be working for Malfoy or Voldemort, and I'm angrier at being used as a vessel for these visions than I was before.
metadata.source_text: Of course, it would have been easy for Lucius Malfoy to put the curse on him. Never out of the Ministry, is he?”

metadata.description: I'm beginning to rely on Snape for Occlumency training even though I hate him; I know he expects results and that he takes this job seriously in his own way.
metadata.source_text: You do know why we are here, don’t you, Potter?” said Snape in a low, dangerous voice. “You do know why I am giving up my evenings to this tedious job?”

metadata.description: I saw things that weren't mine when Snape forced his Legilimency on me — horrible memories, like a hook-nosed man shouting at a cowering woman and a crying little boy watching them.
metadata.source_text: a hook-nosed man was shouting at a cowering woman, while a small dark-haired boy cried in a corner. . . .

metadata.description: I experienced a vision of the Department of Mysteries: the long corridor, the plain black door with a chink of blue light, and a black circular room lit by blue-flamed candles with many doors.
metadata.source_text: He was hurtling along the corridor toward the Department of Mysteries, past the blank stone walls, past the torches — the plain black door was growing ever larger; he was moving so fast he was going to collide with it, he was feet from it and he could see that chink of faint blue light again

metadata.description: I'm starting to believe Snape can dig into my mind — and that breaking into someone else's memories is possible even when I don't mean to. I'm shaken and wary of what that means.
metadata.source_text: He was sure he had just broken into Snape's memories, that he had just seen scenes from Snape's childhood, and it was unnerving to think that the crying little boy who had watched his parents shouting was actually standing in front of him with such loathing in his eyes. . . .

metadata.description: I feel a lot of loathing toward Snape right now; seeing those memories made his younger self look pathetic and cruel, and our lessons are making me angrier and more distrustful of him.
metadata.source_text: that the crying little boy who had watched his parents shouting was actually standing in front of him with such loathing in his eyes. . . .

metadata.description: I've put together that Sturgis Podmore was arrested for trying to get through a door and that Lucius Malfoy could have ensnared him, possibly using him to get the weapon for Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: Sturgis Podmore,” said Hermione, breathlessly. “Arrested for trying to get through a door. Lucius Malfoy got him too.

metadata.description: I'm now convinced that Harry shouldn't be letting these visions happen and that he must work much harder at Occlumency; seeing is dangerous and we should try to forget what he saw.
metadata.source_text: But you shouldn’t have seen this at all, Harry.... Well, I think we should just try and forget what you saw. And you ought to put in a bit more effort on your Occlumency from now on.

metadata.description: I feel protective and a bit urgent with Harry about his mental training; I'm stern because I care and because I fear what the Dark Lord could learn through him.
metadata.source_text: You’re supposed to be learning how to close your mind to this sort of thing,” said Hermione, suddenly stern.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in Snape's lesson, so I don't know the details of what happened in that training session.
I realised Sturgis could have been guarding that door invisible with Moody’s cloak and that Malfoy or someone might have picked him off to get at the weapon.
metadata.source_text: Sturgis had Moody’s Invisibility Cloak, right? So what if he was standing guard by the door, invisible, and Malfoy heard him move, or guessed he was there, or just did the Imperius Curse...

metadata.description: I'm surprised and unsettled that people in the Ministry like Lucius Malfoy could be behind this; I didn't expect such reach and I'd thought Ministry types were more secure.
metadata.source_text: Of course, it would have been easy for Lucius Malfoy to put the curse on him. Never out of the Ministry, is he?”

metadata.description: I'm quieter when Hermione is figuring things out; I get bewildered sometimes but I trust her to work things out and I listen when she speaks quickly and breathlessly.
metadata.source_text: “Sturgis,” gasped Hermione, looking thunderstruck. “Sorry?” said Ron, looking bewildered.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the Occlumency lesson with Snape and Harry, so I can't say what took place or what was seen inside Snape's memories.
I noticed Firenze has a hoof-shaped bruise on his chest, which suggests he was physically attacked by other centaurs.
metadata.source_text: Harry noticed that there was the shadow of a hoof-shaped bruise on Firenze’s chest.

metadata.description: I realized centaurs can be intimidating but also willing to speak with students; being on speaking terms with Firenze made other pupils look at me with awe.
metadata.source_text: When the door was closed and the last student had sat down upon a tree stump beside the wastepaper basket, Firenze gestured around the room.

metadata.description: I see Firenze as an ally of Dumbledore and someone who might protect students; he greeted me formally and said it was foretold we'd meet again.
metadata.source_text: “Harry Potter,” he said, holding out a hand when Harry entered. “Er — hi,” said Harry, shaking hands with the centaur, who surveyed him unblinkingly through those astonishingly blue eyes but did not smile. “And you,” said the centaur, inclining his white-blond head. “It was foretold that we would meet again.”

metadata.description: I've learned that Firenze has been appointed to teach Divination at Hogwarts and that Dumbledore arranged the classroom to imitate his natural habitat.
metadata.source_text: “Professor Dumbledore has kindly arranged this classroom for us,” said Firenze, when everyone had settled down, “in imitation of my natural habitat.”

metadata.description: I now firmly believe Umbridge will get worse and will seek revenge on Dumbledore for appointing Firenze without consulting her; I said she looked hateful when she saw him.
metadata.source_text: “You mark my words, she’s going to want revenge on Dumbledore for appointing a new teacher without consulting her,” said Hermione, closing the newspaper. “Especially another part-human. You saw the look on her face when she saw Firenze . . .”

metadata.description: I feel that centaurs are proud beings not to be treated as playthings; when Dean made a crude joke, Firenze corrected him — that showed me their dignity.
metadata.source_text: “Centaurs are not the servants or playthings of humans,” said Firenze quietly.

metadata.description: Blimey, I learned the classroom was changed to look like a forest and then the ceiling showed stars so we could study the heavens properly.
metadata.source_text: He swished his long palomino tail, raised his hand toward the leafy canopy overhead then lowered it slowly, and as he did so, the light in the room dimmed, so that they now seemed to be sitting in a forest clearing by twilight, and stars emerged upon the ceiling.

metadata.description: I thought Umbridge couldn't get worse, but after Hermione's warning I started to worry she might become even nastier and go after Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: “Impossible,” said Ron, who was tucking into a large plate of eggs and bacon. “She can’t get any worse than she’s been already.”

metadata.description: I feel a bit in awe of Firenze and the centaurs — when they set up the lesson everyone reacted like he was someone important and strange.
metadata.source_text: As he turned to join the rest of the class upon the floor, he saw that they were all looking at him with awe, apparently deeply impressed that he was on speaking terms with Firenze, whom they seemed to find intimidating.

metadata.description: I was not present when Firenze Teaches Centaur Astronomy and Warnings for Hagrid occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Firenze Teaches Centaur Astronomy and Warnings for Hagrid

metadata.description: I've learned that Patronuses are meant to protect you, not just to look pretty.
metadata.source_text: "They’re not supposed to be pretty, they’re supposed to protect you," said Harry patiently.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I now firmly believe we must take immediate action if Umbridge is warned about us; she’s clearly a direct threat to the D.A.
metadata.source_text: "Is she coming?" Harry asked quietly. Dobby let out a howl. "Yes, Harry Potter, yes!"
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I feel responsible for Dobby and protective of him — I won't let him hurt himself and I ordered him to go back to the kitchen and lie to protect us.
metadata.source_text: "Dobby — this is an order — get back down to the kitchen with the other elves, and if she asks you whether you warned me, lie and say no!" said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I've produced a shining silver otter Patronus; the image worked for me and it gambols around me.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s Patronus, a shining silver otter, was gamboling around her.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I realise Patronuses can actually be comforting to watch; they are sort of nice, aren't they?
metadata.source_text: "They are sort of nice, aren’t they?" she said, looking at it fondly.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I care about the safety of everyone in the D.A.; when Dobby arrives terrified I react with fear and sympathy along with the others.
metadata.source_text: Hermione and a few of the other girls let out squeaks of fear and sympathy.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the D.A. meeting in the Room of Requirement, so I didn't see Dobby's warning or the Students' Patronuses.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Meeting Interrupted — Dobby's Warning and Flight

metadata.description: I learned Malfoy tripped me with a Trip Jinx — he was hiding in a niche under a dragon-shaped vase and laughed when I fell.
metadata.source_text: “Trip Jinx, Potter!” he said. “Hey, Professor — PROFESSOR! I’ve got one!”
metadata.scene_title: Capture by Umbridge — Taken to Her Office

metadata.description: I feel more certain now that Umbridge wants to catch and punish me; she looked delighted and seized my arm like she relished the chance to take me to the headmaster.
metadata.source_text: She seized his arm in a vicelike grip and turned, beaming broadly, to Malfoy.
metadata.scene_title: Capture by Umbridge — Taken to Her Office

metadata.description: I'm angrier at Malfoy than before — he hid and then shouted me out as soon as I was down, clearly enjoying getting fifty points and attention from Umbridge.
metadata.source_text: He rolled over onto his back and saw Malfoy concealed in a niche beneath an ugly dragon-shaped vase. “Trip Jinx, Potter!” he said.
metadata.scene_title: Capture by Umbridge — Taken to Her Office

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the corridor incident, so I don't know the exact details of what happened between Harry, Malfoy, and Umbridge.
metadata.scene_title: Capture by Umbridge — Taken to Her Office

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the corridor where Harry was tripped and taken by Umbridge, so I don't know what occurred.
metadata.scene_title: Capture by Umbridge — Taken to Her Office

metadata.description: I learned that Professor Umbridge brought an informant to the Headmaster's office who claims someone reported a meeting in the Room of Requirement.
metadata.source_text: Well, Minister, Miss Edgecombe here came to my office shortly after dinner this evening and told me she had something she wanted to tell me. She said that if I proceeded to a secret room on the seventh floor, sometimes known as the Room of Requirement, I would find out something to my advantage.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I saw that Marietta's face had been jinxed so the word SNEAK appeared in purple pustules across her nose and cheeks, and because of that she couldn't speak.
metadata.source_text: her face was horribly disfigured by a series of close-set purple pustules that had spread across her nose and cheeks to form the word "SNEAK."
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I was ready to lie and play innocent, and Dumbledore's tiny nod and shadow of a wink made me go through with it; I felt it might help, even if it was risky.
metadata.source_text: as Harry stared at him, he shook his head a fraction of an inch to each side. Harry changed direction mid-word. "Yeh — no."
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I noticed Dumbledore signaling me subtly and that made me trust him to have my back a bit more in front of Fudge and Umbridge.
metadata.source_text: as Harry stared at him, he shook his head a fraction of an inch to each side. Harry changed direction mid-word.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this meeting in Dumbledore's office and so I don't know firsthand what was said there.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I wasn't in the Headmaster's office for this confrontation between Harry, Umbridge, and the Minister, so I can't report any direct observations.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge's Office — The D.A. Exposed

metadata.description: I heard Umbridge say the Ministry thinks I tried to recruit students to an illegal society; she told them I organized a Defense group in the Hog’s Head.
metadata.source_text: The purpose of Potter’s meeting with these students," continued Professor Umbridge, "was to persuade them to join an illegal society, whose aim was to learn spells and curses the Ministry has decided are inappropriate for school-age —
metadata.scene_title: Marietta's Betrayal and the List of Names Revealed

metadata.description: I had been certain there was no way to talk my way out of this if Willy Widdershins really heard me — but Dumbledore’s point about timing changed things; I felt a flicker of hope that I might not be guilty.
metadata.source_text: I am merely pointing out that Dolores is quite wrong to suggest that such a group was, at that time, illegal. If you remember, the Ministry decree banning all student societies was not put into effect until two days after Harry’s Hogsmeade meeting, so he was not breaking any rules in the Hog’s Head at all.
metadata.scene_title: Marietta's Betrayal and the List of Names Revealed

metadata.description: I felt stunned and let down seeing Marietta betray us by giving Umbridge the names; she looked empty and I realised people I thought I knew could turn on us under pressure.
metadata.source_text: And to Harry’s horror, she withdrew from her pocket the list of names that had been pinned upon the Room of Requirement’s wall and handed it to Fudge.
metadata.scene_title: Marietta's Betrayal and the List of Names Revealed

metadata.description: I was not present during this Ministry hearing scene, so I did not witness the exchange with Umbridge, Marietta’s reaction, or the list being handed to Fudge.
metadata.scene_title: Marietta's Betrayal and the List of Names Revealed

metadata.description: I was not in the hearing room for these events, therefore I did not see Marietta hand Umbridge the parchment or hear Dumbledore’s defense about the timing of the meetings.
metadata.scene_title: Marietta's Betrayal and the List of Names Revealed

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore intends to present the list of student names as evidence called "Dumbledore's Army," not anything organized by me.
metadata.source_text: "Dumbledore’s Army, Cornelius," said Dumbledore, still smiling as he waved the list of names before Fudge’s face.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals 'Dumbledore's Army' and the Fallout

metadata.description: I suddenly realized Dumbledore was about to use the names as an official statement against the Ministry, and I felt I had to stop him, even though others warned me to be quiet.
metadata.source_text: "NO!" shouted Harry. Kingsley flashed a look of warning at him, McGonagall widened her eyes threateningly, but it had suddenly dawned upon Harry what Dumbledore was about to do, and he could not let it happen.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals 'Dumbledore's Army' and the Fallout

metadata.description: I felt Dumbledore was acting in a way I didn't expect — calm, strategic, and willing to provoke Fudge by taking responsibility — which changed how I saw his tactics in conflict with the Ministry.
metadata.source_text: "That’s right," said Dumbledore pleasantly. "You organized this?" "I did," said Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals 'Dumbledore's Army' and the Fallout

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in Cornelius Fudge's office, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals 'Dumbledore's Army' and the Fallout

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the confrontation in the Minister's office, so I don't have direct knowledge of the exchange between Dumbledore and Fudge.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals 'Dumbledore's Army' and the Fallout

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore refuses to be taken quietly and that he can vanish with Fawkes in a flash of fire — he won't go meekly to Azkaban.
metadata.source_text: I am afraid I am not going to come quietly at all, Cornelius.
metadata.scene_title: Attempted Arrest and Chaos — Dust, Hexes, and Dumbledore's Escape

metadata.description: I've suddenly understood how dangerous my own mind can be — when Dumbledore touched me the pain and that snakelike longing to hurt him hit me hard; I need Occlumency more than I thought.
metadata.source_text: Remember — close your mind —" But as Dumbledore's fingers closed over Harry's skin, a pain shot through the scar on his forehead, and he felt again that terrible, snakelike longing to strike Dumbledore
metadata.scene_title: Attempted Arrest and Chaos — Dust, Hexes, and Dumbledore's Escape

metadata.description: I feel terrible and responsible that the D.A. and all this has led to Dumbledore being forced out, and I owe him for protecting me; he's telling me to learn Occlumency because he wants to keep me safe.
metadata.source_text: Listen to me, Harry," he said urgently, "you must study Occlumency as hard as you can, do you understand me?
metadata.scene_title: Attempted Arrest and Chaos — Dust, Hexes, and Dumbledore's Escape

metadata.description: I was not present during the confrontation in the Ministry office and so did not witness Dumbledore's escape or the hexing and confusion there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Attempted Arrest and Chaos — Dust, Hexes, and Dumbledore's Escape

metadata.description: I was not in the room for the attempted arrest or the chaos that followed, so I don't know what happened when Dumbledore vanished with Fawkes.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Attempted Arrest and Chaos — Dust, Hexes, and Dumbledore's Escape

metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Wreckage, Dumbledore Gone, and Final Orders

I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
