I've learned that Professor Umbridge can make drinks appear with a flick of her wand and that she uses those little tricks to be overly polite while she questions you.
metadata.source_text: To drink, Mr. Potter," she said, smiling still more widely. "Tea? Coffee? Pumpkin juice?" As she named each drink, she gave her short wand a wave, and a cup or glass of it appeared upon her desk.

metadata.description: I'm more certain now that Umbridge is dangerous in a sneaky way — she uses sweetness to hide threats and tries to bully information out of you.
metadata.source_text: "I wish you to have a drink with me," she said, her voice becoming more dangerously sweet.

metadata.description: I now see Filch as someone who has been turned into an ally of Umbridge; he's been won over and will be a useful tool for her against the students.
metadata.source_text: "Umbridge had obviously gone to some lengths to get Filch on her side, Harry thought, and the worst of it was that he would probably prove an important weapon; his knowledge of the school’s secret passageways and hiding places was probably second only to the Weasley twins."

metadata.description: I was not present during the meeting in Umbridge's office, so I don't know what happened in that conversation.
I wasn't in Umbridge's office for the questioning, therefore I can't report on what was said or done there.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I found out Snape reckons I've got the basics of Occlumency and I can carry on by myself now.
metadata.source_text: I’ve told you," Harry muttered. "Snape reckons I can carry on by myself now I’ve got the basics . . ."

metadata.description: I've started to doubt my picture of my parents and feel uneasy about what I saw in the Pensieve; memories of James and Sirius make me question how brave or decent they really were.
metadata.source_text: He felt as though the memory of it was eating him from inside. He had been so sure that his parents had been wonderful people that he never had the slightest difficulty in disbelieving Snape’s aspersions on his father’s character.

metadata.description: I desperately wish I could speak to Sirius again; I feel cut off and helpless without him and I want to find a way to contact him despite Umbridge's surveillance.
metadata.source_text: "I wish I could talk to Sirius," he muttered. "But I know I can’t."

metadata.description: I've discovered that Harry has stopped Occlumency lessons because Snape says he can manage alone, which worries me since I don't think he should stop until he's absolutely sure.
metadata.source_text: "But why haven’t you got Occlumency lessons anymore?" said Hermione, frowning. "I’ve told you," Harry muttered. "Snape reckons I can carry on by myself now I’ve got the basics . . ." "Well, I don’t think Snape should stop until you’re absolutely sure you can control them!" said Hermione indignantly.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that planning and schedules are essential; with only six weeks until exams I believe following a strict timetable will help Ron and Harry do fine.
metadata.source_text: It was the first day of the Easter holidays and Hermione, as was her custom, had spent a large part of the day drawing up study schedules for the three of them... "Well, there you are," she said, handing him his schedule, "if you follow that you should do fine."

metadata.description: I care enough about Harry to nag him about his lessons and exams because I worry for his safety and success; I won't let his refusal to continue Occlumency go without protest.
metadata.source_text: "So you’ve stopped having funny dreams?" said Hermione skeptically... "Harry, I think you should go back to him and ask —"

metadata.description: I've learned there are only six weeks left until our exams and Hermione has scheduled study times for each of us, which I wasn't expecting.
metadata.source_text: It was the first day of the Easter holidays and Hermione, as was her custom, had spent a large part of the day drawing up study schedules for the three of them. Ron had been startled to discover that there were only six weeks left until their exams.

metadata.description: I'm feeling bleak about our Quidditch chances this year and think we have about as much chance of winning the Cup as Dad has of becoming Minister of Magic, so I'm not as hopeful as before.
metadata.source_text: "We’ve got about as much chance of winning the Quidditch Cup this year as Dad’s got of becoming Minister of Magic . . ."

metadata.description: I really blame Marietta Edgecombe for what happened to Cho's friend and I'm angry enough to rant about her, showing I stand by my mates and hate traitors.
metadata.source_text: Ron went into a rant about Marietta Edgecombe, which Harry found helpful.

metadata.description: I found Floo powder in Umbridge's office fireplace after slipping in under the Invisibility Cloak and using Sirius's knife to open her door; the fireplace held a small box with glittering powder.
metadata.source_text: Harry pulled off his Cloak and, striding over to the fireplace, found what he was looking for within seconds: a small box containing glittering Floo powder.

metadata.description: I can pick locks or at least jimmy doors with Sirius's magical knife; sliding the blade in the crack produced a tiny click and the door swung open.
metadata.source_text: He inserted the blade of the magical knife into the crack around it and moved it gently up and down, then withdrew it. There was a tiny click, and the door swung open.

metadata.description: I decided in that instant to act on my own rather than listen to Hermione's pleading; I had made up my mind and ran off to see what was happening despite her begging.
metadata.source_text: But he had made up his mind — hitching his bag more securely onto his shoulder he set off at a run... "Harry — please!" said Hermione weakly. But he had made up his mind —

metadata.description: I noticed Ron wouldn't give me his opinion and avoided looking at me; he told Hermione to give it a rest, so I feel he's backing off and letting me decide for myself.
metadata.source_text: Ron seemed determined to give neither his opinion nor his advice. He would not look at Harry... he said in a low voice, "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."

metadata.description: I've learned that Harry was planning to go off despite my protests; I pleaded with him not to do it and tried to dissuade him as the bell rang, but he left anyway.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, don't do it, please don't do it!" Hermione said in anguished tones as the bell rang at the end of the class.

metadata.description: I feel more desperate and worried than before about Harry taking risks; hearing the screams and seeing him run makes me genuinely frightened for his safety.
metadata.source_text: People exiting the classrooms all around Harry were stopping in their tracks and looking up at the ceiling fearfully... "Harry — please!" said Hermione weakly.

metadata.description: I perceive that Ron is less willing to argue with Harry or press him; when I tried to dissuade Harry, Ron told me to give it a rest, so I see him stepping back.
metadata.source_text: Ron seemed determined to give neither his opinion nor his advice... he said in a low voice, "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."

metadata.description: I learned that Harry was intent on going off by himself and that Hermione was upset about it; I told Hermione to give it a rest and let Harry decide.
metadata.source_text: Ron seemed determined to give neither his opinion nor his advice. He would not look at Harry... he said in a low voice, "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."

metadata.description: I feel Harry should be allowed to make his own decisions right now, so I've stopped trying to force my opinion on him and told Hermione to back off.
metadata.source_text: when Hermione opened her mouth to try dissuading Harry some more, he said in a low voice, "Give it a rest, okay? He can make up his own mind."

metadata.description: I noticed I'm less involved in arguing with Harry and Hermione over his choices; by not offering my view and telling Hermione to stop, I've shifted into a quieter role.
metadata.source_text: Ron seemed determined to give neither his opinion nor his advice. He would not look at Harry...

metadata.description: I managed to Floo-connect by sticking my head into the fireplace and reached Grimmauld Place even though only my head travelled; my knees stayed on Umbridge’s cold floor the whole time.
metadata.source_text: I had traveled by Floo powder before, of course, but then it had been his entire body that had spun around and around in the flames ... This time, his knees remained firm upon the cold floor of Umbridge’s office, and only his head hurtled through the emerald fire.

metadata.description: I told Sirius and Lupin exactly what I saw in the Pensieve about my father when he was fifteen; I went straight into the story because my knees were killing me and time was limited.
metadata.source_text: He therefore plunged immediately into the story of what he had seen in the Pensieve.

metadata.description: After hearing Lupin and Sirius and seeing the memory, I’ve started to feel sorry for Snape; I didn’t expect to feel that way about him after what I saw.
metadata.source_text: I just never thought I’d feel sorry for Snape.

metadata.description: I’m annoyed and discomposed that Snape stopped giving me Occlumency lessons, but Lupin insists learning Occlumency is the most important thing, so I reluctantly agree I’ll try to tell Snape to carry on.
metadata.source_text: He told me he’d never teach me Occlumency again ... 'Harry, there is nothing so important as you learning Occlumency!' said Lupin sternly.

metadata.description: Talking to Sirius and Lupin about my father changed how I see James — they admit he was an idiot at fifteen but insist he was a good person who grew out of it, which makes me less quick to judge my dad only by that memory.
metadata.source_text: He was only fifteen — 'I’m fifteen!' said Harry heatedly. 'Look, Harry,' said Sirius placatingly, 'James and Snape hated each other ... I think James was everything Snape wanted to be ...' 'Your father was the best friend I ever had, and he was a good person.'

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in Umbridge’s office or the Floo visit to Grimmauld Place, so I do not know what happened firsthand.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events in Umbridge’s office or the Floo visit to Grimmauld Place, so I do not know what happened firsthand.

metadata.description: I wasn’t there for Harry’s Floo connection to Grimmauld Place or his conversation with Sirius and Lupin, so I can’t report what I didn’t witness.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t there for Harry’s Floo connection to Grimmauld Place or his conversation with Sirius and Lupin, so I can’t report what I didn’t witness.

metadata.description: I gave Fred and George my Triwizard gold last June so they could set themselves up — they didn’t steal anything, I put the Galleons in their hands.
metadata.source_text: Because they got the gold from me. I gave them my Triwizard winnings last June.

metadata.description: I don’t regret giving them the money; I think they’ll be brilliant at a joke shop and I’m glad I helped them even if people will gossip.
metadata.source_text: And I don’t regret it either — I didn’t need the gold, and they’ll be great at a joke shop . . .

metadata.description: I’m resigned that Ron’s mum won’t blame Fred and George now that I told Ron they used my gold — Ron can tell her and I won’t hide it anymore.
metadata.source_text: ’Specially if she thinks they’re receiving stolen cauldrons or something . . .

metadata.description: I’ve learned that lots of students are faking symptoms from Skiving Snackboxes and calling it ‘Umbridge-itis’ so Umbridge can’t trace the source.
metadata.source_text: After putting four successive classes in detention and failing to discover their secret she was forced to give up and allow the bleeding, swooning, sweating, and vomiting students to leave her classes in droves.

metadata.description: I’ve become more determined that Harry should resume Occlumency lessons because he’s still muttering in his sleep and trying to block his mind.
metadata.source_text: You are trying to block your mind, aren’t you?" said Hermione, looking beadily at Harry. "You are keeping going with your Occlumency?

metadata.description: I think Ron might do better without Fred and George around because they undermined his confidence; I’m noticing how much effect they had on him.
metadata.source_text: I think Ron might do better without Fred and George around. They never exactly gave him a lot of confidence . . .

metadata.description: I reckon Montague’s injury could help Gryffindor’s chances in the Cup if Montague doesn’t recover before Slytherin play Hufflepuff.
metadata.source_text: if Montague doesn’t recover before Slytherin play Hufflepuff, we might be in with a chance of winning the Cup.

metadata.description: I’m bitter that Mum might think I should’ve stopped Fred and George leaving and that she might blame me; I’m convinced it’ll be my fault when she hears.
metadata.source_text: I’m going to be in deep trouble. I wouldn’t be surprised if she’s sent a Howler again." "It’ll be my fault Fred and George left, you wait.

metadata.description: I feel less blame now that Harry says he gave Fred and George his Triwizard gold — that means Mum can’t blame me for their leaving.
metadata.source_text: It’s all your fault, Harry — Mum can’t blame me at all! Can I tell her?

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid brought a giant back into the forest — he calls him Grawp and he’s enormous, curled up and sleeping with ropes around the trees.
metadata.source_text: He’s been hurting you all this time, hasn’t he? That’s why you’ve had all these injuries!

metadata.description: I promised Hagrid straight away because I couldn’t break my word — even though the idea of looking after a violent giant made me feel sick inside.
metadata.source_text: Of course we’ll help you," said Harry at once.

metadata.description: I feel even more protective of Hagrid now; he trusts me with something huge and personal, and I don’t want to let him down.
metadata.source_text: I knew yeh’d say yes," said Hagrid into his handkerchief, "but I won’ . . . never . . . forget . . .

metadata.description: I found out that Hagrid’s half-brother Grawp exists and that he’s about sixteen foot tall, tied up, and difficult to teach because he barely speaks English.
metadata.source_text: Yeah . . . well, tha’s what it sounds like when he says his name," said Hagrid anxiously. "He don’ speak a lot of English. . . . I’ve bin tryin’ ter teach him. . . .

metadata.description: I’m horrified and unconvinced that bringing Grawp here was right — I used to trust Hagrid’s judgment, but now I’m really worried about danger to students and to Grawp himself.
metadata.source_text: He’s been hurting you all this time, hasn’t he? That’s why you’ve had all these injuries!

metadata.description: My view of Hagrid is complicated now: I still care for him, but I’m shocked he smuggled a giant back and put himself at risk to do it.
metadata.source_text: Hermione simply stared at him, her mouth open.

metadata.description: I saw Hagrid wake Grawp by poking him with a broken bough and Grawp roar awake; he’s huge, clumsy, and smashes trees and nests when he wakes up.
metadata.source_text: When he was around ten feet away, he lifted a long, broken bough from the ground, smiled reassuringly over his shoulder at Harry and Hermione, and then poked Grawp hard in the middle of the back with the end of the bough.

metadata.description: I noticed Grawp is about sixteen feet tall with a face like a gray full moon, a stubby nose, lopsided mouth, big yellow teeth, small greenish-brown sleepy eyes, and very large hands.
metadata.source_text: They looked up into his startlingly huge face, which resembled a gray full moon swimming in the gloom of the clearing. The nose was stubby and shapeless, the mouth lopsided and full of misshapen yellow teeth the size of half-bricks. The small eyes were a muddy greenish-brown and just now were half gummed together with sleep.

metadata.description: I’m a bit more worried now about Hagrid’s plans; I thought teaching Grawp English might be possible, but seeing how dangerous and uncontrolled Grawp is has shaken me.
metadata.source_text: Oh Hagrid, don’t," moaned Hermione, but Hagrid had already raised the bough again and gave Grawp’s knee a sharp poke.

metadata.description: I feel protective of Hermione — I pulled her behind a tree when Grawp lunged and stayed close while she shook and whimpered, so I’m more conscious of looking out for her in dangerous situations.
metadata.source_text: Grawp’s hand had shot out of nowhere toward Hermione — Harry seized her and pulled her backward behind the tree, so that Grawp’s fist scraped the trunk but closed on thin air.

metadata.description: I heard Hagrid try to introduce me to Grawp and ask if he could call me Hermy because Grawp can’t remember my full name — and I agreed even though I was terrified.
metadata.source_text: Turning to Hermione he said, "Would yeh mind if he called yeh Hermy, Hermione? On'y it’s a difficult name fer him ter remember . . ." "No, not at all," squeaked Hermione.

metadata.description: I discovered that Grawp will grab at people suddenly — he lunged for me and I had to cling behind a tree while Harry pulled me back, so he’s unpredictable and physically dangerous.
metadata.source_text: GRAWPY, NO!" Grawp’s hand had shot out of nowhere toward Hermione — Harry seized her and pulled her backward behind the tree, so that Grawp’s fist scraped the trunk but closed on thin air.

metadata.description: I’m now convinced Hagrid’s idea of us teaching Grawp English is wildly impractical; after seeing a giant like that awake and interested in tearing up trees, I really don’t believe we can manage him safely.
metadata.source_text: I don’t believe him," said Hermione in a very unsteady voice, the moment they were out of earshot of Hagrid. "I don’t believe him. I really don’t believe him . . ."

metadata.description: I felt frightened and relied on Harry when Grawp lunged; I’m reminded that in danger I look to him for help and support, which makes me feel closer and more dependent on him in those moments.
metadata.source_text: Harry seized her and pulled her backward behind the tree, so that Grawp’s fist scraped the trunk but closed on thin air.

metadata.description: I heard the crowd singing "Weasley is our King" for Ron and I know he’s just come back from the Quidditch pitch triumphant with the Quidditch Cup, everyone carrying him on their shoulders.
metadata.source_text: HARRY! HERMIONE!" yelled Ron, waving the silver Quidditch Cup in the air and looking quite beside himself. "WE DID IT! WE WON!"

metadata.description: I’m pleased and proud that the whole school is cheering for our Quidditch victory; hearing them chant makes me feel like what we did really mattered to everyone.
metadata.source_text: Weasley is our King, Weasley is our King, He didn’t let the Quaffle in, Weasley is our King . . .

metadata.description: I can tell people admire me now after the match; being hoisted on shoulders and cheered shows that my teammates and classmates value what I helped achieve.
metadata.source_text: They beamed up at him as he passed; there was a scrum at the door of the castle and Ron’s head got rather badly bumped on the lintel, but nobody seemed to want to put him down.

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid brought a giant back from the forest and hid him there — Grawp is about sixteen feet tall and Hagrid wants us to help teach him English.
metadata.source_text: Grawp’s about sixteen feet tall, enjoys ripping up twenty-foot pine trees, and knows me," she snorted, "as Hermy.

metadata.description: I’m starting to think Hagrid has really lost his mind over this giant, but I still feel stuck because we promised him and I don’t like breaking promises.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I’m starting to think he has. But unfortunately, he made Harry and me promise.

metadata.description: I’m aware that Hermione and I kept our promise to Hagrid and that makes me feel responsible — Hagrid expects help and I can’t just walk away despite the danger.
metadata.source_text: He decided to tell us why he’s been covered in injuries ever since he got back from the giants. He wanted us to go into the forest with him, we had no choice, you know how he gets. . . .

metadata.description: I know that the only part of the match Harry and I actually saw was Davies’s first goal; we missed Ron’s saves because Hagrid took us into the forest.
metadata.source_text: As a matter of fact, the only bit of the match Harry and I saw was Davies’s first goal.

metadata.description: I’m beginning to think Hagrid might be mad about bringing a giant back, but I still feel bound by the promise Harry and I made to help teach him.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I’m starting to think he has. But unfortunately, he made Harry and me promise.

metadata.description: I’ve found that Grawp knows me as 'Hermy', which is unsettling — it changes how I view Hagrid’s judgement and the risk he’s dragging us into.
metadata.source_text: Grawp’s about sixteen feet tall, enjoys ripping up twenty-foot pine trees, and knows me," she snorted, "as Hermy.

metadata.description: I learned that Ginny actually caught the Snitch out from under Chang and that she was furious afterwards, even chucking her broom when she got back to the ground.
metadata.source_text: Did you see the look on Chang’s face when Ginny got the Snitch right out from under her nose? ... But you saw her chuck her broom away when she got back to the ground, didn’t you?

metadata.description: I’m convinced Hagrid can’t have brought a giant back, I just can’t accept it at first — then I get more worried when Harry and Hermione confirm he did.
metadata.source_text: No, he can’t have . . ." "Well, he has," said Hermione firmly.

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and protective about Hagrid dragging us into trouble; I keep thinking of past disasters like Norbert and Aragog and worry Hagrid’s friends always cause problems for us.
metadata.source_text: Remember Norbert? Remember Aragog? Have we ever come off better for mixing with any of Hagrid’s monster mates?

metadata.description: I learned that exam rules forbid Auto-Answer Quills, Remembralls, Detachable Cribbing Cuffs, and Self-Correcting Ink — and that cheaters will be punished most severely.
metadata.source_text: Auto-Answer Quills are banned from the examination hall, as are Remembralls, Detachable Cribbing Cuffs, and Self-Correcting Ink.

metadata.description: I feel relieved that producing a Patronus can win me favour in an exam situation — doing it earned applause and let me finish early instead of more tests.
metadata.source_text: I heard, from my dear friend Tiberius Ogden, that you can produce a Patronus? For a bonus point . . . ?

metadata.description: I care about Hagrid and want to do well in Care of Magical Creatures so I won't let him down; my respect for him makes me determined.
metadata.source_text: Harry was determined to perform well in Tuesday’s Care of Magical Creatures exam so as not to let Hagrid down.

metadata.description: I've been told that O.W.L. results will be sent by owl in July — that's when we'll officially find out how we've done.
metadata.source_text: An owl will be sent to you some time in July,

metadata.description: I'm anxious and obsessive about being exactly right when tested; I keep snatching the book back to check answers and get agitated if I'm unsure.
metadata.source_text: She was very agitated and kept snatching the book back from him to check that she had gotten the answer completely right, finally hitting him hard on the nose with the sharp edge of Achievements in Charming.

metadata.description: I get snappish under stress and lash out verbally; when the others won't argue back I end up snapping at younger students instead.
metadata.source_text: Only!" said Hermione snappishly. "I've got Arithmancy and it's probably the toughest subject there is!"

metadata.description: I know that exams are stressful and that only four O.W.L. exams remain after the Potions practical ended.
metadata.source_text: Only four exams left,

metadata.description: I'm relieved that some exams can be delayed in my mind until the holidays — hearing results come in July makes me feel I can wait a bit.
metadata.source_text: Excellent," said Dean Thomas in an audible whisper, "so we don't have to worry about it till the holidays . . .

metadata.description: I notice when friends are tense or anxious in exams and that affects how I feel about the whole thing; seeing Hermione snap shows how stressed she is.
metadata.source_text: Only!" said Hermione snappishly. "I've got Arithmancy and it's probably the toughest subject there is!"

metadata.description: I saw Hagrid watching from his cabin window while I finished the creatures exam, and I even gave him a quick thumbs-up before heading back to the castle.
metadata.source_text: Harry could see Hagrid watching anxiously out of his cabin window. When Harry’s examiner, a plump little witch this time, smiled at him and told him he could leave, Harry gave Hagrid a fleeting thumbs-up before heading back up to the castle.

metadata.description: I didn't do well in Divination — my crystal ball stayed blank, my tea-leaf reading came out all wrong, and I mixed up life and head lines on a palm so badly I told the examiner she should have died.
metadata.source_text: Even by Harry’s low standards in Divination, the exam went very badly. He might as well have tried to see moving pictures in the desktop as in the stubbornly blank crystal ball; he lost his head completely during tea-leaf reading, saying it looked to him as though Professor Marchbanks would shortly be meeting a round, dark, soggy stranger, and rounded off the whole fiasco by mixing up the life and head lines on her palm and informing her that she ought to have died the previous Tuesday.

metadata.description: I reckon there's no point pretending I care about Divination any more — I'd rather drop it than keep wasting time on nonsense about planets getting friendly.
metadata.source_text: “We shouldn’t have taken the stupid subject in the first place,” said Harry. “Still, at least we can give it up now.” “Yeah,” said Harry. “No more pretending we care what happens when Jupiter and Uranus get too friendly . . .”

metadata.description: I'm worried about Professor McGonagall — hearing she was carried back up to the castle made me hope Madam Pomfrey can fix her; I feel concerned for her properly.
metadata.source_text: “I just hope Professor McGonagall’s all right,” said Lavender tearfully. “They carried her back up to the castle, we watched through the dormitory window,” said Colin Creevey. “She didn’t look very well . . .” “Madam Pomfrey will sort her out,” said Alicia Spinnet firmly. “She’s never failed yet.”

metadata.description: I've done all right in Arithmancy; I think I performed well enough to be satisfied with my result.
metadata.source_text: “Well, I think I’ve done all right in Arithmancy,” she said, and Harry and Ron both sighed with relief.

metadata.description: I believe Umbridge dislikes part-humans and would try to get Hagrid out because of that prejudice; it explains why she'd move against him.
metadata.source_text: “Umbridge hates part-humans,” said Hermione bitterly, flopping down into an armchair. “She was always going to try and get Hagrid out.”

metadata.description: I now see more clearly that Hagrid was vulnerable — between Umbridge's prejudice and his closeness to Dumbledore, I feel more protective and angry on his behalf.
metadata.source_text: “She’d have sacked him anyway,” said Dean. “He was too close to Dumbledore.” “That’s true,” said Harry, sinking into an armchair beside Hermione’s.

metadata.description: I told the examiner about an ugly man with a wart in my crystal ball and then realized I'd been describing the examiner's reflection — and that made me feel pretty stupid.
metadata.source_text: He had just made Harry feel rather better by telling him how he told the examiner in detail about the ugly man with a wart on his nose in his crystal ball, only to look up and realize he had been describing his examiner’s reflection.

metadata.description: We're never taking Divination seriously again; I'm chucking my tea leaves in the bin if they tell me to read anything like 'die, Ron, die'.
metadata.source_text: “And from now on, I don’t care if my tea leaves spell die, Ron, die — I’m just chucking them in the bin where they belong.”

metadata.description: I feel resigned and a bit gloomy about failing Divination with Harry, but telling him about my crystal-ball mix-up cheered him up and reminded me we're in it together.
metadata.source_text: “Well, we were always going to fail that one,” said Ron gloomily as they ascended the marble staircase. He had just made Harry feel rather better by telling him how he told the examiner...

metadata.description: I've just seen Voldemort torturing Sirius in the Department of Mysteries — I know exactly where: a room full of shelves covered in little glass spheres at the end of row ninety-seven.
metadata.source_text: There’s a room in the Department of Mysteries full of shelves covered in these little glass balls, and they’re at the end of row ninety-seven . . . He’s trying to use Sirius to get whatever it is he wants from in there. . . . He’s torturing him. . . . Says he’ll end by killing him . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry Awakens in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I believe those visions are real and not merely nightmares — Occlumency was supposed to stop me seeing things like this, but I can’t ignore what I saw: Sirius is trapped and I’m the only one who knows.
metadata.source_text: You don’t get it! I’m not having nightmares, I’m not just dreaming! What d’you think all the Occlumency was for, why d’you think Dumbledore wanted me prevented from seeing these things? Because they’re REAL, Hermione — Sirius is trapped — I’ve seen him — Voldemort’s got him, and no one else knows, and that means we’re the only ones who can save him, and if you don’t want to do it, fine, but I’m going, understand?
metadata.scene_title: Harry Awakens in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I feel abandoned and panicked because Dumbledore, Hagrid, and now McGonagall are gone; I’d always expected Minerva to be solid and dependable, and learning she’s been Stunned and taken to St. Mungo’s makes me feel like I’ve lost the last adult I could tell.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore had gone, Hagrid had gone, but he had always expected Professor McGonagall to be there, irascible and inflexible, perhaps, but always dependably, solidly present. . . . "She’s not here, Potter," said Madam Pomfrey sadly. "She was transferred to St. Mungo’s this morning. Four Stunning Spells straight to the chest at her age?"
metadata.scene_title: Harry Awakens in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the hospital wing and corridors, so I can't speak from firsthand experience about Harry's vision or McGonagall's transfer.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t present during the events in the hospital wing and corridors, so I don’t know what happened.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Awakens in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I wasn't in the hospital wing when Harry woke and ran about; I arrived later and so I can't confirm the exact details of Harry's vision or McGonagall being taken.
metadata.source_text: I wasn’t in the hospital wing when Harry woke and ran about; I arrived later so I don't have first-hand knowledge.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Awakens in the Hospital Wing

metadata.description: I saw that Grimmauld Place’s kitchen was empty when I flooed there — no sign of Sirius, just Kreacher with bandaged hands.
metadata.source_text: He knelt down quickly, thrust his head into the dancing fire, and cried, “Number twelve, Grimmauld Place!” ... There was nobody there. ... Kreacher the house-elf came creeping into view. ... “Master has gone out, Harry Potter.”
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I’m convinced my visions from Occlumency are real and not just nightmares — I know Sirius is in danger and I must act now, no matter what anyone else says.
metadata.source_text: I’m not having nightmares, I’m not just dreaming! ... Because they’re REAL, Hermione — Sirius is trapped — I’ve seen him — Voldemort’s got him, and no one else knows, and that means we’re the only ones who can save him
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I feel betrayed and desperate when people doubt what I’ve seen — I’m angrier at anyone who treats my warnings like silliness, even my friends when they hesitate.
metadata.source_text: You don’t get it!” Harry shouted at her. “I’m not having nightmares... Because they’re REAL, Hermione ... and if you don’t want to do it, fine, but I’m going, understand?
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I realised we can use Umbridge’s fireplace and Floo powder to check whether Sirius is at Grimmauld Place before rushing to London.
metadata.source_text: We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him,” said Hermione
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I used to trust that preventing Harry from seeing things was best, but after hearing him and seeing his certainty I think we must at least check Grimmauld Place before stopping him.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore wanted you to learn to shut these things out of your mind, if you’d done Occlumency properly you’d never have seen this —” ... “Harry, I’m begging you, please! Please let’s just check that Sirius isn’t at home before we go charging off to London
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I will stand by Harry and actually go into danger with him — I offered to go under the Cloak and keep watch while he checks the office because I trust him and want to help.
metadata.source_text: I mean, you can — can check whether Sirius is at home or not while I keep watch... Even through his anger and impatience Harry recognized Hermione’s offer to accompany him into Umbridge’s office as a sign of solidarity and loyalty.
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I volunteered to distract Umbridge by telling her Peeves was causing trouble in Transfiguration so we could get into her office quickly.
metadata.source_text: I’ll do it,” said Ron at once. “I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I’m upset by Harry’s insistence but I don’t think he’s just showing off — I’ll help because he’s my mate even if I argued with him moments ago.
metadata.source_text: I never said I had a problem!” said Ron heatedly. ... “I’ll do it,” said Ron at once.
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I still back Harry; despite the row I’m prepared to take the risk and be part of the plan to check Umbridge’s office and protect the others as we try to find Sirius.
metadata.source_text: I’ll do it,” said Ron at once. “I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something
metadata.scene_title: Madam Pomfrey’s News and Harry’s Flight

metadata.description: I realised there's still a member of the Order at Hogwarts — Snape — and he was standing in Umbridge's office when I needed help.
metadata.source_text: There was still a member of the Order of the Phoenix at Hogwarts — Snape.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I'm convinced my visions aren't just dreams anymore; I know they're real and that Sirius is in danger, so I'm determined to act even if others doubt me.
metadata.source_text: I’m not having nightmares, I’m not just dreaming! ... Because they’re REAL, Hermione — Sirius is trapped — I’ve seen him — Voldemort’s got him, and no one else knows, and that means we’re the only ones who can save him
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: Snape's reaction made me see him as unhelpful and like my last hope walked out of the door; I felt betrayed when he left without acting on what I shouted.
metadata.source_text: Harry knew his last chance of letting the Order know what was going on was walking out of the door. 'He’s got Padfoot!' he shouted.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I've learned that we can use Umbridge's floo powder to check whether Sirius is at home before we run off to London, and that timing will be tight — maybe five minutes at best.
metadata.source_text: We’ll have to use Umbridge’s fire and see if we can contact him,... 'Five minutes’ll be enough,' said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I changed from wanting to stop Harry to agreeing to help him as long as we first check Grimmauld Place; I'm desperate but more cautious now because I fear it could be a trap.
metadata.source_text: I’m begging you, please! Please let’s just check that Sirius isn’t at home before we go charging off to London
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I proved my loyalty to Harry by volunteering to go into Umbridge’s office under the Invisibility Cloak with him — I will stand by him and do whatever it takes to help find Sirius.
metadata.source_text: I mean, you can — can check whether Sirius is at home or not while I keep watch... I’ll come, I’ll d-do whatever it takes to try and save him
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I've learned that I can distract Umbridge by telling her Peeves is causing trouble — and I offered to do that straight away to buy time for the others.
metadata.source_text: I’ll do it,' said Ron at once. 'I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I still back Harry but I'm shaken by how urgent he is; I wanted to help straight away, showing I'm willing to act even when things sound risky.
metadata.source_text: I’ll do it,' said Ron at once.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I remain loyal to Harry — I didn’t argue when he insisted on going and I volunteered to take the risky job of heading Umbridge off, so I'm clearly on his side.
metadata.source_text: I’ll do it,' said Ron at once. 'I’ll tell her Peeves is smashing up the Transfiguration department or something
metadata.scene_title: Harry Tells Friends About Sirius and Plans to Rescue Him

metadata.description: I found out Kreacher thinks Sirius has gone to the Department of Mysteries — the elf actually said Master will not come back from the Department of Mysteries.
metadata.source_text: Master will not come back from the Department of Mysteries!
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I realized Snape might be my last chance to get word to the Order, but he walked out of Umbridge's office and didn't help, so my hope in him just collapsed in an instant.
metadata.source_text: He’s got Padfoot! He’s got Padfoot at the place where it’s hidden!
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I feel utterly betrayed and desperate: Snape leaving without acting made me see him as useless to me right now rather than someone I could count on to help save Sirius.
metadata.source_text: Padfoot? ... I have no idea," said Snape coldly. "Potter, when I want nonsense shouted at me I shall give you a Babbling Beverage.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I said that we were trying to tell Professor Dumbledore something important and that the thing we had finished and couldn't deliver was a weapon — that's what I revealed under pressure.
metadata.source_text: I — I was trying to get my Firebolt! ... "Well, he was trying to speak to Professor Dumbledore" ... "We . . . we wanted to tell him it’s r-ready!" "The . . . the weapon," said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: Even though I was sobbing and terrified, I couldn't bring myself to cry real tears under Umbridge's scrutiny; I felt raw and helpless but held part of myself together because showing true breakdown would only make things worse.
metadata.source_text: And Hermione began to cry weakly into the back of Millicent Bulstrode’s robes. Millicent stopped trying to squash her ... there was no trace of a tear.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I know now that Umbridge will stop at almost nothing — she sent dementors after Harry and is willing to use the Cruciatus; I distrust her completely and fear her more than before.
metadata.source_text: The Minister wouldn’t want you to break the law, Professor Umbridge! ... "They were all bleating about silencing you somehow — discrediting you — but I was the one who actually did something about it . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I was grabbed and brought into Umbridge's office with the others and gagged; Warrington shoved me forward and accused Neville of trying to stop him take Ginny.
metadata.source_text: Got 'em all," said Warrington, shoving Ron roughly forward into the room. "That one," he poked a thick finger at Neville, "tried to stop me taking her," he pointed at Ginny
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: Being crudely arrested and gagged made me angrier and more certain that Umbridge and the Inquisitorial Squad are cruel and dangerous, not just petty — they actually want to hurt our friends.
metadata.source_text: Well, it looks as though Hogwarts will shortly be a Weasley-free zone, doesn’t it?" Malfoy laughed loudly and sycophantically.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I feel more protective and loyal toward Harry and the others now; seeing them helpless with my own lips gagged made me determined they won't be left on their own if I can help it.
metadata.source_text: You stationed lookouts around my office and you sent this buffoon," she nodded at Ron
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in Umbridge’s Office and Snape’s Departure

metadata.description: I felt my scar throbbing in the soft evening air and knew that if Voldemort had moved in for the kill my scar would burn white-hot.
metadata.source_text: His scar was throbbing in the soft evening air but it had not yet burned white-hot, as he knew it would if Voldemort had moved in for the kill. . . .

metadata.description: I realised walking into the forest without wands was far more foolhardy than I first thought — the danger here is very real and not to be treated lightly.
metadata.source_text: As they reached the cool shade of the first trees, Harry tried to catch Hermione’s eye; walking into the forest without wands seemed to him to be more foolhardy than anything they had done so far this evening.

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione stride on and deliberately make noise to attract attention made me recognise she was prepared to be bold and provocative, even when I was worried.
metadata.source_text: She, however, merely gave Umbridge a contemptuous glance and plunged straight into the trees, moving at such a pace that Umbridge, with her shorter legs, had difficulty in keeping up.

metadata.description: I've indicated that the hidden object would be somewhere students weren’t likely to find it accidentally — that’s why I pointed into the dark trees.
metadata.source_text: “In there, of course,” said Hermione, pointing into the dark trees. “It had to be somewhere that students weren’t going to find it accidentally, didn’t it?”

metadata.description: I decided we should be heard rather than silent; I want the centaurs to know we are here and to force a reaction, even if Harry worries about it.
metadata.source_text: “I want us heard,” she answered quietly, as Umbridge jogged noisily after them. “You’ll see . . .”

metadata.description: When Umbridge insulted the centaurs I reacted furiously and tried to stop her — I see the centaurs as beings deserving respect and felt compelled to defend them.
metadata.source_text: “Don’t call them that!” Hermione said furiously, but Umbridge did not appear to have heard her.

metadata.description: I learned that centaurs will not act as servants to humans and will refuse to help if they think we're asking them to do our dirty work.
metadata.source_text: We do not help humans! ... We are a race apart and proud to be so. . . . We will not permit you to walk from here, boasting that we did your bidding!

metadata.description: I didn't expect the centaurs to be so openly hostile; I'm now much more wary of relying on them or expecting their help in human matters.
metadata.source_text: You see, Ronan? They already have the arrogance of their kind! So we were to do your dirty work, were we, human girl?

metadata.description: I realise the centaurs don't see us as allies and that they regard themselves as separate and superior to wizards and witches.
metadata.source_text: We are a race apart and proud to be so. . . . We will not permit you to walk from here, boasting that we did your bidding!

metadata.description: I discovered that telling centaurs we expected them to drive Umbridge off was a terrible mistake—centaurs resent being treated like servants.
metadata.source_text: We only came in here because we hoped you’d drive her off for us —

metadata.description: I now realise that pleading and explaining won't necessarily win over the centaurs; they take great offence at being asked to intervene for humans.
metadata.source_text: Please — I didn’t mean that! I just hoped you’d be able to — to help us —

metadata.description: I can see clearly that many centaurs distrust wizards and consider some of us traitors, so my trust in them as potential allies is shaken.
metadata.source_text: We are not all like the traitor Firenze, human girl!

metadata.description: I've learned Grawp attacked the centaurs and that his blood sprayed Hermione and me; that explains why centaurs fled and why we're smeared with blood attracting thestrals.
metadata.source_text: Pebble-sized droplets of Grawp’s blood showered Harry as he pulled Hermione to her feet and the pair of them ran as fast as they could for the shelter of the trees.

metadata.description: I've learned that Sirius was seen in the fire — I can feel it through my scar — and I'm convinced he is alive, but we're further away and I can't see how to reach him from here.
metadata.source_text: Yes," said Harry, as his scar gave another painful prickle, "and I'm sure Sirius is still alive, but I can't see how we're going to get there to help him.

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more desperate than before; losing time and my wand has made me feel panicked and bitter about our chances to rescue Sirius.
metadata.source_text: They had wasted so much time — they were even further from rescuing Sirius than they had been when he had had the vision. Not only had Harry managed to lose his wand...

metadata.description: I don't think Ginny, Neville, and Luna are the people I'd have chosen to help rescue Sirius, but I see their determination and have to accept their willingness to fight beside us.
metadata.source_text: If he could have chosen any members of the D.A. in addition to himself, Ron, and Hermione to join him in the attempt to rescue Sirius, he would not have picked Ginny, Neville, or Luna.

metadata.description: I've learned that being covered in Grawp's blood seems to attract thestrals, because Hagrid uses raw meat and blood to lure them and the thestrals came after we were splattered.
metadata.source_text: Because in case you hadn't noticed, you and Hermione are both covered in blood," she said coolly, "and we know Hagrid lures thestrals with raw meat, so that's probably why these two turned up in the first place...

metadata.description: I'm terrified that the centaurs might have been killed by Grawp and I'm shaken by what I've seen; I feel faint and overwhelmed by the horror of the attack.
metadata.source_text: "Oh no," said Hermione, quaking so badly that her knees gave way. "Oh, that was horrible. And he might kill them all . . ."

metadata.description: I still want to help and I believe my friends from the D.A. should be involved; despite being shaken I want more thestrals to come so we can all attempt the rescue together.
metadata.source_text: "Well, we can’t do anything without wands," said Hermione hopelessly, dragging herself up again... "Just two." "Well, we need three," said Hermione...

metadata.description: I've learned how we escaped Umbridge's office: a few Stunners, a Disarming Charm, and Neville's Impediment Jinx; Ginny hexed Malfoy with a Bat-Bogey Hex and I found Harry's wand afterwards.
metadata.source_text: "Couple of Stunners, a Disarming Charm, Neville brought off a really nice little Impediment Jinx," said Ron airily, now handing back Hermione's wand too...

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and defensive about who gets to go and who doesn't; I don't want Ginny, Neville, and Luna putting themselves in danger and I'm angry at the idea of spreading ourselves thin.
metadata.source_text: "Yeah, but you’re not coming," said Ron angrily... "Look," said Ron, barely containing his anger, "you might be able to fly without a broomstick but the rest of us can’t sprout wings whenever we —"

metadata.description: I still trust Harry's lead and I expect him to decide, but I'm secretly thinking only certain friends should join; my loyalty is to the small trusted group even when others volunteer.
metadata.source_text: Harry's eyes met Ron's. He knew that Ron was thinking exactly what he was: If he could have chosen any members of the D.A. in addition to himself, Ron, and Hermione to join him...

metadata.description: I learned that thestrals can fly extremely fast and launch so steeply you have to cling on or you'll slide off; they streak over great distances and can take you straight to the Ministry's visitors' entrance.
metadata.source_text: Then, with a sweeping movement that nearly unseated him, the wings on either side extended, the horse crouched slowly and then rocketed upward so fast and so steeply that Harry had to clench his arms and legs tightly around the horse to avoid sliding backward over its bony rump.

metadata.description: I used to think flying on thestrals would be impossible to manage, but after doing it I know I can ride them even though it's terrifying — I still hope nobody ever makes me do that again.
metadata.source_text: "Never again," he said, struggling to his feet. ... "Never, ever again . . . that was the worst —"

metadata.description: I feel responsible for the others; leading them into the Ministry made me aware that they're relying on me and I'm prepared to take charge, even when my scar's hurting and I'm uneasy.
metadata.source_text: “Come on,” said Harry quietly and the six of them sprinted off down the hall, Harry in the lead, past the fountain, toward the desk where the security man who had weighed Harry’s wand had sat and which was now deserted.

metadata.description: I've learned that the Ministry's visitors' entrance requires identification and wand registration; there are visitor badges and a routine search at the security desk.
metadata.source_text: “Visitors, please take the badges and attach them to the front of your robes.” ... “Visitor to the Ministry, you are required to submit to a search and present your wand for registration at the security desk, which is located at the far end of the Atrium.”

metadata.description: I feel unsettled: seeing the Department of Mysteries and those odd specimens has made me more anxious than usual — I don't expect what's behind scientific glass to be ordinary.
metadata.source_text: She sounded odd. She moved forward to look through the side of the tank.

metadata.description: I'm silently trusting Harry's leadership; despite my worry, I'm following his lead into the Ministry because the situation seems urgent and we must act together.
metadata.source_text: Hermione, Neville, and Luna squashed themselves in after them; Harry took one glance back at the thestrals... then forced himself into the box after Luna.

metadata.description: That whole thestral flight is mad and frightening — I discovered how horrible it feels to ride an invisible horse up in the sky with nothing to see.
metadata.source_text: “This is mad,” Ron said faintly, moving his free hand gingerly up and down his horse’s neck.

metadata.description: I didn't expect to be so terrified; I reckon I never want to fly like that again — I'm serious, never again.
metadata.source_text: “Never again,” he said, struggling to his feet. ... “Never, ever again . . . that was the worst —”

metadata.description: I'm sticking with Harry and the others; even when I'm frightened I follow along and help where I can, like dialing the telephone box number under pressure.
metadata.source_text: “Whoever’s nearest the receiver, dial six two four four two!” he said. Ron did it, his arm bent bizarrely to reach the dial.

metadata.description: I heard whispering through that tattered black veil and felt like somebody was standing just the other side of the archway.
metadata.source_text: There were faint whispering, murmuring noises coming from the other side of the veil.

metadata.description: I kept thinking Sirius might be captured and tortured; seeing the archway made me picture him bound and I couldn't stop myself from believing he might be really close.
metadata.source_text: And then something slid back into place in his brain: Sirius, captured, bound, and tortured, and he was staring at this archway.

metadata.description: I want to find Sirius more than anything; Hermione nags me to leave but I keep being pulled toward anything that might show he's nearby.
metadata.source_text: Harry, we are supposed to be here for Sirius!" she said in a high-pitched, strained voice.

metadata.description: I've learned that 'Flagrate' will mark a door with a fiery X to keep track of which doorway we've already tried.
metadata.source_text: She drew with her wand in midair and a fiery X appeared on the door.

metadata.description: I now think that archway with the veil is dangerous; whatever it is, it's not safe for us to approach and we should get away from it.
metadata.source_text: I don't know, but whatever it was, it was dangerous," she said firmly, again inscribing a fiery cross upon the door.

metadata.description: I feel responsible for keeping the others safe; I grabbed Ginny and Neville and marched them back because I couldn't let Harry keep going toward that veil.
metadata.source_text: Without speaking, Hermione took hold of Ginny's arm, Ron Neville's, and they marched them firmly back to the lowest stone bench

metadata.description: I can hear the whispering from the other side of the veil too; I turned up beside the archway and said I was there.
metadata.source_text: "I'm here, mate," said Ron, appearing around the side of the archway.

metadata.description: I share Harry and Luna's sense that something's inside the archway; I didn't dismiss their feeling when I joined them.
metadata.source_text: "I can hear them too," breathed Luna, joining them around the side of the archway and gazing at the swaying veil.

metadata.description: I'm with Harry and the others in trying to find Sirius; showing up at the archway with Harry makes me part of the search and I back him up.
metadata.source_text: "I'm here, mate," said Ron, appearing around the side of the archway.

metadata.description: I found a dusty glass ball with my name on the shelf, labeled from about sixteen years ago, so my name is actually recorded there on a yellowed label.
metadata.source_text:
It’s — it’s got your name on,

"My name?" said Harry blankly.

In spidery writing was written a date of some sixteen years previously, and below that: S. P. T. to A. P. W. B. D. Dark Lord and (?) Harry Potter

Harry stared at it.

metadata.description: I felt certain Sirius must have been here, but when I ran the aisles and found no sign of him or any struggle, I started to realise he might not be here after all.
metadata.source_text: I don’t think Sirius is here.” Nobody spoke. Harry did not want to look at any of them. He felt sick. He did not understand why Sirius was not here. He had to be here.

metadata.description: When Ron pointed out the orb and I felt the others' eyes, I felt the heat rising in my face and wanted to hide from their looks; being with Ron, Hermione and Neville made me want to shrink away rather than face them.
metadata.source_text:
The heat was rising in his face and he felt as though he would like to skulk down here in the darkness for a long while before facing the brightness of the Atrium above and the others’ accusing stares.

"Harry?" Ron called.

metadata.description: I saw a dusty glass orb with Harry's name on the shelf and I knew immediately he shouldn't touch it, so I've learned that some objects here are dangerous enough to warn against touching.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, I don’t think you should touch it," said Hermione sharply, as he stretched out his hand.

metadata.description: Seeing Harry reach for the orb made me more convinced we must be cautious; I'm more worried now that impulsive actions could get him into trouble.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, I don’t think you should touch it," said Hermione sharply, as he stretched out his hand.

metadata.description: When I warned Harry not to touch the ball, it made me feel protective and responsible toward him; I felt I must intervene even when he won't listen.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, I don’t think you should touch it," said Hermione sharply, as he stretched out his hand.

metadata.description: I noticed a dusty glass sphere on the shelf that had Harry's name on a label, so I learned there's a ball here explicitly marked with his name and an old date.
metadata.source_text:
"Have you seen this?" said Ron. "It's — it's got your name on," said Ron.

He was pointing at one of the small glass spheres...

metadata.description: At first I called Harry and expected him to be annoyed, but seeing the orb with his name on it made me uneasy; I'm less casual about these finds now because they feel ominous.
metadata.source_text:
"What?" Ron called. "Have you seen this?" ... "It's — it's got your name on," said Ron.

"What is it?" Ron asked, sounding unnerved.

metadata.description: Pointing out the orb to Harry made me realise I care enough to get involved when something might affect him; I'm more watchful over him in strange situations.
metadata.source_text: "Have you seen this?" said Ron. "It's — it's got your name on," said Ron.

metadata.description: I found out that the prophecy I grabbed is about me and Voldemort — that only people mentioned in a prophecy can legally retrieve it from the Department of Mysteries.
metadata.source_text: Because the only people who are permitted to retrieve a prophecy from the Department of Mysteries, Potter, are those about whom it was made, as the Dark Lord discovered when he attempted to use others to steal it for him.

metadata.description: I'm beginning to believe that Voldemort used my dreams to lure me to the Department — he wanted me to fetch the prophecy for him rather than go himself.
metadata.source_text: He thought natural curiosity would make you want to hear the exact wording . . .

metadata.description: I feel even more certain now that Malfoy and the Death Eaters will obey Voldemort's orders and are dangerous; Malfoy plays the polite part while commanding fear.
metadata.source_text: Now give me the prophecy, Potter.

metadata.description: I've learned that smashing shelves can release the glass prophecy spheres and the Seers inside them, causing chaos that can be used as cover to escape.
metadata.source_text: — when I say go —  — when I say go —  — you didn’t come running when he showed you the place where it was hidden in your dreams. He thought natural curiosity would make you want to hear the exact wording . . .

metadata.description: I'm terrified and shaken by how close we came to being caught and hurt, and I'm more certain than ever that stealth and quick thinking matter in these moments.
metadata.source_text: They were almost there when Harry heard something large and heavy collide with the door Hermione had charmed shut.

metadata.description: I trust Harry's quick decisions under pressure — when he yelled 'RUN!' and dragged me forward I followed without question, even though I was terrified.
metadata.source_text: RUN!" Harry yelled, and as the shelves swayed precariously and more glass spheres began to pour from above, he seized a handful of Hermione’s robes and dragged her forward

metadata.description: I realised we can disarm and chase wands back in the Hall — when Neville cried 'EXPELLIARMUS!' both wands flew and were sent toward the Hall of Prophecy entrance.
metadata.source_text: EXPELLIARMUS!" Both Harry’s and the Death Eater’s wands flew out of their hands and soared back toward the entrance to the Hall of Prophecy;

metadata.description: I'm more worried than ever about how dangerous these missions are; getting involved with Voldemort's followers nearly got us killed.
metadata.source_text: They were trapped and outnumbered two to one.

metadata.description: I feel fiercely protective of my friends in a scrap — seeing Harry and the others fight and run makes me more ready to stand by them no matter how scary it gets.
metadata.source_text: They were all yelling, there were cries of pain, thunderous crashes as the shelves collapsed upon themselves

metadata.description: I learned that petrificus totalus can stop even dangerous Death Eaters quickly when I hit Dolohov and another one with it during the attack.
metadata.source_text: “Petrificus Totalus!” shouted Harry, as the second Death Eater raised his wand.

metadata.description: I used to think shouting out might help, but I realised shouting gave away our position and made things worse for us.
metadata.source_text: Harry could hear more footsteps growing louder from the Hall of Prophecy they had just left and knew, too late, that he ought not to have shouted and given away their position.

metadata.description: I felt responsible for Hermione when she was hit and panicked that I’d let her down, which made me desperate to protect my friends even more.
metadata.source_text: Don’t let her be dead, don’t let her be dead, it’s my fault if she’s dead. . . . “Hermione,” Harry said at once, shaking her as the baby-headed Death Eater blundered out of sight again.

metadata.description: I proved that a Silencio can render an enemy unable to speak, which buys crucial seconds in a fight.
metadata.source_text: “Silencio!” cried Hermione, and the man’s voice was extinguished.

metadata.description: I realised I still react with awed disbelief at dangerous magic — even I said, “It’s time,” in an awestruck voice when the head began changing.
metadata.source_text: “It’s time,” said Hermione in an awestruck voice. “Time . . .”

metadata.description: I grabbed Harry’s arm to stop him from attacking the baby-headed Death Eater because I couldn’t let him hurt what looked like a baby, showing I trust our moral choices even under pressure.
metadata.source_text: Harry raised his wand but to his amazement Hermione seized his arm. “You can’t hurt a baby!”

metadata.description: I found that the Reductor Curse can be used in a pinch to blow things up — I used it to try to protect Ginny when she was grabbed.
metadata.source_text: “I used the Reductor Curse and blew up Pluto in his face, but . . .”

metadata.description: I reckon I’m not as steady in an attack as I thought — I ended up dazed and giggling, which was worrying for everyone.
metadata.source_text: Ron’s face was very white and something dark was trickling from the corner of his mouth. Next moment his knees had given way, but he still clutched the front of Harry’s robes... “There you are. . . . Ha ha ha . . . You look funny, Harry. . . . You’re all messed up . . .”

metadata.description: Even when I’m knocked about and a bit odd, I still cling to Harry — I grabbed his robes as soon as I saw him, showing we’re still together through all this.
metadata.source_text: Ron, giggling weakly, lurching forward, seizing the front of Harry’s robes and gazing at him with unfocused eyes.

metadata.description: I learned that the prophecy is precious and dangerous — I had to keep it safe at all costs, holding it above my head to stop the Death Eaters touching it.
metadata.source_text: Holding the prophecy high above his head he sprinted back up the room; all he could think of doing was to draw the Death Eaters away from the others.

metadata.description: I believed I could save Sirius if I reached him, but after he fell through the veil I realized, painfully, that some things are beyond my power to fix immediately.
metadata.source_text: He was laughing at her. 'Come on, you can do better than that!' ... The second jet of light hit him squarely on the chest. ... His body curved in a graceful arc as he sank backward through the ragged veil ... 'There’s nothing you can do, Harry —'

metadata.description: I feel a deeper, raw grief for Sirius; he was more than an ally — he was family to me, and losing him through that veil has changed how empty I feel inside.
metadata.source_text: Harry yelled, 'SIRIUS!' ... Harry's breath was coming in searing gasps. ... 'There’s nothing you can do, Harry —' 'It’s too late, Harry —'

metadata.description: I wasn't present to act in this scene, so I don't have direct knowledge from being there.
I wasn't there to change any beliefs based on witnessing events directly in this scene.
I wasn't present, so I didn't update my opinion of anyone from firsthand experience during these events.
I discovered that grabbing a thinking brain is a dreadful idea — it wrapped me in tentacles and nearly strangled me; brains in tanks are not for playing with.
metadata.source_text: Ron had already caught the brain in his outstretched hands. The moment they made contact with his skin, the tentacles began wrapping themselves around Ron’s arms like ropes.

metadata.description: I laughed and joked even while hurt — I felt daft and giggly, but the danger made me realise being careless can get you badly hurt.
metadata.source_text: There you are. . . . Ha ha ha . . . You look funny, Harry. . . . You’re all messed up . . . 'Ha ha ha, Harry, look at it —' said Ron, watching it disgorge its gaudy innards.

metadata.description: When I clung to Harry in that mess and babbled about Uranus, I realized how much I rely on him — he's the one I grab onto when I'm scared or barely conscious.
metadata.source_text: There you are. . . . Ha ha ha . . . You look funny, Harry. . . . You’re all messed up . . . Ron’s face was very white and something dark was trickling from the corner of his mouth.

metadata.description: I found the Atrium corridor and the telephone lifts by running through the passage when the hidden door opened — the corridor to the lifts was torch-lit and empty and led straight to the lifts.
metadata.source_text: The door right behind him flew open, and the corridor toward the lifts stretched ahead of him, torch-lit and empty.
metadata.scene_title: Escape through the Atrium to the Lifts and the Confrontation with Bellatrix

metadata.description: I felt a hatred like I'd never known before; my feelings toward Bellatrix hardened in an instant and I couldn't hold back — I lashed out with Crucio because I wanted her punished.
metadata.source_text: Hatred rose in Harry such as he had never known before. He flung himself out from behind the fountain and bellowed “Crucio!”
metadata.scene_title: Escape through the Atrium to the Lifts and the Confrontation with Bellatrix

metadata.description: I know now that Bellatrix is cruel and taunting — she mocks me in a baby voice and tries to bait me, so I see her as someone who delights in torment and must be stopped.
metadata.source_text: “Come out, come out, little Harry!” she called in her mock-baby voice... “Aaaaaah . . . did you love him, little baby Potter?”
metadata.scene_title: Escape through the Atrium to the Lifts and the Confrontation with Bellatrix

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Atrium, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Escape through the Atrium to the Lifts and the Confrontation with Bellatrix

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Atrium, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Escape through the Atrium to the Lifts and the Confrontation with Bellatrix

metadata.description: I found out the prophecy I thought I might loose was smashed during the struggle and can't be summoned: there's nothing to Accio, it's gone.
metadata.source_text: The prophecy smashed when I was trying to get Neville up the steps! ... "Nothing there!" he shouted. "Nothing to summon! It smashed and nobody heard what it said, tell your boss that —"
metadata.scene_title: Fight Escalates — Scar Pain, Voldemort’s Arrival, and the Attempted Killing Curse

metadata.description: I realised Voldemort now knows the prophecy's fate; my scar screamed and I knew, horribly clearly, that he would be furious about it.
metadata.source_text: And he knows! ... "Your dear old mate Voldemort knows it’s gone! He’s not going to be happy with you, is he?"
metadata.scene_title: Fight Escalates — Scar Pain, Voldemort’s Arrival, and the Attempted Killing Curse

metadata.description: I see Bellatrix as terrified beneath her fury; she isn't just wild, she's scared of what Voldemort will do to her for failing him.
metadata.source_text: "What? What do you mean?" she cried, and for the first time there was fear in her voice. ... "LIAR!" she shrieked, but he could hear the terror behind the anger now.
metadata.scene_title: Fight Escalates — Scar Pain, Voldemort’s Arrival, and the Attempted Killing Curse

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the scene, so I can't report Hermione's actions or words from the fountain confrontation.
metadata.scene_title: Fight Escalates — Scar Pain, Voldemort’s Arrival, and the Attempted Killing Curse

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the scene, so I don't know what Ron did or said during the fight at the fountain.
metadata.scene_title: Fight Escalates — Scar Pain, Voldemort’s Arrival, and the Attempted Killing Curse

metadata.description: I saw Voldemort appear in the middle of the hall with his wand pointing at me; he spoke to me and called me responsible for his smashed prophecy.
metadata.source_text: Lord Voldemort had appeared in the middle of the hall, his wand pointing at Harry who stood frozen, quite unable to move. “So you smashed my prophecy?” said Voldemort softly, staring at Harry with those pitiless red eyes.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore’s Arrival — Statues Protect Harry and Duel with Voldemort

metadata.description: I felt utterly helpless — my mind was blank and I couldn't move or raise my wand when he cast Avada Kedavra, so my idea that I could always act in a crisis was shaken.
metadata.source_text: Harry had not even opened his mouth to resist. His mind was blank, his wand pointing uselessly at the floor.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore’s Arrival — Statues Protect Harry and Duel with Voldemort

metadata.description: I realised Dumbledore would come to protect me — when the headless statue saved me and Dumbledore appeared and summoned the other statues, I knew he was there to defend me.
metadata.source_text: But the headless golden statue of the wizard in the fountain had sprung alive, leaping from its plinth, and landed on the floor with a crash between Harry and Voldemort... Dumbledore was standing in front of the golden gates.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore’s Arrival — Statues Protect Harry and Duel with Voldemort

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the Ministry, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore’s Arrival — Statues Protect Harry and Duel with Voldemort

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the Ministry, so I can't describe the events as an eyewitness.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore’s Arrival — Statues Protect Harry and Duel with Voldemort

metadata.description: I learned that when Voldemort fires that green light it can shatter living creatures — I watched the centaur take the blast and smash into a hundred pieces.
metadata.source_text: Another jet of green light flew from behind the silver shield. This time it was the one-armed centaur, galloping in front of Dumbledore, that took the blast and shattered into a hundred pieces
metadata.scene_title: Climax of the Duel — Possession, Relief, and Arrival of Reinforcements

metadata.description: I used to feel Dumbledore was almost untouchable, calm as ever, but seeing him sound frightened and order me to stay showed me even he can be alarmed — I now realise he's not always unshakable.
metadata.source_text: For the first time, Dumbledore sounded frightened. Harry could not see why. ... 'Stay where you are, Harry!'
metadata.scene_title: Climax of the Duel — Possession, Relief, and Arrival of Reinforcements

metadata.description: I feel more terrified and helpless toward Voldemort than ever — when he used me to beg Dumbledore to kill me, I understood how utterly dangerous and cruel he is to others and to me.
metadata.source_text: ‘Kill me now, Dumbledore . . .’ Blinded and dying, every part of him screaming for release, Harry felt the creature use him again. . . . 'If death is nothing, Dumbledore, kill the boy . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Climax of the Duel — Possession, Relief, and Arrival of Reinforcements

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the duel in the Great Hall, so I don't have direct knowledge of what occurred there.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the duel in the Great Hall, so I don't have direct knowledge of what occurred there.
metadata.scene_title: Climax of the Duel — Possession, Relief, and Arrival of Reinforcements
