metadata.description: I saw that the Atrium filled with witches and wizards emerging through the fireplaces which had burst into emerald-green flames, and Cornelius Fudge was brought forward looking stunned and out of breath.
metadata.source_text: The Atrium was full of people. The floor was reflecting emerald-green flames that had burst into life in all the fireplaces along one wall, and a stream of witches and wizards was emerging from them.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Dumbledore Reprimands the Ministry and Arranges Explanations

metadata.description: I understand now that Lord Voldemort has returned — Dumbledore says he's been right for a year and that the Ministry has been chasing the wrong men, so I can't pretend the Ministry is in control anymore.
metadata.source_text: Lord Voldemort has returned, you have been chasing the wrong men for twelve months, and it is time you listened to sense!
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Dumbledore Reprimands the Ministry and Arranges Explanations

metadata.description: Dumbledore is standing very close to me and taking charge; I feel protected by him — he pulled me to my feet and is sending me back to Hogwarts himself, so I trust him completely right now.
metadata.source_text: As Dumbledore pulled him back to his feet, Harry saw the tiny gold statues... 'Take this Portkey, Harry.' He held out the golden head of the statue, and Harry placed his hand upon it
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Dumbledore Reprimands the Ministry and Arranges Explanations

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the Ministry Atrium, so I did not witness the duel, the arrivals from the fireplaces, or Dumbledore's confrontation with Fudge.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Dumbledore Reprimands the Ministry and Arranges Explanations

metadata.description: I was not present during the scene at the Ministry, so I didn't see Voldemort, Dumbledore's speech to Fudge, or Harry being sent back to Hogwarts by Portkey.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath — Dumbledore Reprimands the Ministry and Arranges Explanations

metadata.description: I've found out that the Ministry finally admitted You-Know-Who is back and that the dementors have revolted and are siding with him.
metadata.source_text: It is with great regret that I must confirm that the wizard styling himself Lord — well, you know who I mean — is alive and among us again,

metadata.description: I know now that people are starting to believe me because everyone’s talking about You-Know-Who again; the world’s shifted and I’m being listened to more.
metadata.source_text: 'Yes, they’re very complimentary about you now, Harry,' said Hermione, now scanning down the article.

metadata.description: I feel more distant from Snape than ever — I hate him for what I think he did and I don’t see myself forgiving him any time soon.
metadata.source_text: At the sight of him Harry felt a great rush of hatred beyond anything he felt toward Malfoy. . . . Whatever Dumbledore said, he would never forgive Snape . . . never . . .

metadata.description: I've read that the Prophet ran articles calling Harry a lone voice of truth who was ridiculed and slandered, though they omit that the paper did the slandering.
metadata.source_text: 'A lone voice of truth . . . perceived as unbalanced, yet never wavered in his story . . . forced to bear ridicule and slander . . . ' Hmmm," said Hermione, frowning, "I notice they don’t mention the fact that it was them doing all the ridiculing and slandering, though . . .'

metadata.description: I'm less patient with the Ministry’s denials; Dumbledore was right and people are finally being forced to accept that You-Know-Who might be back.
metadata.source_text: He has insisted for a year that You-Know-Who was not dead, as was widely hoped and believed, but recruiting followers once more for a fresh attempt to seize power.

metadata.description: I’m worried about Harry and I want to go with him to see Hagrid, but I’m also angry that he’s keeping important things from us.
metadata.source_text: "Say hello to him for us!" called Hermione, as Harry proceeded down the ward.

metadata.description: I've heard from the paper and everyone that Harry’s being called the Boy Who Lived again and people are writing loads about his part in all this.
metadata.source_text: The Boy Who Lived — 'There you are, Harry, I knew they’d drag you into it somehow,' said Hermione, looking over the top of the paper at him.

metadata.description: I reckon things have calmed down at school now Dumbledore’s back; Filch’s miserable and Umbridge’s out of things, so school’s sorta gone back to normal.
metadata.source_text: "Yes," said Neville, "everything’s settled right back down again."

metadata.description: I’m proud of Fred and George doing well with the joke shop — seems they’re doing all right and people are sending me Chocolate Frogs because of it.
metadata.source_text: "They sent me all these, you know," he told Harry, pointing at the small mountain of Frogs beside him. "Must be doing all right out of that joke shop, eh?"

metadata.description: I found a two-way mirror from Sirius with a note saying he has the other one and I can say his name into it to talk to him.
metadata.source_text: This is a two-way mirror. I’ve got the other. If you need to speak to me, just say my name into it; you’ll appear in my mirror and I’ll be able to talk in yours.

metadata.description: I believed Sirius would come back as a ghost because he’s a wizard and he’d never have stayed away from fighting, but Nick told me Sirius will have gone on, and that’s changed my hope into confusion and grief.
metadata.source_text: He won’t come back. ... He will have . . . gone on.

metadata.description: Talking to Nick made me realise ghosts aren’t like the living; I feel more desperately alone and more aware that Sirius isn’t likely to come back to walk around Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: He will not come back," repeated Nick quietly. "He will have . . . gone on."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the corridors and classrooms described, so I don't know what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the corridors and classrooms described, so I don't know what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I heard Luna say her mother died when Luna was nine because a spell went wrong. She mentioned she still feels sad but expects to see her mother again.
metadata.source_text: "Yes," said Luna simply, "my mother. She was a quite extraordinary witch, you know, but she did like to experiment and one of her spells went rather badly wrong one day. I was nine."

metadata.description: I feel less connected to my old wish to impress Cho now — after Sirius died I found that wanting her seems part of a past I’m no longer in.
metadata.source_text: "Harry was surprised to find that this information did not hurt at all. Wanting to impress Cho seemed to belong to a past that was no longer quite connected with him."

metadata.description: I don't mind Luna talking about Sirius; even though she's odd, I realize we share knowing about thestrals and her kindness makes me accept her company more readily.
metadata.source_text: "Harry nodded curtly, but found that for some reason he did not mind Luna talking about Sirius. He had just remembered that she too could see thestrals."

metadata.description: I've read that the Daily Prophet is full of advice about repelling dementors and reports about tracking down Death Eaters; the paper shows how the Ministry and newspapers are reacting now.
metadata.source_text: "It was now full of articles about how to repel dementors, attempts by the Ministry to track down Death Eaters, and hysterical letters claiming that the writer had seen Lord Voldemort walking past their house that very morning."

metadata.description: I'm gloomier about the situation; I think things haven't really started yet but I expect the danger will escalate soon, which makes me worry for the coming term.
metadata.source_text: "'It hasn't really started yet,' sighed Hermione gloomily, folding up the newspaper again. 'But it won't be long now...'"

metadata.description: I've noticed Harry seems distant since Sirius's death; I'm aware his priorities have shifted and I accept that his feelings about Cho aren't what they were before.
metadata.source_text: "Harry was surprised to find that this information did not hurt at all. Wanting to impress Cho seemed to belong to a past that was no longer quite connected with him."

metadata.description: I've learned from Ginny that Michael Corner sulked after Gryffindor beat Ravenclaw at Quidditch and that she ditched him, so Michael went off to comfort Cho.
metadata.source_text: "'Michael Corner,' she said. 'Michael — but —' said Ron... 'Not anymore,' said Ginny resolutely. 'He didn't like Gryffindor beating Ravenclaw at Quidditch and got really sulky, so I ditched him and he ran off to comfort Cho instead.'"

metadata.description: I reckon Harry's better off without Cho; I told him he's well out of it because he should pick someone more cheerful than Cho for his own sake.
metadata.source_text: "'You're well out of it, mate,' said Ron forcefully. 'I mean, she's quite good-looking and all that, but you want someone a bit more cheerful.'"

metadata.description: I'm proud of Ginny for dumping Michael — I always thought he was an idiot — and I'm pleased she might choose someone better next time.
metadata.source_text: "'Well, I always thought he was a bit of an idiot,' he said, prodding his queen forward... 'Good for you. Just choose someone — better — next time.'"

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the scene described in the Ministry newspapers, so I don't have direct knowledge of what the Obliviator said or the exact details of the Hall of Prophecy disturbance.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events reported at the Ministry and thus cannot report firsthand what happened in the Hall of Prophecy or what the Obliviator meant.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there when the disturbance at the Ministry happened, so I don't know personally whether Death Eaters tried to steal a prophecy or what was actually taken.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events described in that room, so I don't have first-hand observations of the owl, trunk, or leaflet.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there for the scene inside the room and therefore didn't witness the owl, the trunk, or the Ministry leaflet myself.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room when those things happened, so I can't say I saw the owl, the messy trunk, or the purple Ministry leaflet.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I slept through most of the room while my owl watched me; there was a purple Ministry leaflet on the floor giving explicit safety advice about Death Eaters, Inferi, and protective charms.
metadata.source_text: Once or twice she clicked her beak impatiently, but Harry was too deeply asleep to hear her.

metadata.description: I must accept that the Ministry is taking a tougher line and issuing public safety guidance; the presence of the leaflet shows the threat is being treated seriously by officials.
metadata.source_text: The Wizarding community is currently under threat from an organization calling itself the Death Eaters. Observing the following simple security guidelines will help protect you, your family, and your home from attack.

metadata.description: I know that Neville is regarded as a friend of mine and a fellow fighter against Death Eaters, because Mrs. Longbottom referred to him as my good friend who fought at the Ministry.
metadata.source_text: My grandson, Neville — a good friend of Harry Potter’s, incidentally, who fought the Death Eaters alongside him at the Ministry in June and —

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events described in the room with the owl, the trunk, and the Ministry leaflet, so I don't know those immediate details.
I wasn't at the scene with Harry, the snowy owl, and the purple Ministry leaflet, so I can't report on what happened in that room.
I've read Dumbledore's letter so many times I can say it by heart: he plans to call at Number Four, Privet Drive this Friday at eleven P.M. to take me to the Burrow and wants my help on the way.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, If it is convenient to you, I shall call at number four, Privet Drive this coming Friday at eleven P.M. to escort you to the Burrow, where you have been invited to spend the remainder of your school holidays. If you are agreeable, I should also be glad of your assistance in a matter to which I hope to attend on the way to the Burrow.

metadata.description: I've sent my ‘yes’ back by owl, so I've stopped imagining changing Dumbledore's mind; now I've accepted that all I can do is wait and see if he actually arrives.
metadata.source_text: Harry had sent back his “yes” with the delivering owl, as requested, and all he could do now was wait: Either Dumbledore was going to come, or he was not.

metadata.description: I feel Dumbledore is someone I can rely on to arrange things for me — he invites me and asks for my help, and even without packing I trust he'll turn up to take me to the Burrow.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, ... I shall call at number four, Privet Drive this coming Friday at eleven P.M. to escort you to the Burrow, where you have been invited to spend the remainder of your school holidays. ... Hoping to see you this Friday, I am, yours most sincerely, Albus Dumbledore

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Privet Drive that night and did not witness Harry waiting by the window for Dumbledore's arrival.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events at Privet Drive that night and did not witness Harry waiting by the window for Dumbledore's arrival.

metadata.description: I wasn't there when Harry read Dumbledore's letter or when he waited by the window; I don't know the details of that night at Privet Drive.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't there when Harry read Dumbledore's letter or when he waited by the window; I don't know the details of that night at Privet Drive.

metadata.description: I know the streetlamp went out exactly when the minute hand hit twelve and that a tall cloaked man was walking up our garden path — I saw him from my window.
metadata.source_text: The minute hand on the alarm clock reached the number twelve and, at that precise moment, the streetlamp outside the window went out. ... A tall figure in a long, billowing cloak was walking up the garden path.

metadata.description: I'm suddenly convinced Dumbledore might arrive without warning and that I should have warned the Dursleys — I panicked when I remembered I hadn't told them he'd be coming.
metadata.source_text: He had completely forgotten to warn the Dursleys that Dumbledore might be coming.

metadata.description: I can see Dumbledore makes Uncle Vernon go quiet — even Vernon, who usually shouts, looks stunned and unable to bully the man, so I feel Dumbledore is someone Vernon can't push around.
metadata.source_text: It might have been the blatant wizardishness of his appearance, but it might, too, have been that even Uncle Vernon could sense that here was a man whom it would be very difficult to bully.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at Privet Drive, so I don't know what Hermione did or said here.
metadata.source_text: Characters present: Present: Harry Potter | Absent: Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at Privet Drive, so I don't know what Ron did or said here.
metadata.source_text: Characters present: Present: Harry Potter | Absent: Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I learned that Sirius's will was found and that he left me everything: gold in Gringotts, his personal things, number twelve, Grimmauld Place, and Kreacher the house-elf.
metadata.source_text: Sirius’s will was discovered a week ago and that he left you everything he owned.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains the Legacy and Grimmauld Place

metadata.description: I suddenly know I don't want to own number twelve, Grimmauld Place again; the place reminds me only of Sirius trapped there and I never want to set foot in it if I can help it.
metadata.source_text: I don't care. You can have it, I don't really want it." Harry never wanted to set foot in number twelve, Grimmauld Place again if he could help it.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains the Legacy and Grimmauld Place

metadata.description: I feel disgust and resentment toward Kreacher because he betrayed Sirius; even though I understand the danger of Kreacher going to Bellatrix, I don't want responsibility for him.
metadata.source_text: I don't care," said Harry again, looking with disgust at the writhing, stamping house-elf. "I don't want him.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains the Legacy and Grimmauld Place

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Dursleys' sitting room so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains the Legacy and Grimmauld Place

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Dursleys' sitting room so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains the Legacy and Grimmauld Place

metadata.description: I've been told that Kreacher can be sent to Hogwarts to work in the kitchens with the other house-elves — that's where he'll be going if I ask him to.
metadata.source_text: I want you to go to Hogwarts and work in the kitchens there with the other house-elves.

metadata.description: I feel relieved about finding somewhere for Kreacher to be looked after; sending him to Hogwarts seems like a sensible plan and eases my mind.
metadata.source_text: Yeah," said Harry in relief, "yeah, I’ll do that.

metadata.description: I think Buckbeak belongs with Hagrid and not with me; I believe Hagrid will care for him better and Buckbeak would prefer staying with Hagrid.
metadata.source_text: No," said Harry at once, "he can stay with Hagrid. I think Buckbeak would prefer that.

metadata.description: I was not present during this conversation and do not know the specifics of the arrangements made for Kreacher or Buckbeak.
I was not in the room for these arrangements and cannot report on what was said about Kreacher, Buckbeak, or Dumbledore's comments.
I've learned that Voldemort is now using Occlumency against me, which explains why my scar hasn't been hurting as it did before.
metadata.source_text: It appears that he is now employing Occlumency against you.

metadata.description: I've found out that Inferi are bewitched corpses put to a Dark wizard's bidding — actual dead bodies, and they were used by Voldemort when he was strong.
metadata.source_text: They are corpses. Dead bodies that have been bewitched to do a Dark wizard’s bidding.

metadata.description: I used to think my scar would be burning constantly now Voldemort is stronger, but I've changed my mind because the pain hasn't come and Dumbledore says Occlumency is why.
metadata.source_text: No, and I’ve been wondering about that. I thought it would be burning all the time now Voldemort’s getting so powerful again.

metadata.description: I feel Dumbledore is trustworthy and willing to explain things to me; he smiles and lets me keep asking questions, so I trust him more to guide me.
metadata.source_text: He smiled at Harry, who understood that he was not being snubbed, and that he had permission to keep asking questions.

metadata.description: I was not present during this errand with Dumbledore and Harry in Budleigh Babberton, so I did not witness the visit to Horace Slughorn.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't with them on Dumbledore's late-night visit to Horace Slughorn, so I don't know what exactly happened inside the house.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I noticed Professor Dumbledore wearing a large gold ring with a cracked black stone on his uninjured hand.
metadata.source_text: I noticed a ring on his uninjured hand that he had never seen Dumbledore wear before: It was large, rather clumsily made of what looked like gold, and was set with a heavy black stone that had cracked down the middle.

metadata.description: I learned from Slughorn that Horace has been avoiding staying in one place, moving between Muggle houses and using a Freezing Charm on burglar alarms.
metadata.source_text: I’ve been on the move for a year. Never stay in one place more than a week. Move from Muggle house to Muggle house ... one simple Freezing Charm on these absurd burglar alarms

metadata.description: I feel a bit uneasy seeing Dumbledore’s burned fingertips and that cracked ring — it made the back of my neck prickle.
metadata.source_text: the sight of them made the back of Harry’s neck prickle unpleasantly.

metadata.description: Slughorn clearly recognizes me as James’s son and remembers my mother fondly; he treats me with a mixture of curiosity and flattery.
metadata.source_text: You look very like your father." ... "You shouldn’t have favorites as a teacher, of course, but she was one of mine. Your mother ... Lily Evans. One of the brightest I ever taught.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this visit to Slughorn's house, so I didn't see or hear the conversation between Dumbledore, Slughorn, and Harry.
I wasn't present for the meeting at Horace Slughorn's home and therefore did not witness the dialogue about Dumbledore's ring or Slughorn's reminiscences.
I've learned that Horace Slughorn has been out of touch with everyone for a year and that he was deliberately keeping his head down to avoid danger.
metadata.source_text: I have been out of touch with everybody for a year.

metadata.description: I've started to think that being near Dumbledore might actually be safer for people like Slughorn; I can see that Dumbledore's presence discourages Voldemort from direct attacks.
metadata.source_text: I reckon the staff are safer than most people while Dumbledore’s headmaster; he’s supposed to be the only one Voldemort ever feared, isn’t he?

metadata.description: I realise Slughorn will try to collect me as a prized connection — he'd want me in his circle because I'm known as 'the Boy Who Lived' and that makes me valuable to him.
metadata.source_text: He will undoubtedly try to collect you, Harry. You would be the jewel of his collection; ‘the Boy Who Lived’ . . . or, as they call you these days, ‘the Chosen One.’

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Slughorn's home, so I don't know what was said or done there.
metadata.source_text: I have been out of touch with everybody for a year.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the visit to Horace Slughorn, so I didn't witness the conversation or decision for him to return to Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: I have been out of touch with everybody for a year.

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore had managed to persuade Slughorn to help and that Dumbledore brought me to the Burrow late at night.
metadata.source_text: "We were lucky," said Dumbledore, ushering Harry over the threshold. "Slughorn proved much more persuadable than I had expected. Harry's doing, of course."

metadata.description: I noticed Tonks looked drawn and less colourful than usual; her hair wasn't bubble-gum-pink and she left quickly, vanishing in a hurry.
metadata.source_text: "Harry thought she looked drawn, even ill, and there was something forced in her smile. Certainly her appearance was less colorful than usual without her customary shade of bubble-gum-pink hair."

metadata.description: I'm more aware now of how dangerous things are: the Weasley clock showing 'mortal peril' makes me feel that everyone is at real risk since You-Know-Who returned.
metadata.source_text: "Every single one of its nine hands was now pointing at 'mortal peril.'"

metadata.description: I feel grateful and comforted by Mrs Weasley's care; she fusses over me, gives me hot soup, and puts me in Fred and George's room for the night.
metadata.source_text: "Harry! We didn't expect you until morning!" ... "I've got Fred and George's room all ready for you, you'll have it to yourself."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the Burrow; I did not see Dumbledore, Tonks, or the Weasleys that night.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there for Dumbledore's late visit or the conversation about counterfeit protective items; I did not witness Tonks leaving or Arthur's arrival.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I've found a Puking Pastille in my pillowcase — a sticky purple-and-orange sweet — which surprised me when I groped inside the pillow.
metadata.source_text: There was something hard inside the pillowcase. He groped inside it and pulled out a sticky purple-and-orange sweet, which he recognized as a Puking Pastille.

metadata.description: I learned that Horace Slughorn is the name of the teacher Dumbledore wanted me to persuade to come out of retirement.
metadata.source_text: He just wanted me to help him persuade this old teacher to come out of retirement. His name’s Horace Slughorn.

metadata.description: I noticed that Slughorn used to be Head of Slytherin and that he looks a bit like a walrus — that’s how I described him when Ron asked what he was like.
metadata.source_text: He looks a bit like a walrus, and he used to be Head of Slytherin.

metadata.description: I'm thinking Slughorn can't be any worse than Umbridge as a teacher; after what we had with her, my standards for 'good enough' have dropped a bit.
metadata.source_text: He can’t be worse than Umbridge, can he?

metadata.description: I noticed Fleur Delacour kissing me on both cheeks and calling me '’Arry' in her French way; she seems very taken with me and with Bill's family, which made things a bit awkward.
metadata.source_text: setting the tray across Harry’s knees and then swooping to kiss him on each cheek ... “I ’ave been longing to see ’im. You remember my seester, Gabrielle? ... She will be delighted to see you again.”

metadata.description: I've been scrutinizing Harry like he might be sick — I'm clearly worried about him after recent events and watching for any sign of trouble.
metadata.source_text: Oh, I’m fine," said Hermione, who was scrutinizing Harry as though he was sickening for something.

metadata.description: I'm convinced people are behaving oddly because of the return of You-Know-Who; there's a sense that decisions are being rushed, which worries me.
metadata.source_text: It’s all this uncertainty with You-Know-Who coming back, people think they might be dead tomorrow, so they’re rushing all sorts of decisions they’d normally take time over.

metadata.description: I've joined Ginny in being critical of Mrs. Weasley's manner at times; I slipped into a lowered voice to call her 'so full of herself' when criticizing how she talks to Ginny.
metadata.source_text: I know," said Hermione, dropping her voice. "She’s so full of herself."

metadata.description: I found out Harry got to the Burrow about one o'clock in the morning; Mum only told us recently so I was surprised he was already there.
metadata.source_text: When did you get here? Mum’s only just told us!" "About one o’clock this morning.

metadata.description: I thought Harry's trip would be more dramatic — we guessed he'd been off with Dumbledore and hoped for big news, but it turned out to be mostly persuading Slughorn.
metadata.source_text: We thought —" Hermione flashed a warning look at Ron, and Ron changed tack at top speed. "— we thought it’d be something like that." "You did?" said Harry, amused.

metadata.description: I'm annoyed at Hermione and Ginny for taking digs at Mum; when Hermione and Ginny go on about Mum I tell them to lay off her for five seconds because I'm defensive of her.
metadata.source_text: Can’t you two lay off her for five seconds?"

metadata.description: I learned my O.W.L. results: I failed Divination and History of Magic, but I passed everything else, even getting Outstanding in Defence Against the Dark Arts.
metadata.source_text: Harry James Potter has achieved: ... Defense Against the Dark Arts O ... History of Magic D ... Divination P

metadata.description: I feel properly relieved about my exams; I always expected to fail Divination and knew History was bad, but seeing all the other passes made me breathe easier.
metadata.source_text: Harry read the parchment through several times, his breathing becoming easier with each reading. It was all right: He had always known that he would fail Divination, and he had had no chance of passing History of Magic

metadata.description: I'm pleased with Ron — he celebrates with me, punches my shoulder, and acts chummy; it makes me feel like we're doing alright together.
metadata.source_text: Knew you’d be top at Defense Against the Dark Arts," said Ron, punching Harry on the shoulder. "We’ve done all right, haven’t we?

metadata.description: I've found out my O.W.L. results: nine Outstandings and one Exceeds Expectations, which is excellent though I still panic about any mistakes I made.
metadata.source_text: Yep — nine ‘Outstandings’ and one ‘Exceeds Expectations’ at Defense Against the Dark Arts.

metadata.description: I convinced myself I'd failed everything and was hysterical, but seeing my results should show me I haven't failed; I need to calm down and be rational about my performance.
metadata.source_text: I know I’ve failed everything! ... "I — not bad," said Hermione in a small voice.

metadata.description: I still care about Tonks and worry for her; I believe Tonks is suffering from survivor's guilt and losing confidence in her Metamorphmagi abilities.
metadata.source_text: That’s not the point," said Hermione. "She thinks it was her fault he died! ... She’s actually having trouble with her Metamorphosing!"

metadata.description: I've seen my own O.W.L. results and I'm pleased — seven O.W.L.s is good and we’re all doing all right, even if I didn’t get any Outstandings.
metadata.source_text: Seven O.W.L.s, that’s more than Fred and George got together! ... "Only failed Divination and History of Magic, and who cares about them?" he said happily to Harry.

metadata.description: I reckon Fleur will put off most blokes; I still don't think anyone in their right mind would fancy Tonks over Fleur when Fleur's around, though I say Tonks is nicer.
metadata.source_text: Listen, no bloke in his right mind's going to fancy Tonks when Fleur's around. ... "She’s a damn sight nicer than Phlegm," said Ginny.

metadata.description: I'm proud of Hermione and a bit cheeky about her brilliance; I can't help teasing her, but I'm impressed she got so many Outstandings.
metadata.source_text: You’re actually disappointed, aren’t you?" Hermione shook her head, but Harry laughed. "Well, we’re N.E.W.T. students now!" grinned Ron.

metadata.description: I learned that Florean Fortescue, the ice-cream man from Diagon Alley, has been taken — his place looks like he was dragged off.
metadata.source_text: Dragged off, by the look of his place.
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: I feel sick about people I liked being attacked; Florean used to give me free ice creams and hearing he's been dragged off made my stomach drop.
metadata.source_text: He used to give me free ice creams. What’s happened to him?
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: I think of Florean as a good man who did kind things for me, so I now feel more personally affected and angrier about those targeting ordinary folk.
metadata.source_text: He used to give me free ice creams. What’s happened to him?
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: I found out that Igor Karkaroff’s body was discovered in a shack up north with the Dark Mark over it.
metadata.source_text: they’ve found Igor Karkaroff’s body in a shack up north. The Dark Mark had been set over it
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: I'm shaken that people like Karkaroff didn't last long after deserting the Death Eaters; it's made me realise how dangerous this is even for those who run away.
metadata.source_text: well, frankly, I’m surprised he stayed alive for even a year after deserting the Death Eaters; Sirius’s brother, Regulus, only managed a few days as far as I can remember.
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: Hearing about Ollivander being gone and Florean taken has made me see the situation as more directly threatening to ordinary wizards and shops we all know.
metadata.source_text: looks like Ollivander’s gone too.
metadata.scene_title: Birthday Tea: Horrifying News and Missing Wandmakers

metadata.description: I was not present during the birthday tea conversation, so I don't know the details of the reported Dementor attacks or the disappearances discussed.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the scene.

metadata.description: I've seen that taunting someone about their family and connections can provoke them even when they try to appear calm and reasonable.
metadata.source_text: I see that being Dumbledore’s favorite has given you a false sense of security, Harry Potter. But Dumbledore won’t always be there to protect you.
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I'm convinced Dumbledore's absence makes people braver to threaten us, and I used that to mock Narcissa because I wasn't afraid of immediate consequences.
metadata.source_text: Wow . . . look at that . . . he’s not here now! So why not have a go?
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I feel openly hostile toward the Malfoys now; I treated Narcissa and Draco as deserved targets of my insults and don't see them as sympathetic.
metadata.source_text: They might be able to find you a double cell in Azkaban with your loser of a husband!
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I've learned that when Harry points his wand in anger in public, people panic and the situation can escalate quickly, so immediate restraint is necessary.
metadata.source_text: Harry, no! ... Think. . . . You mustn’t. . . . You’ll be in such trouble. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than before that I have to physically intervene to stop Harry from acting impulsively because words alone might not calm him.
metadata.source_text: Harry, no! moaned Hermione, grabbing his arm and attempting to push it down by his side.
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I worry about how others view Harry when he acts defiantly in shops; I see him as brave but also reckless and likely to cause trouble for us all.
metadata.source_text: You mustn’t. . . . You’ll be in such trouble. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I've learned that mocking a family member will make me laugh but also makes me want to defend them fiercely when someone crosses the line.
metadata.source_text: Don’t you dare talk to my mother like that, Potter!
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I'm angrier at Harry's insult to my family than I was amused by the situation; insulting my mum makes me lose my sense of amusement and switch to protection.
metadata.source_text: Don’t you dare talk to my mother like that, Potter!
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: My loyalty to my family is sharpened; I won't tolerate slurs against Mum and I will stand up for her even against my friends if needed.
metadata.source_text: Don’t you dare talk to my mother like that, Potter!
metadata.scene_title: Madam Malkin's: Malfoy Taunts and a Shop Confrontation

metadata.description: I learned that the Malfoys think poorly of people they consider beneath them and will leave a shop in a huff rather than be associated with someone they scorn.
metadata.source_text: We’ll do better at Twilfitt and Tatting’s.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoys Leave in Contempt; Burrow Preparations

metadata.description: I feel more certain now that the Malfoys’ contempt is public and deliberate; their behaviour showed me they will make a scene to show superiority.
metadata.source_text: You’re right, Draco," said Narcissa, with a contemptuous glance at Hermione, "now I know the kind of scum that shops here. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Malfoys Leave in Contempt; Burrow Preparations

metadata.description: I've updated how I see the Malfoys — I know they're openly hostile toward me and will humiliate others to assert themselves.
metadata.source_text: You’re right, Draco," said Narcissa, with a contemptuous glance at Hermione, "now I know the kind of scum that shops here. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Malfoys Leave in Contempt; Burrow Preparations

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the exchange in Madam Malkin's shop, so I didn't see the Malfoys' confrontation or Madam Malkin's reaction.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoys Leave in Contempt; Burrow Preparations

metadata.description: I wasn't in the shop to witness the Malfoys' departure, although I am aware they deliberately bumped into Ron as they left.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoys Leave in Contempt; Burrow Preparations

I learned that the Ministry has given me top-grade security status, which is why I'm getting special transport.
metadata.source_text: He’s been given top-grade security status.

metadata.description: I feel a bit put on edge by being given special treatment; being singled out for protection makes me more aware of danger even if it's supposed to keep me safe.
metadata.source_text: He’s been given top-grade security status.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I notice the Weasleys looking out for me — they arranged the car and my protection — and that makes me feel cared for and slightly burdened by how much trouble my safety causes them.
metadata.source_text: Don’t get used to it, it’s only because of Harry," said Mr Weasley over his shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I've learned that the Ministry has upgraded Harry's protection to top-grade security and provided a special car for our travel.
metadata.source_text: He’s been given top-grade security status.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that official measures will be taken seriously for Harry's safety, though it worries me that such steps are necessary.
metadata.source_text: He’s been given top-grade security status.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I realise how much the Weasley family will bend to help Harry; their hospitality and willingness to use the Ministry car shows they stand by him practically as well as emotionally.
metadata.source_text: It’s good Dad can get us these again," said Ron appreciatively...
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I've noticed that my dad can get us special Ministry cars for trips, and they're pretty comfortable.
metadata.source_text: It’s good Dad can get us these again," said Ron appreciatively, stretching luxuriously as the car moved smoothly away from the Burrow...
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I'm pleased and a bit proud that Dad can arrange things like this; it makes me appreciate what he does for us more than I thought.
metadata.source_text: It’s good Dad can get us these again," said Ron appreciatively...
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I feel closer to Harry because the special arrangements are made on his behalf, and I like that we can share the ride together; it shows we're a proper group looking out for one another.
metadata.source_text: He, Harry, Hermione, and Ginny were all sitting in roomy comfort in the wide backseat.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing for Diagon Alley: Tension and Security

metadata.description: I've got my Invisibility Cloak in my backpack and I figured if Dumbledore trusted it, it's good enough for me to hide from notice.
metadata.source_text: He had stowed his Invisibility Cloak in his backpack and felt that, if that was good enough for Dumbledore, it ought to be good enough for the Ministry
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I'm not so sure the Ministry even knows about my Cloak anymore; I thought maybe they would, but now I reckon they might not.
metadata.source_text: though now he came to think of it, he was not sure the Ministry knew about his Cloak.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I trust Hermione and Ron to follow quick when I tell them to hide and move; they ducked under the Cloak with me when I urged them, even though Hermione hesitated.
metadata.source_text: Get under here, quick," said Harry, pulling his Invisibility Cloak out of his bag. "Oh — I don't know, Harry," said Hermione, looking uncertainly toward Mrs. Weasley. "Come on!" said Ron. She hesitated for a second longer, then ducked under the Cloak with Harry and Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I saw Malfoy turn left and I knew at once that he was heading into Knockturn Alley, because I pointed him out to Harry and the others.
metadata.source_text: "That's him, isn't it?" she whispered. "Turning left?"
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I felt unsure about ducking under the Cloak at first; I hesitated because I wasn't certain it was the right thing to do in front of Mrs. Weasley.
metadata.source_text: "Oh — I don't know, Harry," said Hermione, looking uncertainly toward Mrs. Weasley.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I rely on Harry and Ron's quick decisions when we're in a rush; though I worry about being seen, I follow their lead to keep up with them.
metadata.source_text: For Malfoy had glanced around, then slid into Knockturn Alley and out of sight. "Quick, or we'll lose him," said Harry, speeding up. "Our feet'll be seen!" said Hermione anxiously
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I know Malfoy went into Knockturn Alley because I saw him glance around and then slip away down there.
metadata.source_text: For Malfoy had glanced around, then slid into Knockturn Alley and out of sight.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I feel a bit impatient and think we should hurry after Malfoy; I was quick to urge Hermione and Harry along because I didn't want to lose him.
metadata.source_text: "Come on!" said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I'm used to following Harry's lead when he's sure of something; I chimed in and pushed Hermione along when Harry wanted to pursue Malfoy at once.
metadata.source_text: "Come on!" said Ron. She hesitated for a second longer, then ducked under the Cloak with Harry and Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Invisibility Cloak and Pursuit into Knockturn Alley

metadata.description: I noticed that most shops had no customers — buying Dark artifacts would be a giveaway in these dangerous times, so people keep away.
metadata.source_text: They peered into windows as they passed, but none of the shops seemed to have any customers at all. Harry supposed it was a bit of a giveaway in these dangerous and suspicious times to buy Dark artifacts — or at least, to be seen buying them.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: Seeing Malfoy talking inside Borgin and Burkes makes me more wary of him; being in a shop full of sinister objects with Borgin looks worrying.
metadata.source_text: There in the midst of the cases full of skulls and old bottles stood Draco Malfoy with his back to them, just visible beyond the very same large black cabinet in which Harry had once hidden to avoid Malfoy and his father.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I feel even less friendly toward Malfoy after spotting him pleased and cosy with Borgin in that sinister shop — he seems too comfortable with that kind of place.
metadata.source_text: There in the midst of the cases full of skulls and old bottles stood Draco Malfoy ... Judging by the movements of Malfoy’s hands, he was talking animatedly.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I've realised we can hear what Malfoy and Borgin say if we listen carefully; eavesdropping might give us useful information about their business.
metadata.source_text: “If only we could hear what they’re saying!” said Hermione. “We can!” said Ron excitedly.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I became more determined to find out what Malfoy was up to when I saw him inside Borgin and Burkes; his presence there makes me suspect something secretive.
metadata.source_text: They had drawn level with the only shop in Knockturn Alley that Harry had ever visited, Borgin and Burkes, which sold a wide variety of sinister objects. There in the midst of the cases full of skulls and old bottles stood Draco Malfoy...
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I feel a colder regard for Malfoy now that I saw him looking pleased in a shop of sinister things; I trust him less and want to know more about his dealings.
metadata.source_text: There in the midst of the cases full of skulls and old bottles stood Draco Malfoy with his back to them... Judging by the movements of Malfoy’s hands, he was talking animatedly.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I've learned that Extendable Ears will reach under a door if I feed their long flesh-coloured strings carefully — they work for listening in.
metadata.source_text: “Extendable Ears, look!” “Fantastic!” said Hermione, as Ron unraveled the long, flesh-colored strings and began to feed them toward the bottom of the door.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I believed we could eavesdrop successfully — I was sure the door wasn't Imperturbable and I was right when I managed to get the ears under the door.
metadata.source_text: “Oh, I hope the door isn’t Imperturbable —” “No!” said Ron gleefully. “Listen!”
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: Doing the eavesdropping made me feel useful to Harry and Hermione; I reckon they value me when I can produce something handy like Extendable Ears.
metadata.source_text: “We can!” said Ron excitedly. “Hang on — damn —” He dropped a couple more of the boxes he was still clutching as he fumbled with the largest.
metadata.scene_title: Borgin and Burkes: Spying on Malfoy

metadata.description: I noticed the Cloak flutter when the man passed so close to us, which told me he had almost discovered our hiding place.
metadata.source_text: He passed so close to Harry, Ron, and Hermione that they felt the Cloak flutter around their knees again.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I worked out that the man wanted something mended and that he also wanted to reserve or set aside an item in the shop.
metadata.source_text: “Dunno,” said Harry, thinking hard. “He wants something mended . . . and he wants to reserve something in there. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I began to suspect the man had a specific, secret interest in an object in Borgin and Burkes, so I felt more certain he wasn't an ordinary customer.
metadata.source_text: “He wants something mended . . . and he wants to reserve something in there. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I relied on Ron to keep an ear out and to tell me what he saw, so I felt more responsible for directing our little spying job and trusting my friends to help.
metadata.source_text: “Could you see what he pointed at when he said ‘that one’?”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I realised we needed to stay put and be cautious because any sudden movement could get us caught in the shop.
metadata.source_text: “You two stay here,” whispered Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I became more protective and more on-edge about the situation; I didn't want Harry and Ron moving when Borgin was already suspicious.
metadata.source_text: “You two stay here,” whispered Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I felt it was my responsibility to order Harry and Ron to be still, which made me more like the sensible leader in the moment.
metadata.source_text: “You two stay here,” whispered Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I pulled in my Extendable Ears and heard Borgin go quiet and look worried when the man came in, so I knew something odd had happened.
metadata.source_text: “What was that about?” whispered Ron, reeling in the Extendable Ears.
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I was puzzled and a bit unsettled because I couldn't see what the man pointed at, so I felt useless for a moment.
metadata.source_text: “No, he was behind that cabinet —”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I relied on Harry asking me to check details, which made me feel like I'm expected to help with the spying even when I can't see everything.
metadata.source_text: “Could you see what he pointed at when he said ‘that one’?”
metadata.scene_title: Malfoy Leaves, Borgin's Fear, and Plans to Eavesdrop

metadata.description: I saw Malfoy go into Borgin and Burkes and bully Borgin into fixing something and keeping something else for him; he made it sound like the two items belonged together.
metadata.source_text: He went into Borgin and Burkes," said Harry, "and started bullying the bloke in there, Borgin, to help him fix something. And he said he wanted Borgin to keep something else for him. He made it sound like it was the same kind of thing that needed fixing. Like they were a pair.

metadata.description: Madam Malkin reached to roll up Malfoy’s sleeve and he jumped away when she touched his left arm, so I know the odd reaction was specifically to his left arm.
metadata.source_text: We saw Malfoy jump about a mile when Madam Malkin tried to touch his left arm.

metadata.description: I now think Malfoy might be connected to the Death Eaters — I reckon he’s been branded with the Dark Mark and could even have taken his father’s place as one.
metadata.source_text: He’s a Death Eater," said Harry slowly. "He’s replaced his father as a Death Eater!

metadata.description: I’m wary of Malfoy now; I don’t trust him — he’s up to something and could be dangerous because of his family ties.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy’s father’s in Azkaban. Don’t you think Malfoy’d like revenge?

metadata.description: I’ve observed that Malfoy jerked his arm away when Madam Malkin went to roll up his sleeve; I paid attention to that detail and noted it was his left arm.
metadata.source_text: We saw Malfoy jump about a mile when Madam Malkin tried to touch his left arm.

metadata.description: I’m less convinced that Malfoy is a Death Eater recruit; I still think other explanations are possible and I remain cautious about leaping to conclusions.
metadata.source_text: It seems very unlikely, Harry," said Hermione in a repressive sort of voice. "What makes you think — ?

metadata.description: I’m skeptical of Harry’s suggestion that Malfoy has become a Death Eater; my view of Malfoy’s intentions hasn’t shifted to outright belief in his recruitment.
metadata.source_text: I think he just wanted to get out of there, Harry," said Hermione.

metadata.description: I noticed Malfoy might have been trying to avoid having his arm touched; Harry said it was his left arm that got janked away, so I’ve picked up that physical detail.
metadata.source_text: We saw Malfoy jump about a mile when Madam Malkin tried to touch his left arm.

metadata.description: I’m doubtful that Malfoy could be a Death Eater — the idea that You-Know-Who would let a sixteen-year-old like Malfoy join seems daft to me.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy? He’s sixteen, Harry! You think You-Know-Who would let Malfoy join?

metadata.description: I still think of Malfoy mostly as a bully and a prat, not someone who’d be a true Death Eater recruit, so my opinion hasn’t shifted to seeing him as a major threat.
metadata.source_text: I think he just wanted to get out of there, Harry," said Hermione. "He showed Borgin something we couldn’t see," Harry pressed on stubbornly.

metadata.description: I've realized Malfoy might be asking Borgin to fix something dangerous or Dark, and that could mean Malfoy needs to threaten people to get it done.
metadata.source_text: If Malfoy wants something fixing, and he needs to threaten Borgin to get it done, it’s probably something Dark or dangerous, isn’t it?

metadata.description: I doubt You-Know-Who's limits — I don't think anyone can be sure what he would or wouldn't allow, so I can't dismiss the possibility that he might involve a sixteen-year-old.
metadata.source_text: Does anyone really know what You-Know-Who would or wouldn’t do?

metadata.description: People expect me to have cooler friends because of the publicity, and I can feel the distance that fame creates between me and other students.
metadata.source_text: People expect you to have cooler friends than us

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events on the train or the conversation about Malfoy and Borgin, so I don't have direct knowledge of what was said there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger

metadata.description: I wasn't on the train for these scenes and didn't witness the discussion about Malfoy, Borgin, or Neville showing his new wand.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I've been invited to lunch by Professor Slughorn — he actually sent me a parchment tied with violet ribbon asking me to join him in compartment C.
metadata.source_text: Harry, I would be delighted if you would join me for a bite of lunch in compartment C. Sincerely, Professor H.E.F. Slughorn

metadata.description: I'm beginning to think Malfoy might be up to something more important than bullying first years; him skipping prefect duty feels wrong to me.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy’s not doing prefect duty. He’s just sitting in his compartment with the other Slytherins, we saw him when we passed.

metadata.description: I feel more suspicious of Malfoy now — I want to watch him closely and find out what he's doing, even if everyone else doesn't take me seriously.
metadata.source_text: If Harry could only enter, unseen, behind him, what might he not see or hear?

metadata.description: I've noticed that Malfoy might prefer the Inquisitorial Squad to being a prefect; being in the Squad could make prefect duty seem tame by comparison.
metadata.source_text: Maybe he preferred the Inquisitorial Squad.

metadata.description: I think being in the Inquisitorial Squad would explain why Malfoy wasn't out bullying first years; my view of his motives has shifted a bit.
metadata.source_text: Maybe being a prefect seems a bit tame after that.

metadata.description: I'm treating Malfoy as someone whose choices I should reconsider — he's not simply behaving as before; there's a different angle to his actions now.
metadata.source_text: Maybe he preferred the Inquisitorial Squad.

metadata.description: I saw Malfoy sitting with the other Slytherins instead of doing prefect duty — he was just in his compartment when we passed.
metadata.source_text: Malfoy’s not doing prefect duty. He’s just sitting in his compartment with the other Slytherins, we saw him when we passed.

metadata.description: I'm a bit surprised — Malfoy not taking the chance to boss people about is out of character for him, so my opinion of what he'd do has shifted.
metadata.source_text: Not like him, though, is it? Well — that is — but why isn’t he out there bullying first years?

metadata.description: I still think Malfoy’s a prat — I showed it with the rude gesture — but his absence from prefect duty has made me wonder about his priorities.
metadata.source_text: The usual," said Ron indifferently, demonstrating a rude hand gesture.

metadata.description: I found out Draco Malfoy was the one who did whatever left me stuck and bleeding on the train; I know he caused that whole mess.
metadata.source_text: “Draco Malfoy,” said Harry bitterly.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Train and Tonks' Aid

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more bitter about Malfoy now — I feel like I can’t trust him and I’m furious that he got me into such a ridiculous and dangerous situation.
metadata.source_text: “Draco Malfoy,” said Harry bitterly.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Train and Tonks' Aid

metadata.description: Tonks helped me and fixed my nose — I feel grateful and a bit embarrassed, but I see she’s willing to step in and help when I need it.
metadata.source_text: “No problem,” said Tonks, without smiling.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Train and Tonks' Aid

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the Hogwarts Express platform, so I don't know what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Train and Tonks' Aid

metadata.description: I wasn't at the moment on the train when Harry was discovered and helped by Tonks, so I can't say what I would have seen.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Train and Tonks' Aid

metadata.description: I learned that Tonks sent a silvery, four-legged Patronus to send word to the castle that she'd found me — like Dumbledore has used Patronuses to send messages.
metadata.source_text: Was that a Patronus? ... Yes, I’m sending word to the castle that I’ve got you or they’ll worry.
metadata.scene_title: Walking to Hogwarts — Tonks and Harry Converse

metadata.description: I’ve noticed Tonks seems older and much more serious and purposeful now; she’s not the same inquisitive, joking person I remembered from last year.
metadata.source_text: Last year she had been inquisitive (to the point of being a little annoying at times), she had laughed easily, she had made jokes. Now she seemed older and much more serious and purposeful.
metadata.scene_title: Walking to Hogwarts — Tonks and Harry Converse

metadata.description: I don’t blame Tonks for Sirius’s death, and I realize it wasn’t her fault at all, but I can’t bring myself to talk to her about Sirius; I avoid the subject with her.
metadata.source_text: He reflected uncomfortably that Hermione would have suggested he say something consoling about Sirius to her, that it hadn’t been her fault at all, but he couldn’t bring himself to do it.
metadata.scene_title: Walking to Hogwarts — Tonks and Harry Converse

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the Hogsmeade lane, so I don't know what Tonks and Harry said or did there.
metadata.scene_title: Walking to Hogwarts — Tonks and Harry Converse

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the Hogsmeade lane, so I didn't witness Harry and Tonks walking to the school or their conversation.
metadata.scene_title: Walking to Hogwarts — Tonks and Harry Converse

metadata.description: I learned the great gates at Hogwarts are chained shut and won't open for a simple "Alohomora!" — they're bewitched in a way regular unlocking charms won't touch.
metadata.source_text: "Alohomora!" he said confidently, pointing his wand at the padlock, but nothing happened.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at the Gates and Locked Entrance

metadata.description: I've changed my mind about getting in by force or trickery; I thought I could just climb a wall or pick the lock, but Tonks makes me realise that's not possible with these protections.
metadata.source_text: "I could climb a wall," he suggested. "No, you couldn’t," said Tonks flatly. "Anti-intruder jinxes on all of them. Security’s been tightened a hundredfold this summer."
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at the Gates and Locked Entrance

metadata.description: I'm feeling irritated with Tonks right now — she's being flat and obstructive when I'd rather she help me find a way in, so my patience with her is wearing thin.
metadata.source_text: He was cold, he was hungry, and he was quite keen to leave this new, gloomy Tonks behind.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at the Gates and Locked Entrance

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at the Hogwarts gates, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at the Gates and Locked Entrance

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the locked gates or with Harry and Tonks then, so I can't say what occurred at that moment.
metadata.scene_title: Arriving at the Gates and Locked Entrance

metadata.description: I recognized Severus Snape by his hooked nose and long, black, greasy hair when the glowing yellow light drew near and I took off my Invisibility Cloak to be seen.
metadata.source_text: it was ten feet away from them, and Harry had pulled off his Invisibility Cloak so that he could be seen, that he recognized, with a rush of pure loathing, the uplit hooked nose and long, black, greasy hair of Severus Snape.

metadata.description: I felt a rush of pure loathing for Snape all over again when he sneered at me and made a point of my not wearing robes; my dislike for him hasn't softened at all.
metadata.source_text: that he recognized, with a rush of pure loathing, the uplit hooked nose and long, black, greasy hair of Severus Snape.

metadata.description: Snape treated me with open contempt, sneering and tapping the padlock while mocking my appearance, so I now see him as actively hostile and contemptuous toward me right here.
metadata.source_text: “Well, well, well,” sneered Snape, taking out his wand and tapping the padlock once, so that the chains snaked backward and the gates creaked open. “Nice of you to turn up, Potter, although you have evidently decided that the wearing of school robes would detract from your appearance.”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what happened firsthand.

I discovered I was covered in dried blood on my face and that Hermione could clean it away with a spell, so my face could be made to look normal again.

metadata.description: I've changed how I think about Professor Trelawney a bit — I always thought she was a fraud, and finding out she made that prediction linking me to Voldemort made me even less keen on being around her.
metadata.source_text: "Having always considered her a bit of a fraud, Harry had been shocked to discover at the end of the previous term that it had been she who had made the prediction that caused Lord Voldemort to kill Harry’s parents and attack Harry himself."

metadata.description: I noticed Hagrid waving at me and I grinned back; Hagrid and I are friendly enough that he greets me openly even at the staff table.

metadata.description: I just learned that Professor Slughorn is back at Hogwarts and has taken the Potions post — people all over the Hall were murmuring "Potions?" when Dumbledore announced him.
metadata.source_text: "We are pleased to welcome a new member of staff this year. Professor Slughorn" — Slughorn stood up... — "is a former colleague of mine who has agreed to resume his old post of Potions master."

metadata.description: I'm furious and surprised that Snape has been given Defence Against the Dark Arts — I thought Dumbledore didn't trust him for that job, so hearing he got it changes how I see the situation.
metadata.source_text: "Professor Snape, meanwhile," said Dumbledore, raising his voice... "will be taking over the position of Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher."

metadata.description: I loathe Snape all the more after seeing him sit there and raise a hand to the Slytherin applause; there's a look of triumph on his face that makes me hate him even more.
metadata.source_text: Snape, who was sitting on Dumbledore’s right, did not stand up at the mention of his name; he merely raised a hand in lazy acknowledgment of the applause from the Slytherin table, yet Harry was sure he could detect a look of triumph on the features he loathed so much.

metadata.description: I've realised that some injuries can't be cured, like old curses or poisons without antidotes — looking at Dumbledore's sleeve made me say it looks as if the hand has died.
metadata.source_text: "It looks as if it’s died," said Hermione, with a nauseated expression. "But there are some injuries you can’t cure . . . old curses . . . and there are poisons without antidotes. . . ."

metadata.description: I'm shocked and reproachful when people joke about the Defence Against the Dark Arts post; I didn't expect Harry to be so loud about Snape getting the job — it changes how worried I am about school safety.
metadata.source_text: "Harry!" said Hermione, shocked and reproachful.

metadata.description: I've become more protective of Harry in front of big announcements — when he shouted at Snape getting the job I reacted sharply, showing I care and will call him out when needed.
metadata.source_text: "But Harry, you said that Slughorn was going to be teaching Defense Against the Dark Arts!" said Hermione.

metadata.description: I've learned that the Defence Against the Dark Arts job is jinxed — no one lasts more than a year, and people actually died doing it, like Quirrell.
metadata.source_text: "That job’s jinxed. No one’s lasted more than a year. . . . Quirrell actually died doing it. . . ."

metadata.description: I'm oddly hopeful that Snape won't last the year — I said I'm going to keep my fingers crossed for another death, even if that sounds grim, because of the jinx on the job.
metadata.source_text: "Personally, I’m going to keep my fingers crossed for another death. . . ."

metadata.description: I think Slughorn might not want to stay long-term and that Snape could return to Potions — I'm considering staff moves as temporary, not permanent.
metadata.source_text: "He might just go back to teaching Potions at the end of the year," said Ron reasonably. "That Slughorn bloke might not want to stay long-term. Moody didn’t."

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid spent time with Grawp and that Dumbledore has arranged a new home for Grawp up in the mountains — a big cave where he's much happier than in the forest.
metadata.source_text: I was with Grawp," said Hagrid happily. "Los' track o' the time. He's got a new home up in the mountains now, Dumbledore fixed it — nice big cave. He's much happier than he was in the forest.
metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation

metadata.description: I'm starting to think saying You-Know-Who's name might not be as simple as I thought; I argued Dumbledore uses the name, but Hagrid's warning made me realise others feel differently about saying it aloud.
metadata.source_text: I wish yeh'd stop sayin' tha' name, Harry," said a reproachful voice behind them. "Dumbledore uses that name," said Harry stubbornly. "Yeah, well, tha's Dumbledore, innit?" said Hagrid mysteriously.
metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation

metadata.description: I feel reassured by Hagrid — he seems proud and happy about Grawp's improvement and relaxed enough to tease and scold me, so I trust him more as someone who looks out for us.
metadata.source_text: "I was with Grawp," said Hagrid happily. "Los' track o' the time... Oh yeah, he's really come on," said Hagrid proudly.
metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation

metadata.description: I've found out Hagrid was with Grawp and that Dumbledore sorted him a new home in a cave up in the mountains where Grawp's happier than in the forest.

metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation

metadata.description: I reckon Grawp's not as terrifying as I remembered; Hagrid says he's 'really come on', so I'm less certain Grawp's just a dangerous brute anymore — maybe he's improved a lot.
metadata.source_text: "Oh yeah, he's really come on," said Hagrid proudly.
metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation

metadata.description: I feel a bit dismissive but intrigued about Hagrid's plan to train Grawp as an assistant — I snorted, showing I think it's daft, but I still pay attention to Hagrid's pride in him.

metadata.scene_title: Back of the Hall Debrief and Hagrid’s Explanation
