metadata.description: I've just learned that Professor Slughorn will accept N.E.W.T. students with 'Exceeds Expectations' in Potions, so I can carry on with Potions even though I didn't get an 'Outstanding'.
metadata.source_text: Professor Slughorn, however, is perfectly happy to accept N.E.W.T. students with ‘Exceeds Expectations’ at O.W.L. Do you wish to proceed with Potions?

metadata.description: I found out that Snape likes to make the D.A. kids practice nonverbal spells and stages gruesome pictures to teach what the Dark Arts do — Cruciatus, Dementor’s Kiss, Inferius and all.
metadata.source_text: The Dark Arts... These pictures give a fair representation of what happens to those who suffer, for instance, the Cruciatus Curse... feel the Dementor’s Kiss... or provoke the aggression of the Inferius.

metadata.description: I got the impression that Snape really does revel in the Dark Arts more than I'd thought — he talks about them almost with pleasure; it worries me that Dumbledore lets him teach Defense.
metadata.source_text: Did you hear him talking about the Dark Arts? He loves them! All that unfixed, indestructible stuff —

metadata.description: I expect Snape will keep picking on me; he watched me longer than anyone and blamed me for cheek when I called him 'Professor' — I don't think he treats me like a normal pupil.
metadata.source_text: His black eyes roved over their upturned faces, lingering for a fraction of a second longer on Harry’s than anyone else’s... 'Detention, Saturday night, my office,' said Snape. 'I do not take cheek from anyone, Potter . . . not even ‘the Chosen One.’

metadata.description: I've learned that nonverbal spells give you the advantage of surprise because an opponent can't hear what you're about to do, which is exactly what I said from memory of The Standard Book of Spells.
metadata.source_text: Your adversary has no warning about what kind of magic you’re about to perform... 'Your adversary has no warning about what kind of magic you’re about to perform,' said Hermione.

metadata.description: I realised that Snape's way of explaining the need for bravery and quick thinking in Defense sounds a bit like Harry's own description of facing Voldemort; I now see a similarity in their emphasis.
metadata.source_text: Well, I thought he sounded a bit like you... You said it wasn’t just memorizing a bunch of spells, you said it was just you and your brains and your guts — well, wasn’t that what Snape was saying?

metadata.description: I noticed Harry's reflexes are very sharp; when Snape turned his wand on him, Harry's Protego was powerful enough to knock Snape off balance — that changes how I see Harry's defensive skill.
metadata.source_text: Do you remember me telling you we are practicing nonverbal spells, Potter?... He turned his wand on Harry so fast that Harry reacted instinctively; all thought of nonverbal spells forgotten, he yelled, 'Protego!'

metadata.description: I've learned that I've got the same N.E.W.T. subjects as Harry and we've both got free periods now — brilliant news for messing about between lessons.
metadata.source_text: A few minutes later, Ron was cleared to do the same subjects as Harry... 'Look,' said Ron delightedly, gazing at his schedule, 'we’ve got a free period now... excellent!'

metadata.description: I'm more impressed with Harry than ever; what he did against Snape was brilliant and gutsy, even if it got him detention — I think he's the right man to be Captain.
metadata.source_text: That was brilliant, Harry!' chortled Ron... 'You really shouldn’t have said it,' said Hermione... 'He tried to jinx me, in case you didn’t notice!' fumed Harry.

metadata.description: I feel proud to be mates with Harry after what he did to Snape; we're closer because he stood up and reacted for himself, and Dean and Seamus grinned when he called Snape 'Professor.'
metadata.source_text: Behind Snape, however, Ron, Dean, and Seamus grinned appreciatively... 'Detention, Saturday night, my office,' said Snape... 'I do not take cheek from anyone, Potter . . . not even 'the Chosen One.'

metadata.description: I've just received a note from Professor Dumbledore asking me to come to his office at 8 p.m. on Saturday for private lessons — and he signs off with a strange P.S. about Acid Pops.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, I would like to start our private lessons this Saturday. Kindly come along to my office at 8 p.m. I hope you are enjoying your first day back at school. Yours sincerely, Albus Dumbledore P.S. I enjoy Acid Pops.

metadata.description: I realized that 'Acid Pops' is the password to get past the gargoyle outside Dumbledore's study, so that explains the odd P.S.
metadata.source_text: “It’s the password to get past the gargoyle outside his study,” said Harry in a low voice.

metadata.description: Seeing Slughorn beam at Hermione and praise her made me think he's very taken with talented or well-spoken students; he rewards them openly and enjoys their company.
metadata.source_text: “Oho! ‘One of my best friends is Muggle-born, and she’s the best in our year!’ I’m assuming this is the very friend of whom you spoke, Harry?”

metadata.description: I noticed Slughorn favoring Hermione and smiling at me when he linked us; it feels like he already sees me as connected to notable pupils and is warmly disposed toward us.
metadata.source_text: He beamed and looked from Hermione to Harry, who was sitting next to her.

metadata.description: I recognized the Veritaserum by its colorless, odorless nature and know it forces the drinker to tell the truth.
metadata.source_text: “It’s Veritaserum, a colorless, odorless potion that forces the drinker to tell the truth,” said Hermione.

metadata.description: I identified the slow-bubbling, mudlike mixture as Polyjuice Potion and knew its appearance from prior experience making it in our second year.
metadata.source_text: “It’s Polyjuice Potion, sir,” she said.

metadata.description: I know Amortentia is the most powerful love potion, recognizable by its mother-of-pearl sheen and characteristic steam, and that it smells differently to each person according to what attracts them.
metadata.source_text: “It’s the most powerful love potion in the world!” said Hermione. “Quite right! You recognized it, I suppose, by its distinctive mother-of-pearl sheen?” “And the steam rising in characteristic spirals,” said Hermione enthusiastically, “and it’s supposed to smell differently to each of us, according to what attracts us, and I can smell freshly mown grass and new parchment and —”

metadata.description: When Slughorn linked me to a famous potioneer and rewarded me with points, I felt acknowledged by a professor who clearly enjoys associating with talented or noteworthy pupils.
metadata.source_text: “Well, well, take twenty well-earned points for Gryffindor, Miss Granger,” said Slughorn genially.

metadata.description: I read Dumbledore's note over Harry's shoulder and heard him say that 'Acid Pops' is the password for the gargoyle, which sounded odd and made me mutter about Snape.
metadata.source_text: “He enjoys Acid Pops?” said Ron, who had read the message over Harry’s shoulder and was looking perplexed. “It’s the password to get past the gargoyle outside his study,” said Harry in a low voice. “Ha! Snape’s not going to be pleased. . . . I won’t be able to do his detention!”

metadata.description: I felt a bit peeved when Hermione got praised as the best in the year — I reckon I'd have said the same, but seeing her get twenty points made me sulky for a moment.
metadata.source_text: “Well, what’s so impressive about that?” whispered Ron, who for some reason looked annoyed. “You are the best in the year — I’d’ve told him so if he’d asked me!”

metadata.description: Watching Slughorn lavish attention on Hermione and beam at Harry made me realise professors like Slughorn are very keen to flatter and reward clever students, which affects how I see their favouritism.
metadata.source_text: He beamed and looked from Hermione to Harry, who was sitting next to her.

metadata.description: I learned that crushing a sopophorous bean with the flat side of a silver dagger releases far more juice than cutting it, and that the extra juice can immediately change a potion’s colour.
metadata.source_text: Crush with flat side of silver dagger, releases juice better than cutting.

metadata.description: I learned that doing seven counterclockwise stirs and then one clockwise stir can produce the pale pink stage the book describes — the marginal note actually worked for my potion.
metadata.source_text: According to the addition the previous owner had made, however, he ought to add a clockwise stir after every seventh counterclockwise stir.

metadata.description: I used to think luck was mostly random for me, but getting the Felix Felicis made me feel elated and like skill or the right choice can actually make a big difference.
metadata.source_text: He felt elated, something that had certainly never happened before in this dungeon.

metadata.description: I can tell Malfoy expected special treatment from Slughorn, but he didn’t get it — he’ll have to rely on his own talent; I smugly noticed Malfoy’s disappointed look.
metadata.source_text: He could tell that Malfoy had expected to be treated like Harry or Zabini; perhaps even hoped for some preferential treatment of the type he had learned to expect from Snape.

metadata.description: I've seen that Specialis Revelio shows nothing on an old, heavily annotated textbook — casting it didn’t reveal any hidden enchantments on Advanced Potion-Making.
metadata.source_text: Specialis Revelio!

metadata.description: I thought the book might be harmless, but the strange marginalia made me suspicious enough to check it properly; I'm more wary about tips written by unknown previous owners.
metadata.source_text: We ought to check that there’s nothing odd about it. I mean, all these funny instructions, who knows?

metadata.description: I felt annoyed and a bit disappointed that Harry used notes from someone else without consulting us properly; I want to make sure we all understand whether the book is safe.
metadata.source_text: It wasn’t exactly your own work, was it?

metadata.description: I learned that not every textbook you get handed will be in good nick — mine looked puked on and full of scribbles, which might make things harder for me in class.
metadata.source_text: Puked on, by the look of page fifty-two, but —

metadata.description: I felt resentful that I didn't get a better book from Slughorn; I think he could’ve given me the annotated copy but he didn’t, and that annoyed me.
metadata.source_text: Slughorn could’ve handed me that book, but no, I get the one no one’s ever written on.

metadata.description: I was surprised and impressed when Harry won the bottle; I couldn’t quite believe he’d done it, and I asked him quietly how he managed it.
metadata.source_text: How did you do that?

metadata.description: I've learned the half-blood prince is a name people use — 'The Half-Blood Prince' is what the book calls someone, and it's odd because princes are usually men.
metadata.source_text: "The Half-Blood Prince, he was called," Harry said. "How many girls have been Princes?"

metadata.description: I'm more certain now that what Dumbledore will tell me matters a great deal to the prophecy and might help me survive — I'm anxious but hopeful.
metadata.source_text: "It has a very great deal to do with the prophecy," said Dumbledore, ... "and I certainly hope that it will help you to survive."

metadata.description: I feel that Dumbledore trusts me enough to share memories and take me into the Pensieve with permission; that changes how I see him — more open, more responsible toward me.
metadata.source_text: "This time, you enter the Pensieve with me . . . and, even more unusually, with permission."

metadata.description: I think the handwriting looks more like a girl's than a boy's; the identity might not be male.
metadata.source_text: "It might have been a girl. I think the handwriting looks more like a girl's than a boy's."

metadata.description: I'm now inclined to question the assumption that the Half-Blood Prince is male because handwriting suggests otherwise; that thought annoyed me when I said it.
metadata.source_text: "It might have been a girl. I think the handwriting looks more like a girl's than a boy's."

metadata.description: I want to support Harry's pursuits tonight — I told him good luck and that Ron and I will wait up to hear what Dumbledore teaches him, showing I'm invested in his success.
metadata.source_text: "Ooooh! Good luck! We'll wait up, we want to hear what he teaches you!"

metadata.description: I expressed a plain wish that whatever Dumbledore tells Harry will go okay; I'm not involved in the Pensieve visit but I want Harry to be safe.
metadata.source_text: "Hope it goes okay," said Ron, and the pair of them watched Harry leave through the portrait hole.

metadata.description: I'm slightly more concerned about Harry than before; seeing him leave for Dumbledore's office made me voice my worry aloud.
metadata.source_text: "Hope it goes okay," said Ron...

metadata.description: I stayed with Hermione to wait for Harry and offered encouragement, which shows I'm backing him even if I don't fully understand what's coming.
metadata.source_text: "Hope it goes okay," said Ron, and the pair of them watched Harry leave through the portrait hole.

metadata.description: I heard the ragged man speaking Parseltongue and realized he was talking to the dead snake on the door; I recognised the language straight away.
metadata.source_text: He’s speaking Parseltongue?

metadata.description: I learned that Merope Gaunt was Voldemort’s mother and that Tom Riddle senior was the Muggle she loved.
metadata.source_text: So Merope was . . . Sir, does that mean she was . . . Voldemort’s mother?

metadata.description: I’m surprised and a bit unsettled to discover Voldemort’s family came from those miserable Gaunts; I didn’t expect his mother to be called Merope or for him to have a Muggle father.
metadata.source_text: That’s right," said Dumbledore. "I am glad to see you’re keeping up.

metadata.description: Seeing Ogden hurt and frightened made me feel pity for him; he seemed a decent, nervous Ministry man who didn’t deserve being attacked.
metadata.source_text: Er — I’m sorry — I don’t understand you," said Ogden nervously.

metadata.description: I was not present for this scene and so cannot describe the events or dialogue that occurred at the Gaunt cottage.
I was not there during the encounter at the Gaunt cottage and do not have first-hand knowledge of what happened between Ogden and the Gaunts.
I've learned that Merope Gaunt ran off and married Tom Riddle, and that she stopped giving him the love potion so he left her while she was pregnant.
metadata.source_text: You see, within a few months of their runaway marriage, Tom Riddle reappeared at the manor house in Little Hangleton without his wife.

metadata.description: I'm a bit clearer now: I used to have muddled ideas about Voldemort's past, but hearing Dumbledore makes me think the past really matters to the prophecy.
metadata.source_text: It has everything to do with the prophecy.

metadata.description: I think Ron and Hermione are trustworthy enough to be told what Dumbledore told me, so I can share this with only them.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I think Mr. Weasley and Miss Granger have proved themselves trustworthy.

metadata.description: I was not present during Dumbledore's account of Merope Gaunt and Tom Riddle's marriage, so I do not have firsthand knowledge of those events.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I think Mr. Weasley and Miss Granger have proved themselves trustworthy.

metadata.description: I wasn't there in Dumbledore's office when he told Harry about Merope, Tom Riddle, and the orphanage; I only hear about it from Harry afterward.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I think Mr. Weasley and Miss Granger have proved themselves trustworthy.

metadata.description: I've just found that someone sent me a brand-new Advanced Potion-Making from Flourish and Blotts via Hedwig, and I can hide the Prince's book by switching the covers so I keep the annotated copy.
metadata.source_text: A moment later, an identical package landed in front of Ron... 'Ha!' said Harry, unwrapping the parcel to reveal a new copy of Advanced Potion-Making, fresh from Flourish and Blotts... He pulled the old copy of Advanced Potion-Making out of his bag and tapped the cover with his wand, muttering, 'Diffindo!'... He then swapped the covers... and said, 'Reparo!'

metadata.description: I'm beginning to accept that the Quidditch team's sudden popularity is down to me being in the spotlight — people really are fascinated by what I've been through and what I'm called now.
metadata.source_text: Oh, come on, Harry,' said Hermione... 'It's not Quidditch that’s popular, it's you!... And now they're calling you 'the Chosen One' — well, come on, can't you see why people are fascinated by you?'

metadata.description: I miss Hagrid and don't like not talking to him, even though I'm relieved we're rid of Grawp for now; I still care about Hagrid despite the trouble.
metadata.source_text: 'I hate not talking to Hagrid,' said Hermione... 'We'll go down after Quidditch,' Harry assured her. He too was missing Hagrid, although like Ron he thought that they were better off without Grawp in their lives.

metadata.description: I've realised that people are fascinated by Harry because he's proven Voldemort returned and survived two fights; the Wizarding world has had to accept his truth.
metadata.source_text: 'Everyone knows you've been telling the truth now, don't they? The whole Wizarding world has had to admit that you were right about Voldemort being back and that you really have fought him twice in the last two years and escaped both times.'

metadata.description: I feel that Harry is more interesting and desirable than ever; I'm impatient for him to recognise how his fame explains the team's popularity.
metadata.source_text: 'Oh, come on, Harry,' said Hermione, suddenly impatient. 'It's not Quidditch that’s popular, it's you! You’ve never been more interesting, and frankly, you’ve never been more fanciable.'

metadata.description: I hate that we're not talking to Hagrid; I'm upset by our silence with him and want to go see him as soon as possible after Quidditch.
metadata.source_text: 'I hate not talking to Hagrid,' said Hermione, looking upset. 'We'll go down after Quidditch,' Harry assured her.

metadata.description: I've remembered how awful the skrewts were and I'm not about to pretend I enjoyed Hagrid's creature lessons — those things were a nightmare.
metadata.source_text: 'Speak for yourself, I haven't forgotten the skrewts,' said Ron darkly.

metadata.description: I'm convinced we're actually better off without Grawp around; even if I miss Hagrid a bit, I don't want that giant teaching us or being part of our lives.
metadata.source_text: He too was missing Hagrid, although like Ron he thought that they were better off without Grawp in their lives.

metadata.description: I feel annoyed and dismissive about Hagrid's lessons now, especially after hearing about his gormless brother and imagining us teaching Grawp silly things.
metadata.source_text: 'And I'm telling you now, we've had a narrow escape. You didn't hear him going on about his gormless brother — we'd have been teaching Grawp how to tie his shoelaces if we'd stayed.'

metadata.description: I set a simple flying test: groups of ten must fly once around the pitch so I can see who can actually stay airborne.
metadata.source_text: asking all applicants for the team to divide into groups of ten and fly once around the pitch.

metadata.description: I'm getting seriously annoyed with how many non-Gryffindors or incapable flyers turned up; I don't want them wasting time or places on the team.
metadata.source_text: If there’s anyone else here who’s not from Gryffindor,” roared Harry, who was starting to get seriously annoyed, “leave now, please!”

metadata.description: I noticed McLaggen looked a bit annoyed and wondered if he expects special treatment because he thinks he's one of Sluggy's favourites.
metadata.source_text: He thought he saw a flicker of annoyance pass over McLaggen’s face and wondered whether McLaggen expected preferential treatment because they were both “old Sluggy’s” favorites.

metadata.description: I've learned that Hagrid has giant grubs which he keeps to feed to Aragog; the grubs are meant as Aragog's food.
metadata.source_text: I put down his rock cake all the same. “Jus’ giant grubs,” said Hagrid. “And they grow into . . . ?” said Ron, looking apprehensive. “They won’ grow inter nuthin’,” said Hagrid. “I got ’em ter feed ter Aragog.”

metadata.description: I'm upset and worried now because Hagrid is distraught; I didn't expect Aragog might be dying and Hagrid's reaction makes me feel there's little we can do.
metadata.source_text: And without warning, he burst into tears. “Hagrid!” cried Hermione, leaping up, hurrying around the table the long way to avoid the barrel of maggots, and putting an arm around his shaking shoulders. “What is it?”

metadata.description: I feel sympathy for Hagrid: I want to help and comfort him because he's so attached to Aragog and clearly devastated.
metadata.source_text: Hermione patted Hagrid’s shoulder, looking at a complete loss for anything to say.

metadata.description: I learned Hagrid says the grubs won't grow into anything because they're for feeding Aragog, not to turn into creatures.
metadata.source_text: “They won’ grow inter nuthin’,” said Hagrid. “I got ’em ter feed ter Aragog.”

metadata.description: I'm apprehensive and worried about Aragog; I reckon the colony's been acting odd since Aragog got ill and it's not safe for anyone but Hagrid to go near them.
metadata.source_text: “I don’ think there is, Hermione,” choked Hagrid, ... “I don’ reckon it’d be safe fer anyone but me ter go near the colony at the mo’,” Hagrid finished, ... “Yeah, I think we saw a bit of that side of them,” said Ron in an undertone.

metadata.description: I've noticed Hagrid's deep bond with Aragog; seeing Hagrid so upset shows me just how important Aragog is to him.
metadata.source_text: And without warning, he burst into tears. ... “It’s . . . Aragog. . . . I think he’s dyin’. . . . He got ill over the summer an’ he’s not gettin’ better. . . . I don’ know what I’ll do if he . . . if he . . . We’ve bin tergether so long. . . .”

metadata.description: I've been told I must do detention with Professor Snape at half past eight tonight and I'll be sorting rotten flobberworms for Potions, and Snape didn't ask me to bring protective gloves.
metadata.source_text: He says you’re to come to his office at half past eight tonight to do your detention — er — no matter how many party invitations you’ve received. And he wanted you to know you’ll be sorting out rotten flobberworms from good ones, to use in Potions and — and he says there’s no need to bring protective gloves.

metadata.description: I learned from Hermione that Filch ran Secrecy Sensors over everyone and confiscated things like a shrunken head, so any Dark object brought in should have been detected.
metadata.source_text: Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the entrance hall. Any Dark object would have been found, I know for a fact Crabbe had a shrunken head confiscated.

metadata.description: I was thinking Malfoy might have brought something dangerous into Hogwarts, but after hearing about the searches and owl checks I’m less sure how he could have done it.
metadata.source_text: If it’s not at their house, he must have brought whatever it is to Hogwarts with him — But how can he have done, Harry? ... All the owls are being checked too.

metadata.description: I felt annoyed that Slughorn ignored Ron when he invited us; I don’t like seeing my mate snubbed, and it made Ron clearly sullen and cross.
metadata.source_text: It was as though Ron was not present; Slughorn did not so much as look at him.

metadata.description: I've read and know that the entire stock of Ministry Time-Turners was smashed last summer; there’s an item about it in the Daily Prophet.
metadata.source_text: We smashed the entire stock of Ministry Time-Turners when we were there last summer. It was in the Daily Prophet.

metadata.description: I've been told Filch checked everyone with Secrecy Sensors on arrival and confiscated dark items, so an illicit Dark object should have been detected if it arrived with a student.
metadata.source_text: Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the entrance hall. Any Dark object would have been found, I know for a fact Crabbe had a shrunken head confiscated.

metadata.description: I thought Malfoy could have brought something dangerous to school, but having remembered the searches and owl inspections I now doubt he could have done so without it being found.
metadata.source_text: All the owls are being checked too ... Well, Filch ran over all of us with Secrecy Sensors when we got into the entrance hall.

metadata.description: I noticed Slughorn’s flattery when he singled me out for his party; he made a point of bowing to me and praising my presence, which I found awkward but flattering.
metadata.source_text: I hope very much that Miss Granger will favor me by coming too." Slughorn made Hermione a little bow as he finished speaking.

metadata.description: I saw in the paper that Dad visited the Malfoys’ house as part of a second search and that Arthur Weasley said his team acted on a confidential tip-off.
metadata.source_text: ‘This second search of the Death Eater’s residence does not seem to have yielded any results. Arthur Weasley of the Office for the Detection and Confiscation of Counterfeit Defensive Spells and Protective Objects said that his team had been acting upon a confidential tip-off.’

metadata.description: I felt miffed and embarrassed when Slughorn ignored me at the party invitation; I’m not one for big flattery and I didn’t like being left out like that.
metadata.source_text: It was as though Ron was not present; Slughorn did not so much as look at him.

metadata.description: I got cross with Harry when he defended Slughorn’s invitation and accused me of being invited; I felt tossed aside and left the table to go to bed.
metadata.source_text: Listen, it’s not my fault Slughorn invited Hermione and me to his stupid party, neither of us wanted to go, you know! ... Well, as I’m not invited to any parties, I think I’ll go to bed.

metadata.description: I learned that Liberacorpus is a counter-jinx that can bring someone down if they're suspended in the air — I had to shout it to make Ron fall back onto his mattress.
metadata.source_text: Praying that this was the counter-jinx, Harry thought Liberacorpus! with all his might. There was another flash of light, and Ron fell in a heap onto his mattress.
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I'm starting to think the Half-Blood Prince might be connected to my father — the idea popped into my head when I remembered Dad using that dangling spell on Snape.
metadata.source_text: My dad used this spell," said Harry. "I — Lupin told me." ... Now, however, a wonderful possibility occurred to him. Could the Half-Blood Prince possibly be — ?
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I covered up something from Ron and Hermione by saying Lupin told me about my dad using the spell; I feel protective or awkward about showing where I really saw it.
metadata.source_text: My dad used this spell," said Harry. "I — Lupin told me." This last part was not true; in fact, Harry had seen his father use the spell on Snape, but he had never told Ron and Hermione about that particular excursion into the Pensieve.
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I've learned that the potion book contains unknown handwritten incantations that people are trying out without approval, and those spells can do things like suspend people by the ankle.
metadata.source_text: Was this spell, by any chance, another one from that potion book of yours?" she asked. ... "Dangling people upside down by the ankle?" said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that the Half-Blood Prince was possibly a dodgy person; I don't trust someone who invents spells to dangle people or keeps secret handwritten instructions.
metadata.source_text: Because I'm starting to think this Prince character was a bit dodgy." ... "I just think it's very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don't even know what they're for, and stop talking about 'the Prince' as if it's his title, I bet it's just a stupid nickname, and it doesn't seem as though he was a very nice person to me!
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I feel at odds with Harry and Ron over the Prince and about their willingness to experiment; I'm frustrated with them and think they're being reckless rather than careful.
metadata.source_text: "Always jump to the worst conclusion, don't you?" ... "It’s got nothing to do with that!" said Hermione, her cheeks reddening. "I just think it's very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don't even know what they’re for..."
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I found out that the spell made me dangle upside down — it was a laugh but it really hoisted me off the bed by my ankle until Harry fixed it.
metadata.source_text: Aaaaaaaargh!" ... Ron was dangling upside down in midair as though an invisible hook had hoisted him up by the ankle. ... "There was another flash of light, and Ron fell in a heap onto his mattress.
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I'm more relaxed about the Prince's spells; I still think it was funny and not dangerous, and I don't see why Hermione is getting so worked up about it.
metadata.source_text: "It was a laugh!" said Ron, upending a ketchup bottle over his sausages. "Just a laugh, Hermione, that’s all!"
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I sided with Harry against Hermione and teased her, thinking she dislikes the Prince because he's better at Potions than she is, so I'm defensive of Harry and the book.
metadata.source_text: "You don't like the Prince, Hermione," he added, pointing a sausage at her sternly, "because he's better than you at Potions —"
metadata.scene_title: Ron levitated by a jinx; Half-Blood Prince speculation

metadata.description: I remembered my dad used that spell — I’ve actually seen him do it in the Pensieve, though I didn’t tell Ron and Hermione the truth at first.
metadata.source_text: My dad," said Harry. He had only just remembered. "My dad used this spell," said Harry. "I — Lupin told me." This last part was not true; in fact, Harry had seen his father use the spell on Snape, but he had never told Ron and Hermione about that particular excursion into the Pensieve.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I had the idea that the Half-Blood Prince might be the source of the book’s spells — it suddenly seemed like a real possibility to me.
metadata.source_text: Now, however, a wonderful possibility occurred to him. Could the Half-Blood Prince possibly be — ?
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I feel a bit sarcastic toward the Death Eaters — I reckon they’d be friendly to me if they weren’t trying to kill me; I say they’d love to have me, but I mean it biting.
metadata.source_text: "And they’d love to have me," said Harry sarcastically. "We’d be best pals if they didn’t keep trying to do me in."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I know we’ve seen lots of people use that dangerous magic — I remember people being dangled in the air and made to float along, asleep and helpless.
metadata.source_text: "Maybe your dad did use it, Harry," said Hermione, "but he’s not the only one. We’ve seen a whole bunch of people use it, in case you’ve forgotten. Dangling people in the air. Making them float along, asleep, helpless."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I’ve grown more convinced that it’s irresponsible to perform spells without knowing their purpose; I’m annoyed when people treat the Prince like a hero or a formal title.
metadata.source_text: "It’s got nothing to do with that!" said Hermione, her cheeks reddening. "I just think it’s very irresponsible to start performing spells when you don’t even know what they’re for, and stop talking about ‘the Prince’ as if it’s his title, I bet it’s just a stupid nickname, and it doesn’t seem as though he was a very nice person to me!"
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I now think Death Eaters are mainly half-bloods pretending to be pure and that they hate Muggle-borns; I believe they’d be happy to have people like Harry and Ron join, which changes how I view their composition.
metadata.source_text: "The Death Eaters can’t all be pure-blood, there aren’t enough pure-blood wizards left," said Hermione stubbornly. "I expect most of them are half-bloods pretending to be pure. It’s only Muggle-borns they hate, they’d be quite happy to let you and Ron join up."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I remembered the Death Eaters at the Quidditch World Cup and saw their behavior as abuse of the magic — it wasn’t the same as when Harry and his dad were joking about spells.
metadata.source_text: Ron came to his aid. "That was different," he said robustly. "They were abusing it. Harry and his dad were just having a laugh.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I’m indignant at the idea my family would ever be accepted by Death Eaters; I believe my lot are 'blood traitors' and that’s as bad as being Muggle-born to them.
metadata.source_text: "There is no way they’d let me be a Death Eater!" said Ron indignantly, a bit of sausage flying off the fork he was now brandishing at Hermione and hitting Ernie Macmillan on the head. "My whole family are blood traitors! That’s as bad as Muggle-borns to Death Eaters!"
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I think Hermione dislikes the Prince because she’s jealous about Potions — I said she doesn’t like him because he’s better than her, half teasing and half serious.
metadata.source_text: You don’t like the Prince, Hermione," he added, pointing a sausage at her sternly, "because he’s better than you at Potions —
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Half-Blood Prince, Slughorn's invitation, and interrupted anecdote

metadata.description: I've been using Quidditch practice as an excuse whenever Slughorn sends those little violet-ribbon invitations so I can avoid going to his gatherings without hurting feelings.
metadata.source_text: Well, I’ve had Quidditch practice, Professor," said Harry, who had indeed been scheduling practices every time Slughorn had sent him a little, violet ribbon-adorned invitation.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I think I can keep dodging Slughorn for a bit longer; saying I have an appointment with Professor Dumbledore seems to work as a polite escape from Monday night invitations.
metadata.source_text: I can’t, Professor, I’ve got — er — an appointment with Professor Dumbledore that evening.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I notice Slughorn treats Ron like he’s not worth much attention when he leaves, which makes me more aware that Slughorn favours certain students over others.
metadata.source_text: And with a regal wave, he waddled out of the shop, taking as little notice of Ron as though he had been a display of Cockroach Clusters.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I can see that Slughorn assumes I enjoy these social evenings; he says, 'Miss Granger loves them,' so he expects me to be keen on his gatherings.
metadata.source_text: Miss Granger loves them, don’t you?” “Yes,” said Hermione helplessly, “they’re really —
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I feel a bit helpless about Harry wriggling out of another invitation; I didn’t think avoiding Slughorn would become such a recurring thing.
metadata.source_text: I can’t believe you’ve wriggled out of another one,” said Hermione, shaking her head.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I find that Harry and Ron treat Slughorn’s invitations lightly and joke about the idea of being left with McLaggen and Zabini, so I view those evenings as awkward rather than enjoyable.
metadata.source_text: they usually had a laugh with Ginny, imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I’ve noticed Harry keeps scheduling Quidditch practice whenever Slughorn invites him, so those practice claims are clearly his way of avoiding Slughorn’s socials.
metadata.source_text: Well, I’ve had Quidditch practice, Professor," said Harry, who had indeed been scheduling practices every time Slughorn had sent him a little, violet ribbon-adorned invitation.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I feel a bit put out that Slughorn took no notice of me and treated me like a display of Cockroach Clusters when he left; it’s obvious he’s partial to others.
metadata.source_text: And with a regal wave, he waddled out of the shop, taking as little notice of Ron as though he had been a display of Cockroach Clusters.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I’m inclined to laugh along with Ginny and Harry about Hermione being stuck with blokes like McLaggen and Zabini at Slughorn’s events, which makes me see those parties as more of a joke than a serious social chance.
metadata.source_text: they usually had a laugh with Ginny, imagining Hermione shut up with McLaggen and Zabini.
metadata.scene_title: Slughorn recruits students for practice nights; Harry evades invitation

metadata.description: I recognised a silver goblet as one I saw at Sirius's house because it had the Black family crest on it.
metadata.source_text: "You took that from Sirius’s house," said Harry, who was almost nose to nose with Mundungus and was breathing in an unpleasant smell of old tobacco and spirits. "That had the Black family crest on it."
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I'm convinced Mundungus nicked things from Number Twelve — I actually think he stole from the place the night Sirius died.
metadata.source_text: "What did you do, go back the night he died and strip the place?" snarled Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I feel even angrier and more distrustful towards Mundungus now; I treated him as a thief and wanted him stopped before he got away.
metadata.source_text: Harry had pinned Mundungus against the wall of the pub by the throat. ... "Give it to me!" ... "OU CH!" Harry had pinned Mundungus against the wall of the pub by the throat.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I noticed they were selling deluxe sugar quills and thought they'd keep someone entertained for hours.
metadata.source_text: “Oh, look — they’ve got deluxe sugar quills — those would last hours!”
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I became alarmed and worried that Harry was taking things too far when he attacked Mundungus; I think he mustn't choke people like that.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, you mustn’t!" shrieked Hermione, as Mundungus started to turn blue.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I'm frightened for Harry when he loses his temper — my view of what he'll do in a fight has hardened; I now see him as capable of frightening violence in the heat of the moment.
metadata.source_text: "Harry!" squealed Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I picked up a silver goblet and felt it was familiar, which led to the discovery that it belonged to the Black family.
metadata.source_text: Ron had stooped down and picked up something silver. "Hang on," Ron said slowly. "This looks familiar —"
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: Seeing Harry leap on Mundungus made me more uneasy about the whole situation; I didn't expect Harry to attack someone like that.
metadata.source_text: Ron continued to look moody and merely shrugged when Hermione asked him where he wanted to go next.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I felt alarmed and taken aback at Mundungus when he snatched the goblet back; my opinion of him slid further toward him being a dodgy, untrustworthy sort.
metadata.source_text: "Thank you!" said Mundungus, snatching the goblet out of Ron’s hand and stuffing it back into the case.
metadata.scene_title: Harry roughs up Mundungus; Tonks appears and calms him

metadata.description: I learned that Professor McGonagall told us Malfoy was in detention with her in Hogsmeade, so he couldn't have been the one who walked the parcel into the castle.
metadata.source_text: Mr Malfoy was not in Hogsmeade today.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I'm less certain Malfoy personally delivered the necklace now; if he was with McGonagall then he must've used someone else or an accomplice to get it inside Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Mr Malfoy was not in Hogsmeade today.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I still suspect Malfoy and don't trust him — I think he's involved with dodgy people and could have arranged the necklace through cronies, even if he wasn't physically there.
metadata.source_text: He must have used an accomplice, then.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I've found out that Borgin had that necklace on display and told me only the price when I asked; he didn't say it was sold, so it might still have been in the shop when I looked.
metadata.source_text: And Borgin just told me the price, he didn’t say it was already sold or anything
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that whoever arranged the necklace was trying to avoid touching it or drawing attention — they asked Borgin to keep something and Malfoy refused to carry it because it would look ridiculous.
metadata.source_text: Because he didn’t want to touch it, obviously!
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I think Malfoy is sneaky enough to use other people; I no longer imagine he would do something that crude himself if he could recruit an accomplice to avoid suspicion.
metadata.source_text: He must have used an accomplice, then.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I've noticed that the attack wasn't very well planned — the curse never even reached the castle, so whatever they tried wasn't exactly foolproof.
metadata.source_text: The curse didn’t even make it into the castle.
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I'm thinking this wasn't a clever job — whoever did it wasn't very bright or didn't think the plan through, so I don't fear some perfect, unstoppable plot right now.
metadata.source_text: It wasn’t a very slick attack, really, when you stop and think about it
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I reckon Malfoy isn't one of the world's great thinkers; I'm more inclined to see him as blustering and reckless rather than cunning mastermind material.
metadata.source_text: But since when has Malfoy been one of the world’s great thinkers?
metadata.scene_title: Return to Hogwarts after Mundungus; discovery of Katie Bell's curse

metadata.description: I learned that Katie Bell was cursed by a necklace and that she was lucky — she only brushed it through a tiny hole in her glove, otherwise she might have died instantly.
metadata.source_text: She appears to have brushed the necklace with the smallest possible amount of skin: There was a tiny hole in her glove. Had she put it on, had she even held it in her ungloved hand, she would have died, perhaps instantly.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of Katie's Accident and Discussion of the Curse

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that the curse was deadly serious and that quick, expert intervention matters — I feel impressed and a bit relieved that Professor Snape could do enough to stop it spreading.
metadata.source_text: Luckily Professor Snape was able to do enough to prevent a rapid spread of the curse —
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of Katie's Accident and Discussion of the Curse

metadata.description: I realise that Dumbledore trusts Snape's knowledge of the Dark Arts more than Madam Pomfrey's, which alters how I view Snape's role when dangerous magical injuries happen.
metadata.source_text: Professor Snape knows much more about the Dark Arts than Madam Pomfrey, Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of Katie's Accident and Discussion of the Curse

metadata.description: I was not present during the discussion between Dumbledore and Harry about Katie's accident, so I did not witness the details or the conversation in the office.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of Katie's Accident and Discussion of the Curse

metadata.description: I was not in Dumbledore's office when Harry and Dumbledore discussed Katie Bell's condition and the necklace curse, so I don't know their exact exchange.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of Katie's Accident and Discussion of the Curse

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore was told by McGonagall about my suspicion concerning Draco Malfoy and Katie's accident.
metadata.source_text: She told me of your suspicions, yes,
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Relates the Origin of the Locket and Merope's Decline

metadata.description: I'm a bit resentful that Dumbledore treats lessons as more important than investigating Katie's harm; I feel the lesson comes at the wrong time after such a gap.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt slightly resentful at this: If their lessons were so very important, why had there been such a long gap between the first and second?
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Relates the Origin of the Locket and Merope's Decline

metadata.description: I still suspect Draco Malfoy might have had a hand in Katie's accident and expect Dumbledore to look into anyone responsible; I haven't dropped my worries about him.
metadata.source_text: did Professor McGonagall tell you what I told her after Katie got hurt? About Draco Malfoy?
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Relates the Origin of the Locket and Merope's Decline

metadata.description: I was not present during this conversation in Dumbledore's office and so I do not know what was said or done there.
metadata.source_text: Absent
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Relates the Origin of the Locket and Merope's Decline

metadata.description: I was not in Dumbledore's office for this lesson or the Pensieve memory, so I didn't witness the discussion about Merope or the locket.
metadata.source_text: Absent
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Relates the Origin of the Locket and Merope's Decline

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore can show memories by putting them in a Pensieve — he said we were going to enter his memory and that it would be rich in detail and accurate.
metadata.source_text: This time, we are going to enter my memory. I think you will find it both rich in detail and satisfyingly accurate. After you, Harry . . .
metadata.scene_title: Merope's Fate and Transition to the Pensieve Memory of Tom Riddle

metadata.description: I was surprised by how Dumbledore behaved — I expected him to insist on accompanying the boy in the memory, but he didn't, which made me rethink how much he lets people act for themselves.
metadata.source_text: Harry thought that Dumbledore would insist upon accompanying Riddle, but once again he was surprised.
metadata.scene_title: Merope's Fate and Transition to the Pensieve Memory of Tom Riddle

metadata.description: Seeing Dumbledore speak so gently to that boy has made me feel that Dumbledore is patient and quietly helpful, willing to guide even when I'm unsure what he'll do next.
metadata.source_text: “I’m afraid I don’t know,” said Dumbledore, his voice gentle.
metadata.scene_title: Merope's Fate and Transition to the Pensieve Memory of Tom Riddle

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this exchange in the Pensieve memory, so I don't have direct knowledge of Hermione's reactions or input.
metadata.source_text: She was greatly weakened by long suffering and she never had your mother’s courage. And now, if you will stand . . .”
