metadata.description: I’m obviously pleased to be with Lavender — I’m into this whole romance nonsense and don’t mind the showing off, even if others laugh.
metadata.source_text: There was a loud squeal of “Won-Won!” and Lavender Brown came hurtling out of nowhere and flung herself into Ron’s arms.
metadata.scene_title: Common Room Reunion and Debate about Malfoy

metadata.description: I learned that Tom Riddle physically murdered Muggles himself, put Morfin's wand by him, and used magic to plant false memories so Morfin would confess to crimes he didn't commit.
metadata.source_text: Voldemort Stupefied his uncle, took his wand, and proceeded across the valley to ‘the big house over the way.’ There he murdered the Muggle man... Then he returned to the Gaunt hovel, performed the complex bit of magic that would implant a false memory in his uncle’s mind, laid Morfin’s wand beside its unconscious owner...
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I'm angrier than before about the Ministry and how rubbish their detection can be — they can tell magic happened but can't tell who did it if it happens inside another witch or wizard's house.
metadata.source_text: But how come the Ministry didn’t realize that Voldemort had done all that to Morfin?" Harry asked angrily. "He was underage at the time, wasn’t he? I thought they could detect underage magic!"
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I feel more distrustful toward the Ministry and more reliant on Dumbledore, since he showed me memories and trusts me with the job of getting Slughorn's true recollection.
metadata.source_text: No, I think it would be foolish to attempt to wrest the truth from Professor Slughorn by force, and might do much more harm than good; I do not wish him to leave Hogwarts. However, he has his weaknesses like the rest of us, and I believe that you are the one person who might be able to penetrate his defenses.
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I've learned from Dumbledore's explanation that the Ministry can detect magical activity but cannot identify the caster when magic is done inside another witch or wizard's home.
metadata.source_text: You are quite right — they can detect magic, but not the perpetrator: You will remember that you were blamed by the Ministry for the Hover Charm that was, in fact, cast by —
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I'm troubled and more convinced that relying solely on the Ministry and parental enforcement for underage magic is inadequate and can lead to grave injustices.
metadata.source_text: They rely on witch and wizard parents to enforce their offspring’s obedience while within their walls." "Well, that’s rubbish," snapped Harry. "Look what happened here, look what happened to Morfin!" "I agree," said Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I respect Dumbledore's careful judgement more, since he prefers persuasion over coercion with Slughorn and values protecting Hogwarts while pursuing the truth.
metadata.source_text: No, I think it would be foolish to attempt to wrest the truth from Professor Slughorn by force, and might do much more harm than good; I do not wish him to leave Hogwarts.
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I've understood that Tom Riddle asked about Horcruxes as a student and that Slughorn later tried to hide or alter his memory of that conversation.
metadata.source_text: Sir, I wondered what you know about . . . about Horcruxes?" ... "I don’t know anything about Horcruxes and I wouldn’t tell you if I did! Now get out of here at once and don’t let me catch you mentioning them again!"
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I'm more suspicious of Slughorn now; he isn't the harmless, chatty professor I thought — he meddled with his own memory to hide something important.
metadata.source_text: As you might have noticed," said Dumbledore, "that memory has been tampered with." "Tampered with?" repeated Harry. "Certainly," said Dumbledore. "Professor Slughorn has meddled with his own recollections."
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I feel uneasy about Tom Riddle; seeing him so composed and knowing he already had Marvolo's ring and had killed his father makes me respect how dangerous he must have been even as a student.
metadata.source_text: Harry recognized Voldemort at once. His was the most handsome face and he looked the most relaxed of all the boys. His right hand lay negligently upon the arm of his chair; with a jolt, Harry saw that he was wearing Marvolo’s gold-and-black ring; he had already killed his father.
metadata.scene_title: School Notices, Apparition Talk, and Dumbledore’s Important Memories

metadata.description: I've learned that Golpalott's Third Law is written in Advanced Potion-Making and relates to antidotes for blended poisons, but the Prince's notes don't explain how to use it.
metadata.source_text: There was Golpalott’s Third Law, stated word for word as Hermione had recited it, but not a single illuminating note in the Prince’s hand to explain what it meant.

metadata.description: I'm beginning to think my reputation as the best potion-maker here isn't what it used to be — after Slughorn peered into my cauldron and nearly coughed, I felt my standing drop.
metadata.source_text: It took Harry only five minutes to realize that his reputation as the best potion-maker in the class was crashing around his ears.

metadata.description: I reckon Hermione's become even more formidable in Potions; she's way ahead of me now and I feel edged out when she acts smug about outperforming everyone.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s expression could not have been any smugger; she had loathed being outperformed in every Potions class.

metadata.description: I've learned and can recite Golpalott's Third Law: the antidote for a blended poison will be more than the sum of antidotes for each component, and identification of ingredients is essential.
metadata.source_text: Golpalott’s-Third-Law-states-that-the-antidote-for-a-blended-poison-will-be-equal-to-more-than-the-sum-of-the-antidotes-for-each-of-the-separate-components.

metadata.description: I'm worried that if Dumbledore couldn't get Slughorn to reveal what he knows, Slughorn must be determined to hide the truth; therefore approaching him will require a careful strategy.
metadata.source_text: He must be determined to hide what really happened if Dumbledore couldn’t get it out of him," she said in a low voice... "I think it’s going to be difficult to get the information, Harry, you’ll have to be very careful about how you approach Slughorn, think out a strategy.

metadata.description: I feel confident in my abilities and a bit superior in class situations like Potions; when others flounder, I step in and perform, and I expect them to keep up.
metadata.source_text: Hermione had left her stool and was halfway toward Slughorn’s desk before the rest of the class had realized it was time to move... Hermione’s expression could not have been any smugger; she had loathed being outperformed in every Potions class.

metadata.description: I've learned that Harry was advised by me to hang back after Potions and ask Slughorn directly, because I reckon that approach might work.
metadata.source_text: Ron reckons I should just hang back after Potions this afternoon. . . .

metadata.description: I'm a bit uneasy seeing Hermione so sure and clever; when she flares up at my suggestion I notice she's confident and quick, and I sometimes doubt my own judgment beside her.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, well, if Won-Won thinks that, you’d better do it," she said, flaring up at once. "After all, when has Won-Won’s judgment ever been faulty?"

metadata.description: I feel protective of Harry and try to help him, but I also copy what he does in Potions and end up as clueless as him when he doesn't know the next step.
metadata.source_text: Ron kept forgetting that he could no longer rely on Hermione to help him out of trouble when he failed to grasp what was going on... Ron was now standing there looking rather gormless, having copied everything Harry had done.

metadata.description: I learned that a bezoar — a stone from a goat's stomach — will act as an antidote to most poisons, because I read it in the Half-Blood Prince's book and remembered Snape's first lesson definition.
metadata.source_text: A stone taken from the stomach of a goat, which will protect from most poisons.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I've decided it's best to play things cool with Slughorn for now; I'll let him think I've forgotten about Horcruxes so I can get closer without raising alarm.
metadata.source_text: He decided that, for the time being, he would let Slughorn think that he had forgotten all about Horcruxes; it was surely best to lull him into a false sense of security before returning to the attack.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I reckon Slughorn can be flattered and softened — he's meddlesome but susceptible to showy tricks and praise, as when he roared with laughter and compared me to my mother over the bezoar.
metadata.source_text: You’ve got nerve, boy!... Oh, you’re like your mother. . . . Well, I can’t fault you. . . . A bezoar would certainly act as an antidote to all these potions!
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I've learned that meticulous antidote-brewing involves many precise ingredients and effort — my bottle contained fifty-two components and even a piece of my own hair as I tried to finish.
metadata.source_text: Hermione... had soot on her nose, looked livid. Her half-finished antidote, comprising fifty-two ingredients, including a chunk of her own hair, bubbled sluggishly behind Slughorn...
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more exasperated than usual because Harry used a shortcut and stole the limelight with a bezoar instead of bothering to complete the proper antidote work.
metadata.source_text: Hermione... looked livid. Her half-finished antidote... bubbled sluggishly behind Slughorn, who had eyes for nobody but Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I feel undermined by Harry's cheek; although I value proper potion-making, I also recognise that his boldness can win favour with teachers like Slughorn, which annoys me.
metadata.source_text: And you thought of a bezoar all by yourself, did you, Harry? ... That’s the individual spirit a real potion-maker needs!
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I learned I can't cope with horrible potion fumes — I gave up on my antidote and was just trying not to breathe in the awful smell from my cauldron.
metadata.source_text: Ron had given up completely, and was merely trying to avoid breathing in the putrid fumes issuing from his cauldron.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I'm frustrated and a bit defeated about my potion-making here; seeing Harry get praised for a bezoar while I gagged makes me feel useless at times.
metadata.source_text: He sniffed Ernie’s potion and passed on to Ron’s with a grimace. He did not linger over Ron’s cauldron, but backed away swiftly, retching slightly.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I wince when Harry talks about Voldemort and feel uneasy; his determination to probe Slughorn for information worries me but I understand he thinks it's necessary.
metadata.source_text: Look, I had to try and soften him up so I could ask him about Voldemort, didn’t I? Oh, will you get a grip! ... Ron winced at the sound of the name.
metadata.scene_title: Potion Chaos and the Half-Blood Prince’s Tip

metadata.description: I've learned that Slughorn has gone back to treating me warmly but, annoyingly, he hasn't invited me to any of his little evening parties — and neither have Hermione or Ginny.
metadata.source_text: When Harry did not question Slughorn again, the Potions master reverted to his usual affectionate treatment of him, and appeared to have put the matter from his mind. Harry awaited an invitation to one of his little evening parties, determined to accept this time, even if he had to reschedule Quidditch practice. Unfortunately, however, no such invitation arrived. Harry checked with Hermione and Ginny: Neither of them had received an invitation and nor, as far as they knew, had anybody else.

metadata.description: I'm starting to suspect Slughorn might be pretending to forget things on purpose so I can't question him further — he's not as absent-minded as he looks.
metadata.source_text: Harry could not help wondering whether this meant that Slughorn was not quite as forgetful as he appeared, simply determined to give Harry no additional opportunities to question him.

metadata.description: I don't trust Malfoy when he's muttering with Crabbe and Goyle; I'm watching him closely now and I'll follow him if I see him skulking so I can find out what he's up to.
metadata.source_text: I tell my friends what I’m up to, if I want them to keep a lookout for me," Harry said, just loud enough for Malfoy to hear him... "Well, I’m keeping an eye on him from now on," he said firmly. "And the moment I see him lurking somewhere with Crabbe and Goyle keeping watch outside, it’ll be on with the old Invisibility Cloak and off to find out what he’s —

metadata.description: I've discovered nothing in the library that explains what Horcruxes actually do; even the restricted section and the nastiest books have no explanation — only a warning in Magick Moste Evile.
metadata.source_text: I haven’t found one single explanation of what Horcruxes do!" she told him. "Not a single one! I’ve been right through the restricted section and even in the most horrible books, where they tell you how to brew the most gruesome potions — nothing! All I could find was this, in the introduction to Magick Moste Evile — listen — 'Of the Horcrux, wickedest of magical inventions, we shall not speak nor give direction. . . .'

metadata.description: I'm shocked and a bit rattled — the library failing me is unheard of; I'm so surprised I even forgot my annoyance at Harry over the bezoar trick.
metadata.source_text: Meanwhile, the Hogwarts library had failed Hermione for the first time in living memory. She was so shocked, she even forgot that she was annoyed at Harry for his trick with the bezoar.

metadata.description: I've been cross with Harry for the bezoar trick, but my shock at not finding Horcrux information made me forget being annoyed, so my irritation toward him has temporarily eased.
metadata.source_text: She was so shocked, she even forgot that she was annoyed at Harry for his trick with the bezoar.

metadata.description: I've learned that Malfoy was arguing with Crabbe and using Crabbe and Goyle as lookouts for whatever he's planning — Harry told me he heard Malfoy instructing them to keep watch.
metadata.source_text: I don’t know how much longer, all right?" Malfoy shot at him... "Look, it’s none of your business what I’m doing, Crabbe, you and Goyle just do as you’re told and keep a lookout!" "I tell my friends what I’m up to, if I want them to keep them a lookout for me," Harry said...

metadata.description: I'm furious that the Hogsmeade trip was canceled, especially because it was on my birthday — I feel like that's a real blow and not much consolation given recent events.
metadata.source_text: To general indignation, a sign went up on all common room notice boards that the next trip into Hogsmeade had been canceled. Ron was furious. "It was on my birthday!" he said. "I was looking forward to that!"

metadata.description: I'm siding with Harry's plan to keep tabs on Malfoy — I back him when he says they'll use the Invisibility Cloak to follow Malfoy if he sees him skulking.
metadata.source_text: "Well, I’m keeping an eye on him from now on," he said firmly. "And the moment I see him lurking somewhere with Crabbe and Goyle keeping watch outside, it’ll be on with the old Invisibility Cloak and off to find out what he’s —"

metadata.description: I know how to use the Marauder's Map: I tap it, say the words, and it shows who is where in the castle.
metadata.source_text: I solemnly swear that I am up to no good,

metadata.description: I reckon Malfoy disappears from places around the castle in a way that doesn't make sense to me; I don't trust that there's a simple explanation.
metadata.source_text: There had to be an explanation for Malfoy’s periodic disappearances, but he simply could not think what it could be.

metadata.description: I feel exasperated and slightly alarmed by Ron's sudden romantic meltdown; I don't want him acting ridiculous and I'm ready to call him out if he does.
metadata.source_text: Harry gaped at him. He had not expected this and was not sure he wanted to hear it.

metadata.description: I wasn't directly quoted in this scene, but I am aware of school routines and that students' relatives are reported missing in the Prophet, which affects us all.
metadata.source_text: further disappearances had been reported in the Daily Prophet, including several relatives of students at Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I have no new personal dialogue here to change my beliefs, though I'm likely concerned by the disappearances mentioned in the news.
metadata.source_text: further disappearances had been reported in the Daily Prophet, including several relatives of students at Hogwarts.

metadata.description: I wasn't part of the exchange, so I haven't changed my view of Harry or Ron based on this passage specifically.
metadata.source_text: they were woken on the first of March by Seamus and Dean leaving noisily for breakfast.

metadata.description: I've got loads of birthday stuff — a heavy gold watch and Chocolate Cauldrons are brilliant, and Mum and Dad have given me things I think I'll use when I come of age.
metadata.source_text: Seriously good haul this year! See what Mum and Dad got me? Blimey, I think I’ll come of age next year too. . . .

metadata.description: I think I'm in love with Romilda Vane; I can't stop thinking about her and I can't stand that she probably doesn't notice me properly.
metadata.source_text: I think . . . Harry, I think I love her

metadata.description: She's all I can think about right now, and that makes me distracted from Harry and everything else — I'm not myself and I'm easily provoked when anyone mocks how I feel.
metadata.source_text: I can’t stop thinking about her!

metadata.description: I found out those Chocolate Cauldrons Romilda gave Ron were spiked with a love potion — that’s why he attacked me out of nowhere.
metadata.source_text: They’re the Chocolate Cauldrons Romilda gave me before Christmas, and they’re all spiked with love potion!
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I thought Ron had attacked me because he was angry, but I now know he wasn’t himself — the potion made him behave wildly and I feel sorry for him.
metadata.source_text: I thought that he would deserve another punching if I permitted Ron to declare undying love for Romilda Vane. “Yeah, I’ll introduce you,” said Harry, thinking fast.
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: Even though I was tempted to let Ron run amok, I decided he’s still my friend and I’ll help him — I’ll introduce him to Romilda and get him an antidote.
metadata.source_text: But on the other hand, they were supposed to be friends, Ron had not been himself when he had attacked, and Harry thought that he would deserve another punching if he permitted Ron to declare undying love for Romilda Vane.
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I realized Romilda’s name means something to me — hearing her name made me desperate and hopeful, I wanted Harry to introduce me straight away.
metadata.source_text: “Romilda?” he repeated. “Did you say Romilda? Harry — do you know her? Can you introduce me?”
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I believed at first my feelings were real, but after the antidote I understood they were caused by the potion and not true love — I felt devastated when I came back to myself.
metadata.source_text: For a moment, Ron beamed at them. Then, very slowly, his grin sagged and vanished, to be replaced by an expression of utmost horror.
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I trusted Harry to help me — I barged into Slughorn’s room because I wanted him to see Romilda, and I relied on him and Professor Slughorn to fix me.
metadata.source_text: “Harry’s going to introduce me to Romilda Vane.” ... Ron burst through the door ... and muttered, “She didn’t see that, did she?”
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I was not present during these events in the dormitory, so I didn’t see the Levicorpus, the love potion revelation, or the incident in Slughorn’s office.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events in the dormitory and Slughorn’s office.
metadata.scene_title: Cancelled Hogsmeade, Marauder’s Map, and Ron’s Love Potion

metadata.description: I managed to save Ron by getting a bezoar down his throat, and because of that his breathing eased and Madam Pomfrey says he'll have to stay in the hospital wing for about a week taking essence of rue.
metadata.source_text: . . . and then I got the bezoar down his throat and his breathing eased up a bit, Slughorn ran for help, McGonagall and Madam Pomfrey turned up, and they brought Ron up here. They reckon he’ll be all right. Madam Pomfrey says he’ll have to stay here a week or so . . . keep taking essence of rue . . .

metadata.description: I think the poison was in the drink — Slughorn poured it out — and I can’t stop turning cold at how lucky it was that there was a bezoar in the room when I needed it.
metadata.source_text: So the poison was in the drink?” said Fred quietly. “Yes,” said Harry at once; he could think of nothing else and was glad for the opportunity to start discussing it again. “Slughorn poured it out —” “Lucky there was one in the room,” said Harry, who kept turning cold at the thought of what would have happened if he had not been able to lay hands on the little stone.

metadata.description: I've started to think the attacks might be connected to people other than simple schoolyard enemies — Voldemort might want people like Slughorn out of the way, so the motive could be much bigger and more dangerous than petty quarrels.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore reckons Voldemort wanted Slughorn on his side,” said Harry. “Slughorn was in hiding for a year before he came to Hogwarts. And . . .

metadata.description: I feel the Weasleys owe me a lot now — Mrs. Weasley, especially, is very grateful and hugged me, and Mr. Weasley said it was a lucky day when Ron sat in my compartment on the Express.
metadata.source_text: Mrs. Weasley seized hold of Harry and hugged him very tightly. “Dumbledore’s told us how you saved him with the bezoar,” she sobbed. “Oh, Harry, what can we say? You saved Ginny . . . you saved Arthur . . . now you’ve saved Ron . . .” “Half our family does seem to owe you their lives, now I stop and think about it,” Mr. Weasley said in a constricted voice. “Well, all I can say is that it was a lucky day for the Weasleys when Ron decided to sit in your compartment on the Hogwarts Express, Harry.”

metadata.description: I've noticed that both the necklace attack on Katie and Ron’s poisoning ought to have been fatal but weren’t, and that neither attack reached the intended victim, which tells me something important about the attacker’s methods.
metadata.source_text: Well, for one thing, they both ought to have been fatal and weren’t, although that was pure luck. And for another, neither the poison nor the necklace seems to have reached the person who was supposed to be killed.

metadata.description: I'm beginning to believe the person behind these incidents is more dangerous than we first thought because they don't seem to care how many people they finish off before reaching their actual target.
metadata.source_text: Of course,” she added broodingly, “that makes the person behind this even more dangerous in a way, because they don’t seem to care how many people they finish off before they actually reach their victim.”

metadata.description: I'm still Ron's friend and I have been visiting him; even though I've been very quiet and shaken today, I remain concerned for him and engaged with what's happening.
metadata.source_text: She had taken almost no part in Harry and Ginny’s obsessive discussion about how Ron had been poisoned, but merely stood beside them, clench-jawed and frightened-looking, until at last they had been allowed in to see him.

metadata.description: I've been in the forest all day with Aragog and didn't get up to dinner; when I woke in hospital I said I had been reading to Aragog and Professor Sprout told people about me being injured.
metadata.source_text: Bin in the forest all day!” he panted. “Aragog’s worse, I bin readin’ to him — didn’ get up ter dinner till jus’ now an’ then Professor Sprout told me abou’ Ron! How is he?”

metadata.description: I'm surprised and a bit dazed that I'm in the hospital and that people are fussing over me; I sound groggy but I'm asking how I am and reacting to visitors.
metadata.source_text:
Er-my-nee,” croaked Ron unexpectedly from between them.

“Bin in the forest all day!” he panted.... “How is he?” “Not bad,” said Harry. “They say he’ll be okay.”

metadata.description: I'm aware people care a lot about me—Hagrid looks shaken, Mum and Dad rushed to see me, and my friends have been waiting outside; I feel surrounded by their worry even as I'm weak.
metadata.source_text:
I don’ believe this,” said Hagrid hoarsely, shaking his great shaggy head as he stared down at Ron. “Jus’ don’ believe it . . . Look at him lyin’ there. . . . Who’d want ter hurt him, eh?”

Before anybody could respond... Mr. and Mrs. Weasley hurried up the ward.

metadata.description: I met Malfoy up at the castle with a couple of girlfriends, and I noticed he was up there while everyone else was down on the pitch.
metadata.source_text: I met Malfoy," Harry told her quietly, as he pulled his scarlet robes over his head. "So? "So I wanted to know how come he’s up at the castle with a couple of girlfriends while everyone else is down here. . . ."

metadata.description: I’m getting properly fed up with McLaggen — I thought he might be useful but he’s just bossy and careless, and I don’t want him on my team even if he could be world-class.
metadata.source_text: I’ve told you," said Harry patiently, "he could be world-class and I wouldn’t want to keep him. He keeps trying to tell everyone what to do, he thinks he could play every position better than the rest of us. I can’t wait to be shot of him.

metadata.description: I’m annoyed at Ron for pretending to be asleep with Lavender; I want him to be honest with her because the pretending is driving me mad.
metadata.source_text: "will you stop pretending to be asleep when Lavender comes to see you? She’s driving me mad as well."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 2) occurred.
I wasn't present during the events of the changing rooms and match, so I didn't witness the Quidditch play or the argument with McLaggen.
metadata.source_text: I met Malfoy," Harry told her quietly, as he pulled his scarlet robes over his head. "So? "So I wanted to know how come he’s up at the castle with a couple of girlfriends while everyone else is down here. . . ."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 2) occurred.
I wasn't present for the commentary in the stands or Luna's remarks from the podium, so I didn't hear her calling Zacharias Smith 'Loser’s Lurgy' or her cloud observations.
metadata.source_text: ". . . but now that big Hufflepuff player’s got the Quaffle from her, I can’t remember his name, it’s something like Bibble — no, Buggins —" "It’s Cadwallader!" said Professor McGonagall loudly from beside Luna.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 2) occurred.
I found out that Malfoy sneaks off with girls who don’t look like they want to be with him and that he’s missed more than one Quidditch match.
metadata.source_text: I saw Malfoy sneaking off with a couple of girls who didn’t look like they wanted to be with him, and that’s the second time he’s made sure he isn’t down on the Quidditch pitch with the rest of the school; he skipped the last match too, remember?

metadata.description: I’m getting more convinced that Malfoy is up to something and it isn’t just in my head after what I overheard between him and Snape.
metadata.source_text: I want to know what he’s up to. And don’t tell me it’s all in my head, not after what I overheard between him and Snape —

metadata.description: I realised I can use house-elves to tail someone; calling Kreacher and Dobby means I can have them follow Malfoy without missing lessons myself.
metadata.source_text: There was a way to have Malfoy followed — how could he have forgotten... Quietly, tentatively, Harry spoke into the darkness. 'Kreacher?'

metadata.description: I know Dobby is fiercely loyal to me now — he’ll do whatever I ask and is desperate to help — while Kreacher deeply resents me and would rather serve the Malfoys.
metadata.source_text: Dobby will do whatever Harry Potter wants him to do! ... 'Master wants me to spy upon the pure-blood great-nephew of my old mistress?'

metadata.description: I know how to silence Peeves briefly with Langlock and how to use Muffliato to stop Madam Pomfrey from hearing us.
metadata.source_text: Harry pointed his wand hastily at the door of Madam Pomfrey’s office and muttered, 'Muffliato!' ... Harry aimed his wand at Peeves and said, 'Langlock!'

metadata.description: I wasn’t present during the events in the hospital wing that night, so I didn’t witness the quarrel between Kreacher and Dobby or Harry summoning them.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn’t present during the late-night events in the hospital wing, so I didn’t see Harry call Kreacher or watch Dobby and Kreacher fight.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I tried to get a memory from Professor Slughorn after my Potions lesson, but he wouldn't give it to me.
metadata.source_text: Well, I asked Professor Slughorn about it at the end of Potions, sir, but, er, he wouldn't give it to me.

metadata.description: I felt ashamed and realised I hadn't done as much as I should have to retrieve the memory; I know now how important Dumbledore thinks that memory is.
metadata.source_text: A hot, prickly feeling of shame spread from the top of Harry's head all the way down his body.

metadata.description: When Ron was poisoned I prioritised him over Dumbledore's task; I would do the same again — my friends come first, even if it disappoints Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: Well, no, sir, because Ron got poisoned —

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this meeting in Dumbledore's office, so I don't know what was said there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during Dumbledore's conversation with Harry, so I cannot report on their discussion directly.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I learned that Voldemort worked at Borgin and Burkes after leaving Hogwarts; I couldn't believe it when Dumbledore said it out loud.
metadata.source_text: At Borgin and Burkes?" Harry repeated, stunned.

metadata.description: I feel even worse about failing to retrieve the Horcrux memory because Dumbledore clearly values my opinion and judgement highly.
metadata.source_text: The idea that Dumbledore valued his opinion this highly made Harry feel even more deeply ashamed that he had failed in the task of retrieving the Horcrux memory, and he shifted guiltily in his seat

metadata.description: I'm surprised and a bit unsettled to learn how much Dumbledore distrusts the idea of Voldemort returning to Hogwarts, and I now see Dumbledore was actively wary of him even then.
metadata.source_text: I had advised Armando against the appointment — I did not give the reasons I have given you, for Professor Dippet was very fond of Voldemort and convinced of his honesty. But I did not want Lord Voldemort back at this school, and especially not in a position of power.

metadata.description: I was not present during the discussion about Tom Riddle and Voldemort, so I do not know the details of the memories Dumbledore examined.
metadata.source_text: If it was difficult to find evidence about the boy Riddle, it has been almost impossible to find anyone prepared to reminisce about the man Voldemort.

metadata.description: I wasn't there for Dumbledore's account of Voldemort leaving Hogwarts or the Pensieve memories, so I can't say what Hokey saw.
metadata.source_text: I shall then be glad of your opinion as to whether the conclusions I have drawn from them seem likely.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I've found out Malfoy has been sneaking up to the seventh floor to get into the Room of Requirement, and that explains why he disappears from the Marauder's Map.
metadata.source_text: That’s where he’s been sneaking off to! That’s where he’s doing . . . whatever he’s doing! And I bet that’s why he’s been disappearing off the map — come to think of it, I’ve never seen the Room of Requirement on there!

metadata.description: I realised Malfoy must have nicked some Polyjuice Potion from Slughorn’s stores in the dungeon; that would let him disguise Crabbe and Goyle so they can stand guard unseen.
metadata.source_text: He could’ve nicked some any time during that lesson. . . . Nicked what?... Polyjuice Potion. He stole some of the Polyjuice Potion Slughorn showed us in our first Potions lesson.

metadata.description: I used to be unsure how to catch Malfoy, but now I believe we’ve him cornered because we know where he’s going and what he’s using — I’m actually excited and confident about spying on him.
metadata.source_text: How good’s this? We know where Malfoy’s going! We’ve got him cornered now!

metadata.description: I’ve set Kreacher and Dobby to follow Malfoy, and they reported back — I trust them enough to help gather this information even though Hermione gets touchy about house-elves.
metadata.source_text: Well . . . they’ve been following Malfoy for me, Night and day," croaked Kreacher. "Dobby has not slept for a week, Harry Potter!" said Dobby proudly

metadata.description: I've learned that the Room of Requirement can change its properties depending on what someone needs — it could make itself Unplottable or become different for different users.
metadata.source_text: I think it’ll be part of the magic of the room. If you need it to be Unplottable, it will be.

metadata.description: I’d thought we could simply sneak in and see what Malfoy’s doing, but now I think Harry won’t know what to ask the Room to become because Malfoy may be using a different need to define it.
metadata.source_text: But you don’t know what the room becomes when Malfoy goes in there, so you don’t know what to ask it to transform into.

metadata.description: I’m still protective about house-elves and uncomfortable with Harry assigning them to spy, so I gently scold him and try to ensure Dobby isn’t overworked — I care about their well-being.
metadata.source_text: You haven’t slept, Dobby? But surely, Harry, you didn’t tell him not to —

metadata.description: I know Harry can Apparate — he’s only done it once, but he did manage to disappear and reappear in his hoop in lessons, so he shouldn’t have trouble in July.
metadata.source_text: At least you can Apparate, though! You’ll have no trouble come July!" "I’ve only done it once," Harry reminded him; he had finally managed to disappear and rematerialize inside his hoop during their previous lesson.

metadata.description: I keep thinking Lavender won’t let go, but the more I hint I want to finish my essay the tighter she holds on — I’m starting to wish she’d dump me so I could get my work done.
metadata.source_text: But the more I hint I want to finish it, the tighter she holds on. It’s like going out with the giant squid.

metadata.description: I’m grateful Hermione helps with my essay and even lends me things, and I tell her I love her in a daft, embarrassed way — I know she doesn’t want Lavender to hear.
metadata.source_text: "I love you, Hermione," said Ron, sinking back in his chair, rubbing his eyes wearily. Hermione turned faintly pink, but merely said, "Don’t let Lavender hear you saying that."

metadata.description: I've worked out that Malfoy might have been using Crabbe and Goyle disguised as girls to listen in or to warn him, and that we've actually passed them without realising.
metadata.source_text: Those two girls I saw him with when he missed Quidditch — ha! Crabbe and Goyle!" "Do you mean to say," said Hermione in a hushed voice, "that that little girl whose scales I repaired — ?" "Yeah, of course!" said Harry loudly, staring at her. "Of course! Malfoy must’ve been inside the room at the time, so she — what am I talking about? — he dropped the scales to tell Malfoy not to come out, because there was someone there! And there was that girl who dropped the toadspawn too! We’ve been walking past him all the time and not realizing it!"

metadata.description: I now reckon Malfoy is more dangerous or sneaky than I thought — he might have shown Crabbe and Goyle his Dark Mark to keep them in line.
metadata.source_text: "Well, they wouldn’t, would they, if he’s shown them his Dark Mark?" said Harry.

metadata.description: I still believe getting Slughorn's memory is the priority, but I feel justified wanting to find out what Malfoy is doing until I can get that memory.
metadata.source_text: "I haven’t forgotten about Slughorn, but I haven’t got a clue how to get that memory off him, and until I get a brain wave why shouldn’t I find out what Malfoy’s doing?"

metadata.description: Hermione is being sensible and bossy in the best way — she keeps reminding me that Slughorn's memory is what we should be concentrating on, which annoys me but I know she's right.
metadata.source_text: "But, Harry, before you get all excited, I still don’t think you’ll be able to get into the Room of Requirement without knowing what’s there first. And I don’t think you should forget" — she heaved her bag onto her shoulder and gave him a very serious look — "that what you’re supposed to be concentrating on is getting that memory from Slughorn. Good night."

metadata.description: I read the Prophet and learned that Mundungus Fletcher has been arrested and sent to Azkaban for impersonating an Inferius during a burglary, and that Octavius Pepper has vanished.
metadata.source_text: "But it’s all right, he’s not dead — it’s Mundungus, he’s been arrested and sent to Azkaban! Something to do with impersonating an Inferius during an attempted burglary . . . and someone called Octavius Pepper has vanished. . . ."

metadata.description: I'm still convinced that the right approach is to persuade Slughorn to give up the memory by appealing to his better nature rather than tricking or bewitching him.
metadata.source_text: "You need to persuade Slughorn," said Hermione. "It’s not a question of tricking him or bewitching him, or Dumbledore could have done it in a second... you should go and find Slughorn and start appealing to his better nature."

metadata.description: I trust that Harry cares about the memory from Slughorn, but I am exasperated with him for wanting to run off after Malfoy when our primary task is getting that memory.
metadata.source_text: "But, Harry, before you get all excited, I still don’t think you’ll be able to get into the Room of Requirement without knowing what’s there first... that what you’re supposed to be concentrating on is getting that memory from Slughorn."

metadata.description: Blimey, I've realised I really can't Apparate properly yet and I might as well do extra practice sessions in Hogsmeade before deciding to take the test.
metadata.source_text: "You’d do better," said Hermione... "I’ll do the practice sessions in Hogsmeade before I decide about taking the test."

metadata.description: I find the idea of Crabbe and Goyle transformed into girls hilarious and that makes me think Malfoy must be getting away with some cheeky, bullying tricks.
metadata.source_text: "He’s got Crabbe and Goyle transforming into girls?" guffawed Ron. "Blimey . . . No wonder they don’t look too happy these days. . . . I’m surprised they don’t tell him to stuff it. . . ."

metadata.description: I still back Harry on trying things his way sometimes, but I want practical advice — like practising Apparition — and I enjoy teasing and joking even when things are serious.
metadata.source_text: "Wish I could Disapparate like a house-elf," said Ron, staring at the spot where Dobby had vanished. "I’d have that Apparition Test in the bag."

metadata.description: I found Gregory Goyle alone on the seventh-floor corridor while most students were in their common rooms.
metadata.source_text: and there, alone in the seventh-floor corridor, was Gregory Goyle.

metadata.description: I heard what sounded like a quickly stifled old gramophone when I knocked at the office the second time.
metadata.source_text: though on the second occasion he was sure he had heard the quickly stifled sounds of an old gramophone.

metadata.description: The Room of Requirement can be open even if the Marauder's Map doesn't show it; I believed if Goyle stood guard outside it, the room was open whether the map registered it or not.
metadata.source_text: if Goyle was standing guard outside it, the room was open, whether the map was aware of it or not.

metadata.description: I felt more powerful and confident when I thought Malfoy was trapped behind the wall and couldn't appear; it made me want to try every way to force him out.
metadata.source_text: It gave Harry a most agreeable feeling of power as he tried to remember what form of words he had not yet tried.

metadata.description: I became frustrated and impatient after many failed attempts to get the wall to reveal a door, even kicking it in anger.
metadata.source_text: Losing his patience completely, Harry ran at the wall and kicked it.

metadata.description: I felt sympathy and shared my grief when I said I missed Sirius and apologized after I saw Tonks' eyes fill with tears.
metadata.source_text: I miss him, as well. . . ." "What?" said Tonks blankly, as though she had not heard him.

metadata.description: I've noticed Tonks abandoning her post to go see Dumbledore when he wasn't there, and I find that behaviour odd and concerning.
metadata.source_text: She’s supposed to be guarding the school, why’s she suddenly abandoning her post to come and see Dumbledore when he’s not even here?

metadata.description: I'm more worried now; Tonks acting strangely makes me concerned about what is happening at the school and why she would rush to Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: It’s a bit odd," said Hermione, who for some reason looked very concerned.

metadata.description: I find the idea that Tonks might have loved Sirius plausible enough to consider, though I remain unsure and puzzled by her motives.
metadata.source_text: It’s a thought," said Hermione slowly.

metadata.description: I managed to Apparate, even if I overshot and landed nearer Scrivenshaft's than Madam Puddifoot's, so I have made progress with Apparition.
metadata.source_text: I was supposed to be Apparating to outside Madam Puddifoot’s Tea Shop and I overshot it a bit, ended up near Scrivenshaft’s, but at least I moved!

metadata.description: I reckon Tonks is 'gone a bit funny' and has lost her nerve since what happened at the Ministry; I think it's made her shaky.
metadata.source_text: If you ask me," said Ron ... "she’s cracking up a bit. Losing her nerve after what happened at the Ministry.

metadata.description: I'm inclined to dismiss Tonks' upset as being emotional and quickly attribute it to women being easily upset, rather than consider deeper reasons.
metadata.source_text: Women," he said wisely to Harry, "they’re easily upset."

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid sent a tear-soaked note telling us Aragog died and asking us to come to his burial at dusk.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Aragog died last night. ... It would mean a lot to me if you’d nip down for the burial later this evening. I’m planning on doing it round dusk, that was his favorite time of day. ... Hagrid

metadata.description: I reckon Malfoy’s mission is going badly — he looked thinner and paler, without his old swagger, so whatever Voldemort sent him to do isn’t working.
metadata.source_text: But there was no air of smugness, excitement, or superiority; none of the swagger that he had had on the Hogwarts Express, when he had boasted openly of the mission he had been given by Voldemort. . . . There could be only one conclusion, in Harry’s opinion: The mission, whatever it was, was going badly.

metadata.description: I feel like I can’t rely on Malfoy being boastful anymore — he’s not the same arrogance he showed before, so my view of him as openly confident has shifted.
metadata.source_text: But there was no air of smugness, excitement, or superiority; none of the swagger that he had had on the Hogwarts Express, when he had boasted openly of the mission he had been given by Voldemort.

metadata.description: I found out from Hagrid’s note that Aragog died last night and Hagrid asked us to attend the burial at dusk, though he knows we aren’t supposed to be out that late.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Aragog died last night. ... It would mean a lot to me if you’d nip down for the burial later this evening. I’m planning on doing it round dusk, that was his favorite time of day. I know you’re not supposed to be out that late, but you can use the cloak.

metadata.description: I’m more convinced than ever that Harry must get that memory — all these dreadful happenings, like werewolf attacks and Death Eater violence, tie straight back to stopping Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: Harry, you’ve got to get that memory ... It’s all about stopping Voldemort, isn’t it? These dreadful things that are happening are all down to him. . . .

metadata.description: I trust Harry’s judgment when he says he’ll try Slughorn and, if needed, use Felix — I see he’s willing to take big risks for the greater goal.
metadata.source_text: Well . . . okay. If I can’t get Slughorn to talk this afternoon, I’ll take some Felix and have another go this evening.

metadata.description: I learned from Hagrid’s note that Aragog had died and Hagrid wanted us to come to the burial at dusk, which I thought was mental given Aragog’s history.
metadata.source_text: Dear Harry, Ron, and Hermione, Aragog died last night. ... It would mean a lot to me if you’d nip down for the burial later this evening. ... Hagrid

metadata.description: I’m angrier than before about Aragog — after what it tried to do to Harry and me, I want even less to go and cry over its body.
metadata.source_text: He’s mental! ... That thing told its mates to eat Harry and me! Told them to help themselves! And now Hagrid expects us to go down there and cry over its horrible hairy body!

metadata.description: I feel more protective of Harry and less willing to risk him for sentiment — if it came to saving Aragog I’d be even more against it now.
metadata.source_text: We’ve risked a lot to help Hagrid out, but after all — Aragog’s dead. If it were a question of saving him — "— I’d want to go even less," said Ron firmly.

metadata.description: I found out Filch had forgotten to lock the front door — I opened it and breathed the smell of clean air and grass before heading out.
metadata.source_text: When he reached the entrance hall he saw that Filch had forgotten to lock the front door. Beaming, Harry threw it open and breathed in the smell of clean air and grass for a moment before walking down the steps into the dusk.

metadata.description: I discovered Professor Slughorn was in the vegetable patch talking to Professor Sprout about picking plants at twilight and carrying leaves for his third years.
metadata.source_text: Professor Sprout headed off into the gathering darkness in the direction of her greenhouses, and Slughorn directed his steps to the spot where Harry stood, invisible... 'most authorities agree that they are at their most efficacious if picked at twilight.' 'Oh, I quite agree,' said Professor Sprout warmly. 'That enough for you?' 'Plenty, plenty,' said Slughorn, who, Harry saw, was carrying an armful of leafy plants.'

metadata.description: I learned Aragog had died and Hagrid was devastated; Hagrid wanted company while burying him, so I decided to go and tell the truth to people who might help.
metadata.source_text: 'Well, sir, it’s Hagrid,' said Harry, who knew that the right thing to do just now was to tell the truth. 'He’s pretty upset. . . . But you won’t tell anyone, Professor? I don’t want trouble for him. . . .'

metadata.description: I felt certain the Felix Felicis was guiding me — I knew going to Hagrid’s was the right thing even though I couldn’t see the whole way; the potion made the path feel lit step by step.
metadata.source_text: Why he knew that going to Hagrid’s was the right thing to do, he had no idea. It was as though the potion was illuminating a few steps of the path at a time: He could not see the final destination...

metadata.description: I think Slughorn’s curiosity can be useful — he agreed to come to Hagrid’s and help pay respects, even if I noticed he was thinking about venom's value; I feel he can be persuaded to act kindly.
metadata.source_text: 'Well,' he said, with a most convincing hesitancy, 'well, if you wanted to come, Professor, Hagrid would probably be really pleased. . . .' 'Yes, of course,' said Slughorn, his eyes now gleaming with enthusiasm. 'I tell you what, Harry, I’ll meet you down there with a bottle or two.'

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the burial at Hagrid's; I didn't go with Harry to see Aragog laid to rest and so I don't have first-hand knowledge of those events.
I wasn't there for Aragog's funeral; I couldn't come with Harry and Hagrid and missed the burial and Slughorn's speech.
I learned that Slughorn procured a memory for me: he pulled out a silvery thread from his mind with his wand, bottled it, and gave it to me.
metadata.source_text: Still looking into Harry’s eyes, Slughorn touched the tip of his wand to his temple and withdrew it, so that a long, silver thread of memory came away too, clinging to the wand-tip. ... Slughorn lowered it into the bottle where it coiled, then spread, swirling like gas. He corked the bottle with a trembling hand and then passed it across the table to Harry.

metadata.description: I found out that my Refilling Charm worked silently when I pointed my wand under the table and the bottles began to refill without anyone noticing.
metadata.source_text: he pointed his wand under the table at the emptying bottles and they immediately began to refill.

metadata.description: I became certain I am the Chosen One and that I must kill Voldemort; this conviction lets me demand Slughorn's memory because Dumbledore and I need it.
metadata.source_text: I am the Chosen One. I have to kill him. I need that memory.

metadata.description: I now see Slughorn as someone ashamed but ultimately capable of doing the brave thing — he gave me the memory despite his fear and embarrassment.
metadata.source_text: He put his other hand inside his cloak and took out a small, empty bottle... He corked the bottle with a trembling hand and then passed it across the table to Harry.

metadata.description: I was not present for the events in Hagrid's hut; I did not witness Aragog's funeral or Slughorn giving Harry a memory.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not present during the conversation in Hagrid's hut and did not see Slughorn extract or bottle any memory for Harry.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I've learned that the password to the Fat Lady's portrait changed at midnight, so if I arrive after that I'm locked out and have to sleep in the corridor.
metadata.source_text: Well, the password changed at midnight, so you’ll just have to sleep in the corridor, won’t you?
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I've learned from Nearly Headless Nick that Dumbledore returned to Hogwarts about an hour ago and was reported to be in his office after attending to some business.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore returned to the school an hour ago.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I believed Dumbledore might not be back yet, but now I'm excited because I think he'll be in his office and I can tell him I secured the memory.
metadata.source_text: Professor Dumbledore returned to the school an hour ago.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I feel like Dumbledore is the person to go to about security and problems; when the Fat Lady says to take it up with the headmaster, I immediately think of him and want to tell him my news.
metadata.source_text: If you’re angry, go and take it up with the headmaster, he’s the one who’s tightened security.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the corridor and at the Fat Lady's portrait, so I don't know what Hermione did or said here.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the corridor and at the Fat Lady's portrait, so I don't know what Ron did or said here.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Returns to the Castle and Sneaks to Dumbledore

metadata.description: I was not present when Entrance to Dumbledore’s Office and the Reveal of the Memory occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Entrance to Dumbledore’s Office and the Reveal of the Memory

metadata.description: I was not present when Entrance to Dumbledore’s Office and the Reveal of the Memory occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
metadata.scene_title: Entrance to Dumbledore’s Office and the Reveal of the Memory

metadata.description: I've learned that a Horcrux is an object in which someone can hide part of their soul so they cannot wholly die if their body is destroyed.
metadata.source_text: A Horcrux is the word used for an object in which a person has concealed part of their soul.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains Horcruxes — Memory of Slughorn’s Conversation

metadata.description: I now believe that Tom Riddle (Voldemort) tried to make himself immortal by splitting his soul and hiding pieces in objects, and that this explains how he survived my attack.
metadata.source_text: At the same age as you are now, give or take a few months, Tom Riddle was doing all he could to find out how to make himself immortal.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains Horcruxes — Memory of Slughorn’s Conversation

metadata.description: I feel more certain that Dumbledore was right to be cautious about Voldemort; I trust him more because he explains that the diary I destroyed was actually a Horcrux-like piece of Riddle's soul.
metadata.source_text: You handed it to me, Harry, the diary, Riddle's diary, the one giving instructions on how to reopen the Chamber of Secrets.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains Horcruxes — Memory of Slughorn’s Conversation

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in Dumbledore's office when Slughorn's memory was viewed, so I don't know exactly what was said in that Pensieve memory.
metadata.source_text: For a moment or two, the headmaster looked stunned. Then his face split in a wide smile.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains Horcruxes — Memory of Slughorn’s Conversation

metadata.description: I wasn't in Dumbledore's office when the Pensieve memory was shown and cannot say what I would have seen or heard about Riddle and Horcruxes.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore landed beside Harry just as Riddle asked, 'Sir, is it true that Professor Merrythought is retiring?'
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Explains Horcruxes — Memory of Slughorn’s Conversation

metadata.description: I've learned that the diary was a Horcrux — a piece of soul hidden inside an object so the owner could not wholly die.
metadata.source_text: Well, it worked as a Horcrux is supposed to work — in other words, the fragment of soul concealed inside it was kept safe and had undoubtedly played its part in preventing the death of its owner.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals the Horcrux Theory and Voldemort’s Plans

metadata.description: I used to think Voldemort might have been desperate and alone in seeking immortality, but now I realise he deliberately cut his soul into parts and intended multiple Horcruxes — that's far worse than I imagined.
metadata.source_text: The careless way in which Voldemort regarded this Horcrux seemed most ominous to me. It suggested that he must have made — or been planning to make — more Horcruxes, so that the loss of his first would not be so detrimental.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals the Horcrux Theory and Voldemort’s Plans

metadata.description: I feel a new, heavier responsibility toward Dumbledore and our mission; learning he destroyed one Horcrux and risked his life to stop Voldemort makes me see him as personally invested and willing to sacrifice.
metadata.source_text: You are forgetting . . . you have already destroyed one of them. And I have destroyed another. "You have?" said Harry eagerly. "Yes indeed," said Dumbledore, and he raised his blackened, burned-looking hand. "The ring, Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals the Horcrux Theory and Voldemort’s Plans

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this conversation about the diary and Horcruxes, so I don't have a firsthand account of the exchange between Harry and Dumbledore.
metadata.source_text: The diary had been a Horcrux. But this raised as many questions as it answered.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals the Horcrux Theory and Voldemort’s Plans

metadata.description: I was not in the room when Dumbledore explained Horcruxes and when Harry destroyed the diary, therefore I didn't witness the details of that revelation.
metadata.source_text: I still don't understand," said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Reveals the Horcrux Theory and Voldemort’s Plans

metadata.description: I learned that the ring I heard about was indeed a Horcrux and that Dumbledore found it hidden in the ruin of the Gaunts' house, protected by strong enchantments.
metadata.source_text: I stumbled across the ring hidden in the ruin of the Gaunts’ house.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: I learned that Voldemort made multiple Horcruxes — that the diary was one and the ring another, and Dumbledore thinks four Horcruxes still remain.
metadata.source_text: You destroyed the diary and I the ring, but if we are right in our theory of a seven-part soul, four Horcruxes remain.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: I learned Dumbledore suspects Hufflepuff's cup and Slytherin's locket are Horcruxes three and four, and that Nagini might be a Horcrux too.
metadata.source_text: I would be prepared to bet — perhaps not my other hand — but a couple of fingers, that they became Horcruxes three and four.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: I learned that Dumbledore thinks Voldemort possibly wanted objects from the four founders and that he was turned away from Hogwarts before he could search the school.
metadata.source_text: Four objects from the four founders would, I am sure, have exerted a powerful pull over Voldemort’s imagination... he was turned away, or so I believe, without the chance to search the school.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: I feel more certain now that destroying Horcruxes will make Voldemort mortal and that I'm allowed to help in finding and destroying them — Dumbledore said I have earned that right.
metadata.source_text: And if you do, can I come with you and help get rid of it?... Yes, I think so... I think you have earned that right.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: My understanding of the prophecy shifted: I see Dumbledore's point that the prophecy mattered because Voldemort acted on it, and that I'm not bound by fate — I choose to fight because I want him finished.
metadata.source_text: If Voldemort had never heard of the prophecy, would it have been fulfilled?... I’d want him finished... And I’d want to do it.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of Remaining Horcruxes and Harry’s Role

metadata.description: I feel closer to Dumbledore in a new way because he trusts me to help hunt Horcruxes; his permission lifts something heavy inside me and makes me feel respected and involved.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I think so... I think you have earned that right.

metadata.description: I've just learned that Katie Bell has been released from St. Mungo's and that she doesn't remember who gave her that necklace — she only recalls walking into the ladies' in the Three Broomsticks.
metadata.source_text:
“I’m really well!” she said happily. “They let me out of St. Mungo’s on Monday, I had a couple of days at home with Mum and Dad and then came back here this morning. Leanne was just telling me about McLaggen and the last match, Harry. . . .”

“Yeah,” said Harry, “well, now you’re back and Ron’s fit, we’ll have a decent chance of thrashing Ravenclaw, which means we could still be in the running for the Cup. Listen, Katie . . .”

“. . . that necklace . . . can you remember who gave it to you now?”

“No,” said Katie, shaking her head ruefully. “Everyone’s been asking me, but I haven’t got a clue. The last thing I remember was walking into the ladies’ in the Three Broomsticks.”
metadata.scene_title: Katie Bell's Return and Discussion of Polyjuice

metadata.description: I'm starting to think the person who gave Katie the necklace might not have been simply a woman — they could have looked like a woman by using Polyjuice, since some Polyjuice was stolen from Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text:
“So it must have been a girl or a woman who gave Katie the necklace,” said Hermione, “to be in the ladies’ bathroom.”

“Or someone who looked like a girl or a woman,” said Harry. “Don’t forget, there was a cauldron full of Polyjuice Potion at Hogwarts. We know some of it got stolen. . . .”
metadata.scene_title: Katie Bell's Return and Discussion of Polyjuice

metadata.description: I'm finding myself desperate enough about finding the truth that I nearly let Ginny slip from my thoughts; the Katie situation has pushed my curiosity and urgency sharply to the front.
metadata.source_text: He had to put the question to her at once; his curiosity even drove Ginny temporarily from his brain.
metadata.scene_title: Katie Bell's Return and Discussion of Polyjuice

metadata.description: I've established that Katie Bell was released from St. Mungo's and that she went back to Hogwarts the same morning, but she cannot remember who gave her the necklace — only that she pushed open the bathroom door.
metadata.source_text:
“I’m really well!” she said happily. “They let me out of St. Mungo’s on Monday, I had a couple of days at home with Mum and Dad and then came back here this morning. Leanne was just telling me about McLaggen and the last match, Harry. . . .”

“’You definitely went into the bathroom, then?’ said Hermione.”

“‘Well, I know I pushed open the door,’ said Katie, ‘so I suppose whoever Imperiused me was standing just behind it. After that, my memory’s a blank until about two weeks ago in St. Mungo’s.’”
metadata.scene_title: Katie Bell's Return and Discussion of Polyjuice

metadata.description: No — I didn’t mean it to happen. I thought I might test the spell on McLaggen, but after seeing Malfoy bleeding I know using unknown curses is terrifyingly dangerous.

metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.description: I feel let down by Harry's defence of the book; I don't like defending dangerous practices and I'm irritated that he still sticks up for the Prince's notes instead of seeing how harmful they can be.
metadata.source_text: I don’t believe this. You’re actually defending —
metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.source_text: Where’ve you — ? Why are you soaking — ? Is that blood? ... I need your book, ... Your Potions book. Quick . . . give it to me . . .
metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and defensive about people laying into Harry; even if I worry about what happened, I don't want Hermione to gloat — I'm backing Harry against needless blame.

metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.description: I still stand by Harry even when everyone's shouting; I'm surprised and relieved when Ginny defends him too, so I'm more solidly on his side now.

metadata.scene_title: Bathroom Duel: Sectumsempra, Snape's Intervention, and Punishment

metadata.description: I found out Professor Trelawney tried to get into the Room of Requirement and that there was someone else inside whooping.
metadata.source_text:
I — well — I didn’t know students knew about —

"Not all of them do," said Harry. "But what happened? You screamed. . . . It sounded as though you were hurt. . . ."

"I — well," said Professor Trelawney, drawing her shawls around her defensively and staring down at him with her vastly magnified eyes. "I wished to — ah — deposit certain — um — personal items in the room. . . ."

"Right," said Harry, glancing down at the sherry bottles. "But you couldn’t get in and hide them?"

"Oh, I got in all right," said Professor Trelawney, glaring at the wall. "But there was somebody already in there."

"Somebody in — ? Who?" demanded Harry.

"I have no idea," said Professor Trelawney, looking slightly taken aback at the urgency in Harry’s voice. "I walked into the room and I heard a voice, which has never happened before in all my years of hiding — of using the room, I mean."

"A voice? Saying what?"

"I don’t know that it was saying anything," said Professor Trelawney. "It was . . . whooping."

metadata.description: Dumbledore sent for me urgently; Jimmy gave me his parchment telling me to come to Dumbledore’s office as quick as I can.
metadata.source_text: "Thanks, Jimmy . . . Hey, it’s from Dumbledore!" said Harry excitedly, unrolling the parchment and scanning it. "He wants me to go to his office as quick as I can!"

metadata.description: I'm more convinced the Half-Blood Prince is male; I just know from the way he writes that the Prince was a bloke.
metadata.source_text: "Listen, Hermione, I can tell it’s not a girl. I can just tell."

metadata.description: I feel irritated at Snape because his detentions keep me away from Ginny and seem deliberately punitive.
metadata.source_text: "And he’s hinting now that if I don’t get all the boxes done by the end of term, we’ll carry on next year." He was finding these detentions particularly irksome because they cut into the already limited time he could have been spending with Ginny.

metadata.description: I found an old Daily Prophet clipping showing Eileen Prince, captain of the Hogwarts Gobstones team, and I think Eileen Prince could be the Half-Blood Prince.
metadata.source_text:
Right!" said Hermione, red patches blazing in her cheeks as she pulled a very old piece of newsprint out of her pocket and slammed it down on the table in front of Harry. "Look at that! Look at the picture!"

The picture showed a skinny girl of around fifteen.

"Her name was Eileen Prince. Prince, Harry."

metadata.description: I’m persuaded that the Half-Blood Prince might be someone called Prince, possibly a woman whose father’s surname was Prince and whose mother was a Muggle, making 'Half-Blood Prince' a literal possibility.
metadata.source_text: "Well, why not? Harry, there aren’t any real princes in the Wizarding world! It’s either a nickname, a made-up title somebody’s given themselves, or it could be their actual name, couldn’t it? No, listen! If, say, her father was a wizard whose surname was Prince, and her mother was a Muggle, then that would make her a ‘half-blood Prince’!"

metadata.description: I’m annoyed with Harry for dismissing the idea that a girl could be clever enough to be the Prince; I feel underestimated by him.
metadata.source_text: "The truth is that you don’t think a girl would have been clever enough," said Hermione angrily.

metadata.description: I know the Half-Blood Prince’s bezoar tip saved me once; without that help I might not be here to joke about it.
metadata.source_text: "He was a genius, the Prince. Anyway . . . without his bezoar tip . . ." He drew his finger significantly across his own throat.

metadata.description: I still think the Prince was a genius and that the book and its tips can be proper useful, even if some spells worry me.
metadata.source_text:
"'Course not," said Ron robustly. "He was a genius, the Prince. Anyway . . . without his bezoar tip . . ."

"I mean, I’m not saying that spell you used on Malfoy was great —"

"Nor am I," said Harry quickly.

metadata.description: I’m comfortable giving Ginny teasing permission about boys, but I’ll remind her I can withdraw that permission if needed; I still feel possessive but jokey about relationships.
metadata.source_text: "Watch it," he said, pointing warningly at Harry and Ginny. "Just because I’ve given my permission doesn’t mean I can’t withdraw it —"

metadata.description: I just learned that Professor Trelawney heard a happy male voice celebrating and then was hurled headfirst out of the room when everything went pitch-black.
metadata.source_text: “I would hazard a guess at male,” said Professor Trelawney. “And it sounded happy?” “Very happy,” said Professor Trelawney sniffily. “As though it was celebrating?” “Most definitely.” ... “And then I called out ‘Who’s there?’” ... “Everything went pitch-black and the next thing I knew, I was being hurled headfirst out of the room!”

metadata.description: I found out that Snape overheard Trelawney's prophecy and carried the news to Voldemort, meaning Snape's eavesdropping set the events leading to my parents' deaths into motion.
metadata.source_text: “And now Harry was paying attention properly for the first time, for he knew what had happened then: Professor Trelawney had made the prophecy ... “. . . but then we were rudely interrupted by Severus Snape!” “What?” “Yes, there was a commotion outside the door and it flew open, and there was that rather uncouth barman standing with Snape ...”

metadata.description: Dumbledore believes he has located a Horcrux hidden in a coastal cave where Tom Riddle once terrorized two children from his orphanage.
metadata.source_text: “I believe so.” ... “I believe it to be hidden in a cave on the coast many miles from here, a cave I have been trying to locate for a very long time: the cave in which Tom Riddle once terrorized two children from his orphanage on their annual trip; you remember?”

metadata.description: I feel furious and betrayed toward Snape — I now believe he is directly responsible for Voldemort hunting my mum and dad because he listened at the door.
metadata.source_text: “Snape!” he said, very loudly, ... “Snape’s what’s happened! He told Voldemort about the prophecy, it was him, he listened outside the door, Trelawney told me!”

metadata.description: I no longer see Severus Snape as merely a harsh teacher; I see him as the man whose actions led to my parents' deaths, and that changes everything between us for me.
metadata.source_text: “It was Snape who had overheard the prophecy. It was Snape who had carried the news of the prophecy to Voldemort. Snape and Peter Pettigrew together had sent Voldemort hunting after Lily and James and their son.”

I learned that the cliff was used by Tom Riddle to take young victims and that no ordinary Muggle could reach the rock because the cliffs and sea are too dangerous.
metadata.source_text: No Muggle could reach this rock unless they were uncommonly good mountaineers, and boats cannot approach the cliffs, the waters around them are too dangerous.

metadata.description: I found out the entrance into the cliff was concealed and that Dumbledore could detect and open it by touch and ritual, then heal himself after cutting his own arm.
metadata.source_text: Here," he said. "We go on through here. The entrance is concealed."

metadata.description: I discovered the inner cavern contains a huge black lake with a misty green glow in its middle, and that the Horcrux is likely located toward that central light.
metadata.source_text: An eerie sight met their eyes: They were standing on the edge of a great black lake... A misty greenish light shone far away in what looked like the middle of the lake... "I think the Horcrux is in the middle."

metadata.description: I had expected a simple way to reach the Horcrux, but after my failed Summoning and seeing the lake react, I now believe the defenses are active and dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Accio Horcrux! ... The surface of the lake was once more shining black glass: The ripples had vanished unnaturally fast;

metadata.description: I'm reminded how much I rely on Professor Dumbledore's calm judgement and knowledge; I follow his lead and trust his decisions in dangerous situations.
metadata.source_text: Then, after two solid minutes, Dumbledore said quietly, "Oh, surely not. So crude."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the cliff, the tunnel, or the underground lake, so I cannot say what happened there from personal observation.
I wasn't present for the trip down the cliff, the opening of the concealed entrance, or the exploration of the subterranean lake, so I have no direct knowledge of those events.
I saw Dumbledore make a coppery-green chain and a tiny ghostly boat appear from the lake and learned Voldemort left magical traces other wizards can read.
metadata.source_text: Immediately a thick coppery green chain appeared out of thin air, extending from the depths of the water into Dumbledore’s clenched hand.

metadata.description: I discovered the lake holds dead bodies and that they can move or leap out of the water — they drift beneath the surface and one jumped when I Summoned the Horcrux.
metadata.source_text: When I tried to Summon the Horcrux, a body leapt out of the lake.

metadata.description: I felt less reassured by Dumbledore's calm; seeing corpses and learning they might become hostile made me more frightened and doubtful about how safe we are.
metadata.source_text: There are bodies in here! ... Yes, said Dumbledore placidly, but we do not need to worry about them at the moment.

metadata.description: I learned that the emerald basin cannot be touched, Transfigured, Charmed, or siphoned — only drinking it will let someone reach the Horcrux inside.
metadata.source_text: This potion cannot be penetrated by hand, Vanished, parted, scooped up, or siphoned away, nor can it be Transfigured, Charmed, or otherwise made to change its nature.

metadata.description: I understood that Voldemort set traps not merely to kill intruders immediately but to study and punish them; Dumbledore says Voldemort would keep a survivor alive to learn how they got in.
metadata.source_text: He would want to keep them alive long enough to find out how they managed to penetrate so far through his defenses and, most importantly of all, why they were so intent upon emptying the basin.

metadata.description: I felt burdened and uneasy about my role: Dumbledore expects me to force him to drink and keep drinking if necessary, and that changes how I see our dynamic — I'm both obedient and terrified.
metadata.source_text: It will be your job to make sure I keep drinking, even if you have to tip the potion into my protesting mouth. You understand?

metadata.source_text: You… you can’t stop, Professor," said Harry. "You’ve got to keep drinking, remember? You told me you had to keep drinking. Here…

metadata.description: I discovered that water produced by Aguamenti can be made to vanish by whatever protections Voldemort placed on the Horcrux cave, so only lake water remained reliable.
metadata.source_text: The goblet filled with clear water; Harry dropped to his knees beside Dumbledore, raised his head, and brought the glass to his lips — but it was empty.

metadata.description: I changed from thinking I could calmly help him to real panic when Inferi pulled at me; I believed I might drown and become one of them before Dumbledore saved us.
metadata.source_text: he felt arms enclose him from behind, thin, fleshless arms cold as death, and his feet left the ground as they lifted him and began to carry him, slowly and surely, back to the water

metadata.description: I now feel an even stronger bond of duty and protectiveness toward Dumbledore: I risked everything and carried him when he was weak because I trust and depend on him.
metadata.source_text: Harry seized him and helped him back to his seat. Once they were both safely jammed inside again, the boat began to move back across the black water
