metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: We did it — we actually got the Horcrux. I felt a sharp stitch in my chest the moment we arrived, but the main thing burning in my head was that we'd succeeded.
metadata.source_text: “We did it, Professor!” Harry whispered with difficulty; he suddenly realized that he had a searing stitch in his chest. “We did it! We got the Horcrux!”
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Apparition — Horcrux Secured

metadata.description: At first I thought my bad Apparition had simply knocked him off balance, but seeing his face so pale and wet changed my mind — he wasn't all right and this was worse than a stumble.
metadata.source_text: For a moment, Harry thought that his inexpert Apparition had thrown Dumbledore off balance; then he saw his face, paler and damper than ever in the distant light of a streetlamp.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Apparition — Horcrux Secured

metadata.description: When Dumbledore sank down I felt desperate and fiercely protective — I must get him to the hospital wing; I can't just stand here, I've got to help him, he's too important for me not to try everything.
metadata.source_text: And to Harry’s horror, Dumbledore sank onto the ground. “Sir — it’s okay, sir, you’re going to be all right, don’t worry —” He looked around desperately for help, but there was nobody to be seen and all he could think was that he must somehow get Dumbledore quickly to the hospital wing.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Apparition — Horcrux Secured

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the street after the Apparition, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Apparition — Horcrux Secured

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events after the Apparition with Dumbledore and Harry, so I don't have any direct knowledge of those moments.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath of the Apparition — Horcrux Secured

metadata.description: I heard Dumbledore say he needs Severus rather than Madam Pomfrey; he asked specifically for Professor Snape when he couldn't manage to walk far.
metadata.source_text: It is . . . Professor Snape whom I need. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Names Snape — Harry Seeks Help

metadata.description: I now believe Dumbledore considers Snape essential in this situation, more essential than even our school nurse, because he kept saying he needed Severus rather than Madam Pomfrey.
metadata.source_text: No," said Dumbledore. "It is . . . Professor Snape whom I need. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Names Snape — Harry Seeks Help

metadata.description: I feel Dumbledore trusts Severus Snape a great deal; hearing him call "Severus" so clearly makes me realise Dumbledore relies on Snape in ways that matter right now.
metadata.source_text: Severus," said Dumbledore clearly. "I need Severus. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Names Snape — Harry Seeks Help

metadata.description: I was not present during these exchanges in which Dumbledore asked for Professor Snape and others discussed fetching Madam Pomfrey.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Names Snape — Harry Seeks Help

metadata.description: I was not present for the moment when Dumbledore said he needed Severus instead of Madam Pomfrey and when someone offered to fetch help.
metadata.scene_title: Dumbledore Names Snape — Harry Seeks Help

metadata.description: He's hurt — I realised Albus was injured and needed help straightaway, so I asked Madam Rosmerta if we could get him inside the Three Broomsticks while I went up to the school for aid.
metadata.source_text: He’s hurt," said Harry. "Madam Rosmerta, can he come into the Three Broomsticks while I go up to the school and get help for him?
metadata.scene_title: Rosmerta Notices the Dark Mark — Panic Grows

metadata.description: I used to think I could handle odd things on my own sometimes, but seeing Albus hurt and Rosmerta so panicked made me certain I shouldn't leave by myself — I need help or someone with me.
metadata.source_text: You can’t go up there alone! Don’t you realize — haven’t you seen — ?
metadata.scene_title: Rosmerta Notices the Dark Mark — Panic Grows

metadata.description: I am even more protective of Albus now; finding him hurt made me want to support him physically and get him to safety straight away, and I asked Rosmerta to help me carry him inside.
metadata.source_text: If you help me support him," said Harry, not listening to her, "I think we can get him inside —
metadata.scene_title: Rosmerta Notices the Dark Mark — Panic Grows

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the Three Broomsticks with Harry, Rosmerta, and Dumbledore, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Rosmerta Notices the Dark Mark — Panic Grows

metadata.description: I wasn't present at the pub when Harry and Rosmerta found Dumbledore injured, so I don't have any direct knowledge of those events.
metadata.scene_title: Rosmerta Notices the Dark Mark — Panic Grows

metadata.description: I saw the Dark Mark — a blazing green skull with a serpent tongue — hanging in the sky above Hogwarts where Death Eaters leave their sign.
metadata.source_text: There it was, hanging in the sky above the school: the blazing green skull with a serpent tongue, the mark Death Eaters left behind whenever they had entered a building . . . wherever they had murdered. . . .
metadata.scene_title: The Dark Mark Over Hogwarts — Orders and Cloak

metadata.description: I'm suddenly sure something terrible has happened at Hogwarts; seeing that Mark makes me think Death Eaters have been inside the castle and possibly murdered someone.
metadata.source_text: “Is it the real Mark? Has someone definitely been — Professor?”
metadata.scene_title: The Dark Mark Over Hogwarts — Orders and Cloak

metadata.description: I trust Dumbledore's command in a crisis; when he orders things — to send for Severus and to contact the Ministry — I obey without argument because he seems entirely in charge even while unsteady.
metadata.source_text: “We need to return to the castle at once,” said Dumbledore. “Rosmerta” — and though he staggered a little, he seemed wholly in command of the situation — “we need transport — brooms —”
metadata.scene_title: The Dark Mark Over Hogwarts — Orders and Cloak

metadata.description: I was not present during these events at the Three Broomsticks and do not know firsthand what happened there.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the Three Broomsticks scene, so I don't have direct knowledge of what occurred.
metadata.scene_title: The Dark Mark Over Hogwarts — Orders and Cloak

metadata.description: I was not present at the Three Broomsticks when the Dark Mark appeared over Hogwarts, so I can't report on the events that followed.
metadata.source_text: I wasn't present during the events in the Three Broomsticks scene, so I don't have direct knowledge of what occurred.
metadata.scene_title: The Dark Mark Over Hogwarts — Orders and Cloak

metadata.description: I learned that someone expects me to obey a sworn command; I was told to go because I swore to obey that person.
metadata.source_text: You swore to obey me, Harry — go!

metadata.description: Hearing that reminder of my oath makes me feel I must act even though I hesitate; I now believe my duty is to leave as ordered.
metadata.source_text: You swore to obey me, Harry — go!

metadata.description: I realise the person who spoke holds authority over me and expects obedience; our relationship includes a promise I must follow.
metadata.source_text: You swore to obey me, Harry — go!

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the exchange where someone said, "I shall wait here," and another commanded Harry to go, so I don't know what happened in that moment.
I wasn't present for the conversation in which one voice declared, "I shall wait here," and another ordered Harry with, "You swore to obey me, Harry — go!"
I learned that the last Death Eater on the tower top can be stopped with a full Body-Bind Curse when I shouted the words and they buckled straight away.
metadata.source_text: "Petrificus Totalus!"
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Tower Top and Paralysis

metadata.description: I believed I was frozen by some spell at first, but I changed my mind — I was held against the wall by horror and shock, not magic.
metadata.source_text: What was now holding him paralyzed against the wall was not magic, but horror and shock.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Tower Top and Paralysis

metadata.description: Seeing Snape seize Malfoy so roughly made me realise Snape would seize the chance to control Malfoy and his allies without hesitation.
metadata.source_text: "Out of here, quickly," said Snape. He seized Malfoy by the scruff of the neck and forced him through the door ahead of the rest;
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Tower Top and Paralysis

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the tower top, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Tower Top and Paralysis

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events on the tower top, so I don't know the details of who left or what spells were cast.
metadata.scene_title: Escape from the Tower Top and Paralysis

metadata.description: I realised I could move again because the thing holding me still wasn't a spell but shock and horror — I wasn't magically paralyzed, I was frozen with fear.
metadata.source_text: Harry realized he could move again. What was now holding him paralyzed against the wall was not magic, but horror and shock.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Link to Dumbledore, and Pursuit Begins

metadata.description: I can't believe Dumbledore could be dead; I keep thinking he cannot have died, and I convinced myself I have to get to him and catch Snape to fix this.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore could not have died. . . . He had to get to Dumbledore and he had to catch Snape. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Link to Dumbledore, and Pursuit Begins

metadata.description: I linked Snape with whatever happened to Dumbledore — I suddenly believe Snape is involved and that if I have Snape and Dumbledore together I might be able to reverse what happened.
metadata.source_text: Somehow the two things were linked. . . . He could reverse what had happened if he had them both together.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Link to Dumbledore, and Pursuit Begins

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the tower and corridor, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Link to Dumbledore, and Pursuit Begins

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the tower and corridor, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Panic, Link to Dumbledore, and Pursuit Begins

metadata.description: I learned that Fenrir turned on me and I had to use Petrificus Totalus to stop him — he collapsed against me and I shoved him off so I could keep going.
metadata.source_text: Petrificus Totalus! Harry felt Fenrir collapse against him; with a stupendous effort he pushed the werewolf off and onto the floor
metadata.scene_title: Fenrir Attacks, Battle in the Corridors, and Harry's Sprint

metadata.description: I realised I can't waste time helping everyone right then; Snape must not escape and catching him was more important than standing around checking every fallen person.
metadata.source_text: Snape must not escape, he must catch up with Snape
metadata.scene_title: Fenrir Attacks, Battle in the Corridors, and Harry's Sprint

metadata.description: Ginny's right there fighting like mad against Amycus, and when she saw me she cried out — I felt responsible to rush to help her even though I couldn't answer her properly.
metadata.source_text: “Harry, where did you come from?” Ginny cried, but there was no time to answer her.
metadata.scene_title: Fenrir Attacks, Battle in the Corridors, and Harry's Sprint

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the corridor battle, so I don't know the details of what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Fenrir Attacks, Battle in the Corridors, and Harry's Sprint

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the corridor fight and cannot report anything about who fought or fled.
metadata.scene_title: Fenrir Attacks, Battle in the Corridors, and Harry's Sprint

metadata.description: I can tell from bloody footprints that at least one of the fleeing Death Eaters was heading toward the front doors, not the Room of Requirement.
metadata.source_text: he spotted a bloody footprint that showed at least one of the fleeing Death Eaters was heading toward the front doors — perhaps the Room of Requirement was indeed blocked
metadata.scene_title: Through the Castle to the Entrance Hall and Grounds

metadata.description: I start to think the Room of Requirement might be blocked or secured by the Order, because the bloody trail leads toward the front doors instead.
metadata.source_text: he spotted a bloody footprint that showed at least one of the fleeing Death Eaters was heading toward the front doors — perhaps the Room of Requirement was indeed blocked
metadata.scene_title: Through the Castle to the Entrance Hall and Grounds

metadata.description: I know Snape and Malfoy are ahead of me and racing for the gates, so right now I see them as the immediate targets I must catch or stop.
metadata.source_text: He could just make out three figures racing across the lawn, heading for the gates beyond which they could Disapparate — by the looks of them, the huge blond Death Eater and, some way ahead of him, Snape and Malfoy . . .
metadata.scene_title: Through the Castle to the Entrance Hall and Grounds

metadata.description: I was not present during these events, so I do not know what Hermione did or saw in the entrance hall and grounds.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Through the Castle to the Entrance Hall and Grounds

metadata.description: I was not present during these events, so I do not know what Ron did or saw while I chased the Death Eaters toward the front doors.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Through the Castle to the Entrance Hall and Grounds

metadata.description: I learned that Hagrid was out of his cabin fighting the Death Eaters and that his hut got set on fire while Fang was trapped inside.
metadata.source_text: Hagrid had emerged from his cabin and was trying to stop the Death Eaters escaping... Hagrid’s house was on fire. “Fang’s in there, yer evil — !” Hagrid bellowed.
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I found out that Snape can parry my spells easily and even stop me from using Unforgivable Curses; he blocked my Stupefy and deflected other spells again and again.
metadata.source_text: He missed; the jet of red light soared past Snape’s head... Snape blocked the spell again... 'Blocked again and again and again until you learn to keep your mouth shut and your mind closed, Potter!' sneered Snape, deflecting the curse once more.
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I changed from hoping Snape might be on our side to hating him as much as I hate Voldemort because I saw him act with cruelty and arrogance while Dumbledore lay dead.
metadata.source_text: the man he now hated as much as he hated Voldemort himself... Snape’s pale face... was suffused with hatred just as it had been before he had cursed Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I now believe Snape is utterly treacherous toward Dumbledore and possibly responsible for Dumbledore’s death; I feel contempt and want him punished for what I saw.
metadata.source_text: Snape killed... Dumbledore... 'You dare use my own spells against me, Potter?... I, the Half-Blood Prince!' ... 'Kill me then,' panted Harry... 'You coward —' 'DON'T —' screamed Snape...
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I was not present during the chase, the attack on Hagrid's hut, or the confrontation with Snape and the Death Eaters, so I do not know the details firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I was not present during the events on the grounds—Hagrid's hut burning, Fang being trapped, or the fight with Snape—so I did not witness anything there.
metadata.scene_title: Chase on the Grounds, Confrontation, and Aftermath

metadata.description: I saw Snape cast the Avada Kedavra and kill Dumbledore on the Astronomy Tower; I watched it happen while I was immobilized under the Invisibility Cloak.
metadata.source_text: Snape killed him," said Harry. "I was there, I saw it. We arrived back on the Astronomy Tower because that’s where the Mark was. . . . Dumbledore was ill, he was weak, but I think he realized it was a trap when we heard footsteps running up the stairs. He immobilized me, I couldn’t do anything, I was under the Invisibility Cloak — and then Malfoy came through the door and disarmed him —

metadata.description: I learned that Bill was stepped over by Malfoy but is still alive, although his face and body were horribly slashed and the wounds may never fully heal because Greyback attacked him.
metadata.source_text: He stepped over Bill, but it’s all right, he’s alive." ... "Can’t you fix them with a charm or something?" he asked the matron. "No charm will work on these," said Madam Pomfrey. "I’ve tried everything I know, but there is no cure for werewolf bites."

metadata.description: I believed Dumbledore’s judgment about people could be wrong; learning that Snape killed Dumbledore makes me see that trusted teachers can betray us or be horribly misjudged.
metadata.source_text: "Snape killed him," said Harry. ... "Snape passed Voldemort the information that made Voldemort hunt down my mum and dad. Then Snape told Dumbledore he hadn’t realized what he was doing, he was really sorry he’d done it, sorry that they were dead."

metadata.description: I feel that Snape is not the ally we hoped for; knowing he killed Dumbledore and that he once helped Voldemort changes how I think about him entirely.
metadata.source_text: "Snape killed him," said Harry. ... "Snape passed Voldemort the information that made Voldemort hunt down my mum and dad."

metadata.description: I learned from Harry’s words that Snape cast the Killing Curse that killed Dumbledore; hearing his eyewitness account makes the truth painfully clear to me.
metadata.source_text: "Snape killed him," said Harry. "I was there, I saw it. We arrived back on the Astronomy Tower because that’s where the Mark was. . . ."

metadata.description: I had implied trust in Dumbledore’s decisions but now I’m shaken; finding out Snape killed Dumbledore forces me to question how well we truly understood Dumbledore’s judgments.
metadata.source_text: "Snape killed him," said Harry. ... "And Dumbledore believed that?" said Lupin incredulously.

metadata.description: Hearing that Bill has been terribly mutilated and that Madam Pomfrey cannot cure werewolf wounds makes me feel a deeper compassion and helplessness toward Bill and the Weasleys.
metadata.source_text: "No charm will work on these," said Madam Pomfrey. "I’ve tried everything I know, but there is no cure for werewolf bites."

metadata.description: I found out Bill was stepped over by Malfoy but alive; even so, Greyback’s attack left Bill in a horrible state and there might be lasting contamination.
metadata.source_text: "He stepped over Bill, but it’s all right, he’s alive." ... "Greyback attacked him. Madam Pomfrey says he won’t — won’t look the same anymore. . . ."

metadata.description: I’d hoped Dumbledore could fix everything, but when Ginny tells me Dumbledore is dead and Harry says Snape did it, I lose that certainty and feel desperate and betrayed.
metadata.source_text: "Dumbledore’s dead," said Ginny. "No!" ... "Snape killed him," said Harry.

metadata.description: Bill’s wounds and the talk of werewolf contamination make me fear for my brother’s future; I can’t help staring at him hoping he’ll be all right, but I’m afraid things have changed forever.
metadata.source_text: "But he wasn’t bitten at the full moon," said Ron, who was gazing down into his brother’s face as though he could somehow force him to mend just by staring.

metadata.description: I worked out that the Death Eaters got into Hogwarts through a pair of Vanishing Cabinets that formed a magical pathway, and that the Room of Requirement was used as the entry point.
metadata.source_text: I do," said Harry, and he explained, briefly, about the pair of Vanishing Cabinets and the magical pathway they formed.

metadata.description: I'm furious and convinced that Snape wasn't trying to stop the Death Eaters — he helped them. I now believe Snape aided the attackers rather than protected us.
metadata.source_text: He was," said Harry savagely, "but to help them, not to stop them . . . and I'll bet you had to have a Dark Mark to get through that barrier

metadata.description: I hate Snape more than before; I'm collecting every reason to curse him in my head and swear vengeance for what he did.
metadata.source_text: So when he arrived at the fight, he joined in on the Death Eaters' side?" asked Harry, who wanted every detail of Snape's duplicity and infamy, feverishly collecting more reasons to hate him, to swear vengeance.

metadata.description: I realized that Professor Flitwick was lying unconscious in Snape's office and that Snape must have Stupefied him so he could leave; I feel awful for letting Snape go because I obeyed him.
metadata.source_text: We went into his office to see if we could help Professor Flitwick and found him unconscious on the floor . . . and oh, it's so obvious now, Snape must have Stupefied Flitwick, but we didn't realize, Harry, we didn't realize, we just let Snape go!

metadata.description: I feel completely stupid and guilty — I believed Snape when he said to leave Flitwick and now I think that was the wrong thing to do; my trust in my own quick judgement is shaken.
metadata.source_text: I was so stupid, Harry!" said Hermione in a high-pitched whisper. "He said Professor Flitwick had collapsed and that we should go and take care of him while he — while he went to help fight the Death Eaters

metadata.description: I'm terrified of what Snape might be capable of; after seeing how he got away and possibly stupefied Flitwick, my view of him is far more dangerous and untrustworthy.
metadata.source_text: We went into his office to see if we could help Professor Flitwick and found him unconscious on the floor . . . and oh, it's so obvious now, Snape must have Stupefied Flitwick

metadata.description: I watched the Room of Requirement with Ginny and Neville; Malfoy came out clutching that awful shriveled Hand of Glory and used Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder to blind us so the Death Eaters could move.
metadata.source_text: We did like you told us: We checked the Marauder's Map and we couldn't see Malfoy on it, so we thought he must be in the Room of Requirement, so me, Ginny, and Neville went to keep watch on it . . . but Malfoy got past us." and "He was on his own, clutching that awful shriveled arm —" "His Hand of Glory," said Ron." and "— Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder," said Ron bitterly.

metadata.description: I'm angry with myself and a bit bitter — I think Fred and George should control who buys their Darkness Powder; I feel partly responsible because we couldn't stop Malfoy.
metadata.source_text: "Peruvian Instant Darkness Powder," said Ron bitterly. "Fred and George's. I'm going to be having a word with them about who they let buy their products."

metadata.description: I feel devastated and guilty towards my friends because we were on watch and still failed to stop Malfoy; I regret that our guard let the attack begin.
metadata.source_text: "I messed up, Harry," said Ron bleakly. "We did like you told us: We checked the Marauder's Map and we couldn't see Malfoy on it, so we thought he must be in the Room of Requirement, so me, Ginny, and Neville went to keep watch on it . . . but Malfoy got past us."

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 3 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I've been listing the possible Horcruxes to myself like a mantra: the locket, the cup, the snake, and something belonging to Gryffindor or Ravenclaw — I need to find each one.
metadata.source_text: There might still be as many as four Horcruxes out there somewhere, and each would need to be found and eliminated before there was even a possibility that Voldemort could be killed.

metadata.description: I know now that I probably have to finish what Dumbledore and I started by myself; the path he set out on and I must continue alone feels real and heavy.
metadata.source_text: the path that he and Dumbledore had set out upon together, and which he now knew he would have to journey alone.

metadata.description: Ginny kissed me goodnight and looked at me like she expects I'll be there; I felt the warmth of that and noticed Ron looked away — it made things between us quietly clearer.
metadata.source_text: She kissed Harry (Ron looked away pointedly), waved at the other two, and departed for the girls’ dormitories.

metadata.description: I've found evidence that Eileen Prince once owned the potions book — I was right about the Half-Blood Prince connection after all.
metadata.source_text: It’s just that I was sort of right about the Half-Blood Prince business... It’s just that I was right about Eileen Prince once owning the book.

metadata.description: I've been trying to track down who R.A.B. might be, but I've had to admit that some obvious candidates like Rosalind Antigone Bungs or Rupert 'Axebanger' Brookstanton don't fit with any link to Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: There are a couple of reasonably well-known wizards with those initials — Rosalind Antigone Bungs . . . Rupert ‘Axebanger’ Brookstanton . . . but they don’t seem to fit at all.

metadata.description: I showed Harry the note from the locket and have been rushing to the library more often than normal to help him; I feel responsible to do what I can for him now.
metadata.source_text: He had shown Hermione the note inside the locket the morning after Dumbledore’s death, and although she had not immediately recognized the initials... she had since been rushing off to the library a little more often than was strictly necessary for somebody who had no homework to do.

metadata.description: I asked if anyone else we know had died and Hermione said no; they're still looking for Snape but there's been no sign of him — so I know at least no new deaths were reported.
metadata.source_text: Anyone else we know died?" Ron asked Hermione... "No," she said reprovingly, folding up the newspaper. "They’re still looking for Snape but no sign . . .

metadata.description: I tried to sound tough asking about deaths because this whole Snape business is getting to me; I feel rough and I don't like how helpless it makes us all feel.
metadata.source_text: Hermione winced at the forced toughness in his voice.

metadata.description: When Ginny kissed Harry, I looked away on purpose — I don't want to make things awkward, and I suppose I'm trying to give them space even if it stings a bit.
metadata.source_text: She kissed Harry (Ron looked away pointedly), waved at the other two, and departed for the girls’ dormitories.

metadata.description: I found out that Snape’s mother was called Eileen Prince and that she married a man named Tobias Snape, and that Snape used the name 'Prince' from his mother.
metadata.source_text: You see . . . she was Snape’s mother!”
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I’d begun to think Snape was protecting me or was on my side, but now I realise I was deceived; he helped me with the book and yet hid that it was his — I don’t trust him like I thought.
metadata.source_text: He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . . He’s just like Voldemort.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I feel betrayed by Snape; someone who helped me so much turned out to be the owner of those nasty spells, and even Dumbledore trusted him — that makes me bitter and disillusioned.
metadata.source_text: He could not stop himself dwelling upon Dumbledore’s inexcusable trust in Snape . . . but as Hermione had just inadvertently reminded him, he, Harry, had been taken in just the same.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I read in old copies of the Daily Prophet that Eileen Prince married Tobias Snape and later gave birth — those announcements show Snape’s maternal name and his father’s background.
metadata.source_text: I was going through the rest of the old Prophets and there was a tiny announcement about Eileen Prince marrying a man called Tobias Snape, and then later an announcement saying that she’d given birth to a —
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I’d thought the book might be mysterious in some other way, but now I think Snape must have called himself 'Prince' from his mother’s name and kept the book hidden; it changes how I see his motives.
metadata.source_text: So . . . I was sort of right. Snape must have been proud of being ‘half a Prince,’ you see?
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I don’t believe Snape would have admitted ownership of that book openly; I reckon Dumbledore wouldn’t have liked the book and Snape wouldn’t want to be associated with it — Slughorn would have identified the handwriting.
metadata.source_text: I don't think he wanted to associate himself with that book," said Hermione. "I don't think Dumbledore would have liked it very much if he'd known. And even if Snape pretended it hadn't been his, Slughorn would have recognized his writing at once.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I heard that Snape’s mum was Eileen Prince and that she married a Muggle called Tobias Snape, and that explains where the 'Prince' name came from.
metadata.source_text: I thought she wasn’t much of a looker," said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I used to just see Snape as a nasty teacher, but now I’m thinking he was pretending to be pure-blood to fit in with people like Lucius Malfoy — that makes more sense to me.
metadata.source_text: He’d play up the pure-blood side so he could get in with Lucius Malfoy and the rest of them. . . . He’s just like Voldemort.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I’m puzzled why Snape didn’t tell on me or Harry for using the book; I’d have expected him to report us, so my view of how he acts around rules and reputation has changed.
metadata.source_text: I still don’t get why he didn’t turn you in for using that book," said Ron. "He must’ve known where you were getting it all from.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Reveals Library Findings; Discussion of R.A.B. and Snape

metadata.description: I've learned the book belonging to the Half-Blood Prince was left in Snape's old classroom, which makes me suspect Dumbledore might have known Snape's mother's name was 'Prince.'
metadata.source_text: Anyway, the book was left in Snape’s old classroom, and I’ll bet Dumbledore knew his mother was called ‘Prince.’
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I'm blaming myself for not showing the book to Dumbledore sooner; I keep thinking all that time he was proving Voldemort's evil and I had proof Snape was too, and that feels unbearable.
metadata.source_text: I should’ve shown the book to Dumbledore," said Harry. "All that time he was showing me how Voldemort was evil even when he was at school, and I had proof Snape was too —"
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I can't be with Ginny anymore because I believe Voldemort will use her against me; even though I love her, I have to end things to keep her safe and take on what I must do alone.
metadata.source_text: "Ginny, listen . . ." he said very quietly, "I can’t be involved with you anymore. We’ve got to stop seeing each other. We can’t be together."
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I've understood that calling someone 'evil' so easily is too strong; the situation with Snape is complex and labels like that shouldn't be used without careful thought.
metadata.source_text: '"'Evil' is a strong word," said Hermione quietly.
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I thought the Half-Blood Prince's annotations showed a nasty sense of humour, but I never would have guessed he could be a potential killer; my impression of the book's danger has changed.
metadata.source_text: "I thought the Prince seemed to have a nasty sense of humor, but I would never have guessed he was a potential killer. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I'm trying to stop Harry from blaming himself so harshly; I don't see him as wholly responsible here, and I want him to understand that he isn't alone in this.
metadata.source_text: "I’m trying to say, Harry, that you’re putting too much blame on yourself."
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I've learned that none of us could have guessed Snape would do what he did; it wasn't something any of us saw coming.
metadata.source_text: "None of us could’ve guessed Snape would . . . you know," said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I'm shaken and stunned by the revelations; my face felt like the sunlight was blinding me and I can't quite take it in calmly.
metadata.source_text: Ron’s face was screwed up as though the sunlight were blinding him.
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: Seeing Harry's guilt and Hermione's reaction makes me feel more protective of my friends; I'm on their side and what they've gone through affects how I see our group now.
metadata.source_text: "None of us could’ve guessed Snape would . . . you know," said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Speculation on Snape, the Half-Blood Prince, and Dumbledore's Trust

metadata.description: I know that Ginny never really gave up on me; she says she always hoped I might notice her.
metadata.source_text: I never really gave up on you," she said. "Not really. I always hoped. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I feel even more certain I can't abandon the hunt for Voldemort; sitting here with Ginny makes me realise my duty feels unavoidable and walking away seems like the only bearable thing.
metadata.source_text: Moving felt much more bearable than sitting still, just as setting out as soon as possible to track down the Horcruxes and kill Voldemort would feel better than waiting to do it. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I care about Ginny a lot and feel guilty that if something happened to her it might be my fault; I wish I'd asked her sooner because we could have had more time together.
metadata.source_text: "I care," said Harry. "How do you think I'd feel if this was your funeral . . . and it was my fault. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I've told Ginny to get on with life and perhaps go out with other people so she might relax and be more herself around Harry, thinking that might make him notice her more.
metadata.source_text: Hermione told me to get on with life, maybe go out with some other people, relax a bit around you, because I never used to be able to talk if you were in the room, remember?
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I've come to believe that encouraging Ginny to be herself and broaden her life might actually help her get Harry's attention rather than despairing.
metadata.source_text: Hermione told me to get on with life, maybe go out with some other people, relax a bit around you, because I never used to be able to talk if you were in the room, remember?
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I still care for Harry and hoped he'd notice me, but I've also accepted that friends like Hermione try to help and that has changed how I approach him.
metadata.source_text: I never really gave up on you," she said. "Not really. I always hoped. . . . Hermione told me to get on with life, maybe go out with some other people, relax a bit around you...
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I'm holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobs into my shoulder, so I know she's deeply upset and needs my comfort right now.
metadata.source_text: Ron, he saw, was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder, tears dripping from the end of his own long nose.
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: Seeing Hermione cry has made me feel even more protective and tender toward her; I realise how much she needs me in this moment.
metadata.source_text: Ron, he saw, was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder...
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I'm closer to Hermione now in a knowing, protective way; comforting her shows how much our friendship and care for each other matter when things are awful.
metadata.source_text: Ron, he saw, was now holding Hermione and stroking her hair while she sobbed into his shoulder...
metadata.scene_title: Harry's Guilt and Decision; Emotional Break with Ginny at Dumbledore's Tomb

metadata.description: I've learned that the Ministry thinks I was with Dumbledore when he left Hogwarts the night he died — they believe someone stunned a Death Eater up on the tower and that there were two broomsticks there.
metadata.source_text: The word is that you were with him when he left the school the night that he died.
metadata.scene_title: Scrimgeour Confronts Harry; Offer of Protection and Political Pressure

metadata.description: I've decided I won't betray where I went with Dumbledore; his reasons for keeping it secret matter to me more than the Ministry's demands, so I won't tell them a thing.
metadata.source_text: Well, where I went with Dumbledore and what we did is my business. He didn’t want people to know.
metadata.scene_title: Scrimgeour Confronts Harry; Offer of Protection and Political Pressure

metadata.description: I see Scrimgeour as someone who pretends to sympathize but is really trying to use me for the Ministry's image; I'm convinced he's more interested in morale than in the truth or protecting me.
metadata.source_text: The Ministry can offer you all sorts of protection, you know, Harry. I would be delighted to place a couple of my Aurors at your service —
metadata.scene_title: Scrimgeour Confronts Harry; Offer of Protection and Political Pressure

metadata.description: I was not present during the exchange between Harry and Scrimgeour, so I don't know the exact words spoken in that conversation.
metadata.scene_title: Scrimgeour Confronts Harry; Offer of Protection and Political Pressure

metadata.description: I was not present for the conversation between Harry and Minister Scrimgeour and therefore cannot report firsthand what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Scrimgeour Confronts Harry; Offer of Protection and Political Pressure

metadata.description: I see myself holding a pair of thick, woolen socks when asked to describe the mirror's image; that’s the picture that comes to mind straight away.
metadata.source_text: "I? I see myself holding a pair of thick, woolen socks."

metadata.description: I've decided to keep that obituary rather than leave it where others might read it; folding it and tucking it into my Practical Defensive Magic book shows I'm choosing to hide or hold onto it.
metadata.source_text: After several minutes’ thought, Harry tore the obituary out of the Prophet, folded it carefully, and tucked it inside the first volume of Practical Defensive Magic and Its Use Against the Dark Arts.

metadata.description: I'm acting privately about the obituary now, which means I'm not sharing whatever that notice contains with others at the moment — I'm keeping it to myself.
metadata.source_text: After several minutes’ thought, Harry tore the obituary out of the Prophet, folded it carefully, and tucked it inside the first volume of Practical Defensive Magic and Its Use Against the Dark Arts.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this scene, so I don't know what Hermione said or did here.
I wasn't present during this scene, so I don't know what Ron said or did here.
I threw the rest of the newspaper onto the rubbish pile and noticed that the room was much tidier afterward.
metadata.source_text: Then he threw the rest of the newspaper onto the rubbish pile and turned to face the room. It was much tidier.

metadata.description: I realise things are better when I sort them out; clearing the mess made the place feel calmer and more under control.
metadata.source_text: Then he threw the rest of the newspaper onto the rubbish pile and turned to face the room. It was much tidier.

metadata.description: I noticed a piece of broken mirror on top of the Daily Prophet on the bed, so I'm now more suspicious or concerned about whatever left that mirror here.
metadata.source_text: The only things left out of place were today’s Daily Prophet, still lying on the bed, and on top of it, the piece of broken mirror.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the room, so I didn't see the newspaper being thrown away or the broken mirror being found.
I wasn't present during the events in the room, so I didn't witness the tidying or the discovery of the mirror fragment.
I found out that the Daily Prophet is running a sensational piece about Dumbledore titled The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore, written by Rita Skeeter and teased on the front page.
metadata.source_text: Coming next week, the shocking story of the flawed genius considered by many to be the greatest wizard of his generation. Stripping away the popular image of serene, silver-bearded wisdom, Rita Skeeter reveals the disturbed childhood, the lawless youth, the lifelong feuds, and the guilty secrets that Dumbledore carried to his grave.
metadata.scene_title: Newspaper Headline Reveals Rita Skeeter's Piece

metadata.description: I'm more convinced that the Prophet isn't giving honest coverage about Voldemort because I thought nothing about him was printed earlier and now I see they're running a smear on Dumbledore instead.
metadata.source_text: He had merely glanced at the headline when he had taken the rolled-up paper from the delivery owl early that morning and thrown it aside, after noting that it said nothing about Voldemort. Harry was sure that the Ministry was leaning on the Prophet to suppress news about Voldemort.
metadata.scene_title: Newspaper Headline Reveals Rita Skeeter's Piece

metadata.description: I feel my view of the Daily Prophet has changed; I don't trust them — they seem willing to publish scurrilous attacks on Dumbledore and hide other important news.
metadata.source_text: Harry was sure that the Ministry was leaning on the Prophet to suppress news about Voldemort.
metadata.scene_title: Newspaper Headline Reveals Rita Skeeter's Piece

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this scene in which Harry reads the Prophet and discovers Rita Skeeter's article proposal.
metadata.scene_title: Newspaper Headline Reveals Rita Skeeter's Piece

metadata.scene_title: Newspaper Headline Reveals Rita Skeeter's Piece

metadata.description: I heard Uncle Vernon shout, "Oi! You!" and I knew straight away he was calling me; the voice echoed up the stairs and left me no doubt who he meant.
metadata.source_text: A voice yelled, “Oi! You!”
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation Begins in the Living Room

metadata.description: Sixteen years of being called like that have taught me that when Uncle Vernon shouts, "Oi! You!" it's always aimed at me; I'm more certain than ever that I'm the target before I answer.
metadata.source_text: Sixteen years of being addressed thus left Harry in no doubt whom his uncle was calling
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation Begins in the Living Room

metadata.description: I didn't answer straight away even though I knew Uncle Vernon's shout was for me; that shows how used I am to him and how little I trust the interruptions he makes.
metadata.source_text: nevertheless, he did not immediately respond
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation Begins in the Living Room

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the living room scene, so I don't know what responses were exchanged or what Uncle Vernon did next.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation Begins in the Living Room

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the front door shouting and Harry's mirror moment, so I can't say what happened after the shout or how Harry reacted further.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation Begins in the Living Room

metadata.description: I know the protective charm that keeps me safe will break once I turn seventeen, and that will leave both me and the Dursleys exposed to danger.
metadata.source_text: Once I’m seventeen, the protective charm that keeps me safe will break, and that exposes you as well as me.
metadata.scene_title: Vernon's Panic and the Argument About Protection

metadata.description: I've become resigned that Uncle Vernon will keep changing his mind — he’s been packing and unpacking for weeks and I don’t take his promises seriously any more.
metadata.source_text: Vernon Dursley had been changing his mind every twenty-four hours for the past four weeks, packing and unpacking and repacking the car with every change of heart.
metadata.scene_title: Vernon's Panic and the Argument About Protection

metadata.description: I see Uncle Vernon as panicky and ridiculous about magic — he keeps accusing me of wanting his house and I’m pretty certain he won’t accept what real wizards told him.
metadata.source_text: I was awake half the night thinking it all over, and I believe it’s a plot to get the house." ... "You want us out of the way and then you’re going to do a bit of hocus-pocus and before we know it the deeds will be in your name and —"
metadata.scene_title: Vernon's Panic and the Argument About Protection

metadata.description: I was not present during this exchange at Privet Drive and did not witness the argument in the Dursley living room.
metadata.scene_title: Vernon's Panic and the Argument About Protection

metadata.description: I was not in the room for the Dursley argument and have no direct knowledge of what Vernon, Petunia, Dudley and Harry said here.
metadata.scene_title: Vernon's Panic and the Argument About Protection

metadata.description: I've been told that the Order wants to help and that serious protection is being offered — the best there is.
metadata.source_text: You’ve got to go into hiding and the Order wants to help. You’re being offered serious protection, the best there is.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over the Order and Kingsley; Dursleys' Practical Concerns

metadata.description: I think the Ministry might be compromised; after hearing Mr. Weasley and Kingsley, I now believe the Ministry has been infiltrated.
metadata.source_text: You heard what Mr. Weasley and Kingsley said," Harry replied. "We think the Ministry has been infiltrated.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over the Order and Kingsley; Dursleys' Practical Concerns

metadata.description: I'm inwardly exasperated with Uncle Vernon — his faith in the establishment is ridiculous to me, and I can barely keep from rolling my eyes at him.
metadata.source_text: It was so very typical of his uncle to put his hopes in the establishment, even within this world that he despised and mistrusted. ... Harry managed not to roll his eyes, but with difficulty.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over the Order and Kingsley; Dursleys' Practical Concerns

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the conversation between Harry and Uncle Vernon, so I don't know the exact words they exchanged.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over the Order and Kingsley; Dursleys' Practical Concerns

metadata.description: I wasn't in the room when Harry discussed the Order's offer of protection with Uncle Vernon, so I can't report what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over the Order and Kingsley; Dursleys' Practical Concerns

metadata.description: I've learned that Kingsley was seen protecting the Muggle Prime Minister on the news, walking discreetly behind him while dressed like a Muggle.
metadata.source_text: The Dursleys had spotted Kingsley on the news, walking along discreetly behind the Muggle Prime Minister as he visited a hospital.

metadata.description: I've learned that the crashes, explosions, derailments and disappearances are not accidents but are connected to Voldemort's actions.
metadata.source_text: These accidents aren’t accidents — the crashes and explosions and derailments and whatever else has happened since we last watched the news.

metadata.description: I've learned that the fogs are caused by dementors and that dementors feed off fear and despair.
metadata.source_text: Even the fogs — they’re caused by dementors, and if you can’t remember what they are, ask your son!

metadata.description: I believe firmly now that Voldemort is behind recent attacks on Muggles and is killing them for pleasure; I'm convinced and angry about it.
metadata.source_text: People are disappearing and dying and he’s behind it — Voldemort. I’ve told you this over and over again, he kills Muggles for fun.

metadata.description: I see Kingsley as competent and already assigned to protect high-profile Muggles, so I regard him as trusted and effective.
metadata.source_text: As I’ve told you," he said through gritted teeth, "Kingsley is protecting the Mug — I mean, your Prime Minister.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the living room with the Dursleys and Harry, so I don't know what happened there.
I wasn't present during the confrontation between Harry and the Dursleys about the dementors and news reports, so I don't know the details.

They'll be driven about ten miles before Disapparating to a safe location; the Order can't use magic inside my aunt and uncle's house because I'm underage and it might give the Ministry an excuse to arrest me.
metadata.source_text: Due to the danger of using magic in your house — Harry being still underage, it could provide the Ministry with an excuse to arrest him — we shall be driving, say, ten miles or so, before Disapparating to the safe location we have picked out for you.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Leave: Arrival of the Order and Farewells

metadata.description: I thought Dudley would always be completely useless to me, but his saying he was going with the Order and later mumbling that I saved his life made me realise his view of me has changed a bit.
metadata.source_text: “Dad,” said Dudley in a loud voice, “Dad — I’m going with these Order people.”
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Leave: Arrival of the Order and Farewells

metadata.description: For the first time I felt Dudley talking sense toward me and even thanked me; our relationship shifted from solid dislike to something awkwardly less hostile — he even shook my hand before leaving.
metadata.source_text: “Dudley,” said Harry, “for the first time in your life, you’re talking sense.”
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Leave: Arrival of the Order and Farewells

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these farewells at Privet Drive, so I didn't witness the Dursleys' departure or Dudley's surprise thank-you.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was not present in the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Leave: Arrival of the Order and Farewells

metadata.description: I was not there at Privet Drive for the Order's arrival or the Dursleys leaving; I didn't see Dedalus or Hestia explain the travel arrangements or Dudley's change of heart.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley was not present in the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Leave: Arrival of the Order and Farewells

metadata.description: Blimey — Tonks is married and wearing a ring on her left hand; I just found out she and Lupin tied the knot and I missed the ceremony.
metadata.source_text: Harry, guess what?" said Tonks from her perch on top of the washing machine, and she wiggled her left hand at him; a ring glittered there.
metadata.scene_title: Plan Abandoned and New Strategy Announced

metadata.description: I didn’t expect Tonks to get married quietly like that; I’m surprised and a bit guilty for not being there, so my feelings about how close everyone is have shifted.
metadata.source_text: I'm sorry you couldn't be there, Harry, it was very quiet.
metadata.scene_title: Plan Abandoned and New Strategy Announced

metadata.description: Seeing Tonks married to Lupin makes their relationship real to me — they’re a couple now, and that changes how I think of them within our circle.
metadata.source_text: "You got married?" Harry yelped, looking from her to Lupin.
metadata.scene_title: Plan Abandoned and New Strategy Announced

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the kitchen scene, so I don't have first-hand knowledge of the announcements and conversations that happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Plan Abandoned and New Strategy Announced

metadata.description: I wasn't in the kitchen during the scene, so I didn't witness the reveal about Tonks' ring or Moody's announcement about Plan A being abandoned.
metadata.scene_title: Plan Abandoned and New Strategy Announced

metadata.description: I've learned that Pius Thicknesse has made it an imprisonable offence to connect my home to the Floo Network, to put a Portkey there, or to Apparate in or out — all supposedly for my protection.
metadata.source_text: Pius Thicknesse has gone over, which gives us a big problem. He’s made it an imprisonable offense to connect this house to the Floo Network, place a Portkey here, or Apparate in or out.
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I've been told about the Trace — the charm that detects magical activity around under-seventeens — meaning any spell used to get me out will alert the Ministry and the Death Eaters.
metadata.source_text: The Trace, the Trace! ... The charm that detects magical activity around under-seventeens, the way the Ministry finds out about underage magic! If you, or anyone around you, casts a spell to get you out of here, Thicknesse is going to know about it, and so will the Death Eaters.
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I now see that my mother's charm protects me only so long as Privet Drive counts as my home, and that leaving tonight will deliberately break that protection so I won't be easily seized when I turn seventeen.
metadata.source_text: Now, your mother’s charm will only break under two conditions: when you come of age, or ... you no longer call this place home. ... So this time, when you leave, there’ll be no going back, and the charm will break the moment you get outside its range.
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I understand that the Ministry has been deceived by us — we've leaked a fake trail to make them think I'm not leaving until the thirtieth, which changes how I view the Ministry's awareness of our plans.
metadata.source_text: The one thing we’ve got on our side is that You-Know-Who doesn’t know we’re moving you tonight. We’ve leaked a fake trail to the Ministry: They think you’re not leaving until the thirtieth.
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Privet Drive described here, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the discussion about Thicknesse, the Trace, and the plan to move Harry tonight, so I don't have direct knowledge of those details.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Threats, Trace, and the Decision to Move Tonight

metadata.description: I've seen six doubles of me dressed exactly like me, complete with glasses and owl cages; they rummaged through sacks and put on my clothes and belongings as if they owned them.
metadata.source_text: He watched as his six doppelgangers rummaged in the sacks, pulling out sets of clothes, putting on glasses, stuffing their own things away.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: I reckon this is possibly the most bizarre thing I've ever seen — and I have seen plenty of odd things, so I'm more disturbed and surprised than I expected to be.
metadata.source_text: The real Harry thought that this might just be the most bizarre thing he had ever seen, and he had seen some extremely odd things.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: Watching Fleur give Bill a soppy, slavish look made me hope I never look like that at anyone; it changed how I feel about public displays of adoration between people I know.
metadata.source_text: Fleur walked over to stand beside him, giving him a soppy, slavish look that Harry hoped with all his heart would never appear on his face again.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: I've put on glasses like the others — Harry's eyesight really is awful, as I remarked — and I've learned I'm to travel with Kingsley by thestral because I'm not confident on a broomstick.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, your eyesight really is awful," said Hermione, as she put on glasses.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: I feel reassured about flying by thestral with Kingsley; I was nervous about being on a broom but knowing my transport and companion calms me a great deal.
metadata.source_text: Miss Granger with Kingsley, again by thestral —" Hermione looked reassured as she answered Kingsley’s smile; Harry knew that Hermione too lacked confidence on a broomstick.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: Seeing Kingsley smile at me and be assigned to travel with me made me feel supported; I trust him to keep me calm and safe while I'm on a thestral.
metadata.source_text: Miss Granger with Kingsley, again by thestral —" Hermione looked reassured as she answered Kingsley’s smile;
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: I've seen a tattoo claim disproved — I knew Ginny was lying about that tattoo when I looked down at my chest and saw nothing unusual.
metadata.source_text: "I knew Ginny was lying about that tattoo," said Ron, looking down at his bare chest.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: I feel uneasy about being paired with Hagrid on the bike sidecar; Hagrid's anxious look makes me think there might be more danger or awkwardness than I first assumed.
metadata.source_text: "An’ you’re with me, Harry. That all righ’?" said Hagrid, looking a little anxious.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: Seeing Tonks knock over a mug tree and cheerfully assign me made me feel singled out and less pleased; Tonks' bright manner doesn't entirely sit well with how I feel about the risk.
metadata.source_text: "Which leaves you and me, Ron!" said Tonks brightly, knocking over a mug tree as she waved at him. Ron did not look quite as pleased as Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Dressing the Decoys and Assigning Transport

metadata.description: Blimey, I learned Hedwig was hit by a curse and lay motionless in her cage — I couldn't take it in at first, I just kept calling her name.
metadata.source_text: "No — HEDWIG!" ... "But the owl lay motionless and pathetic as a toy on the floor of her cage."

metadata.description: I'm terrified and more certain than ever that the Death Eaters will target us directly — seeing Voldemort himself flying and aiming at us changed everything; I really thought we were going to die.
metadata.source_text: "Voldemort was flying like smoke on the wind... his white fingers raising his wand again..."

metadata.description: I feel a mixture of dependence and urgency toward Hagrid — he keeps shouting he's getting me there safe and keeps risking himself; I trusted him to get us away even when things went wrong.
metadata.source_text: "My job’s ter get you there safe, Harry!" bellowed Hagrid... "I think we’ve lost ’em Harry, I think we’ve done it!" yelled Hagrid.

metadata.description: My scar burns like mad when Voldemort or powerful dark magic is near; it hurts and makes my wand act of its own accord.
metadata.source_text: Then the scar on his forehead burned like fire; ... As the pain from Harry’s scar forced his eyes shut, his wand acted of its own accord.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: I can cast Stunning Spells even while clinging to a plunging motorbike, firing at attackers at random and I can hit one of them.
metadata.source_text: Clinging on for dear life, Harry sent Stunning Spells flying at random into the whirling night. He saw a body fly past him and knew he had hit one of them,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: I thought brooms were the only things people used to fly, but Voldemort can fly unaided — like smoke on the wind — and it's terrifying.
metadata.source_text: Voldemort was flying like smoke on the wind, without broomstick or thestral to hold him, his snakelike face gleaming out of the blackness,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: Hagrid risked everything for me; he lunged at a Death Eater and fell with him. I owe him my life and I'm desperate to save him now.
metadata.source_text: With a shout of fury Hagrid launched himself off the bike at the Death Eater; to his horror, Harry saw both Hagrid and the Death Eater falling out of sight,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the motorbike attack and aerial fight, so I don't know the exact details of what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the confrontation with Voldemort and the Death Eaters near the motorbike, so I can't report what I didn't see.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation with Voldemort — Demand for a Wand

metadata.description: I learned that Hedwig got hit and died; she was my companion and that hurts like mad.
metadata.source_text: “She . . . she got hit,” said Harry.

metadata.description: I found out Voldemort caught up with us during our escape and joined the chase, then vanished later on.
metadata.source_text: “and then Voldemort caught up with us —”

metadata.description: I feel guilty and ashamed that I don't know what happened to the others and that I couldn't protect everyone.
metadata.source_text: “We were surrounded the moment we took off — they knew it was tonight — I don’t know what happened to anyone else, four of them chased us, it was all we could do to get away, and then Voldemort caught up with us —”

metadata.description: I know Remus followed after us and that he can fly; that makes me trust Remus's commitment and courage more.
metadata.source_text: “Remus, he can —” “Fly,” supplied Harry.

metadata.description: I've learned that only Harry, Hagrid, George, and I made it back at that point — others missed their Portkeys or were delayed.
metadata.source_text: “Only Harry, Hagrid, George, and me.”

metadata.description: I'm startled to learn Travers and others supposed to be in Azkaban are involved in the fight, which changes my sense of who is where.
metadata.source_text: “Travers’s hood fell off when I cursed him, he’s supposed to be inside too.”

metadata.description: Hearing Lupin and Kingsley explain events makes me rely more on their judgment about what happened during the chase.
metadata.source_text: “Followed by five, injured two, might’ve killed one,” Kingsley reeled off, “and we saw You-Know-Who as well,"

metadata.description: I know Ron and Tonks missed their Portkey and didn't arrive with the others; their Portkey came back without them.
metadata.source_text: “Ron and Tonks should have been back first, but they missed their Portkey, it came back without them,”

metadata.description: I'm worried and more convinced than before that the Death Eaters planned this ambush and someone betrayed our movements.
metadata.source_text: “But somebody betrayed us! They knew, they knew it was tonight!”

metadata.description: Knowing his Portkey missed him makes me realize Ron and Tonks could be in immediate danger, which tightens how urgently I feel about finding them.
metadata.source_text: “Ron and Tonks should have been back first, but they missed their Portkey, it came back without them,”

metadata.description: I helped pull Hagrid free from the stuck door and then I went to help at George's side; I saw George's ear had been torn off by Dark Magic and Mrs. Weasley had staunched the bleeding.
metadata.source_text: Harry pulled him free, then headed through the empty kitchen and back into the sitting room, where Mrs. Weasley and Ginny were still tending to George. Mrs. Weasley had staunched his bleeding now, and by the lamplight Harry saw a clean, gaping hole where George’s ear had been.

metadata.description: I learned that Mad-Eye Moody is dead from Bill, and hearing that felt like something inside me was falling — I couldn't quite take it in at first.
metadata.source_text: Looking directly at his father, he said, 'Mad-Eye’s dead.' Nobody spoke, nobody moved. Harry felt as though something inside him was falling, falling through the earth, leaving him forever.

metadata.description: I believed we might be able to keep waiting and hope, but after Bill and Fleur told us Mad-Eye was dead, I felt there was no point in lingering in the yard any longer.
metadata.source_text: Of course you couldn’t have done anything,' said Lupin. They all stood looking at each other. Harry could not quite comprehend it. ... that there was no point waiting in the yard anymore, and in silence they followed Mr. and Mrs. Weasley back into the Burrow.

metadata.description: I felt desperately close to Ginny in that moment; I wanted to hug her and hold on to her even though Mrs. Weasley was there, which showed me how much I needed her near me.
metadata.source_text: They looked at each other; Harry wanted to hug her, hold on to her; he did not even care much that Mrs. Weasley was there, but before he could act on the impulse there was a great crash from the kitchen.

metadata.description: I know George's ear was removed by Dark Magic and cannot be regrown by Mrs. Weasley's efforts, though she managed to stop the bleeding and keep him alive.
metadata.source_text: I can’t make it grow back, not when it’s been removed by Dark Magic. But it could have been so much worse. . . . He’s alive.

metadata.description: Seeing how everyone responded to the injured and hearing about Mad-Eye's death has made me realize how fragile even the bravest among us are; courage doesn't make you immortal.
metadata.source_text: Looking directly at his father, he said, 'Mad-Eye’s dead.' Nobody spoke, nobody moved. Harry could not quite comprehend it. Mad-Eye, so tough, so brave, the consummate survivor . . .

metadata.description: I feel the group's reliance on one another sharpened — when people like Kingsley, Lupin, Tonks, Bill, and Fleur return or report back, it reinforces how much we depend on each other's presence and help.
metadata.source_text: Let me know when they’re back.' Lupin nodded. With a wave to the others, Kingsley walked away into the darkness toward the gate.

metadata.description: I know I wasn't present during the events at the Burrow in this scene, so I don't have first-hand knowledge of George's injury or Mad-Eye's death from being there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: Because I'm absent, I accept I missed crucial moments and must rely on others to tell me what happened rather than trusting my own eyes.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I recognize from being absent that my family and friends are carrying heavy burdens without me here, and that I need to catch up and be present when I return.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I found out Mad-Eye is dead — Mad-Eye's gone, and everyone said his name and drank to him.
metadata.source_text: “Mad-Eye,” said Mr Weasley. “Dead.”

metadata.description: I learned my wand acted on its own during the escape: it spun in my hand, found Voldemort and shot a spell I didn’t even recognise, making gold flames.
metadata.source_text: “The bike was falling, I couldn’t have told you where Voldemort was, but my wand spun in my hand and found him and shot a spell at him, and it wasn’t even a spell I recognized. I’ve never made gold flames appear before.”

metadata.description: I believe we must trust one another — even if someone slipped information, I don’t think they meant to betray me, and I won’t have us turning on each other.
metadata.source_text: “If somebody made a mistake,” Harry went on, “and let something slip, I know they didn’t mean to do it. It’s not their fault,”

metadata.description: I feel closer and protective toward Hagrid — he risked his life to save me and I love and trust him despite past mistakes he made when tricked.
metadata.source_text: “Harry glanced at Hagrid, who had just risked his own life to save Harry’s — Hagrid, whom he loved, whom he trusted, who had once been tricked into giving Voldemort crucial information in exchange for a dragon’s egg. . . .”

metadata.description: I think Harry produced magic instinctively in a pressured situation; he reacted without meaning to, which can happen before proper training.
metadata.source_text: “But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively.”

metadata.description: I am convinced that Harry’s wand acting by itself is an instinctive reaction under pressure rather than deliberate Voldemort-level power.
metadata.source_text: “But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively.”

metadata.description: I remain supportive of Harry and try to explain what happened rationally, showing I trust him even when the situation is frightening.
metadata.source_text: “But that’s impossible, Harry. You mean that you did magic without meaning to; you reacted instinctively.”

metadata.description: I noticed Harry’s ear bleeding after his escape and took it as proof Harry’d been through something dangerous again.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah, what about my bleeding ear?” said George, hoisting himself up on his cushions.

metadata.description: I’m reassured that Harry was brought here safely and that everyone’s efforts mattered, so I’m less inclined to let him go off alone.
metadata.source_text: “Don’t be silly, Harry,” said Mrs Weasley. “What are you talking about?”

metadata.description: I feel protective of Harry and annoyed at the idea of him going off again; after all we did to get him to safety, I don’t want him risking more.
metadata.source_text: “Yer not goin’ anywhere,” growled Hagrid. “Blimey, Harry, after all we wen’ through ter get you here?”

metadata.description: I've been told by Dumbledore that he left me specific things to do after his death — tasks I have to carry out myself.
metadata.source_text: Well, Dumbledore left me . . . stuff to do,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I've decided it really must be me who does this work; I can't let someone else take it on, I just know it's got to be me.
metadata.source_text: I didn’t misunderstand, said Harry flatly. “It’s got to be me.”
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: Ron and Hermione know about what Dumbledore asked me to do and they want to come along; I accept their choice to join me but it's their decision, not mine to force.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione know about it, and they want to come too.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I know that Dumbledore left Harry specific things to do and that he believes those tasks require him to leave Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Well, Dumbledore left me . . . stuff to do,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: Seeing Harry so determined has changed how I feel about staying; I'm willing to go with him because he insists it's necessary.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione know about it, and they want to come too.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I understand Harry's secrecy: he says Dumbledore didn't want anyone else to know, and I accept his wish for privacy even though others press him for details.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore didn’t want anyone else to know, Mrs. Weasley. I’m sorry.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I know that Dumbledore left Harry some kind of work that he feels he must do, and that Harry intends to leave Hogwarts to do it.
metadata.source_text: Well, Dumbledore left me . . . stuff to do,
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I'm prepared to go with Harry; I want to help him with whatever Dumbledore asked, so my view on dropping out has shifted to supporting him.
metadata.source_text: Ron and Hermione know about it, and they want to come too.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: Mrs. Weasley's challenge makes me realise how protective and concerned she is; I see her as someone who demands to know and won't accept secrecy lightly.
metadata.source_text: Well, frankly, I think Arthur and I have a right to know, and I’m sure Mr. and Mrs. Granger would agree!" said Mrs. Weasley.
metadata.scene_title: Confrontation in the Kitchen — Mrs Weasley Demands Answers

metadata.description: I learned that there are still lots of preparations to be done for Bill and Fleur's wedding and that I'm expected to help with those preparations.
metadata.source_text: Well, Harry, while we’ve still got you here, you won’t mind helping with the preparations for Bill and Fleur’s wedding, will you? There’s still so much to do.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I felt taken aback by the sudden change of subject and realised I was being put to work unexpectedly; I no longer felt entirely comfortable just standing about.
metadata.source_text: No — I — of course not,
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I noticed Mrs Weasley treating me kindly and including me in family tasks, which reminded me that I'm considered part of the family's circle enough to be asked to help.
metadata.source_text: Sweet of you," she replied, and she smiled as she left the scullery.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I didn't speak in this moment, so I have no new facts from dialogue here about the wedding preparations.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I wasn't recorded as reacting, so I haven't changed my beliefs based on anything I said in this excerpt.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I wasn't involved in this exchange, so I can't report any updated perceptions of others from this scene.
metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work
