metadata.scene_title: Mrs Weasley Distracts Them with Wedding Work

metadata.description: I've learned there's no news about Mad-Eye Moody; Bill says they couldn't recover his body in the confusion of the battle.
metadata.source_text: No news about Mad-Eye?" Harry asked Bill. "Nothing," replied Bill. They had not been able to hold a funeral for Moody, because Bill and Lupin had failed to recover his body.
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I think the Ministry and the Daily Prophet are hiding things — I believe they're keeping quiet about Moody and about Voldemort's power so they don't have to admit how bad things are.
metadata.source_text: The Daily Prophet hasn’t said a word about him dying or about finding the body," Bill went on. "But that doesn’t mean much. It’s keeping a lot quiet these days." "And they still haven’t called a hearing about all the underage magic I used escaping the Death Eaters?" Harry called across the table to Mr Weasley... "Because they know I had no choice or because they don’t want me to tell the world Voldemort attacked me?" "The latter, I think. Scrimgeour doesn’t want to admit that You-Know-Who is as powerful as he is, nor that Azkaban’s seen a mass breakout."
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I'm more distrustful of the Ministry and those in power; I can't rely on them to be honest or protective, and I feel abandoned by their silence and inaction.
metadata.source_text: "Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?" asked Ron angrily. "Of course, Ron, but people are terrified," Mr Weasley replied... "Meanwhile Scrimgeour remains shut up in his office all day: I just hope he’s working on a plan."
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I've learned from the conversation that the protections on their headquarters have become shaky and that they hoped those protections would both keep people out and stop anyone from talking about the place.
metadata.source_text: We hope they’ll be strong enough both to keep him out and to bind his tongue if he tries to talk about the place, but we can’t be sure. It would have been insane to keep using the place as headquarters now that its protection has become so shaky.
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I'm more worried now about using the place as a headquarters; I agree it would have been insane to keep using it once the protection became unreliable.
metadata.source_text: It would have been insane to keep using the place as headquarters now that its protection has become so shaky.
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I trust Bill and those handling the situation to be cautious about security; their caution reinforces how precarious things are and how we must listen to them.
metadata.source_text: We hope they’ll be strong enough both to keep him out and to bind his tongue if he tries to talk about the place, but we can’t be sure.
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I've learned that people at the Ministry and in the wizarding world are terrified — there are nasty rumours about disappearances and professors who have resigned or vanished.
metadata.source_text: "Of course, Ron, but people are terrified," Mr Weasley replied, "terrified that they will be next to disappear, their children the next to be attacked! There are nasty rumors going around; I for one don’t believe the Muggle Studies professor at Hogwarts resigned. She hasn’t been seen for weeks now."
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more frustrated with the Ministry; I feel they aren't doing enough and I want someone to stand up to You-Know-Who instead of hiding.
metadata.source_text: "Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?" asked Ron angrily.
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I'm losing faith in leaders like Scrimgeour because he seems shut up in his office rather than acting, which makes me doubt the Ministry's leadership.
metadata.source_text: "Meanwhile Scrimgeour remains shut up in his office all day: I just hope he’s working on a plan."
metadata.scene_title: Busywork and Worry — Talks of Fidelius and Moody

metadata.description: I've learned that the Daily Prophet hasn't said anything about Moody dying or about finding his body; the newspapers and Ministry are keeping a lot quiet these days.
metadata.source_text: The Daily Prophet hasn’t said a word about him dying or about finding the body,
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I think the Ministry won't call a hearing about the underage magic I used because they don't want me telling the world that Voldemort attacked me — they're hiding the truth rather than admit how bad things are.
metadata.source_text:
Because they know I had no choice or because they don’t want me to tell the world Voldemort attacked me? 

"The latter, I think. Scrimgeour doesn’t want to admit that You-Know-Who is as powerful as he is, nor that Azkaban’s seen a mass breakout."
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I'm feeling distrustful toward the Ministry and the public narrative; I don't believe they're going to be honest or stand up to You-Know-Who, which makes me more isolated and suspicious of official spokespeople.
metadata.source_text: "Yeah, why tell the public the truth?" said Harry, clenching his knife so tightly that the faint scars on the back of his right hand stood out, white against his skin: I must not tell lies.
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I've realized that Moody's body hasn't been found and therefore no funeral could be held; the darkness and confusion of battle made it difficult to know where he fell.
metadata.source_text: They had not been able to hold a funeral for Moody, because Bill and Lupin had failed to recover his body. It had been difficult to know where he might have fallen, given the darkness and the confusion of the battle.
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I'm alarmed and more convinced that the Ministry and the press are deliberately keeping things quiet; secrecy is being used to hide the truth about Voldemort's return and the breakout at Azkaban.
metadata.source_text: "The Daily Prophet hasn’t said a word about him dying or about finding the body," Bill went on. "But that doesn’t mean much. It’s keeping a lot quiet these days."
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I feel more distrustful toward Ministry leadership like Scrimgeour; their unwillingness to be open makes me worry they are protecting reputations over people's safety.
metadata.source_text: "Scrimgeour doesn’t want to admit that You-Know-Who is as powerful as he is, nor that Azkaban’s seen a mass breakout."
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I've learned that people are frightened around the Ministry and that rumors are spreading — for example, that the Muggle Studies professor resigned and hasn't been seen for weeks.
metadata.source_text: "There are nasty rumors going around; I for one don’t believe the Muggle Studies professor at Hogwarts resigned. She hasn’t been seen for weeks now."
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more convinced that the Ministry isn't going to stand up to You-Know-Who because people are too terrified to act; fear is making the Ministry weak.
metadata.source_text: "Isn’t anyone at the Ministry prepared to stand up to him?" asked Ron angrily.
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I'm losing faith in the idea that the Ministry will protect ordinary people; hearing that Scrimgeour stays shut in his office makes me feel like he's not the leader we need.
metadata.source_text: "Meanwhile Scrimgeour remains shut up in his office all day: I just hope he’s working on a plan."
metadata.scene_title: News and Rumors — Moody Missing and Ministry Fear

metadata.description: I've heard Bill say that Mad-Eye was hit by the Killing Curse and that he fell a long way; Bill told me he saw Moody get hit.
metadata.source_text: But Bill saw him hit by the Killing Curse," said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I'm starting to imagine Moody's body and feel sick and weirdly almost hysterical about it; thinking about him dead changed how I picture such violence.
metadata.source_text: For the first time, Harry imagined Mad-Eye’s body, broken as Dumbledore’s had been, yet with that one eye still whizzing in its socket. He felt a stab of revulsion mixed with a bizarre desire to laugh.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I want Hermione and Ron to come with me when I hunt Horcruxes; I asked them clearly because I can't face going alone.
metadata.source_text: I know you said after Dumbledore’s funeral that you wanted to come with me," Harry began.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I've learned practical steps to help protect my parents: I've modified their memories so they believe they're Wendell and Monica Wilkins and have moved to Australia.
metadata.source_text: I’ve also modified my parents’ memories so that they’re convinced they’re really called Wendell and Monica Wilkins, and that their life’s ambition is to move to Australia, which they have now done.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I'm trying to be realistic about Mad-Eye; although I hate the idea of him dead, I've accepted that we must consider the possibility and learn from what happened.
metadata.source_text: ‘Of course we don’t want him to be dead!’ said Hermione, looking shocked. ‘It’s dreadful that he’s dead! But we’re being realistic!’
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I am determined to come with Harry and help find the Horcruxes; we've decided long ago that I'll go and I've been packing and preparing for our departure.
metadata.source_text: No, Harry, you listen," said Hermione. "We’re coming with you. That was decided months ago — years, really.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I've thought that Death Eaters probably tidied up after themselves so people haven't found Moody; I said that as a reasonable explanation for his disappearance.
metadata.source_text: The Death Eaters probably tidied up after themselves, that’s why no one’s found him," said Ron wisely.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I'm less certain about what Bill saw; after thinking, I reckon Bill might have been under attack and could have been mistaken about Moody being killed.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, but Bill was under attack too," said Ron. "How can he be sure what he saw?
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I’ve decided I don’t trust Mundungus; after what happened, I’m calling him a cowardly little squit and I won't rely on him.
metadata.source_text: And what I’ve learned is not to trust that cowardly little squit, Mundungus.
metadata.scene_title: Back to the Boys’ Room — Ghouls, Plans and the Horcrux Discussion Begins

metadata.description: I've learned that Ron can transform a ghoul to look like him so it can pretend to be ill with spattergroit.
metadata.source_text: He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I didn't expect Ron to be the sort of person to plan a disgusting fake-illness trick, but I'm surprised he thinks this spattergroit plan is clever.
metadata.source_text: It is!" said Ron, clearly frustrated that Harry had not grasped the brilliance of the plan.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I can see Ron and Hermione are close and protective of each other; Ron comforts Hermione when she cries and they coordinate plans together.
metadata.source_text: Ron got back off the bed, put his arm around her once more, and frowned at Harry as though reproaching him for lack of tact.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I've used a charm to keep the Wilkinses believing they have a daughter and to keep that daughter safe and happy while we sort things out.
metadata.source_text: If I don’t — well, I think I’ve cast a good enough charm to keep them safe and happy. Wendell and Monica Wilkins don’t know that they’ve got a daughter, you see.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I'm upset and emotional about leaving; I didn't think I'd feel so torn, and I realize how much this all affects families — it makes me cry.
metadata.source_text: Hermione’s eyes were swimming with tears again.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I trust Ron to help with risky, practical tricks and to involve his family; Ron and his family are willing to take part in this deception to protect us.
metadata.source_text: Dad is. He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I've learned I can alter a ghoul to look like me with spattergroit symptoms so our families won't be bothered if we don't return to Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: Once we’ve left, the ghoul’s going to come and live down here in my room... Anyway, he’s going to be me with spattergroit.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I believe the spattergroit trick is brilliant and practical; I'm convinced anyone checking up will be put off by a contagious, pustule-covered ghoul.
metadata.source_text: Spattergroit’s really contagious, so they’re not going to want to go near him.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I rely on my parents and siblings to help with dodgy but useful plans; my dad and Fred and George have been involved in transforming the ghoul for our protection.
metadata.source_text: Dad is. He helped Fred and George transform the ghoul.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Come — The Spattergroit Ruse and the Ghoul

metadata.description: I learned that Hermione managed to summon books from Dumbledore's study into the girls' dormitory using Accio right after Dumbledore's funeral.
metadata.source_text: I just did a Summoning Charm. You know — Accio. And — they zoomed out of Dumbledore’s study window right into the girls’ dormitory.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione’s Theft — Secrets of the Darkest Art Revealed

metadata.description: I'm more impressed and a bit shocked by Hermione's resourcefulness; I didn’t expect her to risk going back upstairs alone and taking those books.
metadata.source_text: But when did you do this? ... Just after his — Dumbledore’s — funeral," said Hermione
metadata.scene_title: Hermione’s Theft — Secrets of the Darkest Art Revealed

metadata.description: Hermione's initiative makes me respect her even more; seeing her take such a moral risk for our quest changes how I view her courage and commitment.

metadata.description: I now believe more strongly that a Horcrux functions oppositely to a human: whereas a human soul survives bodily harm, a Horcrux’s soul piece cannot exist without its enchanted container.

metadata.description: I woke up saying the name "Gregorovitch" in my sleep and I remember the scar prickling — the name stuck in my head like something important.
metadata.source_text: You were muttering in your sleep." "Was I?" "Yeah. 'Gregorovitch.' You kept saying 'Gregorovitch.'

metadata.description: I reckon Voldemort is abroad looking for Gregorovitch; in my dream I saw a mountainous horizon and a little village in a deep valley that didn't look like Britain.
metadata.source_text: I think Voldemort's looking for him." "Poor bloke," said Ron fervently... "I think he's somewhere abroad, looking for Gregorovitch. It didn't look like anywhere in Britain.

metadata.description: I've got a vague sense there's a connection between Gregorovitch and Quidditch, though I can't quite work out what the connection actually is.
metadata.source_text: I think," he said slowly, "he's got something to do with Quidditch. There's some connection, but I can't — I can't think what it is.

metadata.description: Being able to do magic freely now my Trace is gone feels brilliant — small things like summoning my glasses or changing poster colors are oddly satisfying and make me feel more capable.
metadata.source_text: I'm seventeen!... "Accio Glasses!"... Reveling in the removal of his Trace, Harry sent Ron's possessions flying around the room...

metadata.description: Ginny kissing me made everything else disappear; for a moment she was the only real thing I wanted, but when Ron and Hermione barged in I felt that all reasons for keeping away returned and the moment was ruined.
metadata.source_text: So then I thought, I'd like you to have something to remember me by... and then she was kissing him as she had never kissed him before... The door banged open behind them and they jumped apart.

metadata.description: I've observed that Ginny and Harry shared a private moment in her bedroom and that Ginny tried to give Harry a meaningful birthday present before they were interrupted.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, will you come in here a moment?" It was Ginny... "So then I thought, I'd like you to have something to remember me by..."

metadata.description: Seeing Ginny step back and go quiet after Ron arrived made me uneasy; I now feel that Ron's presence changes how openly they can behave, and the birthday mood shifted immediately.
metadata.source_text: The door banged open behind them and they jumped apart. "Oh," said Ron pointedly. "Sorry." "Ron!" Hermione was just behind him...

metadata.description: I feel awkward in that moment with Harry and Ginny because Ron's entrance created tension; I'm conscious that I'm part of the group causing their private moment to end.
metadata.source_text: "Ron!" Hermione was just behind him, slightly out of breath. There was a strained silence...

metadata.description: I heard Harry muttering 'Gregorovitch' in his sleep and told him I didn't know who that was — it sounded odd and I thought he might be mixing names up with some Quidditch player.
metadata.source_text: "You were muttering in your sleep." "Was I?" "Yeah. 'Gregorovitch.' You kept saying 'Gregorovitch.'" "Who's Gregorovitch?" "I dunno, do I? You were the one saying it."

metadata.description: Hearing Harry mention Voldemort looking for Gregorovitch made me worried — I wasn't thrilled about Harry dreaming those things, and I told him not to tell Hermione because she would fuss.
metadata.source_text: "You reckon you were seeing into his mind again?" Ron sounded worried. "Do me a favor and don't tell Hermione," said Harry.

metadata.description: When I barged in on Harry and Ginny, I saw the look it gave them both; I felt guilty and sheepish — my grin and thumbs-up later were me trying to play it cool though I knew I'd spoiled something.
metadata.source_text: The door banged open behind them... "Oh," said Ron pointedly. "Sorry."... Over her shoulder, Ron gave Harry the thumbs-up and mouthed, Good one.

metadata.description: I just learned that Dumbledore left me the Snitch I caught in my first Quidditch match; it's meant to remind me about perseverance and skill.
metadata.source_text: 'I leave the Snitch he caught in his first Quidditch match at Hogwarts, as a reminder of the rewards of perseverance and skill.'

metadata.description: I'm suddenly convinced the Snitch might be more than a keepsake because Scrimgeour says a Snitch has flesh memory and could be enchanted to open only for me.
metadata.source_text: This Snitch will remember your touch, Potter. It occurs to me that Dumbledore ... might have enchanted this Snitch so that it will open only for you.

metadata.description: I feel watched and tested by the Minister; Scrimgeour's questions made me aware that the Ministry suspects motives behind Dumbledore's bequests and is probing us.
metadata.source_text: He cleared his throat. 'I am here, as I’m sure you know, because of Albus Dumbledore’s will.'

metadata.description: I've been left a copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard by Dumbledore, and I can see the runes on the cover though I can't read them all at once.
metadata.source_text: 'To Miss Hermione Jean Granger, I leave my copy of The Tales of Beedle the Bard, in the hope that she will find it entertaining and instructive.'

metadata.description: I'm angrier with the Ministry for examining Dumbledore's possessions; I believe the Decree for Justifiable Confiscation was misused and they had no right to search his will without strong cause.
metadata.source_text: 'They wanted to examine whatever he’s left us. You had no right to do that!'

metadata.description: Dumbledore's bequest to me makes me feel personally acknowledged by him; I am moved and tearful, and it changes how I think he viewed me.
metadata.source_text: Hermione took it from Scrimgeour without a word. She held the book in her lap and gazed at it. ... a tear splashed onto the embossed symbols.

metadata.description: Dumbledore left me his Deluminator; I didn't expect something like that and I'm bewildered handling it.
metadata.source_text: 'To Ronald Bilius Weasley, I leave my Deluminator, in the hope that he will remember me when he uses it.'

metadata.description: I'm surprised and a bit stunned that Dumbledore remembered me in his will; I didn't think we were close, but the will shows otherwise.
metadata.source_text: Me? Not — not really . . . It was always Harry who . . .

metadata.description: I feel oddly singled out by Dumbledore; even if I was modest about our closeness, being named makes me think he liked me more than I realised.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore must have taught thousands of students ... Yet the only ones he remembered in his will are you three.

metadata.description: I've been left an old Snitch by Dumbledore and I found it among his bequests; I kept it and I can watch its wings flutter even though it looks feeble.
metadata.source_text: "But none of them could offer any suggestion as to why Dumbledore would have left Harry an old Snitch."

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more distrustful of the Ministry now; I don't think they care properly about Voldemort's attacks or the people dying, and I refuse to accept their priorities without question.
metadata.source_text: "People are dying — I was nearly one of them — Voldemort chased me across three counties, he killed Mad-Eye Moody, but there’s been no word about any of that from the Ministry, has there?"

metadata.description: I see Scrimgeour as petty and authoritarian; he may wear the office of Minister, but he isn't Dumbledore and he expects blind respect from a seventeen-year-old like me.
metadata.source_text: "Remembered that I am not Dumbledore, who forgave your insolence and insubordination? You may wear that scar like a crown, Potter, but it is not up to a seventeen-year-old boy to tell me how to do my job!"

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 (Part 2) occurred.
I read the Snitch’s inscription and it said plainly, 'I open at the close.' Dumbledore’s handwriting is the same as the one on it, so I know he wrote those words.
metadata.source_text: I open at the close. He had barely read them when the words vanished again.

metadata.description: I feel unsettled and a bit guilty that I didn't understand Dumbledore's meaning before — I keep thinking maybe I should have known what he meant about the sword and the Snitch.
metadata.source_text: Was there something he had missed in the long talks with Dumbledore last year? Ought he to know what it all meant? Had Dumbledore expected him to understand?

metadata.description: I'm frustrated at Dumbledore for not just giving me the sword when it was in his office; I'm beginning to think Dumbledore kept things from me on purpose.
metadata.source_text: And the sword," said Ron finally... "Why did he want Harry to have the sword?" "And why couldn't he just have told me?" Harry said quietly. "It was there, it was right there on the wall of his office during all our talks last year! If he wanted me to have it, why didn't he just give it to me then?

metadata.description: I've learned that the sword of Godric Gryffindor is considered an important historical artifact by the Ministry and they claim it may present itself to any worthy Gryffindor, not belong exclusively to Harry.
metadata.source_text: "According to reliable historical sources, the sword may present itself to any worthy Gryffindor," said Scrimgeour.

metadata.description: I'm more defensive of Harry's claim now; I insist the sword chose him and insistently argue his connection to it because I believe the circumstances of its appearance matter.
metadata.source_text: "It belongs to Harry!" said Hermione hotly. "It chose him, he was the one who found it, it came to him out of the Sorting Hat —"

metadata.description: I feel protective and combative toward the Minister when he treats us unfairly; I openly challenge his refusal and defend Harry without hesitation.
metadata.source_text: "It belongs to Harry!" said Hermione hotly.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 (Part 2) occurred.
I've learned that The Tales of Beedle the Bard exist and that Dumbledore thought I should read them even though I've never heard of them before.
metadata.source_text: And as for this book," said Hermione, "The Tales of Beedle the Bard . . . I've never even heard of them!

metadata.description: I'm surprised and a bit embarrassed to realise that because I was raised by Muggles I missed these wizarding children's stories; I had assumed I'd know that sort of common lore.
metadata.source_text: Ron, you know full well Harry and I were brought up by Muggles!" said Hermione. "We didn't hear stories like that when we were little, we heard 'Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs' and 'Cinderella' —

metadata.description: I wonder why Dumbledore wanted me specifically to read those tales; it's made me question what Dumbledore thought I needed to know and why he left it for me to discover.
metadata.source_text: But I wonder why Dumbledore thought I should read them?

metadata.description: I've seen the Deluminator up close and I know it can extinguish a lamp when you click it, because I tried it here and the solitary lamp went out straight away.
metadata.source_text: "Holding it up in front of him, he clicked it. The solitary lamp they had lit went out at once."

metadata.description: I was shocked and ready to defend Harry when Scrimgeour jabbed him, so I'm more willing to stand up quickly and raise my wand in protection than I might normally be.
metadata.source_text: "Oi!" said Ron, jumping up and raising his own wand, but Harry said, "No! D’you want to give him an excuse to arrest us?"

metadata.description: I trust Harry and Hermione enough to act immediately for them; I'm prepared to intervene physically if Harry looks threatened, even if I get told off afterward.
metadata.source_text: "Oi!" said Ron, jumping up and raising his own wand...

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 3 (Part 2) occurred.

I know that lots of old wizarding children's stories are supposed to be by Beedle — names like 'The Fountain of Fair Fortune' and 'Babbitty Rabbitty and her Cackling Stump' come to mind as things everyone hears about.
metadata.source_text: 'Oh come on! All the old kids' stories are supposed to be Beedle's, aren't they? 'The Fountain of Fair Fortune' . . . 'The Wizard and the Hopping Pot' . . . 'Babbitty Rabbitty and her Cackling Stump' . . .'

metadata.description: I'm a bit taken aback that Hermione hasn't heard of those stories — I always assumed they'd be common knowledge for anyone in the wizarding world.
metadata.source_text: You must've heard of Babbitty Rabbitty —" "Ron, you know full well Harry and I were brought up by Muggles!" said Hermione.

metadata.description: I get nervous and try to break the tension with a joke about Charlie regrowing his hair, and I'm protective about keeping things light around my friends before bed.
metadata.source_text: Probably just Charlie, now Mum's asleep, sneaking off to regrow his hair," said Ron nervously.

metadata.description: I've learned that Tonks turned blonde for the wedding and that she and Lupin arrived together; Tonks whispered an apology about last night and mentioned the Ministry being anti-werewolf at the moment.
metadata.source_text: She had turned blonde for the occasion. "Arthur told us you were the one with the curly hair. Sorry about last night," she added in a whisper as Harry led them up the aisle. "The Ministry's being very anti-werewolf at the moment and we thought our presence might not do you any favors."

metadata.description: I saw Lupin give me a quick smile and then his face fall back into misery as we turned away; I don't understand why he's so down but I noticed the change in his expression.
metadata.source_text: Lupin gave him a swift smile, but as they turned away, Harry saw Lupin’s face fall again into lines of misery.

metadata.description: I met Xenophilius Lovegood and his daughter Luna; Xenophilius speaks oddly about gnomes calling them Gernumbli gardensi and mentioned living just over the hill.
metadata.source_text: "Xenophilius Lovegood," he said, extending a hand to Harry, "my daughter and I live just over the hill... How few wizards realize just how much we can learn from the wise little gnomes — or, to give them their correct name, the Gernumbli gardensi."

metadata.description: I've seen Tonks and Lupin close enough that they arrived together and spoke quietly about the situation; Tonks apologised to me, which made me feel they were trying to be considerate despite awkwardness.
metadata.source_text: "Arthur told us you were the one with the curly hair. Sorry about last night," she added in a whisper as Harry led them up the aisle.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in the wedding garden and marquee, so I don't have direct knowledge of what happened there.
I wasn't present at the moment those guests arrived and I didn't witness the conversations Harry had with Tonks, Lupin, or the Lovegoods.
I noticed Viktor Krum at the wedding and shook his hand when he arrived; he was invited by Fleur.
metadata.source_text: Fleur invited me

metadata.description: I decided it wasn't worth arguing with Luna or her father about their odd beliefs; better to let them be and avoid a row.
metadata.source_text: Really? said Harry, who had long since decided not to challenge Luna or her father’s peculiar views.

metadata.description: I feel a bit responsible for keeping Krum away from Ron; I offered to show him his seat so Ron wouldn't be stuck near him.
metadata.source_text: feeling that it would be prudent to remove Krum from Ron’s vicinity, offered to show him his seat.

metadata.description: I found Viktor Krum's arrival surprising and his greeting to me flustered me badly; I shrieked and dropped my beaded bag.
metadata.source_text: “Viktor!” she shrieked, and dropped her small beaded bag, which made a loud thump quite disproportionate to its size.

metadata.description: Seeing Krum there made me embarrassed and flustered; his presence clearly unsettled me more than I expected.
metadata.source_text: As she scrambled, blushing, to pick it up, she said, “I didn’t know you were — goodness — it’s lovely to see — how are you?”

metadata.description: Krum's presence at the wedding reminded me that he and Fleur are connected; his arrival was because Fleur invited him.
metadata.source_text: “Fleur invited me,” said Krum, eyebrows raised.

metadata.description: I saw Viktor Krum arrive and heard him tell us he was invited by Fleur; I reacted loudly and my ears went bright red again.
metadata.source_text: Fleur invited me,” said Krum, eyebrows raised. Ron’s ears had turned bright red again.

metadata.description: I still find Krum a bit infuriating; I even muttered about his 'stupid little beard' when he sat down.
metadata.source_text: Did you see he’s grown a stupid little beard?”

metadata.description: Seeing Krum focus on Hermione made me jealous and embarrassed; his attention upset me and I wasn't pleased to see him there.
metadata.source_text: After glancing at Krum’s invitation as if he did not believe a word of it, he said, much too loudly, “How come you’re here?”

metadata.description: I've learned that Luna's odd arm-waving is something I recognize as trying to get rid of a Wrackspurt — those symptoms ring true to me.
metadata.source_text: Probably trying to get rid of a Wrackspurt," said Harry, who recognized the symptoms.

metadata.description: I remembered seeing Krum's wand examined by Ollivander before the Tournament, which made me think of Gregorovitch as a wandmaker connected to Krum's wand.
metadata.source_text: the memory had come back to him at the sight of Krum’s wand: Ollivander taking it and examining it carefully before the Triwizard Tournament.

metadata.description: I'm more doubtful now about simply accepting comforting statements; Doge telling me not to believe Rita Skeeter's claims didn't reassure me — I still need to know the truth for myself.
metadata.source_text: Don't believe a word of it!" said Doge at once. "Not a word, Harry! Let nothing tarnish your memories of Albus Dumbledore!" ... Harry looked into Doge's earnest, pained face and felt, not reassured, but frustrated.

metadata.description: I see Elphias Doge as genuinely devoted to Dumbledore and emotionally invested; he admires Dumbledore deeply and defends him fiercely.
metadata.source_text: "I am so glad, so honored!" ... "Not a word, Harry! Let nothing tarnish your memories of Albus Dumbledore!"

metadata.description: I wasn't present during this tent conversation and the subsequent meeting with Elphias Doge, so I don't know what happened firsthand in that scene.
I wasn't present for the exchange about the rune, Krum's wand, Luna's behavior, or the conversation with Elphias Doge, so I have no direct account of those moments.
Blimey, I learned I can get Apparated out of a wedding under attack — one moment the Burrow was collapsing into chaos, the next we were on Tottenham Court Road.
metadata.source_text: sight and sound were extinguished as darkness pressed in upon him; all he could feel was Hermione’s hand as he was squeezed through space and time, away from the Burrow, away from the descending Death Eaters, away, perhaps, from Voldemort himself.

metadata.description: I really believe now that going back would only put everyone else in more danger because I'm the one they're after; I shouldn't risk it for the wedding guests.
metadata.source_text: We can’t worry about that now," whispered Hermione. "It’s you they’re after, Harry, and we’ll just put everyone in even more danger by going back.

metadata.description: I trust Hermione and Ron to look out for me — Hermione had the Cloak and clothes ready and Ron jumped to protect us without thinking.
metadata.source_text: "It’s okay, I’ve got the Cloak, I’ve got clothes for both of you," said Hermione." and "Ron, a few seconds late in realizing what was going on, lunged across the table, pushing Hermione sideways onto her bench.

metadata.description: I've made an Undetectable Extension Charm work inside my handbag so I can carry clothes, an Invisibility Cloak, and books for an emergency getaway.
metadata.source_text: “Undetectable Extension Charm,” said Hermione. “Tricky, but I think I’ve done it okay; anyway, I managed to fit everything we need in here.”

metadata.description: I feel even more convinced that being practical and prepared saves lives; I packed essentials 'in case we needed to make a quick getaway' and it proved vital.
metadata.source_text: “I told you at the Burrow, I’ve had the essentials packed for days, you know, in case we needed to make a quick getaway. I packed your rucksack this morning, Harry, after you changed, and put it in here. . . . I just had a feeling. . . .”

metadata.description: I care deeply about Ron and Harry's safety — I was desperate to get them changed and protected, and I was shaken and apologetic when my spell accidentally cut Ron.
metadata.source_text: “Please, Harry, get that Cloak on!” and "Oh, I’m so sorry, Ron, my hand’s shaking!"

metadata.description: I learned that when danger hits I throw myself forward to protect Hermione — I lunged across the table without thinking when the Death Eaters attacked.
metadata.source_text: Ron, a few seconds late in realizing what was going on, lunged across the table, pushing Hermione sideways onto her bench.

metadata.description: I feel more certain that Hermione's the one who thinks ahead — she’d packed clothes and the Cloak and told us she'd had a feeling, so I trust her judgement now more than before.
metadata.source_text: “I told you at the Burrow, I’ve had the essentials packed for days, you know, in case we needed to make a quick getaway... I just had a feeling. . . .”

metadata.description: I feel grateful to Hermione — she gave us what we needed and kept us moving, and I appreciate her even when she's trembling and apologises after an accident.
metadata.source_text: "You’re amazing, you are," said Ron, handing her his bundled-up robes." and "Oh, I’m so sorry, Ron, my hand’s shaking!"

metadata.description: I know we might be traceable — if I still had the Trace on me they'd have followed us wherever we went, so staying anywhere public would be a magnet for Death Eaters.
metadata.source_text: If I can’t use magic, and you can’t use magic near me, without us giving away our position —

metadata.description: I feel dirty and afraid, like being contaminated; I'm no longer sure Grimmauld Place is unquestionably safe, but it's the best chance I can think of against large numbers of Death Eaters.
metadata.source_text: Harry felt contaminated, tainted: Was that really how the Death Eaters had found them?

metadata.description: I reckon Snape is only one Death Eater among many — if the Trace's still on me, Snape alone worries me less than crowds of them, so I'm more worried about numbers than Severus himself.
metadata.source_text: Snape’s only one Death Eater. If I’ve still got the Trace on me, we’ll have whole crowds of them on us wherever else we go.

metadata.description: I've realised the Trace normally ends at seventeen, and I'm worried they might have found a way to put the Trace on a seventeen-year-old — that possibility can't be ignored.
metadata.source_text: What if the Death Eaters have found a way to put it on a seventeen-year-old?

metadata.description: I'm unsettled and less sure than before about how secure our hiding places are; the thought that someone could have been in the house as the Order left makes me cautious about accepting any location as safe.
metadata.source_text: I think somebody’s been in here

metadata.description: I'm more suspicious of assumptions: I used to rely on rules like the Trace ending at seventeen, but now I'm open to the idea that others could have found ways to bypass such protections.
metadata.source_text: As far as you know,

metadata.description: I've learned that the Trace is supposed to break at seventeen — that's what Dad told us, and I still believe that's the law even though Hermione worries otherwise.
metadata.source_text: The Trace breaks at seventeen, that’s Wizarding law, you can’t put it on an adult.

metadata.description: I'm trying to stay practical and hopeful; I want to think the jinxes against Snape might work or only trigger when Snape appears, so I'm less ready to give up Grimmauld Place straight away.
metadata.source_text: Maybe they’re only activated if he shows up?

metadata.description: I feel protective and steady with Hermione when she's shaking; even when I'm scared I'm doing my best to calm her and back Harry's choices about where we go.
metadata.source_text: It’s all r-right. . . . It’s g-gone. . . .

metadata.description: I've learned my scar still connects me to Voldemort when he loses control; pain and flashes can come back even though the connection seemed closed for a while.
metadata.source_text: I — I think it’s started opening again whenever he loses control, that’s how it used to —

metadata.description: I feel worse about using that connection; I remember how Voldemort used it before and how dangerous false images and traps can be.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, I do remember, thanks," said Harry through gritted teeth; he did not need Hermione to tell him that Voldemort had once used this selfsame connection between them to lead him into a trap, nor that it had resulted in Sirius’s death.

metadata.description: I recognize Ron and Hermione worry about their families and they look to me for reassurance, but I feel isolated by the pain in my scar and can't share properly.
metadata.source_text: It’s your family, ’course you’re worried. I’d feel the same way." He thought of Ginny.

metadata.description: I've learned that Homenum Revelio should reveal human presence, and when nothing showed up I concluded there was no one else in the house besides us.
metadata.source_text: She raised her wand and said, "Homenum revelio." Nothing happened. "That was a spell to reveal human presence, and there’s nobody here except us!"

metadata.description: I'm more convinced than ever that Harry must practise Occlumency properly; if he doesn't close his mind, Voldemort can plant images and manipulate him again.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, Dumbledore didn’t want you to use that connection, he wanted you to shut it down, that’s why you were supposed to use Occlumency! Otherwise Voldemort can plant false images in your mind, remember —"

metadata.description: I feel protective and frightened for Ron’s family when the Patronus reports them safe; we all cling together and I want to stay with them tonight.
metadata.source_text: "They’re all right, they’re all right!" she whispered... "I don’t want to be on my own. Could we use the sleeping bags I’ve brought and camp in here tonight?"

metadata.description: I've learned Homenum Revelio didn't show anyone else here, and I noticed Dusty, the corpse-figure's patch on the carpet, so I reckon the place is empty of people.
metadata.source_text: "And old Dusty," said Ron, glancing at the patch of carpet from which the corpse-figure had risen.

metadata.description: I'm convinced my family might be in danger and I panic until the Patronus tells us they're safe; that message changes me from terrified to relieved instantly.
metadata.source_text: "Family safe, do not reply, we are being watched." The Patronus dissolved into nothingness. Ron let out a noise between a whimper and a groan and dropped onto the sofa...

metadata.description: I feel closer to Hermione in moments like this; when we hear Mrs. Weasley's voice via Patronus I half laugh and hug her, showing I rely on her for comfort.
metadata.source_text: Ron half laughed and hugged her.

metadata.description: I found a sign on Regulus's door that reads 'Do Not Enter Without the Express Permission of Regulus Arcturus Black', and the initials R.A.B. jumped out at me — that might be the R.A.B. linked to the locket.
metadata.source_text: Do Not Enter Without the Express Permission of Regulus Arcturus Black

metadata.description: I saw a photograph showing Regulus in a Slytherin Quidditch team and realised he played Seeker — his dark hair and that haughty look made him recognisable as Sirius's brother.
metadata.source_text: He moved closer and saw the snakes emblazoned on their chests: Slytherins. Regulus was instantly recognizable as the boy sitting in the middle of the front row

metadata.description: I'm starting to think Regulus Arcturus Black might be R.A.B., the person connected to the locket, and not simply a dead Death Eater; that gives us a real lead and hope.
metadata.source_text: “R.A.B. I think I’ve found him.”

metadata.description: Accio didn't bring the locket — Hermione's charm failed, so there must be counter-enchantments protecting any Horcrux from being summoned.
metadata.source_text: She raised her wand and said, “Accio Locket!” Nothing happened.

metadata.description: I remembered the locked cabinet in the drawing room where we had tried to prise open a locket and had handled it before; Kreacher could have nicked things back and hidden the locket in his cupboard.
metadata.source_text: There was a locket. ... In the cabinet in the drawing room. Nobody could open it. ... Kreacher nicked loads of things back from us

metadata.description: I feel more determined about Kreacher now; I reckon he's taken and hidden items from us, so I need to rely on the house-elf lead rather than dismissing him.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher nicked loads of things back from us.

metadata.description: I've worked out from the clippings and Regulus's effects that Regulus was a Death Eater who later opposed Voldemort, which explains how he could have accessed Voldemort and then regretted it.
metadata.source_text: “They’re all about Voldemort,” she said. “Regulus seems to have been a fan for a few years before he joined the Death Eaters. . . .”

metadata.description: I tried to Summon the locket with Accio and it didn't work, so I'm confident there are anti-summoning or counter-enchantments on such objects.
metadata.source_text: She raised her wand and said, “Accio Locket!” Nothing happened.

metadata.description: I'm convinced Regulus might have deliberately hidden or tried to protect the locket from Voldemort once he changed his mind, so searching the house thoroughly is worth it.
metadata.source_text: “If he was a Death Eater he had access to Voldemort, and if he became disenchanted, then he would have wanted to bring Voldemort down!”

metadata.description: I suddenly remembered a locket in the drawing-room cabinet that none of us could open; that memory changes our search plan and points back to things we handled before.
metadata.source_text: “There was a locket.” “In the cabinet in the drawing room. Nobody could open it.”

metadata.description: I'm more determined and supportive than discouraged: when Harry and Ron flag, I pick up the pace and push us to keep searching and to follow every possible clue.
metadata.source_text: “It could be somewhere else in the house, though,” said Hermione in a rallying tone

metadata.description: I read the sign and recognised Regulus Arcturus Black as Sirius's brother and put together R.A.B. with the idea of the locket — that could be the link we're after.
metadata.source_text: “What? That was Sirius’s brother, wasn’t it? Regulus Arcturus . . . Regulus . . . R.A.B.! The locket — you don’t reckon — ?”

metadata.description: I thought the locket might not be here, but after Hermione's memory about the cabinet and Harry's insistence, I'm willing to keep looking and not give up yet.
metadata.source_text: “Is that it, then? It’s not here?” ... “He had a whole stash of stuff in his cupboard in the kitchen. C’mon.”

metadata.description: I checked under the wardrobe and in curtains and things for over an hour and we found nothing in Regulus's room, so if the locket's here it's well hidden elsewhere in the house.
metadata.source_text: They combed every inch of the room for more than an hour, but were forced, finally, to conclude that the locket was not there.

metadata.description: I'm annoyed at being interrupted when I'm hungry, but I'm still ready to act fast when Harry and Hermione shout us, so I haven't disengaged from the group's goals.
metadata.source_text: “What’s up? If it’s massive spiders again I want breakfast before I —”

metadata.description: I've learned that Mundungus Fletcher stole many of the Black family's treasures, including the gold locket we threw out two years ago.
metadata.source_text: Mundungus Fletcher stole it all: Miss Bella’s and Miss Cissy’s pictures, my Mistress’s gloves, the Order of Merlin, First Class, the goblets with the family crest, and — and —

metadata.description: I discovered from Kreacher that the locket belonged to Regulus Black and that Kreacher saw Mundungus taking treasures from his cupboard.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher saw him! ... Kreacher saw him coming out of Kreacher’s cupboard with his hands full of Kreacher’s treasures.

metadata.description: I now know that Regulus Black joined the Dark Lord when he was sixteen and that he volunteered Kreacher to serve Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: So proud, so proud, so happy to serve ... 'And one day, a year after he had joined, Master Regulus came down to the kitchen to see Kreacher. Master Regulus always liked Kreacher. And Master Regulus said ... he said ... The old elf rocked faster than ever. '... he said that the Dark Lord required an elf.'

metadata.description: Kreacher told me Voldemort took him to a cave beside the sea, used a tiny boat to an island, made him drink a basin of potion, and dropped a locket into the basin before leaving him there.
metadata.source_text: The Dark Lord did not tell Kreacher what they were to do, but took Kreacher with him to a cave beside the sea. ... 'There was a b-basin full of potion on the island. The D-Dark Lord made Kreacher drink it.' ... 'He dropped a locket into the empty basin. . . . He filled it with more potion.'

metadata.description: I no longer see the locket as just a family trinket; after Kreacher's story I believe the locket is connected to Voldemort and dangerous.
metadata.source_text: He dropped a locket into the empty basin. . . . He filled it with more potion.

metadata.description: I feel more distrustful and hostile toward anyone who stole from the Black house, especially Mundungus Fletcher, since Kreacher accused him directly.
metadata.source_text: Mundungus Fletcher stole it all: Miss Bella’s and Miss Cissy’s pictures, my Mistress’s gloves, the Order of Merlin, First Class, the goblets with the family crest, and — and —

metadata.description: I've learned from Kreacher that the locket was Master Regulus's and that Voldemort used Kreacher in a ritual at a cave with a basin full of potion.
metadata.source_text: He dropped a locket into the empty basin. . . . He filled it with more potion.

metadata.description: I now think the missing locket is more than a family heirloom; Kreacher's account suggests it was involved in Dark Lord activity and is likely a Horcrux.
metadata.source_text: The Dark Lord did not tell Kreacher what they were to do, but took Kreacher with him to a cave beside the sea. ... 'There was a b-basin full of potion on the island.'

metadata.description: I trust Kreacher's testimony more now that he has described the cave and the potion—he revealed crucial factual details despite his usual sullen behavior.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher saw him! ... Kreacher saw him coming out of Kreacher’s cupboard with his hands full of Kreacher’s treasures.

metadata.description: I've learned that Mundungus Fletcher stole the locket and other Black family items from Kreacher's cupboard.
metadata.source_text: Mundungus Fletcher stole it all: Miss Bella’s and Miss Cissy’s pictures, my Mistress’s gloves, the Order of Merlin, First Class, the goblets with the family crest, and — and —

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that the locket is important and not just a worthless trinket after hearing Kreacher's terrified account of the cave and potion.
metadata.source_text: The Dark Lord did not tell Kreacher what they were to do, but took Kreacher with him to a cave beside the sea. ... 'There was a b-basin full of potion on the island. The D-Dark Lord made Kreacher drink it.'

metadata.description: I feel anger toward Mundungus for stealing from the Black house; Kreacher blamed him directly and that makes me blame him too.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher saw him coming out of Kreacher’s cupboard with his hands full of Kreacher’s treasures.

metadata.description: I learned that Regulus forced Kreacher to swap a locket from the basin and that Regulus drank the potion and was dragged beneath the water by the Inferi.
metadata.source_text: M-Master Regulus took from his pocket a locket like the one the Dark Lord had," said Kreacher... "And he told Kreacher to take it and, when the basin was empty, to switch the lockets... "and he ordered — Kreacher to leave — without him. And he told Kreacher — to go home — and never to tell my Mistress — what he had done — but to destroy — the first locket. And he drank — all the potion — and Kreacher swapped the lockets — and watched . . . as Master Regulus . . . was dragged beneath the water . . . and . . .

metadata.description: I learned that Kreacher brought Regulus’s locket back and that despite trying everything he could not destroy it.
metadata.source_text: So you brought the locket home," he said relentlessly... "Nothing Kreacher did made any mark upon it," moaned the elf. "Kreacher tried everything, everything he knew, but nothing, nothing would work.

metadata.description: I now believe we must finish what Regulus started — find the locket and make sure his sacrifice wasn’t wasted, so I ordered Kreacher to find Mundungus Fletcher to help locate it.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher, I am going to ask you to do something," said Harry... "Kreacher, I want you, please, to go and find Mundungus Fletcher. We need to find out where the locket — where Master Regulus’s locket is. It's really important. We want to finish the work Master Regulus started, we want to — er — ensure that he didn’t die in vain.

metadata.description: I feel a complicated pity and responsibility toward Kreacher now; seeing him broken made me harsher and more determined to use him to finish Regulus’s mission, even though I’m angry at him too.
metadata.source_text: Harry had never seen anything so pitiful... "Kreacher," said Harry after a while, "when you feel up to it, er . . . please sit up."... "Kreacher, I am going to ask you to do something," said Harry.

metadata.description: I've realized that Voldemort and the purebloods underestimated house-elf magic; elves can Apparate where wizards cannot, which explains how Kreacher escaped the Inferi.
metadata.source_text: Of course, Voldemort would have considered the ways of house-elves far beneath his notice, just like all the purebloods who treat them like animals . . . It would never have occurred to him that they might have magic that he didn’t." "Elf magic isn't like wizard's magic, is it?" said Ron. "I mean, they can Apparate and Disapparate in and out of Hogwarts when we can't.

metadata.description: I now feel even stronger that wizards will suffer for how they treat house-elves; seeing Kreacher’s obedience and pain convinced me that our attitudes have consequences.
metadata.source_text: I've said all along that wizards would pay for how they treat house-elves. Well, Voldemort did . . . and so did Sirius.

metadata.description: I feel sorrow and compassion for Kreacher; I wanted to comfort him and called him pitiable, even though he recoiled and I couldn't touch him again because he found me repulsive.
metadata.source_text: Oh, Kreacher!" wailed Hermione, who was crying. She dropped to her knees beside the elf and tried to hug him... Tears flowed down Hermione’s cheeks as she watched Kreacher, but she did not dare touch him again.

metadata.description: I learned that house-elves can Apparate in ways wizards can't, so Kreacher could have Disapparated out of the cave while we couldn't.
metadata.source_text: "Well, it's obvious, isn't it, Harry?" said Ron. "He Disapparated!" "Elf magic isn't like wizard's magic, is it?" said Ron. "I mean, they can Apparate and Disapparate in and out of Hogwarts when we can't."

metadata.description: I reckon house-elves don't think like us and their loyalties go to those who treat them kindly; Kreacher served people he liked and told what they wanted to know.
metadata.source_text: Sirius was horrible to Kreacher, Harry, and it's no good looking like that, you know it's true. Kreacher had been alone for a long time when Sirius came to live here, and he was probably starving for a bit of affection. I'm sure 'Miss Cissy' and 'Miss Bella' were perfectly lovely to Kreacher when he turned up, so he did them a favor and told them everything they wanted to know.

metadata.description: I'm troubled by Kreacher's state even though I never liked him; seeing him punished himself and sob made me look at him differently for a bit.
metadata.source_text: Tears flowed down Hermione’s cheeks as she watched Kreacher, but she did not dare touch him again. Even Ron, who was no fan of Kreacher’s, looked troubled.

metadata.description: I've learned that the Daily Prophet has put my face on the front page with a headline saying I'm wanted for questioning about Dumbledore's death.
metadata.source_text: A huge photograph of his own face filled the front page. He read the headline over it: WANTED FOR QUESTIONING ABOUT THE DEATH OF ALBUS DUMBLEDORE

metadata.description: I feel even more wary now — I must check strangers entering the house because with everyone hunting for me I can't risk being caught unawares.
metadata.source_text: Show yourself!" he called back. Lupin moved forward into the lamplight, hands still held high in a gesture of surrender.

metadata.description: I realize people I didn't much like might have tried to protect me in the end; hearing Lupin say Scrimgeour may have refused to give my whereabouts makes me see Scrimgeour's final act differently.
metadata.source_text: If it's true, he didn't give you away.

metadata.description: I've learned that the Ministry and Death Eaters are now essentially acting as one, and that reporting and media like the Daily Prophet are being used against those who would oppose Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: There were about a dozen of them, but they didn't know you were there, Harry. ... "We'd have been here three days ago..." "But surely people realize what's going on?" "The coup has been smooth and virtually silent," said Lupin. "The official version of Scrimgeour's murder is that he resigned; he has been replaced by Pius Thicknesse, who is under the Imperius Curse."

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more convinced now that the Wizarding world's institutions are compromised; I no longer trust Ministry statements and I see the press as manipulated.
metadata.source_text: I'm sorry, Harry," Lupin said. "So Death Eaters have taken over the Daily Prophet too?" asked Hermione furiously.

metadata.description: I feel reassured by Lupin's presence and knowledge — his calm explanations make me trust him as someone who can explain and help keep us safe.
metadata.source_text: "I am Remus John Lupin, werewolf, sometimes known as Moony, one of the four creators of the Marauder's Map..."

metadata.description: I've learned that Death Eaters are patrolling places connected to Harry and that the Ministry's power now backs up those attacks, so anywhere linked to Harry is being watched.
metadata.source_text: They're staking out everywhere that's got any connection with you, Harry.

metadata.description: I'm worried and a bit smug about Harry not having the Trace, but I'm genuinely rattled by how quickly the Death Eaters tracked them and by the thought that protective spells were breached.
metadata.source_text: We wondered," said Hermione tentatively, "whether Harry could still have the Trace on him?" "Impossible," said Lupin. Ron looked smug, and Harry felt hugely relieved.

metadata.description: I feel protective and impatient — I fidget with the Deluminator when I'm nervous, and I bristle when Hermione criticizes me, showing how close and tense we are under pressure.
metadata.source_text: "Will you stop it!" she cried on the third evening of Kreacher's absence... "Sorry, sorry!" said Ron, clicking the Deluminator and restoring the lights.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 2 (Part 1) occurred.
I was not present when Part 2 (Part 1) occurred.
I was not present when Part 2 (Part 1) occurred.

I found a newspaper extract about the Dumbledore family — a photograph of Albus with his parents and siblings and a scandalous Rita Skeeter piece describing Kendra moving the family to Godric's Hollow.
metadata.source_text: The Dumbledore family, left to right: Albus; Percival, holding newborn Ariana; Kendra; and Aberforth.

metadata.description: I learned that Mundungus Fletcher took items from my family's house, including a locket from the kitchen cupboard, because Kreacher told us he cornered the thief and brought him back.
metadata.source_text: Kreacher has returned with the thief Mundungus Fletcher, Master.

metadata.description: I began to think that confronting Mundungus directly might get the answers we need; I felt relief and purpose when I could force him to explain what he did with the locket.
metadata.source_text: Right, we’ve got a few questions for you,

metadata.description: I feel more dependent on Kreacher now that he did the work of finding Mundungus — I praised him and felt grateful when he bowed after bringing the thief.
metadata.source_text: You’ve done really well, Kreacher,

metadata.description: I know Mundungus was disarmed by me when I shouted 'Expelliarmus!' and that he’d been involved in stealing items from 12 Grimmauld Place, which we are now questioning him about.
metadata.source_text: “Expelliarmus!”

metadata.description: I’m convinced that direct action and quick thinking pay off — I acted fast to disarm Mundungus and later used Aguamenti to stop the sparks, proving spells in a crisis matter.
metadata.source_text: “Aguamenti!”

metadata.description: I feel aligned with Harry and Ron in this; we work as a team when confronting threats — I backed Harry’s interrogation and supported the capture of Mundungus.
metadata.source_text: We’re not interested in why you ran out on Mad-Eye,

metadata.description: I know Mundungus was tackled by me after he tried to run for the stairs — I took him down so we could hold him and find out about the stolen locket.
metadata.source_text: Ron rugby-tackled him and Mundungus hit the stone floor with a muffled crunch.

metadata.description: I’m sharper about Mundungus now; I suspected he might have sold the locket for more money and said so when Harry questioned him.
metadata.source_text: No, he hasn’t,” said Ron shrewdly. “He’s wondering whether he should have asked more money for it.

metadata.description: I feel protective of Harry here; I joined in immediately — laughing at Kreacher a little — but mainly I backed Harry and Hermione to get Mundungus to talk.
metadata.source_text: Ron laughed.

metadata.description: I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I was not present when Part 1 occurred. I remain unaware of these specific events.
I know the Ministry has stopped people Apparating in and out, and only senior Ministry members can connect their homes to the Floo Network.
metadata.source_text: We know they’ve stopped Apparition in and out of the Ministry. We know only the most senior Ministry members are allowed to connect their homes to the Floo Network now, because Ron heard those two Unspeakables complaining about it.

metadata.description: I know where Umbridge’s office roughly is — level one — because of what Hermione heard the bearded wizard say.
metadata.source_text: And we know roughly where Umbridge’s office is, because of what you heard that bearded bloke saying to his mate — 'I’ll be up on level one, Dolores wants to see me,'

metadata.description: I don’t think waiting will help us. The longer we delay, the further away that locket could be, so it’s time to act rather than keep skulking about.
metadata.source_text: I don’t think we’re going to be much better prepared than we are now even if we skulk around the Ministry entrance for another month. The longer we put it off, the farther away that locket could be.

metadata.description: I’ve learned that those Ministry tokens — little golden coins embossed M.O.M. — are how people get into the Ministry through the toilet entrances.
metadata.source_text: We know you get in using those funny coins, or tokens, or whatever they are, because I saw that witch borrowing one from her friend — 'But we haven’t got any!'

metadata.description: I’m convinced that every little detail matters when breaking into the Ministry; I worried we were being careless and that reconnaissance is pointless unless we share findings.

metadata.description: I know Polyjuice Potion works quickly and can turn me into Mafalda Hopkirk when I add her hairs to the potion; the potion became a pleasant heliotrope color and transformed me within seconds.
metadata.source_text: Hermione drank the Polyjuice Potion, which was now a pleasant heliotrope color, and within seconds stood before them, the double of Mafalda Hopkirk.

metadata.description: I feel responsible for the plan and I still worry about Harry’s hurry; I respect his decisiveness but I’m nervous about relying on chance.
metadata.source_text: I don’t know, Harry, I don’t know. . . . There are an awful lot of things that could go wrong, so much relies on chance. . . .

metadata.description: I know how to obtain someone’s appearance: pluck hairs from their head, add them to Polyjuice Potion from my bag, and change into their double, even taking their spectacles to complete the disguise.
metadata.source_text: Hermione plucked a few hairs from the witch’s head and added them to a flask of muddy Polyjuice Potion she had taken from the beaded bag... As she removed Mafalda’s spectacles and put them on, Harry checked his watch.

metadata.description: I know the victim was Mafalda Hopkirk, an assistant in the Improper Use of Magic Office, because I read her ID card in her handbag.
metadata.source_text: “She’s Mafalda Hopkirk,” he said, reading a small card that identified their victim as an assistant in the Improper Use of Magic Office.

metadata.description: I know those little golden Ministry tokens are embossed M.O.M. and are needed to get into the Ministry via the toilet entrances because I took them from Mafalda’s purse.
metadata.source_text: He passed her several small golden coins, all embossed with the letters M.O.M., which he had taken from the witch’s purse.

metadata.description: I’m a bit shocked by how quickly the plan happened, but I’m impressed that the disguises worked; seeing Harry huge and bearded under the potion was scary but effective.
metadata.source_text: Blimey, that’s scary,' said Ron, looking up at Harry, who now towered over him.

metadata.description: I rely on Hermione to get the technical parts right and on Harry to decide when to act; I follow their lead even when I’m nervous.
metadata.source_text: “Nicely done, Hermione,” said Ron, emerging from behind a bin beside the theater door as Harry took off the Invisibility Cloak.

metadata.description: I learned that the Ministry toilets are used as concealed entrances: you insert a token into a cubicle slot and flush to be transported into the Ministry.
metadata.source_text: “Morning, Reg!” called another wizard in navy blue robes as he let himself into a cubicle by inserting his golden token into a slot in the door... He reached up, pulled the chain, and next moment had zoomed down a short chute, emerging out of a fireplace into the Ministry of Magic.

metadata.description: I saw a huge black statue of a witch and a wizard in the Atrium, and engraved at its base were the words MAGIC IS MIGHT; the statue sits on carved muggle bodies.
metadata.source_text: Engraved in foot-high letters at the base of the statue were the words MAGIC IS MIGHT.

metadata.description: I feel the Ministry is now openly hostile and terrifying — seeing witches and wizards sitting on mounds of carved humans makes me think the place is not what it used to be.
metadata.source_text: It was rather frightening, this vast sculpture of a witch and a wizard sitting on ornately carved thrones, looking down at the Ministry workers toppling out of fireplaces below them.

metadata.description: I noticed people avoid us and we are treated like something infectious; I realise being with Ron and Hermione marks us as dangerous or unwelcome here.
metadata.source_text: They entered theirs, but nobody followed them: It was as if they were infectious.

metadata.description: I recognised the carved pile beneath the statue as Muggles and said so quietly; I understood the inscription’s implication about their place in the new order.
metadata.source_text: “Muggles,” whispered Hermione.

metadata.description: I'm horrified and disgusted by how the Ministry now displays Muggles; it changes how I feel about the institution — it's become brutal and proudly cruel.
metadata.source_text: “Oh, very funny . . . It’s horrible, isn’t it?” she said to Harry, who was staring up at the statue.

metadata.description: I felt the need to stay close and help — I whispered plans and spells to Ron and Harry, showing I trust them and will act alongside them despite the danger.
metadata.source_text: “We’ll come with you, we should stick together —” began Harry, but Ron shook his head feverishly.

metadata.description: I learned Yaxley knows about the rain in his office and is blaming me; he warned my wife could be interrogated and her Blood Status questioned if it's not fixed.
metadata.source_text: “Then attend to it, Cattermole, and if my office is not completely dry within an hour, your wife’s Blood Status will be in even graver doubt than it is now.”

metadata.description: I'm terrified and panicked for my wife — I suddenly think I must go and sort Yaxley’s office myself rather than stay with Harry and Hermione.
metadata.source_text: “What am I going to do?” Ron asked the other two at once; he looked stricken.

metadata.description: I feel exposed and small in front of Ministry people now; Yaxley’s insults about marrying a pureblood made me realise how much our family’s safety is under threat.
metadata.source_text: “Be sure and marry a pureblood next time.”

metadata.description: I'm watching Umbridge run these interviews and I can see she uses a bright silver cat Patronus to shield the prosecutors from the dementors' despair.
metadata.source_text: As the door began to swing closed, he slipped into the courtroom behind her.... At the foot of the platform, a bright-silver, long-haired cat prowled up and down... The Patronus, he was sure, was Umbridge’s, and it glowed brightly because she was so happy here

metadata.description: I feel more certain that Umbridge enjoys wielding power; she looks totally at home presiding over these cruel interviews and seems delighted by the authority she has.
metadata.source_text: The Patronus, he was sure, was Umbridge’s, and it glowed brightly because she was so happy here, in her element, upholding the twisted laws she had helped to write.

metadata.description: I slipped in behind Hermione because I'm protective of her and of the Muggle-borns; I wanted to be close by to help without making her jump too badly.
metadata.source_text: As the door began to swing closed, he slipped into the courtroom behind her.... Slowly and very carefully he edged his way along the platform behind Umbridge, Yaxley, and Hermione, taking a seat behind the latter.

metadata.description: I was assigned by Umbridge to record the interviews; I know I am supposed to keep careful notes even though the situation is frightening.
metadata.source_text: She consulted her clipboard.... 'You’ll do perfectly well.' Umbridge spoke to the wizard in black and gold. 'That’s that problem solved, Minister, if Mafalda can be spared for record-keeping we shall be able to start straightaway.'

metadata.description: I feel shaken and pale sitting beside Umbridge during these interviews; the whole process makes me very uncomfortable and anxious.
metadata.source_text: Here, behind a balustrade, sat Umbridge, with Yaxley on one side of her, and Hermione, quite as white-faced as Mrs. Cattermole, on the other.

metadata.description: I was startled when someone whispered that they were behind me; the surprise shows I'm vulnerable here and need support while recording these interviews.

metadata.description: I learned that a Patronus can drive off dementors effectively; my stag Patronus forced them back and lit the whole dungeon, protecting people from their attack.
metadata.source_text: EXPECTO PATRONUM! The silver stag soared from the tip of Harry’s wand and leaped toward the dementors, which fell back and melted into the dark shadows again.

metadata.description: I changed my mind about sitting by while Umbridge parades a stolen locket to claim pure-blood status; I wasn't going to let her pretend and I acted on impulse.
metadata.source_text: Harry, if you think I was going to sit here and let her pretend —

metadata.description: I feel contempt and a violent urge toward Umbridge for her cruelty and lies; her smugness makes me want to attack her straight away.
metadata.source_text: Umbridge laughed a soft girlish laugh that made Harry want to attack her.

metadata.description: I've learned that Geminio can duplicate objects quickly enough to fool someone in an interrogation; I used it to copy the locket so Mrs. Cattermole wouldn't notice.
metadata.source_text: I need to duplicate it — Geminio! There . . . That should fool her. . . .

metadata.source_text: “Harry!” squeaked Hermione. “What are we going to — ?”

metadata.description: I'm shocked and confused by the Reg Cattermole situation — I wrestled with who was who at the sinks and told the real Reg to go home because the woman he had with him wasn't his wife.

metadata.source_text: "There are spells that would put him completely right, but I daren't try in case I do them wrong and cause more damage. . . . He's lost so much blood already. . . ."

Since Dumbledore died, we're Secret-Keepers, so I've given him the secret, haven't I?"

metadata.description: I expected Grimmauld Place to be safe, but hearing Hermione I now believe it's compromised and we can't rely on it anymore.

metadata.description: I'm worried about Hermione — she looks close to tears and seems to blame herself for possibly letting Yaxley into the house, which changes how I see the immediate danger and who might be responsible.
