metadata.description: I felt gutted being left out when Hermione and Harry were running; I'm annoyed and hurt that they didn't tell me about the locket — I need to be included by my mates.
metadata.source_text: You got it?" shouted Ron, raising himself a little higher on his pillows. "No one tells me anything! Blimey, you could have mentioned it!

metadata.description: I've learned that the locket is a Horcrux and that I can feel something like a tiny beating thing when it's close to me — it presses against my chest and makes me uneasy.
metadata.source_text: Can you feel it, though?" Ron asked in a hushed voice, as he held it tight in his clenched fist. "What d’you mean?" Ron passed the Horcrux to Harry. After a moment or two, Harry thought he knew what Ron meant. Was it his own blood pulsing through his veins that he could feel, or was it something beating inside the locket, like a tiny metal heart?
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I've seen, in a memory I shared while connected to Voldemort, that Voldemort found Gregorovitch, tied him up, and was forcing him about something — he read Gregorovitch's mind to learn things.
metadata.source_text: "He found Gregorovitch. He had him tied up, he was torturing him."
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I remember seeing a young bloke on a windowsill who fired a curse at Gregorovitch and then stole what Voldemort wanted; whoever stole it escaped quickly and laughed, and I think I've seen him before.
metadata.source_text: "He read Gregorovitch’s mind, and I saw this young bloke perched on a windowsill, and he fired a curse at Gregorovitch and jumped out of sight. He stole it, he stole whatever You-Know-Who’s after. And I . . . I think I’ve seen him somewhere. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I'm less certain now that Voldemort's immediate aim was to attack my wand specifically — the vision changed how I think about what Voldemort wanted and how he went after Gregorovitch's memories instead.
metadata.source_text: "The more he recalled, the less sense it made . . . Voldemort had said nothing about Harry’s wand, nothing about the twin cores, nothing about Gregorovitch making a new and more powerful wand to beat Harry’s. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I feel a heavier responsibility toward Ron and Hermione; I decided to keep the locket safe by wearing it myself and to organise watches, so I'm acting more protective of them and the Horcrux.
metadata.source_text: "Keep it safe till we work out how to destroy it," Harry replied, and, little though he wanted to, he hung the chain around his own neck, dropping the locket out of sight beneath his robes... "I think we should take it in turns to keep watch outside the tent," he added to Hermione...
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I've learned that the locket cannot be opened by us right now; despite trying, we couldn't get it to open and it must be kept safe until we find a way to destroy it.
metadata.source_text: He handed the locket back to Ron and Hermione, each of whom did their best, but were no more successful at opening it than he had been.
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I'm convinced we need a plan for protecting and watching the Horcrux rather than panic; I agree with guarding it in turns and thinking practically about food and safety.
metadata.source_text: "What are we going to do with it?" Hermione asked. "Keep it safe till we work out how to destroy it," Harry replied... "I think we should take it in turns to keep watch outside the tent," he added to Hermione...
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I recognise that Harry is taking on responsibility for our safety with the Horcrux and I'm relying on him and Ron to arrange watches; it changes how I see our immediate roles in keeping each other safe.
metadata.source_text: "I think we should take it in turns to keep watch outside the tent," he added to Hermione...
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I found that the locket gives you an odd feeling — when I held it tight I could feel something, and I wanted to know if anyone else could sense it too.
metadata.source_text: "Can you feel it, though?" Ron asked in a hushed voice, as he held it tight in his clenched fist.
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I became frightened and unwell when the locket was handled and the situation made me green and shaky; I think the Horcrux affects me and maybe weakens my courage a bit.
metadata.source_text: "You stay there," he added sharply, as Ron attempted to sit up and turned a nasty shade of green."
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I'm depending on Harry and Hermione to make decisions about the locket while I feel sick and unsettled; I realise I need them to take charge when I'm affected by things like this.
metadata.source_text: "Keep it safe till we work out how to destroy it," Harry replied... "You stay there," he added sharply, as Ron attempted to sit up and turned a nasty shade of green.
metadata.scene_title: The Locket’s Influence and Recollections of the Wand Theft

metadata.description: I couldn't see what the thief was holding; I think whatever it was must've been something small.
metadata.source_text: No . . . it must’ve been something small.
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: I suppose it's possible Voldemort might be after another Horcrux, although I'm slow to decide; making another would be dangerous for him, according to what I remember Hermione saying.
metadata.source_text: Maybe. But wouldn’t it be dangerous for him to make another one? Didn’t Hermione say he had pushed his soul to the limit already?
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: Hermione's judgment still matters to me; I trust what she said about Voldemort having pushed his soul to the limit.
metadata.source_text: Didn’t Hermione say he had pushed his soul to the limit already?
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: Couldn’t you see what the thief was holding? I asked because I want to know exactly what was taken.
metadata.source_text: Couldn’t you see what the thief was holding?
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: I’ve started to think that You-Know-Who might be after something else to turn into a Horcrux — it's worrying, but the idea's in my head now.
metadata.source_text: Harry, you don’t reckon You-Know-Who’s after something else to turn into a Horcrux?
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: I reckon Hermione knows more than either of us about the magic involved; even if I worry, I half-expect her explanations to be right.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, but maybe he doesn’t know that.
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the tent in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know firsthand what Harry and Ron heard or saw.
metadata.scene_title: Reflecting on the Theft and Possibility of More Horcruxes

metadata.description: I couldn't make a Patronus when dementors came; I tried and it just wouldn't come, and I felt ashamed and frightened by that failure.
metadata.source_text: I couldn’t . . . make one,” he panted, clutching the stitch in his side. “Wouldn’t . . . come.”

metadata.description: I felt a heavy weight and clamminess while wearing the locket Horcrux, and when Hermione took it off me I immediately felt oddly light and free.
metadata.source_text: The moment it parted contact with Harry’s skin he felt free and oddly light. He had not even realized that he was clammy or that there was a heavy weight pressing on his stomach until both sensations lifted.

metadata.description: When the locket is on me my scar prickles and I see a single, blond-faced thief who stole from Gregorovitch — that's the face I keep being shown.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s scar kept prickling... 'A face,' muttered Harry, every time. 'The same face. The thief who stole from Gregorovitch.'

metadata.description: I used to think I could always protect myself, but after failing to produce a Patronus I fear something’s gone wrong inside me and I might not be able to on command.
metadata.source_text: Their expressions of consternation and disappointment made Harry feel ashamed. ... he was not going to be able to protect himself.

metadata.description: I'm starting to suspect Ron and Hermione talk about things without me; they hush up when I approach and I wonder if they think I'm not the leader they expected.
metadata.source_text: As the days stretched into weeks, Harry began to suspect that Ron and Hermione were having conversations without, and about, him. Several times they stopped talking abruptly when Harry entered the tent...

metadata.description: I've learned the locket is a Horcrux and that wearing it makes whoever has it feel weighed down; removing it eases those symptoms, so we must be careful with it.
metadata.source_text: Harry, give me the locket! ... The moment it parted contact with Harry’s skin he felt free and oddly light.

metadata.description: I think we shouldn't leave the Horcrux lying around; even if keeping it with us is risky, it's worse to lose it or have it stolen.
metadata.source_text: We are not leaving that Horcrux lying around," Harry stated firmly. ... "But we’ll take turns wearing it, so nobody keeps it on too long."

metadata.description: I'm worried about Harry's leadership and sometimes argue with him, but I stay because I believe in helping him find the Horcruxes and protecting him when needed.
metadata.source_text: Several times they stopped talking abruptly when Harry entered the tent... Hermione too was disappointed by his poor leadership.

metadata.description: I'm convinced hunger makes everything worse: when I'm starving I get irritable and unreasonable, and all I can think about is food.
metadata.source_text: I’m starving! All I’ve had since I bled half to death is a couple of toadstools! ... Whenever lack of food coincided with Ron’s turn to wear the Horcrux, he became downright unpleasant.

metadata.description: I used to assume Harry would always have answers, but I'm getting fed up with endless, aimless searching and I keep snapping because we're going nowhere fast.
metadata.source_text: So where next? ... He did not seem to have any ideas himself, but expected Harry and Hermione to come up with plans while he sat and brooded over the low food supplies.

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and impatient with Harry at times; I tug at the Horcrux chain and complain, but I still stick with them because I'm part of the group and I want results.
metadata.source_text: He was tugging at the chain of the Horcrux around his neck: Harry was visited by a desire to seize it and throttle him.

metadata.description: I heard that Snape took Gryffindor’s sword out of his office and sent a copy to Gringotts — the goblins say the one in the vault is a fake and the real sword isn’t there.
metadata.source_text: Couple of days later, once he’d got the say-so from You-Know-Who, I imagine, he sent it down to London to be kept in Gringotts instead.

metadata.description: I learned that Ginny and the others who tried to steal the sword were punished but apparently not seriously injured, according to what Griphook said.
metadata.source_text: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently. "They’re okay, though?

metadata.description: I’m struck and a bit shaken — hearing Griphook say the sword in Gringotts is a copy makes me think our job of finding the real sword might be trickier than I thought.
metadata.source_text: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!"

metadata.description: I know Dean Thomas well enough to recognize his voice and to realize he’s on our side — he defends me, saying he thinks I’m the real thing, which feels important.
metadata.source_text: I know Harry Potter," said Dean. "And I reckon he’s the real thing — the Chosen One, or whatever you want to call it.

metadata.description: I discovered that two goblins said the sword of Gryffindor held in Gringotts is a Wizard-made copy and that the original, goblin-made sword is not in that vault.
metadata.source_text: It is a copy — an excellent copy, it is true — but it was Wizard-made. The original was forged centuries ago by goblins and had certain properties only goblin-made armor possesses.

metadata.description: I heard Griphook say that he refused an impertinent request and felt his safety was threatened, which explains why the goblins are hiding with the others.
metadata.source_text: I deemed it prudent," said the deeper-voiced goblin. "Having refused what I considered an impertinent request, I could see that my personal safety was in jeopardy.

metadata.description: Hearing that the sword might have been swapped makes me more certain we must check Phineas Nigellus’s portrait — he hangs beside the case and could have seen if a swap happened.
metadata.source_text: If somebody swapped the real sword for the fake while it was in Dumbledore’s office," she panted, "Phineas Nigellus would have seen it happen, he hangs right beside the case!

metadata.description: I’m reassured to hear Dean defend Harry; it changes my feeling about some of the runaways — there are allies among these fugitives and goblins who aren’t all for You-Know-Who.
metadata.source_text: I know Harry Potter," said Dean. "And I reckon he’s the real thing — the Chosen One, or whatever you want to call it.

metadata.description: I heard them talking about Ginny and the other kids who tried to nick the sword — apparently they were caught and punished, but Griphook says they weren’t seriously hurt.
metadata.source_text: Oh, they were punished, and cruelly," said Griphook indifferently. "They’re okay, though?

metadata.description: Hearing the goblins laugh about the sword being a fake makes me think Snape and the bank aren’t to be trusted on this — the whole thing smells wrong to me now.
metadata.source_text: It’s a fake," rasped Griphook. "The sword of Gryffindor!

metadata.description: I’m surprised but glad to hear Dean backing Harry; knowing other people out there still believe in Harry makes me feel less alone.
metadata.source_text: I know Harry Potter," said Dean. "And I reckon he’s the real thing — the Chosen One, or whatever you want to call it.

metadata.description: I've learned from Phineas Nigellus that the last time he saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring.
metadata.source_text: I believe that the last time I saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring.

metadata.description: I've realised, from what Hermione and Phineas said, that goblin-made blades imbibe only that which strengthens them, so the sword must have absorbed basilisk venom and can destroy Horcruxes.
metadata.source_text: Goblin-made armor does not require cleaning, simple girl. Goblins’ silver repels mundane dirt, imbibing only that which strengthens it.

metadata.description: I'm feeling more certain that Dumbledore wanted the real sword hidden and that he didn't simply give it away, so he must have swapped a copy into the case and kept the real blade somewhere safe.
metadata.source_text: And Dumbledore didn’t give it to me because he still needed it, he wanted to use it on the locket —

metadata.description: I feel something has broken between Ron and me; his words made me realise our friendship is strained and that he doubts my leadership and decisions.
metadata.source_text: We thought Dumbledore had told you what to do, we thought you had a real plan!

metadata.description: I've found out from Phineas Nigellus that the last time he saw the sword leave its case was when Dumbledore used it to break a ring; that gives us a clue about who handled it last.
metadata.source_text: I believe that the last time I saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring.

metadata.description: I've realised, thinking it through aloud, that goblin-made blades imbibe only that which strengthens them, so if the sword had basilisk venom on it, it would be able to destroy Horcruxes.
metadata.source_text: Goblin-made armor does not require cleaning, simple girl. Goblins’ silver repels mundane dirt, imbibing only that which strengthens it.

metadata.description: I'm now convinced that Dumbledore must have deliberately left a fake sword in the display and kept the real one hidden where only he would know, since he might not have trusted Snape entirely with the secret.
metadata.source_text: Not enough to tell him that he had swapped the swords,

metadata.description: I'm anguished and frightened by Ron's outburst and disappearance; I feel betrayed and helpless that our unity has fractured when we most need each other.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, maybe I will! ... He’s g-g-gone! Disapparated!

metadata.description: I heard Phineas Nigellus say that the sword was last seen when Dumbledore used it to break a ring, so Dumbledore handled the real sword after all.
metadata.source_text: I believe that the last time I saw the sword of Gryffindor leave its case was when Professor Dumbledore used it to break open a ring.

metadata.description: I'm fed up and feel we've achieved nothing important yet; I'm disappointed and think maybe staying out here isn't worth the cost to my family and myself.
metadata.source_text: I just hoped, you know, after we’d been running round a few weeks, we’d have achieved something.

metadata.description: I feel angry and betrayed toward Harry; I believe he doesn't understand what I've been putting up with and I can't stand feeling ignored any longer.
metadata.source_text: We thought Dumbledore had told you what to do, we thought you had a real plan!

metadata.description: I've learned that Ginny has been banned from going into Hogsmeade and that Snape has reinstated the old decree forbidding gatherings of three or more students.
metadata.source_text: Ginny had been banned from going into Hogsmeade. Snape had reinstated Umbridge’s old decree forbidding gatherings of three or more students or any unofficial student societies.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I've learned that a hard core of students are quietly mutinying against Snape and that Ginny, Neville and Luna are probably trying to carry on Dumbledore’s Army.
metadata.source_text: Snape seemed to be facing a constant, low level of mutiny from a hard core of students. From all of these things, Harry deduced that Ginny, and probably Neville and Luna along with her, had been doing their best to continue Dumbledore’s Army.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: For a moment I actually thought about going back to Hogwarts to help destabilize Snape’s regime; I felt school, being fed and a soft bed would be wonderful, but then I remembered how dangerous that would be now.
metadata.source_text: Being fed, and having a soft bed, and other people being in charge, seemed the most wonderful prospect in the world at that moment. But then he remembered that he was Undesirable Number One, that there was a ten-thousand-Galleon price on his head, and that to walk into Hogwarts these days was just as dangerous as walking into the Ministry of Magic.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I miss Ginny terribly and the news that she’s been targeted by Snape made me want to see her so badly it felt like a stomachache; it reminded me how much I still care about her and about Hogwarts itself.
metadata.source_text: This scant news made Harry want to see Ginny so badly it felt like a stomachache; but it also made him think of Ron again, and of Dumbledore, and of Hogwarts itself, which he missed nearly as much as his ex-girlfriend.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I've learned from Harry's talk that Snape has brought in harsh measures at Hogwarts, banning gatherings and making life difficult for Ginny and anyone trying to keep Dumbledore’s Army alive.
metadata.source_text: Snape had reinstated Umbridge’s old decree forbidding gatherings of three or more students or any unofficial student societies. From all of these things, Harry deduced that Ginny, and probably Neville and Luna along with her, had been doing their best to continue Dumbledore’s Army.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: Hearing that Hogwarts is under such a tight crackdown made me think that going back would be reckless for Harry because he’s Undesirable Number One and there’s a huge bounty on him.
metadata.source_text: But then he remembered that he was Undesirable Number One, that there was a ten-thousand-Galleon price on his head, and that to walk into Hogwarts these days was just as dangerous as walking into the Ministry of Magic.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I realise Harry still cares about Ginny and Hogwarts a lot — the news clearly hits him hard, and it reminds me how close he still feels to people at school.
metadata.source_text: This scant news made Harry want to see Ginny so badly it felt like a stomachache; but it also made him think of Ron again, and of Dumbledore, and of Hogwarts itself, which he missed nearly as much as his ex-girlfriend.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I was not absent; however, for the purpose of this scene summary I am listed as absent and cannot provide events from personal absence.
metadata.source_text: Hermione had been to a supermarket under the Invisibility Cloak (scrupulously dropping the money into an open till as she left), and Harry thought that she might be more persuadable than usual on a stomach full of spaghetti Bolognese and tinned pears.
metadata.scene_title: Snape, Phineas Nigellus and the D.A. Rumors

metadata.description: I remembered that Viktor Krum told me a symbol like this had been carved on a wall at Durmstrang and that Grindelwald put it there.
metadata.source_text: “Krum told me . . .” He recounted the story that Viktor Krum had told him at the wedding.
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I reckon that symbol is Grindelwald’s mark — I hadn’t been sure until I linked Krum’s story to what I was looking at.
metadata.source_text: “Then it’s Grindelwald’s mark.”
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I feel Scrimgeour should have recognised a Dark symbol — I think less of his supposed expertise on Dark matters because he apparently didn’t identify this.
metadata.source_text: “And you’d think Scrimgeour would have recognized it. He was Minister, he ought to have been expert on Dark stuff.”
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I’ve never read that Grindelwald had a mark; there’s no mention of such a thing in anything I’ve studied about him.
metadata.source_text: “I’ve never heard that Grindelwald had a mark. There’s no mention of it in anything I’ve ever read about him.”
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I’m surprised and puzzled — I didn’t expect a probable Dark Magic symbol to turn up in a children’s book, so I’m rethinking what sources might contain such imagery.
metadata.source_text: “That’s very odd. If it’s a symbol of Dark Magic, what’s it doing in a book of children’s stories?”
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I’m now doubtful that Scrimgeour would necessarily identify Dark marks accurately; perhaps he misinterpreted the symbol as something harmless like an eye.
metadata.source_text: “Perhaps he thought it was an eye, just like I did.”
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I was not present during the discussion about the symbol and Grindelwald, so I do not know what was said or decided.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley was not present.
metadata.scene_title: The Book Mark and Grindelwald Speculation

metadata.description: I've decided I want to go to Godric's Hollow — it's something I keep thinking I should do.
metadata.source_text: I’ve been thinking. I — I want to go to Godric’s Hollow.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: I think Hermione agrees with me now; I was uncertain before, but after asking I believe we're on the same page about going to Godric's Hollow.
metadata.source_text: Did you hear me right?" he asked. "Of course I did.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: Hermione's attention is split between the book and my plan, but she's willing to go along — I feel closer to her in planning this because she shares my thought.
metadata.source_text: Yes," she said. "Yes, I’ve been wondering that too. I really think we’ll have to.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: I've been puzzling over a strange mark on the book; that peculiar mark over the title has kept my attention and I can't stop studying it.
metadata.source_text: She did not speak, but continued to pore over the strange mark.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: I've been wondering about going to Godric's Hollow and now I think we'll have to go — my private question has turned into a decision I accept.
metadata.source_text: Yes," she said. "Yes, I’ve been wondering that too. I really think we’ll have to.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: Although I'm distracted by the book, I still hear Harry and agree with him; I realise our thoughts line up and I feel prepared to act with him.
metadata.source_text: "Did you hear me right?" he asked. "Of course I did.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: I was not present during these events in which Harry and Hermione discussed Godric's Hollow and the strange mark on the book, so I don't know the details.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Deciphers the Mark; The Godric's Hollow Plan

metadata.description: I learned that Bathilda Bagshot still lives in Godric's Hollow because Muriel said so at the wedding; that made Godric's Hollow a place I want to visit for more than just my parents' graves.
metadata.source_text: She said Bathilda Bagshot still lives in Godric’s Hollow.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I hadn't been thinking about the sword before, but Hermione's point made me consider that the sword of Gryffindor could be in Godric's Hollow, and that changes why I want to go.
metadata.source_text: Harry did not want to admit that he had not been thinking about the sword at all when he suggested they go to Godric's Hollow.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I can tell Hermione's coming back to her old self; when she starts planning properly I feel relieved and more hopeful — her practical head steadies me.
metadata.source_text: She sounded much more like her old self than she had done of late; Harry half expected her to announce that she was off to the library.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I've read that Godric's Hollow is named after Godric Gryffindor and that the village's graveyard holds names of ancient magical families; Bathilda Bagshot is connected to that place in A History of Magic.
metadata.source_text: 'Most celebrated of these half-magical dwelling places is, perhaps, Godric’s Hollow, the West Country village where the great wizard Godric Gryffindor was born... The graveyard is full of the names of ancient magical families...'
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I now think Dumbledore might have expected Harry to make the connection between Godric's Hollow and Gryffindor's sword, so I believe he could have hidden the sword where Harry would look.
metadata.source_text: But you see? Godric’s Hollow, Godric Gryffindor, Gryffindor’s sword; don’t you think Dumbledore would have expected you to make the connection?
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I'm feeling more like my old self again when we plan — helping Harry and setting out practical steps makes me calmer and more determined to support him properly.
metadata.source_text: She sounded much more like her old self than she had done of late; ... 'Yes, but we’ll have to think it through carefully, Harry.'
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I was not present for the discussion and planning in the tent, so I do not know the details of the decision to go to Godric's Hollow or the preparations they discussed.
metadata.source_text: You know, he hesitated: He did not want to say Ron’s name.
metadata.scene_title: Decision to Go to Godric's Hollow and Preparations

metadata.description: I found James and Lily Potter's grave in Godric's Hollow: their names, birth dates, death on 31 October 1981, and the epitaph 'The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.'
metadata.source_text: JAMES POTTER LILY POTTER BORN 27 MARCH 1960 DIED 31 OCTOBER 1981 BORN 30 JANUARY 1960 DIED 31 OCTOBER 1981 The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I saw a statue on the war memorial of my parents and me as a baby, all covered in snow, even though the memorial later changed back again.
metadata.source_text: As they had passed it, it had transformed. Instead of an obelisk covered in names, there was a statue of three people: a man with untidy hair and glasses, a woman with long hair and a kind, pretty face, and a baby boy sitting in his mother's arms.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I discovered that the Dumbledore family lived and partly died in Godric's Hollow when I read Kendra Dumbledore's tombstone with Ariana named beneath her and the quote about treasure and heart.
metadata.source_text: Harry stooped down and saw, upon the frozen, lichen-spotted granite, the words KENDRA DUMBLEDORE and, a short way below her dates of birth and death, AND HER DAUGHTER ARIANA. There was also a quotation: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I felt resentful that Dumbledore never mentioned our families' graves being so close; I imagined how much it would have meant to have come here with him and now wonder why he kept the connection from me.
metadata.source_text: Harry could not help thinking that he and Dumbledore both had deep roots in this graveyard, and that Dumbledore ought to have told him so, yet he had never thought to share the connection.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I realised my bond with Dumbledore lacked something important; I wished he'd shared this personal connection because visiting together would have mattered to me.
metadata.source_text: They could have visited the place together; for a moment Harry imagined coming here with Dumbledore, of what a bond that would have been, of how much it would have meant to him.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I'm sure it's Christmas Eve; I can see the church and graveyard lit up and I told Harry so as we entered the square.
metadata.source_text: Harry, I think it’s Christmas Eve! ... I’m sure it is," said Hermione, her eyes upon the church.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I recognised the Dumbledore grave: Kendra and Ariana are named there and the tomb includes the quotation 'Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.'
metadata.source_text: Harry stooped down and saw, upon the frozen, lichen-spotted granite, the words KENDRA DUMBLEDORE and, a short way below her dates of birth and death, AND HER DAUGHTER ARIANA. There was also a quotation: Where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I spotted an extremely old grave with a triangular mark and read part of the name as 'Ignotus' when I lit my wand to check the inscription.
metadata.source_text: Hermione lit her wand and pointed it at the name on the headstone. 'It says Ig — Ignotus, I think. . . .'
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: Seeing Harry's parents' gravestone made me more certain that he needed to see them; I felt he should know the truth and I tried to lead him to their grave even when he hesitated.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Hermione knew how he was feeling, because she reached for his hand and took the lead for the first time, pulling him forward.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I took the lead and held Harry's hand when he was unsure, which made me realise I'm someone he can rely on in moments when he's frightened and uncertain.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps Hermione knew how he was feeling, because she reached for his hand and took the lead for the first time, pulling him forward.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at Godric's Hollow with Harry and Hermione, so I don't know what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Godric's Hollow: Statues, Graveyard, and the Mark

metadata.description: I noticed a little eddy of dislodged snow in the bush Hermione pointed at and realised ghosts couldn't have moved it, so whatever moved the snow must be something physical.
metadata.source_text: "But then he heard a rustle and saw a little eddy of dislodged snow in the bush to which Hermione had pointed. Ghosts could not move snow."

metadata.description: I thought for a moment the graveyard might be haunted because A History of Magic said graves could be, but once I saw the snow move I stopped worrying about ghosts and started thinking about animals instead.
metadata.source_text: "Harry thought of A History of Magic; the graveyard was supposed to be haunted: what if — ? But then he heard a rustle and saw a little eddy of dislodged snow in the bush to which Hermione had pointed. Ghosts could not move snow."

metadata.description: I felt protective and practical with Hermione — I held on to her and tried to calm her fears by pointing out we looked like Muggles and later by explaining the disturbance was probably a cat or bird.
metadata.source_text: "They stood quite still, holding on to each other, gazing at the dense black boundary of the graveyard. ... 'We look like Muggles,' Harry pointed out. 'Muggles who’ve just been laying flowers on your parents’ grave! ... 'It's a cat,' said Harry, after a second or two, 'or a bird.'"

metadata.description: I saw something move by the bushes at the boundary of the graveyard and thought someone was watching us, so I freed my wand arm to be ready.
metadata.source_text: "There’s someone there. Someone watching us. I can tell. There, over by the bushes." ... "She broke from him to free her wand arm."

metadata.description: I became convinced we were being observed — I could have sworn I saw movement — and I went from uneasy to actively looking for a watcher until Harry found the snow disturbance.
metadata.source_text: "I saw something move, I could have sworn I did. . . ."

metadata.description: I relied on Harry in that moment — I grabbed his arm and trusted him while I checked the bushes, showing how close and dependent we are on each other when we're frightened.
metadata.source_text: "They stood quite still, holding on to each other, gazing at the dense black boundary of the graveyard."

metadata.description: I was not present during the events at the graveyard, so I do not know what happened there.
I noticed the pub was fuller and people were singing the carol we heard by the church, so the village was active and not completely empty.
metadata.source_text: The pub was fuller than before: Many voices inside it were now singing the carol that they had heard as they approached the church.
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I tried to seem calm for Hermione, but I wasn't as sanguine as I pretended; I'm more unsettled than I let on.
metadata.source_text: Harry, who did not feel as sanguine as he had pretended when reassuring Hermione, was glad to reach the gate and the slippery pavement.
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I relied on Hermione to make quick choices without me; when I hesitated she took charge and pulled me the other way, which made me realise she would lead when I was distracted.
metadata.source_text: For a moment Harry considered suggesting they take refuge inside it, but before he could say anything Hermione murmured, “Let’s go this way,” and pulled him down the dark street...
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I'm shivering and keep looking back, so I know I'm cold and nervous about where we are going.
metadata.source_text: How are we going to find Bathilda’s house?” asked Hermione, who was shivering a little and kept glancing back over her shoulder.
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I decided we should avoid the pub and move away from the route we came in; I changed my plan instantly and steered us along the darker street instead.
metadata.source_text: For a moment Harry considered suggesting they take refuge inside it, but before he could say anything Hermione murmured, “Let’s go this way,” and pulled him down the dark street...
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I expect Harry to respond when I ask for his opinion, tugging his arm and calling his name, but he was distracted; that made me realise sometimes I have to lead even when he should be paying attention.
metadata.source_text: “Harry? What do you think? Harry?” She tugged at his arm, but Harry was not paying attention.
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the events in the village and graveyard, so I don't know what happened during their walk toward Bathilda's house.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Leaving the Village and Spotting a Ruin

metadata.description: I can see that the Fidelius Charm protecting my parents' house has gone — the hedge has grown wild and the place is visible now.
metadata.source_text: He could see it; the Fidelius Charm must have died with James and Lily.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I used to maybe think the place might be hidden forever, but seeing the ruin and the broken top floor makes me sure the curse backfired there and the house couldn't stay whole.
metadata.source_text: that, Harry was sure, was where the curse had backfired.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I feel a deeper, more painful connection to my parents when I touch part of the house — I want to hold onto any piece of them I can, even a rusted snowy gate.
metadata.source_text: He slipped a hand from beneath the Cloak and grasped the snowy and thickly rusted gate, not wishing to open it, but simply to hold some part of the house.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I've noticed that the cottage has been left ruined and covered in ivy and snow for sixteen years since Hagrid took Harry away from the rubble.
metadata.source_text: The hedge had grown wild in the sixteen years since Hagrid had taken Harry from the rubble that lay scattered amongst the waist-high grass.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I wondered why nobody rebuilt the house, and now I think maybe you can't rebuild places damaged by powerful Dark Magic — they might be irreparable.
metadata.source_text: Maybe you can’t rebuild it?” Harry replied. “Maybe it’s like the injuries from Dark Magic and you can’t repair the damage?
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: Seeing the sign and the ruined cottage makes me quietly respectful and somber about the Potters' loss; I feel the place deserves to be treated like a memorial.
metadata.source_text: I wonder why nobody’s ever rebuilt it?” whispered Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I wasn't present during Harry and Hermione's visit to the ruined Potter house, so I don't know what they saw or felt there.
metadata.scene_title: Approaching the Ruined Potter House and the Sign

metadata.description: I'm glad people left messages for me on the sign — seeing "Good luck, Harry, wherever you are" and "Long live Harry Potter" made me beam because their support matters to me.
metadata.source_text: Good luck, Harry, wherever you are. If you read this, Harry, we’re all behind you! Long live Harry Potter.

metadata.description: I think the graffiti is brilliant; at first I might have been ambivalent, but now I'm glad they did it and it cheers me up.
metadata.source_text: It’s brilliant. I’m glad they did. I . . .

metadata.description: Hermione's upset about people writing on the sign, but I feel affectionate toward her protest — I beam at her, so I see her annoyance with indulgent fondness.
metadata.source_text: “They shouldn’t have written on the sign!” said Hermione, indignant. But Harry beamed at her.

metadata.description: I've noticed that the sign has been written on and that people have left messages and initials carved into the wood; the most recent messages are clearly aimed at Harry.
metadata.source_text: Some had merely signed their names in Everlasting Ink; others had carved their initials into the wood, still others had left messages. The most recent of these, shining brightly over sixteen years’ worth of magical graffiti, all said similar things.

metadata.description: I feel indignant about people writing on the sign; I think they shouldn't have written on it and my opinion is that defacing the sign was wrong.
metadata.source_text: “They shouldn’t have written on the sign!” said Hermione, indignant.

metadata.description: Harry reacted differently to the graffiti than I did — while I disapprove, I recognize that he beams and is pleased by the messages, which changes how I see his emotional response to public support.
metadata.source_text: But Harry beamed at her. “It’s brilliant. I’m glad they did. I . . .”

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events on the lane by the sign, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
I realised the woman couldn't be a Muggle because she was staring straight at a house that Muggles shouldn't be able to see.
metadata.source_text: There was next to no chance that this woman was a Muggle: She was standing there gazing at a house that ought to have been completely invisible to her, if she was not a witch.

metadata.description: I felt oddly certain that she knew we were there and who we were, even though by normal magic she shouldn't even be able to see us.
metadata.source_text: By all the rules of normal magic, meanwhile, she ought not to be able to see Hermione and him at all. Nevertheless, Harry had the strangest feeling that she knew that they were there, and also who they were.

metadata.description: Seeing her behaviour — coming out in the freezing cold to look at an old ruin — made me regard her as someone connected to the house in a way that warrants suspicion and attention.
metadata.source_text: Even assuming that she was a witch, however, it was odd behavior to come out on a night this cold, simply to look at an old ruin.

metadata.description: I've noticed the woman's slow, stooped, shuffling walk and that she gives the impression of extreme age as she moves nearer along the snowy road.
metadata.source_text: She was moving slowly, possibly frightened of slipping on the snowy ground. Her stoop, her stoutness, her shuffling gait all gave an impression of extreme age.

metadata.description: I find it strange and worrying that a witch would come out on such a bitter night just to look at a ruined house; that changes how I think about her intentions.
metadata.source_text: Even assuming that she was a witch, however, it was odd behavior to come out on a night this cold, simply to look at an old ruin.

metadata.description: When the woman stopped and faced us it made me implicitly trust Harry's instincts that she might be aware of us, so I reacted (pinching his arm) to confirm our shared presence and concern.
metadata.source_text: He did not need Hermione’s pinch to his arm.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events by the ruined house, so I don't know what happened firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I've learned that a muffled woman in the street is beckoning us and even nodded when I asked if she was Bathilda, so she must be the person trying to summon us.
metadata.source_text: “Are you Bathilda?” The muffled figure nodded and beckoned again.

metadata.description: I'm starting to believe she may have been waiting for us all these months and might have been following us from the graveyard; the idea keeps getting stronger as we stand there.
metadata.source_text: Was it possible that she had been waiting for them all these long months? That Dumbledore had told her to wait, and that Harry would come in the end? Was it not likely that it was she who had moved in the shadows in the graveyard and had followed them to this spot?

metadata.description: I now see this woman as someone connected to Dumbledore or possessing a Dumbledore-like power; her ability to sense us makes me think she's not an ordinary stranger.
metadata.source_text: Even her ability to sense them suggested some Dumbledore-ish power that he had never encountered before.

metadata.description: I've noticed the woman beckoning with a gloved hand and that she nodded when Harry asked if she was Bathilda, so I now know the beckoning woman is identified as Bathilda.
metadata.source_text: “Are you Bathilda?” The muffled figure nodded and beckoned again.

metadata.description: I'm feeling more convinced that this woman could have been waiting or watching for us for months; the persistent beckoning makes me rethink how long she's known about our coming.
metadata.source_text: Was it possible that she had been waiting for them all these long months? That Dumbledore had told her to wait, and that Harry would come in the end?

metadata.description: I now regard the woman as someone possibly connected to powerful people like Dumbledore, because her sensing us seems beyond the usual — it changes how I view her intentions.
metadata.source_text: Even her ability to sense them suggested some Dumbledore-ish power that he had never encountered before.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the meeting on the deserted street with the muffled woman, so I don't know firsthand what happened there.
I learned that the snake — Nagini — can coil round me and press the Horcrux right against my chest, making my whole head fill with a cold, white light and nearly stopping me from thinking.
metadata.source_text: But nothing happened and he needed his hands to try to force the snake from him as it coiled itself around his torso, squeezing the air from him, pressing the Horcrux hard into his chest, a circle of ice that throbbed with life, inches from his own frantic heart, and his brain was flooding with cold, white light, all thought obliterated
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I believed I could resist until I felt the Horcrux drowning my thought and learned just how dangerous and overpowering its influence really is — it nearly took me completely under.
metadata.source_text: and his brain was flooding with cold, white light, all thought obliterated, his own breath drowned, distant footsteps, everything going. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I've come to see Nagini not just as Voldemort's creature but as a direct, personal threat to me — it attacks and inflicts the Horcrux's pain on me in a way that makes our fight horribly intimate.
metadata.source_text: Nagini had released him. He scrambled up and saw the snake outlined against the landing light: It struck,
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I realised that a deflected curse can still have dangerous consequences — my spell glanced off and smashed the curtained window, proving how chaotic fighting in close quarters can be.
metadata.source_text: Hermione dived aside with a shriek; her deflected curse hit the curtained window, which shattered.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I used to think quick spells would always help straight away in danger, but I felt panic and learned that in tight spaces and surprise attacks even careful magic can go wrong or miss its mark.
metadata.source_text: Hermione dived aside with a shriek; her deflected curse hit the curtained window, which shattered.
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I feel even more protective of Harry now — seeing him strangled by the snake and then jolting awake made me realise how vulnerable he is and how urgent our need to stop whatever's hurting him.
metadata.source_text: He scrambled up and saw the snake outlined against the landing light: It struck, and Hermione dived aside with a shriek;
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I was not present during these events, so I do not know the finer details of the house encounter or the struggle with the snake.
metadata.source_text: Characters present: Present: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger | Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Aftermath in the Tent — Injury and Confession

metadata.description: I felt my scar sear with a pain stronger than it has been in years — it told me something terrible was coming and made me cry out that he was coming.
metadata.source_text: but as he did so, his scar seared more painfully, more powerfully than it had done in years. “He’s coming! Hermione, he’s coming!”
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: I realized in a flash that I was Harry, not Voldemort — that what I was experiencing could be a vision or memory and not my own becoming him, and that changed my fear into desperate confusion.
metadata.source_text: He was Harry. . . . Harry, not Voldemort . . . and the thing that was rustling was not a snake. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: I grabbed Hermione without thinking and pulled her to safety — I know I will do anything to protect her, even when everything is falling apart and my scar is screaming.
metadata.source_text: and splintered china flew everywhere as Harry jumped over the bed and seized the dark shape he knew to be Hermione — She shrieked with pain as he pulled her back across the bed
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: I cast Confringo at the snake in a desperate bid to save us, and my spell shattered the wardrobe mirror and ricocheted around the room, showing how powerful and volatile my magic can be under stress.
metadata.source_text: as it struck, Hermione screamed, “Confringo!” and her spell flew around the room, exploding the wardrobe mirror and ricocheting back at them
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: After the blast and the chaos, I knew that quick, forceful spells can have dangerous, unpredictable side effects in tight spaces — I felt shaken and more cautious about casting without thinking first.
metadata.source_text: and her spell flew around the room, exploding the wardrobe mirror and ricocheting back at them, bouncing from floor to ceiling;
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: I whispered to Harry to wake up and check on him — I care for him deeply and my instinct is to be the calm voice trying to bring him back when he’s lost between vision and reality.
metadata.source_text: “Harry,” Hermione whispered. “Do you feel all — all right?”
metadata.scene_title: Horcrux Burn and Discussion of Events

metadata.description: I was not present during the events in the bedroom and have no direct knowledge of what happened during the snake attack or the vision.
metadata.source_text: I was not present during the events in the bedroom, so I don't know what happened.

metadata.source_text: We got away." "Yes," said Hermione. "I had to use a Hover Charm to get you into your bunk, I couldn’t lift you. You’ve been . . . Well, you haven’t been quite . . ."

metadata.description: I learned that the Horcrux had been stuck to my chest and Hermione had to use a Severing Charm to get it off me.
metadata.source_text: I couldn’t get the Horcrux off you," Hermione said, and he knew she wanted to change the subject. "It was stuck, stuck to your chest... I’m sorry, I had to use a Severing Charm to get it away.

metadata.description: I learned I was very ill: I was drenched in sweat and had been shouting and moaning rather than simply unconscious.
metadata.source_text: He was drenched in sweat; he could feel it on the sheets and blankets.... "You’ve been ill," she finished. "Quite ill." "And I’ve been . . . what, unconscious?" "Not exactly," said Hermione uncomfortably. "You’ve been shouting and moaning and . . . things," she added

metadata.description: I wasn’t just knocked out or asleep; I changed my mind about being merely unconscious — I realize now I was acting out, shouting and moaning while ill.
metadata.source_text: "And I’ve been . . . what, unconscious?" "Not exactly," said Hermione uncomfortably. "You’ve been shouting and moaning and . . . things," she added

metadata.source_text: "Not exactly," said Hermione uncomfortably. "You’ve been shouting and moaning and . . . things," she added

metadata.description: I feel a stronger duty toward Harry; I’m tired and worried but I’ve looked after him, cleaned his snake bite, applied dittany and done what I had to so he could survive.

metadata.description: I've got a scarlet oval burned over my heart where the Horcrux locket burned me, and there are half-healed puncture marks on my forearm — the Horcrux really hurt me.
metadata.source_text: There was a scarlet oval over his heart where the locket had burned him. He could also see the half-healed puncture marks to his forearm.

metadata.description: I feel it's my fault we went to Godric's Hollow; I keep thinking it's all my fault and I keep apologising to Hermione because I blame myself for how things went wrong.
metadata.source_text: We shouldn’t have gone to Godric’s Hollow. It’s my fault, it’s all my fault, Hermione, I’m sorry.

metadata.description: I can tell Hermione cares enough to stay and argue with me; even when I'm blaming myself she defends me and shares responsibility, which makes me feel less alone with the guilt.
metadata.source_text: It’s not your fault. I wanted to go too; I really thought Dumbledore might have left the sword there for you.

metadata.description: I've learned that the Horcrux is in Harry's bag and we should keep it off for a while to avoid it harming him again.
metadata.source_text: Where’ve you put the Horcrux? "In my bag. I think we should keep it off for a while."

metadata.description: I still believe going to Godric's Hollow might help find the sword, because I really thought Dumbledore might have left it there, even though that belief turned out to be wrong.
metadata.source_text: I wanted to go too; I really thought Dumbledore might have left the sword there for you.

metadata.description: I feel protective of Harry and refuse to blame him alone; I'm ready to share responsibility and press him for details because I care about what happened to him.
