metadata.source_text: You were right. He knew I’d go back." "The snake was inside her?" He opened his eyes again: Hermione looked revolted, nauseated.
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Repairs the Wand — It Breaks Again

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in Bathilda Bagshot's house, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Hermione Repairs the Wand — It Breaks Again

metadata.description: Where’s my wand? I found out my holly and phoenix feather wand was nearly severed in two, the wood splintered and only one fragile strand of feather keeping it together.
metadata.source_text: "Where’s my wand, Hermione?" ... The holly and phoenix wand was nearly severed in two. One fragile strand of phoenix feather kept both pieces hanging together. The wood had splintered apart completely.
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: I felt utterly panicked and couldn't think properly — my fear made everything a blur and I needed Hermione to fix the wand immediately.
metadata.source_text: He could not think properly: Everything was a blur of panic and fear. Then he held out the wand to Hermione. "Mend it. Please."
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: Hermione is the one I trust to try and fix my wand; I begged her to try because I rely on her skill and calm even when I’m terrified.
metadata.source_text: "Mend it. Please." ... "Please, Hermione, try!"
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: I saw that Harry’s holly and phoenix feather wand was almost completely broken with only a single strand of feather holding the pieces together.
metadata.source_text: The holly and phoenix wand was nearly severed in two. One fragile strand of phoenix feather kept both pieces hanging together. The wood had splintered apart completely.
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: I didn't think Reparo would work on a wand broken like that, but under pressure I tried the charm anyway and the wand did reseal, if only weakly.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, I don’t think, when it’s broken like this —" ... "R-Reparo." The dangling half of the wand resealed itself.
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: When Harry begged me, I felt the gravity of his panic and knew he needed me; my willingness to attempt the repair shows he relies on me in crises.
metadata.source_text: "Mend it. Please." ... "R-Reparo."
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in which Harry's wand was broken and repaired, so I don't know the details of what happened.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Ron Weasley
metadata.scene_title: Guilt, Repair Attempts, and Plans for a Replacement

metadata.description: I learned that my wand split into two again when I tried to cast Expelliarmus at Hermione; the wand couldn't take the strain and broke right there.
metadata.source_text: The feeble attempt at magic was too much for Harry’s wand, which split into two again.
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I felt empty and stunned and started to think that finding a replacement wand might be impossible, because Ollivander was taken and Gregorovitch is dead.
metadata.source_text: He felt empty, stunned. "We’ll — we’ll find a way to repair it." "Harry, I don’t think we’re going to be able to," said Hermione... Harry thought of Ollivander, kidnapped and held hostage by Voldemort; of Gregorovitch, who was dead.
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I told Hermione I would borrow her wand for the time being while I kept watch, which shows I trust her enough to use her wand and accept her help despite what happened.
metadata.source_text: "Well," he said, in a falsely matter-of-fact voice, "well, I’ll just borrow yours for now, then. While I keep watch."
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I realised my Blasting Curse rebounded when the snake came and that the rebound must have hit Harry’s wand, so I think I caused his wand to split.
metadata.source_text: "I’m so, so sorry. I think it was me. As we were leaving, you know, the snake was coming for us, and so I cast a Blasting Curse, and it rebounded everywhere, and it must have — must have hit —"
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I don't think Harry's wand can be repaired now; remembering Ron's broken wand after the car crash makes me believe some wand damage can't be fixed and needs replacement.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, I don’t think we’re going to be able to," said Hermione, the tears trickling down her face. "Remember . . . remember Ron? When he broke his wand, crashing the car? It was never the same again, he had to get a new one."
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I apologised to Harry very quietly and felt responsible; I worry I've hurt him, which changes how I feel about what happened between us in that moment.
metadata.source_text: "Harry," Hermione whispered so quietly he could hardly hear her. "I’m so, so sorry. I think it was me."
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the Forbidden Forest, so I don't know what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Agreement to Share Wands While Keeping Watch

metadata.description: I've found a photograph of a young Albus with a man called Grindelwald and learned that Grindelwald was Dumbledore's friend.
metadata.source_text: Albus Dumbledore, shortly after his mother’s death, with his friend Gellert Grindelwald.

metadata.description: I'm furious with Dumbledore; I feel he left us to groping in the darkness with no map or plan and that's changed how I think about him.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore had left them to grope in the darkness, to wrestle with unknown and undreamed-of terrors, alone and unaided: Nothing was explained, nothing was given freely, they had no sword, and now, Harry, had no wand.

metadata.description: I reckon Dumbledore wasn't the protector I thought; knowing about Grindelwald and Dumbledore's secret history makes me see Albus as more complicated and less trustworthy.
metadata.source_text: Albus Dumbledore, shortly after his mother’s death, with his friend Gellert Grindelwald.

metadata.description: I found a pristine copy of The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore in Bathilda's sitting room with a note from Rita Skeeter tucked inside which explains how the book arrived.
metadata.source_text: It was in Bathilda’s sitting room, just lying there. . . . This note was sticking out of the top of it.

metadata.description: I'm shaken and upset; seeing Harry so angry made me think he blamed me more than he said, though he told me he knew the wand break was an accident.
metadata.source_text: “You’re still really angry at me, aren’t you?” said Hermione; he looked up to see fresh tears leaking out of her eyes, and knew that his anger must have shown in his face.

metadata.description: Having shown Harry the book, I feel closer to him in our shared search for answers, even if I'm frightened by his fury and worried about what we learn.
metadata.source_text: Timidly she pushed it onto his lap, a pristine copy of The Life and Lies of Albus Dumbledore.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for these events and so I don't know the details firsthand.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present at Godric's Hollow during these happenings and have no direct witness account.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't there for the events Bathilda describes, so I can't attest to what I didn't see.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I read that Dumbledore and Gellert Grindelwald were close when they were young and that Grindelwald used the slogan 'For the Greater Good' which Dumbledore may have influenced.
metadata.source_text: Was it lingering affection for the man or fear of exposure as his once best friend that caused Dumbledore to hesitate? ... Is it possible that Ariana Dumbledore was the first person to die “for the greater good”?

metadata.description: I'm shattered — I used to think Dumbledore was the embodiment of goodness and wisdom, but this has made me lose that certainty; I feel betrayed and disillusioned by him.
metadata.source_text: He had trusted Dumbledore, believed him the embodiment of goodness and wisdom. All was ashes: How much more could he lose?

metadata.description: I don't feel Dumbledore loved me; he shared far more with Grindelwald than with me, and that makes me question how much he trusted or cared for me.
metadata.source_text: I don't know who he loved, Hermione, but it was never me. ... He shared a damn sight more of what he was really thinking with Gellert Grindelwald than he ever shared with me.

metadata.description: I've read Rita Skeeter's account suggesting that 'For the Greater Good' became Grindelwald's slogan and that it was carved over the entrance to Nurmengard, Grindelwald's prison.
metadata.source_text: I think that’s the worst bit. ... 'For the Greater Good' became Grindelwald’s slogan, his justification for all the atrocities he committed later. And . . . from that . . . it looks like Dumbledore gave him the idea. They say ‘For the Greater Good’ was even carved over the entrance to Nurmengard.

metadata.description: I still believe Dumbledore changed later in life and devoted himself to fighting the Dark Arts, so although the young Dumbledore must have been wrong, my view of his lifetime actions remains positive.
metadata.source_text: He changed, Harry, he changed! ... the whole of the rest of his life was devoted to fighting the Dark Arts! Dumbledore was the one who stopped Grindelwald, the one who always voted for Muggle protection and Muggle-born rights, who fought You-Know-Who from the start...

metadata.description: I think Dumbledore did love Harry; despite revelations about Dumbledore's past, I still see him as someone who cared for Harry and worked for the right causes later on.
metadata.source_text: He loved you," Hermione whispered. "I know he loved you.

metadata.description: I wasn't present for the discussion about Dumbledore and Grindelwald on the snowy hilltop, so I don't know what was said during that exchange.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I found out the silver doe Patronus wasn't Ron's — my Patronus is a stag, so whatever produced that doe couldn't have been him.
metadata.source_text: "My Patronus is a stag."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: I couldn't believe Ron had actually come back and saved me; I was stunned and felt a rush of relief and disbelief when he stood there alive and soaked.
metadata.source_text: "The silver doe was nothing, nothing compared with Ron’s reappearance; he could not believe it."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: Seeing Ron dive in and save me made me feel that maybe he's truly returned to our side — his action matters more than his leaving did in that moment.
metadata.source_text: "He had returned. He had just saved Harry’s life."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: I got the Horcrux out of the pool and I have the Sword of Gryffindor now, which I hauled up and am holding for inspection.
metadata.source_text: "Oh yeah, I got it out," he said, rather unnecessarily, holding up the sword for Harry’s inspection.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: I've come back because I want to be wanted — I kept thinking I should return and hoped they'd still want me after I'd left.
metadata.source_text: "I’ve — you know — I’ve come back. If —" He cleared his throat. "You know. You still want me."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: By diving in and saving Harry and bringing the Horcrux, I feel I've repaired things between us a bit; doing that shows I'm back with him properly.
metadata.source_text: "He had returned. He had just saved Harry’s life."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the lake, so I don't know what happened there firsthand.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns and Rescue at the Lake

metadata.description: I found an ornate silver sword with a rubied hilt in the pool, and I know whoever cast the Patronus must have put the sword there.
metadata.source_text: So how did the sword get in that pool? "Whoever cast the Patronus must have put it there."
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I realise that the locket Horcrux reacts violently to the sword's presence and that its creature inside prefers to try to kill me rather than be possessed, so the sword clearly threatens it.
metadata.source_text: The locket was twitching slightly. Harry knew that the thing inside it was agitated again. It had sensed the presence of the sword and had tried to kill Harry rather than let him possess it.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I feel we have to act together right now — Ron's holding the Horcrux and I'm convinced we must destroy the locket immediately, so my trust in Ron's role in this moment is firm.
metadata.source_text: The Horcrux was still swinging from Ron’s hand. The locket was twitching slightly... Now was not the time for long discussions; now was the moment to destroy the locket once and for all.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I saw a deer and followed it, and I nearly had to kip under a tree until the deer turned up, so I know the deer led me toward Harry by the pool.
metadata.source_text: And I was just thinking I’d have to kip under a tree and wait for morning when I saw that deer coming and you following.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I thought I might have seen something moving near two trees, but I was running straight to the pool because Harry had gone under and hadn't come up, so I'm less sure about other sightings now.
metadata.source_text: I did think I saw something move over there, but I was running to the pool at the time, because you’d gone in and you hadn’t come up, so I wasn’t going to make a detour to —
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I reckon the sword could be real and I'm willing to trust Harry's judgement about testing it now, so I'm ready to hold the Horcrux and go along with him.
metadata.source_text: "You reckon this is the real one?" asked Ron. "One way to find out, isn’t there?" said Harry. The Horcrux was still swinging from Ron’s hand.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the pool, so I don't know exactly what happened or who did what there.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Discovered and Decision to Destroy It

metadata.description: I found the Horcrux on a flat rock under a sycamore and I can open it if I have Hermione's wand; I know where it is and how to approach it.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked around, holding Hermione’s wand high, and saw the place: a flattish rock lying in the shadow of a sycamore tree.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I believe the person who recovers a magical object is supposed to be the one to use a related tool — because Ron got the sword out of the pool, I now think it's meant to be him who wields it.
metadata.source_text: Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I trust Ron with this awful job; I'm putting the responsibility on him even though it hurts, because I know he has to do it and I accept he must be the one to stab the Horcrux.
metadata.source_text: No, you should do it." "Me?" said Ron, looking shocked. "Why?" "Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I offered the sword up to Harry when he asked for it, so I know I still have the sword and can hand it over if needed.
metadata.source_text: When Ron offered the sword, however, Harry shook his head.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I'm suddenly realising I might be expected to do something terrible with the sword because I retrieved it from the pool; I didn't want to be the one, but Harry thinks I should.
metadata.source_text: "Because you got the sword out of the pool. I think it’s supposed to be you."
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I'm shocked and a bit shaken that Harry is putting this on me, so my view of what he expects from me has changed — he wants me to act when it's dangerous.
metadata.source_text: "Me?" said Ron, looking shocked. "Why?"
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events at the sycamore and flat rock, so I don't know exactly what happened there.
metadata.scene_title: Preparing to Open the Locket — Ron Hesitates

metadata.description: I can open that locket by speaking Parseltongue; the words come straight to my mouth as if I've always known them.
metadata.source_text: “I’m going to ask it to open, using Parseltongue,” said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: Maybe my recent encounter with Nagini made me realise I could speak Parseltongue naturally — it feels like something buried in me came to the surface.
metadata.source_text: Perhaps it had taken his recent encounter with Nagini to make him realize it.
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: I trust Ron enough in this moment to push him to act with the sword; his name being spoken seems to spur him into trying despite how frightened he is.
metadata.source_text: “You can do it,” said Harry, “you can! You’ve just got the sword, I know it’s supposed to be you who uses it. Please, just get rid of it, Ron.”
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: That locket messes with my head worse than it did with Harry and Hermione; when I wear it I start thinking awful stuff and I can't stop putting it back on.
metadata.source_text: “Because that thing’s bad for me!” said Ron, backing away from the locket on the rock. “I can’t handle it! ... it made me think stuff — stuff I was thinking anyway, but it made everything worse, I can’t explain it, and then I’d take it off and I’d get my head on straight again, and then I’d have to put the effing thing back on — I can’t do it, Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: I used to make excuses for how I was acting, but I realise this locket genuinely harms me; it's not just my fault, it magnifies my worst thoughts and I can't deal with that alone.
metadata.source_text: “I’m not making excuses, Harry, for what I was like, but it affects me worse than it affected you and Hermione, it made me think stuff — ... I can’t do it, Harry!”
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: Even though I'm terrified, I'm willing to try again for Harry when he asks; hearing my name helps me pull myself together enough to move back and listen to him.
metadata.source_text: The sound of his name seemed to act like a stimulant. Ron swallowed, then, still breathing hard through his long nose, moved back toward the rock.
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know exactly what happened between Harry and Ron at the locket.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was not present in the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Parseltongue, Locket’s Voice, and Ron’s Inner Torment

metadata.description: I learned that the locket Horcrux can speak with Riddle’s voice and show grotesque, living projections of people to torment whoever holds it.
metadata.source_text: Then a voice hissed from out of the Horcrux. "I have seen your heart, and it is mine."
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I believed we had to force Ron to act, and shouting at him felt necessary — I changed to seeing how much the Horcrux could wound him even as it had to be destroyed.
metadata.source_text: "Don’t listen to it!" Harry said harshly. "Stab it!"
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I saw Ron suffer for us and then act — I feel closer and more grateful to him now, knowing he could break and yet still destroy the Horcrux for our sake.
metadata.source_text: "Ron, stab it now!" Harry bellowed: He could feel the locket quivering in his grip and was scared of what was coming.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I found out the locket can make people see and hear horrible things about themselves — it used words about my mum and about being second best to hurt me.
metadata.source_text: "I have seen your dreams, Ronald Weasley, and I have seen your fears. All you desire is possible, but all that you dread is also possible. . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I thought I might be able to stand up calmly, but the Horcrux proved I could be reduced to a shaking wreck by being reminded I was "least loved" and "second best"; after that, everything felt different.
metadata.source_text: "Least loved, always, by the mother who craved a daughter . . . Least loved, now, by the girl who prefers your friend . . . Second best, always, eternally overshadowed . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I realised, to my shame, how much I cared about what people thought of me and how cruel words could twist me — but I also proved I cared about Harry and could destroy the Horcrux, even when it tore me up.
metadata.source_text: "Your mother confessed," sneered Riddle-Harry, while Riddle-Hermione jeered, "that she would have preferred me as a son, would be glad to exchange . . ."
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I was not present during the destruction of the locket Horcrux, so I did not see or hear what happened between Harry and Ron at that moment.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger is absent from the scene.
metadata.scene_title: Locket Shatters — Ron’s Redemption and Breakdown

metadata.description: I've learned that Ron has returned to the tent carrying the sword and he's wet, because I saw him standing there dripping onto the carpet.
metadata.source_text: She saw Ron, who stood there holding the sword and dripping onto the threadbare carpet.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I reckon everything's more than fine now that Ron's here; I felt relieved enough to say I'm great and that someone was here, even though things were tense.
metadata.source_text: It’s okay, everything’s fine. More than fine. I’m great. There’s someone here.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I feel protective toward Hermione — when she lunged at Ron and started hitting him, I stepped in and used Protego because I needed to stop her hurting him.
metadata.source_text: Protego!
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I realized Ron had come back into the tent because I saw him standing right in front of me holding the sword and looking pale.
metadata.source_text: She saw Ron, who stood there holding the sword and dripping onto the threadbare carpet.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I am furious and I will not calm down after he crawled back here after weeks and weeks away — I'm changed from sleepy to full-on angry, shouting that I will not calm down.
metadata.source_text: You — crawl — back — here — after — weeks — and — weeks — oh, where’s my wand?" ... "I will not calm down!" she screamed.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I think Ron is a complete arse for returning the way he did; I've gone from concerned friend to attacking him physically and calling him names.
metadata.source_text: You — complete — arse — Ronald — Weasley!
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I know I arrived back at the tent and I had the sword with me; I was standing there dripping and hoping Hermione would be pleased or forgiving.
metadata.source_text: She saw Ron, who stood there holding the sword and dripping onto the threadbare carpet.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I felt hopeful that Hermione might react well when I came back — I gave a weak, hopeful smile and half raised my arms, showing I'm sorry or glad to be back.
metadata.source_text: Ron gave a weak, hopeful smile and half raised his arms.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I realise Hermione is furious with me; she punched me and called me names, so our relationship is tense and I must have upset her greatly by leaving.
metadata.source_text: Hermione launched herself forward and started punching every inch of him that she could reach.
metadata.scene_title: Ron Returns to the Tent — Hermione’s Fury

metadata.description: I know Ron found us because his Deluminator somehow played Hermione's voice, produced a ball of light that entered him, and then guided him so he could Apparate to where we were.
metadata.source_text: "This." ... "The Deluminator?" ... "I heard you coming out of my pocket. Your voice," he held up the Deluminator again, "came out of this."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I believe Ron truly saved my life; despite the argument, I know he risked himself and returned to help me, and that matters more than Hermione's anger at the moment.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione," said Harry quietly, "Ron just saved my life."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I'm conflicted but protective: I still depend on Ron and feel loyalty toward him, even when Hermione lashes out; I can see both sides and I defend Ron when necessary.
metadata.source_text: "Hermione," interjected Harry, who considered this a low blow, "he just saved my —"
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I've learned that Ron used a Deluminator which played my voice from his pocket and produced a guiding light that entered him and let him Apparate to the correct location.
metadata.source_text: "The Deluminator?" ... "I heard you coming out of my pocket. Your voice," he held up the Deluminator again, "came out of this."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more distrustful of Ron now because he left us for weeks; hearing his explanation doesn't immediately excuse the fear and danger his absence caused me.
metadata.source_text: "Don’t you tell me what to do, Harry Potter!" ... "You come back after weeks — weeks — and you think it’s all going to be all right if you just say sorry?"
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I view Ron as reckless and unreliable at the moment; even though he says he tried to return, my trust is damaged because we might easily have been killed while he was gone.
metadata.source_text: "I don’t care what he’s done! Weeks and weeks, we could have been dead for all he knew —"
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I know the Deluminator can produce light and voices and, bizarrely, that when a ball of light went into me I suddenly knew where I had to go and could Apparate there.
metadata.source_text: "It doesn’t just turn the lights on and off," said Ron. ... "The little ball of light was hovering there... and then it . . . well, it went inside me."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I believed I couldn't return to them because of the Snatchers and being on my own, but after the Deluminator's light guided me I trusted I'd be able to come back and help Harry.
metadata.source_text: "I wanted to come back the minute I’d Disapparated, but I walked straight into a gang of Snatchers... and I came out miles from where you were."
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I feel guilty and desperate to be forgiven; I thought they'd understand I was doing all I could, and I still want them to know I risked myself to come back for Harry.
metadata.source_text: "I came running after you! I called you! I begged you to come back!" ... "I didn’t do it so well, Splinched myself again"
metadata.scene_title: Ron Explains Where He Went — His Deluminator Story

metadata.description: I learned that we spent two nights at that place and that I kept thinking I could hear someone moving around in the dark and calling out.
metadata.source_text: We were there," said Harry. "We spent two nights there, and the second night I kept thinking I could hear someone moving around in the dark and calling out!
metadata.scene_title: How Ron Found Them and Details of the Rescue

metadata.description: I was convinced someone was nearby during the night because I kept hearing noises and calls; I stopped assuming we were alone and became more on edge.
metadata.source_text: We were there," said Harry. "We spent two nights there, and the second night I kept thinking I could hear someone moving around in the dark and calling out!
metadata.scene_title: How Ron Found Them and Details of the Rescue

metadata.description: I trust Ron to try and look out for us — he stayed on that hill all day hoping we'd appear and eventually used the Deluminator to find us.
metadata.source_text: Well, I stayed on that hill all day," said Ron. "I kept hoping you'd appear. ... and I Disapparated and arrived here in these woods. ... and Harry did.
metadata.scene_title: How Ron Found Them and Details of the Rescue

metadata.scene_title: Xenophilius Explains the Deathly Hallows and the Tale

metadata.description: I realised Xenophilius thinks people who attack folks for wearing a Dark mark are ignorant, and he uses that as an example aimed at me from the wedding incident.

metadata.scene_title: Xenophilius Explains the Deathly Hallows and the Tale

metadata.description: I feel a bit defensive about being called knuckleheaded, but I also sense Xenophilius believes in the Hallows enough to justify why someone might use a controversial symbol.
metadata.source_text: “There is nothing Dark about the Hallows — at least, not in that crude sense. One simply uses the symbol to reveal oneself to other believers, in the hope that they might help one with the Quest.”
metadata.scene_title: Xenophilius Explains the Deathly Hallows and the Tale

metadata.description: I noticed Xenophilius singled me out from the group for the wedding scuffle; that made me realise strangers might judge me on moments I don't like remembered.

metadata.scene_title: Xenophilius Explains the Deathly Hallows and the Tale

metadata.scene_title: Death Rewards the Brothers with Three Hallows

metadata.description: I wasn't there when Death gave the wand and the stone to the first two brothers, so I didn't witness how the youngest brother was asked what he wanted.

metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: I felt startled by the notion that Death could possess an Invisibility Cloak, which made me rethink how literal or symbolic the tale's objects might be.
metadata.source_text: “Death’s got an Invisibility Cloak?” Harry interrupted again.
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: Because I interrupted the story to ask about Death's cloak, I recognised that I participate actively in the telling and questioning of these sorts of tales with my friends.
metadata.source_text: “Death’s got an Invisibility Cloak?” Harry interrupted again.
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.source_text: Hermione closed the book.
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: By closing the book, I accepted the tale's lesson about humility and the inevitability of Death more thoughtfully than before; the neat moral prompted me to reflect rather than argue.
metadata.source_text: Hermione closed the book.
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: My action of closing the book shows I take responsibility for guiding the reading and discussion, which subtly reinforces my role among my friends as the one attending to details.
metadata.source_text: Hermione closed the book.
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: I said that Death could sneak up on people with an Invisibility Cloak, which shows I learned or imagined that such a cloak would make Death stealthy and more like a prankster than a solemn figure.

metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: I made a joke about Death flapping and shrieking then apologised to Hermione, which shows my mood shifted from joking to mildly embarrassed about being crude.

metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: By apologising to Hermione after my silly comment, I demonstrated that I care about how my teasing affects my friends and that I’ll pull back when someone might be offended.
metadata.source_text: “Sometimes he gets bored of running at them, flapping his arms and shrieking . . . sorry, Hermione.”
metadata.scene_title: The Youngest Brother Receives the Invisibility Cloak and the Tale’s End

metadata.description: I've just learned that the three symbols Xenophilius drew represent the Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone and the Cloak of Invisibility — collectively called the Deathly Hallows.

metadata.description: I'm starting to accept that the Elder Wand might be real because Xenophilius says there's endless historical evidence and a bloody trail of owners, which makes me uneasy about writing it off.
metadata.source_text: "Oh, well, in that case there is endless evidence," said Xenophilius. "The Elder Wand is the Hallow that is most easily traced, because of the way in which it passes from hand to hand."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I notice Xenophilius is oddly smug and certain about these matters; I think of him as eccentric but also oddly convincing when he talks history, which changes how I regard his reliability.

metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I've learned that Xenophilius identifies the three parts of the fable as specific magical objects: the Elder Wand, the Resurrection Stone and the Cloak of Invisibility, and he draws the familiar symbol.

metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I'm becoming more skeptical of wild claims that rely on absence of disproof; I feel indignant when Xenophilius tells me to 'prove it is not' — that's not a reasonable standard for truth.
metadata.source_text: "Prove that it is not," said Xenophilius...Hermione looked outraged. "But that's — I'm sorry, but that's completely ridiculous! How can I possibly prove it doesn't exist?"
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I think Xenophilius is narrow-minded in his own eccentric way; I judge him as someone who mistakes certainty for knowledge, and his smug manner makes me distrust his conclusions.
metadata.source_text: "Luna has told me all about you, young lady," said Xenophilius. "You are, I gather, not unintelligent, but painfully limited. Narrow. Close-minded."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I've learned from Xenophilius that if the Hallows are united the possessor would be 'master of Death' — he calls it conquering or vanquishing Death — and he seems to mean that literally.
metadata.source_text: "Those of us who understand these matters...recognize that the ancient story refers to three objects, or Hallows, which, if united, will make the possessor master of Death.""Master," said Xenophilius, waving an airy hand. "Conqueror. Vanquisher."
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I'm less able to keep straight-faced when Xenophilius starts on these theories — I find them bonkers but also oddly compelling when he talks about a wand's bloody history; it makes me uneasy.
metadata.source_text: Hermione, Harry, and Ron glanced at one another..."Exactly," said Xenophilius, as if he had defeated them all in reasoned argument.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I think Xenophilius is ridiculous but harmlessly smug; his weird certainty and the hat make me want to laugh, and I find myself nodding along even if I don't believe him.
metadata.source_text: "Perhaps you ought to try on the hat, Hermione," said Ron, nodding toward the ludicrous headdress. His voice shook with the strain of not laughing.
metadata.scene_title: Discussion of the Hallows, the Peverells, and the Elder Wand’s History

metadata.description: I learned that people think the Elder Wand’s trail is confused — names like Arcus, Livius, and Loxias come up, and nobody can say for certain who ended up with the wand.
metadata.source_text: Who knows where the Elder Wand lies hidden? The trail goes cold with Arcus and Livius. Who can say which of them really defeated Loxias, and which took the wand?
metadata.scene_title: Arguments about the Peverells and a Sudden Intrusion

metadata.description: I realise history might not give clear answers about magical artefacts; what we think we know can be muddled and unreliable.
metadata.source_text: History, alas, does not tell us.

metadata.scene_title: Arguments about the Peverells and a Sudden Intrusion

metadata.description: I am more convinced now that the Peverell family are central to the Hallows story; what began as a question is turning into a plausible historical link.

metadata.scene_title: Arguments about the Peverells and a Sudden Intrusion

metadata.scene_title: Arguments about the Peverells and a Sudden Intrusion

metadata.source_text: IT’S IN HERE! He left me the ring — it’s in the Snitch!
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I became convinced the Deathly Hallows are real and that I possess at least one, possibly two, and that if I gained the Elder Wand I could be master of Death.
metadata.source_text: This explains everything. The Deathly Hallows are real, and I’ve got one — maybe two —
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I began to believe that Voldemort is after the Elder Wand — not a new wand, but an ancient wand — even if Voldemort may not know the Hallows' full meaning.
metadata.source_text: That’s what he’s after. ... Voldemort was not seeking a new wand; he was seeking an old wand, a very old wand indeed.
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I felt isolated from Ron and Hermione because they wouldn’t share my excitement about the Hallows; their indifference left me alone with my certainty.
metadata.source_text: He blamed Ron and Hermione: Their determined indifference was as bad as the relentless rain for dampening his spirits, but neither could erode his certainty...
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I've read and thought carefully: Dumbledore left clear instructions to find and destroy Horcruxes, and that must remain our priority over speculative quests.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left you very clear instructions: Find and destroy the Horcruxes!
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I became more forceful and worried that Harry is getting carried away with distraction; I strongly believe we cannot afford to be sidetracked by the Hallows idea.
metadata.source_text: I’m sorry, but I think you’ve got this wrong, all wrong... Forget the Deathly Hallows, we can’t afford to get sidetracked —
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I feel exasperated and alarmed with Harry’s fixation; I see him as endangered by romanticising a Quest rather than following Dumbledore’s plan.
metadata.source_text: But you said it, Hermione! You’ve got to find out about them for yourself! It’s a Quest! ... I only said that to try and persuade you to come to the Lovegoods’! ... I didn’t really believe it!
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I managed to get the Potterwatch password 'Albus' on the wireless and heard Lee Jordan report deaths and news — that got through to us from the outside.
metadata.source_text: I’ve got it, I’ve got it! Password was ‘Albus’! ... '... apologize for our temporary absence from the airwaves...' 'It is with great regret that we inform our listeners of the murders of Ted Tonks and Dirk Cresswell.'
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I felt less certain about Harry’s Hallows idea after talking it over; I think we should concentrate on destroying Horcruxes like Dumbledore told us.
metadata.source_text: I think we’re supposed to get rid of Horcruxes, Harry. That’s what Dumbledore told us to do. Maybe ... maybe we should forget about this Hallows business.
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I found myself taking charge more as Harry withdrew; I’m trying to rally them, make plans and keep us moving despite the danger and rain.
metadata.source_text: Three Horcruxes left,' he kept saying. 'We need a plan of action, come on! Where haven’t we looked? Let’s go through it again.'
metadata.scene_title: Connecting the Pieces — Cloak, Snitch, and the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I've heard Remus say outright that he believes I'm still alive and that my death would have been loudly proclaimed by the Death Eaters if it had happened.
metadata.source_text: I do. "There is no doubt at all in my mind that his death would be proclaimed as widely as possible by the Death Eaters if it had happened, because it would strike a deadly blow at the morale of those resisting the new regime."

metadata.description: Hearing Remus say he thinks I'm alive and that people are with me in spirit makes me feel both grateful and ashamed; it changes how I see his forgiveness and support.
metadata.source_text: A mixture of gratitude and shame welled up in Harry. Had Lupin forgiven him, then, for the terrible things he had said when they had last met?

metadata.description: Remus's public defence of me and his advice to follow my instincts makes me feel he still supports me; his words shift my sense of how he thinks about me now.
metadata.source_text: "I do," said Lupin firmly. "There is no doubt at all in my mind... 'The Boy Who Lived' remains a symbol of everything for which we are fighting..."

metadata.description: I've learned from the broadcast that several outspoken supporters of Harry, including Xenophilius Lovegood, have been imprisoned and that Hagrid narrowly escaped arrest and is now on the run.
metadata.source_text: "As regular listeners will know, several of the more outspoken supporters of Harry Potter have now been imprisoned, including Xenophilius Lovegood, erstwhile editor of The Quibbler," said Lupin. "We have also heard within the last few hours that Rubeus Hagrid... has narrowly escaped arrest... Hagrid was not taken into custody, and is, we believe, on the run."

metadata.description: Hearing Lupin caution against 'Support Harry Potter' parties makes me more convinced that open demonstrations are too dangerous now; I feel we must be more careful in how we show support.
metadata.source_text: "May I just add that while we here at Potterwatch applaud Hagrid's spirit, we would urge even the most devoted of Harry's supporters against following Hagrid's lead. 'Support Harry Potter' parties are unwise in the present climate."

metadata.description: Remus's warm, firm defence of Harry and his gentle encouragement that Harry follow his instincts makes me see him as steadfast and compassionate toward Harry again; I feel emotional about his support.
metadata.source_text: "I do," said Lupin firmly... "And I'd tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right." Harry looked at Hermione, whose eyes were full of tears.

metadata.description: Bill told me Remus Lupin is living with Tonks again and that she's getting pretty big, so I've learned they're back together and expecting a child.
metadata.source_text: "Bill told me Lupin’s living with Tonks again! And apparently she’s getting pretty big too. . . ."

metadata.description: Hearing Lupin publicly defend Harry and report that supporters are being jailed makes me more certain that staying hidden and cautious is the sensible option rather than bold public shows.
metadata.source_text: "'Support Harry Potter' parties are unwise in the present climate." "Indeed they are, Romulus," said Lee...

metadata.description: When Lupin spoke for me and others about Harry and warned people, I felt relieved and grateful; knowing Lupin and Tonks are together again also makes me feel more optimistic about my friends.
metadata.source_text: "I do," said Lupin firmly... "And I'd tell him to follow his instincts, which are good and nearly always right." "Bill told me Lupin’s living with Tonks again!"

metadata.description: I've learned that being stung can leave my face horribly swollen and nearly blind, and that losing my wand makes me helpless when attackers search the tent.
metadata.source_text: Stung," Harry muttered. "Been stung."

metadata.description: I believe I can be mistaken for someone else if I lie quickly enough; I had to pretend I was Vernon Dudley and a Slytherin to avoid immediate trouble.
metadata.source_text: "Dudley," said Harry. "And your first name?" "I — Vernon. Vernon Dudley."

metadata.description: I feel alarmed about people like Greyback and Scabior; Greyback's relish and Scabior's sneer make me dread what they might do to my friends and anyone they consider a Mudblood or traitor.
metadata.source_text: "A Weasley?" rasped Greyback. "So you’re related to blood traitors even if you’re not a Mudblood."

metadata.description: I've learned that speaking calmly under fear can sound convincing; I said my name was Penelope Clearwater and declared my blood status as half-blood to survive interrogation.
metadata.source_text: "Penelope Clearwater," said Hermione. She sounded terrified, but convincing. "What’s your blood status?" "Half-blood," said Hermione.

metadata.description: I now feel how terror can force someone to answer quickly and betray themselves; hearing Greyback repeat the Prophet caption made me panic and almost reveal the truth.
metadata.source_text: "'Hermione Granger,'" Scabior was saying, "'the Mudblood who is known to be traveling with 'arry Potter.'"

metadata.description: I worry that being linked to Harry will put me in greater danger; the captors clearly single out anyone connected to him and treat them far more harshly.
metadata.source_text: "' . . . known to be traveling with Harry Potter,'" repeated Greyback quietly.

metadata.description: I learned that my stammer and blood status can be used against me; when they mocked me as a Weasley and asked about the Dark Lord's name, I had to stutter out answers to survive.
metadata.source_text: "I’b Bardy," said Ron, and Harry could tell that his mouth was full of blood. "Bardy Weadley."

metadata.description: I feel culpable and ashamed because I said the name, thinking it was only an accident, and now I believe that my slip put everyone at risk.
metadata.source_text: "This is all my fault. I said the name, I’m sorry —"

metadata.description: I know that being a Weasley marks me as part of a family called "blood traitors" by these men; I feel more vulnerable because of my name and family ties.
metadata.source_text: "A Weasley?" rasped Greyback. "So you’re related to blood traitors even if you’re not a Mudblood."

metadata.description: My scar burns with terrible, exquisite pain whenever Voldemort's thoughts reach me; I can feel him pulling at my mind and I have to fight to stay present.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s scar was exquisitely painful, but he struggled with all his strength against the pull of Voldemort’s thoughts: It had never been so important to remain in his own right mind.

metadata.description: Greyback and the Snatchers have recognised me and think they've caught me; they handled my face and shoved my glasses back on to confirm I'm Potter.
metadata.source_text: “I thought you wore glasses, Potter?” breathed Greyback. “I found glasses!” yelped one of the Snatchers skulking in the background. “There was glasses in the tent, Greyback, wait —” And seconds later Harry’s glasses had been rammed back onto his face.

metadata.description: They mean to take me straight to You-Know-Who at the Malfoys’ place instead of bringing me to the Ministry; Greyback suggests delivering me to Voldemort himself.
metadata.source_text: “To hell with the Ministry,” growled Greyback. “They’ll take the credit, and we won’t get a look in. I say we take him straight to You-Know-Who.”

metadata.description: The cellar is filled with other prisoners: Hermione, Ron, Luna, Dean, Ollivander and Griphook are all here and suffering; Bellatrix is torturing Hermione upstairs.
metadata.source_text: Harry could hear Hermione’s breathing, fast and terrified... He saw Luna, all eyes in her white face, and the motionless figure of Ollivander the wandmaker, curled up on the floor in the corner. Craning around, he caught sight of their fellow prisoners: Dean and Griphook the goblin...

metadata.description: I think Greyback isn't trusted enough to be in Voldemort's inner circle; he hasn't been branded with the Dark Mark, so he won't summon You-Know-Who himself.
metadata.source_text: Harry thought he knew why Greyback was not calling Voldemort. ... Greyback had not been granted this highest honor.

metadata.description: Dobby has somehow returned to Malfoy Manor and says he can rescue us; he can Apparate out of the cellar and carry some of us to Bill and Fleur's Shell Cottage.
metadata.source_text: Dobby’s enormous, tennis-ball-shaped eyes were wide... “Harry Potter,” he squeaked... “Dobby has come to rescue you.” ... “You can Disapparate out of this cellar?” he asked Dobby, who nodded... “Bill and Fleur’s,” said Ron. “Shell Cottage on the outskirts of Tinworth!”

metadata.description: Dobby agrees to take Luna, Dean and Mr. Ollivander to Bill and Fleur’s and then come back for the rest of us.
metadata.source_text: “Right. Dobby, I want you to grab Luna, Dean, and Mr. Ollivander, and take them — take them to —” “Bill and Fleur’s,” said Ron... “And then come back,” said Harry. ... “Of course, Harry Potter,” whispered the little elf.

metadata.description: The Deluminator can release captured lights into a room when clicked; Ron used it and little luminescent spheres floated into the cellar, lighting the place like tiny suns.
metadata.source_text: “My pocket!” said Ron. “In my pocket, there’s a Deluminator, and it’s full of light!” ... there was a click, and the luminescent spheres the Deluminator had sucked from the lamps in the tent flew into the cellar...

metadata.description: The shard of mirror showed me Dumbledore's eye for a blink, but then it was gone; the mirror fragment otherwise only reflected the cellar walls.
metadata.source_text: the mirror fragment fell sparkling to the floor, and he saw a gleam of brightest blue — Dumbledore’s eye was gazing at him out of the mirror. “Help us!” he yelled at it... The eye blinked and was gone. ... he saw nothing reflected there but the walls and ceiling of their prison

metadata.description: Dobby has come to help me despite being terrified in his old masters' house; I have to trust him and send him with others to safety.
metadata.source_text: Dobby’s enormous, tennis-ball-shaped eyes were wide; he was trembling... “Dobby has come to rescue you.” ... “Of course, Harry Potter,” whispered the little elf.

metadata.description: I'm being tortured upstairs and it's unbearable; they keep demanding to know about a sword and whether we've been in Gringotts.
metadata.source_text: From above came Bellatrix’s voice. “You are lying, filthy Mudblood, and I know it! You have been inside my vault at Gringotts! Tell the truth, tell the truth!” Another terrible scream — “HERMIONE!”

metadata.description: I'm desperate and terrified for my friends; I keep screaming under torture and can't bear the thought of them being hurt.
metadata.source_text: Hermione screamed again from overhead... Hermione was screaming again: The sound went through Harry like physical pain.

metadata.description: I remain fiercely protective of Harry and the others even while being forced; I insist about the sword being a copy and try to defend the truth despite the pain.
metadata.source_text: “We’ve never been inside your vault. . . . It isn’t the real sword! It’s a copy, just a copy!”

metadata.description: I carried the Deluminator in my pocket and used it; clicking it returned the stolen lights as small luminous spheres into the cellar, which helped light the place.
metadata.source_text: “My pocket!” said Ron. “In my pocket, there’s a Deluminator, and it’s full of light!” A few seconds later, there was a click, and the luminescent spheres... flew into the cellar

metadata.description: I panic and shout for Hermione repeatedly when she's taken upstairs; my fear makes me reckless, like trying to Disapparate without a wand.
metadata.source_text: “HERMIONE!” Ron bellowed... Ron was now trying to Disapparate without a wand.

metadata.description: I want to help Harry and the others; I tell Dobby to take people to Bill and Fleur’s and I try to calm things, but I'm shaken and guilty when I nearly reveal things by shouting.
metadata.source_text: “Bill and Fleur’s,” said Ron. ... “DOB — !” Harry hit Ron on the arm to stop him shouting, and Ron looked terrified at his mistake.

metadata.description: I learned that Wormtail's silver hand can turn on him and strangle him if he hesitates — I actually watched it kill him despite our trying to stop it.
metadata.source_text: The silver tool that Voldemort had given his most cowardly servant had turned upon its disarmed and useless owner; Pettigrew was reaping his reward for his hesitation, his moment of pity; he was being strangled before their eyes.

metadata.description: I believed we had no choice but to fight right then; seeing Wormtail die made me realise how dangerous even their gifts are — mercy can be fatal in that world.
metadata.source_text: The silver tool that Voldemort had given his most cowardly servant had turned upon its disarmed and useless owner; Pettigrew was reaping his reward for his hesitation, his moment of pity; he was being strangled before their eyes.

metadata.description: I know now that Dobby truly cares for me — he risked everything, disobeyed his masters, and came to save me. I felt it when he shouted he had come to save Harry Potter.
metadata.source_text: Dobby is a free elf, and Dobby has come to save Harry Potter and his friends!

metadata.description: I've seen Bellatrix stab people and slash goblins without hesitation; the Malfoys and Bellatrix will use cruelty to get what they want.
metadata.source_text: Good," she said, and with a casual flick of her wand she slashed another deep cut into the goblin’s face, and he dropped with a yell at her feet.

metadata.description: I used to think the presence of the Dark Lord would be avoidable if we were careful; hearing the summons and feeling Harry's scar made me realise how close Voldemort's return can be and how helpless we are sometimes.
metadata.source_text: The Dark Lord is coming, Harry Potter! Your death approaches!" Harry knew it; his scar was bursting with the pain of it, and he could feel Voldemort flying through the sky...

metadata.description: Being threatened by Bellatrix with a knife at my throat made me understand how vicious she is and how much danger my friends are in when they face her.
metadata.source_text: Bellatrix was supporting Hermione, who seemed to be unconscious, and was holding her short silver knife to Hermione’s throat.

metadata.description: I discovered that I can fake Wormtail's voice well enough to fool others for a moment — I used his voice to lie to Lucius while we struggled in the cellar.
metadata.source_text: “Nothing!” Ron called back, in a passable imitation of Wormtail’s wheezy voice. “All fine!”

metadata.description: After seeing Wormtail die because of that silver hand, I'm more certain than ever that our enemies' tools are dangerous and unpredictable; you can't rely on their 'gifts'.
metadata.source_text: The silver tool that Voldemort had given his most cowardly servant had turned upon its disarmed and useless owner; Pettigrew was reaping his reward for his hesitation...

metadata.description: I feel fiercely protective of Hermione — when Bellatrix threatened her, I froze with Wormtail's wand because I couldn't let her be hurt.
metadata.source_text: STOP OR SHE DIES!” Panting, Harry peered around the edge of the sofa. Bellatrix was supporting Hermione... she was holding her short silver knife to Hermione’s throat.

metadata.description: I found Dobby pierced by Bellatrix’s silver knife and I knew he was dead; I took the blade out and wrapped him in my jacket because he deserved a proper burial.
metadata.source_text: Harry’s voice was still saying, “Dobby . . . Dobby . . .” even though he knew that the elf had gone where he could not call him back.

metadata.description: I feel more urgent and determined about the mission Dumbledore left us; losing Dobby sharpened that purpose so I must speak to Griphook and Ollivander right away.
metadata.source_text: I need to speak to Griphook and Ollivander," Harry said. "No," said Fleur. "You will ’ave to wait, ’Arry. Zey are both ill, tired —" "I’m sorry," he said without heat, "but it can’t wait. I need to talk to them now. Privately — and separately. It’s urgent.

metadata.description: I trust Bill and the others enough to involve them in burying Dobby and in protecting Ron’s family, but I must keep the mission secret even from them; the Order knows and that limits what I can say.
metadata.source_text: “We can’t tell you what we’re doing,” said Harry flatly. “You’re in the Order, Bill, you know Dumbledore left us a mission. We’re not supposed to talk about it to anyone else.”

metadata.description: I was injured but alive; Fleur is looking after me and I’m wrapped in a dressing gown, shaky but conscious after the ordeal.
metadata.source_text: “How’s Hermione?” “Better,” said Ron. “Fleur’s looking after her.”

metadata.description: Being hurt like that made me rely on our friends in a new way; I’m grateful and a little shaken, but I still stand with Harry and Ron when he asks for them to come.
metadata.source_text: Hermione gave a weak smile as Ron gave her a one-armed squeeze.

metadata.description: I feel close to Ron and Harry; Ron’s squeeze and Harry’s quiet concern remind me we’re a team even when things go wrong.
metadata.source_text: “How are you?” Harry asked Hermione. “You were amazing — coming up with that story when she was hurting you like that —” Hermione gave a weak smile as Ron gave her a one-armed squeeze.

metadata.description: Hermione’s alive and Fleur is tending to her; I put my arm around her and sat on the grave edge to help cover Dobby with my shoes and support her.
metadata.source_text: Ron sat on the edge of the grave and stripped off his shoes and socks, which he placed upon the elf’s bare feet.

metadata.description: Seeing Dobby dead hit me hard — I’m gutted and thankful Dobby helped us, but I’m also relieved Hermione pulled through and angry about what happened at Malfoy Manor.
metadata.source_text: “Yeah . . . thanks, Dobby.” “Thanks,” muttered Dean. Harry swallowed. “Good-bye, Dobby,” he said.

metadata.description: I’m protective of Hermione and closer to Harry in purpose now; when Harry calls us I follow without question because we all need to stick together.
metadata.source_text: “I need you two as well!” he called to Ron and Hermione, who had been skulking, half concealed, in the doorway of the sitting room. They both moved into the light, looking oddly relieved.

metadata.description: I learned that Griphook remembers showing me to my Gringotts vault the first time I visited; he even called me very famous among goblins.
metadata.source_text: I remember, Harry Potter. Even amongst goblins, you are very famous.

metadata.description: I found out that the Lestranges' vault at Gringotts likely contains something important — probably a Horcrux — because Bellatrix reacted as if we'd seen or taken something terrifying.
metadata.source_text: Bellatrix was terrified when she thought we’d been in there, she was beside herself.

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that the safest hiding places for something precious would be a trusted wizarding vault like Gringotts, maybe even more so than anything left to him directly.
metadata.source_text: The safest place in the world for anything you want to hide, Hagrid told me . . . except for Hogwarts.

metadata.description: Griphook and I are sizing each other up; he’s suspicious and resentful but also intrigued enough to say he might think about helping us.
metadata.source_text: You are an unusual wizard, Harry Potter.

metadata.description: I've seen that Griphook knows goblins feel deeply about their rights versus wand-carriers and refuses to speak about Gringotts' secrets because of their code to guard treasures.
metadata.source_text: It is against our code to speak of the secrets of Gringotts. We are the guardians of fabulous treasures.

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more determined — I will state plainly that I protest the oppression of those the wand-carriers persecute, and I won't be ashamed to call myself a Mudblood in defiance.
metadata.source_text: Mudblood, and proud of it! I’ve got no higher position under this new order than you have, Griphook!

metadata.description: I feel that Harry is trustworthy and not motivated by personal gain; Griphook accepted that possibility after watching how we treated house-elves and goblins tonight.
metadata.source_text: If there was a wizard of whom I would believe that they did not seek personal gain, it would be you, Harry Potter.

metadata.description: I learned that goblins can do magic without wands and that there's a bitter dispute between goblins and wizards about wandlore and metalwork.
metadata.source_text: Well, goblins can do magic without wands.

metadata.description: I'm uneasy but convinced that breaking into Gringotts is possible because it's been breached before, though Griphook insists past breaches had weaker protections.
metadata.source_text: It’s been done.

metadata.description: I think Griphook enjoys keeping us hanging and is playing us a bit; he's not openly helpful yet and seems to take a certain pleasure in our frustration.
metadata.source_text: Little git.

metadata.description: I found out my broken wand cannot be repaired — Ollivander told me a wand that has suffered that degree of damage cannot be fixed by any means he knows.
metadata.source_text: No," whispered Ollivander. "I am sorry, very sorry, but a wand that has suffered this degree of damage cannot be repaired by any means that I know of."

metadata.description: I learned that Draco Malfoy’s wand may now be mine because I took it by force and wands generally change allegiance when won from their owner.
metadata.source_text: "Perhaps not. If you took it —" "— I did —" "— then it may be yours. Of course, the manner of taking matters. Much also depends upon the wand itself. In general, however, where a wand has been won, its allegiance will change."

metadata.description: I discovered that You-Know-Who tortured Ollivander to learn about twin cores and asked about a wand more powerful than his — the Elder Wand.
metadata.source_text: "He tortured me, you must understand that! The Cruciatus Curse, I — I had no choice but to tell him what I knew, what I guessed!"

metadata.description: I was told that Gregorovitch once had the Elder Wand, Grindelwald stole it from him, Grindelwald used it to rise to power, and Dumbledore later defeated Grindelwald and took the wand to Hogwarts.
metadata.source_text: "Gregorovitch had the Elder Wand a long time ago," he said. "I saw You-Know-Who trying to find him.... And Grindelwald used the Elder Wand to become powerful. And at the height of his power... he dueled Grindelwald and beat him, and he took the Elder Wand."

metadata.description: I'm more certain now that the Elder Wand is real and extremely dangerous in Voldemort's hands, and that Dumbledore did not want me to have it because my task must remain the Horcruxes.
metadata.source_text: "Dumbledore didn't want me to have it. He didn't want me to take it. He wanted me to get the Horcruxes."

metadata.description: I feel a complicated shift toward Ollivander: I pity him for being tortured, yet I'm disturbed that he seems fascinated by the idea of the Dark Lord possessing the Elder Wand.
metadata.source_text: "Even now, having been tortured and imprisoned by Voldemort, the idea of the Dark wizard in possession of this wand seemed to enthrall him as much as it repulsed him."

metadata.description: I've learned from Mr. Ollivander that the Elder Wand has a traceable history: it resurfaces through time, has identifying features, and is studied in obscure written accounts by wandmakers.
metadata.source_text: "Yes," said Ollivander. "Yes, it is perfectly possible to trace the wand's course through history. ... There are written accounts, some of them obscure, that I and other wandmakers have made it our business to study."

metadata.description: I'm alarmed and frightened at the thought that Voldemort could learn about Harry's broken wand from spells left on wands at the Malfoys', which would alert him to Harry's vulnerability.
metadata.source_text: "He can’t know that, Harry, how could he — ?"

metadata.description: I trust Ollivander's expertise about wands more now, but I'm unsettled by his obvious fear and how much Voldemort's interest terrifies him.
metadata.source_text: "Ollivander looked terrified. 'He tortured me, you must understand that! The Cruciatus Curse, I — I had no choice...'"

metadata.description: I've learned that Wormtail's wand, which I was forced to make, is chestnut and dragon heartstring, and if I won a wand it is likely to do my bidding better than another wand.
metadata.source_text: "Chestnut and dragon heartstring. Nine-and-a-quarter inches. Brittle. I was forced to make this shortly after my kidnapping, for Peter Pettigrew. Yes, if you won it, it is more likely to do your bidding, and do it well, than another wand."

metadata.description: I'm eager and impulsive now — I want to go after the Elder Wand right away because I think possessing it could stop Voldemort, even though Harry insists our priority is Horcruxes.
metadata.source_text: "The unbeatable wand, Harry!" moaned Ron. "I'm not supposed to . . . I'm supposed to get the Horcruxes. . . ."

metadata.description: I'm frustrated with Harry's choices in the moment; I resent delays and question why he didn't prioritize securing the Elder Wand sooner.
metadata.source_text: "Harry! How long have you known this — why have we been wasting time? Why did you talk to Griphook first?"

metadata.description: I learned that Griphook will help us only if we're willing to give him something specific — not gold, but the Sword of Godric Gryffindor.
metadata.source_text: I have reached my decision, Harry Potter," said the goblin, "Though the goblins of Gringotts will consider it base treachery, I have decided to help you —" "That’s great!" said Harry, relief surging through him. "Griphook, thank you, we’re really —" "— in return," said the goblin firmly, "for payment." Slightly taken aback, Harry hesitated. "How much do you want? I’ve got gold." "Not gold," said Griphook. "I have gold." His black eyes glittered; there were no whites to his eyes. "I want the sword. The sword of Godric Gryffindor."
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I felt hopeful when Griphook said he'd help, but I changed my mind fast when he demanded the sword; I no longer think getting his help will be easy or straightforward.
metadata.source_text: "I have reached my decision, Harry Potter," said the goblin, ... "I want the sword. The sword of Godric Gryffindor." Harry’s spirits plummeted. "You can’t have that," he said. "I’m sorry."
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I now see Griphook as someone who values goblin claims over our wizarding ideas of ownership; he's not simply a helper — he has his own priorities I must reckon with.
metadata.source_text: "I am not a thief, boy! I am not trying to procure treasures to which I have no right!" "The sword’s ours —" "It is not," said the goblin.
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I've observed that Griphook will only help in exchange for a specific non-monetary item: he asked explicitly for the Sword of Godric Gryffindor, not for gold.
metadata.source_text: "Not gold," said Griphook. "I have gold." His black eyes glittered; there were no whites to his eyes. "I want the sword. The sword of Godric Gryffindor."
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I had probably assumed goblins would accept payment in treasure, but seeing Griphook insist on the sword has changed my view: goblin claims of ownership differ fundamentally from our assumptions.
metadata.source_text: "I am not a thief, boy! I am not trying to procure treasures to which I have no right!" "The sword’s ours —" "It is not," said the goblin.
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I now regard Griphook with more caution and cultural respect; he holds strong beliefs about goblin ownership that clash with ours, so I must be careful negotiating with him.

metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I found out the wrong way that Griphook won't tolerate us treating goblin work as stealing; when I suggested taking stuff from the Lestrange vault, Griphook got angry.
metadata.source_text: “We can give you something else,” said Ron eagerly. “I’ll bet the Lestranges have got loads of stuff, you can take your pick once we get into the vault.” He had said the wrong thing. Griphook flushed angrily. “I am not a thief, boy! I am not trying to procure treasures to which I have no right!”
metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I thought we could bribe Griphook with loot from the vault, but I changed my mind after he made it clear goblins see such acts as unacceptable; I won't flippantly suggest that again.

metadata.scene_title: Goblin Demand and Tension in the Smallest Bedroom

metadata.description: I now see Griphook as proud and serious about goblin rights; he's not someone to joke or haggle with casually, or he'll get properly miffed.
