metadata.description: I've learned that Griphook, a goblin, claims goblins say Gryffindor stole the Sword of Gryffindor and that goblin history disputes the wizarding account of the sword's origins.
metadata.source_text: It is true? Harry asked Hermione. Was the sword stolen by Gryffindor?
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I'm less certain that the wizarding version of history is the whole truth; maybe the goblin version could be right, and that changes how I feel about Gryffindor's past.
metadata.source_text: Maybe he’s lying, Harry said, opening his eyes again. Griphook. Maybe Gryffindor didn’t take the sword. How do we know the goblin version of history’s right?
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I feel torn about goblins now: I want to trust Griphook to help us, but I also feel guilty at the idea that Gryffindor might have wronged goblins; still, I'll promise the sword to get help.
metadata.source_text: We’ll tell him he can have the sword after he’s helped us get into that vault — but we’ll be careful to avoid telling him exactly when he can have it.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I've read that wizarding history often leaves out how wizards treated other magical races; I don’t know any account that says Gryffindor stole the sword, but records are incomplete.
metadata.source_text: I don’t know," she said hopelessly. "Wizarding history often skates over what the wizards have done to other magical races, but there’s no account that I know of that says Gryffindor stole the sword.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I'm more convinced we must not deceive Griphook; tricking him would be despicable and would only confirm why goblins hate wizards, so my stance is firmly against double-crossing.
metadata.source_text: That," she said quietly, "is despicable. Ask for his help, then double-cross him? And you wonder why goblins don’t like wizards, Ron?
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I now view the goblins as a group that has been treated brutally in the past and therefore deserving of more sympathy and honesty from us, not cunning or theft.
metadata.source_text: Goblins have got good reason to dislike wizards, Ron," said Hermione. "They’ve been treated brutally in the past.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I know goblins tell stories about wizards always trying to get one over on them, and Griphook wants the sword — goblins think wizards nick things from them.
metadata.source_text: It’ll be one of those goblin stories," said Ron, "about how the wizards are always trying to get one over on them.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I'm more convinced that goblins are dangerous and untrustworthy in battle terms — they’ve killed plenty of wizards and fought dirty — so I'm inclined to be suspicious of Griphook.
metadata.source_text: Goblins aren’t exactly fluffy little bunnies, though, are they?" said Ron. "They’ve killed plenty of us. They’ve fought dirty too.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I was ready to trick Griphook by switching the sword for a fake and scarper before he noticed; that idea shows I regard goblins as enemies we can outwit rather than allies to be treated fairly.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, but we could scarper before he realizes —" He quailed beneath the look Hermione was giving him.
metadata.scene_title: Debate Over Goblin Claims and a Plan to Deceive

metadata.description: I've learned I promised the Sword of Gryffindor to a goblin named Griphook in exchange for his help.
metadata.source_text: I have your word, Harry Potter, that you will give me the sword of Gryffindor if I help you?
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I don't like what we're doing and feel ashamed, but I also accept that we might have no choice; I'm torn between defiance and shame over the decision.
metadata.source_text: I won’t be lying . . . really.” Harry met her eyes with a mixture of defiance and shame. He remembered the words that had been engraved over the gateway to Nurmengard: FOR THE GREATER GOOD. He pushed the idea away. What choice did they have?
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I shook Griphook's hand and gave him my word, which has made our relationship a formal, binding sort of bargain even though I wonder if he reads my doubts in my face.
metadata.source_text: Then shake," said the goblin, holding out his hand. Harry took it and shook. He wondered whether those black eyes saw any misgivings in his own.
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I've realized that the plan we're discussing is something I don't like, despite understanding its purpose.
metadata.source_text: I don’t like it,” said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I'm uneasy about the course we've chosen; saying openly that I don't like it shows my feelings have shifted from theoretical concern to active dislike.
metadata.source_text: I don’t like it,” said Hermione.
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: Seeing Harry meet my eyes with shame and defiance makes me more aware of the burden he's carrying and alters how I view his resolve—he's conflicted but committed.
metadata.source_text: I won’t be lying . . . really.” Harry met her eyes with a mixture of defiance and shame.
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I've found the plan to be downright genius and ready to move, despite any qualms the others express.
metadata.source_text: Well, I think it’s genius,” said Ron, standing up again.
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I'm more optimistic than the others; I don't share their hesitation and now truly believe pushing forward is the right move.
metadata.source_text: Let’s go and tell him.”
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: By standing up and urging action, I show I'm backing Harry and Hermione practically and that I trust Harry's judgment enough to rally behind the plan.
metadata.source_text: Well, I think it’s genius,” said Ron, standing up again. “Let’s go and tell him."
metadata.scene_title: Resolve, Promises, and Setting Out the Plan

metadata.description: I learned that Griphook has visited the Lestrange vault only once, and that the vaults of the oldest wizarding families lie at the deepest, best-protected levels where they store their treasures.
metadata.source_text: I have visited the Lestranges’ vault only once," Griphook told them, "on the occasion I was told to place inside it the false sword. It is one of the most ancient chambers. The oldest Wizarding families store their treasures at the deepest level, where the vaults are largest and best protected. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Griphook Explains the Lestrange Vault; Arrival of Lupin

metadata.description: I got a sudden, sharp fright when Lupin announced himself — I didn’t expect him and it made me worry straightaway about what had happened and why he was there in such a state.
metadata.source_text: "It is I, Remus John Lupin!" called a voice over the howling wind. Harry experienced a thrill of fear; what had happened?
metadata.scene_title: Griphook Explains the Lestrange Vault; Arrival of Lupin

metadata.description: Seeing Lupin stumble in, white-faced and windblown, and then cry out that 'It's a boy!' made me view him as someone urgent and trusted in a crisis — his arrival changes how immediate and serious the situation feels to me.

metadata.scene_title: Implications of Goblin Beliefs; Warning to Be Careful

metadata.source_text: “This is the wand that tortured Neville’s mum and dad, and who knows how many other people? This is the wand that killed Sirius!”

metadata.source_text: Ron’s hair was now long and wavy; he had a thick brown beard and mustache, no freckles, a short, broad nose, and heavy eyebrows.

metadata.description: I’m a bit anxious about my look — I still care about how the beard sits and the nose length, even though Hermione insists it’s not about looking handsome.
metadata.source_text: “Right, but remember, I don’t like the beard too long —” “Oh, for heaven’s sake, this isn’t about looking handsome —” “It’s not that, it gets in the way! But I liked my nose a bit shorter, try and do it the way you did last time.”

metadata.source_text: He held out a slightly trembling hand, and in a dreadful blast of realization Harry knew that the goblins of Gringotts were aware that Bellatrix’s wand had been stolen.

metadata.source_text: "Bought it from Dung ’bout a year ago," said Aberforth. "Albus told me what it was. Been trying to keep an eye out for you."

metadata.description: I’m more aware now that Dumbledore’s life and choices were complicated and that people close to him, like Aberforth, feel hurt and angry about how things turned out.
metadata.source_text: "Funny thing, how many of the people my brother cared about very much ended up in a worse state than if he’d left ’em well alone."

metadata.description: I realize Aberforth liked Dobby and felt sorry when I told him Dobby was dead; Aberforth’s simple 'I liked that elf' showed me he can be quietly kind despite his gruffness.
metadata.source_text: "I’m sorry to hear it. I liked that elf."

metadata.description: I've learned Aberforth helped us: he saved our lives twice by sheltering us and providing the tunnel entrance at the Hog's Head.
metadata.source_text: I don’t know how to thank you. You’ve saved our lives twice.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I feel more reliant on allies like Aberforth; I now reckon I can’t take rescue for granted and that others have risks to warn me about.
metadata.source_text: Look after ’em, then," said Aberforth gruffly. "I might not be able to save ’em a third time.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I’m grateful to Aberforth and I appreciate that he’s willing to help, even if he sounds gruff — I now see him as someone who’s already risked a lot for us.
metadata.source_text: I don’t know how to thank you. You’ve saved our lives twice.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I’ve learned there’s an alternative tunnel entrance in the Hog’s Head that bypasses the sealed school passages and curses blocking the usual routes.
metadata.source_text: They sealed off all of those before the start of the year," said Neville. "There’s no chance of getting through any of them now, not with curses over the entrances and Death Eaters and dementors waiting at the exits.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I feel surprised but convinced that stealth and outside help are now essential; I no longer assume the school’s usual protections will work for us.
metadata.source_text: They sealed off all of those before the start of the year," said Neville. "There’s no chance of getting through any of them now, not with curses over the entrances and Death Eaters and dementors waiting at the exits.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I trust Neville’s resourcefulness more now — seeing him battered but enthusiastic makes me realise he’s been courageous and useful to our cause.
metadata.source_text: Neville laughed gleefully. "What did you do with the dragon?"
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I’ve learned that the dragon they escaped on was released into the wild; we didn’t keep it as a pet despite Hermione joking about it.
metadata.source_text: "Released it into the wild," said Ron. "Hermione was all for keeping it as a pet —"
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I’m more convinced than ever that our actions make headlines among students — people are talking about the Gringotts break-in and the dragon escape, and that changes how others see us.
metadata.source_text: It’s everywhere, everyone’s talking about it, Terry Boot got beaten up by Carrow for yelling about it in the Great Hall at dinner!
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I feel proud of Harry and more protective of Hermione; joking about the dragon’s fate is my way of dealing with how mad everything’s been, but I back my friends completely.
metadata.source_text: "Released it into the wild," said Ron. "Hermione was all for keeping it as a pet —"
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at the Hog's Head and Tunnel Entry

metadata.description: I learned that the Carrows run discipline at Hogwarts now, and that Amycus teaches the Dark Arts while Alecto teaches Muggle Studies as a compulsory, hateful subject.
metadata.source_text: Do you know about the Carrows? "Those two Death Eaters who teach here?" "They do more than teach," said Neville. "They're in charge of all discipline.
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I'm more horrified and alarmed than I was before — I didn’t realise Hogwarts had been turned into a place where teachers force pupils to use the Cruciatus Curse and openly torture people.
metadata.source_text: "Amycus, the bloke, he teaches what used to be Defense Against the Dark Arts, except now it’s just the Dark Arts. We’re supposed to practice the Cruciatus Curse on people who’ve earned detentions —"
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I feel a renewed sense of protectiveness toward Neville and the others; hearing how they've suffered and how people like Crabbe and Goyle enjoy cruelty makes me see Neville's courage in a new light.
metadata.source_text: "That’s how I got this one," he pointed at a particularly deep gash in his cheek, "I refused to do it. Some people are into it, though; Crabbe and Goyle love it."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I've found out that Muggle Studies has been turned into compulsory propaganda at Hogwarts, teaching that Muggles are animals and that the so-called natural order is being reestablished.
metadata.source_text: "Alecto, Amycus’s sister, teaches Muggle Studies, which is compulsory for everyone. We’ve all got to listen to her explain how Muggles are like animals, stupid and dirty, and how they drove wizards into hiding by being vicious toward them, and how the natural order is being reestablished."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I'm angrier and more determined than before — I didn't expect teachers to be using lessons as open propaganda and that pupils are being forced to accept such vile ideas.
metadata.source_text: "Alecto, Amycus’s sister, teaches Muggle Studies, which is compulsory for everyone. We’ve all got to listen to her explain how Muggles are like animals..."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I feel sympathy and admiration for Neville for standing up to the Carrows; his bravery in opposing them and organizing secret communications shows he's become a leader to rely on.
metadata.source_text: "The thing is, it helps when people stand up to them, it gives everyone hope. I used to notice that when you did it, Harry."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I've learned that the Carrows punish students brutally, that some like Crabbe and Goyle enjoy torturing others, and that they even force people to practice the Cruciatus Curse.
metadata.source_text: "Amycus, the bloke, he teaches what used to be Defense Against the Dark Arts, except now it’s just the Dark Arts. We’re supposed to practice the Cruciatus Curse on people who’ve earned detentions —"
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I'm shocked and disgusted — I didn't think Hogwarts could sink so low; hearing about Michael Corner's torture and the Carrows' methods makes me see how dangerous resistance has become.
metadata.source_text: "Michael Corner went and got caught releasing a first-year they’d chained up, and they tortured him pretty badly. That scared people off."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I feel pity for Neville and more respect for him; seeing his injuries and hearing what he did to help others makes me realise he's been shouldering a lot on his own.
metadata.source_text: "Blimey, Neville," said Ron, "there’s a time and a place for getting a smart mouth."
metadata.scene_title: Gratitude, Passage, and Arrival in the Room of Requirement

metadata.description: I learned that Neville’s Gran wrote him a letter saying she’s proud of him and that he’s his parents’ son; Neville actually keeps that letter in the breast pocket of his robes.
metadata.source_text: She sent me a letter," he clapped a hand to the breast pocket of his robes, "telling me she was proud of me, that I’m my parents’ son, and to keep it up.
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I’m surprised and a bit impressed that Neville can grin and laugh about being hunted — I didn’t expect him to be so quietly determined and brave after what happened to his family.
metadata.source_text: Thing was," he faced them, and Harry was astonished to see that he was grinning, "they bit off a bit more than they could chew with Gran.
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I feel more connected to Neville now — seeing him lead us to a safe place and hearing his story makes me respect him more than I did before.
metadata.source_text: ’Course," said Neville. "You’ll see. We’re here."
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I now know that Neville found and is using the Room of Requirement as a hideout for the D.A., and that it can expand to accommodate many people and refuse entry to their pursuers.
metadata.source_text: “Room of Requirement, of course!” said Neville. “Surpassed itself, hasn’t it? ... But it’s expanded as more and more of the D.A. have arrived.”
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I feel reassured that the Room of Requirement can provide secure shelter for the D.A.; my worry about finding a safe base has eased because the room won’t open to the Carrows while someone stays inside.
metadata.source_text: “It’s a proper hideout, as long as one of us stays in here, they can’t get at us, the door won’t open.
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I’m more trusting of Neville’s resourcefulness; he managed to find and expand a perfect hideout and see us safely to it, which changes how I see his strengths.
metadata.source_text: Well, it wasn’t exactly like this when I arrived, it was a load smaller, there was only one hammock and just Gryffindor hangings. But it’s expanded as more and more of the D.A. have arrived.
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I found out that the Carrows tried to use Neville’s Gran to control him, but she fought back and is now on the run while Dawlish ended up in St. Mungo’s.
metadata.source_text: Thing was," he faced them, and Harry was astonished to see that he was grinning, "they bit off a bit more than they could chew with Gran. Little old witch living alone, they probably thought they didn’t need to send anyone particularly powerful. Anyway," Neville laughed, "Dawlish is still in St. Mungo’s and Gran’s on the run.
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I’m properly confused but impressed — I didn’t think Neville would be such a serious risk to the Carrows, and now I’m starting to think we shouldn’t underestimate him.
metadata.source_text: “But,” said Ron, looking thoroughly confused, “aren’t — aren’t we heading straight back into Hogwarts?”
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I like Neville more after seeing his place and how the D.A. reacts; the way everyone cheers him and how he’s kept a hideout shows he’s become important to us.
metadata.source_text: “Look who it is! Didn’t I tell you?” As Harry emerged into the room beyond the passage, there were several screams and yells: “HARRY!” “It’s Potter, it’s POTTER!” “Ron!” “Hermione!” He had a confused impression... they were engulfed, hugged, pounded on the back, their hair ruffled, their hands shaken, by what seemed to be more than twenty people
metadata.scene_title: Reunion, Description of the Hideout, and Neville's Account

metadata.description: I've learned that Dumbledore left a specific task for just the three of us — me, Ron and Hermione — and we're the ones who have to carry it out.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren’t supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I feel urgent that we must leave now because Voldemort may visit Hogwarts next and if he does we'll lose our chance; time is running out and I can't risk telling others.
metadata.source_text: Time was running out fast: If Voldemort chose to visit Hogwarts next, they would miss their chance.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I believe Ron and Hermione are the only ones I can trust with this task — it's meant to be just the three of us, so I need them beside me privately.
metadata.source_text: Well, there’s something we — Ron, Hermione, and I — need to do, and then we’ll get out of here.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I've understood that we must follow Dumbledore's instruction: the task he assigned was specifically for the three of us to do together and not to be shared.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren’t supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I'm more convinced now that secrecy matters for the plan; even though everyone here is loyal and willing, Dumbledore wanted only the three of us to attempt this.
metadata.source_text: We — we can’t tell you. We’ve got to do it — alone.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I still trust Harry and Ron absolutely — we've been chosen together and I accept that that responsibility binds us closer for what's coming.
metadata.source_text: Well, there’s something we — Ron, Hermione, and I — need to do, and then we’ll get out of here.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I've learned that food is one of the five exceptions to Gamp’s Law of Elemental Transfiguration — that's why the Room couldn't produce food and Aberforth had to help.
metadata.source_text: Yeah, well, food’s one of the five exceptions to Gamp’s Law of Elemental Transfiguration," said Ron to general astonishment.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I'm annoyed and a bit hurt that Harry won't tell us what he's doing, but I also get that he thinks it's dangerous; still, I don't accept that easily because we've all suffered together.
metadata.source_text: I never said it had, but I don’t see why you can’t trust us. Everyone in this room’s been fighting and they’ve been driven in here because the Carrows were hunting them down.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I believe in our D.A. and that everyone here is loyal to Dumbledore and to Harry — we kept things going while they were away, and that ought to count.
metadata.source_text: Everyone in here’s proven they’re loyal to Dumbledore — loyal to you.
metadata.scene_title: D.A. Life under the Carrows and Neville's Ordeal

metadata.description: I've learned that Dumbledore left the three of us a job and he wanted just the three of us to do it — we can't tell the others.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I feel now that we have to go alone; even though everyone wants to help, I believe we must keep this to the three of us because that was Dumbledore's wish.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I'm more distant from the rest of Dumbledore's Army in the sense that I can't include them in this — I see them as loyal and wanting to fight, but I have to exclude them for the sake of what Dumbledore asked.
metadata.source_text: "We got your message, Neville! Hello you three, I thought you must be here!" ... "Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I've realized from what Harry said that Dumbledore entrusted a specific task to Harry, Ron and me together, and that he expected secrecy about that task.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I'm now more convinced that secrecy matters here; despite everyone's loyalty, I agree with Harry that some things have to remain private between the three of us for the moment.
metadata.source_text: "We — we can't tell you. We've got to do it — alone."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I feel protective and aligned with Harry and Ron in this; standing between them I know we're a tight unit and that people in the Army are loyal but we must act as a trio for Dumbledore's plan.
metadata.source_text: "We — we can't tell you. We've got to do it — alone."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I've learned that Dumbledore apparently left the three of us a job and that Harry thinks only the three of us should do it — he thinks we mustn't tell the others.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore left the three of us a job," he said carefully, "and we weren't supposed to tell — I mean, he wanted us to do it, just the three of us."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I've started to think differently about keeping people in the dark; I still don't like the idea of leaving our mates to fight alone when we can help, so I'm torn by Harry's secrecy.
metadata.source_text: "Why can't they help?" ... "They can help."
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I'm more defensive of the others' loyalty — I believe the DA have been keeping things going and that they're loyal to Harry, so I don't want to cut them out without good cause.
metadata.source_text: "We’re his army," said Neville. "Dumbledore’s Army. We were all in it together, we’ve been keeping it going while you three have been off on your own —" "It hasn’t exactly been a picnic, mate," said Ron.
metadata.scene_title: Gran's Kidnapping, Rescue, and Growing Resistance

metadata.description: I learned that something might be hidden at Hogwarts that could help overthrow You-Know-Who and that it could be associated with Ravenclaw’s eagle.
metadata.source_text: There’s something we need to find... It’s here at Hogwarts, but we don’t know where. It might have belonged to Ravenclaw. Has anyone heard of an object like that? Has anyone ever come across something with her eagle on it, for instance?
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I’ve changed my mind about keeping everything to myself; I can’t do this entirely alone and I’ve agreed we need others’ help despite Dumbledore’s warning.
metadata.source_text: All right," he said quietly to the other two. "Okay," he called to the room at large, and all noise ceased...
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I’m reminded that Ron and Hermione are the people I trust to share the Horcrux secret with and their support matters — I looked to them and followed their lead.
metadata.source_text: Harry looked from Ron to Hermione, who murmured, “I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.”
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I think we’ve learned that we don’t actually know what the Horcrux in Hogwarts looks like, so we need more people involved to search properly.
metadata.source_text: I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I’ve shifted from wanting secrecy to accepting that Harry shouldn’t shoulder everything alone; I’m urging cooperation rather than isolation.
metadata.source_text: You don’t have to do everything alone, Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I feel that Ron’s opinion is valid here and I supported him openly, which shows I trust his judgment in this search.
metadata.source_text: I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I learnt that we haven’t got to tell everyone it’s a Horcrux — we just need help finding something we don’t even know the shape of.
metadata.source_text: We’ve got to find it fast. We don’t have to tell them it’s a Horcrux.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I’m more convinced that involving other people is the right move because we don’t know exactly what we’re after and we need more eyes.
metadata.source_text: We’ve got to find it fast. We don’t have to tell them it’s a Horcrux.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I feel backed up by Hermione supporting my point to Harry, which makes me think she and I are on the same page about helping him not be alone.
metadata.source_text: I think Ron’s right. We don’t even know what we’re looking for, we need them.
metadata.scene_title: Full Reunion, Plans, and the Diadem Lead

metadata.description: I found that the Marauder’s Map shows our exact positions — Luna’s dot and mine were up on the fifth floor when Filch was moving away.
metadata.source_text: Holding it close to his nose he searched, and located his and Luna’s dots at last. “We’re up on the fifth floor,” he whispered, watching Filch moving away from them, a corridor ahead.

metadata.description: I’m more aware now that prowling the castle at night can make me unbearably nervous — my heart hammered and I realized how much can depend on getting through safely.
metadata.source_text: Harry had prowled the castle at night many times before, but never had his heart hammered this fast, never had so much depended on his safe passage through the place.

metadata.description: Luna’s calm, odd ways actually help — she leads me and thinks of answers when I’m uncertain; I rely on her sensible, serious manner in awkward situations.
metadata.source_text: “Hmm . . . What do you think, Harry?” said Luna, looking thoughtful. “What? Isn’t there just a password?” “Oh no, you’ve got to answer a question,” said Luna.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what happened in the corridor or at the eagle-knocker door.
metadata.source_text: Hermione Granger was not present.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events, so I don't know what occurred while Harry and Luna sneaked through the castle and answered the door's question.
metadata.source_text: Ron Weasley was not present.

metadata.description: I felt my scar throb and went back into Voldemort's mind; he was moving along the tunnel into the first cave and was focused on making sure of the locket.
metadata.source_text: and as his scar throbbed he chose to sink again into Voldemort’s mind . . . He was moving along the tunnel into the first cave . . . He had chosen to make sure of the locket before coming . . . but that would not take him long. . . .

metadata.description: I know now that some of the Carrows will lie and try to blame students to save themselves; they're willing to sacrifice kids to avoid the Dark Lord's wrath.
metadata.source_text: We can push it off on the kids," said Amycus, his piglike face suddenly crafty. "Yeah, that's what we'll do. We'll say Alecto was ambushed by the kids, them kids up there

metadata.description: I've got a stronger protective feeling toward Professor McGonagall; when Amycus spat at her I couldn't stand by and I acted to defend her.
metadata.source_text: He spat in her face. Harry pulled the Cloak off himself, raised his wand, and said, "You shouldn't have done that."

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in Ravenclaw Tower, so I don't know firsthand what happened in the common room.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in Ravenclaw Tower, so I don't have direct knowledge of the confrontation there.
metadata.source_text: Present: None present | Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I can tell Voldemort is coming — my scar burns and I can see him crossing the lake in that ghostly green boat toward the island.
metadata.source_text: He already knows where I am.

metadata.description: I'm acting on Dumbledore's orders: I must find something hidden in the castle that might be the diadem of Ravenclaw.
metadata.source_text: I’m acting on Dumbledore’s orders, I must find what he wanted me to find!

metadata.description: There’s a secret passage into the Hog’s Head that we can use to get students out of the school without drawing Voldemort’s attention to their departure.
metadata.source_text: There’s a way... the passageway leading into the Hog’s Head.

metadata.description: I now believe I can't just run — I have to stay and search for Horcrux-related objects even though Voldemort is coming; this is what Dumbledore wanted.
metadata.source_text: I can’t... There’s something I need to do.

metadata.description: I feel that the teachers, especially McGonagall, will stand and defend Hogwarts for me while I look for the hidden object; she agreed to secure the school.
metadata.source_text: We shall secure the school against He-Who-Must-Not-Be-Named while you search for this — this object.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events in the castle, so I don't know the immediate happenings or what was said there.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I was not there for the confrontation at Hogwarts and therefore didn't witness the duel, Snape's escape, or the students' planned evacuation.
metadata.source_text: Absent: Harry Potter, Hermione Granger, Ron Weasley

metadata.description: I asked Professor Flitwick if he knew where the diadem of Ravenclaw was, and I learned from him that the diadem is long lost and nobody has seen it in living memory.
metadata.source_text:
— Protego Horribilis — the diadem of Ravenclaw?
"A little extra wisdom never goes amiss, Potter, but I hardly think it would be much use in this situation!"
"I only meant — do you know where it is? Have you ever seen it?"
"Seen it? Nobody has seen it in living memory! Long since lost, boy!"

metadata.description: I felt desperate and panicked when I heard the diadem might be lost, which changed my thoughts about what the Horcrux could be and made me realise we might be missing something big.
metadata.source_text:
"Seen it? Nobody has seen it in living memory! Long since lost, boy!"
Harry felt a mixture of desperate disappointment and panic. What, then, was the Horcrux?

metadata.description: I noticed Ginny looking at me pleadingly when she wanted to join the fight, and because I shook my head at her, I felt a bitter ache at letting her down even though I thought it safer for her to stay.
metadata.source_text:
"My whole family's here, I can't stand waiting there alone and not knowing and —"
Her eyes met Harry's for the first time. She looked at him beseechingly, but he shook his head and she turned away bitterly.

metadata.description: I wasn't present during these events at Hogwarts and therefore I do not know the details of the preparations, the discovery about the diadem, or the reunion in the Room of Requirement.
I wasn't there to change any opinions or beliefs about the battle preparations or the diadem because I was absent from the scene.
I wasn't present, so I didn't witness or alter any relationships among the Order, Dumbledore's Army, or the Weasleys during this particular sequence of events.
I wasn't in the Room of Requirement or at the castle during these exact moments, so I don't know what was said by teachers, who arrived from the tunnel, or what Percy said upon returning.
I can't claim any changed beliefs from this scene because I wasn't present to witness the discussions, the evacuation orders, or the family reconciliation.
I was absent, so I did not experience any updates to my relationships with Ginny, Percy, or other members of the Order during the events described.
I've learned that the lost Ravenclaw diadem was hidden by Helena Ravenclaw in a hollow tree in an Albanian forest and that Tom Riddle later took that information from her.
metadata.source_text: He tracked me to the forest where I was hiding. When I refused to return with him, he became violent. — It remained where I had hidden it when I heard the Baron blundering through the forest toward me. Concealed inside a hollow tree.

metadata.description: I worked out that Voldemort must have retrieved the diadem from Albania and then returned it to hide it at Hogwarts, probably the night he asked for a job at the school.
metadata.source_text: — the night he asked for a job! — He hid the diadem in the castle, the night he asked Dumbledore to let him teach!

metadata.description: I'm suddenly certain the diadem could be at Hogwarts and that finding it is urgent if we want to finish Voldemort off; this search just became the main thing for me to do.
metadata.source_text: If that diadem’s at Hogwarts, I’ve got to find it, fast.

metadata.description: I feel a sharper distrust of Tom Riddle; he could be charming and flattering to get what he wanted, and he used that to manipulate Helena Ravenclaw out of the diadem.

metadata.description: I notice Hermione gets so out of breath she can't speak; it makes me more aware of how much stress affects her in tight moments.
metadata.source_text: Hermione so out of breath she could not speak.

metadata.description: I'm so out of breath I can barely speak after running, which shows how winded I get under stress.
metadata.source_text: Hermione so out of breath she could not speak.

metadata.description: I find Ron's suggestion about Crookshanks ridiculous in the moment; his idea didn't seem sensible to me when we're trying to work out a getting-in plan.
metadata.source_text: “Crookshanks?” wheezed Hermione, bent double, clutching her chest.

metadata.description: When Ron blurts out pet-based ideas I feel exasperated; it makes me think he sometimes relies on pets instead of spells.
metadata.source_text: “I can — see the place — if we just had — Crookshanks again —”

metadata.description: I managed to make a twig fly using Wingardium Leviosa when we needed something to reach the Willow trunk.
metadata.source_text: Ron looked around, then directed his wand at a twig on the ground and said, “Wingardium Leviosa!”

metadata.description: I thought we might need Crookshanks, but I changed my mind and realised I could do a simple levitation spell myself.
metadata.source_text: “I can — see the place — if we just had — Crookshanks again —”

metadata.description: I know Hermione gets flustered and breathless and I feel a bit protective and also a bit embarrassed when she reacts sharply to my ideas.
metadata.source_text: “Crookshanks?” wheezed Hermione, bent double, clutching her chest.

metadata.description: I realized the snake was literally guarding Voldemort and that to get to Voldemort I would have to deal with the snake first.
metadata.source_text: The only way forward was to kill the snake, and the snake was where Voldemort was, and Voldemort was at the end of this tunnel. . . .

metadata.description: I hesitated because I thought Voldemort wanted me to come and might be leading Ron and Hermione into a trap, so my certainty about acting on impulse changed into wary determination.
metadata.source_text: Voldemort wanted him to do this, wanted him to come . . . Was he leading Ron and Hermione into a trap?

metadata.description: I felt the weight of responsibility for Ron and Hermione—I'm aware they're trusting me and following me, and Ron's shove showed they're ready to back me, which makes our bond even more urgent.
metadata.source_text: Harry hesitated. ... "Harry, we’re coming, just get in there!" said Ron, pushing him forward.

metadata.description: I've managed to stop the writhing tree by jabbing near its roots; the tree became still when I struck it.
metadata.source_text: It jabbed at a place near the roots, and at once, the writhing tree became still. “Perfect!” panted Hermione.

metadata.description: I felt relief and a quick shift from tension to confidence when the tree went still — I recognised that my action had immediate, crucial effect on our path forward.
metadata.source_text: It jabbed at a place near the roots, and at once, the writhing tree became still. “Perfect!” panted Hermione.

metadata.description: Seeing Harry hesitate made me more ready to support him; I am part of the team that must get him through, and my precise action helped make that possible.
metadata.source_text: “Perfect!” panted Hermione. “Wait.”

metadata.description: I learned that Harry needed a shove to move into the tunnel because he was hesitating, so I pushed him forward and told him we were coming.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, we’re coming, just get in there!" said Ron, pushing him forward.

metadata.description: I felt urgency and a change from anxious waiting to decisive action when I pushed Harry — I believed we had to be bold rather than stand back.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, we’re coming, just get in there!" said Ron, pushing him forward.

metadata.description: By physically pushing Harry and saying we were coming, I showed that I trust and will stand by him; our friendship is proven by backing him into danger to help him succeed.
metadata.source_text: "Harry, we’re coming, just get in there!" said Ron, pushing him forward.

metadata.description: I looked down and realised the body being carried in was Colin Creevey — he must have sneaked back into the grounds even though he was underage.
metadata.source_text: Colin Creevey, though underage, must have sneaked back just as Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle had done.
metadata.scene_title: Bodies Brought In; Colin Revealed Dead

metadata.description: Seeing Colin so small in death has shaken me; I can't think of him as just that noisy kid with a camera anymore — it's real and awful now.
metadata.source_text: He was tiny in death.
metadata.scene_title: Bodies Brought In; Colin Revealed Dead

metadata.description: I feel differently about those like Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle — if Colin followed their example and got himself killed, my opinion of their influence is darker and more dangerous.
metadata.source_text: Colin Creevey, though underage, must have sneaked back just as Malfoy, Crabbe, and Goyle had done.

metadata.description: Seeing Neville lean against the door and look like an old man changed how I feel about him; I now realize he’s far more exhausted and worn down than I might have thought.
metadata.source_text: Neville leaned against the door frame for a moment and wiped his forehead with the back of his hand. He looked like an old man.
metadata.scene_title: Neville Steels Himself and Harry Searches the Hall

metadata.description: Watching Neville set off down the steps again to recover more bodies makes me respect him more; I believe he’s brave and selfless enough to keep going despite how drained he looks.

metadata.scene_title: Harry Resolves to Leave; Night Outside

metadata.description: I felt I would have given all the time remaining to me for just one last look at them, and then realised I might never have the strength to stop looking, so I decided it's better not to look.
metadata.source_text: He felt he would have given all the time remaining to him for just one last look at them; but then, would he ever have the strength to stop looking? It was better like this.
metadata.scene_title: Harry Resolves to Leave; Night Outside

metadata.description: I know how much Hermione, Ron, Ginny and the Weasleys mean to me — I'm desperate to see them, which shows how deeply bound I am to them even when I can't find them in the Hall.
metadata.source_text: but he could not see any of the people he loved, no hint of Hermione, Ron, Ginny, or any of the other Weasleys, no Luna.

metadata.description: I've decided I must do something alone and important, and I'm prepared to lie about handing myself over so Neville won't stop me.
metadata.source_text: No," Harry lied easily. "'Course not . . . this is something else. But I might be out of sight for a while.
metadata.scene_title: Harry and Neville Discuss Nagini and the Horcrux Plan

metadata.description: I feel the need to reassure Neville and keep him from panicking; I trust him enough to tell him part of the plan but not everything, so our bond is tense but still strong.
metadata.source_text: "Where are you going, alone?" Neville asked suspiciously. "It's all part of the plan," said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Harry and Neville Discuss Nagini and the Horcrux Plan

metadata.description: I wasn't present during the events in the grounds at nearly four in the morning, so I don't know what happened between Harry and Neville.

metadata.description: I now believe Neville can take my place in the secret so the number of people who know about the Horcruxes stays at three; I feel we must trust others to continue if necessary.
metadata.source_text: Dumbledore had died knowing that three people still knew about the Horcruxes; now Neville would take Harry’s place: There would still be three in the secret.
metadata.scene_title: Emotional Goodbyes and Vision of Loved Ones

metadata.source_text: We’re all going to keep fighting, Harry. You know that?

metadata.description: I'm suddenly convinced that I'm almost at the end — I can feel I'm nearly there, very close, and that changes how I think about what comes next.
metadata.source_text: You are nearly there," said James. "Very close. We are . . . so proud of you.

metadata.description: Seeing James and Sirius reassure me makes me feel their pride and care; I'm aware they are proud of me and that comforts me in a way that deepens how I see them.
metadata.source_text: You are nearly there," said James. "Very close. We are . . . so proud of you.

metadata.scene_title: Harry Asks for Companionship; Tension at Voldemort’s Camp

metadata.scene_title: Voldemort Awaits; Harry Prepares to Surrender

metadata.source_text: whose heart was now throwing itself against his ribs as though determined to escape the body he was about to cast aside.
metadata.scene_title: Final Exchange: Voldemort Pronounces His Mistake

metadata.description: I decided I must not be tempted to fight — I took off the Invisibility Cloak and hid my wand because I want to stop myself from resisting, even if that feels like giving up.
metadata.source_text: He did not want to be tempted to fight. "I was, it seems . . . mistaken," said Voldemort. "You weren't."
metadata.scene_title: Final Exchange: Voldemort Pronounces His Mistake

metadata.description: I can see Bellatrix's worship for Voldemort plainly; she watches him with fascinated eyes and won't contradict him when he silences her, so I know her loyalty is fanatical and unshaken.
metadata.source_text: Bellatrix had spoken: She sat closest to Voldemort, disheveled, her face a little bloody but otherwise unharmed. Voldemort raised his hand to silence her, and she did not speak another word, but eyed him in worshipful fascination.
metadata.scene_title: Final Exchange: Voldemort Pronounces His Mistake

metadata.description: I learned that Voldemort destroyed the bit of his soul that was inside me — that piece has gone and my soul is whole and my own.
metadata.source_text: Yes, he destroyed it. Your soul is whole, and completely your own, Harry.

metadata.description: I realised that Voldemort used my blood to rebuild his body, and because my blood carried Lily's protection, that tethered me to life while he lives.
metadata.source_text: He took your blood and rebuilt his living body with it! Your blood in his veins, Harry, Lily’s protection inside both of you! He tethered you to life while he lives!

metadata.description: I thought I should be dead because I meant to let him kill me, but Dumbledore has convinced me that dying didn't happen the way I expected and that my sacrifice altered things.
metadata.source_text: I should have died — I didn’t defend myself! I meant to let him kill me!" "And that," said Dumbledore, "will, I think, have made all the difference."

metadata.description: I see Dumbledore as both utterly content and deeply repentant; I'm beginning to understand his remorse and the weight of his past decisions about the Hallows and his family.
metadata.source_text: You know what happened. You know. You cannot despise me more than I despise myself.

metadata.description: I learned that Grindelwald tried to stop Voldemort from getting the wand and even lied about never having had it.
metadata.source_text: Grindelwald tried to stop Voldemort going after the wand. He lied, you know, pretended he had never had it.

metadata.description: I found out that Dumbledore once used the Resurrection Stone; he put it on hoping to see Ariana and our parents and was cursed by the ring.
metadata.source_text: When I discovered it, after all those years, buried in the abandoned home of the Gaunts — the Hallow I had craved most of all, though in my youth I had wanted it for very different reasons — I lost my head, Harry. I quite forgot that it was now a Horcrux, that the ring was sure to carry a curse. I picked it up, and I put it on, and for a second I imagined that I was about to see Ariana, and my mother, and my father, and to tell them how very, very sorry I was. . . .

metadata.description: I changed the way I think about Dumbledore: I now see he was deeply fallible, selfish at times, and yet capable of remorse — he wasn’t the infallible teacher I once thought.
metadata.source_text: I was such a fool, Harry. After all those years I had learned nothing. I was unworthy to unite the Deathly Hallows, I had proved it time and again, and here was final proof.

metadata.description: My understanding of Dumbledore shifted; I now feel both compassion and disappointment toward him because he admits his mistakes and the reasons behind his manipulations.
metadata.source_text: I am afraid I counted on Miss Granger to slow you up, Harry. I was afraid that your hot head might dominate your good heart. I was scared that, if presented outright with the facts about those tempting objects, you might seize the Hallows as I did, at the wrong time, for the wrong reasons.

metadata.description: I heard that Voldemort became obsessed with the Elder Wand after your borrowed wand beat him and after kidnapping Ollivander revealed twin cores, so Voldemort sought the wand to be invincible.
metadata.source_text: I have been sure that he would try, ever since your wand beat Voldemort’s in the graveyard of Little Hangleton. At first, he was afraid that you had conquered him by superior skill. Once he had kidnapped Ollivander, however, he discovered the existence of the twin cores. He thought that explained everything. Yet the borrowed wand did no better against yours!

metadata.description: Dumbledore told me I have a choice whether to go back and face Voldemort or to board a train away; he made clear that returning is my decision to make.
metadata.source_text: “I’ve got to go back, haven’t I?” “That is up to you.” “I’ve got a choice?” “Oh yes.” Dumbledore smiled at him. “We are in King’s Cross, you say? I think that if you decided not to go back, you would be able to . . . let’s say . . . board a train.”

metadata.description: I was not present during this King’s Cross conversation between Harry and Dumbledore, so I did not witness their exchange or the revelations about the Hallows.

I learned that Narcissa Malfoy came right up to me and asked if Draco was alive and in the castle; she needed to know about her son more than anything else.
metadata.source_text: "Is Draco alive? Is he in the castle?"
metadata.scene_title: Narcissa Declares Draco Dead; Voldemort's Triumph

metadata.description: I realised Narcissa no longer cared whether Voldemort won if declaring me dead would let her into Hogwarts to find Draco; her priorities had shifted to her son.
metadata.source_text: She no longer cared whether Voldemort won.
metadata.scene_title: Narcissa Declares Draco Dead; Voldemort's Triumph

metadata.description: After she confirmed Draco's fate to me and then shouted that I was dead, I understood Narcissa's actions differently — she was bargaining for her son rather than loyalties to Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: "He is dead!" Narcissa Malfoy called to the watchers.
metadata.scene_title: Narcissa Declares Draco Dead; Voldemort's Triumph

metadata.description: I learned that if I go completely limp and keep still the Death Eaters can be fooled into thinking I'm dead; they handled me roughly but didn't check for a pulse while Hagrid sobbed over me.
metadata.source_text: he kept himself floppy and lifeless, and when he fell to the ground for the last time, the clearing echoed with jeers and shrieks of laughter.

metadata.description: I've come to believe that showing myself at the right moment can surprise even Voldemort; pulling off the Invisibility Cloak and casting Protego proved I could act when they least expected it.
metadata.source_text: “Protego!” roared Harry, and the Shield Charm expanded in the middle of the Hall, and Voldemort stared around for the source as Harry pulled off the Invisibility Cloak at last.

metadata.description: I feel a deeper, painful loyalty to Hagrid — he carried me gently despite everything and sobbed for me; knowing he would risk himself and grieve makes me care all the more for him.
metadata.source_text: the enormous hands that lifted him into the air were exceedingly gentle. Harry could feel Hagrid’s arms trembling with the force of his heaving sobs; great tears splashed down upon him as Hagrid cradled Harry in his arms

I know there are no more Horcruxes left; it's just him and me now, and one of us has to go.
metadata.source_text: There are no more Horcruxes. It’s just you and me.

metadata.description: I used to be seen as someone who survived by accident, but I don't think that any more — I meant to do what I did, and that choice matters.
metadata.source_text: Accident, was it, when my mother died to save me?... Accident, that I didn't defend myself tonight, and still survived, and returned to fight again?

metadata.description: I won't let Voldemort hurt the people here ever again; I've done what my mother did and their protection comes from my willing sacrifice and intent.
metadata.source_text: I was ready to die to stop you from hurting these people — "— I meant to, and that's what did it. I've done what my mother did. They're protected from you.

I know that Severus Snape’s Patronus is a doe — the same as my mother’s — which proves he loved Lily Potter for nearly all of his life.
metadata.source_text: Snape’s Patronus was a doe," said Harry, "the same as my mother’s, because he loved her for nearly all of his life, from the time when they were children.
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogwarts — Reveal and Confrontation

metadata.description: I know that Albus Dumbledore chose the manner of his own death months beforehand and arranged it with Snape rather than being simply killed by Voldemort.
metadata.source_text: "Yes, Dumbledore’s dead," said Harry calmly, "but you didn’t have him killed. He chose his own manner of dying, chose it months before he died, arranged the whole thing with the man you thought was your servant."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogwarts — Reveal and Confrontation

metadata.description: I believe Dumbledore was not weak but cleverer than Voldemort — a better wizard and a better man — and I hold that conviction calmly against Riddle’s insults.
metadata.source_text: "No, he was cleverer than you," said Harry, "a better wizard, a better man."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogwarts — Reveal and Confrontation

metadata.description: I now see Severus Snape as Dumbledore’s spy and loyal to Dumbledore from the moment Voldemort threatened my mother, rather than as Voldemort’s servant.
metadata.source_text: "Snape was Dumbledore’s, Dumbledore’s from the moment you started hunting down my mother. And you never realized it, because of the thing you can’t understand."
metadata.scene_title: Arrival at Hogwarts — Reveal and Confrontation

metadata.source_text: I killed Severus Snape three hours ago, and the Elder Wand, the Deathstick, the Wand of Destiny is truly mine!
metadata.scene_title: Elder Wand Mastery and the Final Duel

metadata.description: I've changed how I see Dumbledore's plan: it's not that his plan failed for me, it's that it seems to have gone wrong for Voldemort instead.
metadata.source_text: Yes, I dare," said Harry, "because Dumbledore’s last plan hasn’t backfired on me at all. It’s backfired on you, Riddle.
metadata.scene_title: Elder Wand Mastery and the Final Duel

metadata.description: I think of Tom Riddle as less than a man when he won't try for remorse; I call him "Riddle" and urge him to be a man, which shows I've moved from hatred to trying to force him into conscience.
metadata.source_text: Be a man . . . try . . . Try for some remorse. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Elder Wand Mastery and the Final Duel

metadata.description: I know that Severus Snape was never the true master of the Elder Wand because he never defeated Dumbledore; Dumbledore remained the wand's last true master.
metadata.source_text: Severus Snape was never the true master of the Elder Wand. He never defeated Dumbledore.
metadata.scene_title: Victory, Standing Ovation, and Conversation with Dumbledore

metadata.description: I've changed how I think about wand ownership: I believe that simply possessing or taking a wand doesn't make it truly yours — the wand chooses its wizard.
metadata.source_text: Possessing the wand isn’t enough! Holding it, using it, doesn’t make it really yours. Didn’t you listen to Ollivander? The wand chooses the wizard. . . .
metadata.scene_title: Victory, Standing Ovation, and Conversation with Dumbledore

metadata.description: I now see Voldemort as dangerously self-deceived; his confidence in having stolen the Elder Wand is based on misunderstanding, not true mastery, which makes him more vulnerable than he believes.
metadata.source_text: You still don’t get it, Riddle, do you? Possessing the wand isn’t enough! Holding it, using it, doesn’t make it really yours.
metadata.scene_title: Victory, Standing Ovation, and Conversation with Dumbledore

metadata.description: I learned that the Elder Wand recognized a new master before Dumbledore died — someone who never even touched it — and that the true master was Draco Malfoy.
metadata.source_text: The Elder Wand recognized a new master before Dumbledore died, someone who never even laid a hand on it. "The true master of the Elder Wand was Draco Malfoy."
metadata.scene_title: Repairing the Wand; Plans for the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I used to think only physical possession mattered, but I now believe wand allegiance can transfer through disarming and not just by taking a wand physically.
metadata.source_text: You no longer have the phoenix wand: We duel on skill alone . . . and after I have killed you, I can attend to Draco Malfoy. . . ." "But you're too late," said Harry. "You've missed your chance. I got there first. I overpowered Draco weeks ago. I took this wand from him."
metadata.scene_title: Repairing the Wand; Plans for the Elder Wand

metadata.description: I've changed how I see Draco Malfoy — I hold power over the wand he lost, and that makes our connection different; I know I beat him and took his wand weeks ago.
metadata.source_text: "But you're too late," said Harry. "You've missed your chance. I got there first. I overpowered Draco weeks ago. I took this wand from him."

metadata.description: I've learned that the thing hidden inside the Snitch fell in the forest and I don't know its exact spot; I'm not going to search for it again.
metadata.source_text: “The thing that was hidden in the Snitch,” he began, “I dropped it in the forest. I don’t know exactly where, but I’m not going to go looking for it again. Do you agree?”
metadata.scene_title: Final Decisions about the Elder Wand and Farewells

metadata.description: I don't want the Elder Wand anymore; even knowing how powerful it is, I'd rather be happy with my own wand and not carry that power.
metadata.source_text: “I don’t want it,” said Harry.
metadata.scene_title: Final Decisions about the Elder Wand and Farewells

metadata.description: I feel Dumbledore's enormous affection and admiration for me in this moment; his approval comforts me as I decide to keep Ignotus's gift and return the Elder Wand.
metadata.source_text: “I’m putting the Elder Wand,” he told Dumbledore, who was watching him with enormous affection and admiration, “back where it came from. It can stay there.
